10790: In a certain place there is a swamp with a pool in which a church once sank. Some men try to bring the bell up. They succeed, 'in God's name', as one remarks. When the other adds: 'Let it be in the devil's name too', the bell disappears into the depths again. Since then all attempts to bring it up have been in vain. Every Christmas night it can be heard ringing.
13123: A woman goes mad when she hears that her ancestors' estate is being sold to strangers. She flees the convent where she is living at the time and comes back to haunt the rooms of her ancestors' house. She wears a white nun's habit that is easy to see at night. Because she wears a dark hood, her head is not noticed. That is why people think a headless woman wanders the ruins.
13132: Two brothers are in love with the same girl, Alix. The girl chooses one brother, Waleram. Reginald, the other brother, is so furious about this that he murders both Waleram and Alix. Afterwards he regrets his deed and goes to a hermit, who asks God how Reginald must do penance. Reginald must walk to an ocean, accompanied by two spirits. There he will be taken aboard a black ship, where the spirits dice for his soul for all eternity. This ghost ship is still seen on the North Sea six centuries later. Valkenburg castle, where the murder took place, is also still haunted.
13218: A couple in love are walking together across the heath. The boy needs to pee and disappears behind a bush. Before he goes, he warns the girl about werewolves. He gives her a handkerchief that she must stuff into the werewolf's mouth. The beast will then disappear at once. When the girl walks on a little further, a werewolf does indeed come at her. When she stuffs the handkerchief into its mouth, it disappears. The girl runs home and is overtaken a little later by her boyfriend. He has some bits of handkerchief in his mouth, so the girl knows that he was the werewolf. She broke off the relationship.
13227: A white lady walks along with a farmhand and at a certain moment says something unintelligible.
13228: A werewolf usually appears in the shape of a monster or a shaggy dog. On lonely roads a werewolf often rides along on a wagon by jumping onto it and throwing its legs around the driver. After a while the werewolf disappears by jumping onto a pollard oak. It is said that at the spot where a castle and moats once stood, the werewolf often leaps on people. One evening a carter drives past this spot. A werewolf jumps onto his wagon and, by its heavy weight, makes the horse soaked with sweat in a short time.
13230: A mysterious spirit roams about, dwelling in hillocks along lonely roads. When someone passes that spot, that person walks very heavily and with difficulty. He gets lost and does not get home all night. It is said that the person then gets tinne- or teeneschoenen (tin shoes) on.
13231: A man behaves so strangely that people start following him, and they discover that he crawls into a hollow tree and comes out as an animal. The priest advises burning the skin found in the tree. The priest says prayers; the man has to be held down because he wants to pull the skin out of the fire. After the skin is burnt, the man is freed from the devil and no longer has to be a werewolf.
13232: A drunken man meets a man carrying a boundary stone at night. The man asks the drunkard again and again: "Where shall I put it?", and the drunkard answers that he should just put the stone back where he got it. At that very moment the bearer of the boundary stone vanishes.
13233: Someone who has moved a boundary stone walks around with the glowing stone, sighing and asking where he should put it. A farmer who hears this advises the apparition to put the stone back where he found it. After hearing this answer, the apparition vanishes.
13462: In the evening the werewolf jumps on a walker's back and rides along as far as a crossroads. The walker is so frightened by the werewolf that he gets a nosebleed. When the walker comes home, his family knows at once from the nosebleed that he has carried a werewolf. The victims of a werewolf are mostly poachers or smugglers who ply their trade at night.
13463: Ghost cats try to rub against the legs of walkers in the evening. When the walker accidentally kicks the cat, he is suddenly surrounded by a great many cats. The cats walk along as far as a crossroads. When a ghost cat bites someone in the evening, the wound will never heal. An old woman who was bitten in the leg by a ghost cat remained lame for the rest of her life.
13478: A farmhand walks home in the dark in the evening. Several evenings in a row he hears a sound following him, but he cannot see what it is. On an evening with bright moonlight he discovers that a large wolfhound is following him. When he gets home he tells his wife to heat the poker red-hot the next evening, because he is determined to catch the dog and bring it home. The next evening he is indeed strong enough to get the dog home, but when his wife holds the poker ready, the dog suddenly begins to speak. It turns out that the dog is his dead neighbour, who committed a crime. After his death he must still atone for the crime by bothering people on dark evenings in the shape of a dog. The farmhand lets the dog go. He has not seen it since.
13479: Poachers hear barking and the rattling of chains and claim they were chased by phantom dogs.
13480: A man strikes a black tomcat on a gate that blocks his way, whereupon the tomcat says he should try it again. The man also hears the cat laugh, and believes it must have been a witch or the devil.
13526: A rich merchant goes away on business. When he comes home again, he expects his beloved daughter to be waiting for him, but all that awaits him is a fearful silence. Searching his house, he discovers that all his treasures have been stolen and his little daughter has been murdered. Embittered, he leaves the city, but after his death his ghost keeps returning to the churchyard where his daughter is buried. Every night, at the stroke of twelve, the merchant's ghost is seen riding to the churchyard in a fiery carriage without a coachman. No one can stop him.
13527: The foundations of a castle that once stood there still lie in the woods. The legend goes that around midnight a white lady who used to live at the castle is seen haunting those woods.
13528: A will-o'-the-wisp was said to be the soul of a newborn, unbaptised child, floating between heaven and earth, because it could not stay on earth but could not go to heaven either. It was also thought that the will-o'-the-wisp was the luminous marsh grass that moved along like a ball just above the ground.
13529: A mower cutting grass at midnight sees a white lady. When the white lady reaches a ditch, she does not jump over it but floats across it. The mower flees. The mower's neighbour thinks the man probably saw a poacher or smuggler with a white sheet around him. It might also have been someone who wanted to frighten young girls.
13531: Ghost cats follow people who are out alone at night, and then vanish as suddenly and silently as they came. A man who goes to play cards at the priest's on winter evenings is followed by such a ghost cat every time. When the priest blesses the cat, the creature disappears.
13648: At the spot where the ruin of a small castle stands, the "Juffer zonder Kop" (Headless Maiden) wanders every night at twelve. After the last part of the ruin is demolished, the ghost is no longer seen wandering either.
13649: A white ghost hare runs across the market square at night. When someone passes by, the hare jumps onto his shoulder and starts scratching and biting the walker. After a while the creature jumps back to the ground and suddenly vanishes.
14781: On Christmas Eve three cursing and blaspheming men ask a strange gentleman dressed in black to play cards with them. When one of the players goes to pick up a card that has fallen on the floor, he sees that the stranger has goat's feet. He makes the sign of the cross and the stranger disappears through a hole in the wall that never closes again.
14783: A man on his way to the midwife is hindered in all kinds of ways by someone invisible, for if the midwife comes too late, mother and/or child may die in childbirth, and the devil gains a soul if the child has not been able to receive emergency baptism.
14786: The devil's role in building the cathedral in Aken. He lends the money on condition that the first to enter the finished church falls into his power; the builders' trick; the devil's rage leaves the print of his thumb; the devil gives up his attempt at revenge by burying the church, which creates two hills; the devil's curse means that work on the church never ends.
14791: The devil joins in a card game and keeps losing. At midnight the devil scrapes with his horse's hooves, grabs all the money and vanishes.
14794: At night, after an encounter with a black cat, a wagon that is not heavily loaded cannot go any further.
14795: After sunset sunken lanes are avoided; people with a bad conscience in particular may have to deal with a dark figure with claws.
17888: The korenwolf (corn wolf, a field spirit) jumps on people's backs at night and they have to carry him until he disappears again.
35585: A farmer who had stolen land from his neighbour during his life comes back as a ghost after his funeral with a ball of fire on his shoulders, asking: "Where can I put it?" He moves the boundary posts back and is released.
35588: Every evening after dinner Sjang goes out and does not come back until very late. One time they follow him and see him take something out of a tree, and a moment later he was a werewolf. The priest is fetched and Sjang has to produce his things. Out came a sheepskin and a red stick with a red ribbon; these are burnt in the oven while three men hold Sjang down. When everything is charred, he says he is freed.
35589: Some men decide to play cards on Christmas night (to stay awake). At a quarter to twelve three want to stop, but the fourth wants to go on, even if it is with the devil. Then a neat little gentleman comes in and wants to join. He lets the others win handsomely and they forget the time. Then a card falls and one of the players bends down to pick it up and sees to his horror that the stranger has horse's legs. He points this out to the others and they all shrink back, and when the devil comes at them, the one in front makes the sign of the cross, which stops the devil in his tracks. The others also make the sign of the cross and the devil disappears, whereupon the men hurry to the church to confess everything to the priest. He drives out the stench with prayers and the innkeeper has his tavern converted into a farmhouse.
35591: The witch prevents a man who is going to fetch help from the friars from making any progress.
35592: Jan goes to fetch help from the priest, but on the way someone stops him and Jan turns back. When the priest comes later, it is too late; soon the pigs die.
35593: The butter-making fails and the witch doctor came and has them look into a bucket of water. They see Fien's face and the man blames her. She is kept away and the butter has not failed since.
35597: A witch made mice without tails, because she could not make tails.
35602: A miller who is constantly bothered by a cat has had enough and chops off one of the animal's hind legs with his chopper. When he gets home, his wife is lying on the floor with a leg missing.
35603: To get rid of a black cat, you must strike it with a blessed club. Some neighbour woman would then become lame, and she is the witch who had turned herself into the cat.
35606: The witches met in Boshoven, and when my father saw a whole procession of cats going there, he knew they were witches.
35608: A man shoots at a hare, but it simply stays sitting; after 3 shots the shooter gives up.
35609: A man unmasks a witch by walking in her footprints; she looks round and stands as if nailed to the spot.
35614: Every night a white mare appears at a farm, and it disappears around midnight.
35615:
A quarry worker boasts that he will kick a black cat. When he gets home, a black cat is sitting there and he says:
"Why, pussycat, what are you sitting there like that for?"
to which the cat says:
"Why, you drunken fool, what are you asking that for?"
35626: A farmhand who is really a gnome is given permission to go to the fair once he has broken up the manure. He sticks a pitchfork into a dung heap and speaks a formula, after which pitchforks appear in many dung heaps and break up the manure. The farmhand never returns from the fair.
35628: If you shot with shot blessed by a priest, the hare was always dead.
35636: At Christmas you can hear the sunken bells ringing in the Peel.
35643: A hare shot and wounded around midnight gets up and runs away. The bloodstains lead to the house of a woman with shot in her body.
35666: A man from Germany saw witches in a wine cellar in Cologne.
35671: A man met a witch; she said nothing and quickly left, but the man could no longer find his way and wandered around for an hour.
35678: The devil jumps through the window; a newly fitted pane breaks at once, despite the priest reading prayers over it. After a friar reads prayers over it, the pane stays whole.
35684: A man is troubled by mice, suspects a witch, and the priest comes to bless his house and the plague is over.
35700: Gnomes vanish because people no longer want to pay them.
35701: Will-o'-the-wisps - the souls of unbaptised children - lure people to the water and make them lose their way
35724: A dog in the churchyard keeps growing bigger and suddenly disappears.
35725: Witches flew on broomsticks to Germany to feast and dance in wine places.
35730: If the werewolf did something to you, it was your own fault. I never had any trouble from him, except that I once had to carry him, but that wasn't so bad. Sometimes I also put some food outside and in the morning it was always gone.
35732: The ghost of a man who had moved a boundary post was released when someone called out to him to put the post back where he had taken it from.
35742: The child cries for no reason, but was stroked by Marie, who shows the father a little doll with a cut in its back. The father wants to have it, gets it after much nagging, throws it in the fire, and the child stops crying.
35753: Sounds of a party in the attic disappear after a friar from Achel prays.
35757: Elves make people lose their way.
35763: You must not beckon to will-o'-the-wisps. The narrator released a light by saying: "I baptise you alone."
35775: Bert's horse will not go on at Nel's house, and she tells him to come in for a little drink. He does so, and then the horse will go on again.
35780: On the advice of the friars, people look for white mice in the stable; about twenty are caught, and after that the animals are no longer troubled.
35785: Seeing the devil's coach brings misfortune.
35787: Our house was haunted; rattling could be heard from twelve to one.
35803: A wandering witch predicts a thunderstorm and makes the unbeliever lose his way.
35810: When the boys want to share out the apples they stole from the witch Alda, they find toads in their pockets.
35819: A farmhand works at night in the haunted mill. At 12 o'clock black cats come in one by one (although everything is locked). Suddenly he chops off a foreleg of the boldest cat with his mill bill hammer, and in the morning sees a trail of blood to the room of the miller's wife, whose fingers have been cut off (and he quits his job).
35822: A girl promises a barrel of oil to the church every year if she does not keep her promise of marriage. She marries someone else but does not give the oil. After her death she comes to haunt the family until a priest sends her away to the Gravenberg, where she is still often heard calling: "They could help me, but they won't!"
35828: Pears received from a witch, which one must not eat, have turned into toads after a year.
35832: A friar attacked by a robber fixes him to the spot and leaves him standing there until he returns.
35833: A farmer sees that his farmhand is being helped to spread the manure by aardmannetjes (earth men, little underground people) who do the heavy work.
35834: A young witch learns the spell for going to the wine cellar in Cologne and goes there with a completely inexperienced friend, but says the spell wrong: "through hedge and bush" and "never out again". In the morning they are found and burned at the stake that same day, but they repent at the stake, to the sorrow of the devil, who flies through the air as an owl.
35835: Someone sees lights dancing in the fens and flees from them.
35839: A wandering ghost, a mover of boundary posts, is released by a grumpy farmhand who says: "Put it, dammit, where you got it!"
35840: A farmhand becomes a werewolf by means of a leather belt, which he hides. It is found and burnt in the oven; at once the suspected farmhand comes rushing up on horseback, but he is held back, and when the belt has burnt he says: "I am freed!"
35854: A werewolf jumps on a man's back and he has to carry it halfway up the hill. He thinks of having it bled at the place where he was baptised. Tis the smith drags the rugplakker (back-clinger), holding it by the legs, to Sjaak's café, where he bangs open the door and quick Peerke gives the monster a slash, so that blood streams from its head and there stands the farmhand of the "Beese" (a farm in the area), who runs off at once, after which nothing more was heard of the werewolf.
35858: A miner heard a bell thudding. A bell sank there, but it was a heavy stone.
35860: The old mother of a miner heard a mysterious knocking at the back door and says it is Death wanting to come in. Three days later her son died in a mining accident.
35869: A man makes witches' grease from a recipe in a thick Latin book and rubs himself with it, but says the formula wrong and flies through instead of over hedge and bush, so that all his clothes are torn from his body. He also summons a ghost, the spirit of the count of Lichteberg, who has been dead for 300 years. He takes the company up to the attic for a demonstration, speaks some fake Latin, the hatch opens and a yellow head appears on an iron suit of armour, at which the company flees.
35872: People try to burn a werewolf's iron collar in the oven, but the werewolf is there at once and takes it out.
35875: In the evening a man hears barking, shouting, etc. in the air, sees nothing, and runs away.
35876: Late one evening two men pass the Grechter woods and hear beautiful music on the so-called Paap, at which one says: "Step on my foot." He did so and at once they flew over the woods to the Paap, and the cap got caught in an oak. The one immediately joins the revellers, the other watches until the first has had enough and says again: "Step on my foot." On the way back they pick up the cap. From then on the second man wanted nothing more to do with the first.
35879: Ghost coach seen by a small group out late.
35882: A man out late sees the ghost of the Kruisveld, a dishonest farmer, who keeps calling: "Where shall I put it?" He means the boundary stone he had moved at his neighbour's expense. Peet gets angry and shouts at him to put the stone where he got it from.
35883: A man who is attacked at night by a werewolf cuts it. Afterwards he hears that the landlady of the café where they had talked about the werewolf has been wounded in the leg.
35886: In the old days children were frightened with scary stories about witches, for example that black cats are witches. Two men see a cat sitting in a passageway and strike at it, whereupon the animal says: "Do that again!" Little wreaths were found in the pillow of a sick child, and a woman from the neighbourhood was accused of having caused the child's death. It is said that witches fly through the air to go to the sabbath, that a cross of straws on the threshold stops them, and that they bewitch cattle.
41852: A girl promises to marry, and if the marriage does not happen, to give a barrel of oil for the sanctuary lamp in the church. She marries someone else anyway, forgets her promise and dies. Her restless soul returns, but a clergyman manages to banish the ghost.
41856:
The Gravenberg is haunted. An unsuspecting passer-by sometimes receives a blow but sees no one.
A boy finds a great treasure in a crevice in the hill but does not dare take it with him. When he later returns, there is nothing left to find. But the mocking voice of the mountain spirit is heard saying that the treasure can no longer be found.
A girl promises to marry, and if the marriage does not happen, to give a barrel of oil for the sanctuary lamp in the church. She marries someone else anyway, forgets her promise and dies. Her restless soul returns, but a clergyman manages to banish the ghost. Her plaintive voice is still heard: they could have helped me, but they would not.
43985: In the area around Heerlen it is said of someone who has moved the boundary posts that after his death he floats between heaven and earth, or between heaven and hell.
44337: The owner of Schaloen castle puts up a Calvary group (John and Mary in a little chapel, with a crucifix in the middle) to drive away the evil spirit Ruprecht.
46011: It was said that a treasure lay buried on the Kempen heath. Two poor farmers went treasure hunting at night. One night they struck a chest. The devil had entered them; they were blind with greed. With great effort the farmers tried to pull the chest out of the deep pit. Satan suddenly made the ropes snap, a nasty roar of ghostly laughter was heard, and the chest sank deeper into the heath than ever before. The men fled. The treasure has remained there as a warning to those living nearby: do not be greedy!
46364: At the very time the owner of a bewitched horse is with the parish priest, the horse can eat again. The priest gives him relics to put in the doorposts.
46365: A wreath in a bed, a sign of approaching death, cannot be pulled apart. A farmer suspects his farmhand of witchcraft, sends him to work elsewhere and throws the wreath into the baking oven. At once the farmhand is standing by the oven. After the wreath is burnt, the farmhand is freed from the devil.
46369: When a witch strikes a cart, the cart fills up with rats.
46370: Fire-man jumps onto people's backs in the dark and makes them carry him.
46371: Bewitchment at night stops when the family comes to sleep there.
46372: A witch bewitches the cows, which then roam loose outside.
46375: Witte wijven (white women) disappear because of the friars; much witchcraft stopped by ringing the Angelus and by prayer.
46377: The daughter of a witch who can conjure tailless mice will also make mice with tails once she has mastered witchcraft.
46383: People could make playing cards dance.
46385: A card player on Christmas night lets in the devil, who is driven away after being prayed over.
46388: A werewolf that wants to leap on a man does nothing when the man draws his knife, and then disappears.
46392: A witch's family can make mice without tails.
46487: The work of a witch's son is bewitched.
46495: After a cat has fallen into the brewing kettle, the brewer's wife is burned.
46690: A rabbit that has been hit stays sitting.
46691: An unhittable hare is hit with a silver bullet; afterwards there are shot holes in the witch's clothing.
46942: A werewolf also lived in Budel. His werewolf belt was burnt, and after that he was freed from being a werewolf.
46966: At Budel there is a bell in the Kattenkuil that rings on Christmas night.
49013: After the father's death, neighbours help the son lay out the body. One of the neighbours smells something strange and goes outside when the cardboard in front of a window pane falls and a black tomcat sits on the corpse's belly. When the other neighbour throws the dead man's clothes into the fire, they immediately catch fire. A strong sweet smell hangs in the house of the deceased.
49017: Vare Kwöëbke, who has sold his soul to the devil, can therefore ride through the air. When the priest riding along feels a jolt, the driver says they have hit a church tower.
49018: Vare Kwöëbke may only go to the fair once the work in the field is done. He stands at a corner of the field, binds a sheaf and speaks a formula, after which all the sheaves are bound.
49019: After a witch has touched his shoulder, a man is covered in lice. The priest gives a few stumps of the Easter candle which must be laid on the threshold. The witch then cannot get in, and the lice disappear.
49020: Black cat walks along with a woman, will not be chased away and follows her inside. The cat is thrown out of the house, but is immediately inside again.
49021: On the way, being followed by a ghost that flies over the group.
49041: A woman regarded as a witch predicts to a girl that she will soon die, which comes true.
49070: Seeing a black cat at night; a black cat is seen as a bringer of misfortune.
49140: A man who is afraid of nothing believes that the newspaper that flies against him and sticks there is a haunting.
49508: The werewolf turns out to be the man who had warned about the werewolf. When the skin is burned, the man still tries to grab it.
49531: A knight has made a pact with the devil allowing him to live in great wealth for seven years, but afterwards he must give up his soul, which must atone forever. On the eve of surrendering to the devil he gives a great banquet, with a farewell toast to St. Geertrui. On the way to the devil the saint accompanies him, so that the devil cannot exercise his power. The man afterwards lives piously.
57959: A man who deliberately stretched the boundary of his property cannot find rest after his death, and calls out asking where he should put down the boundary stone.
57961: In the evening a horse walks along with a man.
57964: After a black cat that bewitches horses at midnight is struck, the cat turns into a woman.
57967: With a book of spells a boy can make mice without tails.
57969: Werewolf leaps on people in the evening; as a helper with work; transformation into a werewolf by putting on a hidden coat, release after the coat is burned.
57977: A white woman who roams a castle is the soul of a lady of the castle who cannot find rest as punishment for a crime.
57979: A boundary-stone mover who asks on his deathbed where he should leave the stone is told: where the stone came from.
57981: A blacksmith who notices that his wife disappears at midnight tests whether she is a witch.
57982: After being touched by a woman who was said to be a witch, a man has lice.
57984: On a Sunday a hunter wounds a hare, which tells him that he cannot catch it.
57987: The soul of a count who lets the riverbank erode can find no rest.
60730: To banish ghosts and spirits, the help of a clergyman, usually a friar, is called in. The devil can torment and tempt exorcists, but in a monastery the devil does not feel at ease.
60733: A woman suspected of witchcraft passes on lice and makes people ill.
60737: Black is the colour of the devil and death; black cats and dogs bring misfortune; black cards, and spades in particular, hold mysterious powers. The jack of spades is the personification of the devil.
60739: Card players in league with the devil can, by manipulating the jack of spades, make a person who has been talked about come to them. The person does not come by appointment, but by chance or because they feel an urge to come.
60741: Werewolves leap on people, cling to their backs and cause a choking feeling. A werewolf in the shape of a dog accompanies a young man when he meets a girl.
60986: In a pool lie bells that ring on Christmas night.
60987: Use of rye flour as mortar.
63724: Speaking a formula that makes manure spread.
63727: The nightmare (mare) falls on people lying in bed and cuts off their breath; the oppression disappears after asking what is the matter.
63728: Black dog disappears if it is not struck without reason.
63729: Remarks on ghostly apparitions, the returning dead.
63730: Haunting in a house as long as the place of a hidden money treasure remains unknown. After the money is discovered, it is handed over to the heirs.
69249: A premonition of who will soon die.
69250: On stormy nights witches fly about with fiery whips.
69252: At midnight a baker lets in a black cat, which invites six others, after which he throws hot water over the cats. The next morning he finds that his wife has burns.
69254: Witch's daughter can make almost living mice; she is delivered by a friar.
69255: Witches appear mainly as black cats, but also as white and grey ones, never as three-coloured ones.
69258: Breaking a spell on a churn with holy water.
69264: A farmhand who has to turn into a werewolf is freed by burning his little book of magic.
69265: A gun loaded with spurrey seed to shoot the werewolf is reloaded with shot. After the werewolf is shot down, it turns out that their own farmer has been shot dead.
69266: A rich man who wants to own even more has such a hard death that a priest praying over him sweats heavily, and the devil has been present in the shape of a dog.
69267: A cursing man is carried off by the devil, but is released by the devil after he starts to pray.
69270: Robbers leave when a knife struck into the table begins to quiver.
69274: A voice asking where it should put it down is advised to put the boundary stone back in the same place.
69365: Supposed witch must have been the hare the man met.
69366: A witch can be recognised when she looks round at someone who crosses their feet in her footprints.
69367: After speaking a formula, a hunter shoots and turns out to have killed a wolf.
69372: A wizard uses the jack of spades to order a bottle of wine, which immediately appears on the table.
69377: Origin of the name of a hill; lights floating at night at the site of the murder.
69379: A headless woman turns out to be a rolling bush.
69380: Farmhand who can break up manure in a short time turns out to have done it with a little book of magic.
69383: The ghost of a boundary-stone mover finds rest after being advised to put the boundary stones back in the same place.
69384: At night a witch rides horses; after the priest gives a blessing, nothing happens any more.
69392: Summoning work spirits who do the work by reading formulas from a little book of magic. Release from the spell through prayer and the burning of the book of magic by a chaplain.
69396: Imprint of fingers and thumb on the window pane of a wicked man's house; while the man was dying, a large black dog roamed about.
69401: At night a witch rides horses, which in the morning are sweaty with braided manes and tails. After a black cat is wounded, a naked woman is found in the morning who says she is a witch.
69407: The belief that a child got lice from a witch who stroked its head.
69409: A werewolf must be carried all the way home.
69420: Advice to put a moved boundary stone back in its original place gives the man who moved it rest.
69430: A witch makes a mistake when saying the formula for flying on her broomstick.
69434: A black cat sings back in answer to the question of where it comes from.
69652:
A woman in Schinnen always went to fetch water at the well, and by the well house lived an old woman with a hump on her back. The young woman was afraid of the old woman, but her husband never understood why, since the old woman never did her any harm. "Our Lord always said you must beware of those marked by God, and she is, with that back of hers."
One day the young woman fell very ill and had to stay in bed for several days. One night a cat was screeching so loudly outside that the man, out of sheer frustration, threw a drinking bottle at it. It struck the cat hard, and instead of a cat's yowl they heard a human scream.
When the man went to fetch water at the well house in the morning, he saw the old woman with a huge blue lump on her face.
The young woman died of her illness, and less than two weeks later the old woman from the well house left the village.
69745:
A poor farmer once made a pact with a stranger. He would serve the man, and in return the farmer would be as rich as he wished. The farmer's children would also profit from this wealth, but not the third generation.
In the third generation the farm caught fire. They rebuilt the farm three times and each time it burned down again. Then they had no money left and were forced to beg.
126958: Something strange happened when a man died. Another version is that a prank was played by dressing the corpse and sitting it in a chair.
126982: At night near churchyards the devil jumps onto the backs of people's necks.
127014: The devil turns the winnowing mill in the evening.
127017: In the dark the devil unties cows standing in the stable.
127018: The devil in the shape of a goat that knocks on the windows with its forelegs.
127114: A big black dog that comes into the house in the evening and leaves again after a while is taken to be the devil.
127115: On Christmas night a castle sank into a fen as punishment for feasting during midnight mass and refusing to give alms to a beggar.
127148: Some have even played cards with the devil on Christmas night.
127149: A werewolf rides people; the devil is a kind of helper.
127153: Depiction of the devil as a creature with goat's legs and two horns on its head.
127159: In a fen lie stolen bells that ring at midnight on Christmas night.
127162: On Christmas night the bells of a sunken church ring. Aardmannetjes (earth men) living in the area vanish after a church is built, because they cannot bear the sound of the bells.
127168: A werewolf, or devil, jumps onto people's necks and makes them walk round in circles; after he has vanished they are bathed in sweat.
127175: The devil in the shape of a large dog lies under the bed of a dying man who has committed many crimes, and disappears when the man has confessed.
127178: A man can never get rid of the letter he receives from a distinguished gentleman.
127210: Bells ringing in a pond on Christmas night.
127247: A stolen tower bell sinks into a swamp and is later found again.
127268: A hanging bell with which a bellmaker jumped into a fen rings at twelve o'clock at night.
127307: The devil makes the jack of spades dance on the table.
127640: Someone was pulling straw out of a straw stack and then cats jumped over his arm, dozens at a time. They were all witches.
127641: In the old days, if a cat sat on the bridle path, it was a witch.
127643: In Geffen a man had lived a wicked life. He was laid out, and then a black dog lay on him. The priest was to pray it away, but when it left, a terrible stench remained.
127645: In Geffen some rough fellows had been out. One brother asked the other: "Are you there, Cornelis? Where have you got to?" But there was a club foot, with horse's hooves. And that was the devil.
127906: A woman had lived a wicked life. In the old days the neighbours came to keep watch. And when she had died, a small black dog came and sat under the coffin. And that was considered to be the devil.
127910: We had a cats' dance. In the evening a cat would sit in the cart track. They would strike at it, and in the morning a woman in the neighbourhood would be lying in bed with a broken head.
128290: At night in the stable, a farmhand sees a cat braiding the horses' manes. He throws his knife at the cat. At the church, an old woman with a cloth around her head gives the knife back.
128293: The closer magpies sit to the house, the worse the news. Others think it means good news instead.
128294: Owls announce death, but they may also be drawn by the night light beside someone gravely ill.
128298: If they saw a cross in the sheet, someone there would die.
128299: A goldsmith had a sick daughter. When the daughter was cured through a pilgrimage to Kevelaer, the goldsmith promised to offer a golden shoe and went on a pilgrimage to Kevelaer. On the way, near Ottersum, the goldsmith was robbed and murdered. The robber had to flee and hid the golden shoe in the sand of the road. The robber was later caught and hanged. In dry, clear weather the robber returns as a vuurman (fire man) to search for the golden shoe. On misty nights the goldsmith comes looking for the golden shoe. A farmer working with his ox at night met the vuurman. He held his hands over the ox's eyes so the animal would not be frightened by the vuurman, and prayed a few Our Fathers himself until the vuurman had passed.
128420: The woman foresees a death. His shirt was too small.
128450: A German Pole could get far more work done than others. He always did it alone. His piece rate was lowered twice, but he did more and more. His little helper could hardly haul enough wood. They never found out how he did it. The place is still called In der Duvel.
128693: If someone is not buried before a Sunday, another person will die.
128694: Blooming out of season brings a wedding or a death.
128709: 'The old man' is a section that is no longer worked. Someone was chased by the old man. He only just managed to escape.
128717: Around Christmas, Carnival and Easter there are more accidents in the mine than usual. A mysterious knocking at the back door was said to come from Death wanting to come in. The miner who goes in and out through this door dies three days later in an accident in the mine. Miners made their Christmas confession early because it was thought that the mine claimed its victims around Christmas.
128731:
Long ago a farmer lived in Kessel-Hout who got on badly with his wife. One Sunday afternoon he went for a walk with her. He pretended to see a large pike swimming in a pool and urged his wife to come and look at it more closely. He then pushed her into the water and she drowned. From then on lights floated above the pool at night. It was said to be the soul of the murdered woman, who could find no rest.

According to the book 'Baerlo' by Henry de l'Escaille, this folktale turns out to have a historical background. On 20 May 1707 a man was convicted of murdering his wife with a poker and hiding her body in a marsh. He was sentenced to death. He was beheaded at night. His head was placed on a stake facing the marsh. According to the narrator, the place of execution matches that of the folktale.
128732: Five men were keeping a wake for the dead. To pass the time, they played cards and drank. One man said he could do with another bottle. Another man said he knew a way. He threw a playing card outside, and a bottle floated into the room and circled the man's head three times. The other men had to catch the bottle before the end of these three rounds, or it would be smashed on their companion's head. One man caught the bottle in time. The men emptied the bottle that night and never dared to speak of the incident again.
128739: A farmer from Helden was out trading cows. He called in at a house and asked the woman whether they had a cow for sale. They did not, but the woman kept him talking for a while. Suddenly the man noticed that the butter churn standing there was going up and down without the help of hands or machinery. The man left in a hurry. He had heard it said that the woman practised witchcraft.
129903: A man holding his own head in his arms came down from the attic in the evening, usually around November. He sat down by the fire, began pulling the hairs out of his head one by one and threw them into the fire. This could go on for hours. Anyone who came into the room where the man sat got a blob of blood in his face. It was said that the man was an uncle who had been murdered or an uncle who had committed suicide. He had been haunting the house for centuries. The day after the man had been there, a small accident always happened. For example, the pan caught fire or someone fell down the stairs.
129905: An orphan girl is bullied in the orphanage by a nun and everything is taken from her. After the girl has died of illness, the nun becomes pregnant by a friar with whom she is having an affair. As soon as the child is born, the dead orphan girl appears and takes the nun's child away from her.
129907: In an old castle in Tielen there was a blue room that was haunted. At night a woman came there. She sat down and did nothing else; she only came to look. Children did not dare sleep in that room.
129909:
An old woman in Maastricht who lived in a house built over the little river Jeker (Boven de Jeker) was said to be a witch. She was ugly and had many cats. She supposedly turned children into cats.

Maastricht also has the Heksenhoek (Witches' Corner). A witch once lived there.
129910:
You could recognise witches by the fact that they flew at night, never prayed, and crossed themselves with the left hand and the wrong way round (from bottom to top and from right to left). When they walked past a church they spat towards it. They were terribly anti-Catholic. When a priest came by or someone prayed the rosary, a witch would run off screaming. But sometimes this made a witch turn good.
There were also male witches. They were tall and thin, with hollow eyes and big noses. They wore big, dirty hats and flapping coats.
129911: On the Sint-Pietersberg, by the little chapel of Saint Roch, stood three trees that sometimes turned into witches. They would then roam around the Sint-Pietersberg and spread mischief in the surrounding villages. At sunrise the witches turned back into trees.
129912: On the fourth step of a staircase in a house, some people felt a hand on their shoulder. It was a broad man's hand with long fingers. The hand was not malicious, rather fatherly.
129913: Houses and objects can give off a certain feeling. This can be pleasant (sweet) or unpleasant (eerie, oppressive). A feeling of recognition is also possible: a place you think you recognise, although you have never been there.
129914: While out hunting, a man meets a cat. The cat does not want the man to hunt birds. The birds belong to the cat. But the man is not afraid of the cat and simply walks on. The man's dog, however, behaves fearfully. The cat follows the man and keeps talking to him. When the man keeps walking on, the cat leaps onto his neck. The animal grows heavier by the minute, until the man collapses. When the cat asks the man whether he understands now, the man says yes. The man shot nothing more that day.
129929: As a young girl, a nun was visited at night by a procession of the dead. The dead were all people she knew, such as a grandmother, uncles and aunts. The dead told her that she would enter the convent. According to them she had to enter the convent because she was so ugly that she would never find a husband anyway, and because she found men creepy.
129930:
A woman is staying the night in a castle and in the evening walks down the corridor in her nightclothes on her way to the toilet. She meets another woman, fully dressed. The woman smiles. On the way back from the toilet she meets the same woman again, only now she is wearing different clothes. The woman says only: "Don't touch me."
The next morning she asks who the woman was that she met in the corridor during the night. It turns out to be Aunt Amalia, who has been dead for twenty years.
129931: A cat suddenly took on a strange posture in front of a cupboard that used to be a fireplace. Legs braced, fur on end, ears flat and tail up. The cat hissed softly, but actually seemed too frightened to hiss or growl. After a while the cat calmed down again.
129973: Some ways to determine whether someone is a witch.
129999:
On Christmas Eve a gentleman with a horse knocked at a farm. He asked whether he could eat something and rest, and let his horse drink. The farmer let the gentleman in. After the meal the gentleman asked whether the farmer would play a game of cards. The farmer loved that, so they played cards.
At some point the farmer's wife wanted to leave for the village for midnight mass. But the farmer was winning and wanted to finish the game. No problem, said the gentleman, for he had two fast horses. The farmer could take the left horse and the gentleman the right one, and they would easily be in time for midnight mass. The wife, the maid and the farmhand could go ahead with the cart.
The farmhand was surprised, because the gentleman had only one horse. But when he went outside to look, there were indeed two horses. The farmhand did not trust it and decided to swap the horses: he put the left horse on the right and the right horse on the left.
At five to twelve the game was over and the gentleman and the farmer quickly jumped on the horses; the gentleman on the right horse and the farmer on the left. Just before the village they rode past a marsh. By now it was three minutes to twelve. Suddenly a large horse came out of the mists of the marsh. The animal neighed, and the horse the devil was riding (for the gentleman was really a devil) flew headlong into the marsh and sank into the depths. The large horse disappeared into the mist again.
The farmer's horse simply kept going and the farmer arrived at the church just in time. When he got off his horse and wanted to tie it up, there was no horse beside him any more. The horse had vanished.
130000: A young man, Sjang, had a sweetheart in another village. On Sundays he went to see her, but when he went home again in the evening, he had to pass through an area said to be haunted, especially near a little bridge over a brook. His friends asked him whether he wasn't afraid, but the young man said he wasn't even afraid of the devil. So his three friends, Graad, Peer and Driek, decided to play a joke on him and give him a fright. The three friends dressed up as devils and hid by the little bridge, waiting for Sjang. While they sat there waiting, dressed as devils, one of the friends discovered that there were four of them. Frightened, he warned the other two. The friends jumped up and saw a real devil, much bigger than themselves. The devil grabbed one of the boys, Peer, by his clothes. In doing so the boy's clothing tore open and his scapular, with a cross and an image of Mary, became visible. With a tremendous thunderclap the devil disappeared. Peer had been saved by his scapular.
130003:
A man lived rather remotely. On Christmas night he wanted to go to the village to attend midnight Mass. His wife was ill and could not come along.
On the way to the village he passed the Galgenberg, and on the slope he saw an enormous dog with fiery eyes, a devil. The animal growled. The man was afraid and did not dare go on, but he did not want to go back home and miss midnight Mass either, because he wanted to pray for his sick wife.
Suddenly the moon broke through the clouds, and in the moonlight the man saw the cross on the church tower gleaming in the distance. The church bells began to ring for midnight Mass. At this the great dog began to howl. The creature looked round to see where the noise was coming from and its eye fell on the cross. With a tremendous howl the devil dog crossed the road and vanished into the marsh.
130004: This is not really a story in itself, but an addition to VODA_030_04. The narrator says there are several stories about Christmas night and the devil, and he tries to establish what might be true / historically accurate in the story (VODA_030_04) he told earlier.
130008:
A seer predicted that the vast area of marsh, water and heath between Echt, Waldfeucht, Montfort and Posterholt would be reclaimed and turned into fertile farmland with a church, monastery and village on it. This actually happened.
This seer also predicted the following: when the Wandering Jew finds a home, women can no longer be told apart from men, and people fly through the air like birds, then the antichrist will be born. And when the antichrist is grown, the world will end.
130147:
In the nineteenth century the area around Montfort consisted of marshes and pools. People preferred not to venture there after dark. A human-like shade could be seen there, the Vuurman (Fire Man). The poisonous breath of the Vuurman could make people ill. People then got 'het kaaj', or 'the cold', a kind of cold marsh fever. Perhaps people fell ill from the vapours rising from the marsh. Popular tradition held that these were the spirits of criminals whom the lord of Montfort had driven into the marsh without confession.
The marshes have since been drained and turned into meadows, and the disease has long since disappeared.
130281: A man is quite certain that he met a particular woman at night in the shape of a black cat.
130357:
A son and father who live together on a farm often quarrel. One day it comes to blows and the son wants to throw his father off the farm. He drags his father outside, across the yard. By the farmhands' quarters, near the horse stable, the man's deceased grandfather, the father's father, suddenly appears at the spot where he died.
The grandfather tells the man not to drag his father any further than here; that is as far as he dragged his own father.
The son then takes his father back inside, and from that day on they quarrel no more.
131736: Driving away a black dog only succeeds by putting a bit of the wick of the Easter candle with the bullet, after which the dog is hit. The next day a man turns out to have been shot in the leg.
131738: Burning the skin means that the farmhand is freed from playing the werewolf.
131739: A werewolf that makes itself carried falls off a person after that person stabs it with a dagger blessed by priests.
131741: Cats warm themselves when invited and leave when asked to.
131747: A silver coin in the churn to ward off bewitchment.
131748: A rat catcher makes rats come to a bundle of straw where they are burned. The one who says he has no rats gets them.
131750: In the morning the horses have braided manes and tails and the cows are loose in the stable.
131751: A ghost in the form of a young noblewoman is driven away by friars; every year she comes one step back.
131752: Haunting stops when the wish of a restless dead person, that a promised mass still be said, is granted.
131753: A voice asks where it should put it down; it is released after, on a clergyman's advice, it is told to put it down where it got it.
131754: Encounter with a large black dog that walks along.
131755: After being wounded, a werewolf loses its power.
131756: Werewolf loses its power when a person, on the friars' advice, lights a new pipe at a certain spot.
131758: In the evening an encounter with two dolls; after they have vanished, a girl wanders about at night and in the morning sees a tall man at the farm.
131760: Girlfriend and mother turn into witches and fly after rubbing themselves with ointment and saying a spell. The boyfriend does the same but says the spell wrong. He arrives at a witches' gathering; when he names Jesus, everything vanishes and he ends up on a roof.
131761: After a call for a fourth card player, a gentleman appears who turns out to have horse's hooves. The gentleman disappears, leaving a stench behind, when a clergyman blesses him and reads prayers over him.
131763: Hare does work for someone; can work magic.
131764: A werewolf leaps on a man, makes itself carried and disappears.
131765: A rat catcher sends rats and mice.
131768: After a man has struck a cat off a gate, the cat tells him to do it again.
131769: Gun will not fire because it is bewitched by a witch; after the bullet is dipped in holy water, the shooting succeeds.
131772: Fear of meeting the werewolf in the evening; the werewolf makes itself carried.
131777: After a baker refuses to rent her a house, a witch bewitches the dough so that the loaves do not rise. The curate blesses the bakery, after which the spell is broken.
131778: A witch bewitches a farmhand as punishment.
131779: After praying, a woman releases a dead person who returns at night.
131783: A boy goes bald after a witch has stroked his head.
131785: Boy is recognised by the fringe of a handkerchief between his teeth.
131788: Belief that a certain street is haunted; an ox that has broken loose is mistaken for a ghost.
131789: A miller who has bought himself out of fighting in the Holy Land mocks those who do go. In the mill he meets the devil, who takes him to hell, shows him the glowing chair and says he will be sitting in it within three days. The next day the miller is found unconscious and dies after three days.
131791: Witch tells men that their shooting will fail; after they put something from the Easter candle on the gun barrel, the shooting succeeds.
131794: No stories about playing cards with the devil, but there are stories about a werewolf that leaps on people after an evening of cards.
131795: A man gets lost in a meadow he knows well and cannot find the way out.
131796: A black cat blocks passers-by's way; a black cat on the windowsill where a sick person lies.
131798: A man has to go about at night as a werewolf wearing an animal skin; after the skin is burnt, the power is broken.
131801: A man has borrowed money from the devil but cannot pay it back. With tricks he manages to prevent repayment. After the last trick the devil lets him off the debt.
131805: Sighting of a headless woman dressed in white.
131806: A parish priest who returns after his death is banished by a clergyman and comes one step back each year. A man who is hindered on his way by a clergyman wants to shoot him, but his revolver does not fire.
131808: Sighting of a group of cats and a woman who simply vanish.
131810: Meeting a werewolf who makes someone carry him. A sorcerer who catches and burns rats and mice has the power to send rats and mice to people.
131813: A man gets lost and finds the right road after calling on Mary.
131815: Rat and mouse catcher sends rats and mice to people.
131816: The devil's hasty flight is the reason why the church door of the cathedral has come off its hinges.
131819: A man hears the air full of music without anything to be seen.
131822: After shooting at a hare, a woman lies on the ground.
131825: Gnomes work at night in people's homes. They mistake green peas for bombs and flee.
131829: Heard it said that people have to carry the werewolf.
131832: A werewolf, already waiting when a person passes by, makes itself carried.
131835: A woman's invisible follower vanishes after she speaks an incantation and makes the sign of the cross.
131836: Putting holy water in the milk to keep the churning from failing.
131837: A cat on a gate blocks a man's way.
131840: Suspicion that, to lower the farm's rent, it was staged that everything in the dairy had fallen over.
131841: The child feels pain in the place where the witch sticks needles into a doll.
131849: Suddenly seeing human skeletons with the wind blowing through them; seeing a gallows with human skeletons hanging from it.
131852: A wager with the devil over a soul. The man gets his soul back if the devil cannot load a cart with live frogs.
131856: A man has the ace of clubs set down drink, but nobody dares to fetch it. When the man goes to fetch the drink himself, he comes back frightened.
131860: After the werewolf has been beaten by local residents, it becomes known who the werewolf is.
131866: Milk that has disappeared was said to be the work of the devil, witches or ghosts.
131867: In the morning the cattle are loose in the stable and the horses' manes are braided.
131868: At night gnomes polish copper and tin in exchange for food; they stop coming when they are teased.
131869: A werewolf is released when his skin is burnt in an oven.
131871: Boy feels he has to go werewolfing; on a walk he gives a girl a little box that she must throw at the werewolf, and goes off. A werewolf comes at the girl, who throws the box at it. The werewolf disappears, the boy returns.
131874: As punishment for cheating with the weight of sacks of grain and watering down milk, a rich man has a long death struggle.
131875: A stjoephond (night dog) is someone who turns into a dog at night; driving away a black cat by making the sign of the cross.
131878: A horse stands still because a ghost is blocking the way. After the Gospel of St John is read, the horse moves on.
131879: A man is helped by the devil when he cracks a whip.
131881: The day after a man dreams that he cuts off the head of his former wife with a scythe, he receives news that she has had a fatal accident. After her burial in unconsecrated ground, the woman haunts the area in white clothing and without a head.
131883: A witch is injured after the snout of a black cat is burned.
131884: Girl must be a witch, because when the boy leaves, a white dog walks part of the way with him, and the next time the girl knows what happened on the way.
131886: Large white dog blocks the road on the way there and back.
131890: Dog accompanies man as far as the church, where the dog starts whining and will not go past.
131891: Kitten keeps growing bigger along the way, disappears into a hedge where nothing can be seen.
131893: After midnight foals trot around a person, which is seen as the devil or witches' tricks.
131899: After a cat prowling around the house is kicked, a woman has a broken arm; a boy keeps bleeding despite help.
156116: On the Diesterbaan towards the Locht, Pier V.D. had seen an ugly ghost. Only people with a special gift could see ghosts.
156132: A rural policeman walking through the woods heard chattering near a tree in which witches were sitting. The man then cut a piece of bark from the tree so he could recognise it later. The next day the policeman announced that he knew where the witches were hiding. When he climbed the tree with a ladder, however, there was nothing more to be seen.
156138: One evening a match seller asked a farmer for shelter. Because the farmer had no room left, he said: "I have another house a bit further on, but I don't know if you'll come out of there alive". The match seller was not afraid and accepted the offer. At midnight the man sat at the table reading a book. At that moment all the doors suddenly flew open and a ghost came in. The man acted as if nothing was the matter and simply kept reading. The ghost broke open a wall, took money out of it and began counting it on the table. Afterwards the money was put back in the wall. At two o'clock the ghost left. The match seller waited a while and then took all the money out of the wall. When the farmer came in the morning to ask how the night had gone, the man said he had seen the ghost. He said not a word about the money. "Then catch the ghost", said the farmer, and the man answered: "All right, I will. Tonight I'll stay here alone once more, but the next night you must give me three farmhands". When the farmhands came, of course no ghost appeared any more. The farmer was very pleased because he could rent out his house again. A year later the farmer was threshing with his farmhands when a rich man suddenly came up and asked whether there was anything for rent nearby. "Don't you recognize me?", the man asked. "I'm the one who freed you from the ghost last year!" The farmer replied: "No, that can't be, because that was a poor match seller!"
156140: A woman who claimed she was afraid of nothing went to the churchyard to fetch bones. When she was about to take some bones, a voice suddenly said: "Keep off, those are mine!"
156156:
On the Genker-hei, the Meeuwer-hei and the Mechelse hei, a witch from Diepenbeek could bewitch the farmers' carts in the fields.
There was also haunting at the big stones, at Lewie G.'s and at the Kolersberg.
156174: Marie M., a fat woman from Diest, came peddling shirts and other goods. When a child died at the 'Bözzeke', people believed Marie M. was responsible for the misfortune. The parish priest did not want people to make such accusations.
156175: A thief who had broken into the church of Zutendaal could not get away; he was stuck in the window. A painting was made of the scene, and it still hangs in the church.
156183: Will-o'-the-wisps appeared everywhere in the ditches along the old road. They were souls from purgatory.
156201: A girl was walking home in the evening with her mother. When the two women were in the Bloemenstraat, they saw a chain rolling across the ground. A week later they saw a lady in a white apron appear at the same spot.
156211: Will-o'-the-wisps usually appeared at places where a murder or something similar had happened. The lights were usually seen between three and five in the morning.
156213: A young man from Vliermaal who was going to see his girlfriend was warned as he left about a large dog with chains. On the way the young man was attacked by the dog. After a long fight, the boy managed to wound the animal. The next moment the werewolf changed into a man, who begged him not to tell anyone. The young man replied: "No, as long as there are people, I won't tell it to the trees!" Then another long fight followed.
156219: A child was bewitched after accepting a handkerchief from a woman in the village. When the handkerchief was set on fire, the witch came knocking at the door, but they did not let her in.
156224: Whenever the village witch had been somewhere, the children always had something wrong with them.
156237: One evening a man went to a meadow in Horpmaal where he had heard witches' music. The man took two valuable sticks with him. When he got home, he put the sticks beside his bed. The next morning the sticks had turned into straws.
156246: Lowieke F. drove to Scherpenheuvel together with Marie, a blind woman. When in the marshland between Zichem and Averbode a will-o'-the-wisp suddenly settled on the horse, Marie said: "Put the whip in the water so you can baptise the light!" Then Lowieke said: "I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit". At that moment the horse fell. Because Marie had broken her leg in the accident, Lowieke had to drive back home.
156264: A man who was always tormented by the werewolf one day stabbed the beast in the head with a knife. Because the werewolf was wounded in the place where he had been baptised, he changed into a human and said: "If you betray me, I will tear you to pieces!" The man replied: "I will never tell a living being." When the man went to church on Sunday, he turned to the wall and said: "I have made a werewolf turn into a human, but I may not say who it is. That is why I am telling you." Thus the werewolf was released.
156275: A hard-working man who had no children had to work hard to make ends meet. His lazy brother, who had seven children, did not work at all. When one day the man complained to his brother, the brother said: "Why don't you do the same as me? At night I ride a goat to faraway lands to steal there. If you want to come along, come on Thursday evening. But I must warn you of one thing: don't speak of Our Lady or Our Lord on the way, or it will end badly!" The next Thursday the man went to his brother, who at half past eleven fetched the goats from the stable. The two men each sat on a goat, while the lazy brother said: "Over wood and bush! Out through the clouds!" At that the goats flew high into the air. After a while the hard-working brother said: "I hope it isn't much farther. Jesus, Mary, how my backside hurts on this sharp back!" No sooner had he spoken than the goat threw the poor man to the ground. When the man had recovered from the shock, he looked for the way home. Where he had ended up, people said: "Belgium is far from here. You'd best keep going straight in that direction; then you'll get there." The man travelled seven years, seven weeks and four days before he came home again. When he knocked, his wife asked: "Who's there?" The man answered: "It's me, your husband!", whereupon the woman cried: "That can't be, for my husband is lying beside me in bed." The woman had been convinced her husband was dead, and she had remarried. The frightened goat rider ran away and was never seen again.
156281: A boy who always visited friends in the evening was always followed by a big black dog near a ditch on his way home. Usually the boy just left the dog alone. One day, however, he turned around and got angry at the animal. At that the dog changed into a man.
156286: Two men were bringing in the hay when a thunderstorm suddenly blew up. Since the men had only one pitchfork, one of them quickly went to fetch another so the work would be done fast. The woman who gave the man a pitchfork was a witch. The man died because he had worked with a bewitched pitchfork.
156288: Zjanke G. went to Hasselt with a wheelbarrow to fetch fifty kilos of coal. On the way Zjanke suddenly saw a will-o'-the-wisp appear. Because the man believed it was his dead wife, he whistled at the light. The next moment the whole road was lit up, so that the man was frightened to death.
156297: A man said that he was struggling with a plague of rats in his house. Another man then said: "Shall I kill all the rats in your house in one go?" "Can you do that, then?" asked the man. "Certainly," answered the other, "I take a bundle of straw and put it in the meadow. Then I lure all the rats to the straw, after which I set the whole bundle on fire." The man became frightened, however, and said: "No, that is something like witchcraft. We'll get rid of the rats some other way."
156304: A man who had turned into a private road saw a cat sitting on a barrier. The man struck at the cat, but the animal jumped back onto the barrier. The same thing happened a second time. Before the man went to strike the cat a third time, he said: "If you dare jump back up there now, I'll hit you so hard that you'll fly away!" The cat answered: "That doesn't matter, because you'll never come here again anyway."
156317: A baby had been born in a house in Heppeneert. The child's aunt lived across the street. One day the aunt came to visit and touched the child. When the child died some time later, the parish priest was sent for. The priest cut open the child's pillow and found a large wreath of flowers in it. On the priest's advice the family moved to Bocholt.
156322: A little boy had been to mass and to catechism class on Sunday. When the boy came home, his mother saw that the child was completely covered in lice. The mother then burned the new clothes the child had worn that day. Giving someone lice was the least evil a witch could do to a person.
156324: Two boys who lived on the Bonderkuil became paralysed because someone had bewitched them. After the priest had read prayers over the boys, they recovered.
156325: A farmer who had weighed out too little grain all his life had to haunt after his death. The ghost had to come and weigh grain every night. The friar advised the farmer's descendants to pay for the damage. After a chapel had been built, the farmer's soul finally found rest.
156335: A man from Dilsen had a farmhand who could turn himself into a werewolf. When the werewolf's band had been thrown into the oven, the loudly roaring farmhand had to be held back so that he would not jump into the fire. As soon as everything had burnt up, the farmhand left, never to return.
156340: In Overrepen a woman had shouted under the seamstress's window: "When I am dead, I will come haunting here. You will even be too scared to come outside!" After that woman's death, the seamstress's house was indeed haunted.
156345: A woman from Beverst had had a miscarriage. The child then came back haunting so that someone would baptize it.
156346: Will-o'-the-wisps often floated above swamps and meadows. They were the little souls of unbaptised children. Whoever saw a will-o'-the-wisp had to pray until it had disappeared and gone to heaven.
156347: Along the road from Rekem to the mill of Boorsem stood a few hedges and bushes behind which the werewolf hid. The werewolf often leapt onto a passer-by's neck and then had itself carried a little way.
156351: When Nol had gone pruning, he was followed on the way back by a dog with a chain. Nol fought the dog until he saw a chance to run away. A little further on, however, the man was attacked again by the dog, which was in the ditch. Nol wrapped the dog in a piece of barbed wire and fled. Since then he has never seen the dog with the chain again.
156356: On a farm worked a farmhand who could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmer heated the oven extra hot to burn the farmhand's collar. While the farmhand had to go and buy yeast in Weert, the farmer threw the collar into the oven. The moment the band caught fire, the farmhand was standing beside the oven to save his possession.
156358: Witches could infest people with lice by making a certain movement with their hands. If they leaned over a pram, they could bewitch the child.
156365: Witches always tried to get near children. When they stroked a child's head with their hand, the child was covered in lice. It also sometimes happened that children began to cry at night because they had seen the witch. Bewitched children had to be overlezen (exorcised by reading prayers over them).
156375: In a house where a cat always came in at night, someone once broke the animal's leg. The next day a neighbour woman had a broken leg.
156383: A man who had come to live on a farm in Ellich was warned by the people about a place where it was dangerous to walk alone because it was haunted.
156388: A certain K. could make mice from a handful of earth.
156394: On the Stokrooie bridge a cat always roamed about, blocking the way of passers-by. When one day someone had stamped on the cat, people knew who the animal was.
156407: A man who had moved a boundary post had to stand in the field as a ghost after his death, holding a glowing boundary post. He would call: "Where shall I carry it?" Old Pie B. heard it and answered: "Where you fetched it from!" Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
156408: When Pie came home one evening, he was leapt on by a werewolf. The sweating man had to carry the werewolf as far as the oak wood.
156411: A woman who was covered in lice learned from a herbal healer that she was bewitched. The woman went to the brown friars, who gave her relics to put in the window frames. After that the witch could no longer get in.
156432: In the B. family there was a girl who could make mice without tails. Once, when the girl had made mice at school, her friends told the old parish priest of Vinckenrooi. The priest then summoned the girl. He tapped her on the head, after which she could no longer make mice.
156440: All the farmers in Budel had their cows covered by Thieu S.'s bull. One day Johanna G. also came to Thieu with her cow. But because people said Johanna was a witch, Thieu did not dare let her near the bull. Johanna told Thieu he would come to regret it. A few days later Thieu's bull lay dead in the stable.
156447: A woman with toothache went to pray at a mission cross for nine days. During that time she was not allowed to say anything else. One day the woman saw a returned dead person sitting by the mission cross.
156451: On the road from Rotem to Heppeneert stood a peculiar tree. One could only get past that tree by making the sign of the cross.
156459: In Heers there lived a sorcerer who conjured a mouse out of his shoe in church.
156460: Some men from Rutten had got their cart stuck in the field. Then one of the men said: "Hit the edge of the cart, because that's where the witch will be sitting!" When the man had done that, they could move on again.
156486: A werewolf roamed the Molenveld and often made people carry it.
156498: A man going from Gestel to Beringen in the evening suddenly saw a black cat that jumped in front of his feet. The man hit and kicked at the cat, but the animal stayed with him until he got home.
156502: A farmhand returning from Elen one evening saw a herd of piglets on the way. That was probably the work of a witch.
156506: In Vreren there was an uninhabited house that was haunted. When the owner himself stayed the night in the house, the ghost could be caught.
156515: Some men were walking along the canal in Uikhoven in the morning while it was still dark. The last man was leapt on by a werewolf and had to carry the beast a few hundred metres.
156516: A pig butcher was often harassed by a werewolf in the evening. The werewolf jumped on his back and soiled him. One evening, however, the butcher managed to wound the werewolf. Because he had first put the point of his knife in his mouth, he was able to make the werewolf bleed.
156533: At school there was a little boy named Janneke who could conjure mice by throwing breadcrumbs from his pocket onto the ground. After the priest had baptised the boy again, he could no longer make mice.
156539: A witch from Broekom could make mice from a handful of earth.
156557: In a meadow in Vlijtingen a black cat always sat on a post. People said it was the devil.
156558: In Zutendaal lived a man who was called 'Jan-with-the-red-cow'. Near his house there were always many cats. One winter evening Jan had brought some water to the boil to warm himself when suddenly a cat crawled out of the drain. "Good day, Jan-with-the-red-cow", said the animal, to which Jan replied: "Good day, cat, warm your backside!" A little later a second cat came in. After a while the house was completely full of cats. Then Jan mercilessly poured boiling water over the animals. The next day nearly all the women in the neighbourhood had burns.
156563: People believed that the Heikant was haunted. A young man who lived there with his brother suddenly saw a ghost coming towards him with a headscarf in its hand. When the boy asked something, the ghost did not answer. The boy crawled under his bed and took his revolver. The next moment the ghost had disappeared.
156568: A man had hanged himself in a wood in Achel. After his death the suicide came back to haunt every year on the same day, with loud wailing and screaming. After a while the ghost was no longer heard.
156582: A man from Hamelsdorp was driving his cart to Hoelbeek. Suddenly a spoke sprang out of the cart's wheel. A little later the man saw a woman from Hoelbeek walking beside him who had only one arm.
156590: A mother who had just been churched met a woman who wanted to hold her newborn baby and said: "What a lovely child it is!" A few days later the baby was dead.
156591: People possessed by the devil could change into a dog, a cat or a werewolf. When a werewolf had itself carried, it grew heavier and heavier.
156598: A man said to his friend: "Lad, it's time, I have to become a werewolf. Just throw a handkerchief at me."
156600: A boy out for an evening walk with his girlfriend suddenly said: "Wait, I just need to go and pee. If a black dog comes at you in the meantime, throw my red handkerchief at its mouth." A little later a black dog did appear, which pulled the handkerchief out of the girl's hands. When the boy came back, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
156603: Jaak H. often used to dress up as a ghost to frighten people. One day, however, Jaak met a white figure that scared him out of his wits. Jaak was so badly frightened that he fell ill with fear. Since then Jaak never again dared to dress up as a ghost.
156619: In an old monastery on the Motvaart the monks were driven out by Napoleon. After their death the monks came haunting between midnight and one o'clock. The ghosts walked side by side in pairs and spoke not a word.
156623: When witches wanted to fly through the air, they spoke the following spell: "Through hedges and thickets". Anyone who had spoken the spell had to fly along.
156624: When people could not make butter, the cause was usually a witch who had been in the house. After a priest had read prayers over the house, they could make butter again.
156634: Witches lived in the Bellesheskes outside the Moerenpoort. A man who sold potatoes knew he would sell nothing if a witch had been by him in the morning. If the witch had rubbed the horse's muzzle, the man would unharness the animal at once, knowing there was no point in setting off. The children who lived in the Bellesheskes were always dirty and had lice.
156638: Every time Betje walked along the little field path by the chapel, she heard a thin voice saying: "Lisebetsje, Lisebetsje, Lisebetsje". One day Betje and Dilleke cycled together to Hasselt to go to the Heilig Paterke for Zjang. At the chapel the women stopped to find out where that strange voice came from. They never found out.
156644: The maar (nightmare, mare) gave people in bed an oppressive feeling at night. One day a man was advised to hold a knife clasped to his chest with the point downwards. Someone else claimed the knife should point upwards, because otherwise the man would stab himself. That night the maar came again. The next morning she lay dead on the bed with the knife in her chest.
156645: There were many ghosts in the Appelarenbos near the Herk. People said they were the spirits of Méas, who led people astray.
156646: A man from Briegden managed to lure all the rats of a farm in Lanaken to a bundle of straw. Then he set the bundle of straw on fire.
156656: A boy was visiting his girlfriend in Vorst, who was a sister of the wizard Selm. When the boy wanted to go home, Selm said: "Will you get home, or shall I go with you?" Laughing, the boy said he could go alone, and he left. A little further on, however, the boy found that the bridge over the brook had disappeared. The boy tried to jump over the brook but landed in the water. Only the next morning did the boy see that he was standing in the brook that flowed in front of his own house.
156663: Jean V., nicknamed Mitchie, always had bad luck because of the witches Belke and Marzjenneke. Time and again something happened to Jean's family, his animals or his grain. Jean never passed the witches without keeping both thumbs clenched inside his fists.
156666: A woman who lived in Tongeren often heard unbaptized children floating through the air.
156667: A mother had a child that was always crying because an old woman came to visit every day and brought something for the child. On the advice of a French soldier, the mother stopped letting the woman in. After prayers had been read over the child, it recovered.
156695: It was said that the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a band of robbers said to ride flying goats) consorted with the devil. One day one of the bokkenrijders made a mistake when saying the magic formula; he said "through hedge and bush" instead of "over hedge and bush". The man was badly injured when he arrived in the wine cellar of Cologne.
156704: In Stamprooi lived a woman suspected of being a witch. According to the priest, one could recognise a witch by drawing a little cross on the ground. When this was done, the suspected woman looked round. From that moment people knew for sure that she was a witch.
156712: When Jan V.M. was on his way somewhere with his wheelbarrow and his dog, he met a woman who said: "Jan, when you come back later, your dog won't be able to walk any more". On the way back the dog was indeed so limp that Jan had to lay it in the wheelbarrow.
156723: A man walking through the fields in the evening saw a lady in a black silk dress by the ditch, combing her hair. The man asked: "Why are you still sitting there so late?", to which the lady said: "Go on your way. The day is for you and the night is for me."
156725: When the little pillow of a sick child was cut open, some people claimed to see roses, while others saw feathers. It must have been imagination.
156732: It was said that next to the town of Weert there once lay another town called Vijvere. But because the people of Vijvere lived very wicked lives, the devil dragged the town and all its inhabitants off to hell.
