156746: In Lanklaar the church bells had fallen into a pit. During the first mass a sound recording was played on which the bells could be heard ringing.
156750: There was a plank in the Bilzerveld. When someone stepped on that plank in the evening, a white lady appeared.
156761: Jan and Ribus had gone to deliver a load of ironstone to Ham. On the way back the men decided to take a nap in the cart. When Ribus woke up, he saw a large light floating above his head. Because the man had seen the light before, he went to the dean, who said: "Those are souls of unbaptised children. You must say: 'I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit'. Then you will not see the light any more." After the man had followed the priest's advice, he indeed no longer saw the light.
156763: A boy was visiting his girlfriend, who, like her mother, was a witch. The boy pretended to have fallen asleep so that he could spy on the two women. Mother and daughter rubbed themselves with witches' grease and then said: "Over hedges and hedgerows to the wine cellar of Cologne." When the women had flown off, the boy also rubbed himself with witches' grease and said: "Through hedges and hedgerows to the wine cellar of Cologne." The boy arrived at his destination badly injured. He had made a mistake when saying the magic formula.
156764: Because B.'s wife was ill, a certain C. came to look after the children. C. made muisjes (sugared aniseed sprinkles) to keep the children calm. C. had made B.'s wife ill.
156777: A girl returning from Heers with some cows met a witch on the way. The witch asked, "Where did you get such fine cows?", while patting the animal with her hand. When the girl got home, the cows were covered in lice.
156783: In a house the porcelain could be heard rattling every evening at the same time. That was the work of evil spirits. People suspected it was a dead person returning.
156790: A girl always made little mice from a handful of sand during catechism class. After the priest had blessed the girl, she could no longer make mice.
156795: A man who saw something white appear and heard chains rattling was so frightened that he dropped his basket of eggs.
156798: In Beringen there was a wood where it was haunted. The farmhand of the farmer who owned the wood did not believe in ghosts. One day, when the farmhand came home with a sack on his back, he felt something pulling at his sack. The farmer had the trees cut down and turned the wood into a potato field. One day, while people were gathering potatoes, they found a pot full of gold coins in the ground.
156810: A family who could not make butter because of a witch sent for the parish priest. After the clergyman had read prayers over the milk, they could make butter again.
156819: Whoever wanted to sell his soul to the devil had to stand at a crossroads at night with a black hen.
156831: A boy claimed that in Dilsen he had seen the shade of his deceased father sitting there.
156833: Janneke always went on pilgrimage on behalf of other people. On the way Janneke saw kittens. Because Janneke sang out of tune, all the kittens dropped dead.
156836: A farmer whose cows were all dying could not be helped by any parish priest. One day the farmer met a friar, who said: "You must bring a large pot filled with water and a cow's lungs to the boil. You must barricade the gate and set two men on guard." When the witch appeared, the guards beat her until she confessed her guilt. Pins were found in the cows' manger.
156840: A farmer was ploughing a field close to the house of Alda H., a woman said to be a witch. Suddenly the farmer saw that Alda's house was on fire. When the farmer came closer, he saw that Alda was still sitting inside on a chair. The farmer immediately got the woman out of the house. Meanwhile, to the farmer's great alarm, the flames had already come close to the haystack. Then Alda said: "Fonske, because you were not afraid of me, I will let the fire go out." A few moments later the fire had disappeared.
156843: A farmer had a farmhand who went out every evening. One evening the curious farmer decided to follow his farmhand secretly. So the farmer saw the farmhand take a collar out of a tree stump. The next day the farmer pretended he was going to bake bread. When the oven was hot, the farmer hurried to the tree stump to take out the farmhand's collar. The farmhand quickly ran after the farmer, but could not prevent his collar from being thrown into the fire. "What have you done now?" the farmhand wailed. "Now I am damned forever!" Then the farmhand left for good.
156847: A man whose cows were bewitched always heard a lot of noise in the stable at night.
156861: A woman who was seriously ill slept in the attic room. Every day a woman from the neighbourhood came and sat on the attic stairs. She would always ask: "Betje, how are you?", and then keep the sick woman company for a while. One day the woman had such a severe headache that her husband immediately sent for the doctor and the priest. That same evening the woman died.
156862: A man going to work in the morning was terrified when he saw something move beside the ditch.
156866: A carpenter who often had to work late sometimes met strange animals on the way home. One day he had to pass through a turnstile on which three magpies were sitting. One of the magpies said: "Shall we, shall we", then the second: "Yes we, yes we", and the third: "No we, no we, it's old Pie-Ber, the carpenter!" Then the magpies let him through.
156869: One day priest C. van Beek had gone to Weert by way of the Luys family and the Gabriels family. When the priest came back in the evening, he met two men. The men wanted to rob the priest of the silver buckles on his shoes. Ignoring the priest's laments, the men began to undo the buckles. Then the priest said: "Whoever sits stays sitting and whoever stands stays standing." The priest left and the men stayed behind, unable to move. A little further on the priest met someone who said: "You should go over there; there are two men nailed to the ground," to which the priest replied: "Just tell the men they can go."
156882: In Lauw there lived a witch who was burned at a stake. The piece of land where that stake stood was named after the witch. In Rutten the witch was tortured 'à la vieille'. The witch was tied to a ladder by her wrists behind her back, which caused her terrible pain in her shoulder joints. During this torture the witch confessed that she had had relations with the devil. His member felt like an icicle. The devil could make grains of corn float upright. By speaking a formula he could then make horses die or make cows stop giving milk. The witch also confessed that she had bewitched the neighbours' children because those people had refused her a bowl of soup.
156884: When a witch looked into the churn while people were churning the milk, they could not make butter.
156888: In Zepperen three men were threshing grain. For two days one of the men had seen a little man sitting on a beam, who vanished when he came closer. On the third day the man told the others, but they saw nothing. They advised the man to go to the Monnebruurs (the friars). A priest had the man confess and take communion and told him to ask the ghost next time what it wanted. The next day the little man answered: "You must go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for me." Then a handkerchief fell to the ground with a thumb and four fingers burnt into it. The little man had once promised to go on pilgrimage, but because he had not kept his promise, he was not allowed into heaven.
156893: Werewolves caused people a lot of trouble. They stole chickens and often made people carry them.
156897: A farmhand who always sprinkled himself with holy water was protected against the power of witches. One morning, when the farmhand had forgotten to use the holy water, a witch suddenly stood before him. At that very moment a drop of water fell from the roof into the boy's eye. "You were lucky!" said the witch.
156900: A woman who often came home late sometimes saw a werewolf with a red handkerchief in its mouth.
156903: Some people ploughing the field were startled when a magpie suddenly settled on the plough. When they struck at the magpie, the witch came by saying: "Chase that magpie away!" But they did not dare.
156906: A man going to visit his girlfriend saw a big black cat sitting on the wall on the P. along the way. After the man struck at the cat with his stick, the animal was back on the wall almost immediately, though it was a good two and a half metres high. The same thing happened twice more. The man believed the cat was a witch.
156921: A count who possessed ill-gotten wealth met a ghost in his castle at night. "Who are you?", asked the count, and the devil answered: "The day is for you and the night is for me." After his death the count came haunting. At midnight all the doors of the castle opened and a wagon with fiery horses drove in.
156925: In Ophoven lived a witch who could turn herself into a cat and in that way eavesdrop on all conversations. That is why nobody dared to speak ill of the witch. When the witch asked for something, nobody dared to refuse either, because then the witch gave that person lice.
156926: A man walked past the pear tree where Jean van de molen later built. Suddenly the man was leapt on by a werewolf.
156932: A man playing cards in Heusden had the jack of spades from the deck fetch a bottle of gin.
156945: At midnight witches in the shape of black cats came to dance around the water and around the chains in the farms.
156948: In the old days a man lived in Membruggen who could catch rats. He put a bundle of straw in the field and made all the rats crawl into the straw one by one. At the end he would say: "Come on, now the old mother too!" When the last rat was in the straw, the man set the bundle on fire. This sorcerer could also drive the rats to another field, however. To do so he had to read something aloud in three corners of the field. The rats then moved to the neighbouring field by way of the fourth corner.
156951: Because the deceased count came haunting the castle, a priest was called in to banish the ghost. The oak to which the spirit was banished was later called the 'spookeik' (ghost oak).
156960: At the 'Basseng' there was a café run by a witch. Because Sooi J. had not been to the inn for a while, his horse stood still in front of the witch's house. One day Sooi went into the café and said: "If the witch doesn't make my horse go on, I'll beat her to death!" The next moment the horse went on.
156974: On the Beukenberg stood a house that was haunted.
156976: On the hill where the Romans' gallows once stood, a witch lived. That witch turned herself into a cat and then rolled down the hill in a chamber pot.
156995: A man was going to work on Saturday morning. In the woods the man saw a kitten and he said: "Hey, kitten, are you coming along?" Further on the kitten said: "If Kleerke had not spoken so nicely, we would have broken his little neck here." The man was suddenly surrounded by as many as fifty cats.
156998: On Sundays the children went along to Lanklaar, where they sat on a bench next to the chapel. A witch pushed a cigar stub into the mouth of one of the children. When the child came home, it had convulsions. In the end it died.
157006: In Mielen there lived a witch who made the children ill. The witch was driven away.
157011: A man going to visit his girlfriend one evening saw a woman combing her hair on the hill near Spöke. The man walked on, scared to death. A little further on the man was followed by a pack of mewing cats. As soon as the man reached his girlfriend's house, the cats had vanished.
157028: Werewolves had a skin that they hid in some hollow tree or other. In the evening they robbed people and leapt onto their necks.
157053: In Eksel lived a witch who always wanted to harm people. Whoever was patted on the shoulder by a witch always had to strike higher. One day that witch had covered a woman in lice. One could only be freed of the lice by having oneself overlezen (exorcised by reading prayers) by a priest.
157060: A woman saw a beautiful white rabbit sitting beside the brook near the Toekomststraat. She picked up the animal and wrapped it in her apron. When the woman came home and unfolded her apron, to her great dismay a stone fell to the ground. "Take that back quickly, because that's not normal," said the woman's husband. As soon as the woman picked up the stone again, it turned back into a rabbit.
157073: In Romershoven there lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. People said that this woman could pray someone to death.
157080: One day a man from Budel saw a ghost sitting in a tree. The ghost floated over the frightened man and then vanished.
157081: Two men who had been at the pub were walking home together in the evening. Suddenly one of them said: "Don't be alarmed if I suddenly start behaving strangely. Just throw a handkerchief at me then." When the man changed into a werewolf at midnight, the other threw his red handkerchief and ran away.
157091: In the past a white lady used to wander around the Spekbrug.
157092: A man who went to fetch apples from a meadow at dusk was suddenly startled by a large dog standing behind him. The man was so frightened that he no longer dared to pick up the apples.
157098: A child lying in the cradle cried all the time because it was bewitched. The pillow the child slept on turned out to be full of pins.
157115: Will-o'-the-wisps moved up and down in a meadow. They were the little souls of unbaptised children.
157119: At night a white lady in a silk dress sometimes appeared in Opheers. The white lady did no one any harm and would suddenly vanish again.
157122: A man who went to manure the Hölterveld at one o'clock at night saw a priest appear, walking towards the woods while praying.
157130: A farmer had come to live at 't Hobosch in Eksel, the place where the drossaard (bailiff) used to live. The farmer had his farmhands sleep in the castle to guard the place. Because the farmhands were always found murdered in the morning, the farmer often had no farmhand. When a tramp came to ask the farmer for shelter one evening, the farmer sent him to the castle. After the farmer told the tramp he had to be careful because all the farmhands in the castle had been murdered, the man asked for a prayer book, a rosary and a candle. While the tramp was frying bacon in the castle, bones fell down the chimney into the pan. "In God's name, another good slice of bacon!" the tramp said each time, and threw the bones together in a corner. At midnight there was a knock at the door. "Wait a moment, I'm eating. When I'm done, I'll come and open up," said the tramp. When after a while the tramp had three visitors, he said: "Now we can play a game of cards, because there are exactly four of us!" Because the tramp did not quite trust the three visitors, he deliberately dropped a card and bent down. Then the tramp cried out: "In God's name, they all have horses' hooves!" At that, the three visitors vanished without a trace. When the tramp wanted to go to sleep, he heard moaning in the cellar. He went to look and found a man tied to a ring in the wall. As soon as the man was untied, he said: "You have released me. Under the floor there are three large pots of money: the first pot is for the church, the second for the poor and the third for you because you helped me." The next morning the tramp told the farmer what had happened to him. The farmer was so glad that he let the tramp keep all the money. "Wouldn't you like to work for me as a farmhand?" the farmer asked, to which the tramp eagerly replied: "I would like that very much. Because I always say my prayers, I'll be able to handle the three fellows from the castle!" Since then the castle of 't Hobosch was no longer haunted.
157138: A farmer who had struck a cat off a stick was startled when, a moment later, the cat was already sitting on the stick again and said: "Strike again now!"
157141: In Stamprooi many people had seen the devil's coach. That was a coach surrounded by fire, which took the devil to a witches' gathering. When someone had seen a devil's coach, something bad usually happened in the near future.
157147: Because of a witch, the cows and horses in the stable were tied to each other.
157150: A family from Bommershoven walked to the market in Tongeren with a newborn child. On the way they met an old woman, who touched the child. Because the child afterwards always lay crying in its cradle, the people went to the doctor. He could not help, however. The parish priest established that the child was bewitched. In the child's pillow they found feathers forming a kind of cock's head, pointing upwards. That was why the baby was always in pain when it lay on it. The priest said the child would have died if this had been discovered too late.
157157: In Rijkhoven there lived a girl who always began to bleed on Good Friday. This strange phenomenon was caused by the girl's mother, who was a witch.
157176: When walking in Vreeren through the alley near the church, one passed the priest's garden, which was closed off by an iron gate. Nobody dared walk through that alley at night, because at the stroke of midnight the iron gate swung open and shut by itself, although there was no wind.
157177: When you cycled past a witch's house, it could happen that the chain suddenly fell to the ground.
157198: In Koninksem a neighbour came to look at a sow that was about to farrow. When the piglets were born, they all turned into rats. The witch had caused this.
157202: In a village there was always a woman hanging about who had a bad name. One day the woman wanted to give two children a lovely apple. The mother did not allow it. The children would not listen, however, and each took an apple when their mother was not looking. When the mother found the apples a little later, she put them in a kettle on the fire. After a quarter of an hour the mother opened the lid and, to her great fright, saw two toads jump out of the kettle.
157208: A farmer whose cows all became skinny and died sent for two veterinary inspectors from Brussels. The vets, however, could not determine the cause of death. That year the farmer lost nine cows in total. One day the farmer had an old clergyman come to the stable. After the clergyman's visit, the farmer could no longer give his cows fruit because they then grew too fat.
157217: Whenever Bet B. had been near a child and had said: "What a lovely child you have", the child fell ill. After a while the child even died.
157224: In Neerweert lived two unmarried sisters who were said to be witches. One sister was called Marie, the other Betteke. A man from the neighbourhood who was mowing his grass struck at a black cat that kept scratching at his legs. When the man wanted to strike a second time, Betteke lay stark naked at his feet. The black cat had vanished without a trace.
157227: Next to the little chapel on the road leading to the bridge over the canal stood a tree stump where strange things always happened. People were tormented there by the fire-man, and sometimes the werewolf jumped on passers-by's necks there. Because there was no lighting at that spot, people were always very afraid there.
157231: A boy returning from a visit to his girlfriend saw a black cat sitting in a tree. The boy shot the cat and went on. The next time the boy visited his girlfriend, she had a broken leg. At that moment the boy understood that the girl was a witch.
157238:
People used to believe that a dog's howling foretold misfortune. If the dog held its head down, someone would die. If it held its head up, there might be a fire, for example.
One day a man heard a dog howling. The next day he learned that someone had drowned in the Meuleveld (Molenveld?).
157255: A boy walking with his girlfriend announced that he had to go away for a moment and said: "If you meet a dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." When a dog came running up a little later, the girl did what her boyfriend had told her. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
157258: Some men walking home along the Binkel met the count's donkey on the way. Every time one of the men struck a match to light the way, the donkey blew it out. Then the men hurried home, because they thought the donkey was the ghost of a dead person who had returned.
157274: After his death the drossaard (bailiff) came back to haunt in the shape of a black dog. The priest of Eksel banished the ghost for ninety-nine years under a bridge by the high road. The priest died of it.
157281: A woman had been visiting a farmer who kept turkeys. When the woman left the house, she saw a turkey sitting on the ground. So the woman picked the animal up to carry it back inside. But the turkey began to screech and turned into a goat, so that the woman had to put the animal down again. A little later the goat had turned back into a turkey.
157301: In the meadow between Rekem and Neerharen there once stood a large castle. A man walking home around ten o'clock in the evening sometimes saw as many as three hundred cows and calves in that meadow. Some kind of apparition helped the animals through the fence.
157303: A young man went walking in the fields with his girlfriend. However, the young man had to roam about as a werewolf at regular times, so he said to the girl: "I have to go and relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth; then it can't harm you." A little later a big dog did indeed come running at the girl. She threw the handkerchief at the dog, which tore the cloth to pieces. When the young man came out of the bushes a little later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
157309: When Janneke from Maastricht had died, his body was carried to the church in a coffin. In the church the dead man began to pound the inside of the coffin with his fists. During his life the man had promised to go on pilgrimage, but he had never been able to fulfil that promise.
157318: Unbaptised children flew through the air in the form of will-o'-the-wisps.
157352: Two women who lived on the Bessemer went to Maastricht in the morning. At that moment one of the neighbours was busy churning butter. When the two women came back from Maastricht in the evening, the neighbour was still churning. The women went into the house and said: "But madam, are you still churning? You may as well stop, because your butter was sold long ago at the market in Maastricht!"
157353: In the castle of l' Escaille in Hamont witches' gatherings were often held. People then often heard music that resounded as far as the Netherlands. One day a man near the castle came across a whole pack of cats. Those cats were witches heading to the castle in disguise.
157354: A man went to a meadow to chop branches off an ash tree. Although his billhook was very sharp, the man could not cut a single branch from the tree. A little later Boze Griet came by and said: "Not working? I'll give you my billhook; then it will go fine!" Reluctantly the man took Botte Griet's billhook, which looked very rusty and blunt. To his great astonishment, the man could cut the branches from the tree with ease using that blade.
157377: In the old days people often sat in the snow on winter evenings, waiting for a hare to pass by. Sometimes a hare would then sit down next to you and scratch at the barrel of the gun. Such hares could not be hit in any way.
157386: A widow made little mice for the children.
157391: The werewolf jumped on people's backs and then had itself carried.
157396: A boy who was out walking with his girlfriend suddenly said to the girl: "If anyone comes at you, you must throw your handkerchief." As soon as the boy was gone, the girl was approached by a dog or a monster. The girl threw the handkerchief at the apparition. When the boy came back a little later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
157414: A man from Grote-Spouwen who went for a walk in the evening was jumped on by a werewolf. When the man had stabbed the beast in the head with a nail, the werewolf changed into a human. The man had to promise not to betray the werewolf.
157429: A man was startled when he heard noise in the yard at midnight. When the man went to look, he recognised a woman from the neighbourhood and said: "Oh Agatha, it's you! How did you get in?" "By the gate bar," the woman answered. But the man knew for certain that the gate bar had not been open and said: "Get out of here!"
157433: In Vliermaal stood a house haunted by a little old woman. In the evening a small light always burned in the house.
157436: On Sleiberg the witches danced in a ring every night. Where the witches' ring had formed, grass no longer grew. One night a young lady from a fabric shop in Hasselt lost her golden cup during the dance. During the harvest a farmer found the cup among the grain. Because the owner's name and address were on the cup, the farmer decided to bring the golden chalice back to Hasselt. The owner of the cup turned out to be the leader of the witches. As a reward for returning the cup, the man was allowed to choose two tailor-made suits. He did have to promise the witch that he would tell no one anything about the cup.
157451: People who had misfortune with the animals in their stable went to the Poor Clare sisters. Once the people had hung a relic in the stable, the witch could do no more.
157452: A dog always sat near the Dameruskapel. People coming back from Hasselt with their wheelbarrows could not go on because the dog blocked their way.
157453: A miller's hand roamed about at night as a werewolf on the road between Othée and Rutten. One day someone had thrown a red handkerchief at the werewolf. The next day people saw that the miller's hand still had the red threads between his teeth.
157458: A man coming back from Mopertingen saw lots of lights in the field. Because they were the souls of unbaptised people, the man began to pray.
157474: By the little castle of Freyns in Sint-Lambrechts-Herk lay a tall pile of wood. Around eleven o'clock in the evening people heard a sound there as if ten men were chopping wood, although nobody could be seen. The next morning all the wood had vanished.
157483: A man always saw cats leaping about in a lime tree in Genebos. The man made the sign of the cross and struck at one of the cats with a hook. When the man came to the Buiting the next day, he learned that the woman was ill. From her bed the woman called out: "Come and see what you did to me last night!"
157492: A witch brought coffee to some men who were working in the woods. "Are you a witch?" the men asked fearfully, to which the woman replied: "Yes, but I have cabbages in my garden. Every morning I pinch the head off one of the cabbages, and then I have already done my evil for that day. So you need not be afraid."
157502: The cleaning woman of the V. family suffered from a strange illness. A black dog always followed her, which made her cry: "They're tearing me apart! They're tearing me apart!" When the cleaning woman died after long suffering, her daughter Marie found in her mother's bed a picture of Our Lord with cow's feet. The priest threw the print into the fire as fast as he could. The cleaning woman must have been possessed by the devil.
157514: A farmer had a farmhand who was a werewolf. Pastor N. had found the werewolf's band and advised the farmer to burn the thing. When the farmer had sent the farmhand to Roermond with a cart of grain, he threw the collar into the oven. As soon as the band caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his band. When everything had burnt up, the farmhand was released.
157516: At the Kinderhof there was a farmhand who turned into a werewolf in the evening. As a werewolf, the farmhand often made people carry him. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he changed back into a human and could be recognised. When the farmer found his farmhand's collar in a tree stump, he sent the boy away for a few hours. Meanwhile the farmer lit the oven to burn the collar. When the farmer was about to throw the collar into the fire, the farmhand was instantly standing by the oven and cried: "Stop! That's mine!"
157522: Whenever the clouds in the sky formed an Abraham's tree, it would invariably rain the next day.
157527: In the woods a ghost wandered about in the evenings, asking all the time: "Where shall I take it? Where shall I take it?" One day someone answered: "Take it back to the place where you fetched it from!" Since then the ghost has never been heard again.
157531: Dwaaslichtjes (will-o'-the-wisps) were the little souls of unbaptised children who appeared in the woods with a little lamp. In the old days people ran away in fear when they saw such a light.
157540: P. was pushing a wheelbarrow of stolen litter between the pine trees. Suddenly the man heard wonderfully beautiful music. The next moment two magnificent candlesticks fell down between the trees.
157547: A woman came haunting after her death because she had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. Whenever the ghost appeared, it always knelt. After the priest had made the sign of the cross over the ghost, the dead woman was delivered.
157555: People believed that the butcher's wife was a witch. One day a mother who was standing in the shop with her child had quarrelled with the witch. The witch had said: "If you don't admit you are wrong, you will get into trouble yet." When the mother came home, she found that her child's head was turned back to front. Because the doctor could not help, the mother sought advice from the parish priest. The next morning the priest forced the witch to set the child's head straight again.
157561: Kötteke M. could work magic. For example, the man could walk up the wall of the town hall. When Kötteke threw his cap against the church door, the door opened by itself.
157579: In Berbroek a black dog with a red handkerchief roamed about. It was a werewolf.
157589: A man who lived at the Paumeshof often went to the café in Maaseik with friends in the evening. On his way home he heard chains rattling in the field. A moment later someone jumped onto his neck and had himself carried. It was the man's friends, playing werewolf as a joke.
157590: Whoever became a werewolf had to make a pact with the devil for three, five, seven or ten years. One then had to sign one's name in blood in a book. In return one received a bearskin with which, for a certain payment, one had to roam about as a werewolf for a number of hours. Once there was a man who had made such a pact with the devil. While the man was working far away, his bearskin was found and people wanted to throw it into the oven. The man, who had sensed this, hurried back from work, saved his bearskin and was never seen again.
157606: A simple-minded boy from Schurhoven could conjure mice by throwing a scrap of cloth on the ground. After the priest had blessed the boy, he could no longer make mice.
157607: A farmer from Oleye often went to visit his girlfriend in Heers. One day on the way the farmer met some men, to whom he said: "I'll come with you, but first I'll go a little way through the wood. I'll see you over there." When the men were on the hill, there was a big dog standing on the road. The farmer could change himself into a dog.
157610: When Cuvelier was driving through Colmont with his horse and cart, Heksebetje stood watching by her house. Suddenly the cart came to a standstill. Cuvelier was convinced that Heksebetje had made the cart get stuck. The moment he got ready to give the witch a thrashing, the cart started moving again.
157615: A man who went to fetch his girlfriend in the evening was followed by a foal from the Molenveld to the dike of the Maas. Then the foal suddenly vanished. When the man came back with his girlfriend, the same thing happened again.
157619: Vogelsang was haunted. A man had spent the whole night drinking and making merry in a café there. When the first cock crowed in the morning, everything had vanished and the man was sitting on a branch of a tree.
157621: Maareske V.S. always went to milk other people's cows in the meadow. The police had often tried to catch Maareske, but it seemed an impossible task. Once Maareske had hung on to the sails of his turning mill. When he was at the very top, Maareske jumped down in the direction of Vorst. One day Maareske was in the town hall of Tessenderlo. Because he knew the police were on his heels, Maareske turned himself into a mouse and escaped.
157622:
Because so many criminals roamed the woods of Kortenbos, it was decided to hang a statue of Mary on a tree, which a friar from Sint-Truiden had given to Kortenbos. One day a young lady from Schurhoven wanted to take the statue with her. However, she could not carry it, it had suddenly become so heavy. She was forced to hang the statue back on the tree and then went home.
A soldier who wanted to take an offertory box was also forced to put it back, because he could no longer move with the box in his hands.
157624: A farmer was driving home with his horse and cart. On the way the horses suddenly stopped as if they were nailed to the ground. A little further on the farmer saw a woman standing and looking at the horses. When the woman walked on, the horses started moving again too. That woman must have been a witch.
157628: Everyone knew that Bet S. was a witch. One day a curious boy went to visit Bet with the girl next door. Because the boy wanted to see how the witch made mice, the woman began muttering all kinds of spells while the boy had to poke about in the earth with a stick. After a few moments dozens of mice appeared. The boy tried to stamp on the mice, but he could not hit a single one. When the boy told his parents the story, his father forbade him to visit Bet Stijns again. His father was afraid that the witch would give her book of spells to the boy, so that she herself would be freed from the evil.
157645: When a bokkerijder (goat rider, a member of a robber band said to ride the devil's goats) no longer wanted to be a robber, he had to stand at a crossroads with a black hen. The bokkerijder must on no account look back. While the hen grew heavier and heavier, seven coaches would then drive past. In the last coach sat a man dressed all in black, who took the hen.
157650: Before the First World War the mill in Maasmechelen belonged to the Prussians. One day a man was helping the miller sharpen the millstone. Although there was hardly any wind, the mill suddenly began to turn. The witch Antrien had done it.
157651:
In the castle of Widooie there once lived a certain Tiecke, a general who had fought in Russia in Napoleon's army. At night the man could be heard screaming hysterically and shouting orders; he thought he was still in the army.
Later the castle was inhabited by a baron. That man did not go to church and was known as a womanizer. After his death the baron came back to haunt.
157654: At Groeningen, a farm along the Grendelbaan in Diepenbeek, stood a barrier that always creaked and said: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" It was the soul of a man who had once moved a boundary post. One evening a drunkard answered: "Put it there, dammit!" Since then nothing strange has been heard at the barrier.
157658: When Neske P. was visiting a woman, the woman thought to herself: "I wish that witch would leave." A little later Neske said: "You'd like me to leave, wouldn't you, madam?" Afterwards the woman had a fever for three days.
157667: A boy who was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend said on the way: "Stay here for ten minutes, and then I'll come back to you." Because the girl grew uneasy, she was very relieved when she saw her father coming. The father struck with a red handkerchief at a werewolf that suddenly appeared. The next evening the boy came to visit the girl. To her great dismay the girl saw that the red threads of the handkerchief were still hanging between his teeth.
157668: At the fair there was a man who made mice. A spectator who also wanted to learn to make mice was given a book of spells by the sorcerer. Later, on the dean's advice, the man tried to burn the book. But the book always returned to the man by itself. The man could only get rid of the book by letting it be stolen.
157672: A man pushing his wheelbarrow along a road in Hoelbeek could not go on because a cat was sitting on the turnstile. "What are you doing here so late?", asked the man, to which the cat replied: "Nothing."
157682: Theodoor from Kinrooi went with his friends to Molenbeersel. On the way Theodoor met a cat that blocked his path. After Theodoor had kicked at the cat, a hundred cats could be heard mewing in the ditch. Two days later the company went back to Molenbeersel. On the way they each bought fifty nuts at a house. Theodoor happened to have been given two extra nuts. As soon as Theodoor had eaten those two nuts, he got a violent stomach ache. A few days later the man went with his father to the friars of Weert. Theodoor turned out to have two toads in his stomach. If the man did not digest the toads, he would die. Theodoor was cured by a short prayer.
157688: A man had been watching all evening over his horse, which had a stomach ache. His son Frans said: "You go to sleep now, I'll stay with the horse." On the stroke of twelve Frans heard someone knocking on the door. Frans did not open it, but heard the voice of a woman from the neighbourhood asking: "Frans, how is the horse?" Although nobody had said a word about the horse's illness, the witch still knew what was going on.
157713: A man whose hens had chicks was plagued by a cat. The man had struck the cat with a club, but the animal stayed sitting motionless. In the end the man sent for a hunter to shoot the animal. The hunter, however, did not manage to hit it either. After a while the cat went away of its own accord.
157719: A man walking home with the midwife saw a square box lying in the ditch. A little later the box had vanished and a sheep lay in the ditch. When the man came closer, he saw that the sheep was on fire.
157722: The K. family in Vliermaal could not bake bread. After the friars had read prayers over the trough in which the bread was kneaded, it worked.
157737: A man had seen a confessional standing in the middle of the field, where people came to confess.
157755: By the Maas in Rotem there lived a witch who could make mice from the earth of a molehill.
157765: Some young men went to visit the girls in the evening. One day one of the men said: "You have lovely cats." When the men went home that evening, the cats got under their feet. The men struck at the animals. The next day one of the girls had a broken leg.
157767: People were often afraid of the white lady who walked on the road to Colmont.
157775: When people went home across the heath, they were often leapt on by the werewolf. The werewolf, heavy as lead, then had itself carried until the people fell to the ground from exhaustion.
157784: A man returning in the evening from Watelers near Opoeteren met a lit coach with two horses on the way. Although the man had taken the right road, the next morning he was in Niel.
157796: On a farm in Mellaar they were struggling with a plague of rats. As many as fifty rats came running in. The rats were big and strong and they ran over the heads of the occupants while they slept.
157803: A woman whose baby cried all the time sent for the doctor. Because the doctor did not know what to do, people believed the baby was bewitched. When the baby was six months old, it died.
157811: A farmer and his wife lived on a small farm on the Litzberg. When one day a beggar woman dressed in black came knocking, the farmer sent her away without giving her anything. From then on the farmer and his wife had much misfortune in their stable. A black cat was always trying to creep into the stable. One day the farmer broke one of the cat's legs. When the beggar woman came by again some time later, she was limping.
157822: At the presbytery worked a farmhand who had to go and cut heath. Meanwhile the farmer happened to find the animal skin with which his farmhand played the werewolf. The farmer decided to burn the skin in the oven. But even before the skin had caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his animal skin. The farmer dismissed the farmhand immediately.
157823: A man going to work saw a black cat sitting by the house of Nel M. The cat followed the man and then jumped on his back. The animal must have been a witch.
157826: In Stevoort there lived an old woman who could turn herself into a cat. A man who had struck at the cat had fallen ill.
157827: Next to Polieneke the witch lived a little woman who could not find her hen's eggs anywhere. Everyone suspected that the hen was laying her eggs in the witch's attic, but everyone was afraid of Polieneke. One day the little woman's son came home with the news that he had seen Polieneke up on the hill. "Then go and look in the witch's attic quickly," the little woman asked her son. The son did so and indeed found the eggs in Polieneke's attic. At the moment the son wanted to touch the eggs, a voice rang out: "Leave those alone, you brat!" It was only Polieneke's spirit that had spoken, for her body was still up on the hill. Only a few hours later was Polieneke seen returning from the hill.
157831: So as not to dirty the canopy of the statue of Our Lady of Tongeren, it was decided not to take the statue along in the procession. After the procession the people found that the statue was dirty and, moreover, stood in a different place in the church. The statue had gone along in the procession by itself.
157844: At a bridge over an old brook a white lady always appeared at midnight. One day a brave man asked the lady what she wanted. The white lady answered: "Come back here tomorrow at about the same time. I will not be here then. If you can release the apparition you find here tomorrow, you will be immensely rich." The next night the man went to the same place. This time a snake with a key in its mouth lay on the bridge. But the man was so frightened that he fled back home. Three days later the man died of fright. Yet with the key the man could have opened a sunken treasure.
157847: In Geneuth worked a farmhand who had to tend the sheep. One day people had seen the farmhand take a skin out of a tree stump. The next morning the farmhand was sent to the market to buy sheep. But the moment they were about to throw the skin into the fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven. He wanted to take his skin out of the fire, but they held him back. When the skin had burnt up completely, the farmhand left for good.
157852: Some soldiers saw a ghost standing in the churchyard of Stevoort, which said: "I have been sent by God". One soldier replied: "And I by the devil", and he smashed the ghost's skull in.
157856: A woman always saw a will-o'-the-wisp when she went to milk her goat in the stable. After a while the woman decided to ask the priest for advice. The priest told her to ask the will-o'-the-wisp what it wanted. When the woman saw the will-o'-the-wisp again, it turned out to be the soul of a woman who still had something to pay and therefore could find no rest. When the woman had paid the will-o'-the-wisp's debt, the light was no longer seen.
157858: On Christmas Day old B. went hunting near the Mestijn pond in Diepenbeek. Because the man had not been able to hit a single animal all day, he shot at a jay sitting on a branch. The next moment there were suddenly two jays. When the man shot again, there were four. After a while there were as many as twenty jays on the branch. The man was so frightened that he quickly fled home.
157868: There was a plague of rats in the castle. After the priest had overlezen (read exorcism prayers over) the castle, the witch's power was broken and not a single rat remained.
157915: At a farm that always had misfortune, a black witch's cat walked through the gutter.
157916: In Langerlo there were stones on the ground that were called devil's stones because imprints of horses' hooves could be seen in them.
157933: In the evening maanlichtjes (moon lights, will-o'-the-wisps) were often seen. They were the spirits of lost or stillborn children. Sometimes they were also an omen of a serious event.
157936: A boy had found out that his friend was the son of a witch. Because the boy no longer dared to visit his friend, the witch said mockingly: "Little lump, you don't dare come anymore!" One day, when the boy had been visiting an acquaintance, he discovered two tears in his coat, although he had not fought with anyone. On the way, however, the boy had met a few women. A few days later the same thing happened again. After a while the boy realised he had not used holy water for three weeks. After the boy had sprinkled himself with holy water, no more strange things happened. One day, when the boy went to the witch's house, he nearly tripped near the Aerdenhof over a bag lying on the ground. Because the witch admitted that the bag, which contained a sewing ring and a knife, was hers, the boy suspected that the witch had earlier torn his coat with that knife.
157937: In the old days the devil often appeared in the shape of a black man with goat's legs.
157938: People believed the Waar in Sint-Lambrechts-Herk was haunted. Around midnight a man was nearly frightened to death when he tripped over something on that road. A horse was lying on the road, and it made a strange rattling sound as it got up.
157946: If you could not make butter, you had to make the sign of the cross with holy water. A woman who could no longer make butter went on pilgrimage on Sunday morning to the little chapel in Lixhe. Farmers often sprinkled their stables with a palm sprig and holy water against the evil hand.
157960: A miller sent away an ungrateful beggar woman with the words: "You're always coming here! Every time you get something, and still you're not satisfied! You may not come in here anymore!" The next day the miller was so ill that he could not even speak. The dean of Mechelen established that it was already too late to undo the evil. On the ninth day the miller died. When the dead man was lifted from the bed, ninety-nine grains of corn were found on the sheet. That was how many kilos the miller had stolen. At the moment the hundredth grain was due to appear, the man had died.
157964: One night a girl heard someone walking through the living room. An old man with snow-white hair appeared. He wore a blue and white striped shirt and socks like those the shepherds wear in the procession. The ghost hurried past the girl's bed and sat down on a chest in another room. At first the girl thought she had dreamed it, but when she saw the same apparition several times, she decided it could not be a dream. One day people from Bommershoven came to visit to fetch bees. Because those people stayed the night, the girl slept with her sister, while her brother Gust slept in her room. The next morning Gust asked his sister: "Have you seen that man too?" From her brother's description the girl could tell it was the same apparition. Their mother then said: "I have no goods here that I came by unlawfully. It must be someone who used to live here and did not die with a clear conscience. We should ask him what his problem is." After that the children did not see the ghost again.
157973: Near B. a werewolf roamed about, breaking wind and robbing people of their money. When a strong carpenter from Hoeselt was jumped on by the werewolf, the man was determined to overpower the beast. At the third saw pit the carpenter took the werewolf under his arm and went with the beast to Biesenhuiske. In the house the werewolf changed into a naked man from Genoelselderen. "After my death you may reveal my name," the man said.
157974: In Rapertingen there was a sunken road that was haunted. A strange voice was heard calling: "Jef, Lowie,.." The priest of Rapertingen came to read prayers over that place.
157979: A man trimming his hedge saw Alda H. walk past. A little further on Alda suddenly fell into the grass. When the man went to look, he saw the woman lying deathly pale on the ground. Her breathing and pulse, however, were normal. After a quarter of an hour Alda got up and went on. The man later learned that Alda's sister had died at exactly that moment.
157980: A woman coming back from Wijer with a sack of bran met a witch who touched the bran. The woman had seventy-three rabbits. After the witch had touched the rabbits, the animals all died.
157991: A woman who was bewitched recovered after prayers had been read over her.
157993: A woman who had to go and fetch the midwife barely reached her destination. At one moment it started to rain, at another she could hardly go on. People said that a witch was responsible for all those troubles.
158003: At night the Mjatsveulen came haunting by the ditch.
158017: In Lanaken there lived a witch who could walk through the rain without getting wet.
158021: When people were bleaching the washing, the witch took a little stick and made the laundry fly up into the air.
158024: A nursemaid who was chattering all the time had stuffed grass into the child's little mouth so that it would not cry. A man who had seen it quickly went to warn the parents. In the baby's pillow the parents found lots of pins.
158046: Strange things happened at the G. family's home. Sometimes, for example, they could not manage to shut a door. The horses were often untied and there was always noise to be heard in the meadow. Within a period of eight days, three horses had even died. After the Witheren (White Fathers) of Wittem had come to the stable, the Geelen family had no more misfortune.
158049: At the Yvekruis there were always black kittens that got under the feet of passers-by. Long ago a woman had been murdered at that spot.
158052: The Mannetje van Paal (Little Man of Paal) could make rats run up the church tower. The parish priest freed the boy of his magic power.
158064: Four men who were playing cards suspected there was a cheat in the game. When one man went to pick up a fallen card, he saw that one of the players had hooves instead of legs. The man cried out: "God help me!" The next moment the player with the hooves had disappeared and there was a smell of sulphur.
158068: A farmhand who went to see his girlfriend every evening often had to carry the werewolf on the way back. One evening the farmhand managed to wound the werewolf with a knife. As soon as the werewolf lost blood, he changed into a human. To his great dismay the farmhand recognised his own master. The farmer was so pleased with his farmhand that he did not want him to marry his girlfriend and leave the farm.
158072: A pigeon fancier met 'Tin den duvel', who said: "You should not fly your pigeons today, because they won't win anyway." When the man got home, he was covered in lice.
158078: A man was coming back from Eigenbilzen with a cart of oats. In Hamelsdorp the thunderstorm got so bad that the man had to stop. All along the way a dog had been running under the cart. When the man struck at the dog, the beast jumped away each time. The dog kept breaking wind the whole time. It was a werewolf.
158090: When Kajt came into the church on Easter Sunday, room was immediately made for her. People always urged their children not to accept sweets from Kajt.
158091: At midnight the spirits of the dead could be seen wandering around the churchyard.
158124: A man who owned a special collar could turn himself into a werewolf. When someone had found a werewolf's band and wanted to burn it, the werewolf jumped into the oven to save his collar.
158126: A woman walking along the Balderstraat picked up a pretty kitten or little hare and carried it with her. But the animal grew heavier and heavier. It was a witch.
158135: Some experienced archers just could not manage to hit the bird. A little later the wife of Jan P. came by. Although that witch had never shot a bow before, she managed to hit the bird on the first try.
158136: Every time a black cat came into the stable, something went wrong with the animals. One day a sorcerer was sent for, who forbade the cat to come into the stable again. Since then the cat has not been seen again.
158137: Witches' gatherings were often held at the Tolkesboom in Bree. A man from the Meinestraatje in Bree moved to Roermond and later to Maastricht to work for a blacksmith. When the man met two women in Roermond, one of them asked: "Where are you actually from?", to which the man replied: "I'm from Roermond." But the woman did not believe him and wanted to know the truth at all costs. In the end the man admitted that he was from Bree. At that the woman laughed: "Oh, from Bree! Then you must know that big tree? I was there just yesterday!" The woman was a witch.
158142: Everyone was afraid of hoarse Trijn because people believed she was a witch. When the witch sat down on a chair in church, the chair was completely covered in lice.
158143: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend was terrified when a silent white lady suddenly passed by.
158144: Two men went to play werewolf in the lane in Leut. Zjang A., the former mayor of Opgrimbie, once had to carry the werewolf when he went to visit his girlfriend in Maasmechelen.
158148: A man had moved the boundary post of his land to have a bigger field. After his death he came back as a ghost with a boundary post in his hands. The ghost kept calling: "Where shall I put the boundary post? Where shall I put the boundary post?" One day someone had the courage to answer: "Put the post back where you fetched it from, dammit!" Then the ghost was released.
158153: At midnight a ghost knocked loudly on the gate of the farm.
158156: A boy who was out walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to go away for a moment. If you meet anyone, just throw this red handkerchief." When the girl met someone a little later, she did what her boyfriend had advised. A little later the boy came back. He still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
158173: At the L. family's in Binderveld, they could not make butter from the cows' milk. They were sure a witch was to blame, and they also had a suspicion who that witch might be. Someone advised them to put chaff in the cream, and once they had tried to make butter, they were to go and look in the witch's house. No sooner said than done. The Lievezoons family went to ask a suspected woman in the neighbourhood for a tub. When the door was opened, they saw that people there were busy picking chaff out of the butter. Since then they never let that woman into their house again.
158178: Some rogues always went stealing wood at night. A black witch's cat would then come and sit on their cart.
158181: When M. came out of the café at about eleven o'clock, he saw a foal running around in the meadow, making all the apples fall from the trees. The next morning, however, M. found that not a single apple lay on the ground. That foal had been the werewolf.
158188: On Saturday evening the witches flew singing on a broomstick to Cologne after saying: "Through hedge and thicket all the way to Cologne into the wine cellar".
158201: A man walking by moonlight from Gerdingen to Kaulille was leapt on by a werewolf on the way. The man then grabbed the beast by its legs and carried it to the café 'De oude haan' in Kaulille. In the café the werewolf was thrown into the fireplace, after which it was wounded until it bled. The werewolf turned out to be one of the most prominent people of Kaulille.
158202: A miller was annoyed that a cat often crept into his mill. One day the man cut off one of the cat's legs with a knife. When the man came home, his wife lay wounded on the floor: she had lost a leg.
158207: In Wintershoven lived a man who never worked hard. Although the man was exceptionally lazy, he always got his work done. The man surely had help from the devil.
158222: A carter who was out with his horse could not get home. Only towards morning did the horse come home, foaming at the mouth.
158228: A man who was having a nightmare lay tossing and turning in his bed. The man did not even hear someone calling him. When the maar (nightmare, mare) had gone, the man calmed down again.
158229: A man stood at a crossroads with a black hen. A passer-by offered the man money to buy the hen. But the man did not sell it. The second bidder also did not offer enough to get the hen. The man sold the hen to the third bidder. If you sold a black hen at a crossroads, you could ask as much money as you liked; after all, it was the devil who paid it.
158231: A farmhand named Mosses was often away in the evening because he was a werewolf. He would then get people to carry him. Werewolves had to take care never to be cut by people, for if they lost blood, they changed into a human. One day Mosses was sent away for a few days. Meanwhile the farmer had sent for the priest to burn Mosses's collar. When the collar lay in the fire, Mosses instantly stood beside them to save it. But it was too late for that. Once Mosses was released, he went to America.
158234: Jaak V.D., the husband of Maike V.M., could not get into his own house. When the man reached his street, the sweat dripped from his face. The man was being held back by a witch.
158249: Gijske V.R. went to play bingo at about eleven o'clock in rainy weather. In the moonlight Gijske saw a tall gentleman walking past the haunted wood. "You can stand it well", said Gijske, "you have a good coat on". The ghost did not answer, however, and disappeared a little later.
158255: A witch said to a farmer: "The cow is loose." The farmer saw that the witch was right. When he went to the stable, strangely enough the cow was already tied up again.
158266: A girl whose mother would not let her go to the fair stubbornly insisted: "I'm going anyway." After the woman had patted her daughter on the shoulder, the girl fell ill. In the end the child died. People suspected that her mother was a witch.
158267: After farmer V. had quarrelled with a witch, his rabbits fell ill. After a while the rabbits and the pigs all died as well. In the end the farmer had to move away.
158276: After his death a man came back to haunt along the road in the shape of a black dog.
158290: A man met a large dog at a place where nobody dared to go alone. The man was terrified. A little later the dog had suddenly vanished.
158291: A young man had gone to visit his girlfriend on the Heide. When the boy left, he was warned: "If you go through the Waardestraat at midnight, you will see a white cat sitting on the bridge." And so it happened.
158296: One morning a girl noticed that her boyfriend had pieces of cloth between his teeth. That is how the girl knew her boyfriend was a werewolf.
158297: At the Rozenbergske in Bolderberg someone had seen two glowing eyes. That was the ghost of the lord of the castle, Frisse. In the old days, when someone was taken prisoner, that person was sometimes put in the cellar. They had forgotten to take Frisse out.
158306: A boy was always accompanied by a dog whenever he went somewhere at night. A clergyman managed to free the boy from the dog.
158311: Some people sitting outside in the evening suddenly heard noise in the air, although nothing could be seen. A woman then said: "Those must be spirits floating through the air. Let's just sit quietly until they have passed".
158312: A man carrying a lot of money was robbed and thrown into a pond. That same evening the murdered man came to haunt to take revenge. Some girls who were washing by the pond were pushed head first into the water, although they had nothing to do with the murder.
158315: A man who went to the field in the evening saw a coach with four black horses drive past.
158332: By the Briel at the Krombeek there were always cats playing on a little drum and singing: "Terep, dep, terep, dep, dep, dep... We're going to the fair in Hoelbeek." Because the cats sat there, no one could cross the bridge.
158334: One evening a cat had crept into a man's house. The cat mewed the whole time and scratched the man's feet open. The man believed the cat was a witch.
158344: Because as many as four or five horses had died at a farmer's, the parish priest came to read prayers over the stable and bless it. After that the farmer had no more misfortune.
158354: People who had sold their soul to the devil could change themselves into a dog. In that shape they jumped on passers-by's backs and had themselves carried. Such people had a band that they hid in a tree stump. A farmer who found it strange that his farmhand was gone every night sent the boy far away. Meanwhile the farmer threw the farmhand's band into the oven. As soon as the band caught fire, however, the farmhand was already at the oven to save it. They had to hold the farmhand back.
158369: The mother of the watchmaker of Tongeren was a witch. A little old woman who went to the poorhouse to collect her allowance was accompanied by the witch. But when the old woman arrived at the poorhouse, she could no longer find her poor-relief card, so she had to go back home without money. On the way back the witch said to the old woman: "Take a look at the bottom of your petticoat!" The witch had magicked the card into the poor woman's petticoat.
158373: A werewolf was a person who could change into a dog. A werewolf who was wounded and lost blood was released and became human again.
158391: In the past, people often believed their child had got lice from some witch or other. That was rather obvious, because witches were often dirty women who had lice themselves.
158393: Two soldiers staying at a farm learned from the farmer that his wife was a witch and that all the animals in the stable were bewitched. At midnight the soldiers heard cats yowling. At three in the morning the farmer's wife came home. The next evening the soldiers put a bowl of porridge in the gutter. Soon a whole troop of cats gathered around the porridge. The soldier struck at the animals with his sabre, and they quickly ran off. The next day many women in the village were maimed. The farmer's wife had only one arm left.
158394: In the time of mayor G., a young man called Sterke-Dries lived by the castle. He came from Wellen, the land of the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a band of robbers said to ride goats through the air with the devil), and was the father of Marie van Berke-de-Boer. Sterke-Dries could work magic. One day Sterke-Dries was mowing the grain together with the farmer. Because of the constant rain, however, the grain lay flat on the ground in places, so it was hard to mow. "I'll quickly do something about that," Sterke-Dries said to the farmer, and he threw his cap on the ground, and in the blink of an eye all the grain stood upright. When Sterke-Dries had to manure the field, he lay on his back in the sun all day. In the evening he broke up a small heap of manure, saying "All at once!", and suddenly the whole field was manured. Whenever he came home too late in the evening, the heavy gate was locked with a thick iron bar. Sterke-Dries would then throw his cap against the gate, and it opened at once. Nowadays there is nobody left who can work magic like Sterke-Dries. That is why hardly anyone believes this story.
158411: Near Kermt lived a man suspected of witchcraft. One day a cyclist came across a hare that jumped onto the road in front of him. The cyclist kicked the animal in the head and rode on. The next day a man was walking around the village with a bandage around his head.
158416: There used to be a convent near Eksel station. Every year at Christmas bells were heard ringing underground there. Because the nuns then flew through the air, wonderfully beautiful music was also heard.
158419: A man was coming back from Halen with his horse and cart. When the horse passed a certain house, it refused to go any further. The man wanted to beat the horse when suddenly a wise man of eighty came by and said: "Go to the farm, fetch palm with holy water and make a cross in front of the horse's head." After that had been done, the horse went on again. Then the eighty-year-old man said: "When something like this happens, you must not beat it. If you are standing on the right, you must fetch palm from the left side of the road."
158420: A man had gone to fetch wood in the meadows by moonlight. When he had finished the work, the man walked home along the dike, where a large dog blocked his way. When the man tried to step over the dog, the animal turned into a horse. As a result the man was forced to go home by another road.
158441: On his way to the barber a man met a gentleman wearing a long black coat and carrying a stick. "Good day, sir," said the man, but he got no answer. When the man walked back home, he met the gentleman again. This time too his greeting was not returned. A month later the man went to Tongeren with his brother. On the way they met the strange silent gentleman again, while the dogs barked restlessly. At a corner the gentleman suddenly vanished.
158448: A man who had bought a cow found after two days that the cow no longer gave milk. The man made a pilgrimage to Richel and consulted a priest. The clergyman said: "From now on the cow will give milk again. When you make butter, you must do it in three goes. Within three days the witch will come to ask you for something." After the witch had come by one last time, everything returned to normal.
158473: A woman was constantly followed by the witch Bet K. When the witch appeared in the shape of a cat, the woman poured hot water on the animal's head. That is how the witch burned her head.
158475:
Near Wellen a shepherd happened upon a grate in a field. The shepherd, who had a little rose in his mouth, wanted to throw a pebble through a hole in the grate. When he dropped the pebble, however, the rose also fell from his mouth. A few moments later a voice rang out: "Shepherd, if you had kept your rose, you yourself would have been spared too." The shepherd ran away in fright. When he tried to find the grate again the next day with some others, it had vanished.
A treasure can only be found once every hundred years. If it is not discovered then, one must wait another hundred years.
158486: In the old days people often heard beautiful music coming from the sky. Nothing could be seen of the wild hunt; one could only hear the music. One must on no account call or whistle at that music.
158496: Alvermannetjes (elf men) used to live in Mulhem. The dwarfs have vanished since it was decided to ring the church bells at midday and in the evening.
158509: At night the baron of Opleef always came haunting his estate. In the end the ghost was chained to an oak. Because the ghost always cried "Ai, ai, ai!", this place was later called 'Ai-ai'.
158531: Harry V.N. was walking arm in arm with a man from Wijnes on the gravel road connecting Neerrepen with the main road from Tongeren to Hasselt. In the Groemelingenstraat the drunken men saw a large black dog lying there. Because of it the men had to let go of each other and step carefully past the dog.
158533: A man who was tormented by the maar (nightmare, mare) could not move. As the maar came closer, one slowly lost consciousness. To protect themselves against the maar, people used to put their clogs upside down beside the bed.
158536: After Mass the black lady went to visit acquaintances. She wore a silk skirt whose rustling sound frightened people.
158548: The 'drie bonder' was haunted. Two men did not dare pass it alone because they saw someone standing there waiting for them. Another man, however, could see nothing.
158550: A farmer from Schorrebos went to mass in Nieuwerkerken in a brand-new smock. Suddenly someone said to the farmer: "Oh God, you're covered in lice!" The farmer then went outside to shake the lice off his smock. When the farmer came back in, people said again: "Oh God, you're covered in lice!" The farmer had got the lice from a witch.
158552: Four men were playing cards. One of the men had been unlucky in the game for a long time and said: "I wish the devil would come and play in my place." A little later there was a knock at the door. A man dressed in black came in and took the place of the fourth player. Because a club forms a little cross, the devil could not hold that card. One of the players picked up the fallen card and saw that the strange man had horse's legs.
158563: A boy went with his girlfriend to the fair in Tongerlo. On the way, the boy said to the girl: "I have to go and relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." A little later a big black dog did indeed come running at the girl. She threw the handkerchief at the dog, which tore the cloth to pieces. When the girl was dancing with the boy later that evening, she saw the red threads hanging between his teeth.
158567: The ninety-year-old witch Kait could not die until she had passed her arts on to someone else. She had one daughter and two sons. At first the daughter did not dare to visit her mother, but in the end she did.
158580: A farmer who could not make butter had been given a special ribbon by the friars. Because the ribbon did not help, the man went to the friars again. "You should pay attention to who comes into your house," said the clergymen. The witch was a sister-in-law of the man's wife.
158591: A lord of a castle who had enjoyed himself a great deal during his life had died. Instead of praying for the deceased, the people of the castle preferred to play cards. One day a strange gentleman came to the castle who wanted to join the card game. When one of the men bent down to pick up a fallen card, he saw that the strange gentleman had goat's legs. A little later the gentleman had suddenly disappeared.
158593: A Dutch farmer in Winterslag had a farmhand who had special powers because he owned a little magic book and a collar. For instance, the farmhand could spread a hundred carts of manure on the field in no time. He would manure a small part of the field and then read something from the book, after which the whole field was manured. One day, when the farmhand had been sent to Holland before six o'clock, the farmer lit the oven to burn the young man's collar. As soon as the collar caught fire, the farmhand was standing at the oven to save his band. It took five people to hold him back. As soon as everything had burned up, the farmhand was released.
158594: A boy who was taking a walk with his girlfriend suddenly said: "I have to go and relieve myself. If a bear or a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its snout." When the girl saw a dog a little further on, the handkerchief was torn to pieces by the animal. As soon as the boy reappeared, he asked, grinning and baring his teeth: "Well, did you see anything?" To her great dismay the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
158596: One day Neel T. came to ask Harie to shoot a black cat dead with the hunting rifle. When Harie had shot at the cat, it simply walked on, although he was certain he had hit the animal. The next day Mie V.D.T. lay in bed because she had shot in her buttocks.
158612:
A girl was bewitched by her aunt, who had given her the evil eye. The doctor could not help the girl with any medicine and advised the family to go to the Monnebruurs. These friars read prayers over the child. Then they advised the parents to put a requiem under the threshold and to cover the child's eye with a cloth for nine weeks. The friars added: "Now the witch can no longer harm the child. But a woman will come by who will ask to see the eye, and you must not allow her to. For nine days you must pray: the first day nine Our Fathers, the second day eight, and so one fewer each day. When the nine days are over, the child will be healed." After thanking the friars, the family went home with the girl. When they were home, the aunt came to visit and asked: "Finneke, let me see your eye. Why do you still have to wear that cloth if it's healed anyway?", to which the girl replied: "I can't bear the daylight yet." The next day the aunt came by again, but the girl's sister slapped her in the face and sent her away.
The witch who had given the girl the evil eye had also bewitched her own son. When his pillow was opened, a wreath of coloured yarn was found inside. The little son could not walk and always crawled around on a little cushion. Every night the boy cried from eleven o'clock until midnight, just as if he were being pricked with pins. In the end the father took the boy to the parish priest of Nieuwenhoven. The priest read prayers over the child and said: "Your child has been struck by the evil hand. The evil comes to you every day. Drive it away!" The man did not know whom the priest meant, because so many people came by his house every day. Then the priest said: "Burn that wreath, and the witch will immediately be standing beside you." The man set a pitchfork ready to give the witch a beating. His wife said she was afraid there would be accidents; she took the wreath away and threw it into a nearby cesspit.
158614: A man who had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel died before he could keep his promise. After his death the man came back to haunt his family. The cows lay in the manger with their legs tied together. After a priest had come by to pray and sprinkle the stable with holy water, the ghost no longer showed itself.
158618: Witches could make people be plagued by greenfinches. To prevent that, people held a procession. In it they had to leave a gap of half a metre so that the evil hand could get away.
158634: A man who had moved the boundary post of his land came back to haunt after his death. The ghost held a boundary post in its arms and kept calling: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I leave it?" When one day a passer-by answered: "Throw it where you fetched it from, dammit!", the dead man was released and haunted no more.
158637: A man returning from Sint-Truiden met two strange figures in the wood. When the man grabbed one of the two figures by the hair, suddenly everything vanished.
158640: A witch did harm to her own hens because she wanted to spare people.
158648: A child from Ketsingen had been given an apple by a witch. When the child ate the fruit, it nearly choked because a piece of the apple got stuck in its throat. A little later the child had to vomit, which saved its life. Afterwards the witch was made to promise, with a sabre at her throat, that she would never harm anyone again. Since then nothing strange has happened in Ketsingen.
158663: A man going home in the evening was leapt on by the werewolf. Quickly the man took his knife from his pocket and stabbed the werewolf in the head until it bled. The next moment a man stood before him, who said: "If you don't betray me, I'll let you live; otherwise I must kill you now." The man never dared to mention the werewolf's name.
158671: At R.'s in Kleine-Spouwen a newborn baby had died. From then on the place was haunted. At midnight the doors and windows flew open. After the fathers had been to Bosselen Groeslei and had given their blessing, the haunting stopped. Some time later the woman died.
158672: A ghost with a boundary post walked about in a field. The dead man kept calling: "Where shall I put it?" One night someone answered: "Put it where you fetched it from." With that the ghost was released.
158685: By the Maas someone always appeared at midnight, calling: "Ferry me over! Ferry me over!" After something was returned to the ghost, it was released.
158702: A woman of the C. family walked to the bakehouse of a house in the neighbourhood. The frightened family hurried to the bakehouse, but the woman had vanished without a trace.
158722: At Lowieke's there was so much noise in the attic at night that no one could sleep.
158729: Gruesome things once took place in the castle of Dessener. In the cellar the slaves were tortured; their hands were cut open and salt was then sprinkled into the wounds. That castle was haunted for many years afterwards. Sometimes the gate flew open, and a lord drove in with a coach and four black horses. Because of these strange events, nobody wanted to come and work at the castle. When a friar came from Hasselt to banish the ghost, a voice suddenly said: "You can do nothing to me, for you have committed a mortal sin yourself." Then another friar came, who read prayers over the castle and banished the ghost to an oak in the woods. Some time later a poacher had shot four hares and two rabbits in those woods when he saw a carriage approaching. Strangely, no horses were pulling the carriage, and the coach seemed to be made of fire. The poacher made off as fast as he could. When he went to look at daybreak, there was nothing strange to be seen. His hares and rabbits lay exactly where he had left them.
158731: Some men working for the municipality had to do a job near a witch's house. Suddenly one of the workers got a severe pain in his leg. Because the man could not keep working, he hobbled home. When he was almost home, the pain suddenly disappeared. People thought the witch had become frightened and had therefore quickly put an end to her tormenting.
158744: At midnight bells were heard ringing underground at the Waterbroeck. Anyone who dared to come near then sank into the ground.
158758: A farmer was out with his horse and cart. When the farmer met a witch on the way, the horse suddenly refused to go any further.
158759: The mother of Ties W. often went to the mill with her children and a wheelbarrow. One day on the way they met an ugly woman, who said: "What beautiful children you have!" The woman stroked the girl and the little boy on the head and gave them each an apple. Mother W. threw the children's apples away. But she had not seen that the girl had already bitten into her apple. When they got home, the girl was dead. The poor child had become a witch.
158760: A farmer had a farmhand who sneaked outside every night at about the same time. He crawled into a hollow oak tree and a little later came out again in the shape of a big black dog. One day they sent the farmhand far away so that they could burn his animal skin in the meantime. Shortly afterwards the farmhand died.
158763: When the animals in the stable fell ill, people believed it was the fault of a witch.
158764: Around eight in the evening a man went to the ramparts with his black dog. At the gate stood a gentleman dressed immaculately in black. The dog began to bark furiously and wanted to go to the man. But suddenly the animal turned round and ran off with its tail between its legs. After that evening the dog stayed in its kennel for two days. That gentleman was probably the devil.
158777: Two men returning from the Reulis farm in Opoeteren met a horse on the way that blocked their path. When the men said: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, be gone," the horse vanished.
158778: Helm J. kept wondering where his late wife might be. The priest had several times tried to reassure him by saying his wife had always been a good person. One evening a handsome gentleman stood at Helm's door and said: "I've come to tell you your wife is not with me, damn it!" That gentleman must have been the devil.
