158780: Some people went to the friars of Hasselt because they suspected that a witch lived near them. The friars gave the people a relic to put under the threshold of the stable.
158786: A farmer who found cats in his kitchen heard the lead cat say: "If you want to, then do it!" At that the farmer poured boiling water over the cats. The next day all the witches in the village showed burns.
158787: Four men were playing cards. One of the men found it odd that some cards were always missing from the game. Suddenly the man saw the missing cards lying under the table. When the man bent down to pick up the cards, he saw that one of the players had a goat's leg. The man cried out in fright: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph!" The next moment the player with the goat's legs ran quickly outside. It was the devil.
158789: People were very afraid of the vuurman (fire-man), because he had set a farm on fire somewhere.
158805: Police officer Laurent lived in Tongeren. One day his daughter fell off the ladder while fetching hay for the sheep. The girl broke her hand. Because the wound did not heal, the girl's arm had to be amputated. "That was Lala's doing!" said someone from the neighbourhood.
158810: A boy from Voort was courting a girl from Loon. One day, when the boy went walking with his girlfriend, he suddenly said: "Wait here a moment. I'll be back in half an hour. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. After a while the boy came back. The girl noticed that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
158820: When a werewolf's band had been thrown into the fire, the devil stood by the oven to save the band. As soon as everything had burnt up, the werewolf was released.
158831: On the bridge by J.'s farm a white lady appeared who always sat on a chair. At midnight a man had asked the apparition what she was doing there. The white lady had answered: "The night is for me and the day for you." Once, when the chair had been taken away, everything went dark and strange things happened.
158837: To recognise a witch, one had to place one's feet crosswise in her footprints and then make the sign of the cross. If the woman in question was a witch, she would come back.
158843: In Heppeneert there lived a witch who could make mice without tails.
158848: The parents of a girl who was ill every night at twelve o'clock went to Liège, where the priest gave them a medal to put under the first step of the stairs. After that the witch could no longer get in.
158851: A man who had been ill for a long time believed he was bewitched. In the pillow the man slept on, a peacock without a head was found. After that strange object had been removed from the pillow, the man recovered.
158859: A man returning from Zolder heard a creaking in the oak hedge at the Zevenvaart, although there was no wind. The sound came closer and then vanished.
158864: The drossaard (bailiff) was a representative of the king or the duke. Because the drossaard also held judicial power, he had many enemies. After the drossaard's death his spirit was banished to a bridge. At midnight chains could be heard rattling there.
158867: Will-o'-the-wisps were ghosts that followed people and then disappeared into the marshland.
158873: After his death C. came haunting his castle. Because people no longer dared to pass the castle, a new road had to be built.
158874: In Wezent lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. After the son of the shop owner had been to see the witch, he was covered in lice.
158878: A man who worked at the zinc factory saw a hare in the meadow behind the factory. When the man shot the hare, the animal said: "Damn, you've got me!" The man went to pick up the hare and found in the animal's ear a note with the following text: "O, you silly fool, I am finally dead now. I have been kicked and beaten, and now I'm even being carried off by the boss of the zinc factory."
158879: In the alley next to the churchyard, near the grave of Heilig Janneke (Holy Janneke), a boy and a girl often met. One evening, at the place where they had agreed to meet, the girl saw a figure in a white shirt. The girl was convinced it was her boyfriend trying to frighten her. But when she pulled off the white shirt, a skeleton stood before her. The girl fell ill with fear and sought advice from a friar. He said she had to give the shirt back to the ghost. The friar offered to go with her so that the ghost would not harm her. At midnight the friar and the girl went to the alley, where they pulled the shirt back over the skeleton. After that the girl was cured.
158893: An orphan girl living with Jan W. could not sleep at night because there was always a cat in her room. After Jan had shot at the cat, Jona had a large wound on her hand.
158905: On the Boschkant near the fort a witches' fair was often held at night. People then heard the noise of a hundred mewing cats. The man, the woman and the children who lived nearby were held in their beds by a strange force. When some people kept watch one night, nothing happened. After pastor T. had read prayers over the house, no more cats came.
158916: In Maasmechelen there lived a witch who taught her arts to her daughter. Mother and daughter could both make mice. "Children, shall I make some little mice?" the mother said, and the next moment mice came running out of her clog.
158918: A soldier was standing guard with a certain Mesotte from Alken when suddenly a cat came walking up. Mesotte then said: "I'm going to shoot that one in the backside!" The next moment the cat had vanished and an old woman with a bunch of keys came walking up. "Oh, so you wanted to shoot me in the backside!" said the woman. "Here are the keys to my house. Tomorrow morning at six o'clock I'll be sitting on the roof there." The next morning the man was seen sitting on the roof as a cat. Three days later Mesotte was given a cigar by a gentleman, who said: "That's from the cat of three days ago!"
158932: In Herkenrode, ghostly nuns came at night to draw water from the Demer. There used to be a convent there.
158934: A man from Tiewinkel, a hamlet of Lummen, went to market with his horse. When the man passed a woman's house, she slapped the animal on the hindquarters and said: "You might as well leave the horse there." A while later the men brought the horse back from the market after all. The animal was paralysed.
158936: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. Near the "Drie Heef" stood a tall hedge. A man regularly walked his little dog near that hedge. One day the dog found nappies of unbaptised children in the hedge.
158954: When Jan went home from farmer V.'s, he saw a cat sitting on a turnstile. When he reached the turnstile, the man was jumped on by the cat. The cat grew so heavy that the man sank to his knees and lay on the ground. Since that evening the man never again came home through the Ulfart.
158956: A card-playing knight had sold his soul to the devil. As was his habit, the man prayed three Hail Marys to Saint Gertrude every evening. After seven years the knight went to the little bridge where the devil stood waiting for him. "Yes," said the devil, "I will come and take you, but first you must chase away that woman sitting behind you on your horse." The knight was protected by Saint Gertrude.
158961: In Bilzen there lived a man who could conjure mice out of a sack of flour. After the dean had said a prayer, the man could no longer make mice.
158964: A man going to pick nuts saw a witch walk past. When the man crossed his feet in the witch's footprints, she stood still.
158966: One day Charel A. was coming back from Binderveld when he suddenly heard wonderfully beautiful music above his head. All at once Charel saw a whole group of witches dancing and having fun. "Please let me through," said Charel. One of the witches, Trui M., knew Charel and said: "He's an acquaintance, let him through." The other witches all wanted to dance with Charel, but the frightened man said: "I have to go home, my wife is ill," to which one of the witches replied: "That's not true at all: your wife is asleep in bed!" Charel was lucky that Trui was willing to help him, or he would not have got away so easily.
158968: A black cat always roamed around the house of Trui S. Roger never managed to chase the cat away. Since the day Koba C. died, the cat has never been seen again.
158983: A witch who had to go to communion spat out the host. The person who tried to pick up the host got his fingers stuck deep in the stone.
158984: A ghost had been banished under the bridge by the 'brook of Frisse'. Frisse had hanged himself.
158987: A witch had visited a little boy. When the witch had gone, it was found that the boy's little legs were not the same length.
159000: A pedlar came to an old woman who told him that her child was dying. "I'll help you," said the pedlar, and he hid behind the door. A little later the pedlar saw a witch come in. He grabbed her from behind and said: "Now you're going to stop tormenting that child! If you don't admit you're guilty, I'll throw you in the fire". In the end the witch confessed her guilt. Then the pedlar said to the witch: "I'll go with you and smash all the statues of saints that you stick pins into every day". Later about a thousand pins were found in the bed where the sick child slept.
159006: Whoever was ridden by the maar (nightmare, mare) began to sweat heavily. One then wanted to shout, but did not wake up. Some people claimed the maar was a stopping of the blood.
159026: A boy who was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend said on the way: "Wait a moment, I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you in the meantime, throw this red handkerchief at the beast." When the girl met a dog a little further on, she did what her boyfriend had advised. A little later the boy came back to his girlfriend. The girl noticed that the boy still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
159032: A man got lost because he was under the influence of a witch.
159034: On a farm in Germany worked a farmhand named Thies, who always disappeared around midnight from the loft where he slept. At dawn the farmhand came back. Even when the ladder had once been taken away, Thies got outside without any trouble at twelve o'clock. People had been advised by someone to burn the farmhand's belt. When the belt lay in the fire, a terrible stench could be smelled. Five or six people had to hold Thies so that he would not jump into the fire. When the belt had burnt up completely, the farmhand was released. Since then Thies never went away at night again.
159045: A clergyman had banished the ghost of the count to an oak near the castle of Wideux. Later the oak was cut down. The ghost had to stay there until the oak had completely rotted away.
159050: A man was brought home at night by the devil.
159052: One winter, around ten o'clock, a man saw a polar bear with big eyes in the churchyard. When other people came to look at the apparition, there was nothing more to be seen.
159068: Fik L. had seven children. Five of those children developed a swollen neck shortly after birth and died soon afterwards. The children had been bewitched by a neighbour.
159069: A farmer's cart of grain got stuck in front of a witch's house. "Just you wait, filthy witch," said the farmer, and he slashed with his knife between the spokes of the wheel. The next day the witch wore a bandage around her head.
159090: Some people went with a horse one evening to bring a piece of tart to a relative. In the Kuitstraat a wolf sat beside the ditch and said: "Don't let that horse go so fast, the mud is all flying at me".
159098: A woman from Eigenbilzen had lain dying for eight days. In the end the witch did die. A sick child that was bewitched cried all the time when the witch was not nearby. When the witch was present, the child stopped crying.
159120: A farmer drove his horse and cart past 'de tap' in Kerniel. Suddenly the horse stopped for no apparent reason. When the man made the sign of the cross, the horse could go on again.
159126: Because the moneyman's animals kept dying, the man consulted a priest. While the priest was reading prayers, he suddenly could not read any further because the letters were upside down. Since then the moneyman's animals stayed healthy.
159129: A man returning from Tongeren came across a cat between Mal and Millen. The man said: "Minneke pussy, where do you come from?", to which the cat replied: "Janneke V. said to me: Minneke Pussy, where do you come from."
159157: Every time a woman had been to Tongeren with her little son Eugène, the boy fell ill. On the way a witch had rubbed his little head. After the friars had read prayers over Eugène, the boy recovered.
159160: A man driving his cart past a witch's house met someone who asked: "Aren't you afraid the harness will break?" The man replied: "That can't happen, because everything is securely fastened." A little further on, however, the harness broke after all.
159179: The little chapel by the canal was haunted. Every evening a ghostly nun appeared who came to open the red gate of a nearby farm. At night the boys of the D. family saw the nun appear and then disappear again. A man who went to fetch water from the Kloosterbeek at ten o'clock one moonlit evening saw the nun appear. When the man tried to follow the nun in his socks, she disappeared again.
159182: On the Oppenhof stood a tree stump that gave off light at night.
159184: In the evening will-o'-the-wisps appeared by the water of the Jeker. They were forsaken souls. Passers-by then had to pray so that the lights would go out one by one.
159185: In Rummen there was a farmer who had a maid working for him. Although the maid was in reality a witch, she had never harmed the people she worked for. One day, for example, the farmer had a calf that was at death's door. The maid came and said: "But that calf isn't ill!", and she knocked the calf over, after which it jumped up and was cured. When a cow stuck its head out of the stable, the farmer shouted: "A cow is loose! Go and tie it up!", but when the farmhands came into the stable, the cow was already tied up. One day, however, Meranceke, the farmer's little daughter, fell ill: the child got a lump and nothing could be done about it. In the end Meranceke died. After that incident the maid was dismissed after all. In her bed a witches' book was found, but nobody could understand a word of it.
159187: In Weert there was a black cat that always walked along with everyone but never came inside anywhere. One day, on seeing the cat, the man decided to read something aloud from the Gospel of Saint John. At that the cat disappeared for good.
159191: At a farmer's wife's home the baby always fell ill after a certain woman had come to fetch milk. When someone came to drive out the devil, the farmer's wife was advised to put a relic under the threshold and a sprig of palm above the door. If one did not say "Come in", the witch could not enter. When that woman came to fetch milk after that, she indeed could no longer get in.
159206: When Nelis K. came back from Tongeren, he saw a big black dog sitting by the Zwart Kruis. Because the dog would not leave, the man said: "Sacred Heart of Jesus, help me", took off his hat and made the sign of the cross. The next moment the dog had vanished.
159244: At Jef A.'s they could not churn butter. After the priest had sprinkled the tub with holy water, the problems were solved.
159245: A farmhand staying in the house of the deceased drossaard (bailiff) found it strange that his horse was completely covered in sweat in the morning. The Hobos has always had a bad name.
159250: A family from Heusden was always visited by the neighbour woman. After a while there was a large toad in the house. The woman poured a pan of hot fat over the animal. The next moment the neighbour's child came rushing in, saying: "Can you come and look, because mother has burned her back!"
159255: A young man who used to walk his girlfriend home in the evening said to the girl at midnight: "I'm sorry, but today I can't possibly go with you. I have to leave urgently." When the girl went home alone, she met a big black dog on the way. At that moment the girl remembered the advice her boyfriend had once given her and she threw a handkerchief at the beast. The next day the girl found that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
159258: When Nielke S. came back from the village one evening, he saw two hares sitting there. Nielke said to the animals: "Wait, I'll play you a little tune on my bagpipes." When Nielke began to play, the hares took hold of each other and began to dance. They must have been witches.
159259: A witch had visited a child that died a short time afterwards. Anyone who wanted to keep a witch out had to put a broomstick by the door or draw a cross on the threshold with chalk.
159275: People often promised to have a mass said for their deceased relatives. If those people had not kept their promise, will-o'-the-wisps appeared. They were the souls of the dead who hoped to be released through prayer.
159296: When a witch had died in Vechmaal, the people were very relieved. In the past they had deliberately taken a detour so as not to have to pass the witch's house. When someone drove past that house with a cart of grain, the witch would say: "That wagon will tip over before you're home!" And so it happened.
159315: A farmer who had almost finished mowing decided to work a little longer before going home. Suddenly a black cat appeared and said: "You needn't hurry, because you won't get it finished today anyway!" At that the farmer, annoyed, struck at the cat. The next moment, however, he saw a mass of cats in the field, so that he could not go on working and was forced to go home.
159329: Some men out poaching tried to catch a hare. One of the poachers had already shot at the hare, but a little later the animal was jumping about again. Another man had no bullets left in his gun and decided to kill the hare with a stick. His friend said, however: "You won't kill that hare, because it's a witch!" After the other man had struck the hare down with a stick, the animal did indeed jump up again.
159331: In Velm lived a wizard who could turn himself into a tiger.
159341: When people went to fetch water at the well in Opgrimbie, they usually had to carry the werewolf.
159352: A man whose wife had died was walking through an alley in Neerrepen. In the alley a ghost held out its hand. The man shook the hand and went on. It must have been the ghost of his dead wife.
159369: Two men walking home together one evening saw a strange apparition on the way that looked like a communicant.
159370: When someone was ill, people often made all sorts of vows so that the person would get well again. If those people did not fulfil their vow, the sick person came back to haunt after his death.
159385: The Freemasons met in an underground passage. Whoever wanted to join the lodge had to sign in blood and then trample a consecrated host.
159386: A man walking on the Piannesberg suddenly heard strange things. Although there was no wind, the pines made a creaking sound. In Miel's wood the man heard someone calling: "Aho... Aho...".
159391: A woman from Hasselt often came begging at the V. family's. When one day the beggar woman picked lice off herself and put them on the roller used to level the land, father Verheyen had had enough; he grabbed the woman and threw her out. When the man came back in, his wife cried in astonishment: "But Chris, you're completely covered in lice!" The man stuck three lice on a pin, which he laid at a crossroads. Then he set off on a pilgrimage to be rid of the lice. On the way Chris met the wife of the Veld family. The woman, who had just had the beggar woman in her house, was wearing an apron with white and black checks. The white checks, however, were completely black with lice. Then Veld's wife went along with Chris on the pilgrimage. Before the two had reached their destination, the beggar woman passed them. She stood still for a moment, bent down, and then walked on. At that moment Chris and Veld's wife were rid of all their lice.
159412: A little child could make mice from a handful of sand.
159421: A hotel room was haunted every night between twelve and one o'clock. One day a brave man asked if he could sleep in that room. The hotel owner was delighted, because he already feared he would never be able to use the room again. The man had a curtain hung above the bed, with a small slit through which he could watch the ghosts. At twelve o'clock sharp dozens of ghosts came in, who began to dance and make music. It seemed as if the room had turned into a forest with a thick oak in the middle. The ghosts began to dig between the roots of the oak and brought up a large chest of money. The man watched and thought: "I must remember where that imaginary oak stands; then I can dig up the money from under the floor later." The man jumped out of bed and relieved himself on the spot where the oak stood. The next day the man told the hotel owner what he had seen. The floor was broken open at the spot where the tree had stood. The hotel owner was honest enough to share the money found there with the man; after all, he was glad to be rid of the ghosts.
159422: A man who went to fetch wood in the forest with his horse every day did not know why the animal always started limping at a certain spot. Ten metres further on the horse could go on without trouble again. The next times the man took another route, although that way he had to cover a much greater distance. Because the man knew it was a mortal sin to work on Sunday, he deliberately harnessed his horse and went to fetch some earth. When the horse passed the notorious house, it started limping again. In that house lived a woman who bewitched the horse because her brother had wanted to buy the animal at the market in Tongeren. One day the horse almost died after being chased by a swarm of wasps.
159426: A man from Zonhoven had seen a house shaking and rattling. The man believed this was caused by a witch.
159437: An alley in Heks was haunted. The man with the 'Krellehoedje' rode through it alone on horseback at night. In that alley people always heard a strange sound like the rustling of clothes. But when they came closer, there was nothing to be seen. Perhaps there were witches.
159442: On a farm in Lommel worked a farmhand who could turn himself into a werewolf. One day, when the farmer wanted to go to Kerkhoven together with the farmhand, he told his wife to burn the farmhand's collar in the meantime. The moment the band was thrown into the fire, the farmhand immediately set off for Lommel because he felt something was wrong. The farmhand covered a distance of five kilometres in two minutes. Still, the farmhand was relieved when his band had been burnt.
159448: The Sterbos in Stevoort was haunted. One evening a drunk man went from the café to the Sterbos, where he saw a nun standing in the middle of the road. "Come, I'll give you some tobacco," said the man. The nun replied: "Leave everything standing that stands. The night is for me, but the day is for you." Then the man went away. A little further on the man felt the ghost jump onto his back and let itself be carried to the edge of the wood. Two days later the man died.
159457: A man who went looking for the werewolf with a knife did not find it. The werewolf looked like a black dog that sometimes jumped on someone's back and had itself carried. If you could wound the werewolf so that it bled, it turned into a human.
159460: A bricklayer from Mettekoven who worked at the sugar factory in Hoepertingen was coming home along the Voortdreef. On the way the man was followed by a cat that kept getting under his feet. When the man kicked at the animal, some twenty cats came at him. The man was so frightened that he no longer dared to go on.
159461: A bricklayer from Mettekoven who worked at the sugar factory in Hoepertingen was coming home along the Voortdreef. On the way the man was followed by a cat that kept getting under his feet. When the man kicked at the animal, some twenty cats came at him. The man was so frightened that he no longer dared to go on.
159463: On the Ruttenveld behind the meadows, lights burned that moved back and forth all the time. It was said that they were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised.
159464: A boy was in a relationship with a girl. The boy got the fright of his life when the devil suddenly stood before him. The axe he was holding turned into a cat, which attacked him and then ran away.
159469: One day a girl went to visit a sick person. The patient's mother took the girl's hand and rubbed it over the sick person's skin. When the girl got home, she was ill herself. The girl went to the doctor, who asked her whether she had eaten anything special. The girl answered: "Yes, I ate a piece of cake and drank a cup of coffee. That woman kept making signs of the cross over it." Because the girl was bewitched, her father advised her to go to a woman in Liège. That woman took a glass of water and made signs of the cross the whole time. Neither the woman nor the doctor could help the girl. When the girl came back from mass in Beverlo, she sometimes had attacks of her illness. The girl was ill for three years. After the girl had an operation in Leuven, she was cured.
159504: A man nicknamed Americain had a little daughter who was bewitched. One day a woman came to visit Americain and suggested cutting open the child's pillow. In the pillow they found a wreath of roses in which two little roses were still missing. A friar from Tongeren read prayers over the child, and the parents went on pilgrimage with the girl. After some time the daughter was cured.
159506: In Rutten there lived a little boy who could make mice from earth. A clergyman baptised the boy again. The boy was very sad when he could no longer make mice afterwards.
159508: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen near marshes and fens. It was said that they were the souls of stillborn children. Whoever dared to follow a will-o'-the-wisp ended up in the water.
159517: A little boy had got a swollen shoulder after a witch touched him. The boy's father went to the witch with a dung fork and said: "If you don't cure my son soon, I'll stick you on my dung fork!" "All right," the witch said then. After that the boy was cured.
159521: A boy who had hanged himself had to haunt after his death. When the dead boy's brother saw the ghost standing by the fruit tree, he went to call his mother. "What do you want?" the mother had asked. The mother had to keep her vow and go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel so that her son's soul would find rest.
159523: In the old days many poachers came to Meeuwen to hunt hares. One day Marsjepier shot a hare, after which he reloaded his gun. Meanwhile another hare appeared, but Marsjepier could not hit it. The hare came to sniff at the barrel of the gun and then said: "Grietje, where are you?", to which the shot hare replied: "In Marsjepier's sack!"
159530: When the children walked along the Groenstraat, they often saw lights under the Canadian poplars. They were of course glow-worms, but the children's mother said: "Those are the little souls from purgatory coming to ask for prayers". Because the children were afraid, they would then pray an Our Father or a Hail Mary.
159532: When Cilis from Mopertingen was returning from the fair in Bilzen, he was surrounded by five witches. Cilis had to follow the witches and ended up in Hamelsdorp. Because the witches stood giggling at the crossroads, Cilis said: "If I knew it was you who did this to me, I'd cut your throat!"
159544: When it had been discovered that R.'s farmhand was a werewolf, the boy was sent to Diest. Then the pastor came to the farm to throw the werewolf's collar into the fire. At that moment the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his collar. As soon as the band had burnt up, the farmhand thanked the pastor for his help.
159562: The tailor's daughters went out together one evening to do some shopping. When the girls came back, they heard terrifying screaming. The daughters quickly went to call their father, who walked along the road with an axe. At that moment the witch appeared. She had hidden in a pipe that lay under the ground.
159566: The mother of a disabled boy cut open her son's pillow and found all sorts of little flowers and wreaths in it. After the friars had consecrated and blessed the house, the witch could no longer get in. The mother also had a mass said for her son.
159567: One winter evening a farmer and his wife were sitting in the stable with a sow that was about to farrow. Suddenly they heard strange noises, as if the horses had been untied. But when they went to look, nothing turned out to be wrong. Some time later they dug up a skeleton in the stable. Once that skeleton had been taken away, no more strange things happened.
159569: In the house of J.B., strange things always happened at seven or eight in the evening. The cows flew up against the ceiling and the pots and pans danced through the house. One day human and cow skulls were found in the ground there.
159588: A man and a woman were nearly frightened to death when they saw the ghost of a dead person appear in the churchyard.
159594: In the house of a man from Engsbergen there was a window in which no pane could be fitted; the glass always fell out. That man was himself a witch.
159607: A woman was covered in lice after a witch had visited her. The priest tried to reassure people by pointing out that baptised people were in no danger from evil.
159611: When K. was coming back from Kesselt, he saw a pack of cats near the café drinking from a puddle. More and more cats kept appearing. A few years later a friend of his met a little dog at that same spot, which blocked his way.
159618: A hunter had shot a hare. When he came closer, the animal oddly got up again and leapt away. A little later a dog and a cat appeared at the same spot and began digging in the ground so hard that the earth flew all around. The hunter walked on a little and then looked back. He saw a white lady, who said: "If you dare come any closer, I'll shoot!" The hunter was so frightened that he quickly walked away.
159652: In the Donkerstraat in Riksingen a white lady, who was in fact a witch, appeared at midnight.
159655: A boy who found it strange that his girlfriend was always away on Sundays asked if he could come along once. The boy had to sit on the tips of the girl's toes, and if anyone asked: "What are you travelling over?", he had to answer: "Over a coat rack." After the witch had said: "To Cologne, into the wine cellar," they flew off. At the ball in Cologne there was drinking and dancing to their hearts' content. Because the boy was drunk, they put him in a bed. When some women came to tease him, he said: "In God's name, leave me alone!" The next moment everything had vanished. The next morning the boy went to confession with the priest. But he was not allowed to tell everything, or the witches would break his neck. In the evening the boy flew off with his girlfriend again. This time he took care not to drink too much. When the boy wanted to go home, he had to cross a brook. The bridge that normally lay across the brook, however, had vanished. In the morning the boy's girlfriend came and laid the bridge across the brook.
159672: A man from Vliermaal got lost in Rutten because of a witch. If a witch tried to touch you, it was best to hit her on the head.
159679: Janneke saw a cat and asked: "Pussyminneke, where do you come from?" When Janneke was home, a whole troop of cats came to sing at his door: "Janneke asked me: 'Pussyminneke, where do you come from?' If Janneke had not spoken so nicely, we would have broken his neck."
159700: A girl was coming back with her boyfriend from the Hasselt fair when she suddenly saw a strange dog chasing her. The boy, however, did not see the dog. A little later the animal had vanished.
159702: A man returning from the fair around midnight through a sunken lane was annoyed by a little cat that kept walking ahead of him. The man angrily said to the animal: "Go on, you filth, get out of here! If you won't go away, I'll carry you on my arm!" When the man got home, he went straight to bed. The next day his mother said: "You've brought a cat home! I'll chase it away. Who knows what might happen otherwise!"
159705: A woman was walking on the Abdijberg towards the park. Suddenly a black cat appeared that kept running between the woman's legs. After a while the woman said to herself: "What is the matter with that cat?", to which the animal replied: "I am a little woman with a little skirt and a little hat just like you." At that moment the cat grew bigger and bigger until it had taken the shape of a woman.
159709: A man who had to carry the werewolf managed to wound the beast with his knife. The next day a man from the village lay in bed with a stab wound.
159711: The Steenbeek in Winterslag was haunted. The miller who lived there always saw cats appearing.
159712:
A boy cycling back from Hasselt saw a rabbit jump against his wheel on the way. Later that day two girls from the village visited a woman, saying: "We are so hungry!" The witch replied: "I can't cut a slice of bread, because my arm hurts." The witch had injured herself on the bicycle wheel in the shape of a rabbit.
The witch's husband claimed that his wife could not be woken at night.
159715: If one wanted to know whether a woman was a witch, one had to place one's feet crossed on her footprints. A witch would then have to look back.
159716: People from Vurten who could not make butter went to the friars of Hasselt. After the people had made a novena, they could make butter again.
159731: On a castle farm worked a farmhand who turned into a werewolf at night. All the farmhands of the farm had to fetch coal in Liège, and they made a bet as to who would be first at the coal pit. They all decided to leave at night. Some farmhands pulled the axles out of the werewolf's wagon and secretly took his skin with them. While the werewolf was putting the axles back into his wagon, the devil let him know that the other farmhands wanted to burn his skin. The werewolf left the horse cart and ran as fast as he could to the place where the fire was. Just in time the werewolf managed to seize the skin. Meanwhile the devil had made the werewolf's horse cart drive on by itself, so that the werewolf still arrived first in Liège.
159735: Nandus wanted his barn finished before the harvest had to be brought in. One day Nandus was visited by a gentleman who said: "I will finish your barn before the cock starts crowing tomorrow morning. In return you must sell me your soul". Nandus agreed to the proposal and signed a contract in blood. When it was almost morning, however, the man became so frightened that he went up into the loft and clapped his hands until the cock began to crow. Because the barn was not quite finished at that moment, the man was allowed to keep his soul.
159746: Some people were making butter when a witch suddenly came in. From that moment on, strangely enough, the people could no longer make butter. After a holy relic had been laid under the threshold, the witch could no longer get in.
159765: A man had sold his soul to the devil. If the man could not bring the devil an animal he did not yet know, he would have to die. Because the desperate man went about in sorrow, his wife asked him what was wrong. After the man had confessed everything, the woman said: "That's not so bad, I'll help you. I'll take off my clothes. Then you must smear me with syrup and stick me full of feathers." No sooner said than done. When the woman crawled on hands and feet to the devil, he said: "That's a strange beast! And it has no tail. I've never seen that before!" After that the man was free.
159769: A little boy could make mice. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it could no longer make mice.
159787: Because Toon's pigs were all dying, the man went to the friars of Bree. The clergymen gave Toon a small picture that he had to wall into the wall.
159790: A man who could not manage to make butter went to the holy little friar in the Franciscan friary in Hasselt. The man was given three biscuits to feed to the cows and a relic to hang above the stable door.
159807: One evening a woman went to fetch her husband from the pub. Because the man would not come with her, the woman had to go home alone. On the way she was followed by a man with a skull for a head and a long white beard. The frightened woman hurried inside. The next morning, to her great dismay, she discovered that a thick tree had grown in front of her door. Because the door could no longer open or close, the tree had to be sawn down.
159814: A boy from Mopertingen was in a relationship with a girl who lived with her mother. "Do you know your girlfriend is a witch? Don't you always have to leave at half past eight?" someone had said. When the boy went to visit his girlfriend the next Sunday, he pretended to have fallen asleep drunk at the table. At half past eight the boy saw his girlfriend rub herself with witch's grease and then say: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Aachen". As soon as the girl was gone, the boy also rubbed himself with the ointment and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Aachen". The boy arrived in Aachen badly injured.
159841: The witch Lala had sold medals and a pot of beans to a watchmaker in Tongeren. After a few days, however, the man's little daughter fell ill. The mother went to a clergyman in Luik, who said: "Your little daughter has been bewitched by a certain woman. I will give you a relic that you must lay under the threshold. Your husband will want to know who the witch is, but he must not look. And you must look in the mirror of the draper's shop across from your house." The witch tried three times in vain to get into the house. Then she went away. After that the sick girl slowly recovered.
159855: At night a man saw the spirit of his dead sister standing beside his bed. One day the man had run away in fear because he had seen the ghost sitting in the plum tree. Later he said his sister must be holy, because the ghost in the tree had worn a white robe.
159858: Mie P. often came begging at a house in Beverst. People did not dare send the witch away for fear she would fill the whole house with lice. After two crossed straws had been laid under the threshold, the witch could no longer come in.
159868: When Sander L. was coming back from Geneberg in the evening, he came across a cat that rubbed against his legs. Sander picked the animal up and stroked it. Further on Sander heard a voice behind him saying: "Sander, Sander, if you had not spoken to me so nicely, I would have broken your neck."
159879: One Monday morning someone at the Heilige Haag struck with a whip at a cat sitting on a cart. Five minutes later there were some five hundred cats on the cart.
159883: In the Lang Wei behind the church in Wilderen, witches sometimes came to ride the horses. In the morning the animals were drenched in sweat. The people in the neighbourhood could clearly hear the horses galloping at night, but nobody dared to go and look. When they went to look at first light, they saw a ring around the big tree where the witches had ridden on horseback. The grass there was completely gone, and no new grass could be sown there.
159886: If you met a black cat between midnight and one o'clock, the animal would not get out of the way. If you then struck the cat, a maimed old woman would pass by shortly afterwards.
159889: Every time a mother washed her little son, a black cat jumped onto the windowsill, making the child cry. After the father had placed a relic on the windowsill, the cat no longer dared to jump onto it.
159892: During a card game the jack of spades kept falling on the floor. Then Freke said: "I'll have the devil bring a bottle of wine." One of the players replied that he would gladly drink that wine. When there was a knock a little later and a hand appeared holding a bottle of wine, nobody but Freke dared to take the bottle. When the wine was put on the table, the jack of spades was lying on the table too. The next day there was a horse's hoof print in the door.
159912: The parish priest of Sluizen was on holiday when one evening his brother had to go and fetch the midwife. The man put on the priest's habit to go to Millen. On the way a big black dog came at the man. The dog jumped with its front paws onto the man's heels. At a crossroads the dog could go no further, so the animal had to make a detour. A little later, however, the dog came at the man again. When the man got home scared to death, he was glad he had had the priest's habit as protection.
159921: The little woman of the Moes could cure toothache by making a few small crosses over the bad tooth with her dirty black finger.
159934: In Meeuwen there was a werewolf that dug a hole under the barn and so got into the houses. People had already tried to shoot the animal, but whenever the werewolf was nearby, the gun would not work. One day someone did manage to kill the werewolf by attaching something blessed to the gun. Immediately afterwards the werewolf became human again. The man was pushed into the ground. Nearby a dog was also shot, to pass it off as the werewolf. Still, there was a lot of trouble over it, because a person from the village had also disappeared.
159939: Two men had to go and look for something in the church garden in the dark one evening. Suddenly the men heard the rustling of silk clothes. The men were so frightened that they did not dare move. A little later the strange apparition had vanished.
159950: A man from Ketsingen saw a black woman with pearls walking alongside him.
159951: A woman from the Scherpesteenhoeve went on a pilgrimage to Tongeren with her sister. People said a woman came haunting on Henegouwberg, but the two pilgrims had seen nothing.
159955: Cats always came into a house through the water drain. The cats would sit with the people and begin to dance. One day a man threw a stick at one of the animals, breaking its leg. The witch turned out to be a girl from the neighbourhood.
159958: When Nele went to Stokkem, she was followed by meowing cats.
159961: A witch could turn herself into cats, dogs and all kinds of other animals.
159964: A mother who was pregnant with her eighth child was always visited by an old woman. Because the seventh child would then always start crying, the mother went to the brown friars in Sint-Truiden. After the mother had laid a relic under the threshold, the old woman came in through the back door. When the father had shut the back door, the witch could not leave the house until the door was opened again. As she left, the witch predicted that the child would die no matter what. And so it happened.
159965: Jang went to the market in Tongeren with some friends. When they reached the Heilige Haag, the men saw a golden coach with three white horses come out of the Noppenveldje. When the coach was almost upon the men, it flew up into the air.
159974: When Lonne V. went hare hunting at night, he saw hares as big as sheep. The man tried to shoot at the animals, but his gun did not work.
159989: A thirteen-year-old farmhand heard a hellish noise in the stable. The animals had pulled loose their chains and were leaping wildly about. After a priest had come to bless the stable, it was no longer haunted.
159993: In Maarheze there was an uninhabited house that was haunted. In the evening people heard music, as if a brass band were in the house. But when they went to look, there was nothing to be found. As soon as they were outside again, they heard the music again.
160004: When you went outside at night, you could hear the witches travelling through the air with loud music. People left a passage by the chimney so that the witches could dance there.
160005: Cilleke S. could make white mice with the help of a little book. One day the girl made mice in the church. After Cilleke had to hand her little book over to the dean of Peer, she could no longer make mice.
160017: An experienced hunter shot at a hare in the hills of Reppel. Although the hunter had hit the animal, he could not find the dead hare anywhere. A few days later the hunter met an old woman who was said to be a witch. The woman's face and legs were full of shot.
160022: A man was playing cards in a café. When the man bent down to pick up a fallen card, he saw that one of the other players had horse's legs. A little later the man saw a strange vapour. He ran away in fear.
160027: A mother who had already lost seven children was advised by her neighbour to shut all windows and doors tightly at the next birth, so that no one could hear or see that a child was being born. When the child was born, a man and a woman were creeping around the house. The man had come to steal and the woman was a witch who wanted to break the child's neck. "If you don't tell what I'm planning, I won't give away your motives either," said the witch. The man knocked and said: "You must let me in, for I come to bring good fortune. You must take care that the newborn child does not die. Soon a large spider will come in here. You must cut off its legs." When they had done so, a large pool of blood appeared on the floor. The witch had lost her leg and died some time later. In return for his help the man received a large reward, so that he never had to steal again.
160039: In a house in the Klokkestraat in Bilzen a big fire had been lit when suddenly a black dog came in. After a burning wood splinter had been thrown at the dog for the third time, the animal bit into the wood until the fire flew out. After two priests from Hasselt had prayed over the dog, they led the animal to den Eickert. A man who had gone with the priests had to throw the dog against the tree. When the man looked back, he saw a great flame and heard someone shout: "Pull up children, pull up dogs, pull the devil up out of hell!" As a reward the man was given a house in the Onze Lieve Vrouwstraat in Bilzen.
160041: In the village lived a woman suspected of being a witch. When the witch left the church on Sunday, someone placed his feet crossed in her footprints. After that people knew for sure that the woman was a witch.
160044: In a field in Piringen some men were mowing. One of the men announced that he was going behind a tree for a moment because he had to relieve himself. When the man still had not returned after an hour, the others went looking for him. A little further on they saw the man eating a foal in a meadow. When the man came back to the field, he mowed so fast that one of the others said: "If you've eaten a whole foal, it's no wonder you can mow so fast." The man was furious because they had seen him. He left and never came back.
160045: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to go and relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. When the couple were sitting in a café later that evening, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
160052: In Laak there lived a woman who bewitched the stables.
160057: A mother sent her son to the chaplain because her newborn daughter cried all the time. The chaplain promised he would come 'between light and dark'. After the chaplain had recited all the prayers in his book, the baby stopped crying.
160066: The dead miller of the Dalemolen in Lauw came back to haunt in the form of a dog. The dog would sit in the corner with a pipe in its mouth. Many had tried to chase the dog out of the mill, but without success. A friar who wanted to banish the dog was told: "You stole a white loaf when you were still going to school!" Another friar did manage to banish the dog to the pool.
160068: In Genk lived a carpenter who had an eighteen-year-old apprentice. Late in the evening the lad always saw a grey cat. Because the animal aroused his suspicion, he told his master about it: "Every time I want to go up to the attic, the cat is sitting on the ladder. It doesn't harm me, but I'm fed up with it and I intend to cut its head off with this knife." The carpenter warned him: "Don't do that, for it is a witch!" When the boy went upstairs again, the grey cat jumped onto the ladder again. Because the cat was blocking his way, the boy took his knife and lashed out at the animal. Because the cat moved its head just then, the knife cut off one of its ears. When the boy went to church the next Sunday, he saw his girlfriend walking in the street with a large white cloth wrapped around her head.
160072: A girl who lived alone in a cottage went out with her boyfriend every evening. Every evening the pair were followed by a hare as far as the Hoogbrug by the Bampsstraat. The hare sometimes sat on their feet and then grew heavier and heavier. The girl had to go to the friars twice.
160091: A man met a witch who offered him a green plum. Luckily the man had not accepted the plum, for otherwise he would surely have been bewitched.
160094: When the witch touched the animals in the stable, they fell ill or died.
160104: A young man who had gone to visit his girlfriend saw a light flying on the way back. It was the soul of an unbaptised child.
160122: It was said that black cats often sat on the churchyard wall.
160135: People who had a sick little daughter called the doctor in vain. Because the doctor was at a loss, the girl's parents went to the parish priest, who said: "The woman responsible for this misfortune lives across from you. Tomorrow at midnight you will hear her tap three times on the shutters." And so it happened. The next day the people went back to the priest to tell him what they had heard. The clergyman then said: "You must never let the witch in again." After a while the girl recovered. Because the girl's parents avoided their neighbour like the plague, the witch's daughters asked one day: "Why do you never invite my mother anymore?"
160150: A man was coming back from Louis V.S.'s café. On the way, to his great fright, he saw the devil leap out of the hedge. The man came home deathly pale. That night he dreamed about witches. The dream made him so restless that he tossed and turned in bed and broke his toes.
160170: In Villers a black man always wandered about in the evening.
160184: On the day a man from the village died, a magpie sat on the roof in the morning and would not leave.
160189: A man who had found a cat between Ulbeek and Hoepertingen wrapped the animal in his handkerchief. When the man unfolded the handkerchief in a café, there was a stone in it. After the man had folded the handkerchief up again, a cat came out.
160191: The Jackara castle in Wijer was haunted. At the start of the new year the children went to sing New Year songs for the baron of the castle. The children from Schakkebroek got whatever they wanted, while those from Wijer got nothing at all from the baron. Some boys dared each other to spend a night at the castle. They made a bet and a few of them went to the castle. Around midnight a leg bone suddenly fell out of the chimney. A little later another bone fell. In the end all the bones of a skeleton fell down the chimney. The next moment a coffin came into the castle. The boys had to lay the skeleton in the coffin. But they were so frightened that they fled at once.
160203: When children could not lie still in their beds, people said: "That one has the maar (nightmare, mare) on him." Perhaps the word 'maar' was derived from the French 'mort'.
160217: A peddler was always met by a cat at the wood in Eksel. When the man threw a hook at the cat, the animal leapt up at him.
160219: Strange things were always happening at the K. family's in 't Roeren. The animals often behaved strangely, and every evening flax waste was thrown into the well. In the end the parish priest was called, who said: "Just block up that hole in the stable." Once the hole had been blocked up, no more strange things happened.
160224: In the castle of Wideux hung a portrait of a lord. It seemed as if the lord in the painting was really looking at everyone.
160228: At the Oeterbrug a certain man always came along who had to carry the werewolf. One day, however, the werewolf made a mistake: it jumped on another man, who feared neither God nor devils and therefore fearlessly gave it a thrashing.
160240: In the old days, when you had bought a horse, you could keep the animal for a few days and return it to the seller if something was wrong with it. A man driving the dung cart to the field met a witch, who asked: "Have you bought a new horse?" When the man said yes, the witch went on: "Then watch out that the horse doesn't run off!" When the man had emptied his dung cart and wanted to leave again, the horse turned out to have vanished.
160245: In the G. family, a man suffered from a painful illness. "It doesn't matter," said his wife, "I will go to Scherpenheuvel and crawl three times around the church on my bare knees." But the man died before the woman had gone on pilgrimage. One evening the widow saw a small flame on the socks hanging to dry above the stove. The woman assumed the flame came from the stove and beat it out. When the same thing happened again a few days later, the woman ran to her room in fright. But her dead husband pulled the door open and said: "You do know what you promised, don't you?" The widow asked the priest for advice, who said: "If you promised that, then you must do it. When you leave on pilgrimage, you must put your husband's stick by the door and say: 'Go on ahead, I'll follow you.' If you don't, you will often have to carry the ghosts when they leap onto your back." When the woman arrived at the church in Scherpenheuvel, she saw her husband's stick already hanging there. She gave two francs to a poor woman, who was willing to crawl around the church for her. When the widow got home again, she saw that her husband's stick had disappeared: his soul was released.
160256: The B. family's house was haunted. When the women sat knitting in the evening, the yarn flew upwards and stayed hanging in the gutter. In the morning the cows in the stable had white socks on their legs.
160260: A young man coming back from church saw a ghost in a white sheet sitting among the bushes on the way. When the boy tried to hit the ghost with a stick, the white apparition suddenly vanished.
160261: A farmer had a farmhand who was a werewolf. The pastor advised the farmer to send the farmhand away and burn his collar in the meantime. The moment the collar was thrown into the fire, the farmhand instantly stood by the oven to save his band. When everything had burnt up, the farmhand said he was happy.
160275: In Vreren a little boy was playing in the sand. After he had blown over the little heaps of sand, lots of little mice appeared. When people had prayers read over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
160276: Pastor H. told that a witch from the area had as much butter as she wanted, even though she owned only one cow. The witch had a special stick that she had to put into a particular little hole in the door, depending on the house she wanted to steal butter from.
160296: A man who had beaten a cat to death found to his astonishment the next day that the animal had disappeared.
160299: The stable of farmer Corneel B. was under the influence of the evil hand through a black cat that wandered about there every day. When that black cat disappeared, the farmer had no more misfortune.
160300: A farmer had bought a cow, but he could not keep the animal's calves alive: one calf after another died. The farmer's son went to a sorcerer and told him what had happened. He also told the sorcerer that he planned to buy a new cow at the market. The sorcerer said: "When you bring the cow home from the market, make sure you don't meet a woman who says: 'Oh, what a lovely cow!' and touches the animal with her hand." When the son had gone to buy a new cow at the market, he did indeed meet a woman who said: "Oh, what a lovely cow!", but he made sure she could not touch the animal. The sorcerer had also given the son something to put in the stable to keep the witch out.
160303: Some people going somewhere in the evening were followed by a cat. A man struck the cat on its foreleg with a stick, after which the animal ran off. The next day a woman said to be a witch was walking around with her arm in a bandage.
160313: There were always cats on the Grese heath in the evening. When Pol T. came home one evening with his accordion, he struck at a cat that sat wailing on the road. The next moment the man was set upon by some hundred cats, which scratched his face to pieces.
160318: In Janneke T.'s café people danced naked to organ music. One evening the devil came into the café in the shape of a big black dog. The animal had eyes like balls of fire. Because no one managed to chase the dog away, a friar had to be fetched to read from the Bible until the dog left.
160328: A man from Heusden could work magic with the help of the devil. When the man had to manure the field, he manured a small part and then said: "All like this." In no time the whole field was manured.
160339: A young man who came to visit his girlfriend tapped on the window of her room. Then the window opened and a black cat jumped in his face. When the cat went back inside, the girl appeared.
160349: Witches were black women who could make a wheelbarrow or a cart stand still. One day someone beat a witch to death on the cart with a dung hook.
160353: Some people who had gone to watch a child's baptism met countless green toads on the way home, which blocked their path. The witch Rosse M. had also been present at the baptism.
160367: At night noises were often heard in the attic. Most people did not dare go and look.
160375: One Sunday afternoon a farmer went out to see whether he could acquire some more money or property somewhere. Behind a tree the farmer saw a man sitting eating his sandwiches, who asked what the farmer was looking for. "I've come to see if there's anything to be had. Whatever I can get, I'll gladly take!", said the farmer. The man replied: "Oh, then just keep going. When you're tired, draw a line. Everything from here to there will then be yours". In this way the farmer acquired so much land that at harvest time he had too few barns to store everything. The farmer went looking again for the man behind the tree and explained his problem. "Oh, that's no matter", said the man, "sign a contract and tomorrow you'll have your barn to store your grain in. You don't have to pay me. You only have to promise that I'll get your soul when you die". The farmer signed the contract in blood. Towards morning the farmer saw that the barn was almost finished, except for one window. The parish priest advised the farmer to take hold of a crucifix, because that would make the devil powerless. When the devil took hold of the crucifix, he screamed and went up in flames.
160383: In Dorplein lived a farmer who had many maids and farmhands. When the farmer was away, the maids often sat eating in secret. But the farmer always found out, because his brown rooster told him. One day the maids tried to drown the rooster. When the farmer pulled his rooster out of the well the next day, the animal was still alive. The farmer then locked the maids in the cellar, where they had to die. In the end the farmer was hanged.
160393: In Rijkel there was a haunted castle. At night the rattling of chains could be heard there.
160407: A man coming back from visiting his girlfriend on a Thursday evening in winter saw something lying on the ground beside the brook in the moonlight. When the man came closer, the apparition moved and crawled into the hedge.
160417: Some women went to dig potatoes at the Hellemolen in Hees. When the women rested a while in the evening, they saw a little light moving back and forth in the distance near the Nenof. Then the woman of the Hellemolen said: "That is a will-o'-the-wisp. My father saw one too once, when he was out with the wheelbarrow. He sat down on his wheelbarrow to rest a while. When he got up a little later, he could no longer lift the heavy wheelbarrow. As soon as he began to pray for the souls of the faithful, the wheelbarrow became as light as a feather."
160421: Whenever a certain woman from the village stood by the bridge, a farmer's horse began to sweat and could not get across the bridge.
160422: Because his farmhand refused to pray, miller Pie K. said to the boy: "I wish the werewolf would leap on you!" The next night the farmhand had to carry the werewolf. When the boy got home, he was sick with fear. Eight days later the farmhand was dead.
160438: A boy who went to visit his girlfriend in Gessel always came across cats or mice on the way back, blocking his path. The boy's girlfriend was a witch.
160447: In the meadow next to the church a black cat always sat on a barrier. When a passer-by struck the cat, it fell to the ground and then jumped back onto the barrier. The man then fetched a big stone and said to the cat: "Filth, clear off!" The next moment a tiger stood before him. Eight days later a black cat was sitting on the barrier again. When the man came by, he began to stroke the miaowing cat. The animal then jumped to the ground and let him pass.
160459: A will-o'-the-wisp always used to appear by the little chapel. It was the soul of an unbaptised child. Nobody dared to baptise the will-o'-the-wisp. When someone did dare to one day, the light disappeared.
160463: Gjotter, a beggar woman from Borgloon, gave people lice.
160482: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who came out of the marshes.
160492: Lies went from door to door peddling yarn. When Lies had visited, the children were often ill the next day. A man whose bewitched child had died had hung a medal of Saint Benedict above the door, so the witch could no longer get in. A wreath of feathers had been found in the child's pillow.
160495: A woman was frightened because strange things were happening in her house. The door always opened by itself, she heard strange noises in the attic, and under the stove the wallpaper was pulled off the wall. In the end, on her brother's advice, the woman decided to go to a card reader in Tongeren. The card reader asked the woman to take twenty-one cards. Then she established that the woman's house was haunted. The card reader asked the woman whether there had perhaps been a recent death in the family. Indeed, the woman's mother had died a short while ago. The mother had probably made a vow that she had been unable to keep. The woman went to Saint Anthony in Tongeren to pray an Our Father. Since then her house has not been haunted any more.
160500: In the old days witches often made rats or gave someone lice by rubbing their hand over that person's face. When the witch was then asked to take the lice away again, she stroked her hand in the opposite direction, and the lice disappeared at once.
160516: A boy found it strange that his girlfriend always went to do something at the chimney just before he went home. One day the boy hid to spy on his girlfriend. The girl rubbed herself with something and then said: "May the devil now carry me, over hedges and hawthorns". The boy imitated the girl, but he made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said: "May the devil now carry me, through hedges and hawthorns". The boy arrived at the witches' gathering badly injured.
160518: On the Hobos the drossaard (bailiff) came haunting with his coffin under his arm.
160522: A man walking home through the cornfield in the evening was startled by the barking of a little dog. The man cut himself a stick so he could defend himself against the animal if necessary. A moment later the dog barked again. The man jumped into the mud and struck at the animal. But he was terrified when he saw something moving in the mud beside him. Later the man realised that it must have been the sick wife of the farmer from a nearby farmstead.
160549: The priest had seen a girl making mice during catechism class. After the priest had read prayers over the girl, she could no longer make mice.
160560: A man was covered in lice after he had walked past a witch.
160564: A man coming home on New Year's night had to carry the werewolf. The werewolf had made the man lose his way, so that he did not get home until six o'clock. When the man finally reached his house, he asked the werewolf: "Have you enjoyed yourself now?", to which the beast replied: "I in my way and you in yours!"
160570: Some men were playing cards in Pie V.K.'s café when suddenly a black dog came in and lay down under the table. Only after the woman had prayed for a long time did the devil go outside again.
160587: There used to be little mounds beside the cycle path. When people came home late, a black cat always jumped from one mound to the other.
160609: The priest had seen that Jan P. from Kozen could conjure up mice. After the clergyman had read prayers over Jan, the boy could no longer make mice.
160618: An old woman haunted the churchyard of Lauw wearing a cloak and a white veil. When a man one day touched the ghost with a stick, the dead woman said: "If you dare to touch me again, you are dead".
160639: B.'s farmstead in Elch was haunted. At midnight all the doors flew open there.
160640: Some rascals were annoyed by a cat that kept getting under their feet. The boys stamped on the animal until it left them alone. The next day they saw a woman in the village with bruises and a lame leg. That must have been the witch.
160655: When Nol G. was walking home, he saw cats sitting all along the churchyard wall. Nol got scared and hurried home. The windowsill of Nol's house was also full of cats.
160656: A farmer from Lummen working in the stable was bothered by a toad that kept jumping under his feet. After a while the farmer got so fed up that he chopped off one of the toad's legs. The next day the farmer ran into his mother-in-law. The woman had only one leg left. "What happened to you?" asked the farmer, and his mother-in-law replied: "You should know, since you chopped off my leg yourself yesterday!"
160678: A man returning from Kermt heard cats meowing. People usually stayed away from that bewitched place.
160679: One Sunday a boy from Waltwilder went with his girlfriend from Gellik to the fair in Zutendaal. When the two were walking home around midnight, the boy said to the girl: "Wait a moment, I have to go and pee. If a dog comes at you, throw my handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. A little further on the girl was joined again by her boyfriend, who still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. As soon as the girl realised what was going on, she entered a convent.
160681: Betje K. was a witch, so people said. When a witch could not bewitch other children, she had to lay hands on her own family and even her own children. When she could not bewitch people, she broke the heart of a blade of grass. Betje K. had bewitched her own son: his feet were twisted on his legs. Nothing could ever be done about that deformity.
160700: All the farmhands hired by a miller in Maarheze died after sleeping one night in their bed. Yet when the miller himself slept a night in the bed, nothing happened. The next farmhand the miller hired was told, when he was taken on, about the strange events with the other farmhands. The new farmhand took a knife to bed. That night he woke at two o'clock to a strange rustling. He then saw a white mouse trying to bite his hand. The farmhand cut the mouse with the knife and remained unharmed himself. The next morning the miller's wife had a bandage around her hand. Then everyone knew who the witch was.
160704: All the farmhands hired by a miller in Maarheze died after sleeping one night in their bed. Yet when the miller himself slept a night in the bed, nothing happened. The next farmhand the miller hired was told, when he was taken on, about the strange events with the other farmhands. The new farmhand took a knife to bed. That night he woke at two o'clock to a strange rustling. He then saw a white mouse trying to bite his hand. The farmhand cut the mouse with the knife and remained unharmed himself. The next morning the miller's wife had a bandage around her hand. Then everyone knew who the witch was.
160721: In the old days, when people had misfortune with their animals or their health, they believed the evil hand was responsible. People then went to the friars or to the witch doctor.
160726: The vuurman (fire man) was a little light with a small cross on it that burned in the hedge. It was a soul from purgatory.
160734: A man walking home in the evening was followed by two miaowing cats. When the man was home, he heard a sow with a chain walking through the brook. The man took his gun and shot at the sow through the keyhole. The next moment the man's house was on fire. Fortunately he was able to put out the flames in time with holy water.
160737: In the area of Tongeren and Maaseik there used to live witches and werewolves. A woman from Maaseiker Solt who had moved to Gruitrode had to carry the werewolf. The woman managed to wound the werewolf, so that it became human again. It took three hours before some men had dragged the werewolf to the parish priest. When the bell rang at midnight, the priest opened his window and asked: "Is that you, Laurentius and Leo?", to which the men replied: "Yes, we've got him." The priest delivered the werewolf.
160773: In the past, little lights with a fat little head were often seen in the ditches. People said they were the souls of unbaptised children.
160776: A poacher had shot a hare. But when he wanted to pick up the hare, the animal ran away laughing.
160778: A merchant from Runkelen had two horses that stood stamping in the stable and could no longer pull the plough. The merchant had the stable overlezen (exorcised with prayers by a priest). After everyone living in the house had been to confession and communion, the horses behaved normally again.
160782: A mother from Rotem was combing her daughters' hair when a witch suddenly came in and said: "If I want, those children will be full of lice tomorrow." The next day the girls did indeed have lice. The witch predicted that the lice would be gone after a day, and so it was.
160792: Near the road between Luik and Brussel stood an old cottage that was haunted. At night a light would suddenly come on in that house.
160796: When a woman had died, everyone sat praying. Among the people was a witch who could not read or write, but who nevertheless had a prayer book with her. The witch held the book upside down, but kept pulling faces like a priest reading his breviary. When the dead woman's widower asked: "What are you doing?", the witch replied: "I'm praying." "That's not true," said the man, "now get out of here!"
160803: Along the road from Rotem to Dilsen a white lady was sometimes seen walking. People believed that the white lady had put money in the ground somewhere there.
160810: After his death Jef van T. came haunting because he had promised this to his friend, who was a drunkard. When his friend saw the ghost, he never touched a glass of alcohol again.
160815: Driek and Antoon were visiting the witch Mie. When a man on a moped rode past, Mie said: "He's not coming in yet, but he'll be back." A hundred metres further on, the man on the moped was knocked down. He was then brought to Mie's house.
160829: When Toen, the road mender's son, had called upon the devil, the devil appeared at the chimney.
160834: A black priest wandered around in the woods. He was a dead man who had to return because he had not fulfilled his duties.
160839: When Hoepet was walking home at night, he saw a black cat sitting on a turnstile. The man struck at the cat, saying: "What is that field louse doing here?" The animal answered: "Strike again, and you will never strike again!"
160845: A cowherd boy worked at a castle in Rummen. One day a farmer from Wallonia was to come to Rummen to fetch a wagon of hay. Because the weather was so fine, the cowherd lay in the grass with the other farmhands. When they suddenly heard the trampling of horses, they thought the man from Wallonia had arrived. But then they saw a strange coach with four horses drive into the pond. Only the next day did the farmer's brother arrive.
160846: A man who had been playing cards met a woman on his way home, who said: "You'll be walking around a long time before you get home!" The man did not get home until the next morning.
160868: A girl from the Gerdingerpoort went to school in Malta. On the way the girl met an old woman, who said: "Why, girl, your shoe is undone!" Immediately afterwards the girl got a swollen foot.
160873: In Stevoort a foal came haunting at night.
160890: A boy going to see his girlfriend one Sunday was followed the whole way by a black cat. After a while the boy got so fed up that he kicked the cat away. The next day the boy learned that his girlfriend's mother was wearing a bandage around her face.
160893: Because a farmer had much misfortune in his stable, he decided to go and look at the animals one night. In the stable he saw a witch sitting on one of the horses, calling: "Come on, my white one, now it's your turn!" The next moment the horse dropped dead. The witch was the farmer's wife herself.
160896: On a farm in Ophoven there was much misfortune. Within a short time all the animals died, and strange noises were heard there at night. The farm had been bewitched by a woman who lived nearby. After the witch died, everything went well on the farm again.
160907: When people walked along the dike by the Luiter Maeske in the evening, they thought they heard ducks quacking.
160920: A strange man came into an inn in Bergering and said: "If you fetch some empty glasses, I'll fill them." The man took out a black stick, spoke a magic formula and filled the six empty glasses on the table. It was the devil himself.
160923: A little boy had thrown the cellar of a witch full of stones. Afterwards the witch turned the boy's head back to front. When the boy's mother saw this, she ran furiously to the witch and shouted: "If you don't make my child normal again, I'll knock your head off!" The next moment the boy's head was straight again.
160944: In a house in Tervant all the doors flew open at midnight, after which pigs ran through the house. As soon as people went outside, there was nothing more to be seen.
160945: Whenever Harry's wife came downstairs in the morning, she found that the laces of her shoes had been tied together. The woman believed a witch had done it, for she was sure she had not tied the laces herself.
160958: In the Zakstraat there was a black cat that silently got under people's feet and followed them.
160964: A farmer could no longer make butter because the milk was bewitched. After the farmer had gone on a pilgrimage to the friars, he was no longer troubled by the evil hand.
160980: The evil hand was especially dangerous for children who had not yet been baptised. A bewitched child could only be saved by having prayers read over it. The friars usually advised not to let the witch in anymore. When children were older, witches had less power over them; the witch then often filled the child with lice.
160982: Nol from Uikhoven went to visit his girlfriend in Kotem in the evening. On the way back the man was leapt on by a werewolf on the Maas dike. Nol hit the beast with a stick.
160986: A man from Eigenbilzen had given an old woman alms. When the woman thankfully said: "God will reward you", the man replied: "Oh, go away with that God of yours!" After the man died, he had to come back to haunt. The ghost always had to open and close the wooden gate of the farm. Thirty years later a pregnant woman passed the gate. When the gate opened by itself, the woman said: "God will reward you!" The ghost then replied: "Because of that God I have had to stand here for thirty years!"
161005: Some boys were walking back from the fair in Rummen. As they walked along the lane, Sus B. became frightened and urged his friends to walk a bit faster. For he had seen a large black dog that had walked along with them as far as the turnstile. The others laughed at Sus and said: "You and your dog, Sus, you're mad. If there is a dog, let it come. We'll teach it a lesson!" No sooner had they said it than the dog stood there: a black beast, as big as a bear and with eyes like fire. The boys quickly took to their heels and hurried to Rikus B.'s barn, where they sat in fear until morning.
161007: An old woman came to look at the piglets on the Bornehoeve and said: "What lively piglets! In an hour they'll be even more active!" The piglets jumped almost up to the ceiling.
161013: A man walking home in the evening was followed in the woods by a meowing black cat. Fearfully the man looked into its fiery eyes and said: "Come along, sweet little creature." The man thought he was face to face with the devil. When the man reached Mettekoven, the cat said: "You're lucky you were so friendly to me, because otherwise you wouldn't have known what hit you!"
161016: When Piet S. had gone to visit his girlfriend, he quarrelled with the girl's parents, because Piet had fallen in love with another girl. As Piet left, the girl's mother said: "So is it over now with our Marjan?", to which Piet replied: "Yes, it's as good here as it is anywhere." On the way home Piet saw three women who raised a finger in the air and walked backwards. That night Piet got lost. He was convinced that the girl's mother was the cause of it.
161022: A man walking across the heath met a woman who was suspected of being a witch. The woman said to the man: "Go inside quickly, for a heavy thunderstorm is coming." Because there was not a cloud in the sky, the man did not believe her. A quarter of an hour later, however, it began to thunder and rain. The man could no longer find the way home.
161028: In the home of a miner from Opglabbeek almost all the children died. Above the Leuven stove little mouse tails could be seen. If you pulled one out, three or four appeared in its place. The parish priest did not have enough power to overlezen (exorcise with prayers) the house. The friars no longer wanted to travel such a long distance in the evening.
161033: Two werewolves jumped on the back of the same man. The man was so afraid that cold sweat dripped from his face.
161035: After her death a woman from Zutendaal came back to haunt her son. The woman had been married more than once and she had hanged herself.
161045: After a witch had rooted around in a molehill, white mice appeared.
161055: The witch Anneke caused her own children to die.
161061: A child that had been touched by the evil hand was full of lice and cried all the time. After prayers had been read over the child, it was cured.
161063: A woman from Nieuwerkerken no longer wanted to sleep with her husband because he behaved strangely and beat her. The man went to have himself overlezen (exorcised with prayers). His strange behaviour had been caused by a witch.
