161082: At K.'s 'pannesjop' near the tram stop in Rekem a white lady always appeared, of whom people were very afraid.
161089: A man who went to herd the cows in the meadow suddenly saw a fireball coming towards him. The next moment the gate was completely burnt. It must have been the spirit of an unbaptised child.
161093: A man from Diepenbeek went with his brother to work in the coal mine of Herstal to earn half a franc more per day. In a narrow passage of the mine some Walloon miners had seen a white lady.
161094: Witches and ghosts often gathered at the old mill between Vliermaal and Guigoven. At midnight exactly, black cats came, howling and mewing as they danced around an old oak. When they sensed that someone wanted to spy on them, they called out: "Over hedges and hedgerows" and then "Through hedges and hedgerows". The next moment the cats had vanished and the curious people could no longer find their way. They had to crawl through thick hedges, and after a long search they came home all scraped and bloody.
161115: A man who went hunting in the fields with his dog suddenly saw a hare appear. The man wanted to shoot the animal, but at that moment his gun would not work. So the man went home to attach a small cross to his gun. When the man saw the same hare again, he did manage to shoot it. The next day his wife lay in bed with a gunshot wound.
161121: When a man from Bijvoet (Eksel) came past Mie's house with his cart, the horse suddenly refused to pull. Then Mie came outside and asked: "Isn't it going?" The man explained what was wrong, upon which Mie said: "Go on then, I'll let him go." The next moment the horse could go on again without any effort.
161139: Witches always wore long black clothes. They threw rotten apples and dead rabbits, which made children get lice or fall ill.
161145: At 't Geneuth along the Maas stood a large farm where a farmhand worked who was suspected of being a werewolf. Because the people found it strange that their farmhand always went out around eleven or twelve o'clock, they decided to follow him once. So they saw the farmhand walk to a meadow and a little later reappear in the shape of a dog. The farmhand had a devil's band that he had hidden in the meadow. One day the people sent their farmhand to Maastricht so that they could burn the collar in the meantime. As soon as the collar lay in the fire, the farmhand stood by the oven. Because the farmhand was so ashamed, he afterwards left the farm.
161147: In the café by the church the devil sat playing cards in the shape of a man with cow's legs.
161148: At the Hak-plaats in Bocholt there was a farm that was bewitched. All the animals there died within a short time. The friars of Luik came to overlezen (exorcise with prayers) the farm.
161159: Some claimed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who were in purgatory. Others believed that will-o'-the-wisps wanted to point out a treasure.
161184: After Pekelemie had entered a house near the Borreberg, a broom was laid in front of the door. The witch could not get out until the broom had been removed.
161193: After Jan H. had kicked Alda J.'s cat, he was bitten by the animal. Because the wound would not heal, the man went to the doctor a week later. The doctor, however, found that it was already too late. Some time later Jan died of his injury.
161202: Laurentius M. came haunting after his death. The ghost threw a dog over the hedge and a little later it was in the stable. In the end the ghost was banished under a stone.
161227: Jef P. believed that witches could hear everything at sunset.
161241: The castle of Neerrepen and the old Biezen in Rijkhoven were haunted.
161248: A farmer was visited by a gypsy woman who came asking for milk. Because the woman was given no milk, she took an ear of corn, tapped the cow on the back with it and said: "There's your milk." From then on the cow did not give a single drop of milk.
161258: In Hoeselt some boys went catching sparrows. When they raised the lantern by the hedge, a voice rang out saying: "Don't burn my little fur! Don't burn my little fur!" The boys ran away in fright. A little further on, the curious boys regretted not having looked at what exactly was in the hedge. At that moment they heard the voice say: "I'm not that far yet!"
161275: On the evening of All Saints' Day two men went poaching in the fields of Bovelingen. Twelve hares had already passed by, but the men had not been able to shoot a single one because the animals vanished immediately. The thirteenth hare that came by asked: "Did the others pass long ago?" The men were so frightened that they resolved never to go poaching on All Saints' Day again.
161283: A man had married a rich widow from Lanklaar. When the man died, the woman found out that he had spent nearly all her money. Because the man came back to haunt after his death, the priest advised the widow to pray a lot and to have the masses said that she had promised. The woman refused to do anything at all for the dead man, since she had lost all her money through his fault. The widow could not get rid of the ghost. After a while the woman always heard knocking at a quarter to three at night. The frightened widow had her son come over from Luik for three nights, but then nothing happened. On the occasion of the mission the widow was visited by a friar who wanted to help her. The woman had to pray a penance and offer up a communion. After that her late husband never came back to haunt again.
161286: Some people from Termolen were returning from a visit to their family. On the Teut a dead calf dealer appeared who kept saying: "If I give one centime more, the devil may take me!"
161293: A man who had entered a witch's house was scared to death when the witch suddenly vanished. When the man went outside, the witch was standing in front of him again.
161301: A man whose cows were all dying sent his son to the parish priest of Leopoldsburg. The priest asked the boy what the cows were fed and said a little later: "It won't happen anymore now." Nobody knew exactly what the priest had done, but from then on all the animals stayed healthy.
161308: People said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
161320: A boy coming back from a visit to his girlfriend suddenly could not go any further when he walked past a witch's house.
161325: At Lauw mill the papers were thrown into disorder every morning. At night a large black dog had been seen there, holding back the mill wheel. The dog was the ghost of the former miller, who had stolen something from the people who came to live there after him. Because the man found no rest, he came to haunt every night. When a priest came to banish the ghost, the dog said: "Your conscience is not clean; during the harvest you stole ears of corn from someone else's field!" The priest answered: "Yes, but I paid for them!", and then gained power over the ghost. The miller had to drain the bed of the Jeker where the mill stood. At that spot the ghost was walled in. After that the water of the Jeker flowed over the place where the ghost was banished for ninety-nine years and for the years that followed. Opposite the mill a small chapel was built to commemorate the priest's help.
161334: A brewer whose farmhands had all died wanted to know the cause of all that misfortune. While the brewer was brewing, a little black cat suddenly came along. The brewer threw some brew in the animal's face, so that it left. The next morning the brewer's wife did not appear at breakfast. She was lying in bed because her face was completely burned.
161337: A man coming back from Schulen around twelve o'clock on a Sunday night met a white lady. When the man left the cycle path and walked on the road, the white lady also walked on the road. The man then drew his knife and braced himself. But the white lady simply walked past him. It was a white lady with a cloth over her head.
161340: A sick, thin boy was bewitched. When the mother sat up with her son at night, she saw a big cat jump onto the bed at twelve o'clock. The mother began to pray, made the sign of the cross and filled a little pot with holy water. The woman chased the cat out through the window. It was said that the cat afterwards changed into a human. In the end the boy recovered, but he was always weak.
161348: A boy whose father had bought cows was given a piece of soap by a witch. From then on the boy's parents could no longer make butter. "Has anyone perhaps been given something?" the father asked, and the boy answered: "Yes, a woman gave me a piece of soap." The father replied: "Throw that away quickly, for if you accept something from a witch, she has power over you." Because the boy had to milk the cows, the witch also had power over the cows. When the boy had thrown the soap away, his parents could make butter again.
161352: A woman had been in Sus V.'s stable, who had talked about the weather the whole time and then suddenly left. The next day Sus's cows stood with their tails tied together.
161360: A man who was ploughing his field was visited by a witch, who made him a proposal. Because the pious man would not accept the proposal, the witch struck him on the shoulder. The man was in so much pain that he could no longer hold his shoulder straight. Because the man was still suffering severe pain at night, his wife went to fetch the priest. When she came back, her husband was dead.
161364: Parents whose child was ill sent for a clergyman. He established that the child was bewitched and advised the parents not to let the witch in anymore. The child had been given a medal and was eventually cured.
161372: In the evening many people were jumped on by the werewolf at the entrance to a meadow or pasture. A brave man who wanted to teach the werewolf a lesson set out with his little knife. As soon as the werewolf jumped on him, he stuck his knife into the hairy coat, making the beast bleed. Then the werewolf changed into someone the man knew well. "I will never do anything to you again if you let me go now," said the released werewolf.
161388: A man and a friend were taking a statue of Saint Anthony to the church of Eigenbilzen. At midnight the two men saw a person sitting in a glowing armchair in the field of Rosmeer. Someone had unjustly appropriated the field where the ghost sat.
161414: Near Sint-Huibrechts-Hern lived two girls who were seriously ill because they had been touched by the evil hand. One girl died when she was one year old. The other was cured after she had been prayed over.
161421: In Rotem lived a girl who had a disability. People held a woman from the village responsible for the girl's disability. For that woman could make mice out of a molehill.
161439: During the war, people went to have their grain ground at a mill in Opgrimbie. A boy carrying a twenty-kilo sack of grain met a woman who wanted to help him. Suddenly, however, the sack became so heavy that the boy shouted: "Ugly witch, get away from here!" After that the boy could carry the sack without any effort.
161441: A man walking home at night met a werewolf and struck the animal with a stone. The next moment the werewolf changed into the man's brother.
161447: During the French Revolution many farms on castle estates were sold by the fathers for fear that the French would otherwise seize them. After the Revolution, however, many refused to return the properties to the fathers. The people who stayed living on those farms had constant bad luck. A large number of those farms were located in Neeroeteren.
161448: An old woman stroked a little child's hair, saying: "What lovely curls you have!" Two days later the child was dead. That woman must have been a witch.
161456: A boy and a girl went to the parish priest because they wanted to marry. On the way the boy said to his girlfriend: "Wait a moment, I have to relieve myself behind the ditch. If you see a beast, throw my handkerchief at its teeth." The girl did as she had been advised. When the boy came back a little later, the girl noticed that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
161490: On New Year's Day the dead owner of the castle always drove around in a phantom coach with four horses.
161504: A family had a child that cried all the time because it was bewitched. The friars advised the family to put a broom handle in front of the door. After that the witch could no longer get in.
161507: A man who was ridden by the maar (nightmare, mare) went 'weteren' (?) at night. The next morning the man remembered nothing of what had happened.
161518: The witch Maria P. gave everyone lice.
161522: A seamstress was picked up by her boyfriend in the evening after work. On the way the boy said to the girl: "I'm going into the meadow for a moment. If a hare comes leaping about, throw your handkerchief at its mouth." When the girl saw a hare a little later, she did as her boyfriend had advised. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the handkerchief in his mouth. The girl was so frightened that she died three days later.
161525: A man who went poaching was startled when a cat came up to him. When the man tried to chase the cat away, dozens of cats suddenly appeared. The man was so frightened that he ran away at once.
161527: At night, will-o'-the-wisps in all kinds of colours could be seen in the churchyard.
161538: At night a ghost sat on the hedge by the G. family's house in Mal.
161561: A woman whose little child was bewitched went on a pilgrimage to Wijk in honour of Saint Vincent. There one received holy water and could buy a rosary in honour of the Holy Sepulchre. The child suffered from the 'fivelein', which made it restless all the time. The girl, however, was never fully cured and died at the age of sixteen. Pastor Zjengske, who lived on 't Hocht, never wanted to believe that the child was bewitched. The parents, however, strongly suspected who was responsible for their daughter's death.
161562: In Millen there used to be a blue and a red statue of Our Lord. If you sat down at the blue statue at midnight with a black hen, you could meet the devil there and sell your soul. Later the priest had both statues painted green.
161567: Farmer L. lived in Bocholt next to a ditch where some thick tree stumps stood. The farmer had just taken on a new farmhand, who went somewhere every evening. When the farmer had spied on the farmhand one evening, he discovered a collar. The farmer sent for Pastor N. to burn the collar. When the band lay in the fire, the farmhand immediately stood beside them and had to be held back by force from jumping into the oven. When everything had burnt up, the farmhand thanked the farmer and the pastor on his bare knees. The farmhand went away and was never seen again.
161575: A thief who had broken into the church could not get away; he was stuck in the window. The next morning the churchgoers freed the thief.
161576: The gnomes, also called alvermannetjes (elf men), left for another region because they could not stand people coming to spy on them at night.
161598: A man who had moved a boundary post had to haunt after his death. The ghost kept calling: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I leave it?" Because the ghost made so much noise, people decided to send for a priest. After the priest answered the ghost's question with the words: "Leave it where you fetched it from", the ghost never came back.
161622: A man from Zwartberg went with a friend to visit his girlfriend. The parish priest had advised him against it, because he had to pass a dangerous place. On the way the friend had got lost by looking at a girl. The man stumbled into a brook and could no longer find his bearings.
161624: A young beguine wanted to leave the beguinage to run away with her lover. When the beguine crawled through the hole in the churchyard wall, the dead beguines rose from their graves to stop her.
161625: A man walking home at night was followed the whole way by a strange apparition.
161645: A girl who was afraid to go home alone in the evening was given this advice by her boyfriend: "If you see something strange, make the sign of the cross and say: 'If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, depart.'" When the girl saw something strange appear in the moonlight, she made the sign of the cross and said: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, depart." The next moment the strange apparition had vanished.
161660: It was said that a witch lived in an alley in Herk-de-Stad. All the windows and doors of the house stayed shut in the evening. When the witch had sprinkled a house with water, the house was bewitched.
161663:
An old count lived in the castle in Mechelen. After the count died, he came back as a ghost every night at twelve o'clock. He would then drive around the castle grounds in a coach. One day a priest was sent for to banish the count's ghost. While the priest was on his way to Mechelen, a ghost threw him to the ground several times and pushed him into the brook. On arriving at the castle, the priest put on his habit. Through this consecrated garment the priest gained power over the ghost. The cleric then banished the count to the cave in the woods between Bovelingen and Rukkelingen. He was fastened with a thick chain.
Many years later the priest still often said to the children in catechism class: "That Bovelingen, that Bovelingen, it will be the death of me yet."
161690: A man who had to fetch the midwife on his own never got there. Anyone who did not want to get lost had to put on his wife's wedding ring, because it was a consecrated object.
161691: A farmhand coming home in the evening was followed by two cats. Twenty metres from his house the cats stopped.
161696: Every time his neighbour's wife came by, the farmer could not make butter. When he decided to make butter on a different day, it worked.
161698: On a field path in Berbroek a ghost appeared that asked: "Where shall I put my boundary post?" When a drunkard answered: "Put it where you fetched it from", the ghost appeared no more.
161701: When the moon was not shining, a voice could always be heard by the Maas calling: "Ferry me over! Ferry me over!"
161736: In Meeswijk a boy went to the fair with his girlfriend. On the way the boy announced that he had to relieve himself. "If you should meet a dog, just throw this handkerchief," the boy said to the girl. When the boy was drinking a glass of beer at the fair, the girl noticed that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
161761: In a family on the Molenveld, a little child had got 'the old man' through the doing of a witch. Because of this illness the child's skin was completely wrinkled, so that the child looked like an old man. A few days later the child died.
161762: When a wizard was playing cards, he could have the jack of spades fetch a bottle of gin. The bottle then had to be emptied, or else something would go wrong.
161770: Someone said to a father whose child was ill: "That woman from Diepenbeek must have bewitched your child. We'll have to send for the priest." After the priest had prayed over the child, it recovered.
161775: One day Mitchie was going to the field with his horse and cart when on the way he met Marzjenneke, who said: "Where are you going?" Mitchie replied: "I'm going to the field." At that the witch said: "That won't end well!" Before the farmer was even out of the village, his horse came loose from its harness for no reason at all.
161791: At a farm where a man had died, a voice could always be heard calling: "Money tree, money tree!" That is why some believed money was still hidden somewhere there.
161794: The vuurman (fire-man) came at people and set red clothes on fire.
161803: A man from Godsheide (Hasselt) had vowed to go on pilgrimage to Rome. However, the man died before he had been able to keep his vow. After his death the man haunted his house in the shape of a bent man carrying a heavy bundle on his shoulders and a stick in his hand. When someone had the courage to ask the ghost, "What do you want?", the apparition answered, "You must go on pilgrimage to Rome for me, or else I cannot get into heaven." Then the ghost disappeared.
161811:
In the old days a tall black gentleman walked every night by the ruins of the castle of Emmeren. One evening Ber, the former town crier, met the black gentleman near a turnstile cross. Because Ber was afraid, he let the gentleman go first. The gentleman, however, insisted that the man go first. When Ber went on, the black gentleman stayed behind him the whole time.
Everyone was afraid of the black gentleman, but he never harmed anyone. People suspected the gentleman had a secret. But nobody dared to ask him; otherwise he would have been released.
161814: A young family from Herk-de-Stad had a little child that cried all the time because it had been touched by the evil hand. After the friars of Sint-Truiden had given them a relic to put under the door, the witch could no longer get in. After that the child was cured.
161817: In Kessenich lived a five-year-old girl who was blind. It was said that the child had gone blind when she was washed by a witch as a baby. After the priest had rubbed the girl's eyes with something blessed, the child could see again.
161826: A witch met a woman with two small children and said: "That child I'll make a whore, and the other a bedwetter." Her prediction came true.
161829: A mother and a daughter began to pray in a small room and said: "Over hedges and hawthorns". Some people who had eavesdropped on the witches said: "Through hedges and hawthorns" and arrived at their destination badly injured.
161830: In Meeuwen lived a woman who could turn herself into a black cat. One day her husband shot at a cat with his gun. It turned out to be his own wife, but she was not dead.
161835: The white lady walked in a white nightgown through the fields and the streets of Berbroek.
161849: In Heer there lived a boy who was in love with a girl. But because the love was not mutual, the girl went out alone in the evening. When the girl met a big dog on the way, she threw her handkerchief at the animal's mouth. The next day the girl saw that her admirer still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
161859: A witch had caused all the grain to rot.
161868: A twenty-year-old orphan boy moved in with an old woman, for whom he wanted to work in exchange for room and board. Because the woman had no more space, the boy had to sleep in her room. Three nights in a row the boy lay sweating in his bed. He felt oppressed and could not wake up. After that the boy left.
161910: A miner whose only son had died always heard someone calling from the cellar: "Mother! Father!" One day the miner asked: "Is that you, boy?", and the boy answered: "Yes, it is me". From that day on the miner went every evening after work to have a chat with his son. When the mother one day told the parish priest what her husband was doing, the priest said: "But it is the devil your husband talks to every evening! Here is a medal of Saint Benedict. You must sew this medal to the inside of the waistcoat your husband wears when he goes to talk in the cellar". The woman did as the priest advised. The next evening the man stayed in the cellar only a short time. When he came back up, he said to his wife: "Our son is not there today". After a while the woman confessed everything about the medal in the waistcoat. The man did not believe he had anything to do with the devil, and from then on again went to the cellar every evening.
161920: In Zichen-Zussen-Bolder a fourteen-year-old boy nearly died because of a cat. Fortunately, people intervened just in time.
161942: A man who had gone to play cards in Kortijs walked home with a sickle in his hand. On the way the man killed a werewolf. The next day the dead body of a distinguished man from the village was found by the roadside.
161943: In a house where a child had died, a witch came by at four o'clock in the morning to ask for an empty sack.
161954: A mother lying in childbed was visited by a woman with a long nose, who began to sing: "Oh, what a rascal! Oh, what a rascal!" The next moment the newborn child also had a long nose.
161971: In Villers-L'Evêque a farmer had walked in the meadow together with a black gentleman. When the farmer met the black gentleman again after a few years, he ran away. Some time later the farmer's body was found: he had been hanged in the meadow. The farmer had sold his soul to the devil. Because his time was up, the farmer had to die.
161997: When Betteke B. was walking home, she was leapt on by a werewolf.
161998: Lewie G. always saw a ghost when he was on his way to work. A man advised Lewie to stuff his shirt full of big stones and so knock the ghost over by running into it. After he had done so, Lewie never saw the ghost again.
161999: A farmer shot a hare that was nibbling the vegetables in his garden. The next morning the man saw that one of the maids had a wound on her arm with the shot still in it.
162015: A young man from Deurne decided one Sunday evening to go to a play in Schaffen, because his parents were away. When the man was almost home, he met a woman with a cloth on her head and a stick in her hand. "Say, make sure you don't get lost!" the woman said. Thirty metres further on, the young man could no longer find his bearings. Through the woods the man came to a white house where beautiful music could be heard. The man opened the door and immediately recognised everyone present. "But, am I here now?" said the young man, at which the people laughed: "You know us well enough!"
162030: Along the canal in Smeermaas there was a werewolf that jumped on people's necks and made them carry it. The place was called "de Eik" (the Oak) because many oak trees used to grow there. It was said that the werewolf was an ugly old man with a beard, dressed in rags.
162063: At Mr G.'s in a castle in Tessenderlo an old soldier had died. After his death the soldier came haunting and rang Mr G.'s doorbell. The man eventually had to move. A man from Brussels who came to live in the castle afterwards also moved. The next occupant, who was called 'de Zwiep', did not want to stay living in the castle either.
162071: In Maaseik lived a werewolf who disguised himself with a cloth or a cow's head and had himself carried in the evening in remote streets or fields.
162074: In a family living on the Linne, several children had already died because a witch often came to visit. When the witch was no longer let in, not a single child died anymore.
162087: In Leut there was a haunted house. In the house stood a chest of flour. At night the flour flew out of the chest by itself, although there was no wind.
162096: Anyone who suffered misfortune caused by witches was best off going to the friars of Achel. On the way, however, one could be held back by all sorts of things. Many people got lost or arrived at the friars dead tired.
162105: A man who was in a relationship with a witch wanted to go along to a witches' gathering once. As soon as everyone was asleep, the witch said: "First we rub ourselves with witches' grease, and then you must sit on my feet. But on no account may you speak the name of God!" During the flight the man fell asleep. When he woke up, he saw that he was sitting in a pub where people were dancing and drinking. "In God's name, where am I?" said the man. The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the man was sitting against a beech hedge. The priest gave the man this advice: "Go back next night to the place where the pub was." The man did so and was brought back by his girlfriend.
162108: When someone said: "I've been dreaming" or "I've had the maar (nightmare, mare)", people often replied: "You didn't put your chair in its place." Some people claimed the maar was a stopping of the blood and that one could suffocate from it. Others claimed the maar was caused by going to sleep on a full stomach.
162114: At the Slagmolen worked a farmhand who was courting a girl from Donderslag near Meeuwen. When one day the farmhand went to see his sweetheart unannounced, he asked: "Isn't Marie here?", to which they replied: "Yes, she's in the bakehouse sifting buckwheat flour." When the farmhand entered the bakehouse, he saw that the sieve was standing still. Marie stood beside it with her mouth open and a vacant look in her eyes. When a little later a ray of light shone in through the keyhole, the girl carried on sifting as if nothing had happened. The girl was a witch, for sometimes her soul escaped from her body.
162117: A man shot with his gun at a hare sitting next to an old pear tree. The man missed. The animal nodded its head briefly and then ran off.
162119: In Hinnisdaal a passer-by saw someone sitting by the road. When he came back, he saw two men sitting in the same spot and said: "Hey, a while ago you were alone, and now there are two of you!" The man sitting by the road then looked beside him and saw the devil sitting there, dressed all in black. The man got up and walked home. When he got home he dropped dead of fright.
162129: If a child fell ill after a woman had come to visit, that woman was often suspected of having bewitched the children.
162130: When something strange was found in a little child's bed, people believed the child had been touched by the evil hand. The child was then prayed over.
162131: A woman who had always had a bad reputation had died. As was the custom, the neighbours went to keep watch over the body. The neighbours saw a large black dog and heard cats wailing. Suddenly there was a noise as if a bowl of water had been knocked over in the kitchen. But when they went to look, there was nothing to be seen. The next day nobody wanted to keep watch over the body any longer. The dead woman must have been a witch.
162135: A man was working at the church when suddenly a witch came by, who said: "You'll have a hard time getting home today!" At half past one at night the man ended up back at the church of Wijer with his cart.
162148: Farmer Karel Z. woke up at night because he heard noise in the stables. When the farmer went to look, he saw that all the animals had broken loose. The next morning four animals lay dead in the stable. Some time later two more died. The evil hand had caused all that misery.
162158: M. had got lost near the Demer because of a witch.
162162: A man whose wife had died had taken on a maid. When the maid went upstairs one day, she found that the children's beds were full of fleas. Nearby lived a woman suspected of witchcraft. When the man heard from the maid what was going on, he cried angrily: "I'll burn that filthy witch here," and he set fire to a bundle of straw. In this way the man drove all the fleas out through the window. At that moment the witch was standing below at the window watching, and said: "What are you doing now?"
162169: No one was allowed to say good day to the witch, or else the cows in the stable would die.
162171: A boy who went to fetch leek plants from his grandmother was followed by a black cat. The boy made a detour to pass the crossroads by the inn. At the crossroads the cat hesitated for a moment and then turned around. This made the boy certain that the cat was a witch.
162173: When the S. brothers of Munnikenhof in Heks were going to Widooie, a great arch of light suddenly appeared at the spot where they were standing. When they went on, the arch moved as well. When the brothers reached the first houses of Bedeu, a horse came up with a rider wearing pearls and beautifully coloured clothes. The rider rode under the arch. As soon as he had passed the arch, he vanished, together with the horse and the light that had followed the S. brothers the whole way.
162224: A man who went for a walk in the woods with his children came to a small cottage where an old woman lived. The woman was very friendly and offered the group some tasty porridge. When the man and the children left again, they got lost. The witch had seen to that.
162229: At midnight a watchman heard the silk dress of a white lady rustle. Sometimes the white lady could be seen walking in the lane of Ommeland.
162243: A man out walking with a friend made his friend lose his way. Then he said to his friend: "I will make sure you get home again, on condition that you accept these three books of magic." The man had no choice but to accept the books. However, he could not burn them.
162264: A farmer and his son agreed to start mowing the hay at four in the morning. During the night the son suddenly woke because light was shining in his eyes. Convinced that his father had not come to call him in time, the son got up and went to the field. When he arrived there, he heard the church bells strike twelve. The son had not been woken by the first rays of the sun, but by the moonlight. The boy decided to start mowing the hay on his own. A little later the boy saw a cat sitting in the field. Then there were suddenly two cats, and five minutes later the boy was completely surrounded by cats. For an hour the cats stayed in a circle in the field. At the stroke of one the cats left again.
162270: A man going to Hamont one evening saw a cat sitting on a post along the way and said: "In the name of the Father, say who you are". Because the cat did not answer, the man went on: "In the name of the Son, say who you are". Then the man said: "In the name of the Spirit, say who you are". At that the man angrily struck the animal to the ground with a cudgel. When the man had nearly reached Hamont, he met a woman whose head was completely wrapped in a bandage. That was how he finally knew who the witch was.
162284:
A church once sank in the Maten. One day a young lady found a white thread by the Stiemer. When the girl began pulling the thread, a church tower suddenly rose above the water. The young lady was so frightened that she let go of the thread, and the tower sank back into the swamp.
On Christmas night people in the area heard the bells of the sunken church ringing.
162287: The witches often held a gathering at the edge of the wood. When one day Pie-Ber passed by the witches, one of them said: "Wilveren, wilveren", to which another said: "Neeveren, neeveren, it's Pie-Ber the carpenter, let him pass!" Once a man with a hunchback also came to the same place. Then the witches said: "Wilveren, wilveren, javeren, javeren", and they danced with the man, took away his hump and stuck it onto a thick tree standing there. When the man ran into a friend the next day, the friend asked him how he had lost his hump. That friend also had a hump himself and went that same evening to the place the man had named. The witches said: "Wilveren, wilveren, javeren, javeren", and the man was already delighted. But then the witches took the other hump off the tree and stuck it on the man's back, so that he now had two humps.
162292: A man claimed that he often had to carry the werewolf.
162295: A soldier from Rekem saw a cat sitting on a post and knocked the animal to the ground with a stick. The next moment, however, the cat was already back on the post. After the soldier had knocked the cat off the post three times, the animal said: "Strike again now!" At that the soldier quickly took to his heels.
162296: At night knocking was always heard on the gate of a haunted castle. A curious man who went to look died of fright. After that people no longer heard the knocking.
162312: A drunk man who was touched on the neck by a witch was left with a swelling.
162318: A mother carrying her child in her arms met a woman who said: "Oh, what a lovely child that is!" The woman shook the child's hand. The next day the child cried constantly. In the pillow a rose made of yarn was found. Fortunately the rose was not yet finished, or else the child would have died. After the child had been prayed over by the friars, it recovered.
162332: William did not dare go home in the evening because he was afraid of his father, who wanted him to earn money. So the boy decided to spend the night under the pines 'op de Dreef'. When a white lady suddenly appeared, William died of fright.
162348: When D.'s farmstead still stood empty, it was haunted. Around midnight poachers always heard chains rattling in the attic there. Because nobody wanted to live in that house, the D. family was able to buy it for a pittance.
162357: A man from Meers who had gone to visit his girlfriend in Belgium walked home past the cemetery on Sunday evenings. One evening the man saw a white lady walking in the cemetery. From then on the man no longer dared go to the cemetery at night.
162384: The witch of Rutten had bewitched a boy. Because of this the boy could neither live nor die.
162396: In the attic of Koob's farm stood a heavy octagonal chest locked with three chains and three locks. In that chest the ghost of a dead man who had returned had been banished; he had killed all the animals in the stable.
162405: Children who had not been baptised fell into the devil's power and became werewolves or witches. Many witches lived in Meeuwen. Witches could turn themselves into cats and other animals. Clergymen did not always have power over witches and werewolves.
162413: When Ferdinand B. was coming back from Maasmechelen, he saw in Opgrimbie a big man with thick stumpy legs lying on the road. He was so frightened that he made a long detour and prayed the whole way.
162440: A maid who came from the Rest worked for a farmer in Hechtel. Because that maid had bewitched the stable, not a single calf could be kept alive there.
162450: Next to the Tomp stood a haunted castle. A man let two friends dare him to go into the castle. As a reward he would get a bottle of jenever. When the three reached the castle, the ghost cried: "Boo!" At that the men ran home scared to death.
162463: A man passing a house in Sint-Gangelhof ran away when he saw a cow with blood-red eyes. When the man came back later that day with a few others, a woman lay half dead on the ground at that spot. The woman's husband was a drunkard who had fallen into the devil's power through his sin. In the shape of a cow the man came to visit his wife every night. After people had prayed for the man, he was cured.
162468: Long ago at 't Geneuth worked a farmhand who had a collar or an animal skin with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmer had found out that his farmhand consorted with the devil. The next day the farmhand was sent away so that the farmer could burn the skin in the oven in the meantime. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand stood by the oven to save his possession. When the skin had burnt up completely, the farmhand left and never came back.
162489: Some children who wanted to secretly pick pears threw a stone at a cat sitting by the pear tree. When the cat had disappeared, a woman with a bandage around her head was suddenly standing on the other side of the tree.
162491: At de Hemel by the Mothoeve some oak trees were cut down. Among the roots of one of the trees a chest was found, which sank ever deeper into the ground whenever people tried to pull it up. Then a young man said: "Carry on, but do not say a word while you pull the chest up." The chest turned out to contain old money. People said that a white lady came to count that money at night.
162493: Criminals used to be hanged on the Galgeberg. The last person hanged there was Boon-Pee. While his corpse was still hanging on the gallows, a farmer had to work in a nearby field. When the man sat eating at midday, he said jokingly to the corpse: "Well, Boon-Pee, you used to love eating beans! Why don't you join me now?" At that the corpse began to speak: "I invite you too. Come tonight at twelve o'clock, and you may join me." The farmer immediately made off and in a panic told his story to a clergyman. The priest said to him: "You are now obliged to go to him tonight. Take a small child with you, then the ghost will not be able to harm you." At midnight the man went to the Galgeberg with a child in his arms. When the farmer reached the gallows, he heard a sound as if meat was being fried, but he saw nothing. The child had saved him.
162506: A man out hunting with his dog saw a fine cat sitting there. The dog went towards the cat, but came back a little later with its tail between its legs. The man tried to shoot at the cat, but he missed. A few days later the man came across a spotted cat by a pollard willow. Again the dog ran back to its master in fear. When the man had shot at the cat, he heard a voice saying: "Peteromen, you won't do that again!" The next day the witch was paid back (recognised?).
162514: The castle of Dessener was haunted. When the cows had been tied up, a little later the animals stood back to front in the stable, without anyone having been nearby.
162519: Voddemarie came into a house, where she patted someone on the shoulder and said: "You're the best-behaved of them all!" The next day, however, the man had a swelling on his back. Moreover, his muscles were so stiff that the man fell down the stairs.
162540: In Sint-Pieter lived a woman whose child was very ill through the evil hand. In the child's pillow a bird made of feathers was found. Fortunately the bird was not yet finished. After the child had been blessed and the bird burned, the child recovered.
162546: Mop walked to the village in the evening to have one of his clogs repaired. When it got dark, the man suddenly saw a white lady appear. Mop then shouted: "Help, help, I've seen a white lady!", and ran for his life.
162553: The K. family's remote farmstead was haunted at night. Chains could then be heard rattling in the corridor. There used to be a castle there as well.
162599: After his death a man came haunting on a horse. Sometimes the ghost appeared to the cattle dealers in the stable. Only the dead man's wife could see the ghost. In the end the ghost had to be banished.
162605: Witches had power over people especially at night. They would burn candles and stick pins into a pillow.
162606: A girl was bewitched by the witch Voddemarie, who peddled old fabrics around the villages. When the girl was twelve years old, she still could not walk. One day a friar walked through the field and said: "Here I must come to do a great work." The friar prayed over the girl.
162610: A man worked at the Stichel farm in Sledderlo. One evening farmer B. said to his farmhand: "Zjang, tonight you must go to Hengelhoef to fetch pine seed." To be safe the farmhand took a knife, because he would pass stonecutter Gregoor's. Everyone knew it was haunted there. When Zjang came to that spot, he was jumped on by a werewolf. The farmhand managed to wound the beast, so that it changed into a human. Zjang had to promise the werewolf that he would never betray him.
162660: Two forest rangers walking from Achel to Hamont took shelter from a thunderstorm in the Tomp (1). On entering the castle the men heard a woman calling. The castle was haunted. Some claimed that a mentally disturbed woman had taken up residence there.
162663: Old L. did not believe in witches, until six cows suddenly died in his stable within a single month.
162665: Near the tile works in Schulen, many people got stuck with their carts. One day the witch came outside and said: "I'll just touch the wheel with my hand." As soon as the witch had touched the wheel, the cart could drive on again.
162668: The castle of Kwamol (?) was haunted. Chains could always be heard rattling there. It was said that the ghosts were people who had been imprisoned in the dungeons.
162679: A child from Berg grew sicker and sicker every day. The priest came by and had the child's pillow cut open. When a toad with a red ribbon was found in the pillow, the priest said: "The witch who did this will come by your house this very day." Later that day the child's father forced the witch to undo the evil.
162688: Witches and werewolves got their power from the devil. A werewolf could not help having to make people carry him.
162704: One evening a man had laid a meerschaum pipe on the mantelpiece. The next morning he found that the pipe had broken in two. That house was haunted.
162714: A man from Eksel who was coming back one evening from visiting his girlfriend in Zolder lost his way. When he saw a little light, he ended up in a pub where there was singing and dancing in full swing. A girl gave the man a glass and he said: "In God's name, where am I?" The next moment the whole scene had vanished. The man was sitting on a birch stump with a cow's horn in his hands.
162716: Because Neel V.D.S.'s two sick cows would not get better, the man went to the friars. On the way, however, the man got lost, so that after wandering about for a long time he was back home. The next day the man set off for the friars a second time. But it was already too late, for the two cows died.
162719: A man walking home on a Sunday evening saw a large sheep walking on the Pierpont. That sheep could not be hit in any way.
162721: A maid who was suspected of being a witch was sifting buckwheat flour. When someone went to call her around mealtime, they found only her body, from which all life seemed to have gone.
162739: In Lauw a strange man joined a card game. The man let his opponents win time after time. When one of the players bent down to pick up a card, he saw to his great dismay that the strange man had cow's legs. The man said nothing about it, but quickly made himself scarce. When the card game was over, the other players had lost all their money. They had played cards with the devil.
162743: A man who had gone to fetch milk passed a house on the way back where a woman was standing outside. When the man got home, the milk was sour.
162759: An unmarried woman with a limp came out of church with a girl who was soon to be married. On her wedding day the girl had to wait more than an hour for her bridegroom. The man had had car trouble or something like that. Many people blamed the witch.
162766: A man who had gone to visit his brother in the evening got lost on the way home. The man must have been bewitched.
162771: Farmer V. from Stamprooi was woken at night by a hellish noise coming from the stable. The animals were pulling at their chains as if they had gone mad. After the farmer's grandfather had sprinkled the animals with holy water, they calmed down again.
162774: A man coming back from the fair whistled a tune to break the frightening silence. Suddenly the man bumped into something and fell to the ground. The man felt hair everywhere and heard a horse neighing. The man ran back to the fair as fast as he could.
162775: Teke K. had bewitched the cows in the stable, so that the animals became very thin and were always untied at night.
162777: A man kicked at a cat that had been getting under his feet for quite a while. At that, the cat immediately became as big as a calf.
162779: Some men were driving a horse and cart along a dirt road that led to Helshoven. A woman from Voort stood watching by the side of the road. At a certain moment the horses, strangely enough, came to a standstill. That woman had held the horses back.
162791: Machiel A. worked at the Vrankenhof in 't Rooren in Opitter. When the man came home one evening, he saw a will-o'-the-wisp flying above a pool in a meadow. At De Kuil the man lay down on the ground. Otherwise the will-o'-the-wisp would lead him to the water, where he would drown. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who led people to the water because they wanted to be baptised.
162803: A woman who was walking through the Diepe Straat in Vlijtingen to Maastricht met a friar on the way and asked him what time it was. The friar answered: "The day is for you and the night is for me".
162828: Three men returning from Bommershoven in the evening met a strange woman on the way. After walking for two hours the men still had not reached Jesseren. The witch had made them lose their way.
162858: Three men from Lauw were coming back from the fair in Tongeren around midnight. Suddenly one of the men said: "I have to go away for a moment. If anything comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at the apparition and say: 'Pull it apart seam by thread, the way it was woven.'" A little further on the two men met a dog with a long tail. When they had thrown the handkerchief at the animal, the dog began to unravel the cloth completely, so the men had time to make off. A little later the third man rejoined his friends. But he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The man said to his friends: "My hour had come. You see, I sold my soul for a hundred thousand francs."
162876: H. had often struck at a cat, but he never managed to hit the animal. In such cases baptized people had to rub the stick along their hair. After that they would be able to hit the cat.
162877: A boy had for many years been going out with a girl who was said to be a witch. Because people kept warning the boy about the supposed witch, he decided to look for another girl. When the boy had been to see his new sweetheart on a Sunday for the second time, he got a severe pain in his foot. The doctor, however, could find nothing. One day the boy was visited by his ex-girlfriend, who said: "I felt so bad that you're in such pain, so I've come to see you." The girl examined the painful foot and said: "But don't you see that little point? There's a darning needle in there!" After the girl had picked the needle out of his foot, the boy had no more pain.
162883: A woman could not make butter because the milk was bewitched.
162891: In a meadow in Nerem people often heard music when the witches were dancing and singing at night. Witches in the shape of cats often sat by the barriers.
162899: In the 'Kruuskes' between Vucht and Eisden a white lady sometimes appeared.
162916: A married couple had seen a small chest fall from a coach on the Genkersteenweg. When the man had picked up the chest and seen that it was full of money, he said: "Those people will come and ask for that chest back." His wife replied: "No, we're keeping it." But the man was struck by remorse and died soon afterwards. After his death the man came to haunt the Genkersteenweg. Because the ghost kept crying: "Give it back! Give it back!", the people sent for a friar from Hasselt. Without looking back, the friar led the ghost with a stake and a chain to the Maten. After the stake with the ghost had been thrown into the marsh, it still cried: "Give it back! Give it back!"
162934: A boy who was tormented by the maar (nightmare, mare) always began tossing and turning in his bed at midnight. A piece of bacon was tied around the boy's wrist. After eight days the bacon could be removed.
162936: In the Vetwei at the foot of the 'Aberg' there was always a witch dressed in black searching for herbs.
162948: A man walked at night via Gerdingen to Bree to visit his sister, who worked as a maid for a certain T. On the way the man was followed by a cat for a long time. When the cat had disappeared at a certain moment, the man heard a hellish noise; a tree beside the road was suddenly full of magpies and crows. The man did not dare to walk past it.
162964: A woman going to the village met a werewolf on the way. Because the woman was terrified, she struck the beast down. The next day a dead man was found wrapped in a cowhide.
162968: In Lanaken lived a woman who bewitched her own grandchildren. One of those children would always jump out of bed and bang his head against the door and the walls. When they went to the Crosier Fathers in Maaseik, one of the priests said: "That will not be so easy, because it happened within the family!" Fortunately the little boy did survive.
162973: Han went peddling bread rolls. In one house Han had turned a child's head back to front. When the father noticed it, he cried out: "Damn it, Han koekestelle has been here!" Han was forced to set the child's head straight again.
162978: Three men were playing cards in a café near B.'s farm in Rutten. When a stranger suddenly came in, one of the men said: "Look, now we have a fourth man for cards!" But while picking up a fallen card, one of the men saw that the stranger had cow's legs. Suddenly the strange man had disappeared.
163000:
In Waterschei lived a werewolf who had a collar. If the collar could be burnt, the werewolf was released.
There was also a werewolf who draped a sheet over himself and came to steal the farmer's beets.
163006: At T.'s in Wiemelsmaal a ghost always came out of a pond after it had rained. The ghost frightened passers-by and chased them.
163011: One night the farmhand of the M. family shot a hare that was running through the garden. When the farmhand went to pick up the animal, he saw to his great horror that his master's wife was lying there on the ground. Luckily he had not hit her badly. That is how everyone found out that the woman was a witch.
163016: J. from Zonhoven had once had a werewolf on his shoulders.
163033: A wizard visiting a family said: "I can make sure none of you gets home tomorrow. I can make all four of you lose your way. And if I meet anyone, I will stab that person to death."
163040: A man from Deurne was coming back in the evening from Schoonaarde, where he had gone to visit his girlfriend. On the way the man got lost. Some woman or other had bewitched him.
163058: A mother looking for her son was startled when she heard a strange sound among the Canadian poplars.
163071: One day a certain R. went to visit his family in Boekhout. On the way he saw a coach come driving along the castle lane. The haunting in that area was so bad that eventually the Norbertines (white canons) of Batsheers were sent for. When one of the friars tried to stop the count's ghost, the ghost said: "When you were still a student, you once stole a cake from a shop." The next friar who was sent for was thrown into the brook on the way by an invisible hand, while a voice said: "If you didn't have a tonsure, I would have drowned you in the brook." When the friar tried to stop the ghost, it said: "You once stole a cabbage from someone's garden," to which the friar replied: "Yes, but I left half a franc in its place." At that moment the friar gained power over the ghost. The count's ghost was banished for ninety-nine years near the Ster in the woods. Because a voice had then been heard saying: "You must throw the money out of the windows here!", the poor were given free coal from the castle. During his life the count had unlawfully acquired many goods. Many years later, stones were still found bearing the letter "A", from the abbey of Averbode. Whenever someone struck the tree into which the count was banished, a loud sigh was always heard.
163075: After a witch had praised a woman for her good butter, the butter turned into buttermilk.
163077:
In the old days the emperors and kings all had a witch in their service. Those witches could, for example, raise a thunderstorm or a hailstorm. They could have used that power to drive off enemy troops, but they never did. Back then every village had a village witch. She was a sort of herb woman whom people came to for advice. Once Innocentius, Sprenger and Institoris had written their Hammer of Witches, witches were suddenly associated with the devil, and so they were persecuted.
One of the stories from that book went as follows:
A boy told a parish priest that a witch had magicked away his private parts. The priest said: "You must go back to the witch and demand that she give them back to you." The witch said to the boy: "All right. Just this once... In the garden there is a pear tree with a crow's nest. It is in that nest." The boy climbed the tree and thought: "I'm going to pick out the best one!" When the boy had chosen one, the witch said: "No, no, not that one, that belongs to the parish priest of Paris. That one stays here."
163103: One day a man was coming back from Ellikom with his horse and cart. Suddenly, however, the horses stopped. A strange woman passed by. When the woman was gone, the horses could go on again.
163118: Because people believed that the black cat roaming around the Meut was a witch, they went to the Capuchins in Lommel-Fabriek.
163119: A man who had moved a boundary post came back to haunt after his death, saying: "Where shall I leave it?" One day a drunkard answered: "Put it where you fetched it from." The ghost replied: "God be blessed" and then disappeared.
163123: A woman went to the priest because she could no longer make butter. The priest advised the woman not to let a certain woman in any more. After that they could make butter again without trouble.
163134: A Dutchman who had come to Belgium with his horse and cart went to a café one evening. When the man left, he lost his way and drove his horse and cart into the Maas. The man drowned. Since then the man's ghost floated over the Maas crying: "Ferry over! Ferry over!"
163149: In the past a coach used to drive around the grounds of the castle of Rijkhoven. In the end a clergyman banished that coach.
163161: A boy who was taking a walk with his girlfriend announced that he had to go away for a moment and gave the girl a red handkerchief. When a big dog appeared a little later, the girl threw the handkerchief at the animal's mouth. A little later her boyfriend came back.
163166: A woman did not know that the man she had just married was a werewolf. When the man was out walking with his wife, he said: "Go on ahead, I have to relieve myself. If you should meet a dog, just throw this handkerchief." A little later a dog did indeed appear, which tore the handkerchief to pieces. The next night the woman got up and noticed that her husband still had the scraps of the handkerchief between his teeth.
163182: When the jack of spades had brought a bottle of gin, the bottle had to be emptied.
163188: In Schalkhoven a child had got convulsions after being touched by the evil hand.
163189: A child had died at the age of five because of the evil hand. Someone showed the father, in a bucket of water, the face of the witch responsible for the misfortune.
163207: In Gellik there was a street that was haunted. A strange creaking could always be heard there, although nothing could be seen. People believed that the late Manus V.P. came to haunt the place together with his sister.
163215: Some men were playing cards. When one of the players had got up, a strange man offered to play along. But that man always dropped the clubs. The other players looked under the table and saw that the stranger had goat's legs. This happened at the Kaartridder (name of an inn?).
163222: A farmer from Balen had moved the boundary post of his field to have a bigger piece of land. After his death the farmer came back to haunt with a boundary post in his hands, calling: "Where do I leave it? Where on earth do I leave it?" One evening a drunkard coming back from the fair answered: "Just take it back to the place where you fetched it from!" At that the ghost replied joyfully: "I am released! I am released!" Since then there has been no more haunting in the field.
163224: A man riding home from his work at the zinc factory was followed by a big black dog. When the man was almost home, the dog turned out to have vanished. His wife believed the dog was the devil.
163229: A woman always saw a will-o'-the-wisp near a pond. Because it was the soul of an unbaptised child, the parish priest gave the woman this advice: "If you see the will-o'-the-wisp again, you must baptise it. Put your hand in the water and say: 'If you want to become a Christian, I baptise you in the name of God the Lord. I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.' You must also add: 'I baptise you alone', or else thousands of will-o'-the-wisps will come asking to be baptised. And be sure not to sit down, because then the will-o'-the-wisps will push you into the water; that is how badly they want to be baptised." The next time the woman saw the will-o'-the-wisp, she baptised it. But she had not been quick enough, and at once many will-o'-the-wisps appeared. She baptised one more and quickly added: "I baptise you alone". Then all the will-o'-the-wisps were gone.
163230: After a child had accepted an apple from a witch, it fell ill. The doctors were at a loss and even a pilgrimage brought no cure. When the parents cut open the child's pillow, they found a wreath of feathers that was almost closed. If the wreath had been closed, the child would have died. The feathers could only be burned after they had been sprinkled with holy water. In the end the child recovered.
163233: In the past witches could turn themselves into cats.
163241: A witch was hauling trees across the canal together with some men. At the bridge of Beringen the witch suddenly said: "In a moment the girl from the café will ride past here on a man's bicycle." A little later that girl did indeed come riding by. Then the witch said: "Now the girl will turn her bicycle around and ride home." And so it happened.
163245: The F. family in Stamprooi had a child that cried all the time. The father suspected that Marie van het Z. had caused the misfortune by stroking the child's head. When Marie came to visit some time later, she showed a doll that had a cut in its back. The father asked Marie if she wouldn't give the little doll to the child. Marie clearly did not like parting with the doll, but when the father kept insisting, she had to hand it over after all. After Marie left, the doll was thrown into the fire. Because the child stopped crying immediately afterwards, people knew for certain that Marie was a witch.
163247: A young man going to his aunt's in the evening met a man on the way, who said: "Hello S., aren't you afraid to go home alone? You might meet a dog." S. replied: "I'm not afraid of dogs." No sooner had he said this than a dog came after him. S. suspected it was a werewolf and stubbornly walked on. When he passed a crossroads in Keizel, the werewolf could go no further.
163249: The white lady appeared on the road of Herk-de-Stad.
163250: Many witches used to live on the Schans in Opoeteren. One evening a man brought a pan of water to the boil and then called: "Puss, puss!" At once some thirty cats came running. The man poured boiling water over the animals. The next day nearly all the women of Opoeteren had burns.
163258: A boy visiting his girlfriend pretended to have fallen asleep. That way the boy saw the girl say at midnight: "Over hedges and hawthorns" and then fly away. The boy wanted to follow the girl and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns". The boy arrived badly injured at the Ummeser Hugskes, where the witches gathered.
163259: A soldier stationed in Aarlen always saw a cat walking on the stairs. When the man went outside one night and stamped at the cat with his bare foot, he heard a woman upstairs call out: "Boy, leave the cat alone!" The woman was asleep and could not have seen the soldier.
163260: If one laid a broomstick in front of the door, no witches could come in.
163262: A man who saw a werewolf at night cut off the beast's nose. As soon as the werewolf began to bleed, he changed into the man's brother.
163276: A farmer lived on a farm on a former castle estate. When the farmer had lived on his farm for some years, strange things began to happen regularly. At night he often heard a strange sound that stopped whenever he went outside to look. The farmer's pigs would not fatten and most of his hens and sheep died. When the farmer was at his wits' end, he went to a healer in Genk. The healer believed the misfortune on the farm was due to the farmer having put in a new threshold. The farmer had to go on pilgrimage to the Zwartbroek, to Sint-Gillis in Erpekom and to Saint Benedict in Lozen. After that the farmer would have no more misfortune. But the children who were already infected with a disease could no longer be saved. And so it happened: after the pilgrimage the farm was no longer haunted, but all three of the farmer's children died. After that the farmer moved away.
163291: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "Go on ahead, I have to relieve myself. If you should meet a dog, just throw my handkerchief at the animal." The girl did as she had been advised. When the boy came into the café a little later, the girl noticed that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
163310: A child was bewitched after it had been given chocolate by a woman. The child's parents went to the fathers of Rijkel, who said: "Watch out, for a woman will come over your threshold. You must tell her a few things." When father Nerus told the witch what the fathers had instructed him, the witch screamed loudly and then ran away. The child eventually died. In the pillow there was a braided wreath.
163311: Around midnight, ghosts with a white sheet and chains floated about the churchyard. They were the spirits of the dead who could find no rest.
163325: A man who was taking piglets to a farmer tied a palm sprig to the cart so that he would not be bewitched by a notorious widow from the village.
163332: A boy who had got lice through a witch's doing had to put the creatures in a pot and bury the pot in the ground. After that the boy was rid of the vermin.
163336: A woman who was ridden by the maar (nightmare, mare) at night got up and let her animals outside. A cow that had just calved she left in the stable. The next morning the woman knew nothing of what had happened during the night.
163356: A boy and his girlfriend were coming back together from Beverst. Suddenly the boy said to the girl: "I can't go with you, but if you should meet some animal or other, just throw a handkerchief at its mouth." The boy was a werewolf. A man had found his animal skin in a tree, but he had not managed to burn it.
163374: In the old days some hedges were haunted. When people heard rustling there, they made off quickly.
163377:
A girl who had accepted sweets from a witch grew thinner and thinner. Pastor Z. advised the parents to have the girl prayed over by the fathers of Wijk. After that had been done, the girl was somewhat better. In the pillow the child slept on, they found a wreath of feathers. Fortunately the wreath was not yet closed, for then the child would have died. When the mother showed the wreath to the pastor, the clergyman said: "You must not put any faith in such things." The pastor told the child's father to burn the wreath between twelve and one in the afternoon. He added: "Watch carefully, for then the person responsible will come by!" A woman from Rekem did indeed come by. The pastor claimed that people who had not been properly baptised easily fell into the devil's grip and so sometimes became witches. The girl got better, but she nevertheless died at the age of sixteen.
Witches had power above all over weak children. A girl who was bewitched could no longer sleep at night. When a little cross was placed under the doormat, the witch could no longer get in. After a visit to the fathers of Wijk, the child was cured. That child, too, died at the age of sixteen.
163378: In the old days people stood with a black hen at the crossroads between Millen and Sluizen to meet the devil there.
163380: The G. family had a farmhand who was suspected of being a werewolf. One evening the farmer saw the boy take a collar out of an ash tree stump in Beek. When he put the collar on, he turned into a dog. The next day the farmer sent the farmhand away so that he could burn the collar in the meantime. But when the collar lay in the fire, the boy came running to save his band. In the end the pastor released the boy.
163405: The gnomes moved to another region because people no longer wanted to pay them enough for their services.
163407: During the procession from Zutendaal to Munsterbilzen, some men had to carry the statue of Mary. At the border with Munsterbilzen they suddenly could go no further. Mary wanted to stay in Zutendaal.
163431: During the French period many churches and monasteries were sold. But those who acquired such property had no luck. At Terherken, for example, there was haunting. In the mornings the animals stood sweating in the stable and the horses' manes were braided. At their wits' end, they decided to send for a priest. "You must cut the braided manes of the horse lengthwise", said the priest. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was dead. She had been cut in half.
163433: In the village lived two women suspected of being witches. When one crossed one's feet on the witch's footprints, she immediately turned round.
163437: A woman was nearly frightened to death when she saw the ghost of her late husband appear. To make sure it was not her imagination, the woman asked her husband to give a sign of his presence. She took a towel from the cupboard and asked the ghost to put his hand on it. The ghost replied, "I cannot do that, because that towel was only ironed last Sunday." The man came back to haunt because during his life he had made a vow that he had not yet been able to keep. The woman had to fulfil it in his place.
163458: In Rutten a priest had been sent for to pray over a possessed woman. When the priest wanted to make the woman drink some holy water, the witch bit the glass to pieces. Whenever the Gospel of Saint John was read in church, the witches quickly ran outside.
163466: One evening a woman went to pick beans at the mayor's in Peer. When the woman went to bring the beans in, she saw a strange white apparition come leaping towards her. The woman then took a dung fork, stabbed at the apparition and ran away.
163477: On a farm in Aldeneik sixteen cows and one horse died because of the evil hand. The pastor advised the farmer to build a new stable on the other side of the street. The stomach of the last cow to die had to be emptied and boiled in a large cooking pot. As soon as the water began to boil, the witch would appear. But no one turned up.
163482: Between Leut and Meeswijk a man played at being a werewolf. The man wore a leather belt with a spike on his back, so that the werewolf jumped onto the spike.
163488: A man going to the field with horse and cart suddenly could go no further because 't keesmeske was standing by the road. "It's you!" said the man. When 't keesmeske said "Oep!", the horse could pull the cart again.
163503: In Fouron a nun with a walking stick came haunting every night. Because people constantly heard the tapping of that walking stick, they went to the parish priest for advice. When the priest asked one night what the nun wanted, a voice said: "Nothing. Priez, priez." A few nights later the nun went to heaven.
163508: A poacher who had shot at a badger ran away in fear when suddenly a hundred badgers appeared.
163510: Witches could make themselves invisible. That way they could eavesdrop on everyone and were also hard to defeat.
163515: In the lane to Vogelsang a man came haunting, saying: "Frisse, give me your hat and I'll piss in it!"
163518: Two women always went to cut fodder for their animals in a meadow that was not theirs. The police never managed to catch the women, because every time the officers came closer, the witches turned themselves into a bramble bush.
163525: A man was at his wits' end because his house was bewitched. At midnight on the dot the animals in the stable began to bellow and in the kitchen all the plates and bowls fell to the floor. The fathers of Weert advised the man to take the nails out of an Easter candle and push them into the ground in front of the stable door. After that nothing strange happened any more.
163538: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
163549: Vloek-Sus (Cursing Sus) from Romershoven had earned his nickname through his annoying habit of constantly cursing. He had a twenty-year-old daughter who was beaten every day by a ghost. When she sat by the hearth with her parents in the evening, the girl would see the ghost come out of the chimney, and then she would cry: "He's here again!" When the ghost, which looked more like a dog than a man, beat her, she screamed. Several clergymen had already come to deal with the ghost, but because they themselves had once done something wrong, they gained no power over it. One day a young priest came to the house. The ghost reproached the cleric: "Carp thief!", to which the priest answered: "If I took that man's carp, I paid for it to the man whose pond it was!" While he was praying, the priest asked: "Do you want to see who the ghost is?", to which the girl's father said: "Well yes, damn it!" Under the table appeared a man they knew, who had died not long before. The priest banished the ghost to a wood in a hamlet of Hoesselt.
163553: After a witch had stroked her hand over a child's head, the child got lice.
163557: The witches gathered in Zichen-Zussen-Bolder, where they rubbed themselves with something and then flew away after saying: "Over hedge and hawthorn". At the Ummeser Hugskes the witches would then dance and have fun. A man who had eavesdropped on the witches also rubbed himself with the grease and said: "Through hedge and hawthorn". The man arrived at the Ummeser Hugskes badly injured.
163569: The maid Lowiske went to milk the cow at four in the morning. Sometimes she saw a white lady appear, who went with her as far as the brook or the church. One day Lowiske had to go along with the white lady. She thought it was an angel, but it was a woman dressed in white.
163570: Three young men went to visit their girlfriends in Meeuwen. They did not know, however, that the three girls were witches. When the young men went home again, they always waited for each other so they could leave together. While Pier K. and the mayor were waiting, a little cat came along. The mayor went into the bushes for a moment to relieve himself. Then he struck the cat with a stick, so that it ran off wounded. When the two went to fetch the third man, a badly injured woman suddenly walked into that house saying: "I fell off the haystack!" The three young men went home terrified. They were on the road from ten o'clock in the evening until the next morning. The whole time they were surrounded by cats.
163572: One of Nol S.'s children was swimming in a pond when suddenly a woman who was said to be a witch came past. The woman threw a stone into the water. Although she had not hit the child, the boy sank under the water like a stone.
163578: A boy who had to take some pigs away went, against his mother's wishes, to fetch a crate from someone. On the way the boy found that the pigs were lying dead in the crate. Fortunately the pig was not spoiled, because the blood still took up salt. A few days later the boy's brother-in-law came to visit. With tears in his eyes the man said that his hen and her chicks had died. The man had also put the hen in the witch's crate.
163589: A man going to the fair in his new coat met a woman on the way, who said: "What a fine coat you're wearing! Won't you sell it?" But the man would not part with his coat for any money. The woman then walked off angrily. A little further on the man began to itch all over. The man realised that the witch had given him lice.
163605:
Henri from Opitter was ridden by the maar (nightmare, mare) in his bed almost every night. After the man, on a beggar's advice, put an iron file under his pillow, he was no longer troubled by the maar.
People who claimed to be ridden by the maar in fact had a stopping of the blood.
163621: The count of the castle of Wezemaal came back from the hunt around twelve o'clock. Because the chaplain had already begun Mass, the count split the cleric's skull with a sword. After his death the cleric came haunting every night to say Mass. When Mass was over, the chaplain jumped into the castle pond.
163639: A mother had been visited by a woman who came to borrow baking tins. The woman had picked up the baby. The next day the child was full of maggots.
163642: A girl who had been touched by the evil hand at the fair became seriously ill. When the girl lay in bed, she would always jump up and go to the corner of the room. A woman who claimed that a priest had taught her to heal people went to the girl. After the woman had called the girl three times, the child was cured.
163668: In the old days a werewolf sat on the doorstep of the house in the Vermeulenstraat where judge P. later came to live. The werewolf jumped on passers-by's necks and made them carry it. The stone the doorstep was made of had been stolen by someone when the churchyard around the Hoogkerk was cleared. The stone came from the grave of a beguine. That beguine surely cannot have led a pious life, since her soul came back.
163669: Bells had been buried on the Koelbrich during the war. On Christmas night people heard those bells ringing underground.
163677: Suske V.'s daughter had been ill in bed for twenty-five years. When her mother died, the girl was suddenly cured.
163681: A witch made mice come out from under her skirt.
163694: Whenever Heksebetje saw a child, she went up to it and rubbed her hand over its little head, saying: "What a lovely child!" A little later people would notice that the child was full of lice.
163698: A man whose wife was ill met a witch, who said: "Tomorrow your wife will be dead." And so it happened.
163704: Four children had fallen ill after eating 'bokkingen' (smoked herring) that 'de Kemel' had come peddling. The mother took her children to the priest. The priest gave the children a sweet and said: "If the witches give the children anything now, they can safely eat it. It will do them no more harm."
163711: A farmer's wife let her goat graze in a meadow surrounded by a hedge. When the goat stood by the hedge, a woman from Gessel kept saying: "That goat is eating the leaves off the hedge." In the end the farmer's wife decided to bring her goat inside. The next day the goat was dead.
163724:
A carpenter had been working until one o'clock at night making a coffin. After that he still had to go to his brother's to fetch brushes. On the way the carpenter heard witches dancing and making merry in the meadow. When the man reached his brother's, he told him what he had heard. His brother said he had heard it himself once too, and that the next morning he had seen a witches' circle in the meadow.
One evening the carpenter's father had to cross a farmer's large meadow on his way home. Under an apple tree he found a stick that was especially finely made. The father took the stick and crawled through the hedge. Suddenly someone snatched the stick from his hands. When the man looked back, he saw six women sitting in the apple tree.
A while later a bed was broken up in a neighbouring house, and in it they found all sorts of scissors and needles that looked like silver. The carpenter's father was convinced that he had also seen the woman from that house in the apple tree.
163725: At school a little boy threw a blade of grass onto the road, after which dozens of mice appeared. When the other children had told the priest, the clergyman called the boy to him. After prayers had been read over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
163734: The wife and daughter of the schoolmaster of Meeuwen were witches. Because the man believed the cabbages in his garden had been eaten by a hare, he fetched his gun and stood guard. When the schoolmaster wanted to shoot at a hare, however, his gun did not work. After the man had sprinkled his gun with consecrated powder, he was able to hit the hare. The man went to look and saw his own wife lying dead on the ground.
