163755: Jan had gone to the heath to fetch some tree stumps. On the way back his horse suddenly stopped, sweating heavily. A little further on Marie van 't Weverke stood laughing at her door and said: "What's the matter, Jan, isn't it going?" "No," the man answered, "can't you help me?" Marie replied with a grin: "Yes, I might be able to do that!" "In God's name then!" cried Jan. Then a big black dog ran in front of the horse, which dropped dead.
163757: A girl worked as a maid for a family in Maastricht. One day a little woman rang the bell and asked for the maid. The little woman wanted to know whether the maid knew where a certain person lived. "No," answered the maid, "I don't know anyone here in Maastricht." Then the little woman said: "What a beautiful neck you have," and she reached out her hand to touch the maid. The maid slapped the little woman in the face and slammed the door. That little woman was a witch.
163764: In Rekem (?) some men were playing cards. When a man bent down to pick up a fallen card, he saw that one of his fellow players had cow's legs. It was the devil.
163768: Many poachers came to the castle estate of Ham. The hares that hopped about there, however, could not be hit.
163769: During their sabbath the witches gathered in white or black clothing to dance and leap. The witches claimed that they healed people, but in reality they made them ill and caused them to die. Witches sometimes also took little children away. Sometimes the witches sold ointment to people. The witches claimed that the ointment had a healing effect, but in reality people got a rash from it. Witches also sometimes hit people with dead cats.
163795: In Keizel lived a farmer named T. When T. came home one morning from the liberal party's celebration, he found his wife dead in bed. After the woman was buried, she came haunting in the cowshed so that all the cows broke loose. Twice T. had a brown friar come from Hasselt to read prayers over the cowshed.
163813: Bernard V.D. caused cats to sit on someone's windowsill and in their bed.
163821: A wound inflicted by a black witch's cat was very painful and healed only slowly.
163822: In Genk there were devil's stones where the devil had his bed. The devil had left his footprint in those stones. The stones could not be removed or blown up in any way. At night nobody dared to walk past that place because the stones made strange noises. When Thijske N. and Pieter passed those stones one night, they were so frightened that they fled home as fast as they could.
163831: After his death Laurentius M. came back as a ghost that went around untying the animals everywhere. Laurentius' sister lay gravely ill in bed and kept crying: "Mon frère, mon frère, what have I done to you?" In the end a friar from Diest banished the ghost for ninety-nine years and more. Only a friar who had never committed a sin had the power to banish a ghost. The ghost had said: "Even if you give as many barrels of grain to the poor as there are grains in a barrel, I will still not be released."
163843: In Deurne lived an old witch whose son went to Diest against her will. When he left, the witch had said: "We will never see him again." And so it happened.
163849: When Morauke was walking home with Bert, he said to his friend: "Before you get home, I'll be sitting in your room." Although his house was locked, Bert did indeed find Morauke in his room. Morauke had got his magic power from a little book he had received from the devil. Since the day the Gospel of Saint John was introduced, there has fortunately been no more room for such evil.
163855: Will-o'-the-wisps were souls of unbaptised children that appeared by the water at night.
163856: Witches often made children ill by giving them something tasty.
163871: At midnight a beguine always came and sat on the steps of the Benedictine monastery.
163880: A boy who was taking a walk with his girlfriend suddenly felt that he was about to turn into a werewolf. So the boy said to the girl: "I have to go and do a big job. If a beast comes at you in the meantime, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little later the girl threw the handkerchief at a wolf that came running up. When the boy came back, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. That is how the girl found out that her boyfriend was a werewolf.
163885: One day a man from Piringen went to Liège with his farmhands to fetch coal. When they met a wagon with six black horses wearing bells, the man called out: "Left or right?", to know which way he should move aside. A voice from the coach answered: "The day is for you, but the night is for me." The horses of the coach galloped past while their bells rang loudly.
163887: A woman walking past a witch's house suddenly could not move. After the woman had made the sign of the cross, she could go on again.
163903: A man who went to herd the cows in Lafelt with some friends became frightened when he heard it said that something strange was roaming about in the distance.
163911: At school Kloefke made mice from a handful of earth. After the chaplain had made a sign of the cross over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
163913: In the old days it often happened that women bewitched children. The children would then have an open wound in the place where the witch had touched them.
163914: A farmer's wife went to the fathers because many animals had already died in her stable. The priest gave the farmer's wife a small black box with which she had to walk through the stable every day. From then on the farmer's wife did not have so much misfortune.
163915: A man coming back from the fair in Budel went to the inn of Mie V.A. When Deurke H. went to drink from his glass, the bottom fell out. Then Deurke said: "Mie, now I really think you're a witch!", to which Mie replied: "Yes, so I am."
163962: Some men playing cards in Bierbeek made a bet, daring each other to see who could swear the hardest. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that one of the players had a goat's foot. At that all the men ran off except one, who had been given the task of building a blue barn. The devil promised to build the barn in one night if the man would sell his soul. The alvermannetjes (elves) built the barn. After one night everything was finished except the gate. Many years later the gate was still hanging upside down.
163967: In Eigenbilzen lived a family with seven children. Six of the children died after being bewitched. When the seventh child also fell ill, the pastor went to the witch with a medlar stick and said: "If that child does not get better, I will kill you!" After the child had been prayed over, it recovered.
163970: Every time the witch came past while the farmhand was mowing, the machine broke.
163986: On the road to Rutten there were always black cats at night that ran under passers-by's feet. One night a man kicked one of the cats. The cat then jumped up and scratched the man's whole face open.
163999: A farmer could not make butter because the milk was bewitched.
164005: Before a baby was baptised, the parents were very afraid of witches and their evil hand. As soon as the baptism was over, witches no longer had any power over the child.
164020: A man who had fallen asleep in church saw a priest sitting in the confessional between midnight and one o'clock. The confessor had been haunting for years because he had not done his duty towards his penitents.
164024: One morning a woman had dropped a pound of butter. Her husband Jen had hurt his leg with his clogs. In the afternoon Mie came to bring the man coffee. Mie said to Jen: "You had bad luck again this morning, didn't you!", to which the man asked in surprise: "How so?" Mie then said: "Well, your wife dropped the butter, didn't she! And does your leg still hurt?" The witch knew everything without having seen it. When Mie met a man going to work, she said: "Hey, you've forgotten your pliers!" And the man himself did not even know it yet!
164041: On Epiphany the H. family had run out of brandy. The farmhand no longer dared to go to the village, because it was already dark. The cowherd, a brave lad of fifteen, offered to go in his place. To be safe he took a dung fork with him. The farmhand decided to give the cowherd a real fright; he put on a cowhide and sat in a gap in the hedge. When the cowherd heard a terrifying noise on the way back, he struck with the dung fork at the hedge the noise came from. He struck the farmhand stone dead. Back home the cowherd said he had killed a werewolf. "That must have been the farmhand," said the farmer, and together they went to look with a lantern. They tried to pull the cowhide off the dead farmhand, but they could not: he was no longer a real human. So the cowherd was not punished. At the place where the farmhand died, a large cross was put up, called the Devil's Cross.
164045: When a stable was under the influence of the evil hand, the animals were found tied up in a different place in the morning.
164047: At the market in Weert a man met a woman who said he had better go home quickly if he wanted to be home before dark. The man paid no attention to it and stayed at the market a while longer. When the man walked home, he got lost, so that he only found the way towards evening.
164048: Two men who were going together to the old Reppel in Stokrooie had to shelter from the rain in a little shed on the way. Through a crack in the shed the men were spied on by a woman. The woman threw sand in the men's faces. When the men went on after the shower, they ended up in Bolderberg instead of Zolder.
164063: A man walking through a dark forest saw a crow flying, which cried: "Stand still!" The man was rooted to the spot with fear and got lost in the forest.
164095: In Halmaal lived a man whose children all died within a few days of birth. One day the man told his friends about his misfortunes. One of the men advised him to go and see a woman in Luik. The man went to the woman and told her his story. Then the woman said to him: "Shall I show you the woman who is responsible for all this misfortune?", and she showed the man a mirror in which the face of his own mother appeared. When the man was home again, he packed up all his belongings and moved with his wife to Luik.
164098: After the witches had held gatherings in the forest, they all went to a stable to make the animals ill. At twelve o'clock the witches went home.
164099: A man from Waltwilder had wounded a werewolf with a whip. The werewolf then changed into a stark-naked man, who begged not to be betrayed. In return for his silence the man from Waltwilder could always count on the werewolf's help. When the man from Waltwilder was out with three friends, the group was threatened by some boys from Eigenbilzen. As soon as the man from Waltwilder whistled, five or six large dogs appeared, which frightened the boys from Eigenbilzen so much that they left at once. On the way home, the four boys from Waltwilder were accompanied by one werewolf.
164100: A man who had caught a cat on the way locked the animal in a shed. The next day the animal had disappeared. It was a witch.
164105: A hunter who had shot a hare in a wood in Ophoven was surprised because he could not find the animal anywhere. Later he heard that a woman from the village lay in bed because her buttocks were full of shot.
164130: Vuurmannen (fire men) used to cause people a lot of trouble. They led everyone to the water so that they could be baptised.
164138:
A farmer whose animals were always foaming at the mouth believed the beasts were plagued by the evil hand.
There were probably rats in the stable, or the animals suffered from a particular disease.
164148: A man struck at a cat that had jumped onto his shoulder. A moment later, however, the animal jumped onto the man's back. This frightened the man so much that he no longer dared to strike at the cat. As soon as the man reached the village, the cat had disappeared.
164151: Werewolves wore a collar. They often sat on a tree stump waiting until they could make a passer-by carry them. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he became human again and you knew who it was.
164171: In 's Heerenelderen a will-o'-the-wisp appeared in the reeds. People believed it was the soul of an unbaptised child.
164184: A mother went with her daughter and a woman from the neighbourhood to collect the money her husband had earned. When they came back, the daughter's head was full of lice. They had never thought that the neighbour woman was a witch.
164190: A couple, of whom the husband was disabled and the wife ill, had only one cow. When the cow fell ill, they sent for pastor R. from Montenaken. After the pastor had read prayers over the cow, the animal stood up without effort. "You must not let that woman in anymore," said the pastor.
164191: When Leo W. went poaching, he saw a hare that he just could not shoot. Because Leo was at his wits' end, he struck at the animal with the barrel of his gun. The hare then took the gun from him and hit the man hard on the head. When Leo wanted to steal some plums, strangely enough not a single fruit fell from the tree. As soon as the hare had disappeared, there were so many plums on the ground that the man could no longer move.
164199: Two men going to the smith together saw a cat sitting by the road. One of the men took off his clog and threw it at the animal. Because the cat stayed sitting beside the fallen clog, the man put his clog back on and went on. The men briefly visited Sooike V.K. When they came out, the cat was sitting in front of the door. The animal followed the men until they were home. Once home, the men saw as many as fifty young cats sitting and wailing.
164203: During the French Revolution the people of Liège set fire to a house in Dilsen and murdered a woman. The woman's body was thrown into the Helleput (Molenput). Later people said that at night a woman without a head wandered through the Tumbrook.
164223: Under the door of a stable at 't Hoebes was an opening that could not be bricked up in any way. The opening always opened up again.
164234: Jef had had a relationship with a woman who lived at 't Bokt. When the love was over, Jef could no longer pass the woman's house without his horse walking to the side of the road.
164242: In Viversel a mother and daughter were gathering hay together. Suddenly the girl said: "Mum, my leg hurts so much," to which the mother replied: "That's nothing, my child." Shortly afterwards the girl died. The mother was a witch who had given her daughter the evil hand by rubbing the child's leg. The witch had also bewitched her pigs.
164251: A soldier who saw a cat sitting on a turnstile struck at the animal twice. Then the cat said: "Go on, lancer, strike again now!"
164252: A woman who could not sleep saw a white shape wandering over the churchyard around midnight. A little later the shape had vanished. It was probably a dead person who could find no rest.
164266: A man who claimed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children wanted to try to baptise one. But the man never managed to catch a will-o'-the-wisp.
164285: In an old farmhouse two women were doing the washing in a tub when a beggar woman came asking for alms. When the witch had gone, the two women were full of lice.
164296:
When a dog howled, there would be a death in the neighbourhood within three days.
When Pierkes P.'s dog howled one day, the man said: "I don't like hearing that." The next day the neighbour woman was dead.
164300: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who appeared with a little lamp at the place where they had died.
164321: One day Jacob C. was completely covered in lice through a witch's doing. Jacob angrily went to the witch and beat her on the head with a stick until she was willing to take all the lice away again.
164322: By the Platvijvers a ghost in a black hood wandered about every evening, calling: "Where shall I put my boundary post? Where shall I put my boundary post?" One evening someone answered: "You fool, just put it wherever you like!" Since then the ghost has not been seen or heard again.
164325: Every evening a burning coach drove around on the Hobos. In front of the fire sat the dead drossaard (bailiff) in the shape of a large dog.
164352: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
164364: A man who went to play cards in the evenings was always jumped by the werewolf on his way home.
164366: A man had seen a pack of cats come to dance in the attic, and he had broken the leg of one of the animals. The next day an old woman had a broken arm.
164372: A man had visited a woman who was said to be a witch. On the way back the man got lost. Since then the man never visited that witch again.
164397: A man coming back from the café wanted to light his cigar with a match on the way home. But a big black cat kept blowing the cigar out. The man arrived home scared to death.
164409:
In the church of Muizen the Holy Cross is venerated. Muizen used to belong to the parish of Kerkom, but now it belongs to Buvingen.
One day three men tried to take the Holy Cross to Kerkom on a cart. When they reached the Kattestraat, however, they could not move another step. There was nothing for it but to take the Cross back to Kerkom. Since then no stranger could enter the territory of Muizen with a horse on the third of May. Anyone who tried anyway saw the horse drop dead on the spot.
164414: A man walking home at night suddenly saw a big dog sitting on the road. When the man tried to hit the dog with a stick, the animal suddenly vanished. It was a werewolf.
164418: A boy from Gorsem made mice from a little heap of earth during catechism class. After the priest had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
164426: Every morning a boy was asked by his mother: "Have you made the sign of the cross yet?" One morning the boy answered angrily: "You and your little cross!", after which he set off with his sister to the factory in Balen-Wezel. On the way the two saw a strange man who seemed to 'slide' over the ground. The man was almost twice as tall as a normal person and had a square head. When they came to the bridge, the girl said: "That water really stinks here!" The girl had only smelled the apparition, not seen it. The boy and his sister arrived at work an hour and a half late.
164440: On the Meunikenhof the farmhands never dared come home late, because then a ghost sat on the gate. Old Trees had hanged herself, after all, and had to come back to haunt.
164444: A woman from Maasmechelen moved to a garden village in Eisden because her house was haunted. She always saw a strange figure appear in one corner. The woman had already sprinkled the house with holy water, but that had not helped. When she told her landlord what was going on, he replied: "Yes, a murder took place here a hundred years ago."
164445: In Munsterbilzen there was a house that was haunted. At midnight, three brothers of Mieke M. saw all its doors and windows fly open.
164460: A man coming back from the mill in Haren was annoyed by a cat that kept getting under his feet. When the man had kicked the cat, a woman was suddenly standing in front of him.
164466: At the B. family's house, the roller shutters on the windows moved by themselves.
164475: A man from Stokkem was going to Maastricht with a wheelbarrow full of baskets. At a crossroads a black cat suddenly jumped onto the wheelbarrow. Whatever the man did, he could not move the wheelbarrow in any way.
164480: Two farmhands from Batsheers saw a ghost in a white sheet coming towards them on a field path. When one of the farmhands struck at the apparition with a thick stick, the ghost suddenly vanished.
164481: On a farm in Opoeteren worked a farmhand who was very diligent and obedient. In the evenings, however, the farmhand often stayed out late, so that the farmer grew suspicious. The farmhand claimed he went to play cards with some friends in a neighbouring village. One day one of the farmer's children found a leather belt in an oak stump. It was the belt of the farmhand, who was in reality a werewolf. The farmer immediately lit the oven to burn the belt. Although the farmhand was far away, he was by the fire in no time to save his belt. The farmhand did not succeed. The next day the farmhand left and was never seen again.
164482: In Mulken a little boy had taken ashes from the stove to church. When the boy threw some ashes on the floor, little mice ran all over the church.
164486: The heivrouw (heath woman) was a woman in a long skirt who appeared together with a whirlwind and flattened the grain.
164494: A little boy worked for the greatest witch of Paal. That witch always had pigs and butter in abundance, while other people hardly had enough.
164499: When one drew a cross on a witch's footprints, the witch turned round.
164507: At the Pegel a white lady always appeared who vanished when one came closer.
164508: The animals of farmer Sus M. went mad under the influence of the evil hand. One day Sus saw that there was a black cat in the stable. After Sus had shut the cat out, all the animals stayed healthy.
164513: Free V.G. had a jack of spades fetch a bottle of gin. But Free was the only one who dared to drink the gin.
164521: Whenever it rained, a cat always stood on the field path. A man had often tried in vain to hit the animal. It was a witch's cat.
164523:
A farmer had bought a fine calf at the market. The farmer's wife warned her little daughter: "Make sure your aunt doesn't come near the calf." The aunt was suspected of being a witch. The daughter did not take her mother's warning seriously, and when she saw her aunt she said enthusiastically: "Look, aunt, isn't that a fine calf!" The aunt took the calf by the skin and gave it a shake. The next day the calf was ill. The farmer and his wife also had a litter of piglets. When they went to the field, they closed the door of the sty where the piglets lay, to be safe. When they came home, however, the door stood wide open. The aunt said: "There were dealers interested in the piglets. Luckily I got the doors open, so I could show them the animals." The next day the piglets crept into a corner and fell ill. After a few days they all died.
The rabbits died too, because the aunt had stroked the animals' fur.
164528:
A girl who worked as a maid at Sjattenbroeks was frightened when the light suddenly went out at eleven o'clock. She heard a sound as if a dead animal were being dragged across the floor. Five minutes later all the plates broke. Then all the windows blew open.
After relics from the friars had been placed in the farmhouse, it was no longer haunted.
164538: Charel, who always had bad luck, saw that a cat sat on the barn whenever he was threshing.
164546: On the road a ghost appeared in the form of a friar reading his breviary.
164565: Bien V. had heard from someone that his girlfriend from Hoelbeek was a witch. One day Bien was a bit early, so his girlfriend was not yet home. The young man was waiting by the window when suddenly a black cat with big eyes jumped inside. A little later the girl was standing at the window.
164574: A girl attending catechism class in Kessenich had made mice that ran through the church. When the pastor noticed, the girl said: "I can do more," and she stuck a pin in her wrist without a drop of blood flowing. The girl had probably not been baptised properly.
164592: A woman worked as a maid for a farmer in Neerweert. When the farmer and his wife were away, the maids often secretly boiled some milk without telling the farmer. Yet the farmer always found out. One day the woman looked through the keyhole. She saw a rooster sitting there, crowing nonstop. The farmer told the maid it was a ghost rooster.
164614: The cellar of a castle in Rijkel was haunted. People were chained there to a thick stone.
164630: When the area around the little castle was flooded, people had to walk on stones. Something was seen moving over the water without making a sound.
164631: In Schoten (Tessenderlo) lived a witch who could only die after the water in a cooking pot with procession strewings began to boil.
164640: A man from de Vucht could never get past a witch's house with his horse and cart, especially not when he was drunk. The man would then pray the Angelus at the gate.
164646: A shoemaker from Eigenbilzen was always jumped by the werewolf in the Brandereusweggetje. He had to carry the werewolf as far as the smith in Komfolt. The werewolf was a man who was jealous of the shoemaker because he had married the most beautiful woman in Eigenbilzen.
164649: A man out with some friends one evening suddenly met a white lady. One of the men said to the apparition: "Come on then!" The white lady then came up to the man and walked on arm in arm with him. Suddenly the lady had vanished.
164655: Moêns V.D.S. was coming back one evening from visiting his girlfriend in Ham. By a hedge Moêns met a little cat that kept rubbing against his legs. The man suspected the cat was the witch who lived a little further on, and he kicked the animal away. Some time later Moêns got an ailment in his leg that would not heal.
164656: Gin was served in the Wit Kruis in Bilzen. One day during a quarrel a man said that everyone had to go outside, or else he would make the devil come. A little later a black dog came in. The friars banished the dog to a wood near Hoeselt, which was later called the Duivelsbos (Devil's Wood).
164669: Jan T. from Duras was a werewolf. One day when the werewolf attacked a man, the man struck him on the snout, so that he lost blood. Then the werewolf changed into a human. The man recognised the werewolf at once and told his name to everyone. The priest, however, made the man take back his words in church: "People, I said that Jan T. is a werewolf. That is not true, but do watch out for him all the same!" It is also said that Jan T.'s little son said: "My father changes into a dog, and I hit him on his backside with a whip."
164670: One day Lucia said to her naughty son: "If you don't behave, I'll send the devil after you!" The boy was tired of his mother's nagging and secretly left the house. When the boy came to the church path, he saw something strange sitting on the barrier. Every time the boy lashed out at the creature, it showed its claws. The boy was so frightened that he ran back home quickly. After he had slammed the door shut, there was a loud bang. The next day the devil's five fingers were burnt into the door.
164676: A man walked in a woman's footprints to find out whether she was a witch. The witch looked round and then stood still as if nailed to the ground.
164681: A man from Rekhoven had told his wife that he would go to Hasselt with the foal the next day. The woman had replied: "No, you're not going." The next day the foal lay dead in the stable.
164689: A woman walking home one evening with her brother saw a light above the woods that followed them. It was a witch carrying a light.
164700: At the tram stop stood a small white house where a little white cat always came to sit. The children were always wild with excitement when they could play with the cat. A man who was fed up with the children's noise decided to cut the cat's head off the next time it showed up. When the cat came walking to the white house the next day, the man lashed out with his knife. The cat leapt away in fright on three legs. The next day a woman in the village lay sick in bed. She had supposedly broken her leg falling down the stairs, but the man knew better.
164712: At the stroke of midnight a black cat roamed about in the Clovenierenramen neighbourhood, chatting with passers-by. The cat was a witch.
164723: Will-o'-the-wisps moved up and down in a meadow. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
164752: Anyone who saw a black cat in the evening did not dare harm the animal, because it might be a phantom animal.
164799: It was said that a big black man with a black hat wandered around near the castle.
164811: If a magpie sat on the roof in the morning, someone in that house would soon die.
164823: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend suddenly said: "Wait here a moment, I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little later the girl saw a dog coming. As her boyfriend had advised, she threw a handkerchief at the animal's mouth. When the boy reappeared, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
164826: A woman who could not have children had a foster child from Germany or Austria. When the parents reclaimed their child after a while, the woman was beside herself with grief. At Christmas, at about seven in the morning, the woman threw herself under the tram. A few days later she was buried. A friend of the dead woman was in the habit of bringing the horse some clover in the evening in the dark. That woman had several times seen a small black figure of about eighty centimetres appear. As soon as she came outside, the figure ran away. The parish priest reassured her and advised her not to say or do anything. After the procession of the cross had passed that spot, the little black devil was never seen again.
164829: A witch came to Rutten peddling umbrellas. One day she met a little boy, to whom she said: "Watch out, boy, it's going to rain!" When the boy got home, he was completely covered in hair.
164833: A man who came to visit his girlfriend in Kleine-Brogel always saw a cat sitting on the bridge. One day the man had struck at the cat. He never wanted to tell what happened after that, but from then on he no longer dared to strike any cat.
164834: A farmer whose animals were all dying went to ask a friar for help. After the friar had blessed the stable, he said to the farmer: "Now nothing more will happen." Then the farmer bought one animal. Although the animal stayed alive, the farmer never dared to use the stable again.
164855: Near the old military road in Neeroeteren lived the Van de B. family, known for their courage. A farmer from the area always had to carry the werewolf when he came back from his field, where he had been threshing. Van de B. said fearlessly to the man: "I wish a werewolf would come to me some time." One day Van de Broek, together with Riek the Sawyer, came across a werewolf. When the werewolf stopped twenty metres away, Van de Broek said: "Come on closer, I'm waiting for you!" The werewolf laughed just like a person and made off.
164856: In the little castle of H. was a window that could not be closed up in any way. Every time a pane had been fitted in it, it lay on the ground the next day.
164863: A certain Jan from Meeuwen had lived in America for a while and had then returned to Belgium, where he settled in Broekom. When Jan was still living in America, one evening three bees swarmed around his head, singing, "Hi-ha, hi-ha, hi-ha!" The next day the same thing happened. When Jan saw the bees for the third time, he asked what they wanted. The bees were three of Jan's relatives from Meeuwen, who had come to ask him to go on pilgrimage for them.
164875: In France there used to be a gallows where people were hanged. The people who had died there came haunting after their death.
164877: Werewolves often made people carry them. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he became human again. The priest could also recognise werewolves: when he turned around and said 'dominus vobiscum', he saw all the werewolves in the church with a red flame above their heads.
164886: If at birth a child got a different godfather or godmother than the one whose turn it normally was (1), the child would meet with misfortune. A child from Heukelom got a disability that way.
164891:
A man was always followed in the evening by a black dog in the 'witches' street' behind the station.
Another man who had gone to play cards in the evening saw a cat sitting on the road on his way back. The man did not dare kick the animal and said: "Pussy, it's so late for the mush!", to which the cat said: "Yes, Jan heiligen." Frightened, the man ran away.
164896: A woman often went to work for a man who had many children. Strangely, one of the children grew sicker and sicker. After the man had placed a cross under the threshold, the cleaning woman could no longer come in. She was a witch.
164901: A man often suffered terrible pains at night when he was ridden by the maar (nightmare, mare). The man could then no longer move and felt as if his blood stood still in his veins. One day someone advised the man to take a piece of steel to bed with him. From then on the man was no longer troubled by the maar.
164906: A man returning from the fair in Lummen was followed along the way by a black cat. When the man had hit the cat on the head, the animal lay still. The man then dug a hole to bury the cat. A moment later, however, the cat jumped up and ran away. The next day the man met a woman who wore a bandage around her face. The woman said a friendly good day.
164909: In Neerrepen lived two unmarried women with their maid. One evening two beguines knocked on their door and asked if they could have a place to sleep for the night. Because the two women were very hospitable by nature, they agreed at once. The maid, however, did not trust the beguines and at night climbed onto the oven to spy on them. At midnight the beguines got up and opened a chest from which they took a human hand. On each finger of the hand they stuck a candle. Meanwhile the beguines kept talking about "the unborn hand". When the beguines went outside, the maid quickly jumped off the oven and bolted the door. The beguines found they could no longer get in and began shouting and raging. When the maid tried to put out the candles, she could not manage it. She hurried upstairs to wake her mistresses, but the women could not be woken by any means. The beguines shouted: "Give us everything back, or we will cause a great misfortune! If you pour milk on the candles, they will go out. Until the candles are put out, you will not be able to wake your mistresses." The beguines were in fact witches, who had no more power once they had lost their hand. The girl was glad to be able to throw the hand with the candles outside. At that moment the mistresses woke up.
164913: A woman had stroked a little girl's ears. Because the child cried all night from then on, the mother went to a spiritist in Liège. The man gave the mother a burning candle standing on a piece of glass. "When the candle has gone out, you must phone me," the spiritist had said. When the candle had burned down completely, the woman saw in the wax the face of the old woman she suspected. The spiritist told the mother: "You must pray a lot and you must not let the witch near your child again." After that the child slept peacefully again. One day the witch passed the house where the little girl lay asleep in a pram. When the witch threw her keys at the child, the mother immediately took the girl out of the pram. Because of this nothing could happen. One night the child was again especially restless. It also held a little statue clutched in its hands that it would not give up. The father did not want his wife to take the statue from the child. The next morning people heard that the witch had died. The child's mother went to the spiritist again, who said: "It is a good thing you did not take that statue from the child, because the witch wanted to take it with her, and then the child would have died too!"
164925: There were many cats on a farm, including a black cat. People had already advised the farmer to get rid of the black cat, but the farmer's wife could not bring herself to do it. The farmer's wife hid the black cat and often carried it in her arms. In the end the black cat drove the farmer's wife mad.
164943: Marie L. from Beringen was a witch who could cure toothache by rubbing a maggot over the bad tooth.
164948: A card-playing knight had lost a lot of money gambling. Because the knight was desperate, he made a pact with the devil, who would come to fetch his soul twenty-five years later. All his life the knight went every Saturday to offer a candle to Our Lady. When, twenty-five years later, the knight rode on horseback to the place where the devil would appear, he noticed a woman sitting behind him on his horse. Because the knight had already been waiting in vain for the devil for half an hour, he asked: "Well, aren't you coming to take my soul now?" The devil answered: "If you put that woman sitting behind you on your horse on the ground, then we will come, but not before." The card-playing knight realised that Our Lady had ridden along with him to save him.
164951: A midwife going home at night met a black dog that frightened her.
164961: A cowherd from Geisteren went with a friend to buy Dutch piglets in Weert. The boy did not want to leave without his pocketknife. When after a few hours the pair reached the Kindersendijk, the cowherd suddenly noticed that the cart had stopped. His friend was nowhere to be seen. Suddenly the cowherd heard a rustling in the hedges. After a while the friend reappeared in human form. The cowherd then said: "Go on, from now on you walk in front, or else I'll take out my pocketknife," to which his friend replied: "But I just went to relieve myself." The cowherd knew better, however; he never went anywhere with his friend again.
164963: Two men saw a ghost on a small field path. After one of the men struck at the apparition, the ghost vanished.
164980: When V. was coming back from a visit to P. in Aldeneik, a big cat suddenly jumped in front of him. The cat meowed the whole time and followed the man all the way to his house.
164985: Some men were standing by a cow that was about to calve. Because there was a black cat in the stable, one of the men said: "Chase that cat outside!" Another man took a dung fork and struck the animal on the head, whereupon a loud witch's scream rang out. As soon as the cat was outside, the cow gave birth to her calf. The next day the farmer's wife had only one eye left.
164988: In Lauw a silent black woman with rustling clothes wandered about. Because people were afraid of the apparition, the woman was caught: it turned out to be a man from Troot wearing women's clothes.
164990: Some men taking a cart full of piglets to Tongeren saw an oncoming vehicle near the Heilige Haag. The men did not move aside, however. A little later the cart coming from the opposite direction flew up into the air. A great fire appeared above the village.
164994: Near the Brustem gate lived a girl who was always ill. A witch regularly came there to ask for something the family did not have. A clergyman determined that the child was bewitched and advised the father to go to the church of Grivegné. When the man left the church, the child was dead.
164995: A child coming home from school had an apple with it, which it had been given by a woman. The child's mother said: "Just put that apple on the mantelpiece until your father comes home." Because the mother kept hearing a noise inside the apple, she cut the fruit open. Inside the apple was a toad. If the child had eaten the apple, it would have turned into a toad.
165012: Three women who were talking next to the churchyard suddenly saw a ghost in a white sheet appear behind a gravestone. When the ghost cried: "Today me, tomorrow you!", the women ran away as fast as they could.
165015: In the old days people were very afraid of the werewolf. It often jumped on people and made them carry it for a while. One day a man collapsed, exhausted, after he had had to carry the werewolf.
165028: Behind a farm lay a fen that was haunted. In summer, music was always heard by the water, as if flute players were sitting there. One day the parish priest poured a bottle of holy water into the fen. Since then the music has not been heard again.
165029: At a school in Kleine-Brogel there was a girl who could make mice appear from a handkerchief. The girl had learned her tricks from an old woman she had spied on through the keyhole. The old woman was teaching witchcraft to her daughter because otherwise she could not die. The priest immediately freed the girl from Kleine-Brogel from witchcraft.
165042: Three boys of the V. family had seen a little squirrel climbing in the trees in the woods. The boys tried to knock the animal down with a club. The next moment a woman in a black hood stood behind them and said: "Leave that little animal alone!" It was a witch who could change herself into a squirrel.
165047: Huberte's horses were completely covered in sweat in the mornings. Something came in through the keyhole, making a buzzing sound. One evening they managed to swat the bumblebee dead. The next day a woman with a bad reputation had died in the village.
165051: When Graad J. was out poaching around midnight, he saw a whole troop of cats go by. The man was so frightened that he went straight back home.
165065: Whenever Frey was alone, he always saw a row of cats sitting on the barrier by the church. As soon as he had made the sign of the cross, the cats were gone.
165084: A pharmacist used to live on the Koerselsesteenweg in Beringen. One day the pharmacist had to deliver medicines to Beverlo. On the way back the man's horse suddenly could not go any further. The man was tormented so badly that he lay in bed for a week.
165097: Some people asked a witch the way at night. But when the people followed the witch's directions, they kept coming back to the same chapel. When they had made the sign of the cross at the chapel, morning came and they found their way again.
165117: A man who saw a cat sitting on a post in the meadow said: "Pussy, pussy", to which the cat replied: "Had Janneke not spoken so nicely, we would have broken his neck."
165119: In Trekschuren near Hasselt, a strange dog blocked the way of passers-by.
165129: Manus and another man had to mow the grass for a farmer. Because it was very hot during the day, they decided to go at night: they would set off at twelve o'clock. When it was already one o'clock and his friend still had not shown up, Manus set off alone. He had only just started working when a white cat came and sat beside him. Manus then decided to start at the other corner of the field, but after a few minutes the cat was sitting there. After moving a few more times, Manus became frightened and quickly ran home.
165144:
Witches sometimes stuck pins into a little doll to torment children.
Witches could not die until a priest had taken over their arts.
165147: A man went to Hasselt every Friday to sell his butter to a Walloon woman. One day the woman spat out the butter and cried: "That's from a sour cow!" On his sister's advice the man went to the friars of Hasselt. One of the friars read something in a book and then said: "I don't have the power for that. I'll call another friar." Another friar said that T. was responsible for the misfortune and advised the man to give the cows a piece of blessed bread and to pray nine paternosters for five days. After that the milk no longer went sour.
165148: In Maasmechelen lived a boy who always had to carry the werewolf. The boy did not dare resist the werewolf.
165153: If you could make a werewolf bleed, he changed back into a human. A man from Winterslag who was walking through the woods was suddenly jumped by a werewolf.
165155: Although nothing strange could be seen, the animals in B.'s cowshed were always untied at about the same time. One day someone went into the shed to ask what the ghost wanted. It turned out to be a dead daughter of a former occupant of the farm. The woman wanted Masses to be said for her. Once that had been done, the shed was no longer haunted.
165156: A boy who was coming back from the fair with his girlfriend said to her: "I'm going away for a moment. If you see a big dog coming, you must throw a handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been told. When her boyfriend came back a few hours later, she saw that the threads of the cloth were still hanging between his teeth. The girl left the boy at once. She told everyone what had happened to her. On the farm where the boy worked, people found a collar and a pot of ointment, which they threw into the oven. While everything was in the fire, the boy came running up. The boy jumped into the oven and burned up there.
165182: A man was tired of a neighbour woman always coming to borrow his tools. Whenever he needed a tool himself, he always had to go and fetch it. When the family refused to lend her anything the next time, she cried: "I'll get you yet!" In revenge the woman bewitched the family's child.
165183: People who were making butter found chaff in their churn instead of butter.
165191: A man who had no money to build a house sold his soul to the devil. The devil would build the man a house during the night, to be finished before the cock crowed in the morning. If the devil succeeded, he would get the man's soul. When the man saw the busy little devils at work in the night, he became frightened and confessed everything to his wife. "Just wait!", the wife replied. She went upstairs, opened a window and imitated a cock crowing. The next moment the little devils had all vanished. There was still a hole in the roof of the house that had to be closed. The man, however, never managed to close it.
165205: A white calf used to haunt the paved road in Genenbos.
165213: Every evening a farmer saw a will-o'-the-wisp flying around his farm. The man was convinced that a treasure chest was hidden somewhere on his land. When the farmer began digging in his garden one day, he did indeed find a chest, but there was no money in it.
165222: A witch made the animals in a stable fall flat on the ground. The farmer then said to the witch: "If you do that again, I'll stick the dung fork in your belly!"
165233: In Vliermaal a sow lay with her piglets in the sty. Strangely, a large pair of scissors always came at the piglets to stab them to death. After the sty had been blessed with prayers, nothing strange happened anymore.
165258:
Just past the border of Tricht-Wolder lay a meadow where the witches came to dance on Mondays. At midnight a hunchback came by and heard the witches sing: "Monday, Tuesday". He answered: "Wednesday". As a reward for his answer the witches freed the hunchback of his hump, which they hung in an apple tree. The next day the lucky man told another hunchback what had happened to him. The other decided to go to the witches' meadow too. When the witches sang: "Monday, Tuesday", the hunchback answered: "Wednesday and Thursday". At that the head of the witches said: "Take that hump out of the apple tree and give it to this man. Then he'll have two".
The lucky man had always heard the priest boast about his fine wine, and so he wanted to visit the priest's wine cellar himself. The man said: "Over trees and hawthorns to the priest's wine cellar". Once he had arrived, the man helped himself to the priest's wine. The hunchback also wanted to go to that wine cellar and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the priest's wine cellar". The poor man was covered in blood and was found the next day by the priest's maid.
165261:
A witch had come to visit a house where a baby lay in the cradle. When the witch had left, they found the cradle full of maggots. They changed the bedding and put different clothes on the child. A few weeks later the witch visited again, after which the cradle was again full of maggots.
The incident was probably due to the lack of hygiene at the time. Instead of mattresses people used straw sacks, which were always a breeding ground for fleas and lice.
165264:
In the past a witch lived in Mulken who made animals die everywhere. Sometimes she also bewitched children. When people had misfortune because they were under the influence of the evil hand, they went to the clergy in Liège. They showed the witch's face in a bucket of water and then said a prayer to neutralise the witch's power.
On the Mulkebaan lived a family who had just had twins. The girl was perfectly healthy, but the little boy became seriously ill. So the parents went for advice to a fortune-teller in Seraing, who said: "Madam, your little son will recover. The misfortune was caused by a woman who lives on the Mulkebaan. Take this medal and put it under the barrier, so that the witch can no longer get through". Every day the witch went with another woman to fetch food for the rabbits. But when the medal was under the barrier, the witch had to take another route. She said to her friend, who was already further ahead: "Come, let's fetch food for the rabbits somewhere else. There's nothing left there anyway." The witch never came back after that. The parents cut open the pillow from the little boy's bed and found one hundred and eleven pins in it. After that the child quickly recovered.
165281: Some women returning from the mission in Kermt saw a nun on the way who called: "Avoid me, avoid me, or I'll run you down." The next moment one of the women felt a stab in her foot, so that her clog was completely filled with blood.
165287: A man came home panting and sweating, saying: "I had to carry the werewolf!" Because the others laughed at him, the man took them outside. In the snow the man's footprints were still clearly visible. Of the werewolf there were no tracks.
165290: A man walking to the village along a field path in the evening was suddenly surrounded by a pack of cats that blocked his way. When the man had made the sign of the cross, the cats were gone.
165299: At the home of Mieke B. in Molenstede lived a girl who was bewitched. In the house clothes flew around and stones were thrown through the ceiling. A man who wanted to go and see what was wrong with the girl met two tough friends on the way, who advised him not to enter the house. But the man was not deterred. He tried to hold the girl, but she kept flying back and forth. The bewitched girl gradually wasted away.
165303: A man travelling by coach with a canon saw a will-o'-the-wisp in the distance. The canon advised the man not to look at the will-o'-the-wisp, or else he would lose his way. The man was also not allowed to whistle at the light, or else it would get him. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. When you had the chance, you had to sprinkle will-o'-the-wisps with water.
165323: A German soldier stayed the night with a couple in Genk. The soldier, however, had bewitched the woman, so her husband had to have prayers read over her by a friar from Hasselt.
165330: A blacksmith from Gotem had a baby that cried all the time. His sister-in-law advised him to throw away the child's pillow, because it might be bewitched. At first the parents refused, but when they were truly at their wits' end, they took the pillow out of the cot. They cut it open and found dozens of roses in all colours. The parents wanted to burn the pillow in the meadow, but the fabric would not burn. Then they made a cross over the pillow with holy water and threw it into the blacksmith's fire.
165340: Anyone ridden by the 'moor' (nightmare spirit) at night could no longer move. As soon as one made the sign of the cross, one was set free.
165343: People used to think that the sjoofet was the ghost of a dead person who could find no rest in the hereafter and therefore had to wander about.
165347: In Rutten lived a little boy who could make mice from a handful of earth. The little boy had not been baptised properly.
165350: Two poachers went hare hunting one evening. One of the poachers shot a hare and put it in a sack. When a second hare turned up, the gun did not go off. The next attempt to hit the animal also failed. The hare sat up on its hind legs and said: "Say Hans, where are you?", to which the shot hare replied: "In the sack, but I'm ready to leave." The shot hare had bitten through the sack and the other hare said: "Then let's run off together." The next moment the two hares had vanished.
165352: The dead who had promised something or had stolen something during their lives had to come back after their death to keep their promise or to atone for their theft.
165357: A man rode his bicycle past the house of a witch. A little later a cat jumped onto the handlebars. When the man came to a bend, the cat jumped back onto the ground. The witch had turned herself into a cat.
165360: A farmhand and his master, returning from the woods with a cart and three horses, suddenly could not go any further. At the crossroads two women in blue aprons stood leaning against a pine tree. After the men had unhitched two horses, the remaining horse came towards them all by itself with the whole load. Meanwhile the two witches had disappeared.
165361: A man from Schulen had a daughter who lived as a witch in Brussels. On her deathbed the woman refused to confess. After her death the father saw a black dog.
165376: Someone who had spied on a werewolf discovered that the werewolf had hidden a straw band in a hollow tree stump. While the band was being burnt, the werewolf walked about restlessly. After that he was released.
165384: Mina the witch always went to rest on the same stone by the Motvaart. One day Mina asked a woman for a slice of bread. The woman, however, refused to give the witch anything. The next day the woman's daughter struck her foot against the stone Mina always sat on. Because of this the girl was paralysed for the rest of her life.
165410: A man returning from the fair in Schulen got lost. In the end the man had to be brought home by a sorcerer who had power over witches.
165411: A man walking home one evening under a full moon heard a hollow tree humming.
165418: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. The lights appeared by the water so that people would baptise them.
165420: The dead owner of the castle of Machelen always came haunting at night in a fiery coach.
165431: A man whose stable was haunted always heard a lot of noise and found that the cows were jumping about all the time. Because the man always saw a black cat coming out of the stable, he went to the friars. After the man had placed a relic under the threshold of the stable, the haunting stopped.
165438: In the cellar of the castle of Jonckhold stood a chest on which a black dog sat. Because people were afraid of that dog, nobody dared to take the chest away.
165442: In a shop by the church of Dilsen a witch had given a girl lice. The little man of Genk advised the people to go on a pilgrimage.
165465: An altar boy from Romershoven always ran errands for the priest. On the way the boy was followed by a hare that jumped between his legs. Every time he struck at the hare, the animal had suddenly vanished.
165493: When people went to mass in the morning, a little black cat always sat by an old farm at about the same time. Because the cat made a strange noise and had glowing eyes, people no longer dared to pass by and took another road. Some time later that strange cat also appeared on that road.
165500: When Pier worked as a farmhand at the Hobos, the horses were always untied and the animals ran about foaming at the mouth.
165504: Whenever the witch Netje C. had been in a stable, the animals soon fell ill. To protect the farm against the witch, people then put a relic of the holy paterke (little friar) under the threshold.
165506: In Meeuwen a girl saw a fine hare lying in the garden. Her father said she could take the dead hare out of the garden and keep it in the cellar for the priest. When the priest came by a few hours later, however, the hare had disappeared. It must have been a witch.
165509: A man from Velm was drinking beer with friends. When the police came to arrest the company, he assured his friends they had nothing to worry about. The policemen found nothing but stoves in the inn and returned empty-handed. The man had learned his tricks from special books. He could also, for example, walk up the wall or turn a glass upside down without spilling a drop.
165514: At Tingerhoeve worked a farmhand who could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmer sent his farmhand to Maastricht. Meanwhile the farmer went to take the werewolf's collar out of the tree stump to burn it. The moment the collar caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his possession.
165530: In the evening, will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in the fields. They were the souls of the dead who had to haunt because they had done something wicked or because their relatives had not kept a promise.
165534: When the children held a torch procession on the feast of Saint Martin, a ghost's voice called from the hedge: "Don't set my little wig on fire!"
165536:
When a man with a hay cart drove past an old woman's house in Vechmaal, she cried: "That cart will tip over yet!" A little further on the cart did indeed tip over.
Later it turned out that the woman's daughter was also a witch.
165554: In the old days the farmers went to work at night on the field Bedeuj. Often black cats as big as people came, who sang the whole time and helped the farmers with their work.
165573: In the past witches often went about in the shape of a cat or a rat.
165585: A man who had been to visit his girlfriend in Leut had to carry the werewolf over the dike at the Kruiskes (?).
165587: In Corswarem there once lived a man who could turn himself into a foal.
165594: On Kerkedries between Nerem and Sluizen a friar with a prayer book haunted the place. One night the ghost said to a drunken passer-by: "The day for you and the night for me."
165613: A dead farmhand haunted the Pekelshof because he had not kept a vow. Because the maid had already seen the ghost three or four times, she went to the priest for advice. The clergyman advised her to ask the ghost what it wanted the next time. The ghost also had to give a sign, and the maid had to hold a white cloth in her hands. The ghost burned its hand into the cloth and was released.
165614: Clemens V. and Felix T. were coming back from Ham. In a hedge on the Binnenveld, the men heard something calling: "Heu!" Because the calling would not stop, Felix shouted: "Let him go to the devil, damn it!" The next moment all the branches tore off the trees behind the men.
165626: A woman coming back in the evening from the café at Piannes was accompanied by her future husband. Suddenly the woman saw a dog with eyes like saucers coming towards her. Although the man did not see the dog at all, he had to carry the frightened woman home.
165627: A woman had joined the Freemasons together with her brother, a lawyer. Before her younger sister made her Solemn Communion, she received from the priest a host that had not been consecrated. The girl laughed and said to the priest: "Oh, I've often had an unconsecrated host from my sister." The priest immediately understood that the girl's sister must be a member of the lodge. So the priest went to speak with the woman to convert her. But the woman replied: "If I convert, then either I or the person who converted me will not live much longer." Since then the woman was never seen again.
165643: A witch once lived in Tongerlo. One day two boys went looking for birds when they met the witch. The woman said: "Wait a moment! I have some fine beans here; you should plant them." But Jozef warned his friend: "Be careful, that's a witch!" He knew the woman was a witch from Jacob F., who had once eaten rice pudding from her. The next day Jacob was completely covered in lice.
165648: Whenever G. was drunk, he always saw a black dog walking with a chain. Fonske S. always saw that dog too.
165651:
One day a widow with three sons secretly hid the money case of a passing gentleman in a hedge. A while later the gentleman came back and asked: "Have you seen my case anywhere, madam? My life and that of eight others depend on it, for I have a very strict master". The woman lied: "No, I have seen nothing". The woman often went to pray to Mary at the little chapel on the road to Hasselt. When the woman lay dying, her youngest son asked what he should do with the money. "Keep what you have and I will suffer what I can", the woman answered. After the woman had died, people often saw a glowing figure appear near the hedge. When a glowing ghost was seen sitting in front of the chapel with its arms stretched out, the priest went to fetch some altar boys and some holy water. Then the priest exorcised the ghost and banished it to a bush with a chain.
The people were so afraid of the ghost that they all got 'de bevers' (the shivers). That is how the name Beverst came about.
The village of Schoonbeek owed its name to the beautiful brook that flowed there.
165669: If one had seen a black cat at night and was ill the next day, that cat had probably been a witch.
165680: Two soldiers went to spend the night in an empty house that was said to be haunted. During the night a lady came into the house and lured them to the cellar. The bravest soldier went with her. The lady showed him three chests filled with money and said: "One chest is for you, one for the community and one for the owner of this house." Then the haunting lady was released.
165691: A man from Herk-de-Stad got lost after he had met a witch.
165692: A man returning one evening from a visit to the beekeepers on the Krootsberg and the Hiësbeek suddenly heard a strange rushing sound. He saw a burning wheel flying through the air, past the Kikvijver and the Heulenteuleberg as far as the Asserweg. The man was so frightened that he could not remember the words of the Gospel of Saint John. Suddenly the wheel flew towards Neeroeteren. A little later the man could no longer see it.
165696: A man who got up in the morning found, to his great surprise, that his horses had been saddled.
165711: Will-o'-the-wisps were seen mainly near marshes. People who looked at a will-o'-the-wisp often got lost. Some people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
165714: A hunter walking home around midnight saw a foal lying on the road. When the man tried to pass the foal, it stood up and blocked his way. The hunter struck at the foal, after which the animal cried: "Hunter, strike again if you dare!"
165717: Werewolves were often recognised by their girlfriend when she had thrown a red handkerchief at the beast. When the werewolf then turned up again in human form, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
165738: There was a ghost horse near Betho.
165755: An old woman was allowed to shelter in a house during heavy rain. Inside, the woman stroked a little child on the back. Although the child had never been ill, it died shortly afterwards.
165763: A farmhand who had to go somewhere with a cart and two horses met a witch on the way who asked him something. When the farmhand wanted to go on, the horses stubbornly stood still. Only four hours later could the farmhand go on again.
165774: A man going from Borgloon to Buskhoven was followed by a cat all the way to his house. When the man was home, the cat said: "If Jantje K. had not spoken freely, I would have broken his neck." The man is said to have said "pussy" to the cat.
165777: A dying farmer decided to draw up a will in favour of his best farmhand. The farmhand would inherit everything on condition that he married the farmer's wife. During the funeral the farmer's wife told her cousin everything. Together they decided to hide the will under a tree next to the house. From the day the farmer's wife married her cousin, she always had bad luck. Finally the woman had a friar come to the horse stable. The friar suspected something was not right and had the farmhand accompany him. Around two o'clock at night a violent wind blew in the stable and three horses dropped dead. When the friar came back the next day, he found a small hole in the wall. On the third day the friar said to the farmhand: "The ghost will come between midnight and one o'clock. When we hear the wind blowing, you must strike with an axe past that hole in the wall." The farmhand did as the friar had told him. When the friar and the farmhand went inside, the farmer's wife could no longer find her husband. He was lying on his bed with a cut in his neck. The man confessed his guilt and had everything he had obtained unjustly destroyed. He told the farmer's wife to dig up the will and marry the farmhand.
165799: In the past witches often made children ill with their evil hand. The child usually recovered after prayers had been read over it or after the parents had gone on pilgrimage.
165819: A woman on her way with a cart of herring met an old woman, who said: "Don't turn your cart, mind!" The woman turned the cart anyway. Two steps further the cart fell over, so that all the herring fell on the ground.
165825: A young man from Hasselt had to go into the army for four years against his will. After two years of service the man deserted and went to Germany. After thirteen years the man went back to Hasselt, where he stayed with his parents without making himself known. At night the people murdered their guest, not knowing it was their son. The body was buried under a pear tree. The next morning the neighbour asked: "Wasn't your son here?", but the people claimed they had not seen their son for years. Because the murdered boy came to haunt for years, his descendants finally went on a pilgrimage to Rome. But the pilgrims got lost and the last descendant of the murdered boy died in the mountains of Switzerland.
165827: Between midnight and one o'clock a woman in a silk dress came to the cemetery. The woman could not be seen, but the rustling of her dress could be heard.
165831: It was said that Mit was a witch. Near Mit's house stood a tree that was very often full of cats. One evening five women were seen going into her house. Some people went to look through the window out of curiosity: although no one else was there apart from the boy who lay sleeping, they clearly saw six cups on the table. The curious onlookers lay down behind the hedge, where a while later they saw the six witches come out and then suddenly vanish. When Mit lay on her deathbed, she could not die because she first had to pass her powers on to someone else. The priest said she should give the arts to her daughter, so that he could take them away from her later. The witch gave her daughter a book. But when the priest came back, the daughter no longer wanted to hand over the book, because she had already learned things from it and had had so much fun with the other witches.
165846: One evening a man was followed by as many as ten cats all the way to the house of the witch Trui S.
165849: In a café where people behaved badly, a black dog lay under the table.
165858:
A farmer who had just bought a new cow was visited by a woman who stroked the animal's back and said: "That cow will never give milk." The woman was right. Earlier the witch had also put lice somewhere. The pastor advised the farmer to put a relic under the threshold so that the witch could no longer come in.
In Geetbets there also lived a witch who made animals die and sent fleas and lice. Yet that witch always prayed a novena for the children.
165873: To recognise a witch, one had to place one's feet crosswise on her footprints. If the woman in question was a witch, she could go no further.
165881: A man had a child that had been struck by the evil hand. The child always lay crying at night and was full of vermin. After the man had gone on pilgrimage for the child, it recovered.
165887: A witch conjured up tailless mice from a molehill.
165897: Next to a farm lay a ditch overgrown with branches. At midnight the farmer saw the branches bend down and heard a loud cracking. Because he was afraid, the farmer sat on the plough until one o'clock. Then the hedge straightened up again.
165899: A man from Sint-Truiden who had an ailment in his throat often went to pray at the statue of Saint Marcoen in the Monnebrurenkerk. One day the man saw that he was being followed into the church by Bet L. The man then gave the witch a good thrashing. In court the man lost his case, but he was cured of his ailment.
165905: A man was followed by so many cats that he no longer knew where to go.
165906: Every night a will-o'-the-wisp was seen by the Rulbeek, a river in Holbeek. A boy from Donk who was studying to be a priest wanted to baptise the will-o'-the-wisp. When he had poured water over the light, an unbaptised man suddenly stood before him. The boy was so frightened that he died of fear.
165911: People believed that the late C. came haunting in the woods around his castle. Some claimed that a ghost dog also roamed the woods.
165912: The ghost of the drossaard (bailiff) Clerckx was banished by the parish priest of Overpelt to the bridge of Kerkhoven. In the evening chains could be heard rattling there.
165926: When someone had shot a hare, the other hares began to talk or whistle. Whoever was afraid left everything behind and never found it again.
165929: A girl whose mother had died slept alone in the house at night. One night the girl saw her mother appear before her bed. At first the girl thought she had dreamed it, but when it happened every night, the child became frightened. The girl sought advice from a friar, who asked her: "Did you put a shirt on your mother before she was buried?", to which the girl answered "No". The friar told her: "When your mother appears again, you must throw a shirt over her." When the girl had done so, the ghost stayed away.
165933: A man came to a farm to fetch buttermilk. "You'll certainly get some buttermilk", said the woman, "but you'll have to wait a while, because we still have to churn". However hard the maid tried, she could not make butter. When the maid saw a big black cat sitting in the stable, she poured a small pan of boiling water over the animal. That same evening they saw that the neighbour woman's face was completely burned.
165944: A farmer from Niel-bij-As had a farmhand who slept in the horse stable with the cowherd. The cowherd, who grew thinner and thinner, said to the farmhand: "If you had to do what I have to do, you'd get thin too!" At night the farmhand was visited by a woman with whom he had to ride on horseback to Aachen. The next night the farmhand stayed awake to drive the woman off with the dung fork. When the boys were having breakfast the next morning, the farmhand asked the farmer: "Is the farmer's wife still asleep?", to which the farmer replied: "No, something's wrong with her arm". It was the farmer's wife who had to go to the witches' fair in Aachen every night.
165951: A farmer who had lost ten sheep one after another went, on B.'s advice, to K. in Genk. The 'menneke' (little man) of Genk said: "If you have already lost so many sheep, the misfortune will stop now." K. went with the man to his sheep pen. "Let me see one of the lambs," said K. When the farmer lifted a weak lamb, it could suddenly walk again. "You have been struck by the evil hand," said K., "but I will put an end to it. Think of me again after Saint Lambert's day." From then on the farmer had no more misfortune.
165952: When Bloknoke was waiting at the window of his girlfriend in Hoelbeek, he saw that the girl was not home. A little later two cats jumped inside through the window. The next moment the girl and her mother were at home after all.
165960: In Lutselus a man appeared and said to a passer-by: "If you come back here, I will share with you." When beautiful music could be heard at midnight, a human leg fell from the sky.
165963: One day Turkish slaves lay before the statue of Mary in the basilica of Tongeren. Mary had freed the prisoners. The slaves' chains hung for a long time at the altar of Our Lady.
165968: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen between Wijshagen and Opglabbeek. They were the souls of children who found no rest because they had died unbaptised.
165969: A baby had been lying ill in its cradle for a long time when they decided to cut open the pillow from the cradle. In the pillow they found a wreath of feathers. Luckily the wreath was not yet closed, or the child would have died. People believed the wreath had been woven by a witch.
165972: A shoemaker had offered to keep watch at night over a dead neighbour on condition that he could go on working in the meantime. While the shoemaker was working, the dead man suddenly sat up and said: "One does not work beside a dead man." The shoemaker replied: "And a dead man does not speak," and he threw his hammer at the dead man's head, who was now dead for good.
165978: An old man saw a zwarte moek lying in the middle of the road. That was an ugly black ghost. The man knocked the ghost off the road with his cudgel, saying: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, get out of the way." When the ghost rolled into the ditch, the man could continue on his way.
165993: One day a boy who lived on the Hal came to Wullem terrified, crying: "Wullem, Wullem, help me, it's haunted here!" Brave Wullem went outside and saw a white ghost floating. At the sight of the apparition, the two boys ran away in fear.
165996: A young man could make mice from a little heap of earth. After the dean had read prayers over the young man, he could no longer make mice.
165998: A man from Ordingen worked in a factory in Sint-Truiden. In the evening he came home on the last train. One evening in the Zwartveld he saw a troop of cats dancing and mewing. They went to the chapel of Ordingen, where they held their witches' dance.
166000: A woman taking the cows to the meadow found little balls of yarn on the ground. One was not allowed to touch the balls, or something terrible would happen.
166008: The card-playing knight sold his soul to the devil to get money. Saint Gertrude helped the man.
166012: A man who had read in a book of magic made a woman stand still one Sunday. When the man read the text from the book backwards, the woman could move on again.
166020: Every evening on his way home a man was followed by a black cat. The cat walked with him as far as the house of an old woman. When the old woman died, the cat had vanished without a trace.
166025: A witch had used her powers to make a girl from the neighbourhood infertile.
166033: Frisse, the steward of Vogelsang castle, kept sowing more and more fir trees, since every place where firs had been sown belonged to the Vogelsang estate. After his death Frisse came back to haunt. The priest of Hasselt or the one of Diest banished Frisse to a brook, where a hermitage had to be built specially.
166041: A German went to work on a farm where a cow was about to calve. To pass the time the German played cards with some men. Suddenly the card players heard a clattering in the attic as if witches were walking around in clogs. When they went to look, they found there was nothing to see. As soon as the men were downstairs, they heard a clattering in the cellar room. It was witches roaming about.
166059: When one was ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night, one could not call out or move. If one had not put a chair beside one's bed, the maar could ride one.
166077: In Koninksem lived a witch who was called 'Kwakkelgon'. That witch often handed out sweets to the children. One day a little boy from the village suddenly could make little mice. During catechism class the children told the priest. The clergyman then immediately read prayers over the little boy.
166080: Witches sometimes harmed dogs and cats when they wanted to spare the people.
166089: The great-grandfather of a man from Maaseik was a butcher who always got up very early in the morning. Before starting work, the man went to relieve himself on the dung heap. On the dung heap the man had often felt something or someone jump onto his neck. One morning the butcher stabbed the apparition in the head with his knife. A moment later a man stood before him with a wound on his forehead. The unmasked werewolf said: "You must come and fetch a number of sacks of corn and wheat from us, and you may not tell anyone what you have experienced." The butcher did as he was asked and told nothing to his curious wife. On his deathbed, however, the butcher did write down the account of what had happened.
166097: A farmer at Geneuth had a farmhand who went out every evening. One day the farmhand's skin was found in a tree. Then the farmhand was sent away so that the skin could be burnt in the meantime. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand stood by the oven.
166099: A man who had moved the boundary post of a field came back to haunt after his death, asking: "Where shall I put it?" One day someone answered: "Where you fetched it from." With that the ghost was released.
166103: The Wit Paard in Waltwilder was haunted. The ghost made the doors fly open and then flew to the cellar. The friars came to sprinkle the corners of the house with holy water. They left one corner open and then said: "Go on, damned soul!" When the friar afterwards went to confession, the Holy Little Father of Hasselt said: "You did not do it quite right. You should have asked the ghost where the treasures in the cellar lay." After that, people went digging in the cellar. Those people probably did find a treasure, because a short time later they built a house of stone.
166115: A sixteen-year-old boy walked from Opitter to Maastricht to visit his sister. Because it had begun to snow heavily in the evening, the boy had to stay the night with his sister. He slept in the attic in the bed where the late syrup maker used to sleep. After a while the doors suddenly flew open and an invisible ghost came in, making a great deal of noise and starting to throw sacks about. The ghost came and stood menacingly by the boy's bed and a little later went away again. In the morning the boy and his sister found that the sacks the ghost had thrown weighed more than five hundred kilos. People said the ghost was a dead man who had to return because he had stolen a great deal during his life. That was why the dead man had to come and weigh the sacks of grain.
166127: A man who had moved a boundary post had to haunt after his death. The ghost kept asking: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" One day a drunkard answered the ghost's question. Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
166144: In Beek, people had sent for a clergyman to exorcise their bewitched house. The priest from Weert had to walk through water all night before he reached those people.
166149: Two poachers went rabbit hunting in the woods. Suddenly, for no clear reason, all the branches began to crack so loudly that hunting was no longer possible.
166151: When the forester of Rummen was walking home at night, he suddenly heard a calf bawling behind him. The man looked back, but he saw nothing. A little further on the man heard the calf bawling again. Perhaps it was a ventriloquist.
166165: In Wellen lived a man who could make mice from some sand and dust lying on the floor.
166173: Pol C. boasted that he had slept so well the night before that he had heard nothing of the thunderstorm. At that Fien van de Z. said: "From now on you won't sleep so well." Indeed, the following nights Pol did not sleep a wink. In the end Pol went to ask the witch to stop her teasing. Although Fien answered that she could not, from that day Pol slept well again.
166180: A rooster dealer once sank in the Waterbroeck. At twelve o'clock on Christmas night rooster crowing and bell ringing could still be heard there.
