166186: A man was walking through the Bouquetstraat by moonlight when he suddenly saw a frog come out of the beets. The man stamped at the frog. The next moment a cat appeared among the beets. It must have been a witch.
166191: A woman cycling home at night was held back in the woods by a strange force. After trying twice, the woman decided to ride home by another road.
166192: A witch regularly visited the H. family. After a while the child began to cry every day and got red marks all over, as if someone had been beating it. When they no longer let the old woman in, the child stayed calm.
166205: A farmer from Wijchmaal sometimes saw a man in the evening who rode through the field and took some of the hay. One evening the farmer saw it again and called out: "Homo duvelsklo, leave that or take me with you!" When the farmer saw the man coming at him at full speed, he ran home as fast as he could. A little later the farmer heard a loud blow on the door. The devil had burnt his hand into the door.
166209: A man from Kuringen wanted to rent a house on the Kiewit. A woman who lived on Termien also wanted the house, but she did not get it because people suspected she was a witch. In revenge the witch said to the new tenant: "I will drive all the rats of Tulpin to your house!" When the man wanted to bring in his harvest, he found to his great dismay that all the grain had been eaten by rats.
166212: A woman who saw something strange floating above the bushes said in fright: "If you are from God, stay. If you are from the devil, go away." Then the strange apparition vanished.
166214: Two men from Balen coming back in the evening from the Vennen in Kerkhoven met a black dog in the woods. Only one of the two men could see the dog. That man was so frightened that he no longer wanted to come along the next time. When the other man went alone the next time, he could see the dog and threw a stone at the beast. The next moment the dog turned into a ball of fire. At that the man turned around and ran home as fast as he could.
166227: A man threw boiling water over the black cats that danced around his house every evening. The next day many women from the village had burns, including the man's wife.
166228: The werewolf was an ordinary person who owned a collar. He sat behind a bush or in a bend in the road so he could jump on passers-by unexpectedly. After the werewolf had had himself carried a little way, he left his victim alone.
166234: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to go away for a bit, but I'll be right back. If you should meet a dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did what her boyfriend had advised. When the boy came back a while later, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
166263: A werewolf was sent to Sittard with a horse and cart so that his band could be burnt in the meantime. The werewolf had to be held so that he would not jump into the fire to save the band. When everything had burnt up, the werewolf was released.
166265: A woman was herding the cows at the cow post by the Vossenkuil when hoarse Trijn suddenly came by. At that moment the cow began to jump about restlessly. When the witch had gone, the cow gave no more milk and a cat was sitting on the cow post.
166286: Trien M. could make rats and mice. When the witch was dying, she lay shouting and raging the whole time. The priest could not help Trien. Fortunately Trien's daughter took over her mother's arts, so the woman could die peacefully after all.
166289: Because a strange glow was often seen at Kolmont castle in Tongeren, people suspected a treasure was buried there. Mr B., the owner of the castle at the time, went to an exorcist for advice. The exorcist established that a treasure was indeed hidden there, but to find it he needed the help of a young girl. A girl from Vreeren came, was bewitched by the exorcist and then had to start digging. When the girl had dug for a while and thought she saw the chest, a large black dog jumped up, making the chest fall back down. This happened several times. Because the girl became exhausted from digging, the exorcist read a text from a strange book, so the girl could carry on working. Because of the black dog, however, she did not manage to get hold of the chest. That evening, when everyone had stopped searching, the exorcist came back alone to take the chest away. The girl died a few days later.
166317: When Peterke went to play cards, he told his friends that he always had to carry the werewolf. "He jumps on me and puts his paws on my shoulders. Those paws are as thick as cushions." His friends said: "You must grab the werewolf by his paws and drag him inside." Peterke tried it, but the werewolf threw him against the door.
166318: A man going to mass on Christmas Eve saw a burning phantom coach drive past at a terrifying speed.
166321: A girl told the parish priest that her dead mother came haunting every night. When the priest began to pray, the ghost vanished. After that it never came back.
166347: A black dog often sat in the Groemelingenstraat in Neerrepen. One day Frederik and Nol were returning from the tailor with their dog. In the Groemelingenstraat they saw a strange glow. Their dog, which usually always ran ahead, was very frightened and walked behind the men. A little further on they saw something fly away from the tree that stood in Ida's field. At that moment the dog ran ahead again.
166356: A man claimed that a witch had made him lose his way, so that he had walked around the fen all night.
166368: A boy who had gone to visit his girlfriend met a lady in a black silk dress on the way back. The lady silently went along with the boy. When the lady turned onto the road to the castle, the boy was so frightened that he took a long detour.
166373: Some men were playing cards when a strange man suddenly came in. The stranger helped first one player, then another. When one of the card players bent down to pick up a fallen card, he saw that the strange man had goat's legs. It was the devil. A little later the men saw something fly through the house. After that the strange man had disappeared.
166379: After Romanie C. had played in the street with a beggar woman from Waremme, she was full of lice.
166380: Some men returning from Vliermaal heard a strange noise in the Schabos. But there was nothing to be seen in the woods.
166384: Maria had long been on her deathbed. Because she was a witch, she could not die before she had passed her arts on to someone else. Maria kept asking for a certain Bel. Two days after Bel had visited her in the hospital, Maria died. Afterwards Bel went to the priests to have herself exorcised.
166385: A seamstress from Meeuwen had been working all day in a neighbouring village. In the evening the little woman no longer dared to go home because she was afraid of werewolves. Then someone said to her: "Here is a red handkerchief. If you meet a werewolf, just throw that handkerchief at its mouth." The next day the little woman's farmhand had red threads between his teeth.
166387: If you pulled a werewolf by the ears, he became human again.
166401: A woman who could not make butter put some holy water in the butter churn. After that she had butter at once. In the course of the day a witch had come to stand by the butter.
166422: A farmhand who worked on a farm slept in the hay at night. One night the farmhand threw a cat to the ground. The next morning the farmhand was frightened to death when he saw that one of the maids had a wound on her head.
166423: Jefke G. had a café in the Zavel, where there was often fighting. One day an old woman came in and said to the landlady: "Just turn the glasses upside down, for I'll quickly see to it that this fight is over." Then the woman lifted her dress and said: "Mice, mice!" The next moment there were so many mice in the café that all the customers immediately ran outside.
166424: Jan went to the market with a friend. On the way Jan struck with his cudgel at a big dog that kept following him. Because he could not hit the animal, his friend shouted: "Throw a handkerchief!" The man followed the advice, after which the dog ran off with the handkerchief. At the market the men met their neighbour, who still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
166431: A man who saw a good two hundred starlings in a tree got out his gun. Of the thirteen starlings the man had shot down, one was still alive. The man cut off the bird's head. When the man came home, his wife said: "Well, you've cut off a witch's head!" A few days later the man heard that a woman in the village had died.
166434: One day the farmhands of a farm in Piringen went out to the field in the morning to fetch clover. There were always three women in the field who came to cut clover for their rabbits. One of the farmhands said to them: "You may do that, but you must wait until we are finished." When they had loaded their wagon, the farmhands drove off. But on the way to the farm, the wagon suddenly got stuck in the gravel in front of the house of one of those women. They fetched a few extra horses, but nothing helped: they could not get the wagon loose. The farmhands went to get the farmer, who managed to free the wagon with the help of a file. The next day one of the three women walked around with a cloth around her neck: they had nearly filed her head off.
166450: A farmer from Rutten had made a pact with the devil. If the devil could build a barn before the cock crowed for the first time in the morning, he would get the man's soul. When the barn was almost finished, the farmer's wife ran to the henhouse. She slapped her hands on her hips and began to sing, whereupon the cock immediately began to crow.
166453: A man walking across a bridge with a friend felt something walking along with him. When the man stood still, the ghost stood still too. But there was nothing to be seen.
166454: A man who had moved the boundary post of his land came back to haunt after his death. The ghost held a boundary post in its arms and kept calling: "Where shall I leave it? Where shall I leave it?" When one day, on the parish priest's advice, people answered: "Put the boundary post back where you fetched it from!", the dead man was released and haunted no more.
166461: A farmer whose animals all fell ill and died sought advice from the parish priest. The priest told the farmer to make sure the neighbour woman no longer came into the stables. Unfortunately it was already too late for the sick animals. Because the witch could no longer enter the stables, no other animals fell ill.
166464: A woman had given a man lice.
166485: A man from Schulen walking home at night was terrified when he heard a dog's chain rattling behind the hedge. It must have been a man with a chain around his neck.
166495: Frisse, a steward of Vogelsang, came haunting at midnight with a glowing coach and glowing horses.
166499: A man who had heard a ghost knock three times on the wardrobe went looking for the supernatural apparition with a candle and a pointed stick. When he found nothing, he said: "If it is in the name of God, I leave it in the name of God. If it is in the name of the devil, I leave it in the name of the devil." Then the man went to sleep.
166516: Some people sitting outside talking one evening heard a hellish noise in the distance. When the noise stopped, the oldest of the group said: "That was the hellish hunt, those were the evil spirits. When they come, you must do nothing to them, or else they take revenge."
166521: Two men coming back from Riksingen heard a voice in the field call: "Show me where I should put this!" The men ignored the question and went home. A few days later the men went bowling in Riksingen. When they came back around half past eleven, they heard the same voice again: "Show me where I should put this!" One of the men answered: "Just put it where you fetched it from!" At that the ghost said: "Then I am released!" A man who had moved a boundary post during his life had to haunt after his death. The ghost had wandered there for almost a year until someone had the courage to give the releasing answer.
166527: When the doorbell rang around midnight, the castle maid went to open the door. In front of the door stood the deceased lady of the castle. The woman came back and lived another eight years.
166541: A farmer's wife had already lost five animals seven times over. Once the stable had been blessed and a holy object lay under the threshold, she had no more misfortune. One day the holy object had suddenly disappeared. After that, several horses died again.
166545: In the past many cats roamed around Piringen. Black cats were often witches.
166553: A farmhand who read in a little book all the time managed to manure the field in no time. When the farmhand's band had been found, a brown friar was sent for, who threw the band into the oven. As soon as everything had burnt up, the farmhand wailed: "My power is gone. I can do nothing anymore, because my band has burnt up!"
166558: The maar (nightmare spirit) would sit on someone for a few minutes and in this way often suffocated its victim.
166584: A man who had gone to buy coal in Luik passed the house of a witch in Tongeren. At that moment the coal fell through a hole in the cart. When the man got home, he had not a single lump of coal left.
166587: A man from Boorsem claimed he had seen a glowing cow walking along the Maas.
166589: A man and a woman stayed the night in a house. Because his wife was in pain every night, the man decided to keep watch. During the night he saw a cat creep onto his wife's neck. The man grabbed the animal and throttled it. When the couple went to pay the next morning, the landlady sat hunched over in pain.
166604: A shepherd knew a shepherd who could work magic. When that shepherd grazed his sheep on a farmer's clover on the Kerkveld, he could turn his sheep into molehills and himself into a thistle. The farmer would then be furious; for from afar he had seen the sheep grazing on his land, but when he came closer they had suddenly vanished.
166607: Along the gravel road by the Grondeleer bells were heard ringing in the water at midnight. A church once sank in that water. One night two men went to listen to the bells, but they never came back. Once a stone was lowered into the water on a long rope. The bottom of the pool, however, could be reached.
166608: If you could make a werewolf bleed, he took on his human shape again.
166613: A bell once sank in the 'rode beemd' (red meadow) in Kaulille. On Christmas day those bells were heard ringing from underground. They were bells that had a bad godfather or godmother and had sunk into the ground through the devil's doing.
166620: The son of a witch lived with his family in the house where his mother used to live. The family had much misfortune, however: the cows, calves and pigs died, and even two children died. One day the baron had the house demolished and provided another house for the family to live in.
166632: A man was out with his horse and cart. Because of a witch, the horse suddenly refused to pull the cart any further.
166635: When mayor P. was visiting Janneke, he saw the devil come out of a pile of potatoes.
166647: At Hagedoren in Smeermaas someone could be heard calling all the time: "Where should it lie?" When one day someone answered: "Where you took it from, smart guy!", a whooshing sound was heard. Then all went quiet. The calling came from a dead man who had moved a boundary post during his life. Our Lord made him come and put the post back. After that he was released.
166659: A man doing his military service in the citadel of Luik was always visited by a girl between two and four in the afternoon. One day the man saw a grey ball of paper flying through the air, although there was no wind. The man thought he had been dreaming, until a little later the same thing happened. A little further on the man saw an old woman standing by the house. A little later a small kitten was walking around at the spot where the soldier had to keep watch.
166665: A man returning from Maastricht met a dog at the Zeven Wegen. Because the man suspected the dog was a werewolf, he took out his pocketknife. The werewolf did the man no harm, however. At the crossroads the dog changed into a horse with a chain. The werewolf probably wanted to rob the man of the money he had earned in Liège.
166668: After Florent had visited a witch, he was full of lice.
166673: In Kermt lived a woman in whose arm a dog came to lie every night. Finally a brown friar was called in, who banished the dog for ninety-nine years and more.
166684: A timber merchant from Gellik or Caberg had to go somewhere in the evening. The man got lost in a meadow and only found his way again the next morning. When the man walked past a witch's house in the morning, he saw the woman standing behind the window laughing at him.
166685: In a haunted castle chains could be heard rattling at midnight. Sometimes a shape was seen in the garden. People believed that the castle's dead owner came haunting because he could find no rest in his grave.
166692: In Zwartbroek, a village near Weert, there stood a haunted farm. The farm had been built on the 'Krang'. Just after midnight strange things happened in the farm: the flails rattled, the mill began to turn by itself and the animals got loose. In the morning the horse stood in the stable foaming at the mouth and sweating, with its mane plaited. After the friars of Weert had blessed the farm, no more strange things happened.
166702: During the war two boys had gone to visit their girlfriends and came back together at night. In Riemst the boys heard someone walking in clogs. A little later they saw a cat jump into the ditch.
166712: During the First World War, the men from Genk and Zonhoven went poaching in the woods at night. One night they saw a young lady with an umbrella standing under a tree. The men were so frightened that they never went poaching again.
166715: Witches' gatherings were often held in the Tolkensboom in Beek. One day the tree was full of cats again. One cat, however, stood at the foot of the tree wailing because she could not get up. A priest who had watched the whole scene called to the wailing cat: "Hey, how about you staying down here! After all, you've sat in the tree often enough." The cat stayed out of the tree and never climbed into it again.
166722: On the heath in Kerkhoven stood a dilapidated little house. When it was dark, a witch flew on her broomstick to that house. Inside, the witch always sang a strange song with much shrieking and screeching. One evening a man spied on the witch. The spy saw a large black bird arrive, which perched on the witch's hand. The witch stroked the bird, after which it flew away. The man managed to catch the bird and take it home. When he struck it dead, a beautiful girl appeared. The witch had once turned the girl into a bird. The farmer had set the girl free.
166727: In Meer a lady dressed in grey walked about in the evening.
166729: People whose pigs were bewitched had had to buy new animals. When the new pigs were almost fattened, they died.
166737: When Thijs was driving home with his cart in the evening, he met Bosmei on the way. The witch said: "You're out late!", to which Thijs replied: "Yes, but I'm almost home now". Then Bosmei said: "That's what you think!" and went on. At a barrier Thijs accidentally drove into the meadow. Because the man could not get back onto the road, he had to wait until morning before someone helped him back onto it. Eight days later Thijs was dead.
166744: In the past a white ghost wandered about on the Moddelweg.
166746: In the past many people secretly moved the boundary post of their land to own more. When those people died, their souls could find no rest. They came back to haunt with a boundary post in their hands, calling: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" Only when someone had the nerve to answer: "Put it back where you fetched it from!" was the dead person released and could their soul find rest.
166766: When people went home around midnight, they saw the witches flying through the air on their broomsticks, singing loudly.
166772: A boy was followed by a cat as far as the Rulbeek in Schulen. At the brook the animal suddenly disappeared.
166773: It was said that Pauline K. was a witch. Some men were driving a horse and cart in the Zuurbos in Duras when Pauline passed by and asked: "Are you on your way, men?" A little later the wheel of the cart was stuck, so they had to call Pauline. She put something under the wheel and under the horses' hooves, and then the cart moved on again. In Grazen people were churning butter when Pauline came in and asked: "Are you churning butter?" When she had gone, they said: "What will go wrong now; the witch has been here again." When they thought the butter was ready, they found nothing but filth and chaff. They had to fetch Pauline, who said: "I will free you from the evil hand," and she put something under the butter churn and said: "Churn a little more. The butter will be ready in a moment." And that is indeed what happened.
166775: Sjattenbroeks was haunted. At night a ghost always sat on a barrel.
166778: Werewolves sat in the trees and had themselves carried by passers-by. Some people fastened a dagger or a knife to their back. When a werewolf then jumped on them, the beast began to bleed and took on its human shape. The werewolf was then released.
166779: Trees S. had a beautiful white goat. Trees told her neighbour that she did not know how the goat had come to her. When Trees' mother died, however, the goat had disappeared as well. Trees claimed they had sold the goat. The neighbour did not believe her, though, because she had never seen a dealer at Trees' house.
166787: Anyone jumped by a heavy werewolf had to try to wound the beast with a knife or a needle. As soon as the werewolf started to bleed, he left his victim alone.
166803: A farmhand who had to manure the field sat idly on a dung heap all day, waiting. In the evening the farmhand got up and manured a small piece of the field. The next moment the whole field was suddenly manured. The devil must have helped the farmhand.
166826: A man ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) could no longer move or speak. Each time, the maar went away again by itself.
166830: A farmhand always went in the evening to some tree stumps near the house of S. close to Hasselt. In one of the tree stumps the farmhand had hidden a collar. When he put the collar on, he turned into a dog. One day the farmer sent his farmhand away so that he had the chance to burn the collar. When the farmer had thrown the collar into the fire, the farmhand instantly stood beside him to save the collar. After everything had burnt up, the farmhand was relieved because he had been released. The farmhand left and was never seen again.
166833: A miller who had to cross the brook with his cart suddenly could not go any further. Even seven or eight horses could not pull the cart out of the mud. A little later a witch passed by and said: "I'll see to it that the cart gets out of the brook!" The next moment a single horse pulled the cart out of the brook with ease.
166836: A witch had bewitched a man's pigeons.
166839: A man returning from Schulen saw a tall lady walking near the Bolderberg, who followed him all the way to the village of Kermt.
166849: Two witches lived by the little chapel in Kerniel. When a man drove past the chapel with his horse and cart, one of the witches came outside. At that moment the horse stopped.
166891: In Rotem there was a haunted farmhouse. In the morning the potatoes always lay in a corner. These strange events probably had something to do with the fact that the lord of the castle no longer wanted to pay for the procession.
166902: A man who went to visit his girlfriend in Terboekt every Sunday was attacked by a black tomcat.
166905: A farmer who had just bought a fine calf met a witch, who said: "If you don't sell me your calf, it will die." But the farmer did not want to sell the calf. The next morning the animal was dead.
166907: One day Zjang B. struck a white cat that kept getting under his feet. The cat turned out to have white whiskers on one side and grey whiskers on the other. It was a witch who turned herself into a white cat.
166928:
In Heisselt near Jeuk lived a widow who had become pregnant in an inexplicable way. When the widow gave birth, the midwife found that the child looked anything but normal. It was a little black creature on four legs, half human and half frog in appearance. The midwife threw the creature onto a chest, whereupon it began to croak and jumped under the bed. The midwife let the strange creature bleed to death.
Some time later the village 'rode the ox'. A tailor from Genoelselderen dressed in black played the devil, sitting on a white ox and singing the devil's song. Two days after the birth the widow sat digging in her garden, hoping to find the little body of her child.
166934: A young man of about twenty had a girlfriend who worked as a maid in Werm. One evening the young man stood talking at his girlfriend's window. Suddenly he was startled because a large black dog was rubbing against his legs. The dog walked to the well in the meadow. The young man wished his girlfriend good night and set off home. On the way he met a young girl, dressed entirely in black and holding an umbrella. That night the young man did not sleep a wink, so frightened had he been by the strange apparition. The next day he told the farmer what he had seen. The farmer said: "You should have asked the girl what she wanted." It was probably the ghost of the girl who had jumped into the well in the meadow some years before out of heartbreak.
166946: After sexton C. had locked the church, he walked home. Whether he went by Hamelsdorp or past D.'s house, on the way the sexton was always leapt upon by the werewolf. The werewolf that haunted Hamelsdorp was in fact the ghost of old V. The werewolf near D.'s was the ghost of B. After priest M. had read prayers over the sexton, he banished the ghost of B. to the meadow.
166960: A man who owned a book of magic gave his friend the following advice: "When you are alone in the evening, sit on a chair and tie half a kilo of copper to the ceiling with a cord at the height of your face. Then you must think of a dead person you would like to see again". The man did it and was so frightened by the apparition that he quickly went to bed.
166962: In a family in Stamprooi a baby had been born that cried all the time. Since the doctor did not know what to do, some believed the child was bewitched. Because the parents were at their wits' end, they went to ask a friar for help. The friar, however, told them that the baby had been in the grip of the evil hand for too long. A few days later the baby died.
166966: People who had to fetch the midwife always had to go in pairs, because on the way they could be attacked by a witch. Sometimes strangers would jump on their backs and let themselves be carried.
166980: Some people from Congo (1) saw a large ball of fire come out of a marshy meadow. The fireball flew over them to the Boksberg, where it hovered above a clearing. At that spot a man had once murdered a woman. The people ran away in fright because they believed the woman's ghost had come back.
166987: At midnight a rooster was heard crowing in the stable. But when people went to look, there was nothing to be seen.
166988:
Jan of the castle estate of Wermerbos had special powers. He owned witch books, which he had bought in Maastricht. Jan could make mice from a handful of earth or pebbles. Jan could also make predictions. To the people working with him in the field he sometimes said: "Today the food is burnt." or "Today we're getting porridge." Because those predictions always came true, some believed Jan was having an affair with the maid. One day Jan was sitting in the inn, where he summoned a rooster and ordered the animal to stand on a chair and crow. At the place of one of his friends, who worked on the castle estate of Ridderborn, they were plagued by rats. When Jan came to the farmhand in the horse stable, he made the fearsome-looking rats come out one by one from the manger the horses ate from. To the last rat, which had a fierce look in its eyes and tried to turn back halfway, Jan said: "Go on, you too!" From that moment the farmhand was no longer troubled by rats.
At night people often saw Jan sitting reading by candlelight until one or two o'clock in the books he always carried with him. The priest had said several times: "You must throw those books into the fire," to which Jan meekly replied that he would. Because Jan was always walking around with his books again the next day, the priest sent a friar to him, who after long talks managed to convert him. Jan had prayers read over him and promised to go to the Holy Sacrament Mass in Hasselt every Thursday. This time Jan really meant what he said, for he even allowed the friar to burn his books. From then on Jan led an exceptionally pious life and went to Mass every week.
After Jan died, there was still haunting on the castle estate. At night noises were often heard in the attic and on the roof, but when people went to look, there was nothing to be seen. Eventually the castle's residents did penance in Scherpenheuvel, after which peace returned to the castle.
166992: In the Heidestraat stood a little clay house that was haunted. All the occupants of that house had fallen ill and died. A man came to live in the house with his wife and two daughters. The two daughters soon died and the wife fell ill. One night the man saw a red-haired ghost without legs appear in a corner of the house. The man was so frightened that the next day he left the house with his sick wife. Later, children were often frightened with stories about the red man in the house. A long time afterwards the little clay haunted house burned down.
166997: A witch lived in Halmaal. Whenever people walked past her house, something always broke. After the witch's death, people believed her daughter had taken over her mother's arts.
167005: A farmer who lived in the Netherlands refused to pay for the milling of his grain during the war. So he went to the Kikmolen in Opgrimbie at night to have his grain milled. One night the farmer saw cats dancing in a ring, howling. When the cats moved aside to let the farmer and his cart through, they lined up in a row along the side of the road.
167008: The H. family had a little child that just would not grow. At their wits' end, the parents went to the friars. After the friars had read prayers over the child, they advised the parents to cut open the pillow in the cradle. The pillow turned out to be full of needles. From then on the child was perfectly healthy.
167025: A boy could fill the church with white mice. The priest freed the boy from his magic power.
167036: One day old B. was walking over the Galgeberg when suddenly a mewing kitten came running up. With every step the man took, the kitten ran between his legs. The man ran away in fear.
167038: Prisoners who had been wrongly convicted were freed by Our Lady.
167039: A man from Rekem who always had bad luck had a priest come to exorcise the farm. While the priest was praying, the neighbour woman came to stand at the door. At that the priest said: "Close the door, but bear no grudge." From then on the man had no more bad luck.
167053: A werewolf's animal skin was found in an oak tree. After the people had burnt the skin, they never heard anything about a werewolf again.
167054: One evening V. and his brother had gone to play cards in Eigenbilzen. When on the way back the men saw a little cat sitting on a barrier, one of them said: "I'll help that little cat off there." The animal replied: "You'll leave that little cat right where it is!" The next day the men saw the same little cat sitting on the heath near Berenbroek. The carter wanted to thrash the cat with his whip, but he thought better of it just in time.
167060: A wizard could make a horse stand still for as long as he wanted. When the wizard was in a bad mood, people were afraid of him.
167061: Marie van 't Weverke always knew when a child had been born somewhere. Even when no one else knew yet, or when the birth had taken place in a village far away, Marie knew everything.
167067: Two boys were coming back from Thorn at about half past eleven at night. At the pond marsh the boys met two cats that kept running between their legs. A little later the boys saw only the shadowy figure of a woman holding up her finger threateningly. A hundred metres further on the boys met so many cats that they had to spend the night in a nearby house.
167072: A woman who went sewing in Hees was jumped by a dog on the way home. That was the werewolf having itself carried.
167078: The castle of Rummen was haunted. At night noises were heard there and the lights went on and off by themselves.
167081: A black dog sat in the horse stable of a farm. The farmer had already tried to hit the dog with a dung fork, but the animal stayed sitting motionless. The farmer then sent for the priest. After the priest had prayed for half an hour while sweat dripped from his face, the dog ran away.
167103: Papmarie's husband had found a pot of money while digging out a cellar. When the man went to exchange the money in Luik, he got only half of what it was really worth. For that reason the man could not die when his time had come. His master said to the man, "Die in peace. The money is not mine." After the priest had read prayers over him, the man could die peacefully.
167108: A man passing a haunted house was badly frightened when he saw a sheep come out of the house. The man was pursued by the animal all the way. When the man wanted to strike at the sheep, the animal had suddenly vanished.
167118: A woman said to the husband of a dead neighbour: "Well, now you've beaten her into the ground!" For that man always beat his wife. The woman had promised to go to Mass for her neighbour, but she had not kept that promise. At night the woman always heard knocking on the wall. One night a dung heap outside was on fire. After the woman went to Mass in Kermt the next day, the dead woman was released.
167123: A woman from Stokkem was gathering potatoes with a neighbour. Strangely enough, the neighbour could make mice out of clay.
167139: The white lady often wandered in the meadow by the church. She would rattle chains and jump onto the hedges.
167144: A young man was seeing a girl who was said to be a witch. Whenever the boy had been to visit his girlfriend, he always met a big black dog on the way back. One day a friend of the boy shot the dog in the leg. The next day the girl lay in bed with a bullet in her foot. From then on the boy never visited his girlfriend again.
167167: Rode Sjoan had a book of magic that gave him special powers. For example, rode Sjoan could make cats follow someone and jump onto the bed. Rode Sjoan also sometimes conjured a little white rabbit onto a barrier. Whenever people tried to push the rabbit off, it kept jumping back onto the barrier.
167178: A young man who had been to the fair with his girlfriend saw on the way back a house in Heppen whose roof was completely covered with rats.
167181: A farmhand was seeing a girl who was said to be a witch. Strangely enough, every night in the stable where he slept the farmhand saw a black cat come up to be stroked. One day the farmhand cut the cat with a knife. When he went to his girlfriend the next day, he asked: "What happened to you?", to which the girl replied: "I fell". Then the farmhand said: "No, I did that".
167190: With her evil hand, Vreebetje often made a child fall ill or a sow unable to farrow.
167195: Witches often turned themselves into cats and then had themselves carried until the person was almost out of breath.
167200: Our Lady of Tongeren always went along with the procession. When the statue of Mary had been painted, it was dirty again three days later.
167207: A man went with a friend to Leef (Gors-Opleeuw), where he had a date with his girlfriend. While the man set off for his sweetheart's house, the friend went to a café in Leef. When the man reached his girlfriend's house, he looked through the window and saw the girl get dressed, comb her hair and then let herself fall onto the bed. When the man went in and touched the girl's body, she lay motionless as if she were dead. Frightened, the man went to fetch his friend, who said: "We're not staying here; your girl is a witch." As the two went home, the man saw dozens of cats walking about along the way. His friend could not see the cats. The friend advised the man to visit a little old woman from Jesseren. That woman said to him: "If you had behaved properly like Vinus, my father, none of these things would have happened to you." The woman must have been one of the cats he had met on the way. How else could she have known what had happened to him?
167209: A man returning with some friends from the fair in Schulen saw a cat sitting by the Reibeek. When the men struck at the cat, more and more cats appeared. The men ran away in fear.
167213: Whoever vows to go on pilgrimage for a sick person must keep that vow. Otherwise the sick person would come back to haunt after his death.
167214: Some men often went fishing in the Maas at night at 'the drowned little man'. The place was called that because a body had once been found there. The men had to leave before midnight, or else a ghost appeared that kept calling: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" It was a dead man who could find no rest because he had moved a boundary post during his life.
167234: A man who was training as a tailor in Solt came home every day by way of the Broek. Will-o'-the-wisps often floated above those marshes. People said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the returning dead.
167235: A man playing cards in a café cursed the whole time because he lost again and again. Suddenly the café door opened and a big black dog came and lay under the table. The friars had to be fetched to get rid of the dog.
167238: Because Door had been orphaned, he was allowed to become an apprentice to his uncle. When the uncle died, a ghost appeared beside Door's bed. The ghost said: "I am dead, but I may come back to teach you the trade." The parish priest, however, refused to believe it.
167265: After a man had struck at a cat, a witch had a broken arm.
167276: In a house stood a cupboard that always moved by itself in the evening. After the people had the house blessed again by a friar, no more strange things happened.
167278: A weaver from Horpmaal had become possessed by the devil through reading books. Because the man suffered greatly from this torment, he went to the Capuchins of Sint-Truiden for help. While the man was telling his story to a friar, he suddenly saw the devil appear at the window. The man cried: "He's coming to get me!" The friar sprinkled the man with holy water and prayed the whole time. When the friar turned the page of his prayer book, the devil had vanished.
167284: A farmer had a farmhand who always went out in the evening. When the farmer had found his farmhand's collar in a tree stump, he knew the farmhand was a werewolf. The next day the farmer sent his farmhand away so that he had the chance to burn the collar. When the collar caught fire, the farmhand instantly stood by the oven. Because the farmhand came too late to save his collar, he was released.
167287: A boy from Beek who was out walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "Wait here a moment, I have an errand to run." While the girl stood waiting, a big black dog suddenly came at her. The girl remembered the advice her boyfriend had once given her and threw her handkerchief at the beast. A few hours later the girl found that her boyfriend still had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl told the pastor what had happened to her, but the clergyman did not know what to do. One day the pastor found a collar under a tree stump. The clergyman took the band with him to have a farmer burn it. The moment the collar caught fire, the boy stood crying by the fire. As soon as the band had burnt up, the boy was released.
167295: A pretty, good girl was visited by a handsome young man who asked: "Will you come with me to the fair tonight?" The girl agreed. When the young man came to fetch her in the evening, he said: "But first you must tell me your name." "Maria," the girl answered. The next moment the young man had suddenly vanished. For he was the devil, who was powerless when the name of Our Lady was spoken.
167307: Around midnight a man was walking past a burnt-down farm in Munsterbilzen. Suddenly the man saw a white lady appear, who beckoned him to come closer. But the man did not dare. Some time later someone did find the courage to go up to the white lady. Then the apparition said: "Money is hidden here. You must give that money to the church." When that had been done, the white lady was released.
167308: In the mill of Lauw there was a black cat that caused people a great deal of trouble. Even after the cat had once been tied to the mill wheel with a chain, the animal still kept coming back. One day a priest came to bless the mill. But the cat said: "You keep quiet, for you once stole a white loaf," to which the priest replied: "My mother paid for that." The priest noticed a strange smell around the mill and had the plank floor taken up. In the ground a corpse was found. At last the ghost had been found.
167313: A ghost always appeared to Tien, and only she could see it. The woman had vowed to go on pilgrimage. After Tien had made the pilgrimage, the ghost no longer appeared.
167323: After X from the baker's in Stokkem had touched a child, the child was completely full of lice.
167330: In Broekom lived a child who had fallen ill after being touched by a witch. When the priests had exorcised the child, it quickly recovered.
167353: Werewolves had themselves carried to tease people. Werewolves never jumped on people who might be able to overpower them.
167360: A farmer who had much misfortune with his animals after the beggar woman Hekse T. had visited went to a clergyman in Luik. The clergyman said: "Tomorrow the witch will come to fetch a darning needle. Then you will know who is to blame." The next day Hekse T. did indeed come to fetch a darning needle.
167364: Jan B. and Pierre G. had gone to work at the castle. On the way back they suddenly heard a rattling of chains. All at once a white figure jumped down from the castle wall. When B. cried: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph!", there was nothing but smoke to be seen where the ghost had stood.
167367: At 't Geneuth something had been thrown into the fire. Although the farmhand had been sent somewhere, he immediately stood by the oven to save his possession.
167376: Whoever wanted to sell his soul to the devil had to stand at a crossroads with a black hen. The devil would then come by and ask: "Is that hen for sale?" If one answered "yes" to this question, the devil would ask: "Is there anything else for sale, won't you sell your soul?" In this way one could make a pact with the devil. With an animal skin provided by the devil, one had to roam about as a werewolf for a few hours of the night, in return for a fee of ten francs. So one day a man stood at a crossroads with a black hen. After some time the devil came riding up on a goat and said: "Jump on!" When the man had ridden along with the devil for a while, he suddenly cried: "Oh God, oh God!", whereupon the goat took a great fright and threw the man to the ground.
167380: In Nieuwerkerken lived a boy who could blow white mice into being. After the priest had baptised the boy again, he could no longer make mice.
167385:
Whenever people drove past Betje's house with a horse and cart, the cart always got stuck. They then had to call out: "Betje, can't you help us?" After that the cart started moving again.
Betje also often sought out unbaptised babies to do them harm.
167386: Nooi V.B. was a werewolf who could change into a dog.
167390: In Kessenich there lived a witch who ran a café. Every time someone wanted to drive past the café, the horses stopped. Only when one had drunk a shot in the café could the horses go on again.
167392: The Geuzentempel in Alken was haunted. At midnight a light always burned in the tower. During the First World War the Germans fled from that temple and spent the night in a nearby meadow.
167394: Lena went to pray for her paralysed child at the statue of the Black Our Lady of Tongeren. After Lena had prayed for a while, a real grape suddenly fell from the wooden bunch of grapes held by the child Jesus. The woman picked up the grape and gave it to her child. As soon as the child had eaten the grape, it was cured. People often tried to replace the missing grape in the wooden bunch, but the new grape always fell to the ground. Behind the statue of Mary hang the chains of the slaves whom Our Lady had freed. Every seven years a great procession in honour of Our Lady was held in Tongeren. Once, however, the weather was so bad that it was decided to postpone the procession. The next morning the statue of Mary was smeared with water and mud; Our Lady had gone round alone.
167396: A man returning with horse and cart from the miller in Hechtel went into an inn in Spiekelspade. A pretty girl gave him a drink. At a certain moment the girl went to sleep. A little later a kitten crept onto the man's lap. Because he was wearing new trousers, the man pushed the kitten away. When the man set off again with his cart, there was once more a cat on his lap. Further on the man had to unhitch his horse, because there were so many cats on the cart that the animal could no longer pull it.
167399: A man was annoyed that his wife was away every day. One day five or six cats came into the house and began to dance on the hearth. Suddenly the cats were gone. When the wife came home, she kept searching for something, but would not say what she had lost. The man found his wife's wedding ring at the spot where the cats had danced. That is how he found out that his wife was a witch.
167411: In Gruitrode a family had a little daughter who was bewitched. In the evening the girl lay in her bed screaming: "That ugly woman is hitting me! That ugly woman is hitting me!" But the parents could see no one. At their wits' end, the mother took her daughter to the healer of Genk, who gave her three candles. The candles had to be lit every evening shortly before midnight, and then one had to walk around the house three times. As long as the candle kept going out, the evil had not yet been driven away. When the candle stayed lit, the girl would soon be cured.
167432: Four men returning from Eisden saw a mewing cat by the college. The men threw a stone at the animal and went on. The next moment the road was completely full of cats, which said: "Now I'll show you some cats!"
167433: A woman had borrowed a clog from a man. After the man got his clog back, his leg became inflamed. The man went to pray, after which his leg healed.
167434: A man walking past the castle of Damers at night met a white lady. Frightened, the man said to the apparition: "You go on your way, and I'll do the same."
167436: Because the castle of Heers stood empty during the winter months, a man from Horpmaal came to stay there. Every night the castle was haunted between twelve and one o'clock. Cats then roamed about, and sometimes a Zwarte Madam (Black Lady) was seen as well. When the gate flew open at midnight, a coach with burning candles drove in. The man from Horpmaal was pushed out of his bed, but he always crawled back in. One night the man said carelessly: "Oh God, oh God, just let me sleep!" From that moment on the ghosts left him in peace.
167447: Some men from Eigenbilzen were taking a few sheep to the market in Tongeren around midnight. The men thought they heard someone whistling for them to wait. At the Dikke Steen the men saw a strange apparition that was bigger than a horse.
167454: A farmhand went with his girlfriend to the fair in Erpekom. The girl had often been warned that her boyfriend was a werewolf, but she did not believe it. When they were in the woods, the boy said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself behind the bushes. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth; then it can't harm you." A little later a big black dog did indeed come running at the girl. She threw the handkerchief at the dog, which tore the cloth to pieces. When the young man came out of the bushes a little later, the girl asked him why he had been away so long, and the boy replied: "I had seen the dog too." When they went home, the girl turned on the light so they could eat together. Suddenly the girl cried out: "It was you yourself, because the threads of the handkerchief are still hanging between your teeth!"
167466: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who floated above the marshes because they had not got into heaven.
167475: A man going to visit his friend Eugène met two women. When Eugène opened the door, the women had suddenly vanished.
167501: Giel, a man who lived on the Heikant in Opgrimbie, was staying in Germany. The man had gone home at Whitsun and then travelled back to Germany. When Giel arrived, one of his friends said: "Didn't you see anything near Smèirmaas when you went home?" "Yes indeed," said Giel, "a big dog walked beside me there. That must have been you, because people say you are a werewolf!"
167519:
Purnal went with two horses to fetch a cartload of manure. When the cart was fully loaded, however, the horses would not leave, because the witch Ann stood watching. When Ann stopped holding the horses back with her powers, Purnal could leave.
On her deathbed Ann could not die until her daughter had taken over her powers.
167525: Tiske L. had shot a hare. When the man wanted to pick up the dead hare, the animal jumped up and ran between his legs.
167537: In Aalst lived a werewolf with the body of a dog and the head of a human. That werewolf blocked people's way.
167552: The will-o'-the-wisps seen by the water were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
167569: Near the castle of Widooie lay a felled oak. When the count and countess had died, they came haunting by that oak.
167573: A dog roaming about a farm in Hoelbeek was struck on the head with a piece of wood. The next day the farmer had a hole in his head.
167577: Between Hoesselt and Schalkhoven stood an old little house that was haunted. At night people heard noise in the house and the light came on by itself.
167580: At midnight the witches had to go out to do someone harm, whether they wanted to or not.
167599: Some men returning from Hees saw a hare running in the Emerestraat. When the men tried to catch the hare, the animal ran off screaming.
167601: A farmer and his wife could not keep a single animal alive because the stable was bewitched. After they had the stable exorcised, all the animals stayed healthy.
167614: One evening a man was attacked by a werewolf in the meadows of Mal. When the man threw a handkerchief at the animal's mouth, the werewolf ran off. When he got home, the man told his brother what had happened to him. At that the brother began to laugh. The man saw that a thread of the handkerchief was hanging between his brother's teeth, and cried indignantly: "It was you!"
167616: In Horpmaal a goat wandered about that was called 'de Gloaze Geit' because it behaved so strangely. Sometimes the goat stood still in the middle of the road. A while later the goat went on again as if nothing was the matter.
167621: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of people who had died unbaptised. Will-o'-the-wisps usually appeared near water. When someone baptised a will-o'-the-wisp, it was released.
167623: In Boorsem a ghost wandered about saying: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" It was a dead man who could find no rest because he had moved a boundary post. One day the drunkard Pierke answered: "Put it where you fetched it from!" Since then the ghost has never been heard again.
167645: A child constantly had headaches because it had been touched by the evil hand. The pillow the child slept on turned out to be full of pins. After the parish priest had been sent for, the child got better.
167655: In the past, will-o'-the-wisps were often seen moving up and down near a marshy meadow. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
167662: One evening a man saw a beautiful white lady walking in a lane between Mechelen and Rukkelingen. She did not say a word and vanished mysteriously.
167667: A meadow in Beverst was haunted. A beguine with a candle in her hand always appeared there.
167669: A man walking home in the evening met a devil's coach with burning horses. When the coach had passed, the man got lost. Only towards morning did the man find his way home again.
167670: Anyone who had moved a boundary post during his life had to haunt after his death.
167671: A boy who went to visit his girlfriend in Gestel always had to make a detour because a cat blocked his way. When the boy told his father what had already happened to him four times, he was advised to strike at the cat with a stick the next time. After the boy had struck at the cat, the animal jumped in front of his feet again a little further on and said: "Strike me again now." When the boy answered: "If you block my way, I'll beat you to death!", the cat ran away.
167688: When the children went to milk the cow, they heard footsteps around the cowshed, but they saw nothing. Because the children no longer dared to go into the shed, they went to the friars.
167690: A boy who worked as a baker's hand for a certain Usé in Sint-Truiden was in love with a girl from Halle-Booienhoven. One evening the boy met his sweetheart at the market. Because the girl was afraid to go home alone, the boy went with her. On a small hill in Wilderen, however, the pair saw something strange. Six cows came walking along, neatly in a row as if they were people. One cow held its head to the left, the next to the right, and so on. After that the boy never again dared to walk his girlfriend home.
167695: A father was walking home with his son Victor along the Bienenberg. Suddenly Victor stopped because a pack of cats blocked his way. The young man could only go on when all the cats had disappeared.
167697: In Rijkhoven lived a girl who every first Friday of the month fell out of her bed and bled like Our Lord. Everyone believed it was a miracle. During the war the Germans threw money into the house and took pieces of the house away with them. Eventually it became known that the girl was being bewitched by her mother. The girl died very young.
167722: At the Wermerbos farm, the daughter saw a gravestone in her room before going to bed. Frightened, the girl fetched her parents, but when they came back into the room there was nothing to be seen. A few days later the family received word that their aunt had died. The woman must have died at the moment the girl saw the gravestone.
167727: If a witch had thrown a little ball into the butter churn, no butter could be made. The priests of Hasselt then had to come and exorcise the milk.
167729: After the death of the drossaard (bailiff), strange things happened in Overpelt. Even after the drossaard's ghost had been banished for ninety-nine years, dogs came out of his house and the doors and windows flew open for no explicable reason. Later, however, everything became quiet again.
167739: The maar (nightmare spirit) was a standstill of the blood. People ridden by the maar had a dream in which they tried in vain to resist something.
167746: During the winter months a few friends regularly met in a house to talk. After every gathering a woman from the neighbourhood knew exactly what had been said in the house. The friends found this very annoying and once went out into the street to see if anyone was standing there listening. One of the men was convinced that it had something to do with witches or ghosts, and he went to the friars in Hasselt. At first the friar thought someone was eavesdropping on the group, but the man convinced him that this was not the case. Then the friar advised him to check whether there were toads around the house. For the friar knew that witches often turned themselves into toads. That same evening the friends searched around the house for toads. And indeed, outside they found two toads, which looked at them with raised heads. One of the friends hit the toads with a broomstick. He wounded one of the toads on its front leg. The next day he saw a woman from the neighbourhood with her arm in a cloth. "What happened to you?", the man asked, to which the woman replied: "I fell over a log." The man did not believe her and said firmly: "No, no, you came to eavesdrop on me and my friends in the shape of a toad!"
167748: A woman had bought a goat from a witch. For the first few days the animal was perfectly healthy and gave plenty of milk. A little later, however, the goat went wild; it stood on its hind legs and gave no more milk.
167751: A farmer from Hasselt whose cows were all dying went to fetch the priests of Weert. But when the farmer and the priests were on their way to the stable, there was water everywhere in places where there had never been water before. The farmer said: "But Father, let us go back, or we'll drown!", to which the priest replied: "Don't worry, we won't drown." In the stable the priest pointed at a few cows and said: "This cow and that cow will still die, but the others will all live." The priest's prediction came true.
167758: Some children went into the woods to gather withered grass and dry pine needles. Suddenly the children saw some squirrels. When the children had almost caught one of the squirrels, an old woman with a club suddenly stood before them. That woman was a witch who had turned herself into a squirrel.
167762: A man whose child was ill went to the priests. The priests said: "Burn her, that woman!"
167775: In one family a child lay dying. At midnight three quiet strokes of a clock rang out. At the last three strokes the child died.
167778: In Wellen lived a family with many sons. At midnight the door flew open and twenty-four cats came in. They were witches who had come especially for the boys.
167802: A boy walking home late in the evening was followed by a werewolf. The boy wounded the werewolf with a dung fork. As soon as the beast began to bleed, it changed into a man the boy knew.
167803: A woman who had prayed from three to four o'clock at night (1) saw a lady knitting near Jonckhold. When the woman came closer, the lady took the form of a crow and flew away.
167808: In the Binkelstraat in the Buts, a man fell at night over the donkey that people said was a phantom animal. Luckily the man knew it was the donkey belonging to the count's children.
167819: A man who had walked stark naked through the procession got into trouble with the police. His sister said: "Aren't you ashamed of what you did? I would rather you had dropped dead on the spot." Because the man took the reproaches very much to heart, he drowned himself. After his death the suicide came back to haunt at the castle. When his sister was lighting the lamp, she suddenly got a slap in the face. In the end the ghost had to be banished.
167822: Someone who had to carry the werewolf walked to the café with the creature on his back. There they beat the werewolf until he bled and could be recognised.
167833: A man walking home with a flail on his shoulder saw a cat sitting on the road in Molleblak (?). Against his better judgement he struck at the animal. The next moment there were a good hundred cats at his feet. When the exhausted man said: "Oh Lord, oh Lord," all the cats suddenly vanished.
167844: A woman from Munsterbilzen often walked along P.'s wall. A cat always sat on that wall and let the woman carry it.
167846: The plain by the mill between Opgrimbie and Boorsem was called the 'Boorserdel'. Because people believed it was haunted, nobody dared go there in the evening. Around ten or eleven at night a faint light was seen there and chains were heard rattling.
167858: When Free V.G. was playing cards in a pub, he had the jack of spades from the deck fetch a bottle of gin.
167863: Will-o'-the-wisps were souls of children who had been buried unbaptised.
167867: A man noticed that some of his chickens regularly went missing. When the man kept watch, he saw a black cat sneak into the henhouse at midnight and come back out with a chicken. The man then decided to set a snare. The cat, however, always walked around the snare. So the man's father suspected that the cat was a witch, and he placed a crucifix under the threshold. After that the black cat never came back.
167870: A newly married couple coming home at night suddenly saw some twenty or thirty cats appear. "Those are witches," said the woman. The cats began to dance around a tree, whereupon the woman dropped the pots and pans she had bought. At that the cats ran off. When the woman came to collect the broken pieces the next morning, she saw a ring where the grass had been completely danced away.
167884: Between midnight and one o'clock thick clouds of smoke rose near the Méas oak. People believed it was the offering of the spirit Méas.
167885: During catechism class in the basilica of Tongeren, a little boy threw some earth on the floor. The next moment little mice were running everywhere. After the priest had baptised the boy again, he could no longer make mice.
167895: A boy who was walking to Neerharen with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "I'm going to relieve myself here. If a dog comes at you in the meantime, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." On seeing a dog, the girl did what her boyfriend had advised. When the boy came back, the girl noticed to her great dismay that he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
167906: When two men were in the woods, they struck at a black cat that was making a lot of noise. That cat was a witch.
167910: By the wall of the castle park of Betho a witch dressed all in white walked between midnight and one o'clock. Nearby there was also a witch's hut. Nobody dared come to that place at night.
167917: Pierke slept in a farmer's barn. One night Pierke suddenly heard meowing. A little later there was a cat on every corner of the bed. The cat called: "Pierke, Pierke, are you asleep?" Then Pierke heard music.
167921: Werewolves followed people in the evening in the shape of a big black dog. Some werewolves were returned dead; others were incarnations of the devil. There were even people who received a werewolf pelt during their lifetime. If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could recognise him.
167925: Every time a pane was fitted in the windows of the Geuzentempel (Beggars' Temple), the glass had fallen out by the next day.
167931: When a horse in Neeroeteren would not pull the cart, some women from the neighbourhood stood laughing. As soon as the carter took the reins, the horse moved on again. If the carter had known which spoke had been put into the wheel first, he would have smashed it. That way he could have found out who the witch was, because she would then have a broken leg. In this case it was a former fiancée who had been tormenting him.
167944: A butcher coming back from Monnikenhof saw a woman sitting on a small hill, combing her hair. The butcher said: "What are you doing there?", and the woman answered: "That's none of your business!" Then the man said: "I could easily get you off that hill!" The woman retorted fiercely: "If you dare touch me, I'll cover you in lice!" The butcher took his knife and ordered the woman: "Go on, walk ahead of me!" On the way the woman suddenly vanished.
167964: When the weather was bad, the statue of Mary was not taken outside. Because Mary was displeased, she went for a walk in the fields on her own. The next day the mantle of the statue of Mary was smeared with mud.
167981: A witch was always an old woman, never an old man. Anyone who dared to look back while being followed by Bet was afterwards completely full of lice.
167986: In the old days children were told to beware of black cats. After all, a black cat was the devil, and it always brought bad luck.
168002: Some boys went to the churchyard at night because their father had said it was haunted. At midnight exactly, white figures floated above all the gravestones.
168005: A man went to fetch wood in the forest with a cart and four horses. When the man met Bosmie from Lanaken on a paved road, the horses suddenly stopped. As soon as the witch was gone, the horses could go on again.
168006: In Melveren there lived a man who went about as a werewolf. When one day someone had thrown a red handkerchief at the werewolf, people knew who it was.
168013: In the old days people were afraid of black cats because they believed they were witches.
168016: The wild hunt was a pack of cats that gathered to frighten people.
168018: Nolleke van G., a supposed bokkerijder (goat rider, a robber said to ride a flying goat in league with the devil), lived in Elsput beyond the canal. At the C. family's house a black dog always walked on the roof. People believed that dog was Nolleke.
168034: A hunter often let his dog drink at the house of an old woman. When the dog had soiled the woman's washing for the second time, the woman came outside and said: "That was the last time your dog does that!" The next moment the dog lay on the ground as if paralysed. When the man had promised that he would no longer pass the house with his dog, the animal could get up again.
168045: Three men were mowing Toneke's field in the morning. Suddenly the white ladies flew through the air. Because they flew so low, a gust of wind arose that blew the men's hats away and knocked over the trays of grain.
168047: A man claimed that a witch lived in a street in Tongeren, because whenever he rode past there on his bicycle, his chain always came off. And always at exactly the same spot...
168048: A man who had moved a boundary post came back to haunt after his death with the post in his hands.
168079: One night Frans accompanied the chaplain, who had to give a woman the Last Rites. On the way the two saw a will-o'-the-wisp. The chaplain said: "If we still see the light on the way back, we'll go to it". When the men saw the will-o'-the-wisp again on the way back, the chaplain said: "Well Frans, are you coming? Some claim that will-o'-the-wisps are the souls of unbaptised children". Frans answered: "No, I'm not coming! Do you think I want to get lost in the water?"
168098: A witch made a strange movement with her arm as she walked past a meadow where a pregnant pig stood. Because of that, everything went wrong for the poor animal.
168100: A boy from Dilsen went to visit his girlfriend. Through the window the boy saw that his girlfriend had two girls visiting. The three rubbed themselves with witch's grease and said: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Cologne". With that the girls flew away. Then the boy went inside, also rubbed himself with witch's grease and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Cologne". Because the boy had made a mistake when speaking the magic formula, he got stuck in a hedge on the way.
168102: P. had to take a sack with the mill cart to a family with two young daughters. When P. saw a cat, he put the animal in a box and set the box on the stove. Because the cat could not bear the heat on its paws, it began to dance in the box. Finally the animal jumped to the floor. One of the daughters struck P. on the knee and said: "You did that, beanpole!" The next day P. had a pain in his knee. Later a darning needle was removed from the knee.
168109: Suska, the maid of farmer J., could make mice. After the chaplain of Koersel had held a whole series of ceremonies, Suska could no longer make mice.
168118: In the Uikhoverveld a ghost always wandered about at midnight, asking: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" Because people were afraid, they mostly dared not say anything. One night, however, a drunkard answered: "Dammit, put it where you fetched it from!" Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
168128: A man coming back from the churchyard saw a white figure that came down the steps and followed him. It looked like some kind of beast.
168137: A man on his way to 's Heerenelderen met a big yellow dog. After the man had made the sign of the cross, the dog disappeared. Two hundred metres further on, however, the animal was there again. When the man got home, he said to the dog: "Why have you tormented me?" The dog leapt away in fear because the man fired a revolver shot.
168138: A man from Stevoort had special powers because he consorted with the devil. When the man threw his handkerchief into the air, it all turned into mice. The priest had to free the man from evil.
168160: A man walking home was hindered for a quarter of an hour by a cat that kept running between his legs. The man said to the animal: "Pussycat, pussycat." When the man got home, the cat was gone.
168162: Fin claimed that her dead mother had appeared to her at night. The people around her did not believe it.
168172: In catechism class there was a boy who could make mice by throwing his cap on the floor. The priest took the boy's art away from him.
168177: A farmer's potatoes were full of Colorado beetles. So the farmer told Fien that she would have to buy her potatoes elsewhere that year. The next day all the beetles lay dead on the ground. Although no one had ever told Fien about the beetles, she came by right afterwards and suggested that surely she could get potatoes now. So Fien must really have been a witch.
168178: A man who had gone to mow the corn at harvest time saw, on his way back, a man on horseback flying through the sky with a sabre in his hands.
168180: At the Slagmolen in Opitter lived a sixteen-year-old girl whose father was an oil miller. One day a little old woman came to the girl to buy oil. When the woman saw two young lambs in the garden, she said to the girl: "Betje, you must give me one of those." Because the girl refused, the woman tapped Betje's hand with her fingers and said: "You'll regret that." After the woman had left, the girl noticed a death mark on her hand. The spot hurt and would not heal. When after a few weeks the girl went with her father to the healer of Genk, he said: "Ha Jan, are you here with the girl? Had you waited another eight days, she would be lying in the churchyard. Your daughter must go on pilgrimage nine times to Sint-Servaas in Maastricht. She must also pray a novena every evening. On the ninth day the witch will stand at the window." And so it happened.
168186: In Heerenelderen there once lived seventeen witches and seventeen sorcerers. They could turn themselves into magpies and would then sit in the trees. When people saw those witches, they fled. In Heerenelderen many people had ailments in their legs. Those ailments were caused by the witches and sorcerers.
168189: A man walking through Rutten around midnight heard music in a meadow. Six or seven women were dancing there with a cup in their hands. The man walked up to the women, also took a cup and said: "Dear Lord, Christ, God, heaven!" The next moment all the women had vanished. Because the man was left alone in the field, he went to sleep in a nearby mill. The next morning the man went to the field with the miller. Where the women had danced, the grass was completely flattened. The following day two women from Rutten came to beg the man to give back the cup. One of them was a witch.
168199: A farmhand who worked for a farmer had special powers, so that all the work got done by itself. The farmhand had to roam about at night as a werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent to Meeuwen to mow a heath. Meanwhile the oven was lit to burn the farmhand's animal skin. Even before the skin could be thrown into the fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven.
168203: In the Dalemolen there was a man possessed by the devil. In all, seven priests were sent for to exorcise the man. The last priest was kicked to death by the man. After his death, however, the priest came in the form of a ghost to turn the mill sails.
168205: The farm of the H. family in Montenaken was haunted. In the morning the cattle had been untied, and often there was a noise as if plates were being smashed. The people were desperate and went for advice to a brave man from the neighbourhood. The man went into the farm and asked the ghost, "In the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, what do you want?", whereupon a voice answered, "I was promised a mass, but I never got it. As long as that has not happened, my soul cannot find rest." When the people of the farm had had a mass said for the dead person, all remained quiet at the H. family's.
168210: A farmer's wife and her daughter could not manage to make butter. "There's a witch in the churn," the farmer's wife concluded. The priests of Hasselt then gave her something to put in the butter churn. They also predicted that the witch would come by, but the farmer's wife must not get angry then. After that the evil hand was gone.
168215: In Neerrepen stood a house where a black dog always lay under the table. After the house had been exorcised, the dog stayed away.
168225: A farmer was herding the oxen in the field while his two daughters had to herd the cows. In a nearby meadow walked a woman from the village who was said to be a witch. When one girl went to fetch one of the cows from the witch's meadow, to her great fright she saw an animal like a goat walking with its horns close to the ground. Behind the animal rolled something that looked like a lump of butter. Terrified, the girls ran home. Their father believed the witch was responsible for the children's fear and had the parish priest come to exorcise the house. In winter the farmer had tied a lamb up in the barn. But at night the lamb had broken loose and stood bleating beside the farmer's bed. The farmer chased the animal away and shut it in the kitchen. The next morning he found that the lamb was still tied up in the barn.
168233: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil, who helped him with his work. Because the man wanted to break the pact, he had been advised to give the devil a task he could not possibly accomplish. The farmer brought the devil a barrel of spurrey seed, which he had to scoop out down to the last grain. Because the devil could not do that work, the man was free.
168243: A child that had not been baptised properly could later make mice. The child had become a witch.
168244: In Odeur lived a little boy who could make mice. After the priest had baptised the child, it could no longer make mice.
168264: When Edgard was ten years old, the witch Mina C. called: "Come here, you'll get a cake from auntie!" The witch stroked Edgard's head, after which the child eagerly ate the cake. A few days later little Edgard had warts all over his head. Matthieuke was able to free the child from the evil hand.
168288: A young man from Martenslinde went to visit his girlfriend in Hoelbeek. When he knocked, however, nobody opened the door. A little later three cats jumped in through the window. Then the girl's mother opened the door and said: "We were just baking cake. Would you like a piece?" The young man took the cake and put it in his pocket. The next day he found a toad in his pocket. "If you had nicely eaten the cake, you would have had nothing to reproach us for!" the witches said afterwards.
168309: A woman had already had five children, who had died immediately after birth. When the man went to fetch the doctor because his wife was about to give birth for the sixth time, on the way he met a partisan soldier, who wanted to know where he was going. "I'm going to the doctor, because my wife is giving birth. The five children she had before died ten minutes after the delivery." "If that's so," the soldier replied, "then I'll come along with you." In the house the soldier sat on a chair close to the hole through which the dirty water drained outside. During the birth the soldier struck along the wall with his sabre and said: "It will go well now, madam." The next moment a severed hand lay on the floor. The miller's wife lay wounded in bed. When the miller discovered what his wife had been doing all those years, he split her skull with an axe.
168310: When a werewolf jumped on someone's back, he put his paws on the shoulders and his head beside the carrier's head. In this way the werewolf cut off the carrier's breath.
168320: Two men who had been to the café went home together in the evening. Suddenly one of the men said: "I am a werewolf, and when I start, you must throw a handkerchief at me." When the man turned into a werewolf at midnight, the other almost beat him to death.
168321: A man from Dorplein often saw a strange light that changed shape and colour and moved in the direction of the zinc factory.
168322: In Linkhout lived a boy who could make mice. After the priest had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer do it.
168323: A farmer from Kotem sent for the friars because all his animals were dying. After the friars had said prayers over the stable and placed a medal under the threshold, the farmer had no more misfortune.
168342: In the old days witches flew through the air with the words: "Over hedge and bush, all the way to Cologne".
168343: Two men sitting in a café saw some old women scooping water from a well with a basket. The women had to be witches, because they were strong enough to carry a basket full of water up. After all, witches could do anything because they consorted with the devil.
168354: Two men who were innocently in prison prayed to Our Lady every day. One day the prisoners found themselves, with the chains and shackles on their hands and feet, before the altar of Our Lady of Tongeren.
168362: A woman in bed suddenly felt a tightness that left her unable to scream or call for help. Her husband chased the ghost away with a knife.
168364: Someone had seen a woman who could conjure up tailless mice.
168369: A man from Berg went to a concert in Herderen. When the man walked home around midnight, he met an ugly thin woman with a headscarf, dressed in black and carrying a stick. A little further on the man heard the trees creak as if a hundred thousand crows were sitting in them. The man must have been under the influence of the evil hand.
168388: A boy had fallen ill after being bewitched. People prayed for the boy, but it did not help. When the witch came in one day, the boy died through the work of the evil hand.
168390: When Nolke N. was coming back at night from the fair in Vlijtingen, he had to carry the werewolf. The next morning the man found that he had ended up in Valmeer.
168393: A man returning by moonlight from Hazelbroek in Waremme saw in the distance a tall woman in a black rustling dress. Because the woman came from Wallonia, the man said: "Bonsoir madame", to which the woman answered: "Taisez-vous, moi la nuit et vous le jour" (Be quiet, the night for me and the day for you). The man was terrified.
168394: A mother often had a mass said for her dead son, whom she hoped was in heaven.
