When the woman entered the church one day, a well-dressed gentleman walked up to her and said: "You need not have any more masses said, for I am in my place". When the young man spoke, the woman recognised her dead son.
168399: A woman who was going somewhere was followed along the way by a little kitten that kept mewing. The woman picked up the kitten and carried it in her apron. The bundle in her apron grew heavier and heavier. A little later the woman found that there was a boulder in her apron.
168411: On the barrier gate in the meadow sat a black cat that said: "Don't come this way, or else your house will have burned down before you get home."
168417: When someone was ill, people believed the sick person had been struck by the evil hand.
168418: In the Molenveld in Stokkem a child got a hump through the doing of a witch. In the end the child died.
168426: A man coming back in the evening from visiting his girlfriend saw a strange fire beside the road that looked like a cow kettle. A kilometre further on the man saw the fire again. A little further still the man saw a goat by the road.
168429: Whenever Metje van Millen threw a handful of earth on the floor, the living room was full of mice in no time.
168431: In Buvingen a dead woman came haunting her children. The widower went to the Friars Minor in Sint-Truiden, who told him the children should ask the ghost what it wanted. The ghost answered: "Whoever has done well will gain well." After the mother's wish had been fulfilled, the ghost no longer appeared.
168435: Lemme's first wife came back to haunt after her death, because Lemme had appropriated property belonging to his first wife's family. After Lemme had made peace with that family, the woman no longer came haunting.
168436: A house in Piringen was haunted. At night strange noises were always heard there, and in the morning a shirt was found in the barn.
168437: Near the windmill in Boorsem someone could often be heard calling at night: "Where shall I put it, where shall I put it?" One day someone answered: "Put it where you took it from!" With that the ghost was released.
168440: At All Saints and All Souls, people everywhere in Romershoven lit candles so that the will-o'-the-wisps floating about the fields would have light to see by.
168444: During the winter someone always had to carry the werewolf in the evening near the Pekelshof. One day a man saw a shepherd jump onto a tree stump, put on a band and chains with bells, and run off. The man told everything to a farmer of the Pekelshof. A week later the man and the farmer sent the shepherd to the Steenkuil. Meanwhile the man heated the oven and the farmer fetched the werewolf's band from the tree stump. The moment the farmer threw the band into the oven, the werewolf was standing behind him.
168459: After Bet K. had stroked the children's heads, they were full of lice. People had to have prayers read over their children by the Friars Minor in Hasselt. The superior gave the parents a relic to put under the threshold. Because of that, Bet K. could no longer come in.
168460: Witches could infest people with lice. A man from Gelmen had a little child that cried day and night. Someone advised the man to take the mattress and pillows to the meadow at midnight and set everything on fire. In the mattress the man found lots of roses. If such a wreath of roses was closed, the child would die, so people said. Less than twenty years ago some people in Borgloon were seen burning mattresses in their garden at midnight.
168471: Three soldiers who went to eat at a farmer's house learned that the farmer's wife was lying sick in bed. One of the soldiers found that the woman was not ill but had been struck by the evil hand. That night the soldier kept watch with his sabre by the water drain hole. When a cat appeared, the soldier struck at the animal with his sabre. The next day a neighbour woman wore a bandage around her arm. She was a witch.
168475: A farmer whose horses were all dying went to the parish priest for advice. When the horse began behaving strangely again, the priest stood by the animal and began to pray. After a quarter of an hour the horse had calmed down. From then on the farmer was no longer tormented by the evil hand.
168477: In a village lived a woman who was said to be a witch. Some boys wanted to put it to the test. When the woman walked past one day, a boy made the sign of the cross over her footprints with a stick. The witch looked round.
168480: A man walking home late heard something ringing in the chapel beside which someone lay buried.
168494: A boy who had insulted a witch was struck by the sorceress. Shortly afterwards the boy fell ill and in the end he died. Roses were found in the boy's pillow.
168497: A farmer who was never satisfied with the land he owned regularly moved the boundary posts of his field. When the farmer had died, he could find no rest and wandered the fields at night with a boundary post on his back. He kept sighing: "Where shall I put it?" One day the ghost met a man who said: "Well dammit, just put the post back where you fetched it from!" Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
168498: During catechism class a boy threw some earth on the floor. After he had blown over the earth, lots of mice appeared. The other children told the priest what they had seen. But because the priest did not know what to do, the boy's parents sent for the friars of Hasselt. When the friars had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
168506: In a house that a witch had just entered, a relic was laid by the door. When the witch left, she went out through the stable door. That witch could change herself into a hare, a rabbit or a magpie.
168521: A man who was always drunk cursed all the time. When the man came home one night, he saw a big black dog lying under the table. At that the man fell to his knees and began to pray. In the end the dog disappeared again.
168524: A girl from 't Louwel could make tailless mice. She took some earth in her hand and said "There, mouse, run!", and then the earth turned into a mouse. The priest made sure the girl could no longer make mice.
168538: A certain Kièn from Houthalen came haunting after his death. The ghost sat on a horse standing on a heap.
168540: A man who just could not manage to shoot a hare went to the priest for advice. The priest said: "First put the shot in your mouth. Then you'll be able to hit the hare!" When the man did so, the hare turned into a woman from the neighbourhood.
168546: A farmer had bought a piglet at the market in Bree. As the farmer went home with the piglet, he met a woman who asked him for a sandwich. But the man had no sandwich left. The woman then stroked the piglet's rear and went on. When the farmer got home, the piglet was almost dead.
168548: A witch lived in the Broekstraat in Vechmaal. A man taking his horse to the smith suddenly could not go any further, so he had to take another road.
168555: A man went from Neeroeteren to Maaseik around half past eight in the evening. On the bridge of Neeroeteren the man always heard a loud creaking, which only stopped once the man was past the bridge.
168572: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of the windmill field between Boorsem and Opgrimbie could no longer sleep at night. The farmer suspected his sleeplessness had something to do with moving the post, but he could no longer remember exactly where it had stood before. A few days later the farmer heard a voice within him saying: "Put it where you fetched it from!" After the farmer had put the boundary post back, he could sleep peacefully again.
168579: In the farm of Willeme B. in Elch a rattling was always heard in the attic at night. The children were thrown out of their beds and the horses were untied. Even something strange was going on with the water.
168580: A boy from Meeswijk worked at the mill in Leut. When he came home in winter, the werewolf jumped on his neck.
168589: A man had to keep watch over a mortally ill boy. A cat always came and sat in the boy's room, coming in through the drain. One evening the cat was there again. The boy sighed briefly and died the next moment. At that moment the candle at the head of the boy's bed went out.
168602: The Kattestraat in Hechtel was haunted. A man who had been to confession had seen a strange apparition with glowing eyes sitting in the hedge there.
168609:
You must never beckon to a will-o'-the-wisp, because then many will-o'-the-wisps would come at you.
A man once managed to release a soul by saying: "I baptise you alone." At that the will-o'-the-wisp shot upwards and then vanished.
168626: Jef van de S. had hanged himself because his wife had run away. After Jef's death many people saw the suicide's soul wandering about. After someone asked the ghost what it needed, the dead man was not seen again.
168627: A father whose son was good for nothing had often said: "You must get out of here! Even if I have to sell you to the devil!" When one day the father was walking with his son along a sunken lane, a coach stopped beside them. In the coach sat a man who asked: "Say, won't you let your son work for me?", to which the father replied: "That's just what we were on our way for. Take him with you right away!" The man let the son get in and said: "Next year I'll bring him back to this place." A year later the father went to fetch his son at the agreed place. "What did you have to do, boy?" asked the parents. The boy answered: "Father, you always said you would even sell me to the devil. Well, that has now happened. I stood at the gate of hell the whole time." Because his parents did not believe him at first, the boy went on: "I'll prove it. Didn't such and such people die this past year? I had to let them all into hell."
168633: The place by the big stone was haunted. A man who went behind a bush there to relieve himself was suddenly jumped by a werewolf. The man was so frightened that he dropped dead on the spot. He had only three coins in his pocket. If he had had the chance to wound the werewolf, the beast would have turned into a human.
168660: When many children in a family had died, people believed the mother was a witch.
168678: The lord of the castle of Damerus owned a ghost table. When the little table was thrown into the fountain outside, it came back inside by itself in no time.
168687: In Sint-Jesushoven a will-o'-the-wisp appeared at the place where a woman had been murdered.
168690: One day a young man in Koninksem went to visit his girlfriend. In Piringen, at the crossroads with the road to Widooie, the man was attacked by a dog. After a long fight the man could go on, because the werewolf could not cross the crossroads. Whoever could make a werewolf bleed could recognise him.
168704: In Maaseik a witch had given three boys lice because they had laughed at her.
168709: A woman from Kerkom often went to a shop near Sint-Pieter in Sint-Truiden. Because the shopkeeper's little child fell ill, on a friar's advice a relic was placed under the threshold. After that the witch could no longer come in and the child recovered.
168714: The hunchback Janneke M. was coming back on Sunday evening from the fair in Wouteringen when he heard beautiful music in a garden. The drunk man came closer and saw the witches dancing and singing: "Sunday, Monday, Sunday, Monday..." Janneke joined the witches' dance and sang: "Tuesday!" Suddenly all the witches stood still. The old witch came down from her throne and ordered one of the witches to free Janneke of his hump; after all, he had taught the witches a new day, and so he deserved a reward. The next day Janneke was walking through the village without his hump when another hunchback from Lauw asked him how he had lost it. The following Monday the other hunchback also went to that garden after the fair. The man joined the witches' dance and sang: "Tuesday!" This time too the old witch came down from her throne. But this man deserved no reward, rather a punishment: he got the other hunchback's hump on his belly, so that he now had two humps!
168724: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had not been baptised because they were stillborn. Will-o'-the-wisps floated between heaven and hell. They looked like little red glow-worms. When a child was born, people baptised it themselves to be safe. After all, the catechism says that anyone may baptise in times of need.
168735: Marjan's little son had got lice after a witch had stroked the child's head. The mother had washed the child's hair, but the next day the boy had lice again. After the mother had washed the child's head with holy water, the lice were gone for good.
168738: A man returning late in the evening from a rehearsal in Rolen had to relieve himself on the way. As the man squatted behind a bush, a dog suddenly jumped on his back. After the man had wounded the animal in the place where it had been baptised, the dog changed into a beggar from Maastricht who had often been given sandwiches by the man. "Don't tell anyone about this, or you'll have more to deal with!" the beggar said to the man. After a while the man told the priest what had happened to him.
168751: At the Heilige Haag between Vlijtingen and Hees a big dog appeared after midnight and made passers-by carry it all the way to Vlijtingen. That was the werewolf.
168757: Muize Giel could make mice appear from his handkerchief. The priest wanted to rid Giel of his magic and asked the boy to make some mice for him too. The first time it still worked effortlessly. The second time, however, the boy's mice had no tails. The third time Giel could not make any mice at all.
168759: A man from Vliermaal who could not believe that the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a legendary robber band) flew through the air on a goat exclaimed: "I wish I could see that goat for once!" As the man walked home, a beautifully decorated goat suddenly stood in the road. The man sat on the animal's back and said: "To Rome, straight to Rome!" No sooner had he spoken than the goat set off at full speed for Rome. The animal ran through hedges and hawthorns and let no obstacle stop it. Luckily the man got caught on a branch while the goat ran on.
168764: Near the Klotkoeter a dead lady came haunting.
168769: Some women, among them a suspected witch, were digging up potatoes. Suddenly some of the women heard a fluttering. Only the witch's clogs were still standing there.
168800: A man came past a witch's house with a wagon full of straw. A little further on the wagon tipped over, so that the straw fell into the brook.
168804: A farmer could drive away rats by walking around the farm praying. The farmer had to leave one stretch open so that the rats could run away that way. A plague of rats was often caused by a witch.
168806: A house in Lauw was haunted. When people went to look, there was never anything the matter.
168807: A man who had moved a boundary post of his field came back to haunt after his death, saying: "Where do I put it, where do I leave it, where do I put it, where do I leave it." One evening a drunkard answered: "Put it where you took it from. God will reward you." Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
168831: A farmhand who slept in the horse stable was woken at night by the screeching of the cats dancing in the meadow.
168837: One day a woman saw a will-o'-the-wisp that tried to lead her astray. People said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
168855: Because the farmer's wife could not manage to churn butter, farmer Frans went to his aunt for advice. The aunt went along with Frans and was able to make butter after only five minutes of churning. The day before, the aunt had bewitched the cows.
168859: On a farm in Sint-Lambrechts-Herk a large dog came and lay under the table every evening. Once a chapel had been built there, the dog was no longer seen.
168881: A woman came back to haunt after her death because she had vowed to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. After others had gone on the pilgrimage for her, the ghost was released.
168882: On Christmas Day a woman from Dorne walked to Niel to go to mass there. On the way the woman was pestered by a cat that kept getting under her feet. When the woman kicked the cat, the animal scratched her. The wound never healed.
168887:
One of the D. brothers from Tongeren had a reputation for never wanting to pay in an inn. One day this brother went to the inn with a friend, where the innkeeper began to insist: "Johannes, you really must pay me now!" D. turned up his nose, threw some money on the table and asked the innkeeper: "Does the door of this inn shut properly?" The innkeeper answered: "Certainly, with a latch, a lock and a bolt!" D. ordered the innkeeper to shut his door properly, and then went outside with his friend. D. sent his friend away for a few minutes and meanwhile took out his handkerchief. When the friend was back, D. asked him to shake out the handkerchief and then put it back on his hand. Then D. shouted: "Out of the way!" and threw the handkerchief at the door of the inn, which promptly fell down, latch, lock, bolt and all. After that the friend wanted nothing more to do with D.
The other D. brother also had strange powers. One day he was arrested by the police on the Nieuwmarkt in Loon and left handcuffed at the town hall, guarded by four men. "Couldn't we get a glass of beer?" asked D., to which the men replied: "There's plenty of beer in the inn, but we wouldn't dream of paying for it for you!" Then D. took off his handcuffs himself, gave the men two francs to buy beer and put his handcuffs back on. When D. was taken to Tongeren by cart the next day, he met his brother Johannes. Johannes asked him: "Brother, do you want to be free?", to which the brother answered: "No, not yet." Johannes asked once more, but his brother refused again. The next day the imprisoned D. brother had vanished without a trace.
168899: A man who slept in a horse stable was ridden at night by the maar (nightmare spirit), which nearly smothered him.
168911: A lord of Herkenrode had died without confessing. People said that after his death the lord rode through the lane on his donkey.
168915:
Near Sint-Truiden stands the Blauwe Schuur (Blue Barn), a barn built by the devil.
A farmer who had too little room in his barn to store his grain cried out in anger: "I need another barn, even if it's one from the devil!" A while later a gallant gentleman came by and said: "I will build a barn for you. If you like, it can be standing before the cock crows tomorrow morning. In return I want your soul." The farmer agreed to the proposal and went home. But when the farmer lay in bed that evening he could not sleep, and in the end he confessed the whole story to his wife. The clever farmer's wife asked: "Does the barn have to be finished before the cock has crowed?", and the farmer nodded. At that the wife jumped out of bed, opened the window and began clapping her hands to wake the cock. When the cock began to crow, the devil furiously struck the unfinished barn with his fist. The hole in the wall that had not yet been closed could never be built up.
168916: A farmer's wife whose animals were all dying discovered a strange beast in the stable one day. When the woman had caught the beast, it suddenly disappeared again.
168921: A witch who went to her stable at midnight found that her horse was dead. Because the witch suspected some people from the neighbourhood, she went and gave those people lice.
168923: A woman could never keep her child quiet when her husband left for work. At that moment a cat was always miaowing nearby. One day the man pretended to leave, only to sneak back home a little later. Meanwhile the cat was already in the house. Although the child had just been given a clean nappy, the cloth was completely full of lice. The man sent for a friar to read prayers over the child. While the friar was praying, the witch came in. From that day on the witch could no longer get into the house.
168927: A man from Veerle had locked the witches in the church. One of the witches had said: "We'll get you yet!" When the man walked home on Sunday night, he came across dozens of frogs and toads. The next day the man had such a bad fall that he almost broke his leg.
168950: In Corswarem there once lived a man who could turn himself into a calf.
168953: A few days after Lien had given something to a beggar woman, her head began to itch. The maid Anna found that Lien had lice. After the maid had combed Lien's hair thoroughly, the girl still itched. When Lien told her grandmother what had happened, the woman said: "Oh, my child, that woman must have bewitched you!" After Lien had prayed a novena with her grandmother, she was rid of the lice.
168968: A man going from Rutten to Lauw met a cat that blocked his way. The man could not get rid of the cat and after a while he got lost. When it grew light in the morning, the man went back to Rutten. There a woman advised him to put his coat on inside out. Then he would find the way.
168978: At his friend's house a man heard a sound as if a regiment of officers was passing by. Suddenly the stable door flew open and one of the cows sighed loudly.
168993: In Vechmaal an unbelieving man had died. At midnight there was always a dog howling opposite the man's grave.
169005: In Heppeneert lived a knight who spent all his money on drink and card games. When the knight had lost all his money, he sold his soul to the devil. In exchange for his soul the knight was allowed to live for fifteen years without want. Because the knight had been raised Catholic, he had the habit of burning a candle every evening for Saint Gertrude. Fifteen years later the knight gave a great feast for all his friends one evening, after which he had to go to the devil. He rode his horse to the Sint-Geerterbrug (Saint Gertrude's Bridge?). The knight said to the devil, who sat beside the bridge: "It is two minutes to twelve. In a few minutes our contract is over. If you want me then, you can take me. Otherwise I go where I please." The devil said to the knight: "Chase away that black witch sitting behind you on your horse, for like this I have no power over you." A few minutes after midnight the knight said: "Time is up" and rode back home. The knight had been protected by Saint Gertrude, who had come to sit behind him on his horse. In the little church of Heppeneert one can still see the knight and Saint Gertrude standing. The knight's gravestone was walled into the church wall. Hearts and diamonds were depicted on the stone.
169011: A man who had been playing cards was walking home in the evening. On the way he saw a white ghost with a post on its back. Because the ghost called: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?", the man answered: "Put it where you fetched it from!" After that the ghost was never seen again.
169014: A man had struck a cat. The next day a woman was walking around with a broken arm.
169017: A farmer always had bad luck. His wife had died and he could not keep any of his animals alive. When his daughter Valerieke was seven, she got a stiff knee. Doctors could not cure the knee, and even the wizard from Zepperen was at a loss. The girl went to sleep around eight and then woke around ten screaming with pain. Only around three could Valerieke get back to sleep. People said that a woman from Sint-Truiden who kept coming to ask for all sorts of things was responsible for this misfortune. The farmer asked one of his other daughters to go to the Monnebruurs (friars) in Sint-Truiden. One evening the friars came to say prayers over the whole house and sprinkle it with holy water. When the friars came to Valerieke's bed, they asked what was wrong, but they answered: "It is all in your mind. It is not real." Still, they said prayers over Valerieke too. Before the friars left, they told everyone to pray well every evening. When they did, Valerieke slept peacefully until morning, but the stiff knee never really healed.
169034: A woman came to help a farmer's wife churn butter. After the woman had left, the farmer's wife could no longer make butter. That woman was a witch.
169041: A poacher who saw a hare approaching put his gun to his shoulder and got ready to shoot. Then the hare said: "Say, did the other one pass long ago?" The poacher was so frightened that he went home immediately.
169044: In the past, will-o'-the-wisps were often seen near meadows, marshes and ponds. People said they were the souls of unbaptised children.
169052: Some people were ridden all night long by the Mowej (nightmare spirit).
169064: Werewolves often jumped on people's backs and made them carry them. One day a man got the chance to wound the werewolf. The beast immediately changed into a human.
169071: At the 'Duivelskruis' (Devil's Cross) on the road from Hoesselt to Hern sat a black cat. A man passing by struck at the cat several times. The animal, however, kept coming back. It looked as if the cat was spitting fire.
169076: At S.'s place in 't Kortstraatje stood a werewolf that still had a piece of a red handkerchief between its teeth. The day before, a man had thrown his handkerchief at the beast.
169082: Two boys going to the village by moonlight had to pass a haunted spot. A white lady came out of the woods and disappeared into the woods again on the other side of the road. The lady had no legs and floated above the ground.
169101: In Gessel there lived a witch who caused people a lot of trouble. A man peddling shop goods met the witch. The witch felt the man and his goods and said: "Well, Frans, it's getting late. You should go home!" When the man came to a stretch of water, however, he could not get across. Only the next morning could the man go on again.
169113: Some men coming back from Stokrooie between midnight and one o'clock saw a dog with glowing eyes coming towards them. The dog's eyes grew bigger and bigger. The dog the man had with him did not see the phantom animal. When the man later told his mother what he had seen, she answered: "Yes, between twelve and one all the evil rabble is about!"
169122: In Schalkhoven the dead owner of the castle always came haunting in the castle lane.
169143: A man got lice through a witch's doing.
169145: A woman had seen all her children die shortly after birth because a toad had come into the house during the delivery. At the next delivery someone chopped off the toad's front legs. The child lived, but the woman's mother had lost both her arms.
169146: A man was surrounded by strange animals that looked like pigs. When the man took out his gun, the animals ran away.
169154: A farmhand who worked on a farm owned a straw band with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. When the farmhand discovered one day that the farmer's wife wanted to burn his band, he nearly went mad.
169184: In the church of Berlingen Saint Agatha is venerated. In the village there is also a spring called the Sint-Agathabron. The water of that spring is ice-cold in summer and very warm in winter. One day the statue of Saint Agatha was found in the church with a soiled mantle. The statue had gone to the spring of its own accord, and since then the spring was called the Sint-Agathabron. The road the statue had walked along was called the Sint-Agathaweg.
169188: Whenever Jefke met the witch 'Zwarte Kruispot' while out with his pig, the animal refused to go any further.
169190: A man walking from Maasmechelen to Opgrimbie one evening saw a black cat sitting on a turnstile. Because the man believed the cat was a witch, he took a detour.
169197: If one drew a little cross on a witch's footprints, the witch had to look round. That is how some boys found out that Zwarte Fles was a witch.
169199: Someone who could not manage to make butter suddenly saw the butter dripping down the wall. The butter was bewitched.
169210: Pie V.S., a farmhand working in Herk, could make mice from a handful of earth. The priest made the man believe he could make much finer mice if he let himself be baptised. When the man had been baptised, he could no longer make mice.
169211: A troop of soldiers going from Hasselt to Maaseik at night were frightened when they met a dog with a chain on the Galgenheuvel. The soldiers believed the dog was really the devil, guarding the place.
169215: In Rutten a pig without a tail walked the streets. If you could hit the pig, it became human again.
169218: One day Pieter N. went poaching towards Herk-de-Stad. He shot a hare and put it in a sack on his shoulder. A little later Pieter met another hare, which said: "Where are you, where are you?", to which the hare in the sack answered: "In Pieter N.'s sack." Pieter hurried to let the hare out of the sack, for he was convinced this was witchcraft.
169221: A maid who was binding the harvest in the field muttered: "You'd be better off working for the devil than for a boss like this." The next moment a gentleman came up to her and said: "I'll bind the whole field for you, on condition that I get whatever you bind first tomorrow." The maid accepted the gentleman's proposal. Instead of first binding her clothes around herself, the next morning the maid bound something else and threw it to the gentleman. At that the devil began to shout angrily.
169236: In a sunken lane in Melveren there used to be a werewolf. One day Bona, a young man of twenty-five, was walking through the sunken lane when suddenly a werewolf jumped on his back. The creature's paws looked like those of a calf. Bona knew from his mother that he had to pray the Gospel of Saint John to get rid of the werewolf. And indeed, the creature vanished. When the young man came home trembling with fright, he had his mother sprinkle him with holy water at once. His mother, who came from Zepperen, had once seen a werewolf too. After she had gone for help, some men wounded the creature with a sickle. When the werewolf lost blood, he took on his human form again. He turned out to be a man from Zepperen.
169243: A drunkard who wanted to drink wine made a mistake when speaking the witches' formula and said: "Through hedge and hawthorn..." The man arrived at his destination badly injured.
169260: A merchant setting off with his cart in the morning saw a black cat cross the road at the Geebroek. The merchant went straight back home, for it could not be a good day for doing business.
169264: On a farm cats came to drink up the milk every night. One night the farmhand struck one of the cats in the teeth. It turned out to be the farmer's wife.
169278: Will-o'-the-wisps were luminous gases rising from the marshes. But people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. Anyone who had whistled at a will-o'-the-wisp was chased by the light. A man who had fled indoors from a will-o'-the-wisp heard a loud thud. When the man went to look, he saw that a bloody hand had been burnt into the door.
169285: A man who had got lost at night suddenly fell into a nest of hair. It must have been witches' hair.
169298: Magpies and owls brought bad luck. In Millen a mother was getting her daughter ready for her wedding when a magpie called outside. The future bride's sister then said: "Do you hear that? You're not done with this yet!" When the girl arrived at the church, the priest announced that he could not bless a marriage unless a letter from the dean was presented. Because the letter had to be fetched from Tongeren or Borgloon, the girl could not marry until the afternoon.
169311: A man who got up at night and went downstairs saw a strange figure sitting on the stove. It was a woman wearing white clothes with a veil over her head. The frightened man quickly went on. When he came back into the room a little later, the apparition had vanished. Afterwards the man realised that he should have asked what the woman wanted. But he had not dared, for fear that it was a woman who lived a little further on. The next day the man asked that woman whether she had got up the night before. The woman answered: "No."
169331: People whose dog had been stolen went to a clairvoyant. The clairvoyant showed the people in a mirror how the dog had been stolen and who had done it.
169344: A girl and a boy who had been courting for a long time went to Hasselt to buy wedding rings. On the way back the girl unmasked her boyfriend as a werewolf. The girl no longer wanted to marry, not even after a friar had tried to persuade her.
169346: In Maaseik a man heard a clergyman preach about the evil in Congo and other countries where the devil still had a strong hold on people. In the past this had been the case in Belgium too. A man from Neeroeteren could load as much wood onto his cart as he liked; the horse could always pull the load. One day the man met a clergyman, who said: "But lad, how much wood have you put on your cart!" At that moment the horse stopped. The horse would only go on after the clergyman had walked past.
169355: A widower had a woman look after his children when he went to work. But the woman harmed the children and conjured filth into the butter. On a friend's advice the widower went to the friars of Hasselt, who said: "A woman who comes to your house every day is responsible for the misfortune. You must not let her come any more. I will give you something to put under the threshold. Then the witch will no longer be able to come in." When the man had followed the friar's advice, the witch indeed could no longer get in. She became very angry, but after a while she went away.
169359:
A seller walked at midnight on the 'Hoese-Kassei' between Odeur and Rutten. He had a black hen with him, which he wanted to sell to the devil for a lot of money. The devil always appeared on a cart drawn by two dogs.
One night, when the man had brought the devil a white hen, the devil had said: "Now I'm taking you with me!" The man had replied: "Yes, you can do all sorts of things, can't you! You can make yourself big and you can make yourself small. But can you make yourself as small as my purse?" The devil then changed into a little creature even smaller than the purse. The man immediately put the devil in his purse and killed the little creature with his hammer.
169361: At the 'Quatre-Bras' in Lantermangen church hymns were often heard being sung. It was said that they were ghostly priests who came to say the masses they had been unable to say during their lives.
169362: The werewolf was a man who was possessed and tormented people. He disguised himself so that nobody could recognise him when he jumped on passers-by. One day a man who was jumped by the werewolf pulled out a knife. At that moment the werewolf lost his disguise and said: "Don't betray me, or you're done for!" Since then that man was never troubled by a werewolf again. Werewolves often chose as victims people who had to fetch the midwife or the doctor at night.
169368: In Lauw two old women lived in a small house. One evening some men, among them the baker, secretly went into the meadow to shake the two women's plum tree. Although the men heard the plums falling, they did not see a single one. When they wanted to leave the meadow, it seemed as if they were held back by a wall. Strangely enough, the next morning the men did see the plums lying there. The baker was so frightened by the incident that he got jaundice and died shortly afterwards. After that people said that those two women were witches.
169383: A man who had murdered a woman came back to haunt Klotbroek in the form of a fire-man.
169386: Ida often kept company with a woman who was said to be a witch. One day, however, Ida fell seriously ill. Just in time Dean H. was sent for to say prayers over her. Otherwise she would certainly have died.
169389: On the Eetseveld, Reinder and Geertrui lay deathly ill in bed. When the procession to Cobbeberg came through the Valkuilenstraat, doctor V. and doctor R. had to leave the company to go and see the sick. The friar who had visited Reinder and Geertrui had said: "Those two will not die." The friar advised the sick not to lend anything to anyone any more. For a woman lived nearby who often came to ask for milk or scissors. Shortly afterwards Reinder and Geertrui recovered.
169395: The little daughter of a family from Kozen was gravely ill. The father went for advice to a sorcerer, but he said that the child's mother had to come. The mother, however, would not leave her daughter's sickbed. So the sorcerer asked the father to bring him the child, together with the mattress she slept on. The sorcerer examined the mattress thoroughly and pulled out some feathers and a strange doll. The doll did not have eyes yet, because then the girl would already be dead, the sorcerer explained. The feathers came from stolen hens, because a witch had to work with things she had taken unlawfully. The sorcerer went with the feathers and the doll to the parish priest, but he could not help. Next he went to the friars of Hasselt, who were said to have great power. The friars of Hasselt took the mother's powers away from her.
169400: The maar (nightmare spirit) was a nightmare caused by something lying heavy on the stomach.
169412: In Sluizen lived a farmhand who could work magic because he consorted with the devil. When the farmhands were sent to the field to bind the hay, the wizard said: "Let's sit here a while; we'll get it done." Then the farmhand bound one bundle of hay and said: "All like this." In no time all the hay was bound.
169414: A witch was cutting fodder for her animals on a farmer's land. When the farmer saw this, he walked towards the witch to teach her a lesson. Before the farmer reached her, the witch had turned herself into a little birch bush. Angrily the farmer struck the bush with his cudgel. A few days later the farmer met a woman who had bruises on her face.
169416: Tine S. was a witch who came to say healing prayers over sick animals.
169431: On the Vlooienberg in Tongeren there used to be four little houses that were haunted. One night the police decided to investigate. The policemen sat with a paraffin lamp in the large attic shared by the four houses. Suddenly they saw a brick come out of the wall by itself and float into the glass of the paraffin lamp without the flame going out. Terrified, the policemen fled. Even the stones in the street flew up by themselves.
169443: A man who always went off somewhere at ten o'clock in the evening aroused his friends' suspicion. One evening his friends followed the man into the woods, where they could spy on him. In the bright moonlight the man went through a ditch to a tree stump, climbed onto it and a little later came down from it as a werewolf. Between midnight and one o'clock the werewolf roamed through the woods. Meanwhile the frightened friends secretly took away the man's clothes. When the werewolf came back and could not find his clothes, he flew away through the air. The friends heard a jingling as if the werewolf wore bells around his neck. After that night the man was never seen again.
169452: Anyone ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night suffered terrible pains. But if one took a piece of steel to bed, one was never troubled by the maar.
169469: Some men went to fetch a gravestone for a man from the Bolderberg who had died. On the way the men suddenly saw a figure appear in the woods. The ghost of the dead priest came forward, looked at the stone and then vanished again.
169472: Children who had died unbaptised floated about at night as will-o'-the-wisps.
169473: Farmer Willeke B. had always been a peaceable man. But when one day the farmer had a black cat, he changed completely. Willeke went to the inns and spoke ill of everyone. After Neel V.G. had shot the black cat dead, Willeke was his old self again.
169483: In the old Commandery of Bernissem stood the gravestone of the 'commedur' (commander), who came haunting. People believed the man haunted because his Commandery had once been sold as confiscated church property and was later used as a sugar factory.
169484: A man and a woman had three sons, one of whom had been struck by the evil hand. The boy had got a hunchback after an old woman had touched him. One day the brothers of the deformed boy lured the witch to their house. Although the witch claimed she had done nothing at all, the boys said: "If you do not undo the harm you have done right now, we will beat you to death here with this stick." The witch then stroked the boy's hunchback. Some time later the boy no longer had a hunchback.
169486:
Harie X. of Metsteren had a bewitched child. Harie went to the parish priest, who asked him whom he suspected of the witchcraft. Harie did not want to say, but the priest guessed: "I know, it is Bet Priemen," and Harie nodded in agreement. The priest said prayers over the child while the sweat dripped from his face.
When the priests read the Gospel of Saint John, witches sat in church with a beehive on their heads. But only the priests could see that beehive.
169490: A man often went with his friends to the house of an old woman who had several young daughters. After a while, however, the woman had had enough of it. When the man was going home one evening, he was surrounded by cats that scratched him. The man and his friends ran off and never dared to come back. That woman must have been a witch.
169500: People believed that witches consorted with the devil. One evening a little boy secretly went to watch a witches' gathering. Because the witches sensed they were being spied on, one of them said: "Stick a pin in my apron," to which another reacted fiercely: "No, stick something in my socks!" Afterwards the boy had a swollen knee. If the witch had had a pin stuck in her apron, the boy would have been blind. It was the boy's mother who had insisted on sticking something in her socks. She was one of the witches and had sensed that her own child was standing there.
169506: Graatje S. lived in Dorplein. One evening Graatje was home alone, because his wife still had to do the shopping. Suddenly Graatje saw a large rat come out of the oven. The man struck at the animal with tongs. But the animal was unharmed and crawled back into the oven. When the rat appeared again a little later, Graatje killed it with a spade. From then on Graatje S. was paralysed. During the mission a priest came to visit Graatje S. The priest said to Graatje: "I can help you, but then my time here on earth will be over too." Graatje S. answered: "No, Father, I do not want you to die even a moment sooner for me." Graatje S. remained paralysed his whole life.
169519:
Pregnant women were afraid of evil spirits that could be passed on by certain people.
A woman out walking with a small child met a witch who said: "Oh, what a lovely child!" Some time later the child died. Witches could also cause a child to become disabled.
169526: A boy from Munsterbilzen went to visit his girlfriend in Eik on a Sunday evening. When the boy came to the Linde, he saw a cat sitting on the little bridge. The boy knocked the cat off the bridge and went on. A little later the boy arrived at his girlfriend's and saw that her mother had a broken arm. "What's the matter with you?", the boy asked, to which the woman replied: "You of all people should ask! You broke my arm!"
169532: At midnight a coach with twelve horses drove into the castle of Rummen.
169545: Some men mowing the field saw a fine ship sailing past and went to look. Meanwhile a woman quickly buried something in the field. A few days later the woman came to ask for her property back. The men then said: "You will get it back if you tell us what you went to do at that farmer's last time. All the animals there have fallen deathly ill." The woman gave the men a slice of bread to give to the animals. The last time, the cat had taken out of the milk a piece of bread that the witch had put in it. That was how the cattle had fallen ill. Fortunately the animals recovered thanks to the new bread they were given as a remedy.
169546: A woman said to some men: "Tell X that Y is dead." The next moment a cat cried out in alarm: "Is Y dead?!" and it flew out through the chimney.
169556: A butcher coming back from Widooie one evening was followed the whole way by a black woman. After a while the woman vanished without a trace.
169557: In 1914 Andries L. saw a dung cart with six black horses flying through the air above Elch.
169561: If someone had wounded a witch's cat on its leg, the witch had a bandage around her leg the next day.
169577: A woman was often plagued by the maar (nightmare spirit), which gave her a feeling of tightness so that she could not call for help. The maar had nearly crushed her to death.
169594: A young man coming back in the evening from a visit to his girlfriend saw a phantom calf on the Pastoorsweg.
169621: The witch Trineke could see the devils and their master in a cup.
169625: A black cat always sat by the crucifix in Piringen.
169626: A ghost wandered about near the Spekbrug. It floated about thirty centimetres above the ground. It was probably the ghost of someone who had drowned.
169649: A woman was coming home at night along the remote, dark Abdijstraat. When the woman reached the Hel, a black cat suddenly came towards her. The woman asked the cat: "What kind of animal are you?" The cat replied: "I am not a cat, I am a little lady like you, with a hat and a little skirt." Then the woman saw a tall lady following her. When the woman came back a while later with her parents, the black madam had vanished.
169657: By the church path at the Hoogveld stood a hollow oak that was haunted. Whoever dared to stand by the tree in the evening heard a strange voice speaking. The man's father said that the talking oak had stood there for thirty years.
169658: The bridge in Guigoven was haunted. At one o'clock at night the villagers always heard the tinkling of little bells. Then two spirits dressed as priests came past and went in the direction of Vliermaal.
169678: A man from Ketsingen saw a cat sitting on a tree stump. The cat walked a little way with him, constantly running between his legs. When the man went home, he had a pitchfork with him. The cat jumped out of the corn and again got in the man's way. The man grew tired of the game and stabbed the cat through the body with the pitchfork. At that the cat leapt up and threatened: "If you stab me again, I'll burn you and your father!" When the man got home, the cat had suddenly vanished.
169679: Three men from Rutten had often tried to shoot the hare that was eating the cabbages in the vegetable garden. But they never managed to hit it. When the men chased the animal, a man with a tall mitre and a staff suddenly stood before them.
169686: After sunset people did not dare leave the washing hanging outside, or the children would be bewitched the next day.
169698: Because his cows and calves were all dying, T.D. went to a fortune-teller in Liège. The fortune-teller said to the man: "Have you ever lent anything to anyone? If so, you must get the lent object back and clean out your stable." After the farmer had followed the advice, his animals stayed healthy.
169709: The witch Bet stroked her hand over a girl's long hair. The next moment the girl's hair was full of lice. Because the lice could not be got rid of even with paraffin, the girl finally had to have her hair cut off.
169710: Many cats always roamed near the house of a witch in Genk.
169712: In Kerkhoven stood a little church where everyone from the area came to mass. The bell from that church sank into the fen. When people had almost managed to pull the bell up, it sank into the fen again.
169722: A man walking along a small path to Kleine-Brogel saw a pack of fighting cats on the way. When the man struck at the cats, he was scratched by the animals.
169724: Harie went to visit his girlfriend in the evenings. At the gate by the Ter Waardenbrug the man was always accompanied by a white lady. After the woman had walked a little way with Harie, she disappeared again.
169725: During a thunderstorm a man saw a ghostly dog on the road to Berbroek. Suddenly the dog was gone.
169729:
A woman whose child had an ailment in the leg was told by a fortune-teller that a witch was responsible for the misfortune. If the witch came in again, fire was to be thrown at her. But the witch's husband happened to come by just as fire was being thrown at the woman. The husband demanded a court case.
There is no doubt that the woman really was a witch: she could go from Laak to Hasselt in half an hour.
169746: A woman had hung her clean washing on the line to dry. One day the washing lay on the ground, although there had been no wind. A witch from the neighbourhood must have thrown the washing on the ground.
169748: Between the Oeterbrug and the Tongelerbrug Willem F. always had to carry the werewolf. When Fons W. went with Willem, the werewolf never had itself carried. Willem could see the werewolf, but Fons could not. The werewolf always chose his victims carefully.
169750: A man had seen the ghost of his dead friend and that of his mother appear. The ghost of a dead person looked just like a living person. One then had to do what the ghost asked.
169772: Because there was a witch in Takkeboswei, nobody dared go there. One day some brave boys went to Takkeboswei with sticks and dung forks to chase the witch away. "Come on out," said the boys. Suddenly an ugly little old woman appeared and answered: "I am here, boys." Terrified, the boys ran to the Boskee. When they got there, one of the boys said: "If only we had not run away. We should have beaten her." Suddenly the little woman was sitting in the branches of a tree and said: "Boys, there is still plenty of time!" Scared to death, the boys ran off down the Kiezelstraat.
169776: The daughter of a farmer from Opheers had found the farmhand's book of magic in the horse stable. When the girl began to read the book, she suddenly could no longer move. Only when the chaplain read the text from the book backwards could the girl move again.
169792: A man was followed by a dog with eyes like balls of fire. Because the man was afraid of the animal, he hit the dog with a stick. The dog must have been bewitched, for the man did not manage to hit it. In the end the man was even bitten by the dog.
169802: A certain Stien saw the ghost of her dead husband appear at Kattestaart every night. Every morning the wood from the barn lay under Stien's bed. To release her husband's soul, Stien went on pilgrimage to Sint-Gillis in Luik. Luckily a shepherd from the castle had taken the stick, or else they would have had to carry the ghost the whole way. After the prayer to Saint Giles, Stien saw smoke rising. The soul was released.
169808: Octavie went on a pilgrimage to the Sneyers chapel. On the way Octavie met a woman who asked: "Are you going to pray?", to which Octavie answered: "Yes, I am going on pilgrimage for the piglets that will soon be born." The woman then said: "That is a good idea, pray hard, because it may well be needed." When Octavie came home from the pilgrimage, nine piglets had been born, but they all had a hump.
169812: Treeske the witch could turn herself into a cat. One day three young ladies had struck at a black cat. From that day on Treeske walked around with a crooked back.
169833: A farm had many animals that had always been perfectly healthy. When one day a black kitten was born, all the animals suddenly fell ill. After the kitten had been shot dead, the animals were healthy again.
169834: Farmer S. had a farmhand who owned a collar that turned him into a werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent to the field so that his collar could be burnt in the meantime. When they were about to throw the collar into the fire, the farmhand instantly stood by the oven to save his collar. Because the farmhand came too late, he was released.
169840: In Ubbersel (1) lived a man from Hal (2) whose wife was a witch. One day the witch had changed herself into a crow that went about eating the vegetables in all the gardens. After someone had shot at the crow, the witch had a gunshot wound in her leg.
169866: On a farm worked a farmhand who was a werewolf. The farmer had received the following advice from the friar: "I will help the boy, but then you must send him to Maastricht with a horse and cart. Then you must make sure the fire in the oven is lit, so that the farmhand's collar will burn up at once. You must also make sure that some men stand by the oven to hold back the werewolf when he tries to take his collar out of the fire. As soon as someone touches the collar, the werewolf will know what is going on." And so it happened. When the collar was thrown into the fire, the farmhand was by the oven in no time. When everything had burnt up, the boy thanked everyone because he had been released.
169875: Some people returning from Sittard saw a cat sitting on a post in Limbrecht. One of the men knocked the cat to the ground with a stick. Further on dozens of cats suddenly appeared, which mauled the man so badly that he died.
169920: When L. came back from the Kempen, he saw a bramble bush by the little chapel. The bush rolled over the ground and caught up with the man.
169925: The parish priest of Neerharen claimed that witches and ghosts did not exist, but he did say: "You must beware of people who have 'the name'." Witches could give people lice.
169930: In the field by the Herk it haunted on certain days of the year. When a farmer passed that spot with his cart, the horse began to rear so badly that the cart overturned.
169942: Witches could change themselves into cats, frogs and all sorts of other animals. A man said he had seen M. from the Rot in the shape of a hare.
169944: In Beersel a golden calf used to roam about.
169946:
On the road from Troot to Vliermaal, Stas was making mice from a handful of earth when suddenly a clergyman passed by. After the clergyman had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
When the boy grew up, he hanged himself.
169947: At a bridge in 's Heerenelderen a white lady always appeared who tried to push passers-by into the brook. One evening a man managed to jump across the brook. As soon as the man reached the other side, the white lady disappeared.
169948: A man was left alone after his girlfriend had died through the work of the evil hand. The man went to thrash the witch, but it turned out he had no power over the woman.
169951: A young man from Dilsen had got stuck with his cart. Because the horse could not go any further, the boy had to go back home. A clergyman made the horse move on again.
169952: C. the werewolf was a man from Hees. The werewolf often sat in the Groenstraat, where he jumped on farmers and made them carry him.
169961: Trees R. had her eye on Rik K., who wanted nothing to do with Trees because people said she was a witch. One day Rik got violent stomach cramps. Rik lay ill in bed for almost a year. When Trees came to visit him, she said: "You always talked about 'that old witch of R.', but now I have made you pay for it!" A few years later Trees lay on her deathbed. Rik went to see her. The witch's last words were: "Rik, do you remember that I once visited you too?"
169970: Some men walking past F.'s house saw a beautiful woman sitting on a turnstile. When they reached out their hands to the woman, a cat jumped off the turnstile.
169971: A boy out walking with his girlfriend suddenly saw a very pretty kitten. A little later the pair were surrounded by dozens of cats. They were witches.
169984: In a meadow stood a bull that seemed to be bewitched. Nobody knew who owned the bull. The farmers who had their cow covered by the bull had bad luck, because the calves all died.
169986: Jan S. from Meerhout-Gestel had moved the boundary post of his land because he was quarrelling with his neighbour. After his death Jan had to haunt with the boundary post on his shoulders. In the evenings he walked about saying: "Where shall I leave my post? Where shall I leave my post?" The ghost was only released when it had found the place where the post had originally stood.
169992: On Christmas Day Rikske went to Mass in the morning. On the way he met a dog, which changed into a woman and said: "I must hurry, because I have no time!" Rikske replied: "If you do as you did just now, you'll get there in time!" It was a witch.
169994: A woman who went sewing at people's homes was always followed by a werewolf that wanted to drag her into the ditch.
170003: A woman who saw a beggar woman approaching quickly made the sign of the cross. Because of that the beggar woman could go no further.
170008: Witches sometimes changed themselves into cats, which jumped on someone's back and let themselves be carried while growing heavier and heavier.
170010: Next to the Demer was a large pond called the Paardskoet because people went there to wash the horses' legs. A little further on was a pond called the Wijwaterkoet. Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen floating by that pond. It was said that a chapel had sunk in the Wijwaterkoet. One day a passer-by saw a little bird in a bush holding a thread in its beak. The man began pulling the thread and shortly afterwards saw the chapel rise above the water. When the cross on the tower came into view, the chapel sank again.
170013: Farmer M. was walking home late in the evening. When Meiers was in Molenbeersel, a werewolf suddenly jumped on his back. The farmer quickly took his knife and cut the werewolf so that he bled. This made the werewolf change into a human. The man then begged the farmer on his knees not to betray him.
170037: A newborn baby began crying every night at twelve o'clock. Because the doctor could not help, the mother went to a friar, since her brother thought Nel H. had bewitched the baby. The friar gave the mother a medal to hang around the child's neck. After a few days the baby no longer cried at midnight.
170043: A farmer who had just slaughtered a pig was visited by the witch Zwarte Fles. Because of that the farmer did not manage to freeze the meat.
170049: In Congo (a hamlet of Genk) a man had pulled out the boundary post of his field. Because that is a mortal sin, the man could not enter heaven after his death. He came back to haunt the place where he had lived and kept calling: "Where do I leave it?" Nobody knew what to do. In the end someone did answer the ghost's question: "Where you fetched it from!" After that the ghost was gone for good.
170051: In a sunken lane with many old trees, will-o'-the-wisps sat in the evening. People believed those lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
170057: A tailor from Herk regularly had to go to Overrepen for fittings. One day the tailor brought some meat for his customers' kitten. From then on the kitten always came to fetch the man in Herk. It mewed and kept rubbing against the man's legs. The man said to the animal: "Hey, sweet pussy, what are you doing here?" and he picked the cat up. When the tailor was almost in Overrepen, however, the cat became so heavy that the man had to put it down. The next moment there were some hundred cats, which sang: "Jantje Vranken said: pussy, my dear, where do you come from?"
170062: Kötteke M. was a sorcerer who could walk up walls and conjure up mice.
170068: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who came out of the low meadow. If you followed a will-o'-the-wisp, you got lost.
170076: In the Groenstraat people used to see a white lady walking at times.
170088: When Cilia from Millen had finished confessing, an old man stepped into the confessional. On leaving the confessional, the man found that he was full of lice. Fortunately, the evil done by witches has greatly decreased since the coming of the Gospel of Saint John.
170097: Between midnight and one o'clock someone saw a burning pear tree and a white lady walking around it.
170103: Two friends had made a bet that whoever died first would come back after his death to report to the other. The man who died first was nicknamed 'the hump of the mill of Bloir'. One night the man's ghost appeared to the friend, who asked: "Fernand, is that you?" Then the friend asked: "What is the hereafter like?", to which the ghost replied: "Everything carefully counted and nothing forgiven".
170112: In Horpmaal there were two shepherds, one with fat sheep and the other with thin ones. One day the shepherd with the thin sheep asked the other how his sheep came to be so fat. The other answered: "That's very simple: I graze my sheep on the farmers' clover, oats and wheat." "I'd like that too," said the shepherd with the thin sheep, not realising that he was thereby agreeing to dealings with evil. The other shepherd gave him a slip of paper that would give him the power to turn himself into a hawthorn and the sheep into molehills. He did have to put up with the dogs lifting their hind legs against the hawthorn. In this way both shepherds were satisfied: the one because his sheep would finally get fat, the other because he was rid of the evil. From that moment on, however, very strange things happened at the farm where the evil had taken up residence: the windlass above the well began to turn by itself, and so on. At his wits' end, the frightened shepherd sent for the priest. The priest told the shepherd that he himself was the cause of the strange events. In the end the shepherd decided to confess everything to the priest, and he also showed the slip of paper that had led to the evil. After the priest had thrown the slip into the fire, he asked whether the shepherd perhaps had another slip. The shepherd denied it, but after a long search he found another piece of paper, which the priest also burned. A third search turned up no more slips. The priest gave him this advice: "Next time you must not accept anything that someone else has grown tired of. That other man surely had that magic slip from the devil. Besides, you don't get rid of a devil's slip just like that, for one slip soon becomes two!"
170126: During catechism class a little boy had filled the church with mice by tapping the floor with a stick. When the priest saw this, he baptised the boy again. After that the boy could no longer make mice.
170133: A farmer could not keep a single farmhand in service. So the farmer's wife said to her husband: "We don't need a farmhand; I'll do the work myself". But the farmer would not listen and hired yet another new farmhand. When the young farmhand heard meowing, he took out his knife and cut the cat in the legs. The next morning the farmhand saw that the farmer's wife had scratches on her legs. In the end this farmhand did not want to stay on the farm either. Because the farmer's wife kept bewitching the farmhands, the farmer could not keep any workers. Strangely enough, once the farmer's wife had died, the farmhands were willing to stay.
170145: A man walking down a narrow lane stopped when the werewolf suddenly jumped on his neck. After the man made the sign of the cross, the werewolf disappeared.
170165: At the castle of Jonckholt robber knights came haunting, who had shod their horses back to front. One night the castle sank into the ground.
170183: A newly married couple rented a bakehouse from the witch Fien. Strangely, their baby always began to cry loudly at night. One day the father saw the witch Fien come in through the keyhole and beat him.
170188: Every time a woman had churned butter, the neighbour woman conjured the butter out of the churn. A friar from Rekem gave the people this advice: "Next time you make butter, fill the churn with the contents of your cesspit. Then the witch will no longer conjure the churn empty!" From then on the witch never conjured the butter away again.
170193: The large farm of E. in Straten was haunted. It is an old sixteenth-century building located by the Roman road. Some even claim it was once a monastery. In the garden of the farm there is a round ring where the snow melts immediately in winter. A certain Renson used to live there, who had a great deal of misfortune with his livestock. One night a coach with two white horses drove in, while the gates opened and closed by themselves. After a while a friar of the Monnebruurs was brought in, who read prayers over the farm and sprinkled everything with holy water. After that things did improve, but there was always more misfortune on that farm than elsewhere. During the war a bomb fell on the farm, and it burned down completely.
170215: Some girls told at school that their mother could make mice. She would take a little heap of earth in her hand, write a few signs, and a moment later dozens of little mice without tails appeared. The witch's little daughters also tried to make mice themselves.
170220: A man whose cows were all dying was told by someone: "A woman works at your place who is angry because the dog always bothers her. That is why the woman causes you so much trouble." When the man made sure the woman no longer came by, all his cows stayed healthy.
170244: The brewery of Membruggen used to be haunted. Little men walked about wearing caps like those of the alvermannetjes (elves). Something dripped from the chimney that spoiled the beer. People believed the evil hand had something to do with it. In the end the chimney was torn down. Lard was found on the inside of the chimney.
170247: A man working in the field with his horse saw a big dog jump in front of the horse. After the man had made the sign of the cross, the dog was gone. Thirteen seconds later the dog was back again.
170248: One evening red Martin had to carry the werewolf. When the heavy dog jumped on his back, Martin just had time to pull out his knife. Martin cut the werewolf in the paw so that he bled and became human again. The werewolf said to Martin: "If you betray me, you won't live another eight days."
170264: In a meadow in Rutten stood a house where nine witches held a gathering. One day there were only eight witches in the house, when the ninth suddenly fell down the chimney in the shape of a black dog.
170269: Around Niel there were many ghosts and witches. Anyone there who dared to strike at a kitten was surrounded by dozens of cats a few moments later.
170270: A priest always heard footsteps in the corridor in the evening. It was the soul of the previous priest, who had forgotten to say an anniversary mass for someone. After the priest had said the mass, the ghost stayed away.
170285: At the big stone on the Sleddererweg a ghost wandered about saying, "Release me! Release me!" The ghost could not be released because as many masses had to be said as there were spurrey seeds in a barrel.
170289: A boy who was out walking with a girl threw something at a cat. The next day an old woman had a broken arm.
170292: On the Ooie, a district of Zepperen, lived a mother whose little son was bewitched. Someone had said: "If that child is bewitched, it is because of the woman who always brings milk here: after all, she always goes to look into the cradle." Because the child's parents had heard that salt worked well against witches, they put some salt in the milk. Although the witch had not seen this, she said on her next visit: "Why do you put salt in a child's milk? That milk can never be sweet enough!" The child's mother fetched blessed palm sprigs from the friars and put them under the stairs. That way the witch could no longer come in.
170293: A girl from Hees worked on a farm in Kesselt. Because the girl had heard that her boyfriend was a werewolf, she wanted to test the boy. After the girl had visited her parents on Sunday evening, her boyfriend took her back to Kesselt. When the two reached the village, the boy let his girlfriend go on alone. A little further on the girl threw a red handkerchief at a horse that had been following her the whole time. The next day the girl saw that the horse in the meadow had the threads of the handkerchief between its teeth.
170303: Polus was a man who knew neither God nor commandment. Because he had no family, Polus often knocked in the evening at acquaintances' houses, where he would get a herring and a slice of bread. Polus told these people that he often spoke with the devil. Sometimes he would suddenly say: "The bell is ringing, I must be silent." Although the others had heard no bell, Polus would then stay silent for a long time. At the little chapel by the linden tree in the street, Polus always walked with his thumb in his hand, because he believed it was an 'evil' place. One day Polus lay ill in bed. He said his soul had no rest, because the devil had power over him. The people he always visited in the evening prayed for him ceaselessly. A few days later Polus was cured and he said to the people: "I have become someone else since you prayed so much for me. After wandering about the town for a while, I came to the statue of Mary in the Zoutstraat. The statue held out its hand to me. Then I went to the Monnebruurs (Friars Minor) to confess." From that moment Polus was a devout Christian who went to the Holy Family in Stenaart every Monday.
170307: A sick child out walking with its grandmother met a witch. The witch advised the grandmother to put seven cut-up earthworms in a little bag together with a relic. As soon as the earthworms had dried out, the child would be cured.
170325: Father V. had two white horses and lived in a castle. After his death the priest came back to haunt. He threw a glowing chain at passers-by.
170327: A woman had bewitched a child by putting all kinds of strange things in the pillow of its cradle. When a holy object was placed under the door, the witch could no longer get in.
170336: A man from Spouwen went to the market in Tongeren with a cart of grain. When the man arrived, he found that all the sacks were torn. The man had been bewitched by a woman on the way.
170346: The wife of a miner from Liège always sat praying at night for her husband's well-being. One night the woman heard a voice that said: "All that praying is no use. I'll give you something that is of use!" The woman, who had accepted the offer, after a while could no longer eat or drink. When she sent for a friar, a voice rang out that said: "You keep quiet, for you are no good either. You are not righteous either. You once cut a stick from the hedge that could have grown into a mill shaft." Another friar had to be sent for to banish the devil. Since then the woman's husband never worked in the mine again. He went to work in a factory.
170357: When Haamtoon was coming back from Hees, he saw a hare sitting in the middle of the road at the Wentelende Weg to Mopertingen. The man threw a stone at the hare, and the animal vanished at once. A little further on the hare was again sitting in the middle of the road. This time too the man could not hit it. The third time the man did manage to hit the hare. When Haamtoon came closer to pick it up, the animal threw all kinds of filth in his face.
170364: On the road to Lanklaar lived a young couple who had just bought a bed. Some time later the bed was completely full of lice. That could happen if the feathers of the bed had not been cleaned properly. But the woman the couple lodged with got the blame. A friar was sent for to bless the bed.
170379: A woman who had promised to spin the church vestments died before she had been able to fulfil her promise. One night some people heard noise in the church. When they went to look, they saw the woman's ghost sitting at the spinning wheel. After the vestments were finished, the woman was never heard or seen again.
170385: A will-o'-the-wisp always floated back and forth by the railway. It was the soul of an unbaptised child.
170386: In Wellen stood a house that was haunted. Near that house a big black dog and a cat roamed about, always pestering people.
170400: A man coming home in the evening with the beer cart saw, to his great fright, a headless white lady walking in the Tumbrook.
170401: Whenever she was home alone, Fien was always visited by her godmother. After a while Fien became very ill. When the family had gone to fetch a holy object in Tongerlo, Fien quickly recovered.
170403: Some men who had struck at a cat one night got lost. The next morning the men were lying with their heads on a washing line in Zonhoven.
170429: When Jan T.'s wife was dying, the man had promised his wife that he would have a mass said for her. Because Jan forgot his promise, his wife appeared two years later to remind him of the promised mass.
170436: A sinner had drowned in the Broek. While people were keeping watch over the dead man, the door suddenly opened and a large black dog came in. After lying by the stove for a while, the dog suddenly disappeared. It was the devil, who had come to fetch the dead man's soul.
170439: A mother did not want to have her child baptised. The child did not grow and cried all the time. The doctor did not know what to do, and the mother would not let the priest in. Some time before, the woman had been visited by a beggar woman from Tongeren, to whom she had given alms. Perhaps that beggar woman was the cause of the evil. In the end the desperate woman was persuaded to go to the priest with her child after all. The woman could only step over the threshold of the church after she had let the priest bless her. In the pillow the child slept on there was a crown of thorns. After the little child was dedicated to Our Lady, it recovered.
170454: A young man often visited his girlfriend in the evening. One night the man was standing at his girlfriend's window when he suddenly saw the devil standing behind him in the shape of a large black dog. Since that night the man never again dared to visit a girl in the evening.
170455: One of the most educated men in the village claimed that witches could see everything when the bread lay upside down on the table.
170456: Some people going on pilgrimage to Melkwezer stopped on the way to rest a while in a barn. In the barn everything lay in the shape of a cross: a rake under a scythe, two sticks and a horse's reins. When the group moved on and told some local people about the strange barn, the people exclaimed in disbelief: "You dared to go in there? That place is haunted!"
170457: The town of Vijvere used to lie between Thorn and Kessenich. On Christmas night the bells of the sunken town can sometimes be heard ringing.
170458: "It's cold," said a witch, and she threw away her neckerchief. A passer-by was full of lice.
170472: When it was dark in the evening and the shutters were not yet closed, a man thought he saw a pair of spying eyes at the window. One evening the man struck with a piece of wood at the dog sitting on the windowsill. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood was walking around with a cloth around her head. Because that woman always pinched people's shoulders, it had long been believed that she was a witch.
170475: The wild hunt was witches flying through the air and making a lot of noise.
170477: Will-o'-the-wisps were souls that flew through the air. Those lights have disappeared since the ringing of the bells on Christmas Eve.
170479: A woman whose neighbour had a reputation as a witch was worried because her three-year-old daughter compulsively went to the neighbour's house every day. When the woman had sent for the priest, he made sure the little girl no longer wanted to go to the witch.
170483: A man was coming back from Herk-de-Stad around midnight when suddenly a calf jumped out of the ditch. The calf was surrounded by a strange glow and it jumped over the bridge.
170489: Witches often gave people apples. Whoever ate such an apple became a witch too. That is why there used to be many more witches than now; after all, nowadays everyone can buy as many apples as they like.
170492: A cow could not manage to give birth to her calf. When the calf suddenly came out after all, the farmer saw that the witch was standing at the back of the stable.
170496: In Wellen a dog with a chain around its neck appeared every night. Jef D. was not afraid of the dog and wanted to beat the annoying animal to death. When Jef stood on the church steps at midnight, he said: "Now let that dog come!" When the dog came running up, Jef struck at the animal with the words: "In the name of the Father." Because he had missed, Jef struck a second time and said: "In the name of the Son." Jef missed again. Normally he should then have said: "And the Holy Ghost," but because the dog came and rubbed its big tail under Jef's chin, the man became frightened and quickly took to his heels.
170532: A man working in the field could not get home because his thigh had suddenly become paralysed. The man lay in bed for seven weeks. After that the man could no longer make butter. Even when the man had bought another cow in Hasselt, he could not make butter. Because the man was at his wits' end, he sent for a certain Fris from Zepperen. Fris went into the stable, made the sign of the cross over the cow and said to the man: "You must put sulphur in your soup. Tomorrow you must go to mass with your wife. At the church entrance you must say: 'Go on ahead, I will follow you'. Otherwise you will have to carry that whole weight alone."
170538: A witch lived in 't Trot near Schaffen. When her daughter wanted to go dancing, the witch said angrily: "I wish you would drop dead on the dance floor". And so it happened.
170539: An altar boy put a coin that had lain under the missal beneath the threshold of the church. After mass several women could not leave the church until the coin had been removed: they were witches.
170546: A farmer going to a cockfight in Ulbeek with his cock met the witch Pauline O. on the way. The witch said to the farmer: "You needn't go, because the cock is dead". The animal was indeed stone dead.
170553: A man had got a pain in his shoulder after being touched by a witch.
170576: Between midnight and one o'clock a light burned in the church of Beverst. At the altar stood the ghost of a priest saying mass without altar boys. So the sexton and the priest went at night to serve the mass for the ghost. After that the ghost was never seen again.
170599: A farmer who always saw a hare running in his garden fetched his gun and shot the animal. But when the farmer went to look, he saw nothing. That evening the farmer saw his wife lying in bed with a head wound. "What have you done?", the farmer asked, to which the woman replied: "You of all people should ask! You shot at me!"
170603: One evening Parure suggested to Ber W. that they fetch some apples from Marieke's meadow that night. A woman from the neighbourhood gave them a grey apron to carry the apples in. That night Ber climbed into the tree to throw the apples down, so that Parure could put them in the apron. A little later a cat came and sat on the apron, and Ber warned: "You must never chase a cat away at night." Parure thought that was nonsense and chased the animal away anyway. Then dozens of cats suddenly appeared in the meadow, which made music and began dancing around the two men. Ber and Parure no longer dared take the apron with them. They hurried off and never again went to fetch apples anywhere at night.
170604: A woman going to the market in Hasselt heard a voice behind her saying: "Betje, stop for a moment, your shawl is crooked." Betje answered: "For a married woman that doesn't matter much." A little later the woman overtook Betje so fast that it seemed as if Betje was standing still.
