170628: A woman was walking home alone in the moonlight one evening because her husband, a musician, still had to play a concert. Annoyed, the woman thought to herself: "Let the devil play that concert!" When the woman came to a little bridge, a black dog suddenly walked in front of her.
170651: At the D. family's home, the cradle moved by itself from the bedroom to the kitchen every night. Those people had to pray a great deal to be freed from the evil hand.
170657: A man who went to fetch the midwife at about half past twelve at night met a strange woman on the way who did not say a word. The woman wore a veil over her face and had a pram with her, with which she blocked the man's way. The man was terrified and quickly made off.
170660: The stone cross on the heath bore a French inscription. Nobody dared go near the cross in the evening because it was haunted there.
170670: Pauline went with her friend Det to eat cherries at the home of Filomien, the sexton's daughter. Pauline had not told her parents where she was going. When Pauline came home and told them where she had been, her parents were furious: Filomien was a witch, and so it was very dangerous to accept anything from her.
170675: 'The camel' was a witch who went around peddling kippers. A child from Lanaken had fallen ill after eating the kippers. Although the child's mother had sent 'the camel' away, the witch had come by anyway. The sick girl had been given a little cross by her godfather.
170676: A man passed a haunted farm in Romershoven with his cows. Suddenly the cows became very wild and began pulling at their chains.
170682: A woman from Tongeren went peddling at a house where a small child lay in the cradle. The woman picked up the child and said: "What a beautiful child!" The next day the child's little foot was paralysed. The child had been struck by the evil hand.
170727: A witch once lived in Koninksem who could give people lice. When she struck a child on the back, it fell ill. The child could only recover if the witch touched it again.
170729: The castle of Berg was haunted. The doors there opened and closed by themselves.
170744: The castle of Hocht was haunted. A man who went to bind hay near the castle at night was startled when a fierce wind suddenly rose. The man heard a loud scream. A little later all was quiet again.
170747: In Sint Ool there used to be a pagan temple that sank. Since then the bell was heard ringing from underground every year on Christmas night at exactly twelve o'clock.
170768: The orphan boy Theodoor worked as a farmhand at the Looren farm in Kinrooi. Because so many strange things happened, the boy believed the Looren farm was bewitched. On the stroke of nine, the ground under the cow's hind legs began to squeak. As soon as the boy had taken away all the manure, the squeaking stopped. Another cow was mysteriously untied every morning. A third cow had always already been milked in the morning. After the fathers of Sint-Truiden had read prayers over the farm, no more strange things happened.
170778: A man woke up at night because he had heard something in the sheep pen. When the man went to look, he saw that the sheep had been untied and that a few lay dead in the pen. A neighbour woman wearing a neckerchief was standing in the pen.
170781: Some men playing cards at the Voot in Diepenbeek saw a black dog lying under the table. The friars were sent for at once to banish the dog. The man leading the dog on a chain was on no account to look back. On the way the friar walked behind the dog, reading prayers over the animal. But suddenly the dog tore itself loose and ran off, with the glowing chain still dragging behind it.
170786: In Langerlo there were devil's stones weighing as much as ten or twenty thousand kilos. The devil had set his footprint in those stones.
170805: A witch named Lies lived in Rekem. Some people believed that Lies's sister was a witch too. Lambert, a farmer from Rekem, was always visited by that woman. She would come to get some milk, but she never gave anything in return. One day the farmer's wife said to her husband: "Lambert, if only she would pay for that milk for once!" Strangely enough, from that day on the woman no longer came for milk. "I don't need milk anymore!" she would say. Although Lambert no longer had to hand over milk, he found that he had less and less milk every day. When a cattle dealer came by, Lambert sold his cow for half its original value.
170813: In Roy there was a farm that was bewitched. At night the horse mill started turning by itself and the doors flew open. No one knew what could be causing it.
170822: Forester Gierke G. had murdered a man at Vogelsang. When Gierke lay dying, his sisters sat keeping watch by him. At midnight there was a knock at the door. The eldest sister went to open it and saw a glowing horse standing there. The sister who was standing by the bed fell to the ground and died a year later.
170829: Five men went to steal apples in the orchard of Alda H. When the men got home, their pockets were full of toads.
170832: A beautiful girl got a physical defect when she walked past a witch's house.
170835: In the Rechtstraat a billy goat always came haunting, which people called the Falusbok. When one day a clergyman had been called in, the Falus-bok said: "When you were little, you once took a white loaf from the baker!", to which the priest answered: "Yes, but I did pay for it!" At that moment the clergyman gained power over the ghost. He banished the goat to the whirlpool of the Jeker with the words: "I banish you for ninety-nine years and forever."
170860: Will-o'-the-wisps could often be seen by moonlight. They were souls of unbaptised children. Passers-by had to pray if they did not want to be led astray by the will-o'-the-wisps.
170894: In Mechelen a dove always sat on the rim of the well in the evening. People believed the dove was a damned soul from hell. One evening the dove said to a woman who came to draw water: "You must pray so much to get me into heaven." The woman also had to have a number of masses said.
170922: Two men going to a match in Valmeer with a fighting cock met a witch on the way, who said: "Today you won't win". That day the cock did indeed lose. A few days later the man had to slaughter his cock, because the animal was completely covered in lice.
170925: A man from Maasmechelen who played the werewolf in Boorsem was given a sound thrashing.
170931: A man who had been wrongly convicted at a trial said: "I am innocent. That will soon become clear, for the guilty one will testify." The next moment the doors opened and the guilty man appeared, wrapped in chains. He had come back from hell especially to confirm that the convicted man was innocent.
170949: After a boy with curly hair had been touched by a witch, all his curls had disappeared.
170952: A witch had twisted a child's arm. The next day the child had recovered.
170957: The wife of Ber M. was a witch. When a man on a yellow bicycle rode past the witch's house, a cat jumped onto his lamp. As soon as the cat leapt against the man's chest, the man jumped off his bicycle and ran away as fast as he could.
170967: A man was painting his gutter when Truike van de B. came by. Truike said: "Watch out, Harie, you might fall!" The witch's words were hardly spoken when the man fell off his ladder. Fortunately he only had a sprained wrist.
170970: One day Jefke and Bassetje Poepestief went on foot to Beersel. When the two were in Veldhoven, something black suddenly flew through the air. The women of a nearby farm had often noticed something strange too. Some women were standing outside talking when one of them suddenly said: "Look, there's a black hen in that bush!" When the women went closer to look, the hen was suddenly gone. "That hen came to eavesdrop on us," the women said.
170972: On the Regenakker by the little chapel of Our Lady a black lady appeared. A liberal man who laughed at the black lady and at Our Lady had a boil on his neck the following week. Three weeks later he had six boils on his back and six weeks later forty. That was due to the power of the black lady.
170984: A witch could make a cart stand still so that one could not go any further.
170986:
At the K. farm a farmer was standing in the stable with his farmhand when he suddenly saw a fire-man walking on the heath. "Shall I whistle? He's still far away anyway," said the farmhand, and he whistled at the fire-man. The farmer and the farmhand had barely got inside when the flames were already beating against the door. The farmhand and the farmer had become very frightened, and old Peter said to them: "Whatever is at rest, you must leave in peace!" After about ten minutes the fire-man left again.
Fire-men and will-o'-the-wisps were often land surveyors who had not measured properly during their lives; and there were many of them!
170989: All mothers kept their children indoors when they saw a witch coming. As soon as a witch got the chance to shake a child's hand, the child fell victim to evil.
170993: A man from Spouwen had sold his soul to the devil, so that he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the man ran quickly from the field to the bakehouse to save his animal skin, which had been thrown into the fire.
171015: A child had fallen ill after a woman from Wezent had visited. In the end the child died. In the pillow a closed wreath was found. Witches often lured children with sweets.
171020: A man coming back from Valmèir with a cart met a woman in Kiewit, who said: "You won't get far with that either!" A little further on the wagon fell over.
171021: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said on the way: "Go on ahead. I have to relieve myself." The boy gave his girlfriend a handkerchief and said: "If you should meet a big dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little further on the girl did indeed meet a dog. She threw the red handkerchief at the animal. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl never wanted to see the boy again.
171042: A certain V. went to Sint-Truiden with a cart full of brooms. When a cat crawled under the cart on the way, the cart overturned.
171052: A man who had got lice through the doing of a witch went to Sint-Truiden to have prayers read over him.
171057: The Langerenmolen mill belonged to the abbey of Achel. During the French Revolution the friars had a deed of sale drawn up, making the mill formally the property of a certain P. Through this administrative measure the French would not be able to seize the mill from the friars. After the French Revolution, however, P. refused to destroy the deed of sale. Because P. would not give the mill back to the friars, he had to haunt after his death. The ghost sat in a chair that began to glow, and the doors of the stable and the barn flew open with a hellish noise. At midnight precisely it was all over. After a friar had blessed the mill and banished the ghost to the Beesbos, nothing strange happened any more.
171075: A woman who had called someone a 'witch' had to appear before the judge. There the woman said: "Yes, 'witch' is a woman's name, and whoever isn't one need not take it personally". Some time later the bewitched child of that woman's brother-in-law died. The father, who lived in the Bokkestraat, wanted revenge and decided to stab the witch to death with a dung fork in the Tombos along the Priestersweg. Although the witch could not see the man, she seemed to know that she had to make herself scarce.
171081: Something strange had to be going on in the Asbroek. A man who sent his dog into the marsh was surprised that the animal ran home in fright. People claimed that a heipastoor (heath priest) roamed the Asbroek, doing penance for a sin. A plasterer walking home past the Asbroek one evening saw a large priest in dark clothes. The man was so frightened that he bought a revolver the next day.
171096: A boy who was going to the fair in Lummen with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "Wait a moment, I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a big dog comes at you in the meantime, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." When the two came into a café a little later, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
171099: In the Korenstraat a black cat sat on an iron gate. When the man threw a clod of earth at the cat, the animal jumped to the ground. A moment later, however, the cat was sitting on the gate again. It was a witch.
171108: In Zoutleeuw a church sank into a swamp. One day a woman went to fetch water from a spring by the swamp. When the woman pulled up the bucket, she saw that the spire of the church tower was hanging from it. The woman was startled and dropped the tower again, saying "Jesus, Mary!".
171123: People claimed that a white lady walked about in Opgrimbie.
171128: When shepherd Peter V. was walking by the ditch, he suddenly felt two paws on his shoulders and was scratched in the face. At first the man thought it was his friend from Zichem, but a moment later Peter realised that he had to carry the werewolf. Peter took his knife from his pocket to cut the werewolf. Before he got the chance, the werewolf ran off across the meadow in the shape of a foal.
171131: It was said that Jan H.'s wife was a witch. One day Tinus H. was ploughing when suddenly a cat ran across the field. Tinus threw a stone at the animal and hit it on the back. When Tinus visited his brother the next day, he learned that his brother's wife was lying in bed with a back injury. Tinus drew his own conclusions.
171135: In Genk a bell had flown out of the church tower and fallen into the Molenvijver. That is why the pond was called the Klokvijver. On Christmas night, at the stroke of twelve, people heard that bell ringing.
171137: A girl was courting a boy who could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the girl had thrown a red handkerchief at a werewolf. When the girl saw her boyfriend, she noticed that he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
171150: In Hechtel a farmhand had hanged himself from a tree stump, after hiding his money in the hollow of the tree. After his death the farmhand came haunting every night at twelve o'clock to see whether his money was still in the tree stump. A few men had received a relic from the holy little father, which they took with them to the haunted place. They decided to lie down on the ground there and not move, so that the ghost would not see them. One of them, however, accidentally moved his head, after which he was killed by the ghost. A few days later another man nevertheless managed to get hold of the money. Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
171180: A man who had visited some friends in Lauw set off home in the evening. Shortly afterwards, however, the man was back with his friends: he no longer dared go on because five or six ghosts were waiting for him at the ditch.
171206: A kabouter (gnome) worked for farmer H. When the pastor visited the farmer one day, he advised the farmer to send the kabouter (gnome) away for an hour and in the meantime burn the kabouter's white cord in the oven. The moment the cord caught fire, the kabouter (gnome) immediately stood beside the oven. Then the kabouter (gnome) left.
171209: Two men came back from the fair together with a witch. When the witch went into her house, the two men decided to quickly pick some plums from the tree standing there. Immediately they heard the witch shout: "Leave those plums alone and go away!" The men, however, could not move a muscle.
171228: A man called for the ferryman because he had to get to his wife and child on the other side of the water. When the man thought he saw the light of the boat, he went closer and fell into the water. The man drowned. When there was a storm, the people living along the Maas still heard the cry: "Ferry over, ferry over!"
171231: At school there was a child who could make mice by throwing pebbles on the ground. The priest took those powers away from the child.
171237: Werewolves were seen mainly during the month of February. Werewolves were hard to describe because they always appeared in a different shape.
171245: A boy who was out walking with his girlfriend in the evening said to the girl: "Go on ahead, I have to relieve myself. If you should meet a dog, just throw this red handkerchief." A little later a dog did indeed appear, which tore the handkerchief to pieces. When the boy and the girl got home, the girl noticed that her boyfriend still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
171251: A boy from Waltwilder always had to leave his girlfriend's house at midnight. One night, however, the boy decided to stay a little longer. The boy flew through the air with his girlfriend and fell asleep. When he woke up, the boy was in Westphalia, where he saw the witches dancing.
171272: A woman who was said to be a witch predicted that a man was going to die. And so it happened.
171274: A man who had murdered his father had died without ever confessing his crime. Because the dead man could find no rest, he came back to haunt every night at twelve o'clock at the place where he had committed his crime. People would then hear a hellish noise and a little later see a black dog run away. One day a friar was brought in, who sat praying all day. When the dog appeared at twelve that night, the priest seized the animal and dragged it with a noose into the confessional. Then the man called the dead man's family together to pray. After that the friar went into the woods with the family and the dog and said to the animal: "Here I banish you for ninety-nine years and for the time that follows." Since then the wood has been called the Duivelsbos (Devil's Wood).
171279: A woman who was preserving spinach was visited by a witch. The witch said to the woman: "You are preserving it the wrong way. You must do it differently, or else you will have problems." But the woman would not listen and carried on. When they later ate the spinach, everyone got stomach cramps. They even had to go to hospital.
171283: A man who came back to haunt after his death kept calling: "Where shall I put my boundary post?" When someone answered: "Take it back to the place where you fetched it from", the ghost appeared no more.
171293: A woman who was said to be a witch was avoided by everyone in the village. One day a farmhand had to drive a cart past the witch's house. The witch called: "Come this way!", but the farmhand took a detour because he was afraid of the witch. The witch, however, was angry because the farmhand avoided her, and she called: "The cart will overturn!" The farmhand did not believe her and drove on. When he came to a bend, however, the cart overturned, so that the horse lay with its legs in the air.
171294: Some men going to the castle of Holsbeek were followed by a cat. The last one in the line was always scratched by the cat. A little later the animal had vanished. The men were bewitched.
171297: A boy who saw cats in the evening always thought they were witches.
171306: A witch who came to a woman's house for eggs took the woman's child in her arms. Because the child began to cry loudly, the mother went to fetch the priest, who read prayers over the child. The child was bewitched, because it had developed a lump. In the end the child died.
171309: One evening a fierce quarrel had broken out at Fien S.'s house, when suddenly a dog stood in the room. Everyone was struck dumb by this strange apparition. Fien quickly fetched holy water from the cupboard to sprinkle the dog with. Before she got the chance, however, the animal had already vanished. It must have been the devil.
171315: A man who had moved a boundary post to have a bigger piece of land had gone to confession but had not put the post back. After the man's death a white figure appeared on the land, walking back and forth with the boundary post in its hands and calling: "Here I have it. Where shall I put it?" When one evening a drunkard answered: "You fool, put it back where you took it from!", the figure replied: "Now I am saved!" and disappeared. Since then the ghost has not been seen or heard again.
171324:
A man had seen the witches fly away from a meadow after saying: "Over hedges and hawthorns". The man made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns". Because of that the man arrived at his destination badly injured.

A hunchback heard the witches sing: "Lundi, lundi, today is lundi". The hunchback got angry and said: "No, it's mercredi". At that the hunchback was taken along by the dancing witches. When the man got back, he met another hunchback, who said: "Hey, how did you lose your hump?" The man told what had happened to him. Then the other hunchback also went to the witches' dance and also said: "It's mercredi aujourd'hui". The witches said: "What shall we do with him? We still have a hump lying here. We'll put it on his front!" So the hunchback suddenly had two humps: one on his back and one on his belly.
171327: A man was fed up with the cabbages in his garden always being eaten by a hare. The man decided to keep watch at night. When the man saw the hare running at night, he shot his own daughter dead with his gun.
171330: At Sterbos a white lady sat in the woods in the evenings.
171337: A family in Budel had a little child that had fallen ill and cried all the time. Because the doctor could not help the child, the father suspected that Trien B. was causing the suffering. When Trien came to buy butter again, the father voiced his suspicion. At first Trien claimed she had nothing to do with it, but when the father got angry, the witch admitted that she had a doll at home with a pin stuck in it. If she pulled the pin out of the doll, the child would stop crying. A while after Trien had left, the child stopped crying.
171347: The witch Trees B. from Heusden could infest people with lice.
171356: A witch visited a five-year-old girl who had whooping cough. The witch gave the child some money, saying: "Buy yourself something nice with that". But the child was bewitched and died a few days later. The mother had still gone to the fathers of Sint-Truiden, but it was already too late.
171381: A maid who slept in the castle farm heard three knocks on the door of the lady of the castle. When the maid got up and went to look, she saw a man dressed all in white standing in the doorway. On seeing the maid, the ghost angrily slammed the door shut.
171400: Werewolves often sat on tree stumps waiting until someone came by whom they could make carry them.
171408: A boy from Eversel who was going to a café with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "Go on ahead. I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a werewolf comes at you in the meantime, throw my red handkerchief at its mouth." A little further on the girl did indeed meet a big black dog. When her boyfriend came back, she noticed that he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
171422: A werewolf was a person who had been baptised improperly and therefore had to roam about in the shape of a wolf. Werewolves could only be saved if someone burnt their skin.
171428: In the pillow of the child of Zjang O. from Opgrimbie, a feather wreath that was not yet closed was found. When the wreath was closed, the child died.
171429: If you could strike a werewolf on the head, the beast changed into a human.
171442: A farmer who had just bought two piglets let a beggar woman spend the night in his stable. But during the night the farmer was woken by a strange noise. The woman had put a chair next to the stable door and had driven all the pigs onto the stable roof. The frightened farmer quickly sent his youngest brother outside with a palm branch and some holy water. The next morning the beggar woman was standing on the threshing floor; the holy water had held her back. The beggar woman was a witch called 'het Dèpke'.
171452: A farmer could no longer make butter because a witch had come to ask for bread the evening before. After a cross had been made on the threshold, the witch could no longer get in.
171464: A man who had seen a cat at the stone cross in the Molenstraat struck at the animal. The next moment as many as forty cats appeared and chased the man until he was home.
171476: In the evenings the silk lady rustled silently past frightened passers-by.
171479: A girl had secretly gone dancing one evening. Because she was already late, the girl feared her mother would be very angry. A boy asked the girl if he could walk with her. At first the girl refused, but because the boy kept insisting, she let him come along. On the way the boy suddenly said: "You go on ahead. I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at the beast." When the girl met a dog a little further on, she did as the boy had advised. A while later the boy appeared, saying: "I got lost in the woods!" The girl told the boy what had happened and he praised her for her bravery. Because the girl had seen the threads of the handkerchief between the boy's teeth, she did not let the young man in when she got home. The boy then grew angry and bit the girl in the leg. Then he said: "You'll call me when the time comes!" Although the girl's wound would not heal, the poor child did not dare tell her mother she had been bitten by a werewolf. When the girl sent for the boy, the child's mother said: "Look what a wound my daughter has on her leg!" The boy answered: "That's nothing, it will be healed at once!" After the boy had stroked the girl's leg twice, the wound healed. Then the boy confessed to the girl's mother that the wound had been his fault.
171484: In Maasmechelen a house was for rent. But nobody wanted to live in it because people said it was haunted. The ghost was said to sit now in one corner, then in another.
171486: A greedy farmer from Loon had moved the boundary post of his land. After his death the farmer could find no rest and had to haunt his field. When the whole matter came to light, the ghost was released.
171501: In Mal, witch cats danced in a ring around a barrier. In the evening the cats walked along with passers-by.
171519: A farm in Buvingen was haunted. When the ghost appeared, the paintings fell to the floor and the cups danced on the table. When the man was at home nothing happened, but as soon as he left, the ghost appeared again.
171537: In the meadow by the Poel something sat in the hedge that kept calling: "hoo, hoo, hoo..."
171544: A farmer had a young farmhand who always went out after supper. One evening the farmer saw the farmhand sit down on a tree stump with a chain around his head. The farmhand then read in a book for a while and turned into a werewolf. The farmer told everything to a clergyman, who advised him to send the farmhand away for a day and in the meantime burn the neck chain and the little book. When everything lay in the fire, the farmhand instantly stood beside the oven to save his things. After everything had burnt up, the farmhand was greatly relieved and thanked the farmer for releasing him.
171546: In the old days people were afraid to go anywhere in the evening. After all, in many lanes there were werewolves that jumped on passers-by and made them carry them.
171570: On the farm of Hamel castle worked a farmhand who had to play the werewolf. One day the farmer sent the farmhand away with another one to buy coal. Meanwhile the farmer wanted to burn his farmhand's animal skin. But before the skin was even in the fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. Yet somehow the farmhand managed to come back with the other farmhand with a cart full of coal.
171573: A 'spiriet' (spiritist) from Eksel could summon spirits. The farmhand of mayor V. was often summoned. The dead man would then come and knock on the table. If someone was present who did not believe in spirits, it did not work. One day, however, the devil's influence was felt so strongly that they had to stop the ritual.
171594: According to schoolmaster S., the devil's stones in Genk came from the Tower of Babel, which had exploded there.
171624: A man of the Nelkes family from Bree went for a walk on the heath with Giel and Lèètje. When dusk began to fall, they suddenly heard beautiful music coming from high in the sky. It must have been the witches, returning from the wine cellars in Aachen.
171628: At midnight a ghostly foal appeared on the highway and suddenly vanished.
171632: A witch lived on the border between Stevoort and Kozen. When a farmer passed by there with his cow, the witch asked if she could buy the cow. Because the farmer refused, the witch made the cow stand still as if nailed to the ground. The cow only just managed to get as far as the witch's stable.
171639: A man who saw a cat walking in the same spot every evening stabbed the animal with a dung fork. Shortly afterwards a woman from the neighbourhood went to the doctor to have a stab wound treated. "You should have stayed at home", the doctor said to the woman.
171654: In Kozen a man was murdered who sold linen and therefore carried a good deal of money. At the spot in the wood where the man was killed, a voice was afterwards often heard saying: "Pray for the poor linen man, pray for the poor linen man."
171655: A man coming home from work in the evening got lost.
171665: The gnomes left because the steamboat on the canal made too much noise.
171677: A joiner was coming home in the evening from his work at the distillery in Lanklaar. At the Kenzelareboske the man was jumped by a werewolf that wore a chain around its neck and made itself carried. The next time the man decided to come home by way of the flax pit. One evening the man was jumped there too by the werewolf. When the man began hitting the werewolf with a nail on a little board, the beast ran away.
171681: A mother was sitting with her little child on her lap when a woman came in and said: "Oh, what a beautiful little child!" The next day the child had a hernia.
171684: A pious man asked a fellow who was telling indecent things: "Aren't you ashamed?" The fellow replied: "If the devil is there, let him come in!" The next moment a black dog came and lay under the table.
171687: When Janneke V. was coming back from Heers, he came across a troop of black cats that began to dance around him. Suddenly one of the cats said: "If Janneke had not drunk so much, we would have broken his neck!"
171696: A woman went to the parish priest because someone from her family was haunting her. The priest said to the woman: "You must have a mass said. During the consecration the ghost will come to you. You must lay a white handkerchief on your hand". The woman did as the priest advised. The ghost burned its hand into the white handkerchief. When the woman, who had kept the handkerchief a long time, wanted to wash it, she heard a hiss and the handkerchief fell to pieces.
171702: Two families lived in villa 'Labaer'. After supper the people used to play a card game. At ten o'clock the doors were always heard creaking. Whoever was holding the jack of hearts at that moment could see the jack on the card smile. The others could not see it. A few minutes later a loud scream was heard. Then all became quiet again and the card game could continue.
171719: Johanna K. was a witch. Every time a mare was due to foal, the witch came by and asked: "How is the horse doing?" The foal then always died. A farmer went to confession with the fathers and asked them what he could do to protect himself against Johanna. The fathers advised the man to close the gate so the witch could no longer get in. From then on not a single foal died at the farmer's.
171734: A boy was ploughing on the Daasberg. At noon a farmer asked the boy, "Say, what kind of idler was walking behind you the whole time?" But the boy had not seen anyone. When the same thing happened again the next day, the boy told his father what had happened. When the boy went to the priest, the clergyman said, "Go to the field. I will come too. When the ghost stops the horses, you must ask what the ghost wants." The ghost answered, "Walk to Scherpenheuvel twice, or once with two people. During the mass you must hang a handkerchief on your chair. After the consecration I will be released." The ghost burned a black hand into the handkerchief.
171735: A man had lived in great sin for many years. He never went to church, never went to confession, and did much evil. When the man lay on his deathbed, all his children were with him. The man kept staring at one corner of the room and suddenly cried: "No, no, I won't go with you!" The children saw nothing, but a little later the man cried again: "You Satan, don't take me!" One of the children quickly went to fetch a priest. "Yes, Father, I know I have done evil, but now I have been warned. I have seen the devil", the man said to the clergyman. The priest replied: "You need not be afraid. Trust in the goodness of the Almighty." That same night the man died very peacefully. He probably went to heaven.
171738: In Koninksem a black cat often sat on a barrier in the evening. Then nobody could get past.
171759: A man who had met a witch was completely covered in lice. The fathers of Sint-Truiden gave the man a relic to put under the threshold. After that the man was rid of the lice.
171761: At night farmer Peeters often heard his animals snorting and stamping in the stable. But when he went to look, the animals were lying peacefully asleep. It must have been the evil hand.
171762: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who were unbaptised or wrongly baptised. Whoever wanted to baptise a will-o'-the-wisp had to say: "I baptise you alone". Otherwise hundreds of will-o'-the-wisps would come flying to be baptised.
171765: A man coming home from work at about ten in the evening got lost in Eikenen (?). The man walked into a hedge. When the man went to look at the spot the next day and saw no hedge there at all, he knew he had been bewitched.
171771: On a farm in Hees there worked a maid who was a witch. That maid caused a horse to die every year. A bit of hair from the tail stuck out from under the threshold. In the end people did find out that the maid was making the horses die. The same thing had happened on a farm in Val.
171789: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children that came from the marsh. A man who met a will-o'-the-wisp one evening wanted to baptise the light with water from the ditch. The next moment the man was almost pushed into the ditch because so many lights came flying, all wanting to be baptised. Will-o'-the-wisps were sometimes also called stallichtjes (stable lights). They usually came from the marshy land and danced up and down.
171792: Some people coming back from Tessenderlo heard a sound on the Schom that resembled the bleating of a goat. A little later one of the men saw a big dog sitting in front of him. At that the man said: "In God's name, whatever it is, I'm going on." The next moment the animal was gone.
171797: A woman had a litter of nine piglets. One day a witch had come to visit and had said: "You have fine piglets!" From then on the piglets walked around the sty at night as if in a procession. What's more, they even ate each other's tails. The piglets could not be sold until their tails had grown back.
171801:
Two brothers always went to their neighbours in the evening. Every time they came back, a big black dog lay in front of their door. The animal wore a chain around its neck, but it did no one any harm. 
If you were attacked by a werewolf in the shape of a dog, you had to throw a handkerchief at the animal's mouth. The werewolf would then tear the handkerchief completely to shreds.
171808: When Ciliake from the Kattestraat went to visit his uncle on the Calvarie, Alfonsine D.W. infested him with lice. Some time later Alfonsine went to see the uncle, who had had an operation. But the uncle knew he always had to keep his hand higher than a witch's. Alfonsine called the nurse and said: "I don't feel well. There's something on me!" The witch took off her clothes and turned out to be covered in lice herself.
171823: Two friends saw a big cat by Rikus's house. When one of the men wanted to chase the cat away, the other said: "No, we mustn't do that, because it is a witch!" The man had the greatest trouble getting home, because the cat chased him the whole time.
171845: A boy who went to fetch milk was bewitched even though he had put salt in the milk. After the boy's death, all sorts of little curls in the shape of a wreath were found in his pillow.
171853: Witches could make someone stand stock-still, especially if they wanted to harm that person.
171870: A man was in a relationship with a woman from Sint-Huibrechts-Lille, with whom he had arranged to meet at a farm in Kleine-Brogel. Although the man knew the way very well, he got lost. In the end the man went into an inn in Kleine-Brogel, where he asked a friend to go with him. When the man had finally found the woman, they went together to Sint-Huibrechts-Lille around midnight. After the man had taken his girlfriend home, he went back alone. Suddenly, however, there was a hedge in the middle of the road, so that the man could no longer find his bearings. After a long time the man got home.
171878: Will-o'-the-wisps were always seen when a newborn child had died. It was the soul of a child that could find no rest because it had not been baptised. Lontien always saw a will-o'-the-wisp flying above the castle that stood on the Hal in the Maas. People whose child had died usually went to the friars. They then had masses said to release the child's soul.
171885: Jan claimed he always saw a black horse hung with chains coming out of the castle. The horse was said to be searching for the lady of the castle, who had disappeared one night.
171901: An old woman who had kept watch by the body of a dead person was walking home alone. On the way the woman saw a kitten. When she picked up the kitten, the animal grew heavier and heavier. By the road the woman put the cat down again, whereupon the animal said: "If you had not carried me, you would have had no luck!"
171903: On the Klappoel behind the town hall in Borgloon there used to be two houses. In one lived a tailor and in the other a shoemaker. Both men had a hump on their back. The two men were also both musicians: one played the violin and the other the accordion. The man with the violin behaved rather haughtily towards the other, on whom he looked down greatly. On Saint Servatius' day, which that year fell on Friday the thirteenth, a big fair was traditionally held in Borgloon. For the fair, the man with the accordion played music at Friskes. When he walked home around midnight, the man saw a strange glow on the market square. He heard women laughing and chattering as if they were holding a party. The sound seemed to come from the gate of the town hall. While the man stood listening in fright, a beautiful woman came up to him and said: "Musician, you shouldn't be here, but there!", and she took him to the gate. When the man entered the ballroom, he saw many women he knew, but strangely enough they seemed much more beautiful at that moment than usual. The musician began to play his accordion, to the great delight of the dancing ladies. At five to one the leader of the witches said: "That is enough now, musician. We will reward you." Some women began to take off the man's clothes. With a big knife one of the witches cut the hump off the man's back. Because the man was enchanted, he felt no pain. At the stroke of one, the whole scene vanished. For a moment the man believed he had been dreaming, because he was standing all alone on the market square, but when he rubbed his back against the wall, he felt that the hump was gone. What's more, his pockets were full of money. On the way home the man sang merrily: "I am as rich as the water is deep and I've lost my hump!" His neighbour was woken by the noise and shouted: "If you don't shut up at once, I'll throw something at your head!" The man was too happy to argue, and he went to sleep. The next morning the man woke up and again began to sing for joy because he had lost his hump. The neighbour grew curious when he heard the man singing so merrily, and he knocked on the man's door, who told him the whole story. The neighbour was jealous and also wanted to be rid of his hump. Normally the neighbour would have had to wait another seven years before a Friday fell on the thirteenth of a month again. He was lucky, however, because the next year was a leap year. On Friday the thirteenth of the following year the neighbour set off with his violin. Even before the clock struck twelve, the violinist was already waiting on the market square. Once the witches' party had begun, the violinist said: "I will play much more beautiful music for you than the other one did, but you must reward me well for it!" The violinist was so excited at the thought that he too would soon be rid of his hump, however, that he played out of tune the whole time. At five minutes to one, some women undressed the man. One of the witches carried a large dish on which they had kept the other man's hump. The leader took the hump from the dish and stuck it onto the violinist's belly, who now had two humps.
171909: A woman lying in childbed saw a cat come in through the hole where the dirty water drained away. As soon as the cat stood by the cradle, the baby began to cry loudly. When the woman wanted to get up, the cat said: "Just stay lying down, Truike!" The cat was a witch who lived nearby.
171914: A man going at night over the 'Helm' of Lafelt to Vlijtingen was followed by a dog. The man quickly climbed a tree, where he had to stay until morning because the werewolf sat waiting on the ground.
171921: Some men travelling with horse and cart passed the house of the Sjattoo. At that spot the horses suddenly stopped. After a friar had said prayers over the horses, the animals could go on again.
171928: A man whose attic was full of rats was visited by his brother, who gave him the following advice: "You must drive the rats to a place where they are better off. You must walk around the house three times at night and leave a little gap through which the rats can run away." Three days later there was not a single rat left in the attic. The rats were in a house a little further down the street.
171938: A man coming back from his daughter's house saw a cat sitting on a tree stump in Dorplein. The man chased the cat away with a little stick. When the cat came and sat on the stump again and the man wanted to chase the animal away once more, the cat said: "Go on, chase me away again, if you have the courage." The terrified man ran home as fast as he could.
171942: A woman had a cow that could not give birth to her calf because she would not lie down in the stable. Only after nine days did people manage to get the cow down on the ground.
171947: A shepherd coming back from the Papenberg by moonlight saw a ghost appear in the distance. Frightened, the shepherd threw his dung fork towards the ghost and hurried home. When the man came to the same spot the next day, he saw his dung fork standing upright in a bush.
171962: Old M. came back to haunt after his death. After people had gone on pilgrimage for him, his soul was released.
171972:
A man who had visited his girlfriend in Uikhoven was walking home along the Maas around midnight. When a cat ran in front of his feet, the man shouted in annoyance: "Damn it, go away!" and kicked at the animal. A little later three cats came running up to the man. Although the cats kept running between his legs, the man was too frightened to do anything more. When the man got home, the cats had suddenly vanished. If you saw a cat in the evening, you must never kick at the animal. After all, the cats that roamed about in the evening were werewolves.

Many mothers did not let their children go anywhere before they had sprinkled themselves with holy water.
171984: A farm on the road to Tongeren was haunted. Behind the wall stood lots of crosses. Nobody dared pass it after eight in the evening.
171999: A woman whose husband had died always heard knocking in the cellar. The friars banished the dead man.
172045: A man walking through the meadow saw a wheel rolling over the ground by a pond. The man came closer to grab the wheel. But he had nothing but hairs in his hands.
172050: The Bokkensteegje was haunted. People often heard branches cracking in the hedge. The horses would then suddenly stop while something like a white sheet crawled across the road.
172052: In the old days people often had to carry the werewolf. If you could then cut the werewolf with a knife so that it bled, it changed back into a human. But you were never allowed to betray the werewolf.
172059: Near 'de Eik' someone had once seen a white lady walking along a little brook.
172076: When Boze Griet (Wicked Griet) laid her hand on someone's head, one always had to place one's own hand higher than hers. That way the witch had no power.
172107: A farmer had moved the boundary post of his land so that he would have a bigger field. When the farmer had died, he came back to haunt with a boundary post on his back. After the parish priest had told the dead man that he had to put the boundary post back where he had taken it from, the ghost was seen no more.
172113: A knight who had lost all his money at cards sold his soul to the devil. When he rode on horseback to the devil's bridge, the devil was driven away by Our Lady, who sat behind him on the horse.
172116: When the priest was praying in the church, he saw a girl who could make mice, some of which had no tail. After the priest had read prayers over the girl, she could no longer make mice.
172118: Nol V.G. owned a little book with which he could conjure the inn full of mice.
172130: On the farm 'De Berg' in Eigenbilzen worked a farmhand who was suspected of being a werewolf. When a glowing cowhide was found in his bed, they decided to set the hide on fire. At that moment the farmhand came running to save his cowhide. Since that day the farmhand was never seen again.
172150: In a stable in Boekt all the animals got foot-and-mouth disease after a witch had been in the stable.
172158: In the pillow of a bewitched child people found a wreath of feathers, a rosary and two beads, and a bone with two feathers.
172178: Werewolves always came to torment people. But if you could hit a werewolf on the spot where he had been baptised, he took on his human form again.
172183: A woman who came peddling had made all the people in a house ill. The people suffered from severe diarrhoea that nothing would cure. The witch was angry because those people had not wanted to buy anything from her. When the woman came by again, she said mockingly: "I'll cure you quickly. Just eat a nice herring!"
172188: A man walking past the cemetery in the evening ran home terrified when he saw a ghost appear. People who had died long ago came back to haunt.
172200: When pensen (blood or liver sausages) were being cooked on a farm, Voddemarie had the witches gather on the 'Kommer'. She would then spread a cloth on the ground and conjure it full of white pensen (white sausages).
172215: When a werewolf made someone carry it, it grew heavier and heavier. The werewolf took great care not to be wounded, for if it lost blood it changed into a human and could be recognised.
172225: A farmer from Kinrooi had a farmhand who was a werewolf. When the farmhand put a special band around his loins, he turned into a werewolf. One day the farmer discovered that his farmhand had hidden the band in a tree stump. The farmer sent his farmhand far away with horse and cart and meanwhile lit the fire. The moment the band caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his possession. Because the farmhand could no longer save his band, he went away for good.
172235: A man walking along the castle lane of Rummen suddenly heard music. Then the man heard a flock of birds fly past with a lot of noise. That must have been the wild hunt.
172239: Pol K. and his friend Marneffe decided to come back from Hasselt by way of the Mombeekstraat, because they wanted to see the ghost of the Mombeekstraat. On the way the pair were suddenly followed by a little nun who seemed to have appeared out of nowhere. At the little chapel of Hilst the nun suddenly vanished without a trace.
172245: A farmer who had lost four cows in a short time for no apparent reason sent for a certain Karel S. Karel read prayers over the stable until the sweat dripped from his head. While doing so he read something aloud from a black book. From then on all the farmer's cows stayed alive.
172252: A man going to visit his girlfriend met a cat on the Demer bridge between Tuiltermolen and Stokrooie. Because the witch cat kept following him, the man ran away in fear.
172258: The cloths of a bewitched child were full of pins.
172266: A girl who had a spot on her eye could not be cured by a doctor. In the end the child was cured by a woman from Piringen. That woman must have been a witch.
172286: The man who had to build Aachen Cathedral could not finish the work in time. The man was approached by the devil, who offered to finish the cathedral on condition that he would get the first soul to enter the church. While the devil was hanging the door in the church, the man quickly threw a dog into the building. The devil understood he had been cheated and said: "If I had known that, I would have laid the Lustberg on Aachen!" That saying is still inscribed above the door of Aachen Cathedral.
172291: A woman from Hoeselt always heard a strange sighing in a certain spot in her house. On the priest's advice, they decided to make a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. After that the ghost was released.
172296: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in the marsh near the church. Those were the souls of unbaptised children. When water had been poured on a will-o'-the-wisp, it vanished because it had been baptised.
172334: A witch knew everything that happened in the village without having seen it.
172339: On a road across the heath, a man met a tomcat sitting on its hind legs. Because the man was afraid, he took a detour. A hundred metres further on, however, he met the animal again. The man ran home as fast as he could.
172347: In Meeswijk people often had to carry the werewolf.
172350: In Smeermaas there was a house that nobody wanted to rent because it was haunted. At night the paintings flew off the walls for no apparent reason.
172351: A boy going home in the evening struck at a ghost with a dung fork. The next day a farmhand lay on the ground at that spot. The farmhand was a wizard who could turn himself into a ghost.
172353: A man struck with his axe at a dog that wore a chain around its neck. Because the man was attacked by the dog, he threw a red handkerchief at the beast's mouth. The next day the man met someone who had a torn handkerchief around his neck.
172372: In the fields of Horpmaal people always heard someone calling at night: "Where must I carry it?" One day a certain Lovi de W. was walking in the fields when he suddenly heard the calling. Lovi answered: "Carry it back to the place where you took it from!" With that the ghost was released. Since then the voice has never been heard again.
172373: Lucifer was after the soul of a man who would soon die. Fate decided that the devil Peer had to go and fetch the soul. Lucifer warned Peer that a clever friar would come who would want the dying man to confess. The devil Peer left hell for the very first time and went to the sick man's house. When Peer saw the Capuchin, he asked the friar what he had come to do there and then said: "That's not for the likes of you. Now be off with you." But the friar was not intimidated and spoke kindly to the sick man, after which he read some prayers from a book. Then the devil said: "Don't believe the friar, he's after your money. It's much better with us; there you're not tormented with confession!" When the devil Peer had the sick man's soul in his power, he said to the friar: "Well, friar, you did your best, but I've got the soul in my claws now. In fact I bet that tonight I'll get your soul in my power too." The devil Peer and the friar made a bet. They played the card game Pintje Pas to decide who would get the man's soul. The friar won the card game and claimed the man's soul. Then he said to the devil: "From now on you'd better stay at home, for wherever there are friars, no devil comes into the house!"
172376: On a farm a sick child had died. After an old woman had come to make a little cross on the child, the dead child was covered in lice. The fathers of Sint-Truiden came to read prayers over the dead child to rid it of the lice.
172380: A pious Catholic from Aken thought he would like to build a beautiful large church. The devil came to the man and said: "I will build you a church that will already be finished before the cock has crowed tomorrow. In return I want your soul." The man agreed to the proposal. When the church was almost finished, however, the man went with a cock to the place where the devil was working. When the cock began to crow, the devil had to stop his work. That is why the top part of the tower is missing from the cathedral of Aken.
172381: One evening Johanna G. came to farmer Luis's stable while he was milking the cow. Johanna stroked the cow's head with her hand and then left again. Because that night the cow began striking the ground with her horns, the farmer sent for the vet. The cow had to be slaughtered because she had gone mad. From then on the farmer never again let Johanna into the stable.
172385: In a house in Engsbergen a cat came in every evening through the water drain hole. One day they managed to wound the cat with an axe. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had a wound.
172389: A woman who brought her husband his food every evening had to go through the Bokrijk wood with her sister. One evening the woman saw a glowing gentleman on a fiery horse riding along the Canada lane. That was a returned dead man.
172392: In the past people did not dare to go to the cemetery in the evening. They believed that above the graves the dead came to haunt, jealous of others because they themselves had not got into heaven.
172394: In the church sat a girl who could make mice. The priest, who had seen that the child had filled the whole church with mice, called the girl to him. From then on the girl could no longer make mice.
172396: Some people keeping watch in the evening suddenly saw a large dog coming towards them. When they tried to throw something at the dog, a large black cloud appeared and the animal vanished into it.
172402: In Opgrimbie there was a stone called the 'duivelskei' (devil's boulder). People believed the boulder had lain there since the time of the ancient Belgae. A large black priest always came haunting near the devil's boulder. In the end the friars of Rekem smashed the boulder to pieces.
172411: Victor the sorcerer from Kuringen could make mice appear by slapping his hand on his knee. After the priest had read prayers over Victor, he could no longer make mice.
172415: A man going on pilgrimage to Roermond with some friends was followed by a young kitten. Because the cat kept following the company, one of the men struck at the animal. The next moment there were some twenty cats.
172419: A boy coming home from work through the woods in the evening had to carry the werewolf. Because the boy was jumped by the werewolf again the next day, his father gave him a knife to defend himself. When the boy once more had to carry the werewolf, he managed to cut the beast with the knife. The next moment the werewolf changed into a human. The boy's neighbour threatened: "If you betray me, I'll kill you!"
172422: In the old days there were many werewolves between Hamont and Dorplein. One day a man was riding to his work at the zinc factory when suddenly a werewolf jumped on his back. The man had to carry the werewolf the whole way. If you could stab a werewolf between the ribs with a knife, you would see at once who it was.
172425: Anyone a witch tapped on the shoulder was in the witch's power. If one tapped higher than the witch oneself, one remained unharmed.
172441: A man who had been playing cards was walking home at about midnight. Suddenly the man heard a rustling among the trees, after which a white ghost without a head appeared. Because the man was very afraid, he began to pray. Then the ghost disappeared among the trees again.
172449: A seven-year-old boy who was bewitched did nothing but cry all the time. After the child had been prayed over and a blessed palm sprig had been placed under the doormat, the witch could no longer come in. The boy was eventually cured.
172461: Some people from Molenbeersel were always accompanied by two black cats when they went home in the evening. The cats would then crawl into a house through the water drain hole. One evening someone had hit the cats with a stick. When the people went into the house, they saw the mother wrapping a bandage around her daughter's head.
172463: In the old days a knocking spirit sometimes roamed a house. Then strange knocking, creaking and rattling were heard. Nobody dared to go on living in such a house.
172478: A girl taking a wheelbarrow of wood to the field met Clet G., the wife of K., on the way. Clet said: "It's cold, put your neckerchief on!", to which the girl replied: "I'm warm enough!" The next day the neckerchief was full of lice.
172491: In Genoelselderen there lived a little boy who could make mice.
172494: In Vliermaalroot lived a witch who wore velvet clothes. The witch often flew through the air on a broom. Sometimes the witch rode a wheelbarrow that became invisible.
172499: A young man was in a relationship with a girl from Mal. But whenever he went to see her, she and her mother turned out not to be home. One day the boy decided to go to Mal a bit earlier. When he came to his girlfriend's house, the boy saw his girlfriend and her mother rubbing themselves with something. Then they said: "Over hedges and hawthorns, over hedges and hawthorns,...", and the next moment they had vanished. The boy went inside and rubbed himself with the ointment from the little pot he had found in the kitchen. Then he said: "Through hedges and hawthorns, through hedges and hawthorns,..." When the boy reached his girlfriend and her mother, he was badly injured. Startled, the girl said to him: "But Lambert, what have you done!"
172502: A woman who had been plagued by the maar (nightmare spirit) for several nights no longer dared to go to sleep. She always felt a tightness, as if a heavy man were lying on her. The doctor claimed it was a standstill of the blood. One day the woman decided to put her clogs upside down under her bed, so that the maar could no longer get onto the bed. That night the woman slept peacefully.
172517: Lambert from Klein Ternaaien went to visit his girlfriend. On the way Lambert was followed the whole time by a cat that walked between his legs. That time it took three quarters of an hour before Lambert reached his girlfriend, whereas it usually took him only half an hour. The man had tried several times to kick the cat, but he could not hit the animal. Since that day Lambert never went to his girlfriend again.
172522: Near the castle of Printhagen there used to be a haunted chapel. The lords of the castle were buried in that chapel. At midnight the dead lords drove through the castle lane in a phantom coach with three black horses. At that moment the animals in the nearby stables all stood up. Because some did not believe the story, bets were sometimes made in which someone was dared to go to the castle at night.
172530: A mother and her child were always ill because a witch regularly came to the house. After the woman chased the witch away one day, she was never ill again.
172539: The wife of X was a witch. When X was bringing hay to the sexton's barn for some acquaintances one evening, it suddenly began to rain. X decided to carry on working the next day and was given a cup of coffee by the acquaintances the hay was meant for. Suddenly a black cat came in, whereupon one of the women said: "What is that black beast? Get out of here!" Then X said: "Oh, just leave the beast alone." Later people realised that the cat had been X's wife, who had come to see where her husband had got to.
172546: A girl of seven or eight passed the house of a witch on her way to school. Every time the girl walked past that house, she fell ill.
172551: In the wood of Spalbeek there used to be a haunted castle. At midnight an old man always appeared.
172554: One evening six men were playing cards. When one of the men had left, the others went on playing for a while. Some time later the other men went home too. On the way one of them was attacked by the werewolf. The man struck the werewolf on the head, so that the beast began to bleed and took on its human form. The man who had left earlier had a cut above his eye and was at last freed from being a werewolf.
172556: A boy was courting a girl whose mother was a witch. People had already warned the boy, because they knew that the eldest daughter usually took over her mother's witchcraft. One evening the boy pretended to be drunk and to have fallen asleep with his head on the table. At midnight the boy was still lying asleep. So the two women flew out through the chimney. The mother appeared as a grey cat and the daughter as a multicoloured cat. When mother and daughter came back at one o'clock, they saw that the boy was still lying with his head on the table. A little later the boy got up, saying: "Oh, what a heavy head I have!" After that night the boy never went to see the girl again.
172558: Two men who had been playing cards walked home together. On the way one of the men suddenly saw a black dog sitting by the road. His friend, however, did not see the dog. The man threw a stone at the dog, and the animal began to spit fire. At that both men ran home as fast as they could. The men never again went home by that road.
172578: The farm of the V. family was haunted. At night the cows broke loose, making a hellish noise. A spirit had to haunt because a vow had not been kept. Some strangers to whom the ghost had spoken had done what was asked, but that proved not to be enough. So the people of the farm decided to bake two hundred kilos of rye flour into bread every year and hand it out to the people. After that the ghost no longer showed itself.
172583: Trien V.O. told an officer of the soldiers who were staying in Eksel that she could no longer make butter. "That is witchcraft," said the officer. "If you don't believe it, just put some dung in your stable." Trien did what the officer had advised her. When she tried to churn butter, however, the dung lay at the bottom of the churn.
172588: In the evenings a boy walked around the sunken lanes of Hees wearing a horse hide. On the advice of the priest, the parents sent their son to Luik, so that the priest could meanwhile take the horse hide from the barn and burn it. As soon as the hide caught fire, the boy was standing by the oven to save his hide. When the hide had burnt up completely, the boy was delivered.
172596: A woman went to sit up at night with a sick man from Membruggen. On the way the woman was followed the whole time by witches who crept through the hedges.
172600: Will-o'-the-wisps were seen mainly near meadows, marshes and areas with peat in the ground. Will-o'-the-wisps looked like the light of a paraffin lamp. The lights were caused by a kind of gas rising from the ground. People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the dead.
172610: At the black barrier by the Edelhof there used to sit a little woman with long hair who had passers-by carry her.
172614: At a crossroads in the fields stood a linden tree on which hung a figure of Christ. A motionless black cat always sat by that tree.
172617: It was said that some children in Maasmechelen had been bewitched.
172635: On a bewitched farm in Romershoven the cows lay with their legs in the air every morning. After a priest had come to pray over the farm, everything returned to normal.
172639: On the Heide lived a miner whose wife behaved badly. As the woman was walking home, something strange suddenly jumped onto her back at the Hoogbrug. The woman had to carry the strange apparition until she was past the meadow.
172643: A witch visited a family at least four times a week. The witch always went and stood by the baby's cradle. After a while the child fell ill. Because the doctor could not help the child, it eventually died. Just before the child's death the witch came to visit once more. Afterwards she said: "It was as if the baby had been waiting for me."
172645: A man was undressed by a witch. When the man asked for his clothes back, the witch flew off through the air with the clothes.
172659: Near the castle of Wideux lay a felled oak that always came back by itself whenever it was moved.
172660: A man was visited by the devil, who had disguised himself as an ordinary person. When the hospitable man made the sign of the cross before the meal, the devil flew out through the window. After that the man could no longer fit a new pane in the window. Only when the priest had sprinkled the window with holy water could a new pane be put in.
172662: Three men who had gone to the pub after hunting saw a cat sitting by the dike on their way back. One of the men said to his dog: "Does, get it!" The dog dived into the ditch, howled and then lay still. In the end the dog had to be carried home. For a month the animal could not stand on its legs. One of the men had shot at the cat with his gun, but he had not managed to hit it.
172670: In Overpelt lived a drossaard (bailiff) who pursued the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a band of robbers) everywhere and tried to catch the robbers. When the drossaard died, his spirit kept roaming in the shape of a black dog. A clergyman banished the ghost for ninety-nine years. In the house where the drossaard had lived, all the windows and doors flew open at midnight. The cows in the stable were untied. Some dogs were sent into the cellar of the house. Not a single dog came back alive.
172680: A certain Royer arrived at the school gate and said: "Look, there's a white woman walking up the church tower!" His friends could not see anything. One day Royer followed the white woman. When his friends later asked him why he had gone off, he remembered nothing.
172693: When Goor B. was coming back one evening from the smith in Schakkebroek, he saw two dogs lying on the road. They were dogs with a chain and a bell around their necks. Goor was so frightened that he took another road to the Jodestraat.
172697: For two years very strange things happened in a house. Rattling was often heard and the occupants were sometimes pinched by something invisible. A strange glowing light could also be seen. At night the pillows and blankets flew off the bed up to the ceiling. The old grandmother's false teeth suddenly disappeared. Three weeks later they were found on the cupboard. Perhaps electricity was responsible for all these things. Everything one touched was statically charged, so that it flew up and one felt a slight shock. When a new electricity meter was installed, everything was normal for half a year. Then the strange events started again. At first people thought there was a rat or a rabbit, but later they believed the whole matter had something to do with the daughter of the house. In the end the girl could not even go to school because she was tormented all night by the strange phenomena. The girl was shunned everywhere because people knew there was something strange about her. Neither the parish priest nor the dean wanted to take on the problem. The electricians claimed the occupants of the house were mad. One day a ball of fire fell through the roof and exploded downstairs in the house.
172698: A boy who had to take his father two cooking pots of food met a witch on the way, who said: "Ha, Jantje, where are you going?" Jantje answered: "I'm taking my father his food, and that's none of your business." The witch warned the boy: "Watch out! When you come to a ditch, you must jump far enough, or you won't make it across," to which Jantje said: "I can hop over that." When the boy came to a ditch, he fell backwards as he jumped, badly injuring his arm and his right leg. Only after several years did the wounds heal, after Jantje had sent for a priest.
172699: In the past people often went hunting with ferrets. The dogs had to drive the ferrets so that they climbed into the trees, where the hunters could go and catch them. One day a dog came running back to the men, trembling with fear and with its tail between its legs. One of the hunters climbed a tree to get a ferret out of it. But when the man was halfway up, the ferret said: "Come up one more branch!" The man was terrified and quickly let himself drop from the tree. As he did so, a strange glow was seen in the branches.
172706: At the Maas family's house the washing was hanging outside on the line to dry. All day no one had come by except a woman who was said to be a witch. But the witch had not been near the washing line. When they wanted to bring the washing in that evening, everything had disappeared. A few weeks later they met the witch wearing a dress that had hung on their washing line.
172713:
A boy often spent time with a witch who said: "If you want to learn something, you must repeat after me." If the boy refused, the witch threw him into the mouth of a horse or a cow.
One day, when the boy was bringing the cows back from the meadow, he found he had left his clogs in the marsh. The boy said to his mother: "I'll be back with my clogs before you've put the cows in the stable." And so it happened. The boy could also jump over the roof of the house with ease.
The father decided to take his son to the friars in Hasselt. On the way they passed a field of oats that was still green. "When we come back later, the oats will be ripe." And so they were. When the boy came to the friars the first time, his father was at the Hasselt bridge. The second time his father was halfway. The third time he was in Zonhoven. The fourth time the father arrived together with his son.
172720: A mother was visited by a witch who went to the child's cradle and said: "Ooh, you have a lovely baby." The next day the baby had a paralysed leg. That man limped his whole life because of the witch.
172726: A witch whose house had burned down came to stay with a neighbour. In the end the woman had to throw the witch out because she had bewitched the bread.
172727: Jan F. promised his sick wife that he would go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for her. But when his wife had been dead for some time, Jan still had not gone. Jan felt restless, and it seemed as if his wife's weight was resting on his back the whole time. So he decided to go to Scherpenheuvel at once. Because he had to haul a heavy weight, Jan was drenched in sweat when he arrived in Scherpenheuvel. When he came back from the pilgrimage, everything was all right again.
172742: A boy grew thinner and thinner because he was afraid of his neighbour, who was suspected of being a witch. A while later the boy's girlfriend also became skin and bone. After the boy had been prayed over by a clergyman, he recovered.
172749: Around half past eleven a dog with a chain walked through the street in Henis. Everyone was afraid then.
172754: Two people walking past the Heksenberg in Bilzen were surrounded by cats. Suddenly a man appeared with a chalice in his hands. Against their better judgement the women drank from the cup, so that they too became witches. The women went along to Zangerheide, where some three hundred witches were dancing. When one of the women said: "In God's name", all the witches vanished.
172755: A sinner who had just died was laid out in a room. At night a violent storm suddenly rose, which blew all the doors open. When people went to look in the room, they found that the dead man had disappeared. The devils had come to fetch him.
172770: A man cycling home suddenly felt a heavy hand on his shoulder, which made him fall off his bicycle. When the man asked: "Harie, is that you?", he was allowed to go on.
172779: A witch lived with her son and her daughter-in-law. When the daughter-in-law gave birth, the baby was covered in scratches. It died a few hours later. The same thing happened two or three more times. Because the daughter-in-law had grown suspicious, she laid a broom in the gutter. When the mother-in-law came home, her face was covered in scratches. After the witch had been sent away, everything returned to normal.
172815: At night the witches of Sint-Truiden gathered to make music. But the witches could not be seen.
172818: On the Beukenberg stood a haunted cottage. The forester who used to live in it had hanged himself. One day some young men made a bet. One of them had to go to the haunted cottage at the stroke of midnight and draw a cross on the wall with chalk. A brave young man accepted the challenge and set off for the cottage. Meanwhile, however, his friends took a shortcut to the haunted house. When the young man reached the cottage, he was buried under grass and earth. Terrified, the young man ran home that night.
172841: A werewolf had hidden his collar in the stump of an oak tree. One day the werewolf was sent to Maastricht. While he was away, they took the collar from the tree stump to burn it. The moment the collar caught fire, the werewolf was standing stark naked, dancing in front of the oven.
172845: A man who often had to cut the hair of a witch's husband had lice every time he finished his work. On his mother's advice the man from then on refused to cut the hair of the witch's husband. Then the witch came to him and said: "You don't want to cut my husband's hair any more because you're afraid of getting lice, isn't that so? Well, you won't get lice any more!" When the witch had gone, the man's hair was full of lice again.
172848: A man had fired his gun at some cats sitting in his garden. Afterwards a finger lay in the garden with a ring on it that read: 'Luik'. The witches of Luik held gatherings in the garden in the shape of cats.
172861: A man who had to carry the werewolf went into the café with the animal on his neck. There the werewolf was beaten until it bled and could be recognised. The man was very ashamed and left because he had been unmasked.
172862: A father had thirteen children, eight of whom had already died. When the parish priest was sent for, he took a pillow from the bed and cut it open. The pillow was full of little roses. After the pillow had been burned, the other children all stayed healthy.
172868: Louis, son of Trien N., had called a witch an 'old prune'. The witch was so angry that she followed the man all the way home. Louis had hidden under his bed, but the witch found him immediately.
172890: In a sunken road between Aalst and Engelmanshoven the robber Philippes was hanged. After his death the ghost of Philippes came back to haunt.
172893: Some men who had gone to play cards in a café where a witch was sitting got lost on their way home.
172896: A man who had been to the fair in Erpekom had said in a café: "I'm not afraid of witches. I wish they would all come to me!" When the man went home that evening, he was attacked by witch cats. The man was so badly injured that he lay in bed for three weeks.
172898: In the woods stood a large chestnut tree that was haunted. At night the ghosts came to eat all the chestnuts.
172899: A man saw cats fighting in the attic. When he struck at one of the cats, the animal changed into the neighbour woman. A witches' gathering was being held in the attic.
172917: In Maastricht stood a house that was haunted. The people who lived there were real bandits. Because a dog had appeared in the house one night, the friars were sent for. One of the clergymen said: "There are people here among you who have not been to Mass at Easter for seven years. You must go to church." The people, however, did not go to church.
172923: An engaged couple went walking at night. Suddenly the boy said to the girl: "I have to do something. If you see a beast in the meantime, throw this handkerchief at its mouth and say: 'Tear it to pieces!'" When the girl saw a werewolf a little later, she threw the handkerchief and said: "Pull this handkerchief apart thread by thread!" When the boy came back after a while, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
172925: A witch stroked a girl's blonde curls and said: "Oh, what a lovely child!" The next day the child was dead.
172927: In Schakkebroek seven ghostly ladies walked in the field at midnight.
172942: At the meadow of Frans S., Klaas J. was always jumped by the werewolf. The werewolf always kept its paw on Klaas's hand, so that he could not get his knife out of his pocket.
172944: A baby lying in its cradle became gravely ill after a witch had visited. The child was prayed over.
172949: When Zjang P. was walking along the castle lane of Printhagen, the gate opened by itself. Two white ladies came past and went into the building opposite the castle.
172950: Between Lauw and Piringen a man came across a black cat. When the man hit the animal, a white lady suddenly stood before him, who said: "Leave standing what stands and going what goes." Then the man got a slap in the face.
172956: A man threw a dung fork at a witch who appeared in the shape of a cat. At that moment a black dog and a white dog ran between the legs of the man's friends.
172961: The marshland of Jesseren was haunted. In the evening strange flashes of light were sometimes seen there. Nobody ever managed to catch the ghost.
172965: If you were jumped by the werewolf, you had to try to wound the beast. For when the werewolf began to bleed, he took on his human form again.
172968: One evening a man from Millen went to catch birds in the meadow when suddenly a foal put its hoof on the man's shoulder.
172969: When Jan V.H. was driving home with a cart of straw, he whistled at the vuurman (fire-man). The next moment the vuurman set the straw on fire.
172971: One evening a man was stopped by a witch at the barrier by the church.
172983:
It was said that the white lady appeared in the woods of Nieuwerkerken. In a small pond nearby, a white horse was once seen leaping as well.
On the road to Binderveld, a man one evening met three women dressed entirely in white. The women pestered the man and said: "Your wife no longer loves you, for she has taken off her wedding ring." What else the women said to the man he never wanted to tell, because a priest had forbidden him. The man's wife had indeed taken off her ring, because she had to do the washing that day.
172984: The daughter of the witch Rooske was disabled. The witch made her daughter healthy again.
173004: When Nol went poaching one winter's day, he shot three times at a hare. But the gun did not work. After the man had sprinkled the shot with holy water, the gun worked again.
173010: A farmer went with his farmhand to manure the field. While the horse pulled a cart of manure to the field, the farmer and the farmhand were already shovelling a second cart full.
