Because the horse was not yet available, the farmhand suggested pulling the cart to the field himself. "But Jacob," said the farmer, "that will be the death of you! The horse could barely pull the cart!" The farmhand would not be talked out of it, however, and pulled the cart to the field himself. When after a while the farmer suggested taking a rest, the farmhand said: "Oh no, I'll start manuring the field already, then you can plough a stretch of it soon." The farmer did not understand where the farmhand got the energy from, and he went to look in the field. The farmhand manured a small patch of the field and then stuck his manure fork into a heap of manure with the words: "Now each his own." A few moments later the whole field was manured.
173022: When a witch had visited a child, pins were afterwards found in the child's head.
173035: A small child had fallen ill after being touched by the evil hand. One day the mother discovered that the child's pillow was full of pins. After she had thrown the pillow away, the child got better.
173054: A man from Kotem walking home along the Maas one evening suddenly thought he saw a large ball of fire. When he came closer, he saw that it was a glowing cow.
173063: A poacher passing a mill was followed by a white lady. When the man wanted to ask the lady something, she had already vanished.
173067: Two young men from Rosmeer set out together around midnight. At the Elderendal the pair were accompanied by a white lady. In Vlijtingen the woman suddenly disappeared. A little further on, however, the lady sat waiting on a turnstile. The lady accompanied the pair as far as Lafelt.
173081: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen moving up and down near a broek (marshy lowland). Although people claimed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children, some believed they were glow-worms.
173100: Two men transporting a cart of apples saw a meowing kitten sitting on the road. When one of the men wanted to hit the kitten with a stick, the animal stood in front of the wheel. Because the horse put a hoof on the cat, it could go no further and began to sweat heavily. A little later a third man came by, who took the kitten in his arms. The moment the kitten jumped to the ground, a tall woman with a child appeared. That woman was a witch.
173103: A woman always heard a strange ticking in her house that seemed to come from the wall. It sounded like an alarm clock running down. Since no one else heard the sound, the woman went to an old lady, who told her: "That sound is someone's heart slowly weakening. Soon someone in your house will die." The prediction came true.
173118: A boy who had to relieve himself said to his girlfriend: "If you meet a werewolf, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. When the boy came back a little later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
173119: A man going to work at the 'Nieste Meulen' in Tongeren (Luikersteenweg) saw a sow walking by the Jeker, wearing a chain around her neck and accompanied by young piglets.
173126: A witch had summoned a spirit for a woman. From then on that spirit came knocking at the woman's every night.
173141: Three farmers were walking in the evening from Maastricht to Voorshoven when they decided to have one more drink and a cigarette at the market. When the farmers then went home, they heard the werewolf moving in the woods. "There he is already," said Pier B., "I think I'll have to carry him tonight, because I live the farthest." When they reached Jan R.'s house, Pier B. and Graad N. went on alone. The werewolf followed them everywhere. When Pier B. had to part from Graad a little further on, he held his medlar stick ready and walked home alone. Suddenly the werewolf jumped on his back. Pier had to carry the beast until he got home. When the werewolf lay dying, Pier forgave him after the man had repented.
173144: There used to be a castle in Maasmechelen owned by the Jew Abraham. However, he could find no tenant for the castle, because it was haunted. At night the doors flew open and a white ghost wandered about. At midnight two horses were sometimes seen standing by the castle.
173145: One morning the roller shutters of a man in Schulen had grown larger, so that they no longer fitted. The carpenter believed it was witchcraft.
173147: In Riksingen, where Torke lives, a dreadful voice was always heard at night, crying: "I'm hungry! I'm hungry!" One night a brave man answered: "Then eat!" From that moment on the voice was never heard again.
173152: The wife of Graad R. was a witch. When the witch came into Stieneke A.'s house one day, she said: "What a lovely child you have!" The next day the child was ill. Two years later the witch came by again. She said to Stieneke, who then had a two-year-old child: "What a lovely child you have!" After that the child fell ill. From two fortune-tellers in Liège, Stieneke heard the following before he had even been able to say what had happened: "There is a woman from the neighbourhood who visits you and who is causing you misfortune with your children." One of the fortune-tellers had given Stieneke something and advised him to go to the church in Hasselt: "You must go into the church. If the church is closed, you must walk around the church three times. There you will find all the saints." Although Stieneke was not a believer, he did what the fortune-teller had advised him. After that the misfortune came to an end.
173158: The sick Haanke B. and her husband were visited by a woman peddling blankets. Haanke and her husband, however, did not want to buy anything. Then the woman said to Haanke's husband: "It is time you set off, for your wife will not live much longer. When you come to a crossroads, you will hardly be able to go on, but you must keep going all the same." When Haanke came to the fen, a black dog suddenly stood in front of him. The man received holy water from the brown friars. The friars had advised Haanke to pray and had foretold that the witch would come within three days to ask how Haanke was. On the third day the woman was indeed standing at the window.
173162: A witch could make mice without tails.
173166:
A witch lived in Rutten. One day the witch stroked the head of Marie's child, saying: "What a lovely child!" The next day the child had lice. In the end the child even died.
When the witch lay on her deathbed, she could not die until someone had taken over her arts.
173169: A farmer had constant misfortune: he could not keep a single animal alive. He had bought a fine cow, but that animal too had died after a few days. Someone told the farmer it must be witchcraft and advised him to put the heart of the dead cow on the stove. When the heart boiled, the witch would have to appear. Because the parish priest advised him against it, the farmer decided to go to the friars in Hasselt. When the friars came to read prayers over the stable, they had the farmer break down the manger. Under the mangers a fat live toad was found. The friars beat the animal to death and declared that the farmer would have no more misfortune from then on. The friars were proved right.
173174: When V. was returning from the fair in Kuringen around midnight, a violent wind suddenly rose that flattened the oaks to the ground. A little later a ghost coach came past and drove through the gate into the castle grounds of Wideux.
173175: In Bocholt lived a farmer whose pigs always made a lot of noise at night. When the farmer went to look, the animals stared at him with a strange look in their eyes. Although the farmer did not believe in witchcraft, he was finally persuaded to go to a man in Oostham. That man said to the farmer: "Your pigs are in the power of the evil hand. If you want to know who is doing this to you, you must stay standing here. In a moment the witch will appear at the window." And so it happened. The witch was Trien B. from 't Goolder.
173178: Anyone ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night could not stir and could not breathe or scream. It was mainly sick people who were ridden by the maar.
173189: In the past there were hundreds of witches who tormented people. Witches could, for example, cause the animals in the stable to die.
173193: At J.'s farm a farmhand was sent to Maastricht with three horses and a cart of manure. When the farmhand's animal skin was found in the meantime, he came back roaring. In the evenings the farmhand went about as a werewolf and had himself carried by people weaker than he was.
173196: In the evening witches, cats and werewolves roamed the Gewaaibos.
173209: Two men going home through the fields in the evening suddenly saw a white apparition fluttering around their heads. A moment later it had vanished.
173212: E. went with his farmhand to manure the field. When they wanted to leave, however, the rear wheel of the manure cart was stuck in a hole. Then the neighbour woman came outside and said: "Are you stuck? Fools! Just drive on!" When the witch called the horse, the cart moved off effortlessly.
173217: Because will-o'-the-wisps were souls of unbaptised children, they often tried to lure people to the water. You then had to say: "I baptise you alone", or else all the will-o'-the-wisps would come to be baptised.
173240: When Harie D. went to pray for his wife at the Dameruskapel, he saw a foal lying behind the chapel with eyes like lanterns.
173273: One day a certain Vital saw a ghost in the Groemelingenstraat. He was so frightened that he kept trembling for the rest of his life.
173282: During the war three men were hanged and a woman was beheaded on the Hoogbaan. Out of revenge, after her death the woman came to haunt the Timbrook in the form of a headless white lady. People frightened children by telling them about this white lady.
173289: Two girls went to visit a woman. "Where is your wife?" the girls asked the man who was working outside. "My wife is inside," the man answered, "go and have a look." When the girls went into the house, they saw only a black cat sitting on the table. The girls went back outside and said: "There's nobody inside. We only saw a black cat." Then the man went inside with the girls. Strangely enough, now there was an old woman in the house. After that the girls no longer dared to visit that woman.
173295: A dealer from Othée took two calves to Liège every week to sell them there. When the dealer was coming back from the gaming house 'Tôt et Tard', he was attacked by a werewolf at the 'little holy house' between Lauw, Othée and Herstappe. The man cut the werewolf on the head with a knife, so that the animal took on its human form again. It turned out to be a merchant from Villers-l'Evêque who had gone bankrupt. The werewolf said to the man: "If you hadn't made me bleed, I would have murdered and robbed you."
173298: Some men coming back from Loon in the evening were followed by a horse. The men were nearly frightened to death when the horse suddenly disappeared.
173301:
A farmhand said: "Tonight I want to meet someone, even if it's the devil!" That evening a man came into the farm who a little later had suddenly vanished. That must have been the devil. 
When the farmhand at last got to know a girl, he went walking with her. On the way he said to his girlfriend: "If a man comes at you, throw this handkerchief in his face." The girl did as she had been advised. That evening she saw to her great dismay that the farmhand still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
173317: On a farm a horse had fallen ill through the evil hand. The horse died that same year.
173329: A man and a woman coming home together in the evening got lost because of a witch.
173346: One day a werewolf's skin was burnt in the oven. For the werewolf's power lay in the skin.
173351: A woman was always jumped by the werewolf when she lit the stove in the afternoon. One day some men kept watch with a dung fork. After the men had stabbed the werewolf in the head, the beast changed into a man from Vlijtingen.
173373: Evermarus travelled with his friends from Friesland to Maastricht. In Herstappe the company stayed at the castle of Hacco, a robber knight. When Evermarus and his friends continued their journey the next day, they were pursued by Hacco, who murdered them all in Rutten. Some time later Pepin of Herstal found the body of Evermarus, which was miraculously unharmed. Pepin had a grave dug in that place for the dead Evermarus. Two hundred years later a man from Rutten saw a herd of deer playing the play of Evermarus, as is still done today on 1 May. The man was frightened, but one of the deer reassured him: "Do not fear, for we are God's messengers. We only come to glorify the life of Saint Evermarus. Tell the people of Rutten that every year on 1 May they must play as we do here today." There was, however, one woman from Rutten who did not believe any of the story, and on 1 May of the following year she went to shear her sheep near Evermarus' grave. Suddenly a violent whirlwind arose, which scattered the wool everywhere and startled the woman so much that she cut her hand. The wound in her hand never healed. From that day on the people of Rutten played the play of Evermarus every year on 1 May. Once, when the procession could not take place because the weather was too bad, the statue of Saint Evermarus was found completely soiled the next day: the statue had gone round alone.
173378: A dealer who went to bring a pig to a witch was astonished when the woman said: "Come on, people of Lauw, go on inside!" How could the witch know that the dealer was from Lauw?
173383: After a farmhand had whistled at the vuurman (fire-man), the farm went up in flames.
173385: In the past almost all misfortune was blamed on witches. When the cattle died or the children fell ill, a witch was always blamed. In Rekem lived three women who were suspected of witchcraft. When a witch had caused harm somewhere, a friar went to read prayers over the bewitched place.
173387: The miller of Lauw had often robbed the farmers by taking more flour from the sacks than he had actually earned. After his death the miller had to haunt in the shape of a black dog. At night the dog made the mill turn. Eventually the priest banished the ghost animal to the little chapel.
173391: The joiner D.C. from Vlijtingen had been kept company all winter by a robin. One morning, however, the man saw a skull in the place where the robin usually sat. The skull said: "I am a member of the family. You must go to communion three days in a row. Then I will let you know whether I am in heaven or still in purgatory." On the third day the joiner smelled burning. A hand had been burnt into the planing bench.
173393: On Christmas night you were not allowed to drink after twelve o'clock. Otherwise the devil would come and say: "Come for a drink? Then you're mine!" People walking along a brook around midnight did not dare look back for fear the devil would grab them by the ears.
173398: A man said to a friend: "If you can walk as far as there, you'll get a bottle of cognac from me!" The friend accepted the bet at once and started walking. But the friend made no progress, because a big dog kept jumping in front of his feet. The man who had challenged the friend was a wizard.
173406: An eleven-year-old girl had to bring food to her uncle, who was sawing wood in Schalkhoven. On the way the girl had to pass three barriers. At the first barrier she saw as many as fifty cats. On the second barrier sat even more cats, and at the third the child saw as many as a thousand cats. The frightened girl walked on until she came to a barn where some men were threshing. When the girl told what she had seen, no one believed her. Then the men went with their flails to the swing barrier, where all the cats jumped on them.
173408: A witch had visited B.'s parents. That night the two children fell ill. Because the doctor could not help, the parish priest had to come and read prayers over the children.
173414: A child that was plagued by the evil hand cried every night between midnight and one o'clock. A fortune teller had told the parents: "You should see whether a toad comes into the house. But you must not harm the toad, because it might be your neighbour!" When a toad did indeed come in at midnight, the man chopped off one of its legs with his axe. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had lost a hand.
173415: When a woman from the village was pregnant, she was visited by a woman who, on leaving, tapped her on the shoulder and said: "Woman, take care!" A few months later the woman gave birth to a child with an open back. A man from the neighbourhood said to the woman: "I will bless you and pray for you. Otherwise the other children you have will have the same affliction." The child with the open back died, but afterwards the woman had only healthy children.
173423: Needles were found in the pillow of a little child who had died. People suspected that Trien B. was to blame, because it was said that she was a witch.
173424: A man from Olmen who wanted to leave for work in the morning could not get his bicycle outside because it was bewitched. The man then put a holy object under the door, so that the next day he was able to leave.
173425: A married couple from the Kruisstraat went to Sint-Truiden to buy a pig. When they were in Alken, they suddenly saw a ten-year-old girl walking about with a little basket. The faster the couple walked, the faster the girl walked too. Suddenly the girl had vanished without a trace.
173433: A white lady appeared in the woods of Wijer.
173435: People whose funeral had no clergyman present had to come back and haunt after their death.
173436: In Meeuwen a man shot with his gun at a hare that often sat in his garden. The man did not manage to hit the animal, however. Someone advised the man to rub some grease from the Easter candle on the gun or to have someone else load the gun. That same evening the man managed to shoot the hare; it was his own wife.
173445: When Bauwers M. was walking home in the evening, he was jumped by a werewolf. The man took out his knife and cut the werewolf. As soon as the werewolf began to bleed, he had to reveal who he was. He begged Bauwers not to betray him.
173449: When a werewolf sensed that someone was going to burn his collar, he flew through the air to save it. If the collar was burnt anyway, the man was delivered and no longer had to be a werewolf.
173451: The fire-men who wandered about in the evening were damned land surveyors. One evening a farmer, against his better judgement, whistled at a fire-man. The fire-man burnt his hand into the gate of the farm.
173452: A witch lived in Donk. Some people did not dare to enter that street, because then they would get an illness that resembled epilepsy.
173460: Some witches disguised themselves as a foal that blocked people's way in the evening. Other witches disguised themselves as a hare to tease people. When people began to pray, the witches could no longer change into animals.
173461: Geertrui van de Z. from Neerglabbeek could make mice without tails. "I can make mice all right," she said, "but I can't get the tails on them yet, because my mother hasn't taught me that yet."
173476: At Spierhof someone had once hidden a boundary post. At midnight people heard someone calling for half an hour: "Pooh...pooh.. Where is the post?" But there was nothing to be seen. The house that stood nearby stood empty for half a year because that place was haunted.
173480: In the dead of night Jules V. had to go to Genebos to fetch the midwife Bet M. When the man came to the house of the head of the witches, he kicked at a cat crossing the road. The next moment dozens of cats appeared and blocked his way. The man began to sweat and felt oppressed. He saw a meadow fence and said: "In God's name." The next moment all the cats had vanished.
173483: A man drove with horse and cart past the house of Alda, whom he always mocked. Alda said to the man: "Don't drive too fast, or the horse might break its legs." A little further on the horse stumbled and broke both its front legs.
173488: One evening a man was walking home through the Ormelant wood in Wijer. Suddenly the man saw something walking ahead of him that kept growing bigger and bigger. When the man passed the ghost, he muttered: "Good evening," to which the ghost replied: "Let go what goes and stand what stands."
173493: A man often came to a place where a witch lived. Sometimes the man came back with blisters on the soles of his feet. Another time the witch had given the man lice.
173496: In the old days, when people saw a magpie sitting on the washing line, they said: "Oh dear, there sits a witch!"
173513: A boy went with the K.A.J. to celebrate Christmas at the Kluis of Achel. As the boy walked to the Kluis with the others, he heard bells ringing in the Wolvenven.
173514: A boy who was taking a walk with his girlfriend announced that he had to relieve himself for a moment. A little later the girl saw a big dog appear with a pipe in its mouth, walking towards the church. When the girl reached the church, she saw her boyfriend standing there.
173516: The castle of Hostaard was haunted. At night the horses were untied, and the maid woke up because everything shook to its foundations. Doctor Fisse claimed there had been an earthquake. Because the haunting happened every night, the castle was eventually demolished.
173526: A man from Dilsen coming back from Rotem was jumped by the werewolf. The man began to pray to be delivered from the werewolf. When the man got home, the werewolf jumped off his back and said: "If you had prayed one more Our Father, I would have been delivered."
173535: Around ten o'clock in the evening a man was walking in Eversel on the road to Heusden. Suddenly the man heard a sound: "Tink, tink, tink." When the man met a big yellow dog, he went through the ditch into the woods. When he got home, the man saw the dog sitting there again. After the man had struck at the dog, the animal was gone.
173542: A man in Vechmaal drove past a witch's house with a fully loaded cart. A little further on the cart got stuck.
173549: The castle where the Marquis of Afferen once lived was haunted. People living nearby always saw a hand holding a candlestick moving in front of the window in the evening. Since the coming of the Angel of the Lord, the Angelus, the evil had been rooted out. One evening a woman saw a fat pig jump through the thorn hedge there.
173571: The late Koba always appeared at the bed of her son Pier. The priest advised Pier to put his clogs upside down beside the bed. The friars gave Pier this advice: "You must go to Scherpenheuvel. If you meet anyone on the way, you must say: 'I am following those men.' Otherwise they may carry you all the way to Scherpenheuvel."
173580: A man drove with horse and cart past a haunted house in Hoeselt. When a sheep suddenly jumped across the road, the horse refused to go any further. A little later a woman came out of the house and said: "You should feed your horse better and give it a slice of bread!" After that the horse went on again.
173598: At a farmer's on the Geiteling, the vegetables in the garden were always eaten by some animal. When one day the farmer saw a cat walking in his garden, he wanted to shoot it. But the gun would not fire. On a friend's advice the farmer scraped some gold off a blessed wedding ring to put in the gun. After that the farmer did manage to hit the cat. The next day a woman lay dead in bed.
173604: In the evenings a white lady walked back and forth by the lane.
173607: In the pillow of a child that had been struck by the evil hand, a rosary was found.
173610: A woman who always went to herd her cows by the Maas could make mice by throwing a few scraps of paper into the air.
173615: A miller who was still working at night was pestered by some cats. The harder the man tried to chase the cats away, the more cats came to sit by him. The miller wanted to ask his wife for help, but could not find her anywhere. So the man began boiling rapeseed oil to pour over the cats. After that the miller could carry on working in peace. The next day a good many women from the village had a burnt back. The miller's wife was one of them.
173618: On Koles there once lived a witch who kept a café. When people passed by there with a cart, they had to go in for a drink, or else they would get lost or the cart would get stuck somewhere.
173631: Michel Noben went with his wheelbarrow to fetch potatoes in Hoelbekerveld. In the Kattestraat the man suddenly saw a black cat blocking his way. When the man tried to strike the cat, some ten cats appeared, which walked in front of the wheelbarrow. The cats followed the man as far as the little chapel.
173646: The grandfather of the sexton of Vliermaalroot was walking home from Kortessem when he saw women celebrating in a field. The sexton asked: "Are you having a party?" The women invited him to drink with them and gave him a glass. The sexton gratefully raised his glass and said: "God bless you". At that moment everything suddenly vanished; the sexton stood alone in the field with the glass in his hand. He later gave that glass to the priest, because he suspected it must have something to do with witchcraft.
173648: When schoolmaster Gielen went hunting one day, he suddenly saw a hare sitting there. The man shot at the hare three times, but the animal sat motionless. In the end the man gave up and left. A few seconds later the hare ran past schoolmaster Gielen.
173651: To recognise a witch, one must place one's feet crosswise on the footprint of the suspected woman. If the woman is a witch, she will look back.
173658: Walkers sometimes said they could hardly move forward because they felt the werewolf's paws on their neck.
173663: A man who was being chased by a pack of cats was frightened when one of the cats said: "You can't do anything to me". After the man had prayed an Our Father, the cats had disappeared.
173664: In Vlijtingen lived a boy who visited his girlfriend every evening. One evening at midnight the girl said to him: "I'm going out. Aren't you coming?", but he did not much feel like going anywhere. Behind the chimney breast stood a little pot of ointment, some of which the girl rubbed behind her ears. Then she spoke the following magic formula: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Aachen", and she flew away. Left alone, the boy decided he would quite like to go to that wine cellar after all. The boy copied everything he had seen the girl do, and then said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Aachen". When the boy arrived in Aachen, he was close to death, so badly had he been battered on the way. At that moment the boy was lucky that his girlfriend was a witch, for otherwise she could not have relieved him of his pain.
173677: On a farm that was struggling with a plague of rats, the Petter put two sheaves together. After the Petter had read something, the rats crawled into the sheaves. "One fat rat has stayed behind," said the Petter.
173684: When Nol N. was riding to the zinc factory in Budel one morning, a black cat leapt on him. That same evening Nol died.
173691: A woman had to haunt after her death. Her husband had promised to have masses said for her, but he had spent all the money on drink. At night the windows and doors of the house blew open. After masses had been said, the ghost was released.
173693: A man going to Opoeteren saw a strange animal by the canal in Gerdingen. It looked like a horse, but it had fingers. The man suspected it was a witch and hurried home.
173694: A man driving to Liège with a horse and cart suddenly saw that a will-o'-the-wisp had settled on the cart. Because the man knew that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children, he baptised the light with some coffee. The next moment, however, the whole cart was full of will-o'-the-wisps, all wanting to be baptised. Because the man had no coffee left, he drove to a pond where he had enough water to baptise all the will-o'-the-wisps.
173696: In 's Heerenelderen people heard the bells ringing in the Duivelsput at midnight at Christmas. A man who had gone to look never came back.
173697: In Budel a fourteen-year-old child had fallen ill after being struck by the evil hand. The child's parents went on pilgrimage to Hechtel in a covered wagon. As soon as they reached the territory of Hechtel, the horse began to sweat heavily. When they got home, the child was cured.
173721: Thijs K. went hare hunting in the Watelersveld. After a while Thijs suddenly saw a coach with two black horses coming from the Geisterse bridge. Out of the coach stepped three black gentlemen wearing white clothes. The gentlemen came up to the terrified man and stopped right in front of him. The next moment they had vanished.
173744: In Tongeren a little child had fallen ill through the evil hand. The neighbour, who was a witch, had also given the pigs diarrhoea.
173750: The damned soul who sat in the chapel appeared in the yard of Mazy in a horse-drawn coach that left no tracks. When a clergyman from Meeuwen came to look, there was nothing to be seen. One day the apparition was gone.
173751: An unmarried woman lived in one of the three Maashuizen. A man returning from Aldeneik one evening saw a pig sitting in a pit next to that house. Some time later someone else came and shot the pig. The next day the witch was seen walking out of the Maashuis with a bandage around her arm. The man who had come across the pig died of fright.
173778: At night a white horse always roamed a closed-off estate. When people got up in the morning, they could still see its hoofprints. But the horse had vanished.
173781: Ten horses stood in a meadow in Donk. On Sunday morning, strangely enough, the horses were standing on the railway.
173785: A man out walking saw a small black heap on the road that flew away over the roofs. That was a witch.
173798: Some cats were sitting in an attic in Schulen. A man had broken the leg of one of the cats. The next day the witch had a broken arm.
173800: One night a man was walking by moonlight from Mal to Millen. At midnight the man came to a crossroads where a big black dog sat. The man was so startled that he made a detour through the field. For he knew the black dog had been the devil.
173801: At Whitsun some people came back from Germany to walk to Scherpenheuvel. When the people stopped for coffee in Diest, one of them dropped dead. After Naard had been buried, his brother could no longer sleep at night because the ghost of the deceased always came and stood beside his bed. On the priest's advice the brother asked the ghost what it wanted. The dead Naard answered, "I had vowed to go on pilgrimage, and I must keep my vow. You must go on pilgrimage for me, and afterwards you must go and pay two francs seventy-five centimes at the shop." The brother did what Naard had asked. On the way to Scherpenheuvel the ghost walked ahead of him the whole time. In the church the ghost sat on the right side next to a pillar. When the man went to communion, the dead Naard went along too. Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
173825: A woman from Rotselaar was bewitched. When the woman wanted to wash her hands, she could not. Sometimes the woman could not get into her bed, and sometimes she could not get out of it in the morning. After long prayer the woman was finally freed from the evil hand.
173826: In Vliermaal a little child was seriously ill. The doctor could not help the poor child. Every day the neighbour came to ask how the child was. One day a woman advised the child's parents to lay a cross in front of the threshold, so that the neighbour could no longer come in. From that moment the child got visibly better. Later, however, it died of tuberculosis.
173827: A witch from Horpmaal came to ask a boy for faggots. After the boy had given her the faggots, he was completely covered in lice.
173859: A little child from Vrijhern was so ill that it kept flailing its little hands and feet. Because the doctor did not know what to do, they sent for Zoavelanneke from Tongeren. This man told the child's parents to take the little pillow out of the cradle. As soon as they had done so, the child was freed from the evil hand. The little pillow was full of needles.
173880: It was always very foggy at the Spekbrug. A man returning from Uikhoven saw a skull at the bridge. The man said: "If you are of the devil, go. If you are of God, stand." As he spoke these words, he knocked the skull into the water.
173881: A man shook his pear tree, but not a single fruit fell to the ground. Suddenly Jul said to the man: "Jerom, Jerom, I see something above you. It's Anna!" The next day all the pears lay on the ground.
173888: A woman who went begging in Vlijtingen came to a house where she was given nothing. Shortly afterwards those people's cow was dead. The animal had a copper safety pin in its heart.
173892: On the castle wall sat a black cat that always followed passers-by.
173910: When a witch had touched a child, she had the child in her power.
173933: A seamstress walking home in the evening was chased by a big black dog. When the seamstress threw a piece of cloth at the dog's mouth, the animal followed her no more.
173934: A farmer who had much misfortune with the animals in his stable went to a man who lived by the Bilzerpoort in Tongeren. That man said they had to boil the bowels and entrails of a dead cow on the stove. In the steam rising from the pot, the farmer and his wife saw the witch disappear up the chimney. The farmer was shocked when he recognised the witch: it was Metje. Metje was then arrested, after which she was burned alive.
173936: Some men were attacked by a big black cat with eyes as big as saucers. The men quickly fled to fetch reinforcements. When they all went back together, they managed to beat the cat to death with four oak beams in Rosalie's meadow. The next day a little dead woman lay in that spot.
173940: A man from Kermt who had hanged himself came back to haunt after his death in the shape of a snake that crawled in the trees. Wherever the snake had crawled, no more leaves grew. The friars had the body dug up again because it lay face down in the coffin. After the dead man had been turned over, the snake was not seen again.
173964: During the war a bell had been hidden in a pond in the Ilsen-beemd in Wintershoven. When people later wanted to retrieve the bell, however, they could no longer find it. At twelve o'clock at night people still often heard the bell ringing from under the ground.
173981: In Kessenich lived a farmer who had to move house three times because he was plagued by ghosts in his home.
173982: A boy going to visit his girlfriend met a black lady at the pond dyke. The boy said "good evening", but the lady did not answer.
173991: At George's in Veldwezelt the cows were untied every night. The stable doors rattled all night and in the morning the cows were soaked in sweat. In the end a clergyman was called in to drive the evil out of the stable.
174013: When Nangske was coming back from Tongeren, he saw a white ghost at the bridge on the Zavelberg that scared him out of his wits.
174017: When the grandfather of Jong D.B. came back from Gellik, the man was followed by an ugly dog that barked all the time and jumped up at him. After a while the dog ran off along the road to Brankmaal. That dog was a werewolf.
174020: A young man went to visit his girlfriend in Opglabbeek. Because the girl was not very enthusiastic, the boy said: "I think you're a witch." When the boy went home, he was hindered by seven black cats that got under his feet. As soon as the boy reached the territory of Otere (?), the cats were gone.
174027: The ghost of the drossaard (bailiff) was banished to the bridge by the Hoest. Some men roasting a sheep said: "If we could fetch the drossaard here, we could roast him like a sheep." A moment later the drossaard rode his horse through the fire. He dragged all the men along with him on the horse's tail.
174035: After Bosmie had stroked a child's head, the child fell ill. The parents believed Bosmie was a witch and went on pilgrimage in honour of Saint Servatius. Afterwards the child was cured.
174042: By moonlight the count of the castle of Wideux came back to haunt. The ghost walked along the castle lane and at midnight sat down on a tree stump. The ghost had been banished to that oak tree.
174056: A man coming back from the field with his cart at night met a dog that crawled between his legs and would not go away. As soon as the man struck a match, the dog was gone.
174068: Farmer Joris was visited by a witch who came to ask whether she could have a lamb from the ewe. "All right," Joris answered, "if the ewe has two lambs." But because the ewe had only one lamb, the witch got nothing. In revenge the witch made Joris's child ill. The girl's legs became so weak that she could no longer walk.
174072: A man got lost because of the alvermannetjes (elf men). After a while he found his way back after all.
174075: A farmhand who had special powers worked at the castle. When the young man threw his hat against the castle gate, the gate opened by itself. People suspected that the farmhand consorted with the devil.
174083: Some people coming back from Houthalen saw a nodding ghost standing by the road. One of the men, however, did not see the ghost.
174090: In the meadows the ghosts tugged at the heels of passers-by.
174094: A man walking home in the evening met a black cat on the way. When the man had struck at the cat with a thick stick, the animal ran away.
174097: Some men were coming back at night from their work in the coal mine when one of them suddenly said: "I can't go any further. Where are all those sheep coming from?" The other men did not see the phantom sheep.
174099: A farmer had some farmhands who always went out in the evening. The farmhands sat down on a tree stump and then turned into dogs. The priest advised the farmer to send the farmhands away for a day and meanwhile burn their collars. When the farmer had thrown the collars into the fire, the farmhands were immediately standing beside him to save their collars.
174120: A farmer had long had misfortune with his livestock. It often happened that in the morning three animals lay dead in the stable. There were white mice in the stable that made the animals ill.
174123: A woman walking to the farm 'de Schans' one evening saw a strange apparition in the oak wood. When she went back along the same road the next day, she saw nothing strange anymore.
174133: In a house, witches' cats always came in through the drain in the evening. One evening the man poured boiling water over the cats. The next day almost all the women of the village had burns on their faces. They were witches.
174134: Werewolves were people who had special powers. When Jannes went to visit his girlfriend, he was jumped by his cousin, who was a werewolf. Jannes had to carry the werewolf all the way to Reppel.
174138: While milking, Peer N.'s farmhand had crushed a cat's front legs in the stable door. Shortly afterwards a maid lay in bed with injured legs.
174139: Near Men M. lived a woman who went to Wallonia for a few months each year to earn some extra money in farm work. The woman had stayed in Wallonia until the end of autumn, when the beets had been lifted. When the woman came back home, she was completely covered in lice. Whatever she did, she could not get rid of the vermin. A year later a woman came to see her and said: "You must burn one louse, and then the other lice will have no more power. The witch who saddled you with this plague will have to suffer terrible pain when that one louse is thrown into the fire." So the woman burned one louse. After a few days she found that there was not a single louse left on her body.
174145: Whenever one saw a black cat somewhere, it was always a witch.
174147: 'Den Houten' from Eigenbilzen had sat down on a calf. But the calf grew bigger and bigger, so that the man could no longer get off. In the field by the Winkelomstraat the calf threw the man to the ground. The calf was a werewolf.
174159: A man returning from Holland by coach had lost a large chest of money. The man said to a woman mowing grass nearby: "Woman, if you have found the money, please give it back to me. If I arrive in Maastricht like this, I will lose my head." The woman lied and said she had found nothing. Because of this the man was beheaded in Maastricht. When the woman was dying, she said: "Keep what you have and I will suffer what I can." After her death, however, the woman came back to haunt, so the priest had to be called to banish the ghost to the Waterval.
174160: A drunkard who had accidentally got himself locked in the church woke up at night when the ghost of the late priest appeared. The priest turned round and asked, "Is there anyone here to serve mass?" The drunkard answered, "Yes, I used to do that as a child." After the mass the priest said to his altar server, "You have released me. I have been haunting here for fifty years, but I found no one to serve mass. Long ago I forgot to say a mass for a man from the village who had asked me to."
174174: Because a school was to be built, some men went to help dig. In the ground they found human bones. They also found a skull with a hole in it. In the evening the men sat joking about their gruesome finds. The man with the hole in his skull must have been a boxer, they said, laughing. Suddenly the light went out and the men heard a loud blow, whereupon everyone fled in terror. It must have been a returned dead man whose bones they had mocked.
174178: A man was coming back from the fair in Riksingen with his two brothers at about eleven o'clock at night. The three men were followed all the way to their house by a black cat. On the way the group had passed a little house where an old woman lived.
174195: A farmhand who had left his collar hanging on his bed was sent to Holland with horse and cart so that the farmer could meanwhile burn the collar. The farmhand had to be held back so he would not jump into the oven to save his band. As soon as everything had burnt up, the farmhand was delivered.
174226: In the house of Poeke-smid a large dog walked around every evening. Although the occupants always locked the door, the dog somehow always got in. The priest could not help the people. One day a friar came from Tongeren, who exorcised and banished the animal.
174230: An old farmer lived with his wife on a farm in Ophoven. While the farmer was at Mass on Sunday morning, an ugly old woman came to visit the farmer's wife. The woman stroked one of the cows on the back and then left again. When the farmer came back from church, the cow lay dead in the stable.
174255: One day a man picked up a piece of bacon from the road. After the man and his daughter had eaten the bacon, they got red scabs all over their faces, and their skin came loose from their skulls.
174260: A café landlady tapped a man who was going outside on the shoulder with the words: "Make sure you get home safely, eh!" But the man got lost and only reached his house the next morning.
174266: Near the Duivelsbaan in Tongeren there was a pit in which bells could be heard ringing at midnight on Christmas night. A church had sunk into that pit. Bishop Sint-Servatius had foretold: "Tongeren will perish and Maastricht will rise." No one ever knew exactly how deep the pit was. Whoever went to listen to the bells never came back.
174269: A boy walking past a wood with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself here. If anyone comes at you, hit him in the face with your handkerchief." The girl did as she had been advised. When the couple got home a little later, the girl found to her great dismay that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
174270: Driek R. was having supper with his family in the evening when suddenly a strange man came in. The child said at once: "That man has strange feet." Driek looked at the man's goat's legs and knew the devil was standing before him. When Driek's wife wanted to sprinkle the devil with holy water, he had already vanished.
174276: A man from Maastricht was carried home through the air by a bokkerijder (goat rider, a robber said to ride a flying goat in league with the devil). When the man felt pain in his leg on arriving home, the bokkerijder said: "You didn't hold your leg high enough when we flew over the tower."
174288: Mina had to help a woman from Veldwezelt give birth. Every time Mina lit a blessed candle, the candle went out. The devil was in the room.
174289: A man from Weert had to flee to his sister's house because he had been in a fight. While the man was eating at his sister's, a woman came in who patted him on the shoulder and said: "It's terrible for your sister that her husband has died." When the man went back home, he noticed that he was completely covered in lice. Because the man could not get rid of his lice, he always had to shout: "Get out of the way, because I have lice!" But the witch could not stand that. As a result the man was suddenly rid of his lice.
174290: People who could not make butter put blessed bread in the milk. Because they still could not make butter, the people sent for the chaplain. After he had blessed the milk, butter could be made.
174291: A man found it strange that his wife got up every night at twelve o'clock. One day the man heard a woman in the neighbourhood say that her baby always started crying at midnight. When the man got up the next night to spy on his wife, he saw her light the fire and prick a little rubber doll with pins. The next day the man secretly threw the rubber doll into the fire. A little later he found that his wife had burned.
174299: A woman who sold animals met a woman who said: "But what a lovely little goat you have!" By evening the little goat was dead.
174312: At night the maar (nightmare spirit) came and lay on people, so that they could no longer breathe.
174315: A farmhand had hidden a band in a tree, with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent away so they had the chance to burn his band. But as soon as the band caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save the thing.
174332: When the witch Minneke came in somewhere, the knives began to move by themselves and the bread turned over by itself.
174336: A farmer who saw a werewolf with a cowhide sitting on the straw stabbed the beast to death with his dung fork. A little later the farmer saw that he had stabbed his farmhand to death.
174352: A man had bet a few glasses of beer that he dared to walk through the 'old street' alone at night. At that haunted spot the man met a horse that blocked his way and reared up as many as five times. In the end the man still won the bet.
174362: In Kessenich, alvermannetjes (little elf-men) lived in an old mill. Anyone who got up at night could see the mill turning. When the mill could no longer turn, the alvermannetjes (little elf-men) moved to another village.
174363: Thomas had to take a wagon of beer to Bree. On the bridge between Bovenwezent and Rekem a cat suddenly jumped onto the wagon. Thomas had tried several times to chase the cat off the cart, but the animal stayed calmly where it was. When Thomas was almost in Elen, he saw the cat finally jump off the wagon.
174364: In Mettekoven a man who had died unbaptized came back to haunt. Every night the man's daughters saw a big black dog appear that knocked everything over. After the friars had blessed the house, the ghost was no longer seen.
174365: At night the silk lady went to pray in the churchyard. Her dress rustled when people passed her.
174367: A little child had died because a completely closed rosary was stuck in the pillow of its cradle.
174369: A mother whose child was always ill was told by a neighbour: "If you keep living here, you may soon have to go to the graveyard!" For in the village lived a woman suspected of witchcraft. She always gave the children something to eat or drink. In the end the mother decided to move to be safe. After that the house was occupied by a young couple with a little child who was very plump and pretty. After a few months the child had become skin and bone. These people did not stay in the house either. The next occupants were informed and warned by the neighbours. Because the woman was pregnant and did not want to take any risk, these people moved away too.
174381: Sometimes a witch would say: "Oh, what a lovely painting! You should wipe it, because there's some dust on it." One must then never wipe the painting immediately, for then one was bewitched.
174383: A witch had infested a girl with long blond curls with lice.
174386: By a house in Lauw was a hedge in which sat a strange little man with a cow's head. In the Kleinstraat a strange creaking was always heard at night, though nothing could be seen in the morning.
174390: A man often saw the maar (nightmare spirit) appear in his sleep. It was a skeleton holding a scythe to behead people. After all, the maar had to do with the French word for 'death'.
174392: On a farm in Beek the horse was neatly combed and decorated with roses every morning. The farmer suspected that a witch came to ride the horse at night.
174398: A bell lay sunken in a marsh in Laak.
174404: A woman had cooked blood sausage. But when she wanted to take the sausages out of the pot, the woman found that the pot was empty. At that the woman said: "Whoever wants to eat sausage can drink the broth!"
174411: In Opgrimbie lived a witch who pushed her child off the milking stool when the cow had to be milked. One day the woman lay in bed with an injured face, although she had not been outside.
174414: The house of Neel T. was haunted. Between midnight and twelve o'clock the tinkling of broken glass was often heard there, though nothing was ever broken. After a clergyman had read prayers over the house, no more strange things happened.
174417:
Armand C.'s father worked for a farmer in Opgrimbie and had to walk through the Sint-Jansbos every day. Because the man often met a werewolf in that wood, he took a dung fork with him and had some friends accompany him. The men did indeed see the werewolf, but the closer they came, the further the animal drew back.
The werewolf had a pelt with long hair and had to walk on its two hind legs. If you could wound a werewolf, its pelt fell to the ground.
174430: Werewolves often made passers-by carry them. Werewolves were people who had special powers.
174432: A werewolf often jumped on someone's back and then made its victim carry it.
174435: In Mechelen-Bovelingen there once stood a monastery of the Templars. It was said that these friars shod their horses back to front. Because the Templars led a debauched life, God punished them and their monastery sank into the ground during a heavy downpour. Since then the local people have often heard the bells ringing from under the ground.
174447: A dead man came back to haunt in the shape of a horse. The animal had a little light in front of its head. The horse could step through the window without breaking the glass.
174449: Fons van D. rode on a wagon to Gelmen together with old Koen. Near the Engelingen mill the men saw a kitten that kept mewing. Koen became so nervous that he ordered Fons to strike at the kitten with the whip. Just as Fons was about to strike, the kitten jumped in front of the wagon's wheels. The horses were sweating and would not go any further. A little later Berke van K. came by, and Fons said: "Berke, wouldn't you like a nice kitten?" Berke eagerly took the little animal and went on his way. When Berke had put the kitten down a bit further on and then looked back to see where it was, he saw an old woman slowly walking away.
174453: Some women went to steal apples from a farmer at night. When the women wanted to leave the meadow, the way was blocked by a big horse. The women could not climb over the hedge, because a witch stood there. When the sun rose, the women could leave. For the sun had power over witches.
174456: Some people had a special collar with which they could turn themselves into a werewolf. One day a man was seen climbing a stack of brushwood bundles and coming down a little later in the shape of a dog. When the werewolf's collar had been discovered, they sent for the priest and sent the man far away. The moment the collar was thrown into the fire, the werewolf was standing by the oven to save his band. While the collar burnt, the werewolf had to be held tight. In the end the man was overjoyed because he was delivered.
174458: A man who was manuring his field was pestered by a cat. Because the man found the animal very annoying, he stabbed the cat with his dung fork. When the man came home that evening and saw one of the maids lying on the bed covered in blood, he was frightened to death. A doctor established that the maid had been stabbed in the back with a dung fork.
174470: A witch lived in Bolderberg. If she had rubbed the cows' heads, the animals gave no more milk. When that woman no longer came by, the problem was solved.
174474: A beggar woman's husband had recently died. At night the dead man came to haunt his wife. When the woman asked him what he wanted, the ghost answered, "The yarn we bought in Maaseik has not been paid for yet. You must go and pay for it, or else my soul cannot find rest." When the woman had paid for the yarn, her husband could go to heaven.
174477: A maid no longer dared to go outside in the evening to fetch water, because at night she saw the pump handle move by itself.
174493: A man who was struggling with a plague of rats read the Gospel three times on a friend's advice. The next moment all the rats disappeared along a path the man had cleared.
174500: The B. family in Solt had a farmhand who always went out in the evening. One evening, however, the farmer saw the farmhand sit down on a tree stump and then turn into a dog. The next day the farmer sent his farmhand to the woods on a pretext. Meanwhile the farmer looked in the tree stump, where he found the boy's collar. The farmer then lit the oven and threw the collar into the fire. At once the farmhand came rushing up to save his collar. But it was already too late. The farmhand went away and was never seen again.
174501: It was said that there was a werewolf in Mie's cottage. The werewolf was unmasked when people saw red threads from a handkerchief between his teeth.
174507: A man who was coming back alone from Kortessem at night saw a priest he did not know approaching in the distance. When the man asked where the priest was going, the priest answered: "Someone in the village is ill and I must go there". The next day the man asked everyone whether they knew of anyone who was ill. As soon as the man found out that nobody was ill anywhere, he realised he had seen a ghost.
174510: On the farm where F. later came to live, there once lived a farmhand who was a werewolf. One day it was discovered that the boy had hidden his animal skin in a magpie's nest in a Canadian poplar. The farmhand climbed into the tree as a man and came down a little later as a dog. The farmer decided one day to send the farmhand far away with the horses, so that he would have the chance to burn the animal skin. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. It was too late for that, though. When the animal skin had burnt up completely, the farmhand said in relief: "Now I am delivered!" A good thing too, for werewolves did nothing but torment and rob people.
174513: When Caroline and Fin were in Velm, they saw a man to whom Fin said: "You'll give us a lift, won't you." The man replied: "That's what you think!" Fin reacted fiercely: "I wish you'd break your neck!" A little further on the man fell off his wagon.
174514: The V.D.P. family feared neither God nor commandment. One day, when the people were handing out carrot slices as hosts, the lamp began to move and a gentleman dressed all in black came in. After the devil had sat down in a corner, everyone quickly ran outside.
174532: In Ulbeek lived an unbelieving woman who was said to consort with the devil. For the woman could heal burns and certain illnesses by reciting a magic formula she had learned from her mother.
174543: A farmer whose pigs were all dying sought advice from a friar from Hasselt. The clergyman advised the farmer to make sure that a certain woman could no longer come in. After the farmer had put barbed wire around his farm, his pigs stayed healthy.
174549: A man going to his field near Kortenbos by moonlight at half past eleven was surrounded by meowing cats. At the stroke of twelve the cats were gone.
174560: A man who had moved a boundary post came back after his death to haunt with the post in his hands, calling: "Where must I leave it, where must I leave it?" When someone answered: "Bring it back to the place where you took it from", the ghost threw down the post and vanished.
174563: Witches often flew to the cellar in Berlin. They first rubbed themselves with witch's grease and then spoke a magic formula. A man who also wanted to fly to the cellar in Berlin rubbed himself with the grease as well. But the man made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said "through hedges and hawthorns" instead of "over hedges and hawthorns". When the man arrived in Berlin, he was badly injured. Moreover, he had not thought to bring a pot of witch's grease for the return journey, so he had to stay in that cellar.
174568: In Ophoven lived a witch who could infest people with lice. Anyone who had lice had to bring the witch something. If the witch was in a good mood, she would take the lice away again.
174570: A witch predicted to a man that he would drive into the brook.
174587: At night a man saw a woman with a white sheet floating above the ground.
174590: A man coming back from Leute was surrounded by dancing witches in the Leutestraat. The witches held a drum and sang: "Rebdebedeb, we're going to the witches' sabbath". One of the witches gave the man a silver cup, and he said: "God bless you". The next moment the man stood with the cup in his hand and all the witches had vanished. The next day a young lady from Maastricht came to fetch the cup.
174602: In Rotem witches came to curry the horses and braid their manes to help the people.
174609: In a narrow field path a beautiful black cat sat on a stick. A man who saw the cat every night decided to speak to the animal once. The man said: "Truuske Minneke, where do you come from?" The animal replied: "Janneke V., where do you come from?" The cat struck Jan in the face, so that the frightened man quickly ran away.
174611: A farmer who had six children went somewhere one morning. On the way the man was constantly hindered by a calf that kept running against his legs. The animal followed the farmer as far as a small chapel at a crossroads. Shortly afterwards the farmer fell ill and died.
174612: When Jank was coming back from Vliermaal in the evening, he saw a dog staring at him with big eyes. A little further on the dog jumped onto the man's shoulders and made itself carried as far as the village.
174624: At D.'s by the church in Waltwilder it was haunted. The ghost blew out a candle three times in a row. When a friar came to banish the ghost to a palm shrub, the spirit said: "You stole a pen." The friar replied: "I still need that pen to banish you."
174626: A woman who worked in Wallonia had vowed to go on pilgrimage for the recovery of her sick son. But because the son suddenly died, the woman had not kept her vow. When the woman went to fetch water in the meadow one evening, her son appeared among the trees. Startled, the woman asked, "Is that you, Martin?", whereupon the ghost answered, "Yes, mother. You had promised to go on pilgrimage. If you do, I will be freed from purgatory." The next moment the ghost vanished. But the woman was never able to go on the pilgrimage, for she died of the shock of seeing her dead son.
174641: A girl was working somewhere when a pillar suddenly fell on her foot. At that very moment a witch nearby had whispered something unintelligible.
174644: A girl was going with a boy who, unknown to her, owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the boy was out walking with his girlfriend. After a while he said to the girl: "If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." When she saw a dog, the girl did as her boyfriend had advised. When the boy came back a little later, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
174648: A man from Binderveld kicked at a dog that came at him one night. The next moment a witch stood before him.
174663: A farmhand of Palmenhof was sent away so that the farmer could meanwhile burn his collar. The farmhand was greatly relieved when he was delivered from being a werewolf.
174665: A man coming back from Sluizen was suddenly stopped by trees and water blocking his way. After he had made the sign of the cross, he could pass again.
174690: One must never pick up hairpins lying in the street. After all, they could be bewitched.
174691: A man saw a white lady working in the potato field at night. The next day there was nothing strange to be seen in the field.
174720: A farmer had a farmhand who owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmer sent his farmhand to the market in Genk. Meanwhile he took the collar from the tree stump and lit the oven. As soon as the collar caught fire, the farmhand was standing by the oven. At that moment the farmhand seemed possessed by the devil, for he even wanted to jump into the fire to save his collar.
174732: A boy out walking with his girlfriend saw that the moon was starting to shine and said to the girl: "Hurry home, because I have to relieve myself behind a bush. If a beast attacks you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." When the girl was almost home, a wolf came at her. The girl threw the red handkerchief at the animal. The next day the girl's boyfriend came to visit. To her great dismay she saw that he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
174741: It was said that the place between two hedges in Stevoort was haunted. One evening a curious boy went there to look. The boy saw a dog that followed him. A moment later the dog had vanished.
174747: In the past there were many ghost hares in the woods of Weert. Such hares could only be shot with blessed shot.
174755: A witch who often came begging lived by the canal. If the witch did not get on well with someone, she bewitched that person's cows, so that the animals died. In the end that witch was burned. To protect oneself against the evil hand, one had to pray.
174765: When Willem K. and Lambert M. had finished planting the potatoes, they thought they heard someone on the hill calling for help. There was nobody to be seen on the hill, but there was a screeching black cat as big as a dog. Lambert wanted to strike the animal with his spade, but Willem held him back and said: "If you strike, we may both die." The next moment the men were surrounded by countless cats. As soon as music sounded in the distance, all the cats had vanished.
174766: Anyone ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night could not stir. The maar could only be kept away by putting one's clogs upside down beside the bed or by laying two crossed straws in front of the door.
174772: In Peer there lived a woman who gave apples to everyone. Whoever ate the apples fell ill, however, because the fruit was full of toads.
174782: Twice a week Jan went from Goolder (?) to Bocholt to fetch draff. When the man came back, he always had to help the witch Trien onto the cart. That witch could change herself into a cat. Trien was seen like that at Boschheuvel (Kaulille) and at Eetseveld (Opglabbeek).
174791: Sometimes a witch in Elen lit candles at night. If the witch wanted to curse someone, she stuck pins into those candles.
174798: Some people who went to milk in the woods were afraid because they were always followed by a white woman. Since the parish priest could not help, the people went on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. The white woman followed them as far as the church. During the consecration she vanished.
174821: At midnight a terrible noise could always be heard in the Geuzentempel (Beggars' Temple) in Alken. The building also had a window that could not be closed up in any way.
174825: When Willem F. was mowing by the Ketsingengat, he suddenly saw a werewolf sitting there in the shape of a black dog. After a statue of a saint had been hung at that spot, the werewolf was not seen again.
174826: A man who had been ill for years believed he was bewitched. A fortune teller claimed that at midnight she saw someone standing in the doorway, but the other people saw nothing. A clergyman gave the sick man's brother a box full of pins. The brother had to throw those pins away in the field and come back by a different road. The man, however, was never cured.
174836: Behind the castle where two sisters lived was a hill with chairs on it. Every day those chairs were mysteriously moved.
174839: A man who lived in the Bessemerstraat went to visit his girlfriend on Sundays. Whenever he passed through the 'vlood' (marshy lowland), he always saw a mysterious light in the sky.
174843: A mother whose baby was always crying was told by her neighbour: "The witch Dina, who often visits you, is tormenting your child. When Dina is herding her cows, she takes a little doll and keeps pricking it with pins. You must not let that witch in any more".
174855: When there was a newborn child in a house, no witch could be let in. In Tongeren children had often been bewitched. The witch would then make the child get a hunchback or become paralysed.
174861: Three brothers from the Kempen could inherit a beautiful castle from a distant cousin. Whoever dared to spend the night in the castle would be the heir. The first to sleep in the castle was Isidoor. But when a foot fell out of the chimney at midnight, he fled home. The same happened the next night to Theofiel. William was the last to try. That night a torso, two arms, two buttocks, two legs and two feet fell out of the chimney. In no time the bones turned into a complete skeleton standing upright. The ghost took a chair, sat down and began playing cards. William was scared to death. When he had his fear under control, he pulled up a chair and played a game of cards with the skeleton.
174864: A girl went with her boyfriend to the parish priest to register their intended marriage. On the way the boy said: "I have to relieve myself," and he disappeared behind the hedge. The girl's black handkerchief was torn to pieces by a beast. When the boy came back a little later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
174876: In the Beker Broek near the Mariahof a bell lay sunken in the ground. Every year on Christmas night the bell was heard ringing twelve times.
174883: When Harry B. was coming back from a dance, he suddenly saw a large fireball floating through the air. All at once the fireball burst apart. At that moment the man felt a strange stab in his neck. Although nothing could be seen on the man's neck, three weeks later Harry was struck down by an illness that eventually killed him.
174884: A werewolf was a big dog that jumped on passers-by's backs in the dark.
174909: A man was driving his horse and cart to Bree. When between Kinrooi and Bree a cat suddenly jumped between the spokes of the wheels, the horse had the greatest trouble pulling the cart. On arrival in Bree the cat had vanished and the horse could pull the cart effortlessly again.
174910: A man had to help Mina decorate the parade float that drove around just after the war. Although the man had already been working for quite a while, Mina said: "Juul, you mustn't go home yet. First you have to hang the flowers on the float, and then you can churn butter." When Juul had somewhat reluctantly finished all the chores, Mina gave him cake and coffee. Because he had eaten so much, Juul fell asleep at the table. When he woke up, it was already half past two and Mina had vanished without a trace. Juul searched every room in the house for Mina, but could not find her. Suddenly Mina was standing behind him.
174921: The card-playing knight sold his soul to the devil to have money to build a new barn. Because the man often played cards, his mother or his wife had prayed a lot for him. When the man went to the brook to meet the devil, he was protected by Our Lady, who sat behind him on his horse.
174923: A boy who had not been baptised properly made mice at school. After the priest had read something from a book, the boy could no longer make mice.
174926: A man was taking potatoes to the market in Sint-Truiden. At a café in Nieuwerkerken the man saw a black cat sitting on the doorstep. When the man wanted to strike the animal, the cat said: "Am I in the way?" The next moment the cat had vanished.
174928:
When witches had rubbed themselves with a kind of grease, which they kept in the hollow of the chimney, they could fly. The witches often flew to Cologne after speaking the following magic formula: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Cologne". One day a man had eavesdropped on the witches. The man also rubbed himself with the grease and then said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Cologne". Because he had spoken the formula wrongly, the man flew through the thorns and was badly injured.
When the witches flew through the air, beautiful music could be heard. At the Boskelle farm people had often heard it. Once a man stood listening to the music with his gun in his hand. When he shot in the direction of the sound, a silk scarf fell from the sky.
174937: A man going to the windmill of Vlijtingen met a raging horse with little flames around its head. The man was so frightened that he ran straight home.
174951: The mistress of the mill of Ophoven was seriously ill. At night all kinds of noises were heard around the mill, though nothing could be seen.
174965: A farmer wanted to let his cow drink in the brook when a witch suddenly came by. The witch muttered something, which made the cow fall into the water. After the farmer had spat in the witch's face, the cow was able to crawl out of the brook again.
174975: Two boys were no longer allowed by their father to go walking once spring had come. When one of the boys asked why not, his father answered: "Then there's a werewolf sitting on the rampart. That's a very ugly man with teeth like a seal. If such a werewolf jumps on your back, you have to walk around Maaseik with him three times. The second time you can try to take the werewolf's collar off. If you manage it, he's gone for good. Otherwise he starts screaming after the third round and then disappears."
174986: When people could not make butter, they often believed the culprit was someone who had visited during the churning. A priest then had to come and say prayers over the milk and the animals to neutralise the influence of the evil hand.
174987: A woman who went round sharpening people's scissors often stood by a child's cradle and said: "Oh, what a lovely child!" If the child then fell ill, people believed that woman was a witch.
174996: One night a man went alone to fetch a midwife. When he came into an alley, he saw the hedges swaying violently back and forth, though there was not a breath of wind. He also heard an infernal noise that filled him with great fear.
175013: A man saw a large illuminated cross among the trees near the castle of Jageneau.
175014: A farmer had to get up every night because the horses in the stable had been untied. After the parish priest had said prayers over the stable, no more strange things happened.
175022: The witches' spell went as follows: "Over hedge and hawthorn to the wine cellar of Aachen". A man from Niel who had spied on some witches wanted to try it too, but he made a mistake. The man said "through hedge and hawthorn" instead of "over hedge and hawthorn". The poor man arrived at his destination covered in blood.
175028: Some people had caught a heifer in the Riemsterdal. When they were almost home, the heifer tore itself loose and clapped its hooves.
175031: In the old days the werewolf often sat on the dunghill. When someone went there to relieve themselves, the werewolf often jumped on that person's back.
175067:
Parish priest K. had said in his sermon that fifty-two witches lived between 't Boshuis and 't Hof. When the daughters of J.F. from Westerlo wanted to go to Scherpenheuvel, strangely enough they could not manage to light a light. The witch master established that the women were bewitched. When the witch master accused the witch of the evil, she said: "That man's tongue ought to disappear from his mouth". The witch master died of cancer of the tongue.
When a witch came to borrow buttermilk, one could become bewitched. The most dangerous witches, however, were those who came to borrow sourdough.
175076: A farmer who had much misfortune in his stable went to the fathers of Weert for advice. One father came with him to the stable and could predict exactly which animals would still die and which would survive.
175094: A witch from Hoelbeek had bewitched her husband. When the parish priest came to give the man the last rites, the witch stood crying. Then the priest said: "Don't cry, for you did it yourself!"
175095: A woman walking along a path through the meadow saw a cat sitting on a barrier. At that moment the woman could not move another step.
175102: A man driving with horse and cart along the paved road saw a witch standing outside. At that moment the man could go no further. Only when the witch went inside could the horse pull the cart again.
175103: A maid who worked in Maastricht was afraid of a woman who often came peddling. That woman was suspected of being a witch. Some time before, that woman had stroked a child's head. In the evening the child fell ill and a few days later it was dead.
175105: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. Those lights lured people to the water until they drowned.
175120: A little child that had been struck by the evil hand got a hunchback. When the mother had been on a pilgrimage to Offelken, she saw a large spider on the way back. She did the spider no harm, however. After that the child recovered. Something strange had been knotted into the child's pillow.
175125: One evening a fine saddled pony was wandering about in the Broekstraat. When a man sat on the animal's back, the pony shot forward at lightning speed. Because the man feared for his life, he cried: "Oh God, what will become of me now!" The next moment the pony threw the man to the ground.
175143: In 1904 or 1905 the nuns moved into a convent in Lanklaar. They did not know, however, that a freethinker had once lived in that house. Every night the nuns heard chains rattling. Even after the priest had blessed the house, they still heard the rattling. In the end the French government decided to demolish the building.
175153: In Widooie lived a witch who could infest people with lice. In one house a cross was hung above the door to stop the witch coming in. When the witch came to a woman to ask for alms or a sandwich, the woman first made the sign of the cross with holy water.
175155: E.'s farm was bewitched. Whenever the woman came down the stairs, she always felt someone pulling at her dress. Sometimes it was so bad that the woman almost fell down the stairs.
175170: A boy visiting his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to go home quickly now, because my friend is waiting." While his girlfriend walked part of the way with him, the boy protected her from the werewolf that jumped on people and made itself carried. When the couple were married and one day came home past a copse, the young man said: "You walk on ahead." The girl turned deathly pale with fear. When she got home she saw a black dog running away, laughing.
175177: A young farmhand named F. was herding the pigs in Heurne-St.-Pieter. The boy did nothing but curse the whole time. When he was in the Beeksteeg (also called the Morellesteeg), a violent thunderstorm broke out. That evening the pigs came home alone. The boy was never seen again. People suspected that the devil had taken him with a bolt of lightning.
175200: One day a man from Gors-Opleeuw came to fetch Siena, the midwife from Loon. The man had come alone because both his parents were ill. On the way, in the Gillebroek in Kerniel, they saw a beautiful black silk glove lying on the ground. Siena picked up the glove and gave it to the man, saying: "You can still use that for pulling up nettles." But the man threw the glove back on the ground. At that moment a big black dog appeared and took the glove in its mouth. When the midwife reached the pregnant woman, she was incapable of anything, so frightened was she.
175203: A man whose wife had died heard someone knock on the door. When the man opened it, his wife, dressed in white, stood at the door and said, "You still have to go on pilgrimage." After the man had gone on pilgrimage, the ghost no longer showed itself.
175206: A witch kept killing a horse's foal.
175219: A beggar woman knocked at a house where a newborn baby lay in a cradle. The beggar woman stroked the baby's head and said: "Oh, what a lovely child!" When the woman was outside again, the child began to scream loudly. The beggar woman had bewitched the child.
175232: There were always many black cats in the house of Trui V.S. Although it was said that Trui was a witch, a farmer often went to play cards with the woman. When Trui went outside one evening to fetch wood, at least ten meowing cats jumped inside. As soon as Trui came in, the animals ran outside again.
175234: In the street a barrel rolled back and forth by itself.
175236: Even with three dogs and a lantern, Trien did not dare go past Zjang's meadow, because a werewolf sat there. Nèt often had to carry that werewolf.
175242: On seeing a flash of lightning, a man hurried inside. At that moment, however, a ball of fire came rolling into the house. When the man took a crucifix from the wall, the ball of fire disappeared through the roof.
175245: Jan V., who lived in Sluizen, was riding one day over a bridge in Neerem, where the Jeker flows. A little cat was sitting on the railing of the bridge. Jan stroked the animal's back and said: "Hello, pretty pussycat!" Suddenly the cat flew up and began to sing: "Janneke V. asked of me: 'Pussycat, where do you come from?'" Luckily Jan V. had been very friendly to the cat.
175263: A farmer whose stable was bewitched went to ask the parish priest for advice. The priest came to sprinkle the stable with holy water and also poured some holy water into the animals' drinking water. After that no more strange things happened.
175284: Some men did not dare to pass a turnpike barrier in the evening because a black cat was sitting on it. Then one of the men said: "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, flee!" The next moment the cat had vanished.
175285: A farmhand from Kiewit had to carry a woman's sheets on the cart so they could be bleached. Because the farmhand had laid the sheets on top of each other, the woman was angry and said: "Whoever has done this to me, I will punish". Some time later the man got problems with his legs.
