179692: In Kevelaar the priest still preached about the town of Vijvere, which is said to have sunk because of the wickedness of its inhabitants. On a plain where peat was dug, horseshoes were found, clear proof that horses had once walked there.
179696: A witch went about in the evenings with a magic wand to turn people into dogs or cats.
179703: A man who went to look at his heifers was invited into a witch's house on the way. Because the man had accepted peaches from the witch, he was ill for eight days.
179706: In the Kasteeldreef in Sint-Lambrechts-Herk a coach with four horses always drove at night between twelve and one o'clock. It seemed as if the coach drove through the iron gates, but the next morning there was not a scratch to be seen on them.
179707: Celestinus was making syrup while his friend Methieu kept him company. That day, however, the syrup would not set. When the man tried again, it failed once more. "The witch Bet is working in the field a little further on!" said Methieu. "She must have bewitched the syrup!" A little later Celestinus realised that he had simply forgotten something. Methieu, however, remained convinced that the witch was the cause of the problem.
179710: A man walking in the woods on a summer evening suddenly heard a rushing sound in the air accompanied by beautiful music. The man believed it was witches flying through the air.
179731: Will-o'-the-wisps were little souls of unbaptised children that moved up and down.
179740: On a farm the girls regularly sat outside to enjoy the fine weather. One day, however, a jet-black dog appeared, which frightened the girls to death. The dog came back regularly, and one evening it turned into fire. In the place where the dog had sat, VUURSPOOK (fire ghost) was written in black letters. After the girls had wiped away the letters, they never saw the dog again.
179744: Witches often tried to pass their power on to someone else. When witches gave you something to eat, you had to bury it quickly, or else you would become a witch yourself.
179747: Because the pigs on a farm all died, people believed the animals were bewitched.
179762: A witch who had bewitched a skinny boy from the neighbourhood could not die until she had passed her arts on to her daughter.
179780: A man had gone to live in the house of Marie T., a notorious witch. One morning all the windows were open and the goats were standing in the field. Shortly afterwards the man left the bewitched house.
179783: A girl from Schaffen went to the ball against her mother's wishes. Her mother, who was a witch, had said: "May you drop dead at the first dance!" When the girl was dancing with Paul V.D.V., she fell dead to the ground.
179788: A witch had struck her own leg with the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
179825: A man walking along the Diepe Straat in the Stielebroekskes met a friar who needed an altar server. After the man had served mass for the priest, the clergyman vanished. The next day exactly the same thing happened. After that the man never saw the priest again.
179839: The fire-man came flying from the meadows and set a woman's house on fire. When the priest began to pray the Gospel of Saint John, the wind turned at once, so that no other houses caught fire.
179846: In Deurne lived a farmer whose cows were plagued by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). Because the farmer always heard the noise of chains in the stable in the evening, he went to have a look. One day the cows walked up the wall. Another time the cows walked outside two by two. After the farmer had been to the Paterke, everything returned to normal.
179856: The brewery of Membruggen used to be haunted. Whenever the man went to sleep in the hayloft in the evening, someone always took his cap off his head. But the man saw nobody.
179864: A man frightened the wits out of the women in the meadow and took the washing off the line. He had even been guilty of graver sins, such as murder and arson. One night, when the sinner was sleeping in a farmer's stable, he was visited by the devil. The man was so frightened that the next day he went to Averbode to repent. The man had to pray a great deal before the devil left him alone.
179872: A man coming back in the evening from his work in Luik was followed by a big dog that kept jumping against his legs. When the man took a stick to hit the dog, the animal suddenly vanished.
179876: The werewolf was a kind of dog. When people walked home in the evening, they often had to carry the werewolf. A butcher who had already had to carry the werewolf once took a knife with him the next time, which he held at shoulder height. When the werewolf jumped on the butcher, it wounded itself and so became human again.
179877: Two men coming back from Hamal were followed by a cat. On the way the men had kicked the cat several times. When the men got home, they saw a woman come outside, who said: "If you dare kick me one more time, I'll make sure you can't move anymore!"
179888: A father who had already lost one child had a child who was ill. A woman from the neighbourhood had brought a scapular to cure the child, but it had not helped. One day someone said to the father: "You must keep that woman out of here!" Someone forced the woman to go to the sick child. After the woman had pulled a few pins out of the pillow, the child recovered.
179892: The bricklayer in Neeroeteren was often plagued by strange cats. Whenever he dared to strike at a cat, he was immediately surrounded by dozens of cats.
179896: A sick man vowed to go to Scherpenheuvel nine times if he recovered. But when the man had recovered, he did not go on pilgrimage. After his death the man had to haunt. He said to his wife, "I am your husband and I am obliged to wander about as long as the vow has not been kept." The woman went on pilgrimage, followed by a walking stick. When the woman was in Scherpenheuvel for the ninth time, she felt something pinch her arm. It was her husband, whose soul was finally released.
179897: In Gelieren there lived a witch who bewitched people into the woods and made them lose their way.
179915: Finneke van de L. was seriously ill, but she could not die. On her sickbed she would jump up and cry out in fear: "They're coming to beat me again!", but nobody saw anything. Jossa went to the sorcerer of Zepperen, who suspected that the woman was bewitched. Jossa proposed: "Tell me who the witch is, and you'll get half my fortune," but the sorcerer refused. The sorcerer predicted that the first woman to come and see Finneke after she had died would be the witch. After long suffering Finneke did die. The first to come and see was Parent's wife.
179916: A man who had many cats in his attic hit one of the animals on the paw. The next day an old woman had a broken arm.
179919: A boy from Eigenbilzen was walking his girlfriend home one evening. When the pair reached the village, the boy said to the girl: "Go on alone from here. You needn't be afraid. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. The next day the girl found to her great dismay that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
179940: In the past a ghost wandered through Ophoven. The parish priest banished the ghost to a pit in his garden. The pit was covered with cement. Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
179965: Some people going to the market early in the morning 'in den Briel' in Bilzen met hoarse Trijn on the way. Because Trijn came from the fields, she was soaking wet and her clogs were caked with mud. When the people arrived at the market, Trijn had already been standing there for quite a while in fine clothes and polished clogs.
179975: If you went and stood in the Kruisstraat in Kuringen, the devil came and you could sell your soul. Once you had done so, you could take on all kinds of shapes.
179976: A boy had to bring coffee to his father, who was mowing in the field. On the way the boy met an old woman who held up a clover flower and said: "Look what lovely seed!" When the boy reached the field, he was completely covered in lice and fleas.
179989: In Martenslinde three little hares ran about that no one could catch. When a house in the village was demolished, money was found in the ground. Since then the little hares have not been seen again.
179993: A woman from Opheers had vowed to go on pilgrimage. Because the woman had died before keeping her vow, she had to haunt after her death. After the ghost had gone on pilgrimage, it was never seen anywhere again.
179995: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in the meadows by the churchyard. They were the little souls of unbaptised children.
180011: Some men who lived in Boshuize in Dilsen were coming back from the fair in Rotem around midnight. In the Tumbrook the men suddenly saw a headless white lady walking. One of the men was not afraid and walked home arm in arm with the lady. When the lady let go of the man's arm, it was as if a violent storm arose.
180020: At midnight the dead count drove around in a coach on the grounds of the castle of Mechelen.
180026: A man going to play cards at a friend's in the evening saw a cat sitting on the road near the Hussenhof. The man threw a clod of earth at the animal's head. When the man went to relieve himself in a field a little further on, he could not get back to the road. After the man had crawled around on hands and knees for two hours, he reached the Hussenhof again at midnight. The cat had made him lose his way.
180034: On a farm in Beringen three cows had died within six weeks. The farmer believed a witch was causing the misfortune and so sent for the chaplain. The clergyman read from his prayer book and gave the farmer a medal to hang in the stable. After that the farmer had no more misfortune.
180043: A man from Mulken walking under the chestnut trees in the Fontaine lane one evening suddenly saw a white lady appear. "Good day, miss!" said the man. The lady, however, did not answer. When the man struck at the apparition, he saw that it was Fränske, the stammerer from Broek.
180046: A young man often called on the Q. family, who lived opposite the shop in Meers. The young man, also called the Brilleman, sold all sorts of things, including medicines. Because the Q. family always had bad luck with their animals, they decided to ask the Brilleman for advice. They told him that their horse had recently been in foal, and that the foal had died again. "Let the horse get in foal once more," said the Brilleman, "and then make sure you keep the witch out!" The Brilleman predicted that the foal would be a stallion and that this time it would not die. A woman who often came to the Q. family to fetch things stopped coming in the following months. And so a healthy stallion was born in the Q. family's stable, just as the Brilleman had predicted.
180049: A maid called Marie worked at Abroxmolen. One day Emmanuel C. had to come to Abroxmolen to slaughter the animals. Although it was really still too early to slaughter, Marie had insisted that the butcher come anyway. When Emmanuel finished his work at half past two, he walked home. On the way he met a big white cat. Emmanuel said to the animal: "You'd better stay in your cage instead of bothering people. Go away, or I'll hit you!" The butcher carried a stick on which the parish priest had dripped some wax from the Easter candle. Yet the cat was not afraid, and a little further on sat calmly waiting for the man. Then Emmanuel threatened: "Watch out, because when I get to Beek, I'll tell everyone you're a witch!"
180050: Some children from Lutselus (Diepenbeek) always set a plate on the table at mealtimes for their deceased grandmother. One day the priest told the children to ask their grandmother what she wanted. The ghost answered: "I want a washed and ironed napkin." When the ghost got what it had asked for, it said: "No, I don't want that one, because it was washed and ironed on a Sunday." Then the dead grandmother was given another napkin. Thereupon the dead grandmother burned her blackened hand into the cloth and said: "Everything is charged hereafter and little is forgiven."
180071: A woman from Lommel who was married to a Walloon had been given the nickname 'Zwarte Fles' (Black Bottle) because she was always dirty and because she had once thrown a bottle at Jan V.M. in a fit of rage. The Zwarte Fles tormented a family, in whose house she rattled chains at night.
180073: In Ophoven lived a woman who peddled soap. One day the soap seller stroked a newborn baby's head, saying: "Oh, what a beautiful child!" The next moment the child began to cry. In the end they had to take the child to the parish priest.
180074: A man coming back from the Waalbeemd could no longer find the way home. The 'dolende man' (wandering man) had made him lose his way.
180079: Will-o'-the-wisps sometimes appeared on high ground in Kozen. It was said that these lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
180095: A man and a woman were coming back from Mass in 's Heerenelderen. Because they saw a yellow cat sitting in the ditch along the avenue, they took another road. But there a black cat was sitting on a tree stump. The man and the woman bravely went on until they met a small red cat that miaowed the whole time.
180109: A will-o'-the-wisp was burning nitric acid. In the past people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children.
180124: A woman coming back from Koninksem found a witch at her home. The woman had asked the witch to bring her a new hat from Tongeren. Before the woman had even had a chance to take off her coat, the witch put the new hat on her head, saying: "I've brought you a new hat. After all, I've never done anything for you before." When the woman took off the hat a little later, she noticed that her head was full of lice.
180126: A woman coming back from Koninksem found a witch at her home. The woman had asked the witch to bring her a new hat from Tongeren. Before the woman had even had a chance to take off her coat, the witch put the new hat on her head, saying: "I've brought you a new hat. After all, I've never done anything for you before." When the woman took off the hat a little later, she noticed that her head was full of lice.
180132: One winter evening when I had put the children to bed, I heard a werewolf at the window. Werewolves are people who have made a pact with the devil after standing at a crossroads with a black hen. When the devil accepts the hen, the man receives a skin and money. In return he must regularly roam about as a werewolf for some time. The morning after that winter evening, the werewolf's paw prints were in the snow. When my husband was still alive, he once fought for two hours against a werewolf he had met on his way back from Bettenhoven. Luckily my husband had a small axe with him, with which he wounded the werewolf while saying the words: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph!" At that moment the werewolf's skin fell to the ground: there stood my husband's best friend. My husband said to him: "I wish you a hundred hours away from here!" The werewolf then had to leave for the place he had been banished to. When my husband came home, he was still so bewildered that at first he did not recognise me.
180146: Two sick boys agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what the hereafter was like. When one of the boys had died, the other went to his dead friend's house. There was a light on in the house, but as soon as the friend entered, the light went out. The young man was so frightened that he no longer dared to go and look.
180154: A little boy who went to catechism class could conjure the whole church full of mice by rummaging in a little heap of earth. After the priest had read the Gospel of Saint John, the boy could no longer make mice.
180170: A man who was constantly pestered by a cat fetched his gun and shot the animal from a distance. When the man went to look, an old woman was lying on the ground. That woman was surely a witch.
180182: A wizard made a woman stand still. However much the woman cursed, she could only go on when the wizard wanted.
180189: A woman who was coming back alone from Maaseik in the evening was jumped by the werewolf. The woman died of fright.
180203: A woman went to the priest for advice because her dead husband kept coming to haunt her. The priest advised her to ask the ghost what it wanted. "I had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, but I was unable to keep that promise. Will you do it for me?" the ghost asked. After the woman had gone to Scherpenheuvel together with the ghost, the dead husband was no longer seen.
180208: A beggar woman often came by Willem P.'s house and caused the man a lot of misfortune. One day Willem kicked at a cat that had sneaked into the house. The next day the beggar woman was wearing a bandage around her head.
180209: On a highway in Alken stood a villa called the Geuzentempel (Beggars' Temple). Its windowpanes were regularly smashed to pieces, because ghosts came in through the windows. Hundreds of mice often ran along the highway. It is said that the heretic Voltaire once spent a night in the Geuzentempel.
180217: A man coming back from Koersel was followed by a little cat near a witch's house. When the man had drawn a cross on the road with a stick, the little cat could go no further.
180219: In the old days people were very afraid when they had seen a black cat, because they believed they would then have bad luck.
180220: A woman who refused to go to the witch Zwarte Fles (Black Bottle) was punished with two red-haired children.
180232: A man went with three others to fetch pines in the woods. When the man put his saw to one of the pines, however, the tree began to sway dangerously back and forth. The four men were so startled that they made off as fast as they could.
180239: In Neerglabbeek there lived a girl who could make mice without tails. Her mother had not yet taught her how to make mice with tails.
180258: Van E. was unhappy with his calf. When a man passed by, he said: "I could kill this calf. It's lame and it will never come to anything," to which the man said: "Then give it to me!" The man was given the calf, which had only just been born. The man fattened the calf, but it stayed lame. One day a tailor from Truielingen called on the man. The tailor said to the man: "This calf isn't sick, it's bewitched! Shall I tell you who bewitched the animal?", to which the man replied: "No, don't, because I might do something terrible! I'll sell the calf." As soon as the calf was sold, the dealer took it away. When the animal crossed the village boundary, it was suddenly cured.
180259: Witches often appeared in the shape of a cat. When you struck at a witch cat, more and more cats appeared.
180262: The animals of farmer Jef B. all fell ill and died. The parish priest had already come to read prayers over the stable, but that had not helped. One day Jef saw a black cat leaping onto the animals. When Jef no longer let the black cat into the stable, not a single animal fell ill again.
180277: A farmhand who worked for three women always had to bring wood inside in the evening. In the morning the wood had been burned. One evening the farmhand decided to spy on the three women through a hole in the attic. At midnight the women made a fire with the wood. One of the women had a little doll in the shape of a pig; another woman had a little doll representing a cow. As the women stuck pins into these dolls, the animals began to scream loudly. After the farmhand had told the village what he had seen, he ran away.
180282: A farmer had a farmhand who always went out in the evening. One evening the farmer saw the farmhand climb onto a tree stump and turn into a werewolf. The next day the farmer sent the farmhand to Neerpelt with a cart of fruit. Meanwhile the man went to the tree stump, in which he found the farmhand's collar. When the collar was already in the fire, the farmhand was suddenly standing by the oven to save the band. But because the farmhand came too late for that, he was delivered. After the horses had been fetched from Neerpelt, the farmhand disappeared for good.
180284: People from Genenbos always heard a strange noise when they lay in bed at night. The door would then open quietly, but nobody was to be seen. It must have been a dead person coming back.
180285: In the Weerter Broek between Beek and Stamprooi a land surveyor had divided the land unjustly. In the night after Christmas several mayors came to the Broek to settle the matter. Some young men from a farm in Beek could not contain their curiosity and went out at night to watch the mayors divide the land. At about two in the morning the boys came back to the farm. One of the boys fainted and the others were too shaken to speak. They never revealed what they had seen that night.
180316:
A werewolf was a person who changed shape when he put on a special collar. The werewolf often jumped on someone's back and then made them carry him. The werewolf always chose his victims carefully; for example, he never jumped on a strong man. Some said that a werewolf drooled when he sat on someone's back.
If the werewolf's collar could be burned in an oven, the man was set free.
180355: Because Karel P. from Heppen's horse was bewitched, the farmer had to build his stable in another place. After that the horse behaved normally again.
180362: A woman who was cutting spurrey in the field suddenly saw some gooseberries among the spurrey. Because the woman did not trust the matter, she went home immediately.
180381: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend met a white lady in the 'Brulbos' between Vliermaal and Neerrepen. The lady walked arm in arm with the man as far as the brook, where she let go of him. As soon as the man had jumped over the brook, the lady vanished.
180386: A family was coming back from the fair in Scherpenheuvel. On the hill in Heusden they had to pass the house of a witch. The witch was standing outside and said: "Oh, what a lovely child you have!" Because the father did not trust it, he called to his wife: "Marie, come on, quickly!" A little further on a foal was rolling around in the meadow. That was the witch, restless because she had not been able to bewitch the child.
180387: During a hunt Neer saw a hare that kept running about with its ears straight up. Neer did not manage to shoot the hare. The man loaded his gun with nails and waited until the hare was in a tree. Neer shot the hare through the ears so that the animal was pinned to the tree.
180391: A woman could not go to her churching because she fell ill every time. So the woman sent for a father from Sint-Jansberg to say prayers over the house. The father advised the woman not to tell anyone in the neighbourhood when she planned to go to her churching. She certainly must not tell the midwife, for she was the witch who kept making the woman ill.
180396: A woman who had been bewitched during her pregnancy gave birth to a blind child.
180397: When Simon H. came back from his card night, he had to carry the werewolf.
180402: The child of a farmer from Kaulille had fallen ill after a witch had visited. The parish priest advised the farmer to light the hearth when the witch came again. The farmer said to the witch: "Woman, release the child in the cradle now, or else I'll throw you in the fire". Then the woman took a little wax doll out of the child's cradle. The next day the child was cured.
180411: One had to beware of black cats, because they could be witches. Anyone who walked alone in the dark was often jumped on by the werewolf. In the past witches were tied to the gallows or the pillory.
180417: A priest had to exorcise a house that a dead person came to haunt.
180419: A man saw a headless cow walking in a meadow. Frightened, the man ran home to tell his family what he had seen. When the others came to look, the cow had disappeared.
180420: Bosmei often went stealing in the woods. When the police were on her heels, she turned herself into a cat.
180427: After his death Jan S. from Gestel had to haunt. Every evening at nine o'clock the ghost walked from Gestel to Kwaadmechelen, calling: "Where must I leave my post? Where must I leave my post?" The people all answered: "Don't do that, lad!", but it did not help. One day a drunkard answered: "That doesn't matter, lad, put it back where you took it from". With that the ghost was released.
180433: At G.'s place a little bird always flew through the sheepfold. Whenever that happened, the sheep jumped up and then fell down dead. After everything had been told to the parish priest, the clergyman gave them a medal. The little bird was taken out of the fold and the medal was laid at the entrance of the fold. The priest had also said: "You will find out who did this to you. A woman will come by to borrow something. When you offer her a chair, she will not want to sit down." And so it happened.
180455: In Buvingen there once lived a witch who knew everything.
180474: A girl from Boorsem had a friend in Rekem who was said to be the daughter of a witch. One day the girl went to visit her friend unexpectedly. The girl knocked but heard nothing. When the girl opened the door, she saw a black cat that had hidden in a corner. Because the girl was afraid, she quickly went back home. Later that day her friend came to see her and asked: "Were you at our house this morning?" The girl answered: "Yes, but there's no need anymore. The problem I came about has already been solved." The girl did not dare tell her friend what she had really found out. She did go to confession with the friars. The priest told her: "Just leave those people alone, and nothing will happen to you." For it was always said that the eldest daughter of a witch was a witch herself.
180477: At the crossroads in Kesselt black cats always roamed around nine o'clock.
180501: The wife of Victor-Pol V. was attacked in the Hoogveld by a strange apparition that pushed her into the ditch. Afterwards the woman had a small chapel built by the Tierstraat.
180502: There used to be some large oaks along the Leenstraat. The thickest oak was hollow inside. Because a priest sat in that oak, the tree was called the Pastoorseik (Priest's Oak). When a man was coming back from Kortessem along a field track one night, he met a white priest with an altar boy. The man asked: "Who is ill, Father?", but there was no answer. The priest went with the altar boy towards the Eikenbos. It was the priest from the Pastoorseik.
180510: A farmer from Eigenbilzen had great trouble mowing the grain because it had been a wet year. One evening the farmer was visited by a gentleman, who said: "I will do the work for you, on condition that you sell me your soul." The farmer accepted the offer and signed the contract with his blood. Then the farmer had to mow one sheaf and say: "Now all of it like this." After that all the work was done. The alvermannetjes (little elves) had sent the devils to help the man.
180528: In Nolke's meadow there was a ridge you had to crawl through. A black cat always sat on that ridge. One day a man hit the cat. The animal leapt up furiously and said: "Do that again!" But the man got away as fast as he could, for he broke out in a cold sweat of fear.
180531: Some men going threshing saw a hare running along the way. Suddenly the animal was gone. A little further on they saw the hare again at the nine bonder (a measure of land) in Houtain.
180532: After a woman from Diepenbeek had baptised a will-o'-the-wisp, an old man suddenly stood before her. It was the soul of a man who had died unbaptised. Because the woman had not said "I baptise you alone", hundreds of will-o'-the-wisps appeared a little later. They were the souls of unbaptised children. Since so many will-o'-the-wisps had appeared, the parish priest of Diepenbeek had to come to drive the lights away.
180537: A father had placed some small iron crosses in a woman's hands. The woman took the crosses out of her hand with tongs, whereupon the crosses jumped back into her hand by themselves. That woman must have been a witch.
180543: A farmer who could no longer manage to fatten his pigs sent for the parish priest. The priest sat in the pigsty all day. When the clergyman came out in the evening, he had gone completely grey.
180550: Anyone who suspected a witch was nearby must never continue along a main road. A man who had seen lots of partridges on the road took a small path. After that the man was no longer followed by the animals.
180554: A brave man knocked a cat into the water at 't Vonderke near Peer. The next moment there were as many as a hundred cats, which attacked the man and scratched his face open.
180556: At night a large dog came to the horse cemetery. One day someone found money in the cemetery. That man went mad and hanged himself.
180561: In Sint-Dool in Dorne a church had sunk into a marsh. People had often planted pines there, but not a single tree would grow. At the spot where the church had stood, bells were heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night. Brave Jan had bet that he dared go to Sint-Dool at twelve o'clock on Christmas night. Jan came back deathly pale. He never wanted to tell anyone what he had experienced.
180566: A man from Bolderberg whose child cried all the time went to the friars for advice. A clergyman gave him something to put under the thresholds of the front and back doors. The next day a woman came by who was used to coming to look at the child every day. This time, however, the woman could not come in. The woman was a witch. Pins and needles had been stuck in the child's pillow.
180579: A miller still had one sack of grain to grind when suddenly a witch passed by and said: "You'll have no luck with that!" When the miller lifted the sack, it turned out to be torn all over.
180597: Harieke H. lived in the Gerdingerstraat near 't Stift in Bree. One day, as Harieke was walking from Gerdingen to Bree, a werewolf suddenly jumped on his back on the way. At the house of doctor V., Harieke tried to get rid of the werewolf by rubbing the animal against the gate. But the werewolf held on tight. When Harieke was almost home, his wife came to meet him. Harieke said: "Quickly fetch some light so we can see what is sitting on my back!" But the werewolf was already gone when Harieke got home. Harieke then searched for the werewolf for hours to teach the animal a lesson.
180598: Behind the iron barrier in Klein Hilst stood a row of thick chestnut trees. Dré V. did not dare pass the barrier because a big dog sat on it. When Dré went to the wooden barrier by Tieu's house, the dog was suddenly sitting there to stop him. It was a ghost dog.
180604: Pierre R. from Kotem was a big strong man who always had to carry the werewolf. When Pierre was jumped by the werewolf, he broke out in a cold sweat. The man was always very relieved when he got home.
180607: A tailor from Hoelbeek walking home in the evening met a heifer on the way. The man tied the heifer to a rope and took the animal with him. But when he got home, the heifer had grown so big that it could no longer fit into the stable. The animal was a witch.
180610: A man had dressed up as a ghost to frighten two women. When the women ran off screaming, the man said: "Don't be afraid. It's me!" But the women saw two apparitions. The second apparition was the devil. The man crawled into his bed at home and never got out of it again.
180633: A brewer whose farmhands had all died decided to sell the brewery. At that moment, however, a new farmhand arrived who was determined to work in the brewery. When the new farmhand was working at night, a small kitten came along. The farmhand broke the kitten's forelegs with a dung fork. The next day the brewer's wife had two broken arms.
180646: A woman always woke at midnight when the ghost of her dead uncle from Wouteringen stood beside her bed. Because she did not know what to do, she went to ask the priest for advice. The next time her uncle appeared, the woman said, on the priest's advice: "All good spirits serve the Lord," to which the ghost answered: "So do I." Then the woman asked her dead uncle: "What do you want from me?" The ghost said: "A pilgrimage to Zammelen." After the woman had venerated Saint Amandus in Zammelen, the ghost was no longer seen.
180658: Two girls coming back from the village in the evening had to pass the house of a witch. Exactly at that spot a black cat appeared, which followed the two girls the whole way. One of the girls tried to kick the animal, but did not succeed. Strangely enough, the cat had a tail three times as thick as that of a normal cat.
180661: A man who went to work in Wallonia was always followed by a black dog. If the man had no stick with him, the dog jumped onto his neck.
180673: When a witch had been near a child, the child often fell ill. The child then had to be prayed over by the parish priest. Anyone who wanted to protect themselves against witches had to use holy water.
180678: The old houses on the Vlooienberg were haunted at night.
180680: One evening Marten was coming back from Bree on foot when a werewolf suddenly jumped on his back. The priest who lived near Potleen had already wanted to give Marten something to protect himself against werewolves. But Marten thought it unnecessary and was convinced he could defend himself. When Marten was jumped by the werewolf that evening, he carried the beast as far as Lom's house. There Marten said to the animal: "Now that's far enough." Marten squeezed the werewolf's body until the animal bled and threatened: "If I meet you one more time, I'll squeeze you to death." Marten made the werewolf promise on its knees that it would never bother anyone again.
180694: A farmer from Genendijk who was going to Tessenderlo in the evening met a cat and said: "Well, pussycat, you're out so late", to which the cat replied: "Yes, if you hadn't spoken to me so kindly, I would have broken your neck".
180699: Anyone ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night suffered terrible pains and usually died soon after. But if one took a piece of steel to bed, one was never troubled by the maar.
180706: A parish priest used to haunt the castle and the woods. Sometimes women walked past that place with a basket full of food. In the evening a big black dog would then be lying on the food.
180719: When Bernard V.D. was driving his cart through the sand, he said: "I will turn every grain of sand that I push into the wheel tracks with my foot into mice." And that happened. Bernard owned a little magic book.
180721: Every time Thieu V. had gone to visit his girlfriend, he was harassed by black cats on the way home. After a while Thieu suspected the girl of being a witch. When Thieu stopped visiting his girlfriend, he was no longer bothered by black cats.
180727: Some people going on a pilgrimage for a sick child were followed by a black cat. When the child died, the cat suddenly vanished.
180728: In the old days there were women who could make themselves invisible at night and then go outside. They would put a broom in the bed so that their husbands would not notice they were gone. One day a clog maker was visited by such witches who had made themselves invisible. He heard them say: "Wilveren, wilveren", to which another said: "Neeveren, neeveren, it's Pie-Ber the carpenter." The next Sunday Pie-Ber sat in church behind some women whom he heard praying like this: "Oats and hay, oats and hay, oats and hay", to which the others answered: "Chaff and straw, chaff and straw, chaff and straw". Because Pie-Ber liked a joke, he joined in: "Horse dung, horse dung, horse dung." At that one of the witches turned her head and asked: "Do you belong to our society too?" Pie-Ber started laughing and went to sit elsewhere.
180732: In the Brouwersstraat in Tongeren a white rabbit ran to the friars' garden. Someone had caught the rabbit. When that person came home, the rabbit turned out to have changed into a stone.
180756: A farmer whose animals had all fallen ill sought advice from the fathers of Weert. The fathers advised the farmer to check whether there were white mice in the stable. The farmer found as many as twenty white mice among his animals. After he had killed all the mice, his animals stayed healthy.
180773: Turkish slaves prayed to Our Lady. At a certain moment the slaves' shackles fell to the ground. The next morning the shackles lay in front of the door of the church of Tongeren. The shackles were hung up behind the altar.
180781: Koob E. from Kaulille had bought a healthy piglet at the market in Hasselt. As he was wheeling it home in his wheelbarrow along the Donderslag (1), he met the witch Trien in the Goolderbossen, who stroked the piglet's back. Before Koob got home, he found that the pig was dead.
180791: In the old days people saw burning wagons with six or seven horses flying through the air. Such wagons were called 'battle wagons'.
180799: Two women went out stealing in the evening in the shape of cats. A man had caught one of the cats. A while later another man caught the other cat, which called: "Nel, where are you?" Then a voice rang out: "In that man's sack".
180805: On the Geiteling lived a farmer who had seven horses. At night a witch came to take the horses, so that in the morning the animals stood in the stable drenched in sweat. One day the farmer bashed in a cat's head. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had to be taken to hospital. The horses died.
180806: One evening a man was followed by Jane, the black woman who wandered about the village. When the man ran away, the woman went off into the meadows.
180812: The young lady of the castle was often plagued at night by the maar (nightmare spirit), which gave her a feeling of tightness.
180817: At the entrance of the castle lane stood a barrier on which two mermaids sat. Because it was said in the old days that the mermaids had once come down from the barrier, people did not dare go near the castle lane.
180836: A man coming home one evening was followed for fifty metres by a goat.
180841: If one drew a little cross on a witch's footprint, the witch had to look round. That is how some boys found out that Zwarte Fles was a witch. Zwarte Fles spoke French and many other languages because she was a witch and because she had worked for a baron. Whenever the witch had to appear in court, she always won the case because the lawyer she had worked for came to defend her.
180850: A woman was making butter when suddenly a neighbour came in. At that moment the woman could no longer make butter.
180856: A certain Gerrits from the Melbekerstraat in Herk was walking to his work in Diepenbeek at night. Suddenly the man saw a cat with large green eyes sitting on a barrier. When the man tried to hit the cat, the animal suddenly grew bigger and bigger. The man no longer dared to strike and quickly went home.
180858: Chains were dug up on the Galgenheuvel which used to be used for hanging criminals. A dog also often roamed near the Galgenheuvel: that was the devil, who wanted to keep people away from the hill.
180862: One day Pieter L. went poaching in Sussen's meadow. When six hares came running along, Pieter shot them all. A little later a seventh hare came and asked: "Have my brothers come by here yet?" Pieter was so startled that he looked round at the hares he had shot: they were all jumping about, and they ran off hastily with the seventh hare.
180863: A farmhand returning in the evening from a visit to his girlfriend was, to his great fright, followed by a pig without a tail.
180870: At St. Ool between Niel and Thorn a bell had sunk in the time of the Norsemen. That bell always rang at Christmas.
180882: The mother of Harieke and Net was a witch. The woman always stood by the toll gate calling: "Children, come here!" Because the children were afraid of her, the witch grew angry. Every child the witch touched fell victim to the evil hand.
180883: A man was at a blacksmith's in Gelinden late in the evening. When the man left for home, the smith said: "Don't go past the Paardskerkhof in Engelmanshoven, because you know there's a foal roaming there that isn't right." The man answered: "I'm afraid of nothing and I dare go that way." But when the man walked across the Paardskerkhof, a werewolf suddenly jumped on his back. Its legs hung over his chest and looked like those of a foal. The man had to carry the werewolf until he got home. Then the man went to bed, where he died of fright.
180888: A mother had bought apples from a woman peddling door to door. The mother gave one apple to her child and threw the rest to the pigs. The next day the child was ill and all the pigs lay dead in the sty. The woman had much misfortune afterwards and had to go on a pilgrimage for her child.
180897: In the old days, when the witches held gatherings, they said: "Over hedge and over hawthorn to Kuringen into a wine cellar". Then they flew through the air on their brooms, making a rushing sound. One day a young witch made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and through hawthorn...". Because of that the witch literally had to fly 'through' the hedges.
180906: At a woman's house a black cat sat in the barn every evening at about the same time.
180924: A boy coming back from the fair saw two cats sitting on a turnpike barrier. When the boy made the sign of the cross with the words "Ave Maria!", the witch cats vanished.
180934: In Sluizen lived a witch who often conjured fire or water onto the road, so that people had to take a detour.
180940: Behind the Cavalerie in Leopoldsburg was a large wood where many will-o'-the-wisps floated about. It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children, who had to wander about.
180942: A man coming back from the mill with his wheelbarrow was startled when he heard the call of an owl. With every three steps the man took, the loud screech of the animal rang out. The faster the man walked, the more often the owl called.
180956: A man coming back alone in the dark from a card evening saw on the way an apparition with a chalk-white face. The ghost was also wearing a long shroud. Terrified, the man went inside. A few days later the man met the ghost again. A long time afterwards the ghost appeared once more at the end of the night by the dung heap. As soon as the man came closer, the ghost vanished. At each appearance the ghost was a little further away from the man. Afterwards the man realised he should have asked what the ghost wanted, for it was probably a dead person who had returned.
180988: When Vien V.W. was coming back from the fair in Schulen, she discovered that her boyfriend was a werewolf. In a café by the Vellekersmolen Vien saw that her boyfriend had the threads of a handkerchief between his teeth.
181001: A man said to his wife: "Marie, I have seen a black crow. Within three days one of us will be dead." A while later the man died.
181006: A coal merchant who did not have enough money to buy a piece of land made a pact with the devil. In exchange for the money the man had to do the devil's will for three years. The first year the man had to bring the devil everything that had grown on his field. The man mowed all the wheat and decided to give the devil the stubble left standing in the field. The second year, too, the devil wanted everything the man had harvested from his field. That year the man had planted potatoes. He kept the potatoes for himself and gave the devil the tops. (1) The devil, who had already been tricked twice by the man, asked for a head of livestock in the third year. It had to be an animal the devil did not know, however. When the man came home, he smeared his wife with syrup and covered her with feathers. Then he put the dog's collar and chain on his wife and went with her to the devil. As soon as the woman came crawling up on hands and knees, the devil said to the man: "You have won!" Then the man got his money.
181024: A werewolf whose skin was thrown into the oven was delivered.
181027: In the chapel of Daaleinde a priest came to say mass every evening at eight o'clock. A new farmhand from the Kempen came to work at B.'s farm and immediately understood what the whole scene meant. The farmhand said: "It is a priest who said a mass without an altar server. I was an altar boy myself; tomorrow I will serve the priest." The neighbours were very surprised that the farmhand dared to go near the ghost. As he had said, the next day the farmhand served the priest at mass. After the service the priest said: "I have said mass here for a hundred and eleven years, and there was never anyone willing to serve me. Now you have finally done it, and I thank you for it." From then on the priest was never seen again, for the farmhand had released his soul.
181032: A woman whose baby was four or five months old was visited by a witch. The witch gave a bag of sour sweets to the child lying in the cradle. Because the child had already put a sweet in its mouth, it became seriously ill. After a while the baby fortunately recovered. When the witch came back a second time, she gave the baby two sugar waffles. The next day the child was deathly ill again. The woman then went with her baby to the superior of the friars of Rekem. After the woman told the friar what had happened, the clergyman prayed over the child and said: "It is a godly disgrace! I will show you who is responsible for this evil." The friar showed the woman a mirror in which the witch could be seen giving the waffle to the child.
181047: People who could not sleep at night often said that the maar (nightmare spirit) was sitting on them. To protect oneself against the evil hand, one had to pray a lot or put holy water beside oneself. With a palm twig one had to bless the corners of the room with holy water. People ridden by the maar sweated heavily. Later it was believed that it simply had something to do with stomach ache.
181054: During Mass a bewitched former student had stolen 700 BEF from the priest's cupboard. Some schoolgirls had seen the thief flee into the fields. After a while the boy was found asleep against a tree stump. The thief was chained up in the corner where the wood was stacked. Some time later nine men dragged the boy to the healer of Genk. The boy was so much in the power of evil that it took the men nine days to bring him to Genk. The healer told the boy to put on a clean shirt every day. After a friar had heard the boy's confession, he was freed from the witchcraft.
181059: Jan P. had a child that was bewitched. The parents had tried all sorts of things, but nothing seemed to help. At their wits' end, they went to the parish priest of Offelken. Because the child was too weak to come along, the parents went alone. The priest said to them: "You would have done better not to come, for the matter is already lost: your child is lying on copper pins, around which a wreath of horsehair has been laid. When the wreath is finished, it will be too late." The desperate mother replied: "But that's impossible! The child's mattress is shaken out every day!", to which the priest said: "When you shake out the mattress the day after tomorrow, a woman will come asking for buttermilk. You must not give that woman anything for free, even if you only ask one centime for it. Or you can put salt in the buttermilk; that is also good against witches." When the parents got home, they cut open the child's mattress and found hundreds of copper pins inside, and the most beautiful wreath of horsehair they had ever seen. When the witch came asking for buttermilk two days later, they chased her away. But by then the child was already doomed to die.
181061: A family had three young sons. A woman regularly came to the family to buy butter and cheese. When she came, she would take the children on her lap. After a while one of the sons became paralysed. He could not move his little body and cried all day. The doctors were at their wits' end. One day there was a Witheer (a Norbertine canon) in the village, and this friar invited the mother and the sick child to come to the church after the Eucharist. The mother had to lay her son flat on her lap, after which the friar placed a medal on the child's forehead. For half an hour the friar recited prayers for the child. After only five minutes, sweat was dripping from the friar's face. Afterwards the friar said to the boy: "You will soon be healed," and he advised the mother to put the medal under the threshold so that the witch would stay out of the house from then on. When the witch came to the door, the mother must not say "Come in," for then she would regain her power. If someone in the street said: "What a beautiful child!", the mother had to answer: "It is a child God has created!" After three weeks the boy was completely healed. The witch never came by again.
181064: In the past people in Ophoven often saw ghosts wandering about with a boundary post. These were the souls of people who had moved a boundary post during their lives. The parish priest advised people to tell those ghosts that they had to put the boundary post back where they had taken it from.
181065: A man who was fighting a black cat was frightened almost to death when suddenly a woman with a knife in her hands stood before him.
181075: The card-playing knight of Heppeneert had bad friends and moreover got involved with the devil. To get money, the knight signed a contract with the devil in his blood. As soon as his time was up, the knight rode on horseback to the devil's bridge, where the devil sat grinning, waiting for him. Suddenly the devil ran away. The knight could not get off his horse because Saint Gertrude sat behind him. The knight was saved and mended his ways.
181092: A poacher who had shot at a rabbit was frightened when he heard the other rabbits start to whistle.
181113:
The werewolf always sat by the road waiting for someone to pass on whose back he could jump. If the werewolf could be made to bleed, he became human again.
One day there was a brave man who wanted to teach the werewolf a lesson. After drinking himself some courage, the man set out with a knife in his hand. When the werewolf jumped on the man, the beast was wounded by the knife and immediately turned into a human. The wounded werewolf said to the man: "You won't see me here again, but if you betray me, I'll kill you."
181119: A man going along the 'Goelesteeg' to his girlfriend came across a black cat. After the man had kicked the cat, the animal came back again. When he wanted to kick the cat a second time, it began to miaow menacingly. At that the man went on, scared to death.
181137: A man coming back from the shoemaker in Wijchmaal saw a strange figure on the Petersdijk. Because the man was afraid, he took another road. When the figure could be seen there too, the man said: "Good day." The next moment the figure sank into the ground. It looked like a nun.
181159: A witch came into a café where a baby lay in a cradle. After the witch had taken the baby out of the cradle, the child cried incessantly. The child's mother went to the parish priest, who advised her to send for the chaplain. The chaplain came to pray over the child. The baby, however, turned blue, and then took on all the colours of the rainbow. In the end the child did recover.
181167: If a black cat was sitting in the corn, one had to make a sign of the cross in the sand with one's foot. If the cat looked round, it was a witch. A stick with a darning needle was a good remedy against witches.
181171: A brother and sister coming back from the market in Diest met a big dog on the way. The woman did not see the dog, but the man did, because he had been born on a Sunday.
181177: A girl saw the ghost of her dead father appear every time she had to herd the cows. Her father had, after all, been killed by one of the cows.
181198: In Kozen there lived a witch who could bewitch animals by means of an evil prayer.
181201: When Mrs C. was walking to church in the morning, she saw a pig sitting on an iron gate. As soon as the woman made to turn back, the pig said: "Come on ahead, I won't do you any harm!" The woman went home anyway.
181207: A woman always came to a shop in Niel to buy plattekaas (fresh soft cheese). However, she always came at a moment when the plattekaas had run out. When the woman left the shop, the shopkeeper was covered in lice. One evening the shopkeeper sent for the priest, who said: "Undress and go wash yourself. You must not speak to that woman any more." After that the lice were gone.
181213: On a farm worked a farmhand who owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. While the farmhand was in the field, his band was thrown into the fire. At that moment the farmhand immediately came back to pull his band out of the oven.
181215: Nol often went to work with his horses on the Zuur meadow in the evening. When a few women came past clearing their throats, the horses took a great fright. Those women were witches.
181233: In a haunted farm, the dishes fell to the floor for no explicable reason. In the stable the cows were often heard lowing too. The priest had read prayers over the farm many times, but it did not help. When the farmer was at his wits' end, he went to the Trappist friars in Achel. The friars gave the farmer something consecrated that he had to place under the threshold of the house. From then on no more strange things happened.
181239: A man went to visit a witch without first sprinkling himself with holy water. Because cats were crawling all over him, he spoke the name of God.
181242: Heilig Janneke (Holy Janneke) was so devout that he crawled to church on his knees. Janneke had a grocery shop where people could also have their guns cleaned. One day French soldiers burst into the little shop because they had heard guns could be found there. The soldiers looked everywhere, but found nothing but flowers. Heilig Janneke had turned all the guns into roses.
181246: A man from Lafelt was plagued by rats. One of the Irish soldiers stationed there built a fire and made all the rats run screaming to the fire. The last rat was a very fat one, which screamed even louder than the others. In this way the farmer was freed from the plague of rats.
181251: A family from Widooie had bought a farm in Vechmaal. Every time they went to fetch straw and passed the witch's house on the way back, the cart fell over, so that the straw ended up in the brook. If they took another road, nothing happened.
181274: When people suffered from a plague of rats caused by a witch, they had to pray the Gospel of Saint John in three corners of the farm.
181279: A house in Lauw was haunted. A ghost with a bell followed people and stopped when they stood still.
181285: Some men from Overrepen were out in Neerrepen when they suddenly saw a black cat. When one of the men struck at the animal, many cats suddenly appeared. Since the Angelus was introduced, such evil was no longer met with so often.
181304: Will-o'-the-wisps were little souls of unbaptised children. The lights led people to the water to make them drown.
181309: A mother sent for a friar for her baby, which had been struck by the evil hand. The friar said: "The woman who bewitched your child will come by within nine days to ask you for something." When the farmer heard this, he shouted angrily: "If that witch comes here, I'll beat her to death!" A few days later a woman came by, to whom the farmer's wife said: "Just go back where you came from!"
181330: When Charel V.O. was coming back from the Berg, he saw four candles by M.'s field that he could not touch. A little later the candles had disappeared.
181337: Many witches used to live in Beek. The young girls of the V. family were witches too. In the evening some young men kept them company until bedtime. Then they waited until everyone went to sleep. Next they went to tap on the girls' bedroom window. But when no answer came, the boys went to wait under a pear tree a little further away. Although the boys were sure that the girls' windows were closed, two cats suddenly jumped in through the windows. A few moments later the girls came to open the door, saying: "Come in now; now we're here!"
181339: The sister of Jean, who lived on the Luikersteenweg, had to come back to haunt after her death. Jean had promised his unmarried sister that he would take care of her child. After the woman's death, however, the child was no longer with Jean. Because his sister came to haunt, Jean took the child back into his home.
181345: A farmer simply could not find a farmhand to hire. When the farmer was at his wits' end, he cried out: "I must have a farmhand, even if I have to fetch him from hell!" A few days later the farmer was visited by a certain Fleris, who was looking for work as a farmhand. From the moment the farmer hired Fleris, strange things happened. When people wanted to go to church on Sunday, Fleris always managed to keep them so long that they were late. When a horse cart got stuck, Fleris pulled it free effortlessly. One night a fire broke out in the village. When the villagers woke in the morning, it was as if there had never been a fire. Gradually everyone began to distrust Fleris. The priest advised the farmer to serve the farmhand porridge with garlic. Although Fleris liked porridge, that time he turned up his nose and said: "Porridge and garlic - Fleris leaves and luck goes too!" Fleris then left and was never seen again. After Fleris left, however, the farmer had so much misfortune that he eventually had to sell his farm.
181359: A drossaard (bailiff) who had had many people hanged had to haunt the Hobos after his death. The ghost appeared as a dog with a glowing chain around its neck and sat down at his desk. In the end the drossaard was banished "for ninety-nine years and more" under a bridge near Lommel.
181368: The maar (nightmare spirit) was an invisible force that squeezed someone's throat shut for about five minutes to smother that person.
181371: At the Uilenkoetsbrug in Alken stood an oak barn that was said to have been built by the devil. A farmer who had no money to build a barn was at his wits' end because the harvest had to be brought in. One day the farmer met a gallant gentleman, who made him the following offer: "If I get your soul, you will get a barn from me." At first the farmer did not know what to do, but in the end he followed his wife's advice: "Sell your soul for six years or so. If you do not die within that time, the devil will never own your soul." When one morning the barn suddenly stood there, the farmer and his wife grew worried after all. The farmer then gave a lot of money to the church and visited many friars. Because of that, the farmer did not die before the six years were up.
181372: At a turnstile in a meadow in Kortessem, people heard the voice of a ghost.
181381: For a hundred years a woman dressed in white had haunted an oak tree in Heusden. The woman had once done something wrong at that spot. Only the man who lived in the nearby house had the power to make the woman disappear. When the woman said: "I by night...", the man had to answer: "I by day..." After that something more had to be said, but the man would not tell anyone what. None of the neighbours dared to draw a little cross on the tree with chalk at night.
181390: If one walked in a witch's footprints, the witch would turn round and ask: "What are you up to?"
181393: Whenever the miller went to sharpen his millstone, he was followed by a cat. Because the miller feared the cat might well be the devil, he asked 'red Vanderbeek', a friend of his, to come along with him. When the cat came walking up that evening, it said: "Hey, red, aren't you afraid of me?", to which V. replied: "Not even of the devil!" Vanderbeek took a piece of iron and struck at the cat with it. The next day Antrien had bruises on her head.
181395: A man working in the field was suddenly covered in lice and could not move. A witch had passed by and said: "Good, Trees".
181416: A man who could turn himself into a horse at night carried his horseshoes in his pocket during the day.
181417: In a house in Rosmeer, a strange rustling was always heard at night, as if there were rats. One day, when the woman went to gather kindling, she thought she had seen a monster. The man, who believed his wife was mistaken, saw a skeleton standing at the window one Saturday evening. The next morning the man saw the skeleton's footprints in the snow. In the end the man sent for pastor K. to bless the house.
181426: In a house in Neerrepen a cat always crept in through a small hole. One day the woman poured hot fat over the animal. The next day the neighbour woman's face was badly burned.
181450: In Alt-Hoesselt an unbaptised man had died. After his death the man came to haunt at midnight in the house of his two daughters, where he turned everything upside down. The girls had already sought advice from several friars. In the end there was one friar who was willing to come and bless the house, and so drove out the devil for good.
181476: Two travellers saw a light burning in a farmhouse in the distance. Tired and hungry, the men made for it. Although a monster of a dog lay three metres from the gate, the travellers fearlessly entered the farm. The men made a fire and baked cakes with the flour they had found in a sack. When the first cake was baked, however, something strange happened: a leg fell out of the chimney. The eldest traveller said: "Drop whatever you like, but stay out of my pan." A little later the men had already baked five cakes. Meanwhile another leg, a torso, two arms and a skull had fallen out of the chimney. Suddenly a ghost stood before the men and asked them to go to the cellar. The travellers let the ghost go first. Once in the cellar, they saw a large heavy stone. "Lift that stone!" the ghost ordered. But the men let the ghost lift the stone itself. Under the stone a heap of gold coins lay hidden. Then the ghost said: "Half of the money is for you. With the other half you must have masses said." The men went to the friars with half of the gold coins, and with the other half they were able to lead a carefree life.
181486: A coach with two glowing horses always drove past D.'s barn. D., whose animals all died, noticed that it often looked as if his barn was on fire. When D. had torn down the barn, the coach no longer appeared.
181490:
In Kwaadmechelen there worked a maid who owned a magic book. With that book the maid could fill the house with mice. One day her mistress threatened: "If you don't make sure you get rid of that book, you can't go on living here." Because the village priest did not have enough power, the maid went to the friars of Borgloon, who freed her from the book.
Later the village priests gained more power, so that all the witches eventually disappeared.
181498: A woman who had a hundred or a hundred and fifty rabbits was suspected of being a witch. When the woman went to fetch grass in the field in rainy weather, the grass remarkably stayed dry.
181507: In the broek (marshy lowland) of Schulen will-o'-the-wisps appeared at night. One must never whistle at those spirits. If one did, the next day there would be a red hand burnt into the door.
181529: Zjanke V.D.'s neighbour said admiringly: "Zjanke, what beautiful hair you have!" After she had run her hand over Zjanke's hair, the poor man was covered in lice.
181548: Every evening a man went to the cellar to talk there with his dead son. One day the wife gave her husband a medal of Saint Benedict. That evening the son did not speak. After the man had thrown the medal away, he could talk with his son again.
181552: At 't Hobbes the cows were all found one morning tied by their tails to a beam. So people said: "Whoever is the first to step over the threshold here tomorrow, it was them!" The next morning a little old woman knocked and said: "I had to come and see what was going on here." The woman was beaten black and blue.
181555: A drunkard sitting in the café on a Sunday struck the table with his medlar-wood cudgel and shouted: "I'll fight today yet, even if I have to fight the devil!" When the man came outside, something jumped onto his back. The drunkard had to fight so hard that hardly anything was left of the medlar-wood cudgel.
181586: The prelate of Averbode owned zwart goed (church property seized and sold off). When he rode on horseback to the poor people and saw the farmers working in the field, he said: "Oh, that brings us in so much!" One day some men shot the prelate dead. Since then a headless horse has walked along the lane to Averbode.
181594: If someone unknowingly walked in a witch's footsteps, they could go no further. Only when the witch wished it could they then go on.
181597: At midnight one could see the devil arriving in his coach at a crossroads.
181600: In a house where many children had died, a will-o'-the-wisp flew around at night. After a priest had read prayers over the house, the light was not seen again.
181602: The mother of a certain Cosemans from Niel-bij-Sint-Truiden was visiting her aunt in Brussels. Because it was a warm summer evening, the two women decided to take a little walk. In a wood the pair witnessed a great party where witches were dancing. The mother was so amazed that she cried out: "Jesus, Mary, what is that?" In an instant everything had vanished. The mother was tied to a chair in the wood. When morning came, a little old man appeared and said: "It's your fault we had no fun. Now get away quickly and make sure we never see you here again!" When the mother found her aunt, the aunt said she had got lost and had spent the whole night looking for the way.
181620: In the past witches often crept into houses to spy on people in the shape of a cat or a hen. A woman who was knitting saw a hen come in. At that moment the yarn became so tangled that the woman could not knit any further.
181627:
A little woman from Horpmaal came to a maid and said: "What lovely combs you have in your hair! You must give me one for Bertha!" The woman stroked the maid's beautiful hair with her hand. That night the maid could not sleep. When she got up, she found that her hair was full of lice.
Whenever that woman from Horpmaal was nearby, people always drew a cross on the street. That way she could not pass.
181645: Some men were sitting talking when suddenly seven cats crawled in through the sink drain. The cats sat down jauntily by the fire and a little later disappeared the way they had come. Later the men heard someone say: "Luckily you did nothing to the cats, otherwise they would surely have broken you on the wheel!"
181647: A woman who went with her mother to her husband's house was always followed by a big black dog. One evening the woman said to the animal: "If you dare to come again tomorrow, you're dead!" The werewolf did not show itself again.
181648: In Lanaken there lived a certain Trien who was suspected of being a witch. Whenever Trien came to church, she always had a cooking pot, a pan or a coffee grinder with her, which she set down at the back by the holy water font. Then Trien usually sat on the chair of the wife of the brewer Martens. One day the brewer's wife had said to a man: "We aren't going to Mass, you may sit on my chair." When the man sat on that chair on Sunday morning, a woman said to him: "Just get up, you won't stay sitting there anyway. As soon as Trien comes, you'll have to stand up." The man said: "I won't get up, I'm allowed to sit here," to which the woman replied: "You will get up, you'll see!" A little later the woman said: "Oh God, she's standing behind you!" At that moment the man fainted and had to leave the church.
181656: In Sluizen a werewolf roamed about, chasing passers-by. Whoever could make a werewolf bleed could recognise him.
181658: The R. family had a shop on the Steenweg in Sint-Lambrechts-Herk. Whenever someone wanted to weigh something there at night, a ghost dog came in and put its paw on the scales. The people had been dishonest.
181676: A bewitched girl cried all night. In the child's pillow a three-cornered pelt was found. Fortunately the pelt was not yet completely finished.
181678: An unmarried woman with three children was suspected of being a witch. One day the witch had left her children with someone and said: "I'll come and fetch the children later." Because the witch did not come, the woman decided to take the children back to their mother herself. At the house where the witch's mother lived, the washing was laid out to bleach. "Just walk over the washing, it all has to be washed again anyway," said the witch's mother. But the woman played it safe and walked around the washing. On the way back the woman got lost.
181684: Jef L. had a black stallion that had fallen victim to the evil hand. The animal often tugged at its chain as if it were mad. In the end the stallion had to be slaughtered in Belgium.
181686: Because Cilis no longer wanted to be a werewolf, he went to the brown friars of Maastricht for advice. Cilis had to tie the little book he had received from the devil to a long stick and then, without looking back, go to all the villages where he had ever been as a werewolf. While he did so, Cilis was followed by a thousand devils who kicked him and shouted at him. When Cilis got back to Eigenbilzen, he saw a burning coach with four horses flying through the air. The devil sitting in that coach took the little book from the stick. Where the devil had touched the stick, the wood was completely burnt.
181704: A man met a cat at night. He held a stick in his hands, with which he wanted to hit the cat. Because it was a black cat, he quickly thought better of it and gently stroked the animal's back with the stick, asking: "Pussycat, where do you come from?" The cat replied: "If you hadn't flattered pussycat, you would have been sorry!"
181710: The ruins of the castle of Emmeren were haunted. It was said that a sow with copper teats roamed there. When the sow went about at night with her piglets, the neighbours heard a hellish noise. The sow went from Emmeren to Holland, Ham, the Meers and the Berg. In the morning people found large pits there where the sow had rooted up the earth. The pits held water with a thin layer of rust on top. That is why people believed the piglets had iron snouts.
181711: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." When the girl saw a dog, she did as her boyfriend had advised. A little later the boy appeared with the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
181714: A man passing a witch's house with horse and cart suddenly could go no further. After a long time the man was able to drive on.
181732: In Rikbos in Kleine-Spouwen a burning skeleton walked about, crying: "Raise children, raise dogs!"
181733: Two men travelling with horse and cart suddenly could go no further when they met Nie's mother. When the men turned the cart around, they could move again. There was nothing for it but to drive back to Sint-Truiden.
181748: A witch came to ask for straw from a farmhand who worked on a farm. When the farmhand refused on his master's advice, he was suddenly covered in lice.
181765: A woman whose newborn child was constantly hovering between life and death sent for the parish priest of Waltwilder. The clergyman began to read prayers and then said: "The woman who is to blame for this will come in shortly." When the woman was in the house, the priest said: "If you are innocent, you may stay seated here. Otherwise you must go outside." The witch left. In the little pillow the child slept on, a pin was found. An hour later the child died.
181778: In Kortebos (Tessenderlo) a man came haunting. During his life the man had hidden something that was never found.
181814: A boy who had not been baptised properly could make mice from a handful of sand. After the priest had baptised the boy again, he could no longer make mice.
181817: Witches' gatherings were often held at the Tolkesboom in Bree. The witches were each given a whip there. One day there was a new witch who wanted to fly along with the other witches. But the new witch did not yet know the magic formula well. Instead of "Over hedge and bush to the wine cellars of Aachen", she said: "Through hedge and bush to the wine cellars of Aachen". She will surely have regretted that later!
181825: A man who went for a walk one evening in the dark saw a hare sitting on a field path that did not run away. Because the man could not catch the hare, he went home to fetch his hunting gun. The moment the man pulled the trigger, the bullet exploded in the gun. When he got home, the man saw the hare sitting behind the Leuven stove.
181830: A boy had heard it said that his girlfriend was a witch. One evening the girl said to the boy: "Off you go now, it's time for bed". But the boy stayed standing outside the door and saw the girl go to the cellar and rub herself with witch's grease. After the girl had said: "Now on our way, from here to Leuven into the wine cellar over hawthorn and hedge", she flew away. The boy copied the girl, but made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said: "Through hawthorn and hedge". The boy arrived at his destination badly injured.
181837: A miller had taken on a new farmhand. One night the farmhand chopped off a paw of the miller's cat. The next morning the boy found that the miller's wife had lost an arm.
181839: A farmer who had much misfortune with the animals in his stable went to the friars. On the way the farmer was tormented in various ways by the witches responsible for the trouble. At one moment it began to rain, at another the farmer could not move forward and it seemed as if he were nailed to the ground. When the farmer finally arrived, the friars said that the witch would have won if he had turned back home.
181844: A man who had lost his way was followed by a dog. The man was bewitched.
181847: In the P. family an unmarried daughter had had a child. The baby had been strangled and then thrown into a well. Because the baby had not been baptised, after its death it became a will-o'-the-wisp that came to haunt. From then on strange things often happened in the house, so that nobody wanted to stay with the P. family any more. One day a beggar came knocking at P.'s door. The people asked whether he wanted lodging. The beggar eagerly accepted. He did notice that the people locked the doors with sturdy locks, but he thought the women might be afraid of him. On the stroke of midnight all the locked doors suddenly flew open and something stormed up the stairs with a hellish noise. The beggar hastily grabbed his clothes and ran out of the house as fast as he could.
181852: When a pigeon fancier's pigeons arrived late or did not come back at all, this was blamed on the black hand.
181881: One evening a man was walking over the Stokrooiebrug. When he looked down, he saw lots of cats sitting around a fire. A moment later someone came along who said: "Well, my little cats, warm your little bottoms!" The cats replied: "If this man hadn't spoken so nicely, we would have broken his little mouth!"
181883: Jesuits used to live at the Langeren mill. Because the fathers feared the mill would be seized by the French, a deed was drawn up transferring the mill to a certain P. After the French Revolution, however, P. refused to give the monastery mill back to the fathers. When Pijpers had died, it was said that he had to come back to haunt the mill. When the last of P.'s descendants dies, the mill will come back into the possession of the fathers.
181887: Around midnight Marte was coming back by moonlight with his wheelbarrow from Wijchmaal, where he had been visiting his aunt. On the way the man was followed by a cat, while he heard wonderfully beautiful music in the woods. When the man urged his dog to catch the cat, dozens of cats suddenly stood around him. The dog had vanished. The next day the animal lay badly injured in its kennel.
181893: Some people owned a chain with which they could turn themselves into a dog. In Bocholt worked a farmhand who went out every evening. One day the curious farmer saw the farmhand crawl into a tree stump and come out again a little later in the shape of a dog. The farmer sent his farmhand to Maastricht with some grain, so that he could meanwhile throw the collar into the oven. As soon as the band had burnt up, the farmhand was delivered. After that he went away for good.
181897: At a wedding in Gelieren the guests went from one café to another. Suddenly the bridegroom said to his bride: "I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. Go on and take this handkerchief. If you meet a dog on the way, throw the handkerchief at its mouth." A little later the girl did indeed meet a dog. She did as she had been advised and threw the handkerchief at the animal's mouth. When the newlyweds reached W.'s, the girl found in fright that her husband still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
181917: One day the daughter of the schoolmaster of Kerniel went to Hasselt with her mother, her sister and her brother. At noon they ate their sandwiches in a café. When they came out of the café, an old woman walked past who kept staring conspicuously at little Harie. A little later Harie's head was crawling with lice.
181954: When Maria visited Tin de M., the witch patted her on the shoulders and said: "You'll never see more than what you see now." When the woman got home, she had a painful spot on her eye. After the woman had gone to a healer for two years, she lost the sight in one eye. The witch Tin herself had an eye condition.
181956: In a meadow in Piringen, people heard ghosts calling and beating a drum.
181979: When the women went to fetch water, they were sometimes jumped by a werewolf sitting in the trees. The werewolf jumped on its victims' necks and broke wind. After the women had had to carry the werewolf a little way, they ran home screaming. When the men came to look at the well, there was nothing to be seen.
181983: A man struck with a stick at a cat that kept running against his legs. However often the man struck, he could not hit the animal. When the cat finally jumped into a tree stump, ten o'clock struck inside the tree stump.
181995: Some women always got together to make butter and chat. A woman who always had chaff in her butter went to the friars of Sint-Truiden. After the woman had put a relic under the threshold, one of her friends could no longer come in.
181999: People who consorted with the devil had to roam the woods at midnight as werewolves. A young man out walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "You go on. I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at the beast." When the girl met a dog a little further on, she did as her boyfriend had advised. An hour later the young man reappeared, saying: "I was gone a long time. I met someone and stood talking with him." Because the girl saw the threads of the handkerchief hanging between her boyfriend's teeth, she said indignantly: "Go away!"
182002: A baby had been ill for two months and no doctor could help it. When a woman cut open the child's pillow, she found a wreath of hair. The strands of hair were braided very tightly together. Fortunately the wreath was not yet fully closed, otherwise the baby would have died. Some time before, the mother had sent for a friar because the child had a fever.
