After the friar from Rekem had come to bless the house on Sunday, people had said: "Blimey, Marie, the witch who did this to you will surely come by." On Monday Joke T. was standing in the shop.
182019: In Lanaken there lived a witch who went peddling everywhere. The witch always had sweets in her pockets to lure children. One day a child died in a house where the witch had been. Under the mattress the child slept on, a wreath was found.
182034: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "Wait a moment, I have to relieve myself. You go on in the meantime. If you meet a dog, just throw your handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. When her boyfriend appeared a little later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
182043: In Ophoven there was a haunted house. One night some neighbours decided to keep watch by the house. Shortly after midnight all the roof tiles flew off the roof for no explicable reason.
182047: It was said that a castle had sunk into the ground by the chapel of Kuenen. A young man coming back one evening from visiting his girlfriend saw a white lady appear by the chapel. The lady made the young man promise to come back at twelve o'clock that same night. The lady would then have the key to a treasure chest in her mouth. When the young man came back at midnight, he saw a snake with a key in its mouth at that spot. The young man was terrified and ran back home. Three days later the young man died.
182064: A maid who worked on a farm in Klein-Gelmen was coming back one evening from visiting her parents in Groot-Gelmen. When the maid saw a werewolf sitting in a sunken lane, she struck the beast with a stick. When the body of the dead farmhand was found the next day, the maid nearly went mad with grief: the farmhand was her sweetheart.
182065: A girl herding the cows in Opgrimbie met a woman from Daalgrimbie, who said: "Hey, you're wearing a pretty skirt!" A few days later the girl got an ailment in her leg, which meant she had to walk on crutches for three months.
182066: Peter from Hoelbeek was standing with his cart by the dung heap when a woman went into the house. Peter could not leave with his cart until the woman had left the house.
182073: In the V. family's café the devil hid behind the stove in the shape of a dog. At night nobody dared to enter that wicked café any more.
182076: A woman from Beek was kneading dough in the evening when suddenly one of her friends came in. The friend said: "I have to go," whereupon the woman immediately took her broom and flew off with the dough still on her hands.
182078: The bell of the church of Laak had sunk into a marshy meadow and rang on Christmas night.
182081: A child was deathly ill after being struck by the evil hand.
182106: A coachman named Sus worked at the castle of Max D.M. When Sus came home at about eleven o'clock, he saw the dead cook Trien sitting on a chair. As soon as Sus came closer, the ghost vanished.
182123: Will-o'-the-wisps moved up and down above meadows. It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were souls of the dead who had not fulfilled their duty and had to return until they were released.
182130: A woman from Troot had heard that a big dog with a chain was roaming the village. She then gave people this advice: "Throw a red handkerchief at the dog's mouth, and then he will turn back into a human." That evening in the café they saw a man who still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
182133: When a witch came near children, the children began to cry.
182137: During the war Tut went to fetch a sack of flour at the mill of Muizen. On his way back he saw a light and followed it. The will-o'-the-wisp led him all around, through the beets and the mud. In the morning the man finally found his way back. He said: "I'll never go out at night again. Those will-o'-the-wisps want to lead people to the water to be baptised, and that's how they make you lose your way."
182139: People who had much misfortune in the house often thought they were bewitched and therefore had their house prayed over.
182155: A farmer had a maid who was cursing all the time. One day when the farmer was mowing the corn, the maid met a gallant gentleman who praised her for being able to curse so well. The gentleman went on and walked into the cornfield. Nothing ever grew again in the places where the gentleman had walked. That man must have been the devil.
182158: At midnight the white lady walked across the bridge in the Sterbos.
182164: A hunter always saw a hare running about near his home. He had often tried to hit the animal, but had never succeeded. The hunter's farmhand offered to load the gun himself and shoot the hare. The farmhand shot his own daughter's leg off.
182175: A boy had met a girl at the fair in Tessenderlo. A few days later the boy went to visit the girl in Eindhout. When the boy went back home that afternoon, he felt the wind brushing past his ears, although there was no wind at all. When the boy saw the girl again, she asked whether he had noticed anything strange the last time. The girl was a witch. She had taken over her mother's arts.
182181: In Weert there lived a woman who was said to be a witch. All the children who called the woman a witch fell ill for a few days.
182185: One must never accept an apple or a pear from a witch.
182197: When Fik's father had died at midnight, a white floating ghost with a long beard suddenly appeared.
182203: A poacher who had chased a hare in vain all night was told the next day by a little old woman: "Because you spent all night trying to catch that hare, you are now too late for Mass. And you didn't even catch the hare!"
182212: A man who had moved a boundary post had to haunt after his death with a boundary post in his hands. The ghost called the whole time: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" One day someone answered: "Drop it where you took it from". At that the ghost dropped the post and vanished.
182214: A boy had said that he would like to be bewitched for once. When the boy came back along the Vaart in the evening from visiting his girlfriend, he was harassed by a cat that would not go away. The mother of the boy's girlfriend was a witch.
182216: On a farm the celery just would not grow, while the neighbours had no problem at all. The farmer found it strange that Fien F., a woman who often visited him, took pleasure in the celery not growing. After the farmer sprinkled the ground with holy water, the celery did grow.
182220: Seven cats had come into a farmhouse through a gutter and went to warm their paws by the fire. One of the cats said: "Lieske said you should just keep your paws warm". Then the cats had disappeared.
182221: There was a witch who sat with a hen on her lap all the time. Every time the witch stroked the hen, the animal laid an egg.
182239: A farmer from Membruggen had unlawfully taken a farmhand's farm for himself. After his death the farmer had to come back to haunt. A ghost with chains around its neck came out of a pit in the ground. The dead farmer said: "I come from hell. I come to ask whether you will give back everything I stole to the farmhand." And so that was done.
182240: The werewolf often hid among the bushes. When a man came by, the werewolf made him carry it.
182251: A man had filled the holes in his land with soil from the churchyard. One stormy evening there were three knocks on the window. The same thing happened twice more. The third time a loud thunderclap rang out, making the house shake on its foundations. Terrified, the people ran upstairs.
182259: In Widooie a witch had crawled into the henhouse. When people came to look, the witch pelted them with chicken droppings.
182266: A werewolf had hidden his collar in a linden tree. In the evening the werewolf jumped on the necks of passers-by and made them carry him. The werewolf drooled and urinated on his victim.
182274: Lowieke from the mill saw a black cat walking over the churchyard wall one evening. A little further on he saw a dog with a chain sitting in the ditch. Because the dog followed him, Lowieke ran home as fast as he could.
182295: One evening Hans H. was walking home drunk along the Roman Kassei and the street that was later named 'Kerkstraat'. By the old ditch at the 'hophof' Hans saw something strange. A kind of sack, in which a living creature seemed to be, was rolling over the ground by the ditch. The man took an unfortunate fall when he struck at the strange apparition in panic. This gave the thing the chance to jump onto Hans's back. The man fled home as fast as he could. After that incident Hans lay in bed for three days. When he got up again, he had a hump on his back, which earned him the nickname 'Hans Kroef'.
182318: Farmer B. had a cowherd boy who could cover his master in rats and mice when he was angry. When the farmhand went to work for farmer T. in Zammelen, he did the same there.
182324: A poacher saw a hare and a dog playing together. The poacher did not dare to shoot, because he suspected the animals were witches.
182349: A man who had moved a boundary post to enlarge his field came back after his death to haunt with the words: "Where must I lay it? Where must I lay it?" One day a man answered: "Lay it where you took it from!" Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
182350: A man coming back from the pub heard a strange sound near 'de Kat'. A barrel was rolling through the leaves.
182380: In Opitter hardly anyone dared to go to the churchyard. One day there was a woman who boasted that she was afraid of nothing. Her friends made a bet with her. The woman had to go to the charnel house in the churchyard and bring back some bones. When the woman picked up some bones in the charnel house, a voice said: "No, leave them, for those are mine." At that the woman threw the bones back on the ground and said: "Here, you can have them back." She chose some other bones and took them to her friends.
182424: An engaged girl met a werewolf and threw some piece of clothing at the beast. When the girl met her boyfriend a while later, she found that he still had the threads of the cloth between his hands.
182462: The 'Binkel' between Hern-Saint-Hubert and Neerrepen was haunted. A young man who went walking there with his girlfriend said on the way: "Go on ahead. I have to relieve myself." The boy gave his girlfriend a handkerchief and said: "If you meet a big dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth. Then the dog won't be able to hurt you." Further on the girl did indeed meet a dog. She threw the red handkerchief at the animal. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl never wanted to see the boy again.
182464: The 'Binkel' between Hern-Saint-Hubert and Neerrepen was haunted. A young man who went walking there with his girlfriend said on the way: "Go on ahead. I have to relieve myself." The boy gave his girlfriend a handkerchief and said: "If you meet a big dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth. Then the dog won't be able to hurt you." Further on the girl did indeed meet a dog. She threw the red handkerchief at the animal. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl never wanted to see the boy again.
182468: The hill in Jesseren was haunted. One day some young men shot the tiles off the roofs there. After that it was no longer haunted.
182471: Zwarte Anna could cover people in lice.
182479: A woman who saw a white cat sitting in a bend of the Kuringer Baan kicked at the animal and went on. A little further on the same white cat was sitting on a stone by the road. This time the woman no longer dared to kick at the animal.
182484: Witches who had turned themselves into cats sometimes jumped onto someone's back. A cat that let itself be carried grew heavier and heavier. Still, one was not allowed to put the cat down, because that was dangerous.
182489: A woman had come to visit a farmer's wife and had said: "May I see your pig?" The next day the pig had turned completely blue.
182492: When Jan saw a cat come in through the water drain hole, he said: "What a pretty kitten!" The animal replied: "If Jan hadn't spoken so nicely, I would have broken his neck".
182500: A man who lived in a remote house saw one evening two eyes looking at him through the window. That was the black madam.
182504: A young man tapped on the window of his girlfriend's house. But nobody opened the door. A little later the man heard something buzzing. When he knocked again shortly afterwards, the door was opened.
182507: A poor man had fallen asleep in a church that was about to collapse. When the devils gathered in that church, one of them said: "There lies a sinner, marked with a cross." Because the man had made the sign of the cross, the devils had no power over him.
182509: Because the friars of the Templar order drank too much, their monastery sank into the ground. After that the monastery bells were heard ringing at Christmas in the meadow of Mechelen-Bovelingen. No one ever found a stick long enough to reach the bottom of the spring.
182510: During a drinking party in a café a man boasted that he was not afraid of the devil. A little later a gentleman with goat's feet, dressed all in black, stood beside the man and said: "Come with me then, if you're not afraid." The frightened landlord quickly made the sign of the cross. The next moment the devil had vanished.
182513: A smith had hired a farmhand and went to the woods to fetch him. But the smith saw no one and returned alone. Some time later the farmhand came to the smith alone and said: "Didn't you see those two black men? I was with them. And didn't you hear me whistle my tune?" The smith answered: "Yes, I did see two men dressed in black, but you were not with them." That the farmhand consorted with the devil later became clear from many strange events. Once, for example, the smith could not shoe a horse because the animal was so wild. The farmhand patted the horse on the back and shod it effortlessly with its hoof in his hand. The farmhand was even able to carry a horse.
182515: Fons had been to the fair in Opitter together with schoolmaster F. from Tongerlo. When the two men went back to Tongerlo around midnight, schoolmaster F. was jumped by a werewolf at the bridge over the canal. The poor man had to carry the werewolf until he was drenched in sweat.
182519: A farmer whose animals were all sick had someone come to bless the farm. While this was happening, a big black dog ran out of the farmhouse. So the farm had been bewitched.
182521: In the village several children had died after a witch had touched them.
182523: Near M.'s house, a little bell could always be heard ringing in a meadow. Because the sound was so beautiful, people called it 'God's bell'. After Leen had told the pastor about the ringing, the clergyman went to the meadow one evening with a book. When the pastor came back, he said: "Now you will no longer hear the ringing."
182527: Because the drossaard (bailiff) had committed many injustices and had many people hanged, he had to come back to haunt the Hobos after his death. The drossaard then appeared with a glowing chain around his neck. Two white friars went with a horse and a cart of sand, in which the drossaard's ghost was supposed to be, to a bridge to banish the spirit. On the way the sweating friars did nothing but pray. At a certain moment one of them said: "Come on back, lads, for we haven't got him!" The drossaard was sitting at the window of his house laughing.
182544: A man travelling with horse and cart suddenly could go no further when he passed a witch's house. As soon as the man began reciting the Gospel of Saint John, the horse could go on again. Since then the man has had no more trouble from the witch.
182556: A shepherd of the Root was sent to the Kempen. Meanwhile his band was taken from the cherry tree and thrown into the fire. The next moment the shepherd was already standing by the oven to save his band.
182561: A witch had visited a newborn baby. Later that day it was found that the child could no longer pee. That was the witch's fault.
182563: A witch who was visiting a woman said: "These two little children will both die tonight." The witch's prediction came true. A while later the animals in the stable fell ill. After a priest had read prayers over the house and the stable, the misfortune stopped.
182573: A farmer found it strange that his farmhand always went out after supper. One evening the farmer secretly followed his farmhand. He saw the boy crawl into a hollow tree stump and come out again a little later in the shape of a dog. The next day the farmer sent his farmhand away so that he could meanwhile burn the belt lying in the tree stump. As soon as the belt caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his possession. It took four or five people to hold the farmhand back. When the belt had burnt up, the farmhand said: "Now I am saved, now I am delivered from everything!"
182579: A dog with a chain was in fact a bewitched young man. If you could make such a dog bleed, he took on his human form again.
182591: A man who had stolen a lot of land ended up in hell after his death. The man had to walk about on earth all night with a boundary post in his hands, calling: "Now I have it, where shall I lay it!" When one night a drunkard answered: "Lay it where you took it from!", the ghost replied: "Now I am released".
182626: In 't Goolder lived a witch who could make the houses shake and who lured the children to her. Many people moved away to be rid of that witch.
182632: A woman often came to a farm to ask for a glass of water. But every time the woman had come by, something went wrong. So the farmer decided not to let the witch in anymore. From that day on, however, the drinking water became so murky that it was useless. When the farmer let the witch in again, the water became clear again.
182636: A man who was threshing was visited by a witch who turned a handful of sand into mice.
182642: Three women who went to fetch water at Kelchterhoef saw a clergyman appear. One of the women fainted with fright and the others quickly went inside. Three months later the clergyman appeared again, but this time he was much bigger. The clergyman came back to point out his money.
182650: An old man who had lived on a farm in Halingen came back to haunt after his death. He could find no rest because during his life he had unlawfully taken many possessions for himself. At midnight the ghost sat in the horse stable and untied the animals. At such moments a bright light shone as if it were broad daylight. Although they never saw him, the farm must truly have been haunted, for no farmhand wanted to keep working there. When the priest came to exorcise the stable, he banished the ghost to the Hondsveld for ninety-nine years.
182653: Because all of Helmke H.'s sheep were dying, the shepherd went to Dean R. in Hamont. After the dean had read prayers over the stables, he said to Helmke: "A woman with a dog will come to ask for alms. You must give her a piece of blood sausage." That same evening a beggar woman did indeed come knocking. Helmke gave the woman alms and her dog a piece of blood sausage. From then on all the sheep stayed healthy.
182654: A man had bought a heifer from a woman who was said to be a witch. When the heifer had been in the stable for a few hours, the people of the farm were covered in lice.
182666: Will-o'-the-wisps made people lose their way and were moreover often a bad omen. Some people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
182685: A white lady appeared by the brook. She was a dead woman who had to haunt because she had done something evil during her life.
182687: A brewer had a farmhand who always brewed at night. In the morning the farmhand was found in the brewing kettle. One day one of the farmhands said to the brewer: "Your wife has known that for a long time! I'm not afraid of her. Let her come tonight!" At night a miaowing cat appeared and brushed against the farmhand's leg. When the farmhand cut off the cat's claws, he heard something tinkle. A wedding ring had fallen on the floor. The brewer's wife was missing a finger.
182692: Near the Schans in Opoeteren a man went to thresh his grain. When the man went home, he was surrounded by cats. The man struck at the animals with his flail, but it did no good: the cats kept growing in number. At that the man hurried home as fast as he could.
182693: On Spikelspaai stood a farm that had much misfortune. Because almost all the cows died, they finally went to the friars of Hasselt. There they were given a relic to put in the post of the stable. Whenever there was misfortune somewhere, it was always blamed on an old woman who was taken for a witch.
182705: At the S. family's on 't Roeren, the animals were plagued by the kwade hand (evil hand). The cows made a lot of noise, fell ill and died. The blankets the farmer hung over the sick animals every evening lay neatly folded in the manger in the morning. The priest came to read prayers over the farm. The clergyman pushed little holes into the wall with his finger and then had them bricked up immediately. After that everything on the farm returned to normal.
182714: A child who had been touched by a witch had swollen little arms in the evening. Because the child kept crying all the time, the mother sought advice from a friar. The friar established that the child had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand) and advised the mother to visit the witch so that she could undo the harm. When mother and child were at the witch's, the witch said: "Oh dear, sweet child, what is that?" After the witch had rubbed the child's arms, the child became healthy again.
182722: In the past, tarts were often baked for the fair. A mother wanted her son and daughter to take the milk to the baker in town in the morning. Because the children had to get up very early for this, they slept on the bench in the living room that night. During the night the children and their parents were woken by a strange noise. The children opened the window and then clearly heard trumpets sounding and laughter and chattering of women's voices. The children ran to their parents in fright. The father was not afraid and went outside to see what was going on. When he came back in, he said that a witches' dance was being held in the secretary's meadow. The witches came from Wijer and were on their way to Sint-Truiden. The next day the children saw in the meadow a fine round ring where the grass had been completely worn away by the dancing.
182723: A witch lived in Maasmechelen. When the witch needed firewood, a passer-by said: "You don't need to go to the woods for that. Just take that withered little tree standing here next to the house!" The witch replied: "Yes, but that one still has to bear fruit next year," at which the man laughed at her. A year later, strangely enough, the little tree was full of red apples.
182755: A girl saw a wizard open a door by throwing his cap against it. The wizard beat his hands against the door until they bled. Because the man wanted to be freed of his magic power, he went to the Crosier Fathers. The wizard had to walk around the church three times.
182758: A man who had murdered a woman in Diepenbeek came back to haunt in a pear tree in Klotsbroek. The man was made to disappear into a ditch. Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
182773: The old mill of Mal and the castle of Nerem were haunted.
182779: In Haren the friars had to come and read prayers over the pigs. The animals did not grow because they were bewitched. The friar who came to bless the pigs became so exhausted that sweat dripped from his face.
182787: A man whose child was ill went to Hasselt to fetch ointment of the Holy Sacrament. The man had to come back by a different road. On the way back the man met the witch, who asked him what he had gone to fetch. That night the woman came into the house and picked up the child. The child died in her arms.
182816: In Smeermaas lived a widower who had remarried. The spirit of his dead wife appeared in the form of a shadow at the communion rail where the man sat. The woman had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, but she had never done so. Therefore the man had to go on pilgrimage for her.
182830: Two days after his death a learned man from Houthalen appeared at his desk, where he sat rummaging through his papers. The widow told the priest what she had seen. The following week the dead man drove past his house at midnight in a glowing coach. In that street, which was called the Koetsstraat, no bush ever grew. One Sunday the man was dug up. Two horses were needed to pull the cart with the coffin. In the Laambroek the horses began to sweat so badly that the coffin had to be buried on that spot. The dead man was banished for ninety-nine years and a day.
182836: Witches sometimes came to dance in Horpmaal. When a child was not entirely healthy, people believed it had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand).
182840: A man whose cabbages were being eaten by hares kept watch with his gun. After the man had shot a hare, he went to look and recognised a neighbour woman.
182846: A man who had a date with his girlfriend at the Zwarthoek always saw a white canon come to haunt at midnight.
182854: In Hoeselt there was a house in which nobody wanted to live because it was haunted. One day a curious boy went to have a look inside. When he came out, he was deathly pale and said: "I have seen a white ghost."
182855: A young man was walking back from the fair. When he reached the Berg, he suddenly heard wonderfully beautiful music. When he passed the Sint-Jobskapel, he saw that witches were dancing. It seemed as if they danced without their feet touching the ground. In the middle of the witches' ring danced the Black Lord, about whom the young man had heard many tales. When the dance was nearly over, two kind women came to the frightened young man: "Don't be afraid; we've come to fetch you for a dance." At the Black Lord's signal the witches began dancing again, and the young man danced with the most beautiful woman of all. He felt as light as a feather and wished the dance would never end. When the music and the dance stopped, the Black Lord's wife said: "We are glad that this young man has come to us. Give him some of our best wine." At once three young ladies came running with golden cups and a large wine jug in their hands. The Black Lord raised his cup and said: "To the health of the beautiful women!" The others then raised their cups too, saying: "Long live the Black Lord!" At that moment there was a terrible bang. It was dark and everyone had vanished. The young man had carelessly cried out: "By God's grace!", so that he now stood alone with his cup in front of the Sint-Jobskapel. When he had recovered a little from his fright, he trudged home. Although it was almost morning when he crept into bed, he could not fall asleep. He brooded the whole time and fell ill. A few days later a woman came by asking whether she could buy any gold objects. The young man's mother answered: "We have nothing like that in the house." The woman then became very angry and cried: "Then call your eldest son!" When the son came to the front door, he began to tremble, for he recognised the woman at once: she was the young lady who had handed out the golden cups on that night. The woman said: "Sir, I have come to take back the cup you took with you." The young man was relieved to be able to give back the cup, for he had known no peace since it came into his possession. "You can count yourself lucky that you got off so easily", said the woman, and then she left.
182857: A hunter had seen a fine hare. The man tried twice to shoot the animal, but his gun did not work. When the hare had disappeared, the gun worked again. It must have been a ghost hare.
182860: When Gradus H. was mowing, he chased a cat away. The next moment the man was surrounded by many cats.
182861: In Montenaken a black cat roamed about at night. Everyone was afraid of the cat because it was the devil.
182881: Corneel V. from Achel saw a cat sitting on a post next to a bridge. Corneel knocked the cat off the post while asking: "Pussycat, what are you doing there?", to which the cat answered: "Little Corneel, what are you asking me there?" The cat sat back on the post and said: "Otherwise just knock me off again."
182894: A man who suspected his girlfriend of being a witch announced that he wanted to end the relationship. For every time the woman touched him, the man was covered in lice. Through the witch's power, however, the man had to go back to his girlfriend after all.
182900: A farmer who could no longer make milk cried angrily: "That filthy witch must have been here again!"
182906: A woman was herding the cows at the cow post by the Vossenkuil when hoarse Trijn suddenly passed by. At that moment the cow began to jump about restlessly. When the witch had gone, the cow gave no more milk and a cat was sitting on the cow post.
182929: When B. was returning from Tongeren-Berg, a spirit walked beside him and said: "I stole a chalice from the church of Tongeren-Berg. Now you must go and buy a new chalice and give it to the church." B. told everything to the priest, who went to put the chalice back. After that the ghost was released.
182952: A nun had to keep an old man company. The man had always led a debauched life and knew neither God nor commandment. When the man lay dying, he refused to repent. Just after the man died, a black dog crawled out from under his bed. The animal ran outside, and when people went to look, there was nothing more to be seen.
182955: A woman who believed her stable was bewitched went to a clergyman, who gave her a thorn from Christ's crown of thorns. But when the woman got home, she could no longer find the thorn. The woman decided to walk around her house three times while praying the Gospel of Saint John. After the first time, however, the woman had forgotten the text.
182978: One afternoon a midwife saw a black cat sitting on her child's little bed. From then on the child had become much better behaved.
182983: In Meeuwen a farmhand had to go and manure the field. The farmer said: "Get a move on, so I can start ploughing!", to which the farmhand replied: "I have plenty of time; just make sure the plough is ready!" The farmhand manured a small patch of the field, then stuck a manure fork into the ground and said: "Now all like this." The next moment the whole field was manured. Because the farmer did not trust the matter, he sent the farmhand away. The farmhand wanted revenge for being dismissed. When the farmer had ploughed the whole field, the little heaps of manure were lying on top again.
182994: Every evening Narke saw a glow near his barn that looked like fire. When the man came closer, he no longer saw any fire. But there was a witch walking around.
183004: Women who lived in a remote place outside the village were often taken for witches. A witch could bewitch a horse by laying her hand on the animal's back. One day a man came to the smith in Lauw to have his horse shod. The horse was touched by a witch, after which the animal began to tremble and roll its eyes. The man immediately went with the sweating animal to the friars at the beguinage. Prayers were read over the horse and the man was given a little prayer that he had to say twice a day for nine days. After that the horse got better.
183008: A man who saw a pack of cats dancing said to one of the animals: "You won't have to come anymore, because I'll break your paw". When the man came home, his wife lay in bed with a broken leg.
183010:
A house in the Kruisstraat in Alken was haunted. Every three or four weeks a terrible noise was heard in the chimney, as if huge amounts of water were being poured down it. Sometimes it also sounded as if glass was being smashed in the chimney. One night Klaaske U. was coming back from the fair and wanted to stop at the house in the Kruisstraat for one more glass of gin. The door of the house was open, but nobody was home. Klaaske went in to have a look and saw twelve cats walking one after another through the sink. The occupants of the house were at their wits' end, so they decided to tear the house down completely and build a new one on the same spot. But wooden beams from the old house had been used for the new one, so the new home was haunted too.
Something similar happened in Binkom. A farmhand of about eight wanted to go up the stairs to the attic. When he looked up, he saw two white ghosts standing there, looking down at him. One Sunday evening the farmhand wanted to light the lamp with a match. A strange sound came from the box of matches. When the sound stopped and the farmhand lit the lamp, there was a loud bang, as if someone had struck the cupboard with an axe.
183014: After Deurke S. had died, some people sat up at night keeping vigil by his body. Around four o'clock, wood for the stove had to be fetched from the shed. Unfortunately nobody managed to get the shed door open. Then the witch Marie B. said: "Then I'll go myself." With one hand Marie opened the door effortlessly.
183016: A headless priest came haunting together with an altar boy. When the altar boy rang the bell, the bystanders had to kneel.
183017: For some unknown reason a farmer could not keep a single farmhand. When the farmer had once again taken on a new farmhand, the young man went to sleep in the attic. The farmer's wife, a witch who could turn herself into a donkey, went up to the attic at night. The farmhand immediately jumped on the donkey and rode the animal to the blacksmith. The next day the farmhand saw that the farmer's wife had horseshoes on her hands.
183031: A white sheep always came into the church. It was a ghost animal.
183034: When children had been touched by a witch, they fell ill and died of "the black hand".
183036: Some frightened girls hurried past a tree in which an owl always sat. A little further on an old woman lived in a little clay house. When the girls passed by, the woman said: "Ha, ha, I'll get you yet!"
183046: In the old days the Botermarkt in Stokkem was haunted.
183056: In Hoesselt lived a man whose children were bewitched. After the man had laid two sticks in the shape of a cross in front of his door, the witch could no longer get in. When the witch came to fetch her milk, she called: "I can't get in." Only when the man had removed the cross could the witch enter. After a while the man went to a clergyman, who said: "You must make a big fire. Then you must let the witch in and make her renounce her arts." The man did as he was advised. When the witch knocked, she said: "It's going to be a hot day today." The man could not restrain himself and replied: "Your cursed backside will feel that today all right!" At that the witch grew suspicious and left.
183058: A man and a woman had agreed that whoever died first would come back to tell the other what it was like in the hereafter. After the woman had died, a white figure appeared every evening. One day a man asked the apparition: "What is it like up there?", to which the ghost answered: "Good if you make it good and bad if you make it bad." Since then the ghost was never seen again.
183077: In a café in Lummen two men were mocking the holy Mass. A little later a big black dog came and lay under the table. Because no one managed to chase the dog away, the priest was sent for to exorcise the café. That dog had been the devil.
183081: A man who went to work at the mill had got lice even though he put on a clean shirt every day. When the man went to eat at noon, three women were sitting at the table. One of the women said to the other two: "You mustn't come too close to me, because I have lice." At that the man admitted that he had lice too. The woman gave him this advice: "You must catch a few lice with a needle and stick that needle above the stable door." When the lice on the needle have perished, you too will be rid of your lice. And so it happened.
183087: In Martenslinde three young hares ran about. Two of the hares could be caught easily. But whenever the third had been caught, the other two escaped. When Jozef V.K. had struck at the third hare with his stick, he could not find his stick again.
183092: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. Whoever saw a will-o'-the-wisp had to baptise it with holy water or with water from a brook.
183110: A woman who arrived in Germany one evening together with her brother was accompanied by a white lady.
183117: An old man often saw ghosts near the castle of Romershoven. Perhaps the former owner of the castle came to haunt there.
183139: A farmer going on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel with horse and cart saw two witches sitting in the ditch. When the farmer asked: "What are you doing there?", one of the women answered: "Just keep quiet, for you're not home yet!" On the way back the horse bolted and the cart was damaged. In the end the man died from all that misfortune.
183141: A fourteen-year-old girl from Ophoven had been struck by the evil hand and fell ill. Because the girl did not get better, her parents went on pilgrimage to the friars of Weert. On Weert territory the horse began to sweat heavily and could barely go any further. When they came back from the pilgrimage, the girl was cured.
183143: The statue of Mary of Opheers was always carried in the procession of Kortenbos. When one day they wanted to dress the statue in a new mantle, the garment turned out not to fit. So the hands and feet of the statue were sawn off. The joiner and the woman who was to dress the statue became completely paralysed shortly afterwards.
183146: A man from Romershoven who was going to the shoemaker in Diepenbeek was attacked by a werewolf near D.'s house. After the man had thrashed the werewolf, the beast suddenly changed into a good friend of his.
183149: After the death of Marieke M., a woman who had done many bad things during her life, her house was haunted. The priest advised the people to remove some earth from around the house and take it far away. After that no more strange things happened in the house.
183157: A man who was coming home with his wife from the pig fair at around eleven o'clock in the evening met the ghost of Jan Sloef on the way. The ghost wore a white shirt and shuffled along in his slippers. The man said: "Good evening", but the ghost did not answer.
183170: A married couple going to Tongeren met a little woman in the Stationsstraat who said: "I'm not going to Tongeren, because that is much too far." But when the man and woman arrived in Tongeren, they already saw the little woman standing by Ambiorix. The little woman said: "I'm here even earlier than you, and yet I didn't walk fast!" To which the wife replied: "Yes, but you consort with the devil!" After the priest had read prayers over the witch, she lost her power.
183180: A gentleman came into a café and joined a card game. When one of the men picked up a fallen card, he saw that the gentleman had a horse's leg. Since then that café has been called 'Het wit paard' (The White Horse).
183185: Will-o'-the-wisps constantly moved up and down through the air. A reckless man went looking for the will-o'-the-wisps and drowned in the swamp.
183195: One day Pier-Jentje and his father were pestered by some cats. When the father kicked at the cats, they were suddenly surrounded by a hundred cats.
183197: When Giel F. went to cut reed in Achel, a fierce wind suddenly arose, so that the man could not go on.
183199: After Jenneke had been to Brussels, she had died. Because during her life the woman had promised to go on pilgrimage to Briestem, Zepperen and Rijkel, her soul could find no rest. After her husband had gone on pilgrimage for her, the woman was released.
183219: A man who could turn himself into a werewolf had hidden his animal skin in an ash tree. When someone wanted to burn the animal skin, the werewolf sensed something was wrong and went to save his skin.
183221: A mother with a newborn baby was visited by a woman who asked: "Do you have much milk?", to which the mother replied: "No, not so much." The woman then gave the mother a little bottle to drink empty; then she would have enough milk for her baby. But the next day the mother had not a drop of milk left, and the baby's health also got worse. The mother was then advised to pray to the Three Sisters with the baby in her arms. Meanwhile she was not to let anyone else carry the baby for a moment. Shortly afterwards the mother had milk again and her baby also got better.
183222: People who were jumped by a werewolf had to carry the beast a little way.
183223: At the village constable's house there were always many cats in the attic. One day the man chopped off one of the cats' paws. The next day the witch wore a bandage around her arm.
183232: Keên's wife had touched the cows in Jo's stable and had said: "What lovely cows, Jo!" The next day the cow was ill.
183261: The werewolf often made people carry him. But one day a man had tied a knife to his back. When the werewolf jumped on the man, he was wounded. Werewolves that lost blood became human again.
183262: A man coming back from Luik was followed by a big dog. A little later the animal suddenly vanished.
183269: A girl from Neerharen did not know that her boyfriend was a werewolf. One day the pair went walking, when the boy said to the girl: "I'm going to relieve myself behind a bush. Hold this red handkerchief in your hand, then the werewolf won't be able to harm you." A little later a werewolf appeared and snatched the handkerchief from the girl's hands. When the pair came home that evening, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The boy went away and was never seen again.
183279: On the castle lane of Printhagen a white lady drove around in a coach with four horses.
183286: The alvermannetjes (elf men) left the Kempen because they could not bear the ringing of the church bells. Afterwards the alvermannetjes went to the coal mines; after all, small black men worked there too.
183287: By the mill there was a rabbit that ate all the cabbages. People had often tried to shoot the rabbit, but had never managed to hit it. A friar from Rekem had advised the man to put a piece of blessed candle in the gun instead of a cartridge. That way the man did manage to hit the rabbit. After that the animal never came back.
183308: The architect who was to make the plan for Cologne Cathedral sat in the woods brooding over his work, which was only half finished. Suddenly a gentleman with a horse's foot came up to the architect and said: "I know what your problem is. And I have the solution here with me. I will give you the complete plan of Cologne Cathedral on condition that you sell me your soul." The architect agreed to the offer and sold his soul. When the church was nearly finished, the architect told a clergyman what had happened to him. The clergyman made sure the man could keep his soul. The disgruntled devil consequently had to fly away with the man's body. Where the devil flew out, there was a hole in the church that could never be closed.
183311: The architect who had to draw up the plan for the cathedral of Keulen could not get his work finished. One day the man was visited by a gentleman with horse's feet. This gentleman offered to finish the plan, on condition that he would get the soul of the first living creature to enter the church. When the church was finished, however, they sent a bear inside. The devil was so furious that he grabbed the animal and flew with it through the church roof. No one has ever managed to close the hole in the roof.
183336: Two farmers were working in a field near Wallonia during the harvest. One of the farmers said that after his death he would come back once more to say good day to his friend. Some years after that farmer had died, the other farmer was mowing his field. Suddenly he saw something moving among the grain. Because the farmer immediately thought of his dead friend's promise, he ran away terrified.
183338: At the corner of a wood in Opgrimbie a witch had once been burned. Since then people no longer dared to go to that place because they believed the witch came to haunt the wood.
183343: A witch gave an old woman some carrot seed. The next day, however, the woman's son fell ill. After the priest of Offelken had read prayers over the child, he got better. The priest advised the woman from then on to pay for everything she received.
183346: A ten-year-old boy took a lump of earth in his hand and said: "Little mouse, off!" Then lots of little mice came out of the earth. The boy was made to be baptised again.
183369: A young man coming back from his girlfriend's at night saw a cat sitting on the road. The boy then took his gun and shot off one of the animal's legs. When the young man visited his girlfriend the following week, the girl had a broken leg.
183370: A man out walking with two friends said: "You go on ahead, I'll catch up." Because the man consorted with the devil, he could turn himself into a ghost, so he could pass his friends unnoticed.
183382: People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children.
183384: A man went to the friars of Sint-Truiden because his child had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand). After prayers had been read over the child, it was cured.
183398: A man who worked in Fexhe-lez-Slins (Wallonia) always saw a pack of cats on the way. The further he went, the more cats he saw. Because he was afraid, he picked up a stick and said: "Stay as far away from me as the grace of God is from you." The next moment the cats went away.
183404: In Hoeselt there lived a woman who had seized her sister's inheritance. When the woman was dead, she came to haunt at night with the words: "My money, my money!" Because the dead woman's daughter was very frightened, she sent for the priest. After long prayer the priest banished the ghost into a tree. The tree split in two and the ghost was never seen again.
183410:
The werewolf often hid behind a hedge to jump on a passer-by. After the werewolf had been carried a little way, he left his victim alone. Werewolves were people possessed by the devil.
Later some people dressed up as werewolves to frighten or rob others.
183416: When the priest said a word wrongly at a baptism, the child was not properly baptised. When such a child had died, it came back in the form of a will-o'-the-wisp. If one called around midnight: "Come, I will baptise you!", a thousand will-o'-the-wisps came flying at once.
183429: A man and his brother had to fetch a witch in Genoelselderen and take her to the stake. When they took the witch off the cart and threw her into the fire, the men were completely covered in lice.
183431: A tailor who had to deliver a made-to-measure suit went through a meadow. But the poor man could no longer find the way out of the meadow. In the end the witch helped the tailor.
183433: Drossaard (bailiff) Clercx had been banished to a bridge in Kerkhoven. Three days later his brother Tuuske Clercx rode on horseback over the bridge to Kerkhoven. When the man rode back, he fell off his horse right in front of the bridge. Tuuske was so shaken by this incident that he died three days later.
183448: The mayor of Neerglabbeek once had a relationship with a girl from Meeuwen. One day, when the young man went to his girlfriend, he met a witch on the way who said: "Aren't you afraid?", to which he replied: "No, I'm not afraid." The witch warned him: "Then don't be startled" and then vanished. In the evening the young man was walking back home when he was suddenly harassed by magpies that kept flying around his head. After that the young man never visited the girl again.
183449: In the past there was a café in the Beekstraat where a lot of drinking went on. One day a strange little old man came into the café. Because the man said nothing, they poured brandy over him, whereupon the man turned into a dog. Because everyone was afraid, they sent for the dean of Hasselt. That dean, however, did not dare to exorcise the dog. In the end the holy little friar of Hasselt drove out the devil. All the workmen from the Raamstraat in Vinkebos went to watch. Harieke S. was too afraid to go and watch.
183451: In Sterbos a white lady with poultry appeared at midnight.
183452: A sick man raged so wildly at night that he could not be kept in bed. The man's relatives were advised to send for Suske, who worked at the hospital. Suske came to the sick man with a cord with a key hanging from it. When he held the cord above the sick man, the key began to turn. From this Suske concluded that the man was in the power of a dark force. Suske advised the relatives to hold a knife over the man's heart the following night. No sooner said than done. When the clock struck twelve, a loud bang rang out, all the doors flew open at once and the sick man was lifted up to the ceiling. After that nothing more happened.
183472: Fien C. from Kuringen had a crooked back and walked with two sticks. One day someone said: "Fien is a witch. If you put your feet crossed on her track, she has to stop." A man who once tried it got a terrible fright when Fien turned round and made threatening gestures with her stick.
183478: A man coming back from Melbeek in the evening lost his way. At the border with Diepenbeek the man thought he saw a pond, and so he turned back. If he had felt the ground, he would have known it was not a pond. The 'dolende man' (wandering man) had made him lose his way.
183482: A fruit grower was out one evening with his mother when the mother suddenly said: "Frans, let that bicycle pass!" Frans, however, saw no bicycle at all. A year later, at that same spot, Frans saw a glowing apparition that looked like a stoat.
183485: A beggar woman came to mother C. in Lozen, walked to the cradle, stroked the child and said: "But madam, what a lovely child you have!" The beggar woman had barely left when the child began to cry. Neither the doctor nor the priest could stop the crying. People even went on pilgrimage for the child. A beggar woman also came by the V. family in Beek and stroked the child. After that the child got an inflammation in its little leg. The child died at the age of ten.
183491: The kwade hand (evil hand) was mainly associated with old people who had a crooked back and walked with a stick. If such a person had been in the stable, an animal would lie dead within two days.
183495: Turkish slaves were freed by Our Lady after praying the rosary. The slaves' shackles were hung behind the altar of the church.
183497: A girl returning from Lanaken with her father was followed on the Klein hei by a kitten that made a sound like a sheep. At the Rooivaart the kitten went along with a boy as far as Lambert Vrancken's at café 'De Vrede'. When the kitten jumped onto the wall at Cilineke's, the boy struck at the animal, which then turned into a sheep.
183505: A headless horse roamed about in Budel. Nobody knew who the horse's owner was.
183506: A boy who played the werewolf was sent to Hasselt one day with the wheelbarrow. Meanwhile the boy's animal skin was burnt.
183508: At the earthwork of Kwamol many people were killed during a battle. After his death a traitor appeared in the form of a ghost that sat praying in the middle of the earthwork field. One day the ghost stayed away.
183522: A man went to a witch who sat wailing in the woods. When he had hit the witch on the head with a stick, she said: "Hit me again!", and then ran up a tree. The man took to his heels and could still hear the witch weeping in the distance.
183530: A woman from Peer heard someone calling for help at night. She saw a little old woman sitting on a chest and said: "I'll help carry that chest." A quarter of an hour later the chest suddenly became so heavy that they had to drop it. When something black came out of the chest, the women quickly ran to a house. The next day a black hand was burnt into the door.
183546: In Grimmertingen a werewolf roamed about with a red handkerchief in its mouth. It looked like a human on four legs. The werewolf was foaming at the mouth the whole time and constantly harassed passers-by.
183547: When the white lady met a man between Wouteringen and Lauw, she walked on arm in arm with him. She tried to make the man lose his way or to push him into the marsh by the Jeker.
183550: When Louis came home, he saw a big black dog. He was told that the dog was a witch.
183557: A man who heard someone call out that his horse was dying could not get his trousers on. So the man took another pair of trousers, which he did manage to put on. As he left his house, the man saw a figure walk past the door.
183559: A man coming back from Spouwen saw a horse standing on the road between Hees and Kesselt. The man decided to ride the horse home. But after a while the animal said: "I've carried you long enough. Now you carry me for a change!" Then the horse put its legs on the man's shoulders and made him carry it. That horse was the werewolf.
183570: A farmhand who was a werewolf was sent far away so that his collar could be burnt in the meantime. But the moment the collar caught fire, the farmhand was immediately standing beside the oven to save his band.
183572: In the old days a ghost with a long beard wandered about in Alken. The ghost set a black dog on the frightened children.
183580: A girl became bewitched after a woman tapped her on the shoulder in the shop. Because the doctor could not help, people went on pilgrimage for the girl to the abbey of Tongerlo. The priest went down to the cellar with the girl and had her eat bread and salt. Then the girl had to say a prayer for nine consecutive days. After that the girl was perfectly healthy again.
183586: Someone had swept the household rubbish together and left the brush standing on the little heap. Because of this the witch could not come in.
183599: Some men who had gone to mow clover were going home along a field path. Suddenly a violent whirlwind arose that sent the clover flying high into the air. That wind was caused by witches.
183604: K.'s wife was a witch. One day a farmer threw a chicken with a broken leg on the ground. The witch, who had seen it, said to the farmer: "You must bind that leg with two matches." The farmer replied: "Yes, I'll do that later!" The witch responded: "No, you must do it now, otherwise it won't heal!" But the farmer ignored the witch's advice. That same evening the farmer was blind.
183619: A father whose son was good for nothing had often said: "You have to get out of here! Even if I have to sell you to the devil!" One day, when the father was walking with his son along a sunken lane, a coach stopped beside them. In the coach sat a man who asked: "Say, won't you let your son work for me?", to which the father replied: "That's just what we were on our way for. Take him along right away!" The man let the son get in and said: "Next year I'll bring him back to this spot." A year later the father went to fetch his son at the agreed place. "What did you have to do, boy?" his parents asked. The boy answered: "Father, you always said you would even sell me to the devil. Well, that has now happened. I stood at the gate of hell the whole time." Because his parents did not believe him at first, the boy went on: "I'll prove it. Didn't such and such people die this past year? I had to let them all into hell. One of the damned was even the parish priest, for those clergymen aren't all so holy, you know!"
183623: One night a man saw a meowing cat sitting in a tree. For a good half hour the man tried to hit the cat, but the animal kept jumping away. In the end the man did manage to beat the cat to death. The next day the man met someone from the neighbourhood, who said: "You killed my cat! My wife saw it herself." The man denied having anything at all to do with the animal's death. Some time later the man went with a minor ailment to the woman, who was known for her healing skills. The witch then said: "I used to have a fine cat, but now that she is dead, I can no longer heal."
183624: The J. family had a cow that was paralysed and grew thinner and thinner. The sorcerer of the Bilzerpoort in Tongeren came to look at the cow and said: "I cannot cure the cow, because it is the kwade hand (evil hand) that makes her ill. Go quickly and look at the gate, and you will see who the witch is." It was Truuskes E., the farmer's wife's mother. They had been quarrelling with that woman for a long time, and that was why she had bewitched the cow.
183629: Anyone who came across a black cat had best pretend not to have seen it. For if you kicked at a black cat, you would be surrounded by many cats.
183646: A man coming home at night saw the ghosts of the priest and his altar boy standing at the corner of the street.
183647: Women who came peddling often bewitched children by tapping them on the head and saying: "Ah, lovely child!" The child then fell ill and cried from midnight to one o'clock. Those peddler women were witches who consorted with the devil. If a medal had been placed under the threshold, the witches could not come in.
183676: A man told his friends he could make a dog come in. A little later a black dog did indeed come in and lay down on the floor. A girl watching was very afraid of the dog. Then the man said to the animal: "Come on, get up again, the people don't want you here." When the dog walked out, the door opened and closed by itself. It was the devil.
183680: In the Netherlands a woman came peddling to a girl who had a little child. When the girl said she did not want to buy anything, the woman stroked the child's head with the words: "Your mother will yet regret that." A while later the child fell ill. After the friars of Stein had prayed for the child, it was eventually cured after all. In return for the help, the friars were given some grain.
183702: On a bridge stood a dog that would not let anyone pass.
183717: A girl saw the spirit of her dead mother every night. The dead woman could find no rest because she had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. After the father had gone on pilgrimage with four francs and four eggs that his dead wife had given him, the ghost never appeared again.
183744: In Dorplein lived a witch named Johanna T. Close to her little house stood an old oak with a girth of a good three metres. Between midnight and one o'clock the tree was always full of magpies. After Johanna had died, there were no more magpies in the tree.
183748: A woman suspected of being a witch came to a calf standing in the stable. The calf got diarrhoea and died shortly afterwards. This happened through the kwade hand (evil hand).
183766: When old Jans was walking home together with some friends, to his great fright he saw a white lady appear. The lady walked past the men and then disappeared.
183767:
Between Bocholt and Reppel a man always had to carry the werewolf. But one day the man managed to wound the werewolf. Since then he never had to carry a werewolf again. When the man discovered he had lost his watch at the spot where he had always had to carry the werewolf, he still did not dare go and fetch it.
Werewolves could only be cut with a knife that had first cut through earth or bread. A werewolf could also be wounded with black birch wood.
183779: The black iron gate at the back of the castle used to be haunted. No one dared to walk past it, for a white beguine always appeared.
183781: A child from Mopertingen that would not grow was called Killekrop. The father decided to go on pilgrimage with his child. When the man was crossing a bridge, he heard someone call: "Hey Killekrop, where are you going?" Although the child had never spoken a word, it answered: "To Our Lady of Hammerstad, to grow and get healthy!" The man was so startled that he threw the basket with the child into the water. In the water two devils appeared, who cried: "Hake, haki!"
183803: A man who went hunting on the Locht saw a hare sitting there and said: "That is such a strange hare. It doesn't behave at all like other hares." The man tried to shoot the hare but did not manage to hit it.
183805: A priest who had forgotten to say a word during mass had to haunt after his death. When an altar boy repeated the ghost's words, the priest was released.
183809: Three men from Broekom, among them old Polus, had been to Loon. When they came to a turnstile, a talking cat was sitting there. Polus had a stick with him and struck at the cat. He missed and tried again. He missed again. Polus no longer dared to strike, but the cat asked: "Why don't you strike a third time?"
183810: White ladies had often been seen near the farm of B. One evening some boys decided to go looking for the white ladies. The boys held hands so that they blocked the whole road. Six white ladies in long dresses appeared. They passed through the boys like shadows and said: "We know you, but you do not know us."
183812: A certain P. had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for his sick wife. However, the woman died before the man had the chance to go. One evening the man sat in a corner praying a rosary for his wife, when he suddenly felt someone tap him on the shoulder. The man said: "Marie, I will go!" The next day the man went on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. His wife's spirit went ahead. Since that day the man has neither seen nor heard his wife again.
183815: A man coming back around eleven o'clock from Meeswijk, where he had visited his girlfriend, saw a small light in the corn. The light flew further and further away and finally disappeared high in the sky.
183822: A man thought he heard music somewhere and saw a castle. When the man came closer, he saw only some wood standing there.
183828: A farmer who had vermin in his stable sent for a man from Hasselt. The man went into the stable briefly and said: "If anyone wants to come into the stable, you must not allow it." Two days later the problems in the stable were solved.
183841: At a farmer's, a cow had died twice in a row through the kwade hand (evil hand).
183844: A witch foretold to a boy that he would find something in a certain place. "I will make the sign of the cross, and then a cross will appear on that object too," the witch added. And so it happened.
183847: The werewolf jumped on people's backs and urinated on its victims until they were soaking wet. One had to carry the werewolf until almost home.
183869: Whenever a man left very early in the morning for Tongeren or Liège, he always met a cat in the Krabberstraat.
183886: In Beringen many cats always gathered at eight o'clock in the evening. The witch cats would sit miaowing in a large pine wood. At two o'clock they were gone again. Sometimes a few brave people went to pelt the cats with stones. When a cat bled, the witch could be recognised.
183892: At a man's house in Dilsen there were always cats walking around.
183901: A miller who was having trouble grinding the corn saw a cat's paw under the door every time he was at work. One day the miller chopped off the cat's paw. The next day a woman lay in bed with a severed arm.
183907: A man from Mal who was coming back from the fair in Nerem around midnight saw a black lady on the way, sitting combing her hair. The lady said to the man: "Just go on, you are not disturbing me." The man walked on, scared to death. A little further on he saw in a meadow a black dog rubbing its back against the branches of a tree. The man was so frightened that his hair stood on end and pushed his cap off his head.
183928: A girl playing in the garden went to her father and said: "Dad, the little goat keeps pushing me," to which the father replied: "But I don't see any goat!" Because the child was very frightened, the man called in the chaplain of Paal, who resolved the matter.
183931: When Selm V.B. was digging up potatoes, he was visited by a gentleman who said: "That patch of ground is full of mice." Selm said that he would like to learn to make mice himself. The gentleman then gave him a magic book that he had to read all the way through.
183947: The farmhand of the mill in Hees often turned into a werewolf because he had sold his soul to the devil. One evening, at the Heilige Haag between Vlijtingen and Hees, a man was jumped by a wolf, which made him carry it all the way to Hees. Later it was discovered that this werewolf was the farmhand of the mill in Hees.
183957: A man cycling through the woods in the evening suddenly heard beautiful music, although there was nothing to be seen anywhere.
183962: A soldier went to a fortune teller, who predicted he would make a long journey. A while later the man went to Hasselt. When he came home, his brother had just been given the last rites.
183963: A man who had gone to play cards in Maarheze came home at midnight. As he walked past the house of Smeets the smith, he suddenly saw a big dog on the road. He ran home as fast as he could. The next day he had a severe headache. The pain lasted two weeks and then suddenly disappeared. Later the man learned that his neighbour had shot his black dog because it had killed chickens. That had happened at the very moment the man had seen the dog on the way.
183968: A brewer told a soldier who had once worked as a brewer's hand that he could not manage to brew good beer. "I'll come and brew tonight," said the soldier. That night the soldier saw a big black cat walking around the beer vat. The soldier took his sabre and chopped off one of the cat's paws. The next morning the brewer found it strange that his wife stayed in bed so long. In the end he found that his wife was missing an arm. The woman confessed her guilt and was burned as a witch.
183979: A man coming back from B. by moonlight with some friends got lost. The people did not get home until five o'clock the next morning. That was Trien's doing.
183992: The B. family had been burgled. The wizard Fons V.E. turned himself into a dog and so overheard a conversation that revealed who the thief was.
183999: A man out poaching was suddenly frightened by a headless white figure flying about and screaming. The man got away as fast as he could. Since then he never went poaching alone again.
184004: In Sterbos a ghostly nun walked up and down a lane.
184010: Berbke G. took a newborn baby in her arms with the words: "Oh, what a lovely child this is!" The next day the child was dead. When the dead child's mother fell ill, the priest cut open the pillow. It was full of poisonous flowers. They did not manage to throw the pillow into the fire because Berke was always nearby. A few days later the priest went to see the sick woman again. When her husband wanted to come too, he was followed by as many as twenty cats. In the end they did manage to burn the bewitched pillow.
184012: If one had seen a black crow, raven or magpie, one would surely have bad luck that day.
184018: De Witte said to a man who still had a long way to go: "I'll get you a horse." The next moment a horse came flying up, which carried the man to his house and then disappeared. The man went to bed and never got up again.
184022: One day Door from Kinrooi was walking along a brook with some friends when he suddenly saw a cat crossing the road. Door kicked the cat into the brook. Then a loud screeching rang out, as if a hundred cats had been kicked into the brook. A few days later, however, Door fell ill. There turned out to be two toads in his belly. A friar from Weert made the toads leave Door's body by the natural way, after which the man was cured.
184023: In Lummen lived a man who cursed a lot. Because the man was often surrounded by black cats, the friars came to read prayers over his house.
184027: When a man was cleaning his birdcage, his finch suddenly flew off. While he was looking for the bird, a woman came knocking and asked what was the matter. "My finch has flown out of the cage," said the man, to which the visitor replied: "Don't talk nonsense; that's no finch, it's a frog!" The man then quickly kicked the frog out of the house and sent the woman away. The woman lived in Membruggen, a village known for its many witches.
184028:
Witches were usually dirty little old women. A witch also lived in Boorsem.
A farmer from Boorsem had neatly bound his harvest into sheaves. In the evening the farmer saw the witch walking around his field and pulling some grain out of every sheaf. A year later the farmer's field was full of weeds. Moreover, a violent thunderstorm had knocked all the crops to the ground. Because people had hung palm twigs everywhere, the harvest was good again the following year.
184030: One day the robe of the statue of Mary in the basilica of Tongeren was covered in mud. The statue had gone along in the procession by itself.
184031: Some men standing guard at the French border were joined by a boy named Poujèt. The boy could hang from the ceiling by his feet. Poujèt bent down and talked with a gentleman who had appeared in the shape of a black dog. When the gentleman had vanished, the boy made the other men promise not to tell anyone what they had seen. The boy touched his shoe and then vanished without a trace.
184037: A man went to ask his neighbour for help bringing in the fodder for the animals, which had dried. The woman sent her daughter to the field to help. When the girl and the neighbour's eldest son had gathered a big heap of fodder, a terrible whirlwind rose up and sent everything flying. The neighbour's son immediately cried that it must be the work of a witch. After the same thing happened a second time, the girl ran away because she was terribly afraid of the witch.
184040: A man who was plagued by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's harmful touch) went to the heksenmannetje (witch doctor) in Diest. The man suspected that Clet C. had bewitched him. The witch doctor said: "Tomorrow the witch will come and ask to cut roêier (?) in the woods, but you must not allow it." When the man was in church the next day, he suddenly saw that his blue smock was full of lice. Later his whole house turned out to be full of lice.
184060: A black cat always sat by a brook in Opglabbeek. One day a man broke one of the animal's legs with a stick. The next day the witch came to complain.
184073: Farmer L. had a farmhand who was possessed by the devil. One day the farmer found the collar of the farmhand, who had to roam about at night as a werewolf. When the farmer was about to throw the collar into the fire, the farmhand was immediately standing by the oven.
184078: Thijske, who worked for Ghay G., lived in a small clay cottage next to P. When the man walked through the church lane one evening, he saw a cat. Thinking it was his own cat, the man called the animal. Then the cat jumped into the man's cloak and let itself be carried. After a while, however, the animal became so heavy that the man had to drop it. The cat was the devil.
184084: A young man whose animals were all dying went to the friars of Hamont. Two friars came along to the farm and told the farmhand to light the fire. Then the friars lay down and prayed until the ground cracked open. The bones found in the ground were burned in the oven. After that the young farmer had no more misfortune.
184100: The werewolf was half human and half animal. The werewolf sometimes jumped on passers-by's backs and then made them carry him. At a cross or a crossroads the werewolf could go no further. Many people believed the werewolf had something to do with the devil.
184106: On the road to Winterslag stood an old chapel behind which black cats always sat miaowing.
184171: One Sunday at about eleven o'clock the V.H. brothers took a cow to the Kamp to have it slaughtered. On the way the brothers met a big dog. The next moment the dog had vanished and Jan S. stood on the road. Jan asked: "Do I still have time for eleven o'clock mass?" A little later Jan changed into a dog again.
184183: Around midnight the meadow of Geebroek was haunted: a large dog with a chain roamed about there.
184196: Remy, son of Mieke V., had heard that his girlfriend, whom he had been with for four and a half years, was a witch. Because Remy wanted to get to the bottom of it, he went to his girlfriend and pretended to have fallen asleep with his head on the table. That is how Remy saw his girlfriend and her mother rub themselves with witch's grease and then speak a magic formula, which went: "Over hedge and over thicket to a shop in Cologne, where we'll go and drink wine". The next moment the two women had vanished. When Remy went back home, he saw a kitten by a pond. He took his stick and struck at the animal. The next day his girlfriend lay sick in bed.
184206: In the fields in Berg black cats often sat in the corn in the evening. Around eleven o'clock the animals began to screech, so that hardly anyone dared go there any more.
184223: An old blacksmith coming back drunk from the fair saw a silken lady standing there. When the man said: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph!", the woman had disappeared.
184226: A Walloon farmer said to an ugly cat that was making his animals sick: "If you come again, I'll shoot you dead!" After that the witch cat was not seen again.
184241: When someone could not make butter, it was a sign that a witch had been in the house.
184248: In the pillow of a sick child, a knife, a scythe and a pair of scissors were found.
184250:
In the past, babies often died shortly after birth. Sometimes a wreath was then found in the little pillow. When that happened, people said that the black hand had come to take the child.
In fact, the black hand was simply the hand of the mother who had not cared for the child properly.
184255: On summer evenings the men often sat together in the street. When one of them said: "Now the little hare should come!", a hare would indeed come running up. The men would then always say: "Shall we catch the little hare?", although they knew they would never succeed. Once they had tried by placing two chests across the road so that the little hare could not get through. All together they had chased the animal, but every time it slipped away. They never caught the hare.
184258: A man was climbing over a turnstile in a meadow near the castle of Dompaerts in Alken when he was suddenly jumped by a werewolf, which made him carry it a little way.
184281: Henri S. received the gift of driving away rats from a woman. In the old days, people who could drive away rats had to pass their gift on to someone else before they died. In Maastricht lived some men who could give people magic power. Once you had that magic power, you never lost it again.
184283:
The mayor had gone to collect the money for the sugar beets at the sugar factory in Sint-Truiden. A man went with a brave boy to fetch the mayor in Tongeren. On the way the man suddenly heard a noise as if horses were galloping up. The next moment a beast jumped on the man's back. The beast was so heavy that the boy had to hold the man upright. After a while the boy said to the werewolf: "That's enough now", and threatened the animal with an axe. Then the werewolf ran away.
To be able to hit a werewolf, one first had to moisten one's weapon with spit. Werewolves could also only be hit on the spot where they had received the Holy Confirmation.
184284: In Klotsbroek in Genk, a woman was hanging out the linen one morning. A witch passed by and said: "It will be something (?)" Although the sun had shone all day, the linen was still soaking wet in the evening.
184291: A woman who found it strange that her husband got up every night decided to spy on him once. That is how the woman discovered that her husband threw a horse hide over himself and walked about the fields like that. One day, when the man was working five kilometres away, they wanted to burn his horse hide. As soon as the hide caught fire, the man was already standing by the oven.
184296:
In Genk lived a sick child that had scabs of blood all over its skin. Mina C. said: "Help that poor child leave this world. O God, don't pray for that child, for it will die anyway!" Three days later the child was dead.
The witch Mina C. was blamed for the child's death.
184302: Grake and Daniel went to Hoeselt together every week to sell meat and bread. In Hoeselt there was a witch who wanted to sell Daniel a goatskin. Daniel refused and said: "No, Grake will buy it." But because Grake did not want to buy the skin either, the witch said: "If you don't buy that skin, you won't get home without accidents!" When Grake drove home, the wheel came off the cart, so that the man could go no further.
184316: The area near the statue of Mary in Dorplein was haunted. Whoever walked past the statue in the evening heard chains rattling, though nothing could be seen. The pastor had sprinkled the statue with holy water several times, but that had not helped.
184321: A man whose wife was angry because he had come home too late said vehemently: "You mustn't be angry! I was followed by an old woman with a walking stick. Suddenly the woman changed into a big black dog."
184332: When R. went poaching, he saw a headless dog with a key in its mouth (?).
184336: In the meadows of Koninksem, the witches made music at night by banging the lids of cooking pots together.
184337: In the old days, when people saw a cat, they always believed it was a witch. People who had a lot of misfortune with their animals went to Oostham. On the ninth day those people had to put a bottle of holy water with a palm branch on the table. At a certain moment that bottle burst.
184338: The deceased owner of a castle near Wellen always came to haunt at night because he could find no rest.
184355: When Dirk R. was on his way with the wood cart, the horses suddenly stopped. The priest rid R. of his little book of magic. Dirk had got the book from a boatman. Even people who could not read were still able to read the text in a book of magic.
184357: A strong man from Koninksem went to work in Widooie. On the way the man went to relieve himself among the bushes when a werewolf suddenly jumped on his neck. The brave man grabbed the beast with both hands and carried it along like that to the farm. Then he beat the werewolf until it bled on the spot where he had been baptised. When the werewolf took on his human form, he turned out to be the farmhand of the farm.
184370: One evening a man went to fetch coal with his brother. At the spot where a witch in the shape of a cat sat by the road, the man's lamp suddenly went out.
184372: When Jan V. was coming back from Wellen, he suddenly could not go on because he was surrounded by cats. When the man made the sign of the cross, all the cats ran away.
184379: People who were out late in the evening often had to carry the werewolf. If the werewolf could be made to bleed, he turned into a human. Whoever could beat the werewolf in human form could also take him on in werewolf form.
184390: Two drunk men riding home through the Hemmen saw a white lady opposite the Schans.
184397: D.'s farmhand was always jumped by a werewolf at the Hooikant in the evening. Such a dog could only be chased away with a red handkerchief.
184404: A castle once sank in Batsheers. The street along which the castle stood is still called 'Kasteelstraat'.
