184420: A man went on a retreat with some friends. When the man went to fetch the son of Clet G., Clet said: "Sit down at the table and eat well, because you'll need it!" On the way to the church the man got severe diarrhoea.
184425: The baby of the V. family cried in its cradle all the time. A beggar woman who visited the family advised them to cut open the baby's pillow. From the pillow they pulled a rope many metres long. Since then the baby has not cried any more.
184433: A man returning from Vlijtingen was followed near the meadow by a hare with a little bell around its neck. When the man got home and opened the door, the hare had changed into a dog with flaming eyes. It was a werewolf.
184438: At the castle of Heppeneert lived a knight who had lost all his money at card games. When the knight had sold his soul to the devil, he was allowed to live in luxury for seven more years. The knight's sister was a pious woman who prayed a lot. Seven years later the knight went to the bridge where the devil sat waiting for him. But the devil had no power over the knight and said: "First chase away that woman standing behind you!" Since then that bridge has been called the Sint-Geerterbrug (Saint Gertrude's Bridge?).
184456: A man who had seen a witch go into his stable laid a cross in front of the threshold, so that the witch could not get out. The man said to the witch: "If you confess that you bewitched my animals and promise never to come back here, I will take the cross off the threshold." The witch gave in and she never came back.
184459: A man who went hunting on Christmas Day saw a hare about ten metres away. When the man tried to shoot the animal, however, his gun would not fire. A second and a third attempt also failed. A while later the hare ran off, and when it was a good two hundred metres from the hunter, the man, oddly enough, did manage to shoot the animal.
184466: A little boy had died after getting lice through a witch's doing.
184474: A man from Lommel slept restlessly and always woke up sweating because he was ridden by the 'moort' (nightmare spirit).
184488: When a werewolf crawled under a table, it came out from under it as a rabbit.
184493: A miller's hand who went to an inn in the evening left his horse standing outside. When the hand came back out, he found his horse in a sunken lane a little further on. The hand jumped on the horse and felt that he was sitting on a man's shoulders.
184496: A man going to visit his family suddenly realised he had brought nothing for the children. Between Neerrepen and Riksingen, however, the man saw a cherry tree. He decided to pick some cherries to give to the children. The man paid no attention to the black cat sitting under the tree. When the man walked back home the next day, an old woman was standing by the tree. The man asked: "Are they ripe yet, Mie?", to which the woman replied: "Were they perhaps riper last night?" That woman was a witch.
184505: A man coming back from visiting his girlfriend in Heppen met a cat or a dog in Leopoldsburg. The man lost his way, so that he did not get home until morning.
184514: Two boys coming back from Tervant with their mother heard a strange sound behind them on a remote forest road.
184516: In a house in Niel an animal always came to haunt the attic. After a pilgrimage had been made, the animal did not appear again. The occupants of the house had once promised to go on a pilgrimage but had not kept that promise.
184526: A man was walking past the churchyard in the moonlight with his parents and his brother. When they saw a big black dog lying on the veterans' memorial, the father decided to go and fetch parish priest J. He tapped on the priest's window and said: "It's Berty. There's a pitch-black dog lying in the churchyard." The priest answered: "Yes, I know. That is a dead man who comes back. Just leave the dog there." Because the black dog had once said: "Leave me alone", people did not dare to chase the animal away.
184542: Near Hengelhoef, a farm in Houthalen, a man saw a procession with a praying pastor approaching. At Jannesmenneke the procession disappeared into the ground.
184544: In Aken people wanted to build a church so beautiful and large that everyone would talk about it. Unfortunately the church council did not have enough money to pay for such a building. One day a gentleman came riding up in a coach. The gentleman offered to provide the necessary money in return for the soul of the first living creature to enter the finished church. When the church was nearly finished, they thought of a way to fulfil the return the man had demanded. They decided to chase a live sheep into the church first. The devil, who was just flying in with the last door, was so furious when he saw that they meant to cheat him that he promptly dropped the door. The door still hangs crooked in the church, and no one has ever been able to open it. To take revenge, the devil wanted to bury the town of Aken under a mountain. When the devil was walking to Aken on a hot summer's day with the mountain on his back, he met a girl and asked her: "Is Aken still far from here?" Jokingly the girl replied: "Do you see my worn-out shoes? I bought them new in Aken. That's how far it still is." The devil, who was already dead tired, gave up and dropped the mountain on the spot. The mountain lay not far from Aken, because the girl had fooled the devil when she said Aken was still far away.
184546: An elderly woman went peddling at a farmer's wife's house. When they were in the stable, the woman said to the farmer's wife: "What a beautiful cow you have in your stable!" A few days later the cow was lame. The farmer's wife suspected the woman was a witch and did not let her in any more.
184549: A man was annoyed that every day a cat sat scratching at the drain hole in the wall. One day the man chopped off one of the cat's paws with an axe. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood had her arm in a bandage.
184556: Jef went to church with a Dutchman. When a woman was walking ahead of them, the Dutchman said: "Shall I make that woman look round?" and he placed his feet crosswise on the woman's footprint. The next moment the woman looked back and said: "Will you get out of my footprints!"
184563: A drunkard returning from a visit to a pig dealer on the Oude Baan saw a strange apparition, which called: "Where must I lay it? Where must I lay it?" To this the man answered: "Damn it, just lay it where you took it from!" With that the dead man was released.
184571: On a farm the butter was bewitched and the animals were all untied. When a scapular was thrown into the cream, everything went back to normal.
184583:
Werewolves mostly jumped on women's necks.
When a man went to visit a girl the werewolf himself was in love with, that man was jumped by the werewolf so that he would go back home. Thus a man going to see his girlfriend was jumped by a werewolf in the Kruisstraat. The next time the man took a club with him to defend himself. After the man had hit the werewolf, he pulled away the sheet and saw that the werewolf was in fact an ordinary person. A werewolf often sat in the Rozenstraat too.
184599: Two men were walking on the Heibloem along a stream that flowed through the woods. Suddenly the men heard coughing, while a strange light appeared in the sky. The men kept seeing the light until they reached the end of the stream. Then the light disappeared.
184601: A woman always prayed for the will-o'-the-wisps. They were little souls still in purgatory who wanted to go to heaven. On Palm Sunday the woman had a palm sprig blessed.
184618: A witch could cover a pig in lice.
184619: In the Genatte in Bree, people secretly went to cut reeds early in the morning or late in the evening to weave baskets. It was said that witches' gatherings were often held in the Genatte. Each time the people had cut some reeds, they put them on a little pile. When they came back to the pile a while later, there was always a cat sitting on it.
184633: A werewolf had a lot of hair on his body and always had to go outside at full moon. A man and a woman who knew their son was a werewolf sent the boy to Luik to fetch coal with horse and cart. Meanwhile the parents lit the fire to burn the werewolf's skin. But the boy came back and was able to remain a werewolf.
184640: The son of the drossaard (bailiff) rode on horseback to the mill in Peer. When someone told him that his father sometimes appeared as a ghost, the young man laughed and replied: "Well, if that is so, I wish he would come right now!" The next moment a big black dog jumped onto the horse's back.
184641: In the old days the ghost of a dead woman came to haunt the churchyard in Muizen.
184642: A witch who was talking with a pigeon fancier predicted: "Your pigeons won't win a prize today!" And so it was.
184655: A man who had lost all his money walked cursing through the fields and said: "The others can do everything and I can never do anything!" A little later the man met a gentleman who asked him what was the matter. The man explained his problem and added: "I've already thought of selling my soul to the devil." The gentleman replied: "But you can do that right now, and then you'll have as much money as you like! When your time is up, I'll come and fetch you." The man agreed and sold his soul to the devil. After that the man lived in great luxury. Three days before his time was up, the devil allowed the man one more wish. The man then set the devil a task: the devil would get the man's soul on condition that he could guess the name of the animal standing in the stable. The clever man smeared his wife with syrup, stuck chicken feathers on her skin and put a collar on her. When the devil appeared at midnight, the woman was standing on all fours in the barn. Because the devil could not find the name of the animal in the stable, he vanished. A little later Satan himself appeared. Satan said: "That beast has no tail and it has an udder at the front. I don't know. You are free."
184667: In the old days people often had to carry the werewolf. It was said that there was a werewolf in the Tombos between Daalwezent and Opgrimbie.
184679: A certain Zwenne was going through the Vetwei from Neerrepen to Overrepen. By the church the man kicked at a black cat. The next moment three or four black cats appeared. When the man lashed out at the animals again, there were as many as twenty black cats. At that the man ran off as fast as he could.
184691: A young man walking through the fields with his girlfriend one Sunday met a witch from Mechelen who had come to live in Opgrimbie. The witch came closer, pinched the girl's arm and said: "Girl, what a lovely jacket you're wearing!" Not two hours later the girl urgently had to see the doctor because her arm was completely swollen. One could only protect oneself against the witch's power by striking higher than the witch.
184693: At the Lozere in Montenaken will-o'-the-wisps often appeared. Those lights led people to the marsh to make them drown. For will-o'-the-wisps were souls of the dead. Those souls could release themselves by taking a living soul.
184705: A witch came to a shoemaker to collect her repaired shoes. When the witch had to pay, she blew in the shoemaker's face until the man turned completely black and was in great pain.
184712: A man from Ketsingen was coming back from Mass when he saw a white cat sitting on a barrier in the meadow by Anneke's house. When the man tried to crawl under the barrier, the cat jumped in front of him. As soon as the man stood up, the cat was sitting on the barrier again. The cat disappeared when she saw that the man wanted to hit her.
184715: Old Pie was talking with his niece, who patted him on the shoulder. After the conversation Pie went inside, whereupon he suddenly became very restless and his face turned blue. The priest came to read prayers over Pie, but it did not help. The man only calmed down after a Redemptorist father in Sint-Truiden had read prayers over him.
184730: A man hurried to his pigeons because he still had to put rings on their legs. "You can walk fast," a witch said to the man. The next moment the man could go no further.
184733: A man from Neerheim had been to the court of justice in Maastricht. When he came outside, he could not find his walking stick. The man decided to take someone else's walking stick and have a mass said for that person. After the man had died, a rattling was always heard in the clock case of a house. As soon as a mass had been said, the man was released.
184736: A woman stroked a horse, saying: "What a beautiful horse!" The next moment the animal's mane was completely tangled.
184750: The witches held their monthly gathering in Boshoven. One day a man saw a whole troop of cats heading for Boshoven. He was convinced they were witches.
184751: A farmer's wife from Schakkebroek had a cow that had fallen ill after calving. The witch who came to visit knew everything that had happened.
184753: You should never open an umbrella in the house, for that brought seven years of bad luck. A woman had seen an umbrella move by itself.
184755: A man standing beside his horse at midnight had seen a ghost. However, he did not dare go and look.
184756: Everyone knew that Bet was a witch. The villagers who raced pigeons often went to Bet for advice. Sometimes she said: "You don't need to let them fly, because they won't come back anyway!" The pigeons then indeed came far too late. Bet could also predict when it would rain. When the witch lay on her deathbed, she could not die unless her daughter took over her arts. When someone from the village set off with his cart, Bet's daughter told him he would have trouble with his cart that day. Because that prediction came true, people were sure that the daughter had taken over Bet's arts.
184760: A man was driving a beer wagon from Diepenbeek to Vreren around midnight when he suddenly met a woman as big as a giant. A little later the woman had disappeared.
184777: Januske H. had to carry the werewolf as far as the meadows. When Januske said he would take the werewolf to the church, the animal jumped off his back.
184779: Every time Hari went poaching in the woods of Mombeek, a little rabbit came and sat in front of him. Hari had often tried to shoot the rabbit, but he had never succeeded.
184784: When Jef was coming back from Kermt in the dark, he met a woman in Kuringen who pushed him onto a field track and said: "To the right, to the right!" Suddenly the woman had vanished and the man saw a house with a light on. The man went up to the house and knocked. The door was opened by the woman who had kept saying: "To the right, to the right!" The man was bewitched.
184787: As a joke a man had gone with a white hen to the blue statue of Our Lord in Millen. The devil can't have been pleased; the hen should have been black!
184793:
When someone had bad luck, people said that person had been touched by the evil hand.
When children had 'fieflèn' (?), they were taken to Vlijtingen, where an earthworm was tied around the child's hand. As soon as the worm had dried up two or three days later, the child got well again.
184810: There were two kinds of vuurmannen (fire men). There were large ones and small ones, which were called will-o'-the-wisps. Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children.
184814: A cow could not give birth to her calf because a witch had been in the stable.
184838: A woman was going with her two sisters from Neerrepen to Riksingen. At Poes-Dries's house the women suddenly saw an escaped horse that was to have been slaughtered. The women fled and crawled under the barbed wire. The horse fell dead in front of the barbed wire.
184859: In Wellen lived a witch who had a cupboard full of little wax dolls. By pressing on the dolls, the witch could cause people pain.
184892: A woman driving to Weert one evening saw behind her a strange light that kept moving back and forth.
184896: Will-o'-the-wisps did no one any harm if they were left alone. It was said that they were the little souls of unbaptised children.
184902: At a house in Herk-de-Stad a black dog with a chain and a bell came to haunt. The dog pushed with its snout against a stone lying on the ground. Under the stone a will was found that involved a lot of money. The notary had come back to haunt in the shape of a dog. Since then the dog has not been seen again.
184917: A woman who had visited her grandmother saw a black cat sitting there on her way back. The woman wanted to hit the cat with a twig when she suddenly remembered that, according to her grandmother, black cats were sometimes witches' animals. When the woman walked on, the cat said: "Lucky for you that you thought better of it, or I would have shown you a thing or two".
184919: At the little chapel in the Rekestraat in Buvingen the witches often came to dance around a tree. People then heard music, but nobody saw anything. The next day a large circle was found around the tree, which was very often full of magpies.
184920: On the Boseind in Maasmechelen there was a werewolf. One day the werewolf's skin was found and thrown into the oven. When the skin caught fire, the werewolf was already standing by the oven.
184921: When people had borrowed something from a witch, they often got into trouble.
184925: The French hussars quartered with S. were struggling with a plague of rats. The commanding officer made all the rats crawl into a thick bundle of straw. The last rat that came running up was a very fat one. Then the straw was set on fire.
184928: The kaartridder (card knight) was playing a game of cards in the evening. When one of the players bent down to pick up a fallen card, he saw that the knight had horse's legs. It was the devil.
184940: A man who was soon to be married often stayed out late in the evening. His mother said: "Is it really necessary to stay out so long? I wish you would run into the werewolf! Then you'll come home earlier next time!" People believed a werewolf roamed the Sintelseberg in Lanaken. When the man came home one evening around midnight by moonlight, he saw something hairy lying in a ditch on the Sintelseberg. When the man walked past the ditch, the dog suddenly jumped barking onto the road. Because the man did not react, the dog calmed down again a little later.
184946: A man whose wife was in childbed made sure that the sister of the village witch could not get to his wife. The witch's sister was even willing to give the man a pound of butter if she could go and see the newborn baby.
184949: In Gelinden lived a maid whose family was bewitched. Many of the children had died after being bewitched. When one day the father was called to help a cow calve, he first took his horses to the stables because he had seen the witch standing a little further on.
184957: A boy out walking with his girlfriend said on the way: "I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you in the meantime, throw my handkerchief at the beast." The girl did as her boyfriend had advised. When the boy came back, the girl found that he had a piece of the handkerchief between his teeth.
184964: A woman always took a detour because she did not want to pass the Bonderkuil. For there wandered the ghosts of the bokkenrijders (goat riders, gangs of robbers said to ride goats through the air) who had been burned there.
184966: The chapel that stood in Sint Ool sank into the ground. It was said that the bell rang twelve times from under the ground on Christmas night. Crazy Jan once went to that place on Christmas night. When he came back he would not tell what he had experienced, but he never wanted to go there again.
184967: A werewolf was a man who dealt with the devil. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he took on his human form again and you could recognise him.
184979: A witch had said to a woman: "I curse you. The worms will crawl through your belly and devour you." The woman died of pain in her bowels.
184995: A man who worked at the mill always came along a narrow path by the Jeker. Because a werewolf wandered along that path, the man's sisters went with their brother one day. Although they had a knife with them, the women ran off in fear when they saw how big the dog was.
184997: A man walking through an alley at night saw a woman in a white dress. When the man told his friends about it, they said: "If we see her again, we will go up to her." But they never dared.
185000: Near the castle of Wideux lay a felled oak where the deceased count came to haunt. Three times people tried to move the oak. Each time, the next day the tree lay back in its usual place.
185013: A young man who cycled home between midnight and one o'clock always met fifteen cats that blocked his way. An old witch lived in the neighbourhood.
185025: A baby had died after being bewitched.
185034: A man in Herderen who was going to the doctor was attacked by the werewolf on a back road. When he got home, the man fainted from fear. When the werewolf's skin had been found, it was thrown into the oven. At that moment the werewolf stood by the oven to save his skin. That is how people found out who the werewolf was.
185048: A hunter had shot a fine hare. He put the dead animal in his game bag and went home. When the man wanted to show his catch to the people, they all laughed at him: the game bag contained only some sand.
185056:
Betje visited her friend Annemie from time to time. One day Betje took Annemie's baby out of the cradle to admire it. Some time later, however, the child fell ill. The child could no longer walk and lost its fingernails and toenails. No doctor's treatment or pilgrimage could help the child. Because Betje had not visited for a year, Annemie decided to go and see her herself with the child. Annemie carried the child on her back and said to Betje: "Take the child off my back for a moment, so I can put it on my lap."
Betje never showed herself in Annemie's house again. The child's father was so furious that he had wanted to burn Betje in the barn on a pile of brushwood bundles.
The child died at the age of seven.
185059: A witch from Martenslinde had bewitched the cows on a farm. The animals stood with their hind legs in the air and laid their heads in the manger. After the parish priest had made a cross on the stairs, a good hundred cats appeared on the roof. Then the priest made a cross on the stable door. After that everything returned to normal.
185068: Anyone touched by a witch fell ill or got lice. Children, too, were often the victims of witches' torments.
185071: One day a farmer's wife had seen a little bird sitting on one of the cows in the stable. Strangely enough, the cow was dead the next day. When four cows had already died, the farmer's wife told a visitor about her problem. The man then said: "You must catch the little bird, because it is a witch. You must burn off the animal's feathers and then let it fly. Then you must put a blessed candle under the threshold, because another witch will come by. If she says anything, you must answer: 'Come on in'." The woman did what the man had advised. The next day a woman came by who said: "You should be ashamed to burn such a little bird alive!" The farmer's wife then said: "Come on in quickly!" The woman answered: "First you must take that thing away from under your threshold. Only then will I come in."
185080: Marie G. had beautiful peaches in her orchard, but she refused to give away even a small share of the fruit. Although the fruit was not yet ripe, two men secretly went one evening to fill a basket with peaches. The next day, however, the peaches were rotten.
185085: A farmer could no longer make butter because a witch had come in. When the farmer opened the butter churn, he saw it was full of chaff.
185102: Around the Dameruskapel a black coach with two black horses always drove. Although no one sat in the coach, someone was nevertheless holding the reins.
185105: A man coming back from the shoemaker in Klein-Spouwen around midnight met an enormous woman dressed entirely in black. The man said "good evening", but the woman did not answer and walked on.
185109: A man who was going to have a millstone sharpened was attacked by cats near a small chapel. People believed the cats were witches.
185123: In the Biesterd (1) a man saw a cat sitting on a turnstile. After the man had struck the cat to the ground, suddenly there were two cats. In the end there were so many cats that the man could not get through. Frightened, he cried out: "Oh dear Lord, let me get home safe and sound!" The next moment all the cats had vanished.
185128: At the Bemmertmolen worked a farmhand who changed himself into a dog whenever the police were after him.
185132: A girl from Berg was walking home one evening when she suddenly met a dog. The girl threw her handkerchief at the dog and walked on. The next day the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
185135: In Sluizen lived a little woman who was said to be a witch. A brave man who was going to slaughter a pig said: "Grietje K. may give me a hunchback, but I'll drink from her glass!"
185149: A beggar woman had touched a baby in a house in Wezent. When the beggar woman had gone, the child became paralysed. People believed the child was bewitched.
185156: A man out walking with a friend was getting ready to shoot at a bird sitting in a tree. At that moment the friend said: "Stop, that's my wife!"
185161: A young man who was going to the fair with his brother at around eight o'clock was startled on the way by a strange noise. It sounded as if an elephant were walking behind the hedge. But there was nothing to be seen. When the two came back around midnight, it was raining and blowing hard. At the spot where they had heard the strange noise a few hours earlier, the boys saw a crumpled piece of paper lying on the road. As they walked past it, the paper struck against their heels.
185164: A shepherd who worked on his grandfather's farm owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. When the collar had been thrown into the oven, the shepherd lost his powers.
185198: In D.V.'s meadow opposite Zjang V.N. stood an empty house that was haunted. When Jan V. was coming back from Tongeren, he saw a cat come out of that house. Jan said to the animal: "Dear pussycat, you're out late!" The next moment a hundred cats appeared, formed a circle around the terrified man and sang: "Jan V., where do you come from? Little pussycat, what are you doing with him?" When Jan V. reached the church, he threw his cap on the ground to call on God on his knees. At that the cats vanished at once.
185201: A woman in childbed was visited by a witch who came to borrow an apron. "I don't have an apron," said the woman, to which the witch replied: "Yes you do, you have one more in the cupboard." The woman then said: "Yes, but you're not getting it!" The woman gave the witch a handful of coffee beans and said: "Make a cup of coffee when the children come home from school." The coffee was so hot that the children could not hold the cups.
185213: Two women coming back from the churchyard saw nothing but mice running in front of them.
185221: A deceased land surveyor from Vreren came back to haunt after his death. Because the man had always measured land wrongly, he now walked about with a boundary post in his hands, calling: "Where must I put it?" One day a drunkard answered: "Just hurry and put the post where you took it from!"
185224: At Hostaard a canon had been banished to a hazel bush. V., who had had to lead the ghost there, had looked back against his better judgement. When he came home, he was deathly pale.
185240: Because it had been a warm summer, there was a lot of fruit on the trees in Weert. A witch, however, could not bear that the Nies family had so much fruit. One day a strong wind began to blow, so that all the fruit fell from the trees. On the other side of Weert there had been no wind at all.
185247: One evening Gust R. went to the fair with his girlfriend and her sister. Suddenly the girls had vanished and Gust saw two cats walking.
185256: A man who suffered from severe headaches could not be helped by any doctor. In the end the man went to a father at Achel, who gave him a relic and advised him not to let a certain woman into the house any more. Since then the man has had no more headaches.
185258: A man had had to carry the werewolf until he got home.
185276: Kludde leapt onto people's necks and then made them carry him.
185284: André G.'s parents had been looking for their little son all day, but they could not find him anywhere. When the boy came home in the evening, he had a swelling. He had probably spent the whole day in a witch's house.
185285: A farmhand who worked for a farmer had strange powers. On his own the farmhand could load the cart full of manure and pull it outside. People knew, however, that the farmhand was a werewolf. He had a collar from the devil. When the farmhand sat down on a tree stump and put on the collar, he turned into a werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent away so that people had the chance to burn his collar. The moment the collar had been thrown into the oven, the farmhand immediately came running to save it. When the collar had burnt up completely, the farmhand said with relief: "Now I am at peace, for now I am released."
185300: Some friends went out on a Sunday evening in Kwaadmechelen. When the boys were saying a mock Mass as a joke in an inn, there was suddenly a knock at the door. A black dog came in and lay down under the table. Because the dog would not leave the inn, the priest of Kwaadmechelen was sent for. After long prayer the dog finally went outside. Some time later the joker who had said the Mass in the inn had to fetch the midwife for his pregnant wife. On the way the man was pelted with stones. Because complications arose during the birth, the men had to fetch the doctor in Tessenderlo. At 't Folderke in Genendijk the men met four people without heads. When the men brought Doctor C. to the pregnant woman, they were hindered by all kinds of strange apparitions. The woman's child was stillborn.
185302: The witch Tin K. said to a man: "If you touch that stone, you'll break your arm!" And so it happened.
185306: In Piringen a strange man always drove around in the evening in a coach with six horses. When anyone asked the man something, he answered: "The night is for me." People believed that this man was the devil.
185321: An old woman who was said to be a witch wanted to come and look in someone's stable. The next morning all the animals stood with their rumps against the wall. The animals would not move anymore.
185325: The fire-man looked like a bundle of straw standing burning in the field.
185327: In Gestel a dove sat on the roof that nobody could hit. The dove was the witch V.
185331: A man walking past the churchyard got a great fright when a dead man suddenly jumped on his back. After the man had carried the dead man for a while, the ghost disappeared again.
185333: A farmer went with some farmhands to have grain ground at the Lauw mill. As they passed a meadow, they heard cats and dogs screeching. The horse suddenly stood still. One of the farmhands suggested fetching an extra horse in Lauw, but the others knew that was pointless when witches were involved. So they struck the axle of the wheel hard while letting the horse pull. Suddenly the animal started moving again.
185348: A man on his way to eleven o'clock mass saw on the heath of Spikelspaai a big dog running full speed down the hill. When he reached the bottom, the man met a gentleman who asked: "Could I still make it to eleven o'clock mass in time?", to which the man replied: "If you run like you did just now, you will!" That gentleman was a werewolf.
185353: One day Toon V.D.B. hit a cat with a stick. When the man came home, he was arrested by the police because he had supposedly beaten up his neighbour woman. After the man had explained everything, he was released after all.
185357: A boy going to the fair with his girlfriend said: "I have to relieve myself. If anything comes at you in the meantime, throw this handkerchief at the apparition." A little later a dog did indeed come running up and tore the handkerchief to shreds. When the boy came back, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
185361: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field ended up in a corner of hell after his death. The dead man had to come back to put the boundary post in the right place again.
185383: In the marshy meadows of the Laker vin bells were heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night.
185396: Some women were talking while they were cooking sausages. Suddenly the sausages flew out of the pot and floated up the chimney. The sausages were bewitched.
185398: A boy struck a werewolf with a stick. Because the werewolf began to bleed, he was freed.
185414: A house in Stamprooi was haunted. Between midnight and one o'clock, chains could always be heard rattling.
185415: Will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in churchyards. In fact it was the vapour of the corpses rising from the ground.
185419: At midnight Zjang came home from his work at the dairy in Langerlo. At the stroke of twelve Zjang saw a black cat sitting on the churchyard wall. It was the ghost of a dead person buried there. The gamekeeper had tried several times to shoot the cat, but he never succeeded.
185420:
In a meadow in 's Heerenelderen, close to the road to Mopertingen, there was a pit called the Duivelsput. Because the church of Tongeren had sunk into that pit, the bells were heard ringing there every year on Christmas night. Anyone who came too close to the pit was pulled in.
A poacher who did not know it was Christmas night came near the Duivelsput when suddenly the bells began to ring and two little black men with big eyes and a big mouth came out of the woods. The poacher quickly fired his gun and made himself scarce.
185434: In Vorst there was a house that was bewitched. At night the cows were untied or the chickens flew off their perch. One night the attic was full of cats sitting and watching. When Jo went to the fathers of Tongerlo, he received a holy relic, after which the witch could no longer get in.
185437: Witches often came to dance in Mal. Two witch cats danced with each other.
185440: In Berlingen there lived a man who had moved a boundary post. After his death the man came back to haunt with a boundary post on his shoulder, calling: "Where must I put it? Where must I put it?" When someone said: "Put it back where you took it from!", the ghost was released.
185460: In Vrullingen near Wellen a boy went to the fair with his girlfriend. On the way the boy suddenly said: "You go on; I'll catch up with you! If you meet a dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." When the girl met a dog a little later, she did as her boyfriend had advised. A little later the boy came back. The girl saw that the threads of the handkerchief were still hanging between his teeth.
185465: Old Willem, who slept at night in the horses' feed stable, was often ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit). The horses would then start rearing in their stable. The man felt very tight in the chest and could no longer move. When the man slept on his side, he was never troubled by the maar.
185467: A seamstress who was working in 's Heerenelderen did not dare go home in the evening because the road she had to take was haunted.
185476: A witch bent over a baby's cradle and gave it a kiss. When the witch had gone, the cradle was full of nasty little creatures.
185489: A werewolf was sent away so that his band could be burnt in the meantime. The next moment, however, the werewolf was already standing by the oven to save his band. To wipe out the werewolves, the Angelus was introduced.
185495: Anyone ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night could not get up.
185496: A priest came haunting in the woods of the Wolfskuil.
185498: In Corswarem lived a dangerous witch who had been recognised by her hairy feet.
185501:
In the old days people sometimes had to carry the werewolf.
To frighten children, they were also often told about the werewolf.
185516: When Rikus was attacked by a werewolf, he wounded the beast. As soon as the werewolf began to bleed, he changed back into a human.
185525: A little child who could not sleep at night was prayed over by the Crosiers. In the child's pillow a wreath was found. An old woman from the neighbourhood never slept between midnight and one o'clock.
185528: A girl who went walking with her sister's child had been advised by her mother to stay away from the daughter of a witch in the neighbourhood. When that daughter lay dying, the fathers of Hasselt came in a horse-drawn carriage. At the moment the witch died, a black crow sat on the roof of her house.
185539: Joske could not die because he had something on his conscience. Just before his death the man said to his children: "Keep what you have; I will suffer what I can." When the man had died, he came haunting in the woods in the shape of a black hen. The hen cried the whole time: "Give it back, give it back!"
185541: Where the Duivelsput now is, heathen Tongeren used to lie. On Christmas night at midnight bells were heard ringing in the pit. A temple sank into the Duivelsput.
185542: A shepherd from Wellen could not manage to cover a well. After two days the lid had always disappeared. In the well stood a chest with a black dog sitting on it. When people tried to haul the chest up, the dog jumped away, after which the chest sank back into the well.
185558: Some men returning from Halen saw a pretty little cat in an avenue of oaks. Louis knocked the cat away with a stick. The cat did not cry out, and a little further on it was following the men again. Another man tried to stab the cat with a knife, but he missed. Charel V., who had a medlar stick in his hand, did not manage to hit the animal either. The cat followed Charel all the way into his house. Although Charel had shut the door, the cat had vanished by the next morning.
185563: In Diepenbeek there lived a witch who had a mark on her face. The witch was jealous because young Fik looked healthier than her own son. When Fik was eleven, the witch came to visit him. She pressed the mark on her face against the boy and so brought him under the influence of evil. From then on Fik always had bad luck. He became disabled in one leg, and when he was twenty he caught a severe pneumonia.
185564: A woman who could not make butter was given two medals by the friars of Hasselt to put under the threshold and in the stable. Because of this the witch could no longer come in. A week later the woman could churn butter again.
185571: The churchyard was haunted. A black dog and someone with a sheet over their head often appeared there.
185579: A farmer out for a walk met a woman who lived between Budel and Hamont. The woman asked the farmer for matches, but unfortunately the farmer had none to give her. At that the woman grew angry and cried: "I'll get you yet!" When the farmer got home, one of his best cows was dead.
185591: If a black cat crossed the street in front of you, you would have bad luck. Moreover, black cats were said to turn into witches at night.
185620: After his death a thief came back to haunt with the words: "I can't hold it any longer, I can't hold it any longer!" To this someone answered: "Put it back where you took it from. If you don't do it, I will." With that the ghost was released.
185622: Because L. came haunting in Bilzen, two friars were sent for to lead the ghost away on a rope and banish it.
185636: A man worked at the mill between Opgrimbie and Borsem. One day the miller's son said to the man: "When you go to Opgrimbie, you must not stop at the smith's. Even if they call you, you must keep going." Once before, the man had stopped because a woman with a stick had called to him. The man had to take a sack of wheat for the woman and have it ground. When the man wanted to leave again, the horse could go no further. The animal stood on three legs. Because the horse could no longer walk, the man took it home and fetched another horse to pull the cart. A vet from Opgrimbie did not know what to do with the injured horse. A few days later someone came by who wanted to buy a heifer in calf. When the buyer saw the injured horse, he walked up to the animal, made a few signs of the cross over its leg, said a prayer and then said: "The horse will be ill for another three days or so, but after that it will walk normally again. Just put it in the stable, because in the meadow it is far too cold at night." Three days later the horse was indeed cured. The smith's wife had bewitched the animal.
185648: In the evening as many as twenty mewing cats sat at the tram stop. One was not allowed to kick the animals, or one would be attacked. For those cats were witches.
185654: In Geleen (NL) there lived a woman who had lost as many as seventeen or eighteen animals. Her little son had been lying in bed deathly ill for a long time. When the child's mother went on pilgrimage to Tongeren, the friar gave her relics that she was to hang above all the doors. But the friar had said: "The boy will die. When he has died, you must cut open the pillow he sleeps on." In the pillow the mother found lots of little roses. On the friar's advice the roses were burned. The friar had also said: "The woman responsible for this lives near you. She will come by once more to borrow a loaf of bread, and after that you will not see her again." And so it happened. The mother never dared tell her husband what had really happened, because then he would have killed the witch.
185674: A man had spied on a witch as she left for the wine cellar in Leuven. Because the man also wanted to go to that wine cellar, he copied the witch. But he made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said "Through hedges and hawthorns" instead of "Over hedges and hawthorns". The man arrived at his destination badly injured.
185678: In the field, a barrel rolled across the ground.
185680: A coachman from Houthem in the Netherlands had had to take some people to a party in Maastricht. As he drove home through a valley, the horses suddenly stopped. The man got out to see what was wrong. In front of the horses lay a strange black sheep with eyes as big as saucers. When the sheep saw the coachman, it immediately disappeared behind the carriage. After that the horses could go on again.
185681: After his death mayor K. from Eksel came to haunt the churchyard in the shape of a big dog holding a burning torch in its mouth. In this way the dead man wanted to let people know that they had to pray for him.
185684: A boy threw a stone at a black cat that always roamed around near the farm. When Nel S. came to fetch milk a few days later, she wore a cloth around her head. That proved that Nel S. really was a witch.
185686: On a farm there worked a farmhand who had had to carry the werewolf as many as twenty-five times. The werewolf always grew heavier and heavier, until one could no longer stay on one's feet. The werewolf looked like a big black dog, but in reality it was a human. For if one could wound a werewolf, one could recognise him the next day.
185702: When Rikus V.H. was going to Maastricht, he saw something black lying near the Kwattel. It was the skin of a werewolf.
185703: One must never strike at a cat.
185707: In Loon, Jan bought a cow from the old mayor. The milk of that cow foamed so badly that Jan could not make butter from it. An old woman regularly came by Jan's to get whey and cheese. Jan was always very kind to Finneke, but one day he could not spare any milk because the cow had calves. When the calves had been sold, the old woman came by again. Jan said to her: "Finneke, we have had a lot of bad luck. We can't make butter from our milk. It would be good if you went to Mass once in honour of Our Lady of Gotem." Finneke answered: "If it's up to me, you will soon be able to make butter." The next day Jan was working in the field when Finneke suddenly came to call him: she had managed to make butter, and all the foam stored in the cellar had turned into butter too.
185711: A little child had stroked a kitten's head, even though the mother had advised against it. A while later, however, the child fell ill. After the friars of Rekem had read prayers over the child, it became healthy again.
185723:
A witch had visited a woman with a little child. "What a lovely child!" the witch had said, and she stroked the child's head. When the witch had gone, the child began to cry. Among the child's cloths the mother found lots of spiders. "That ugly witch was here today, because today is the good Monday," said the mother. Whenever one mentioned a witch's name, one always had to add: "because today is the good ...day", or else one would fall under the influence of the evil hand.
If one went somewhere late in the evening, one had to cross the cart track crosswise. If the washing had been left outside until after sunset, it had to be rinsed with clean water so as not to be bewitched, according to the parish priest. The ringing of the bells in the morning, at noon and in the evening, also called the Angelus, was meant to root out the evil floating through the air.
185727: Some children playing in the barn could make mice. After the children had been baptised, they could no longer do it.
185730: A boy who had not yet been a soldier forgot one day to make the sign of the cross. "Now you're in for it, little man!" said a witch. And indeed the boy was drawn in the conscription lottery.
185734: At midnight, the procession of Averbode passed through the barn of the 'kleine hoef' (little farm) in Tessenderlo.
185736: When the sexton was going to Meeuwen, he saw on the way a ghostly figure holding out a hand to him. The sexton threw two francs to the ghost. The next day, however, the money was still lying in the same place.
185749: A farmer had a farmhand who was a werewolf. One day the farmer sent his farmhand away and took the boy's collar out of a hollow tree stump. When the farmer was about to throw the collar into the oven, the farmhand was instantly standing beside him, because he wanted to get the collar out of the fire.
185750: A musician coming home through the woods at night with his brother and his wife got lost. Only around five in the morning was the man found in the gravel pit in Neerharen. The witch Kait had led the man astray.
185756: A man coming back from the village had to pass a barrier on which a black cat was sitting. After the man had knocked the cat down, the animal jumped back onto the barrier and said: "Knock me off again!" At that the man quickly ran away.
185762: One evening a boy had been to a party with his girlfriend. Because the boy had not danced with his girlfriend, the girl's mother cried angrily: "I'll get him yet!" When the boy went home, a ghost walked beside him the whole time, which no one else could see. After people had prayed, the boy was freed from the ghost. The girl's mother was a witch.
185763: A man was always followed by a dog when he went to visit his girlfriend Trieneke V.B. After a while the man no longer even dared to go to his girlfriend.
185765: A man driving to Meeuwen met a cat on the way, which jumped onto the tail of the cart. On the way back the cat jumped off the cart at the same spot.
185768: Some men were walking on the Flikkeberg between Lauw and Thys. They had been to Wouteringen because one of them had toothache. In Wouteringen there lived a man who could sell someone's toothache to a ghost, so that the patient was freed of the pain. The man knew at once which tooth it was, without anyone telling him. When the group came back, they heard a strange noise on the Flikkeberg. The men stood still, because otherwise the witches would come at them and make them ill.
185771: On the Kommer in Henis a woman with a bouquet of flowers walked every night. Some men in the inn were talking about the strange apparition when one of them said: "When I see that woman, I'll take her bouquet of flowers from her." Some time later a woman from the inn went walking on the Kommer with a bouquet of flowers. The boastful man took her flowers from her and afterwards got a blow on the head. From then on no one dared to go to the Kommer any more.
185797: After his death a farmer came back to haunt near a boundary post that stood on his field. After the people had moved the boundary post, they did not see the ghost again.
185807: A man walking home along the old canal around midnight met a dog and said: "Hey, Pol", convinced the animal was his own dog. When he realised he had not brought his dog that time, he struck at the strange animal with a club. But he did not manage to hit the dog. Before he dared strike a third time, the man ran home quickly.
185813: A girl said to her boyfriend: "If you meet some beast or other at night, throw my handkerchief at the animal." When the boy met a werewolf one evening, he did as he had been advised. The next morning the boy saw that his girlfriend still had the red threads of the handkerchief between her teeth.
185814: After a man had knocked a black cat off a gate, the gate was completely covered with black cats.
185815: In the Otterbamd people used to hear a bell ringing that lay under the ground. On Christmas night many people came to the Otterbamd to hear the bell ring at exactly twelve o'clock.
185816: In Genk there lived two women who were always quarrelling. One woman owned a stable with animals, while the other had nothing at all. When one of the animals died, the one woman accused the other of being a witch.
185829: A farmer whose cows were all falling ill went to the parish priest for advice. The priest came to the stable and laid a blanket over the sick cow. The next morning the blanket lay folded in the manger. The priest then advised the farmer to block up all the holes in the stable. After that the evil hand could no longer make the cows ill.
185834: Jef and Gust always saw a haystack floating through the air near Jef V.T.'s place.
185848: In Hoelbeek there lived a witch who conjured mice out of wax in the church. When the witch pulled the mice by the tail, the animals vanished at once.
185879: On the day before Epiphany, the wife of farmer B. from Maastricht said: "If only our son were here now!" The farmhand replied: "I'll see to it that your son is here at midnight, on condition that you give me the black mare." But nobody knew that the farmhand was a werewolf who consorted with the devil. On the black horse the farmhand flew to Sint-Truiden. When he came back with the son, the son struck the church tower of Herderen with his foot. On the stroke of twelve they arrived in Maastricht. The next day the farmhand was dismissed on the spot because it had been discovered that he was a werewolf.
185888: A farmer's bewitched cows could not bring a single calf into the world. In the past, children were not allowed out on the street for fear of witches.
185894: A farmhand working in the stable was nearly frightened to death when a crow suddenly flew in. It was the ghost of the late farmer.
185896: The son of Gieleke, who lived on the Kwakkel, saw his dead aunt come haunting and sit on his bed. When the boy had asked the ghost what it wanted, he went on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. On setting out he had to say: "Whoever wants to come along must just follow." Otherwise he would have had to carry the ghost the whole way.
185900:
Strange things happened in the stable of a farmer in Zepperen. Several times the animals stood in the morning with their chains tangled together, or with their tails tied to each other. Sometimes the animals were drenched in sweat for no reason. At his wits' end, the farmer sent for a certain Koe-Jan to solve the problems.
Everyone living on the farm had to go to bed except the farmer, who had to accompany Koe-Jan to the stable. Koe-Jan made a big fire and began to read from a book. Suddenly someone knocked on the stable door. The farmer wanted to open it, but Koe-Jan forbade him. When there was a knock for the third time, the farmer was allowed to open. The witch came in, rubbing her hands: "How cold it is, master!" Koe-Jan did not allow her to warm her hands at the fire and ordered: "Now you will undo all the evil you have done here, or else I will have you burned alive!" The witch was glad her life was spared and did what was asked. From then on no more strange things happened in the stable.
185904: When Tijs H. worked as a farmhand in 's Heerenelderen, he often saw a dog with a chain around its neck. One evening Tijs was walking home. At the Lange-Lieven-Heer stood a turnstile behind which the dog with the chain sat. Tijs said to the animal: "I'll teach you a lesson. Now it's time for you to go." Tijs took his stick and stroked the animal's flanks with the words: "In the name of God." But the dog was not afraid and calmly walked on.
185926: In Riksingen a little child was bewitched. Because the doctor did not know what to do, the parents sent for Garenmarie, the mistress of the witches. Garenmarie had the child's parents open the windows. A few moments later the witch who had made the child ill appeared. Garenmarie said to the witch: "If you do not cure that child, you will die!" Eight days later the little girl was freed from the evil hand.
185928: A witch from Nieuwerkerken made everything in a house fall to the floor.
185933:
A werewolf was a man who was possessed and threw an animal skin over himself.
Wullem L. once had to carry a werewolf.
185949: On Niesteke's farm the horses never lived longer than a few days. While the friars came to pray over the stable, everyone had to stay indoors. At midnight all the windows and doors suddenly flew open and more than a thousand horses were running around. From then on Niesteke had no more misfortune.
185951: Some men from Koninksem went to fetch the midwife from Rutten. The midwife was followed by a cat the whole time. When the men wanted to kick the cat, the midwife said: "No, keep your hands off it!" When the midwife was standing by the childbed a little later, the cat was sitting on the windowsill. The midwife then opened the window and shouted: "Away from here!" The next moment the cat had vanished.
185961: A man had often been to Maastricht with his sick wife. Even before the man had crossed the bridge in Vucht, his horse would start foaming at the mouth. In the evening the sick woman always saw a cat sitting on the edge of her bed. Strangely, nobody else could see the cat. When the woman had died, a wreath was found in her bed in which every existing flower had been worked. The friar of Urmond advised the man to burn the bed. The woman who came to watch the scene would be the witch. While the man was burning the bed, his own mother came walking up. Because the man raised his dung fork at his mother, the spell of the witch was broken.
185970: Some people stood talking in a circle when the holiest among them suddenly saw the devil appear in the shape of a black dog. When a boy came walking up, the dog suddenly vanished. The holy man then thought: "That must be a good boy." But Our Lord let him know that the devil was no longer needed there, because that boy was the biggest gossip there ever was.
185982: At a crossroads in a wood in Kerkhoven a priest had had a crucifix put up. At that spot two men used to haunt, counting gold coins at a little table. "That is mine, that is yours, but who is the rest for?" they said every time. A man who had often watched this same scene said one day: "The rest is for me, damn it!" The next moment the ghosts had vanished. Later a young man built a house at that crossroads. He took away the figure of Christ to put it in the front wall of his house. A week later the man died in an accident.
185988: A man out walking met a woman who asked him the way. When the woman had passed, the man was covered in lice.
185992: In Nerem, near R.'s factory, people had tied a witch to a tree. Everyone from the neighbourhood helped bring bundles of brushwood to lay around the tree. As soon as enough brushwood had been gathered, the fire was lit. When the fire had been burning for half a day, the witch, strangely enough, was still standing unharmed beside the tree.
186011: In the Rozestraat behind the Minderbroederskerk a white rabbit always sat at night. When someone grabbed the rabbit, it turned into a stone.
186014: When S. came back from the pub, he often saw will-o'-the-wisps floating by the water. People believed these lights were the little souls of unbaptised children. One day the man baptised a will-o'-the-wisp with the words: "I baptise you in the name of the Father and the Son". Because with those words the man baptised only one light, the next moment nearly all the lights came at him.
186017: A man who had fallen asleep under an oak was frightened to death when he woke up on the back of a bokkerijder (goat rider, a robber said to ride a flying goat in league with the devil) flying through the air. Suddenly the man felt a sharp pain in his leg. The bokkerijder told the man it was his own fault; he had not pulled his leg up high enough.
186026: At Fons H.'s place on the Rode Hei a witch always appeared at midnight, which made the cows raise a hellish racket. Jef managed to shoot the witch dead when she appeared in the form of a cat.
186034: When the witches wanted to fly to Aachen, they spoke the following magic formula: "Over hedge and wood to Aachen". But a new witch made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and wood to Aachen".
186035: The witch Mitteke had covered a farmer's new heifer in lice. After the witch, on the farmer's orders, had stroked the cow with her hand, the animal was rid of the lice.
186052: In the Wolvenven bells can sometimes still be heard ringing. The sunken bells probably hung in a small chapel that once stood there.
186054: Whoever had to fetch the midwife never went alone. For people going to the midwife were always harassed on the way by a black dog. That was the devil, who wanted to get the baby into his power.
186064: The village of Sint Ool (Dorne) was named after Saint Odilia. In the past there was a small church in Sint Ool. A knight wanted to marry a Dutch noblewoman in the little church of Sint Ool. Because the lady was the daughter of a witch, she stayed at the back of the church during the wedding ceremony. Suddenly the church collapsed completely. The priest who had led the wedding ceremony came haunting after his death at the place where the church lay underground. Since then, every year on Christmas night at exactly twelve o'clock, the bell could be heard ringing from under the ground.
186089: A poacher who could not manage to hit a hare put some ash from the censer into his gun. When the poacher had shot the hare, a woman was wounded.
186092: In Millen a woman of the K. family visited people who had a small child. Because the woman had held the little girl, the poor child had become lame. The child cried all the time. In the end the father had the witch come back and said: "You must undo the evil you have done here. If you don't, I'll split your head in two." At that the witch made the child healthy again.
186101: A child who had been touched by a certain woman from Gessel was covered in lice the next moment.
186115: When a woman from the village was pregnant, she fell seriously ill. Even the doctor had given up all hope. A group of women from the Leuren (Tongeren) decided to go and pray for the woman in church for nine consecutive days. After the novena a turtle dove was placed on the woman's belly. If the dove died, Lutgarde would live, but otherwise not. The little dove died on the woman's belly. After a while the woman recovered.
186116: A mother from Waltwilder found it strange that her children were full of lice and were getting very thin. A woman often came to visit who would pat the children on the shoulder. When the mother mentioned this to a man one day, he replied: "Oh, that's not so bad. That woman is a witch. If she pats your shoulder again, you must hit her on the head. Then the witch has no more power, because she cannot strike higher. I will also give you something to hang above the door. Then the witch will no longer be able to come in." When the mother had done so, the woman indeed could no longer come in. Indignantly she said: "You must think I'm a witch!", to which the mother replied: "You must undo the evil you have done here!" After that the children became perfectly healthy again.
186118: A man tried twice to strike at a cat sitting on the road. When the man made a third attempt, the cat said: "Strike again!"
186119: On the heath in Genk lived a woman with her daughter. The daughter had a suitor whose friends often said: "Do you know what you're doing? Her mother is a witch!", to which the boy would reply: "Yes, I know what I'm doing." Still, the boy had grown somewhat suspicious from his friends' questions, and he wanted to find out whether the girl's mother really was a witch. The next Sunday the boy pretended to be blind drunk and knocked at the girl's door. Inside he dropped onto a chair and pretended to have fallen asleep. After a while he heard the mother say to her daughter: "It's time for us to go", and she climbed onto a chair by the chimney. With her hand she took a little pot from the chimney breast and rubbed its contents first on herself and then on her daughter. The boy watched all this out of the corner of his eye. The mother came to stand beside the boy and listened to his breathing: "He's sleeping so soundly that we can surely go for three hours." Then mother and daughter said together: "May the devil carry us over hedge and bush to the wine cellar in Cologne." With that the two flew off up the chimney. When the mother and the girl were gone, the boy's mouth began to water at the thought of that wine cellar too. Just as he had seen the two women do, he rubbed himself with the grease. But he had not remembered the words properly, for he said: "May the devil carry me through hedge and bush to the wine cellar in Cologne." At once the devil seized the boy and dragged him through hedges, bushes and thorns to Cologne. When the boy arrived there, he was covered in blood. The girl's mother was very angry when she saw the boy in Cologne. To punish him for his curiosity she changed his arms into two cow's legs. The Black Fathers had to bring the boy back home, for he could no longer manage on his own. But he had to learn to live with the cow's legs.
186121: A man who worked in the quarry of Weert was coming back from an evening of drinking gin. The man, who had just boasted to his friends that he wasn't afraid of witches' animals, met a black kitten on the way. The man said: "Why, pussycat, why are you sitting there like that?", to which the cat replied: "Drunkard, what are you asking me now?"
186138: A man going from Roy to Tongerlo at night suddenly saw a strange animal leap onto the road near K.'s house. The man said jokingly: "Won't you come home with me?" The animal stared at him strangely with eyes that seemed to be of fire. The man grew afraid and struck at the animal with a stick, saying: "In God's name!" The animal moved on, but a little further it stood looking at the man again. The man ran home as fast as he could.
186143: When a dead person came back, it was a sign that he had not kept a promise. In Schakkebroek a ghost came to lie on a split door.
186155: One was not allowed to look at will-o'-the-wisps, because then one could get lost. People were often lured to the water because the will-o'-the-wisps wanted to be baptised.
186164: A sorcerer could walk through water without getting wet. He could also make white mice from some mud. The sorcerer left the village after the priest had warned the people about him.
186166: A woman going from Sint-Huibrechts-Lille to the Bemmertmolen met a little old woman on the way who said: "You'll get lost! Shall I come with you?" The woman answered: "No, there's no need, I've walked that road a hundred times." But she had gone less than a hundred metres when she lost all sense of direction. Because the woman got hopelessly lost, she had to be taken home in the end.
186167:
Witchcraft has to do with a kind of allergy.

Example 1:
A man who often came to fetch flour from the miller always behaved strangely. While waiting for the flour, he would turn round and, with his arms crossed, watch the canal where a bridge was being built. One day the man said: "Miller, I wonder who they'll carry across that bridge first", to which the miller replied: "Lewie, you mustn't think too much about such things. That's not good". As soon as the bridge was finished, Lewie was the first to be carried across it.

Example 2:
François B. had to carry the stones for the building of the new cemetery in Hasselt. During that work François always laughed himself silly. When the cemetery was finished, François was the first to be buried there.
186173: The brewer's farmhand had to take a beer cart to Meeuwen. On the way the farmhand came across a little kitten. When the farmhand had kicked at the cat, the animal suddenly grew bigger and bigger. The farmhand kicked a second time, after which the cat grew bigger again. Just as the farmhand was about to kick for the third time, he heard the kitten say: "Now kick once more!" The farmhand no longer dared.
186191: A man who had gone to bring in the harvest came across a cat on the way home. The man kicked at the cat, whereupon the animal suddenly grew bigger. When the man kicked a second time, the animal grew bigger still. At that the man became so frightened that he quickly took to his heels.
186201: A woman who went sewing in Hees was always accompanied by a dog as far as Vlijtingen. That was a werewolf.
186210: In Piringen there lived a witch who sometimes came to ask if she could weigh a baby. In this way she could get the child in her power. Many people did not know the woman was a witch. Those who did know dared not refuse her anything.
186216: In Zonhoven a dead woman appeared who had promised something to Our Lady of Scherpenheuvel. The children had to pray for the woman and go to Scherpenheuvel for her. At a certain moment the woman came to tell the children that they had prayed enough. The next moment the dead woman flew up through the roof of the church of Scherpenheuvel.
186232: In Mechelen there was a haunted farm. When people walked past it, they heard the doors slam, although no one was to be seen. After the priest had read prayers over the farm, it was no longer haunted.
186235: The merchants coming from Tongeren always saw a white lady appear in Hamal. A man who often went hunting in Hamal always wore his clogs back to front so that the white lady could not follow his tracks.
186241: A man who saw a magpie sitting in a tree shot at the bird. Under the tree the man found a woman's finger with a ring. The next day the neighbours said: "There is a woman lying in bed. Last night she lost her finger".
186262: In the castle of Alden Biesen there was a haunted room. The farmhand Jan let the other farmhands dare him to go to that room at night. In return for his feat Jan was given buckwheat to bake pancakes. When Jan was baking pancakes in the haunted room, he heard a voice saying: "I'm falling, I'm falling." Jan replied: "Fall till you go to the devil, but don't fall in my pan!" The next moment a bone fell down the chimney. The same thing happened several more times. Jan had thrown all the bones into a corner and calmly began to eat. After a while a complete skeleton stood in the corner, which said: "I'm hungry."
186281: A woman who no longer managed to make butter sadly told a friar that she could not give him any butter. After the friar had blessed the woman, she could make butter again.
186287: Whenever a farmhand drove a fully loaded cart past the house of Heksebetje, the cart always came to a standstill.
186304: In Piringen lived a werewolf who had a relationship with a girl who worked in the village. When the pair were walking in the Kerkstraat, the young man felt that he was going to turn into a werewolf. He wanted to reassure the girl with these words: "I often get something that makes me walk on hands and feet. If that happens, throw a red handkerchief between my teeth, then I can't harm you." The girl was so frightened that she immediately quit her job and left the village.
186320: People said that Trien B. was a witch. Trien could make mice without tails by rummaging in the earth with her hand.
186323: A man wanted to fool a witch who often came to his house. When the witch came knocking one day, the man brought out a sign reading: "Beware, swine fever". The man was proud that this way he did not have to let the witch in. That same evening, however, the man had to call the vet because the pigs would not eat. After that the man had to bring out his sign again, because the animals really were infected with swine fever.
186328: A man who was out hunting saw a rabbit, but he could not hit the animal. A little later a witch came up with the words: "You mustn't shoot my cat, you hear!" The witch had changed the rabbit into a cat.
186329: At the fair in Tessenderlo a young man had met a girl who was said to be a witch. When the boy cycled home, he let the girl sit on the front of the handlebars. A little later the girl had changed herself into a dog.
186330: At Vogelsang a clergyman came haunting in the evenings, floating over the lanes, fields and streams. During the day the clergyman lay in a room, bound by three chains.
186333: When people had a cow that would not get in calf, or a mare that could not deliver her foal, they believed a witch had caused the trouble.
186336: At the fair a witch had drunk from Hanke W.'s glass. When the man wanted to go home, he took off all his clothes and went home in his shirt.
186343: Anyone touched by a witch was covered in filth.
186345:
The castle of D. was haunted. All sorts of strange things happened. For example, a double M was drawn on the meal for the cows. When the cows had eaten straw, they could not digest it, and so on. One afternoon a dead man was seen lying in the doorway of the horse stable. When people came closer, there was nothing to be seen anymore.
In the past the Templars lived in the castle of Dompaerts. Those Templars shod their horses back to front.
186346: When a witch stroked a child's head and said: "Oh, what a beautiful child you are!", the child had lice the next day.
186348: In a fen in Kinrooi a bell was sometimes heard ringing at Christmas. After a failed attempt to raise the sunken bell, it sank even deeper.
186353: In Hoelbeek at least twenty Templars came haunting. The Templars were priests who drank a lot and did not keep their celibacy. Later people still used the expression: "Drinking like a Templar".
186362: A band was found in a horse stable. After the band had been burnt, everything went back to normal.
186363: In Stamprooi a mother went for a walk with her newborn baby. On the way, however, they met a witch. After that the baby began to cry loudly. After the parish priest had prayed over the child, it no longer cried.
186372: A woman who was cutting grass struck at a magpie that kept pecking at her hands. The magpie turned out to be a woman from the neighbourhood.
186379: A brother lived with his sister in a house in Meeuwen. The brother, who often went hunting, had frequently seen a hare in the garden and decided to shoot the animal. A little later it turned out that the brother had shot his sister.
186380: A boy said to his girlfriend: "If some beast or other tries to attack you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." When the boy came back a little later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. It was a werewolf.
186381: On a field in Spalbeek, near the border with Stevoort, a white lady appeared at night.
186388: Two people visiting the T. family saw a cat walking around there. When they went home in the evening, the cat was still there. The animal sat down and moved its tail. A shoe was hanging from the underside of the tail.
186390: On the farm Meulder Berghs there worked a farmhand who was going with a girl from the village. When the farmhand was taking his girlfriend home on a Sunday evening, he felt that he was about to turn into a werewolf and said: "I have to relieve myself." While the girl stood waiting for her boyfriend, a dog with glowing eyes suddenly came at her. The girl threw her handkerchief at the animal and was unharmed. When she met her boyfriend the next day, the girl saw to her great horror that the threads of her handkerchief were still between his teeth.
186394: A farmer could not keep a single cow alive. No parish priest or friar from the area could help him. In the end the farmer had yet another friar come, who said: "I will come to you tonight. Make a big fire in advance, put a large cooking pot on it, and put a piece of a cow's entrails in it." When the friar was at the farmer's that evening, two men with clubs stood guard and tree trunks were propped against the gate so that no one could get in. A witch, however, knocked over the tree trunks, opened the gate and went inside. The two guards managed to catch her and beat her with the clubs. The friar made the witch kneel before the fire and confess what she had done. The witch confessed and took a whole bag of pins out of the cows' mangers.
186406: Zwarte Hans came out of an inn drunk. He put his cap in the middle of the street, saying: "If there is a devil, let him come now and put money in my cap!" The next moment the man was seized by a shadowy figure, which threw him over the bridge. Zwarte Hans sobered up at once and trembled with fear.
186408: A woman was bewitched after a witch had bumped into her in the street. To avoid being bewitched, one had to hit the witch on the head.
186426: A castle in Germany was so badly haunted that the lord of the castle lived in another building. One day a man came who wanted to rent the castle and promised the lord that he would drive out the ghost. When the man went to sleep in the castle, he kept his eyes only half closed. At midnight the man saw a ghost appear, which took gold coins out of the wall and began to count them. As soon as the ghost had vanished, the man took the gold and left. As a result the castle was delivered.
186428: A woman was plagued by the devil, who always came and sat on her neck. The woman described the devil as a very handsome young man. To be rid of the devil, the woman did nothing but pray.
186430: A miller had made a pact with the devil to be able to build and extend the Dalemolen. After ninety-nine years the man had to haunt in the shape of a large black dog. Two priests had already come, but they had not managed to banish the ghost. To the third priest the dog said: "You cannot banish me, for when you were still a student, you stole grain from a field." A next priest did succeed in banishing the dog to a whirlpool in the water. At that moment, however, the ghost said: "You banish me, but in ninety-nine years I will come back!"
186444: Some miners were eating at midday when Suske suddenly said: "I must confess to you that I am a sorcerer. When I was still working in Luik, a woman wanted to see my magic. I sat in an umbrella on the table and made a thousand mice run across the table. At night I made everyone fall out of bed."
186448: A man whose brother always had a nosebleed found it strange that a witch was always standing at his door, watching. When the man's brother came walking up one day, he wanted to give the witch a thrashing. The brother died young.
186450: Some children from Heers had been given fruit by a witch. A few hours after eating the fruit, the children fell ill. They were under the influence of the evil hand.
186454: A girl had told the parish priest that she always saw a light jumping through the meadow. On the priest's advice the girl asked the light what it wanted.
186467: An old man who lived by the railway had to fetch a bucket of water from the well every day. One day the man's kitten came along with him. But as the man walked back home, the kitten led him astray. Then the man, who by now was half an hour from his house, said: "Kitten, witch or not, you're getting this bucket of water over you!"
186482: In Zichen people believed that the little souls of dead children came to sit on the banks of the ditches and gave off light. In reality such lights were glow-worms.
186488: A merchant going home in the evening was jumped by a werewolf on the way. The man managed to scratch the werewolf on the neck. When the man went to the shoemaker the next day, he saw that the shoemaker had a bandage around his neck. The shoemaker was a werewolf.
186515: A drunkard coming back from the inn saw rich young ladies dancing in the Broek of Sluizen. When one of the witches offered the man a cup of wine, the drunkard took the cup and said: "God bless you all!" The next moment all the witches had vanished. Because the man was left alone in the meadow, he decided to take the cup home with him. The next morning, however, the man saw that it was a golden cup with the name of one of the witches in it. It was a witch from Maastricht. The man then decided to bring the cup back in the hope of getting a nice reward. When the man arrived in Maastricht, the woman's maid claimed that her mistress was not at home. After much insisting the man was let in after all. Once the witch had received her golden cup, she gave the man a hard slap in the face. "If I had known that, I'd damn well never have gone there!", the man said to his wife afterwards.
186521: A man coming back from Caberg, where he worked for a farmer, was jumped by a werewolf on the way. The werewolf laughed at the man.
186540: In the past a sow used to roam near the castle of Emmeren, coming to haunt the place with her piglets.
186543: A butcher who was going to salt the meat in the evening saw something strange rolling over the ground on the way. After a while the man said: "Now you'll tell me who you are, or I'll stab you to death!" When the man wounded the strange apparition with his dung fork, it turned out to be a werewolf in a sack; it was his best friend.
186545: In the past there were witches who made the farmers' animals ill.
186560: A man walking from Vliermaal to Schalkhoven in the evening was followed by a big dog. When the man made the sign of the cross, the animal suddenly vanished.
186574: In Tongeren a ghost walked on the churchyard wall.
186590: A man who had brought in the hay at night with his wife and had then dozed off for a moment suddenly saw a light appear by the brook. When the woman saw the light, she began to scream loudly. She was so afraid of the will-o'-the-wisp that she had to be taken home. Two drunkards had once drowned in that brook.
186601: A man who had kicked at a cat was suddenly surrounded by twenty-five cats.
186602: On the Luizenberg in Gingelom lived a witch who could cover people in lice.
186604: A maid of a rich German gentleman told her employer that his late wife was standing at the door. The gentleman replied: "If that is true, then my two grey horses in the stable will walk up the stairs and hang their heads out of the window." The next moment the two horses left their stable, walked up the stairs and hung their heads out of the window. The dead woman had indeed come back.
