186605: A man who had moved a boundary post during his life could not enter heaven and had to haunt after his death with the post in his hands. The parish priest advised the ghost to put the post back in its original place. After that the dead man must have reached heaven after all, for the ghost was never seen anywhere again.
186620: A woman came to look in on people who could not make butter. When the woman opened the lid, the churn was full of butter.
186623: Children of witches could not sleep at night because their little beds were full of pins. Moreover, witches could not die until they had passed their arts on to their eldest daughter. The witch Mina C. always had cats sitting on her shoulders.
186626: A man had promised to go on pilgrimage to Our Lady. Because he had not kept his promise, the man's wife came haunting. When the man had gone on pilgrimage, the ghost was no longer seen.
186628: Jan F. saw a pretty little dog in a street and decided to take it with him. But the dog grew heavier and heavier, so that Jan finally had to put it down. When he looked back a little later, he saw two glowing eyes. The next day a burnt handkerchief lay at that spot.
186637: Vuurmannen (fire men) were the little souls of unbaptised children who came to haunt and made people lose their way. If you stuck something in the ground and set it on fire, nothing could happen. Such lights may also have been gases rising from the ground.
186644: In Wintershoven lived a man who was followed everywhere by a cat. One day he asked the animal: "Tuuske, Minneke, why are you here?", to which the cat replied: "Janneke V., why do you ask me: 'Tuuske, Minneke, why are you here?'" The cat had scratched Janneke on the leg. The man resolved to leave the cat alone; after all, it might well be a witch!
186646: A felled oak lay in the castle lane of Wideux. Every time the oak was moved, it was lying back in its old place the next day.
186655: A witch could make someone's house burn down.
186659: In Vlijtingen there lived a girl who had a relationship with an officer. Although the officer was a gallant gentleman, the girl's parents did not think him suitable company for their daughter. The officer agreed with the girl that he would come and carry her off on his horse. When the officer tapped three times on the girl's window at night, she climbed out of the window and sat in front of her beloved on the horse. When they came to a churchyard, the officer said: "The moon and the stars shine bright, but death is dark." The next moment the officer and the horse had vanished without a trace. When the girl had recovered from her astonishment and realised she was not dreaming, there was nothing left for her but to return home.
186660: A farmer took his cows to the meadow in rainy weather. When he came back, the farmer saw that his umbrella was covered in threads. The witch Rooske had done that.
186663: Anyone touched by a witch was covered in lice a few hours later. When a witch had laid her hand on a child's cradle, the child often fell ill. Usually the child then died of that illness.
186664: In Boshoven there lived a witch who could make mice without tails.
186665: When someone touched a phantom dog, it ran away or kept growing bigger.
186674: In Stokrooie there was a child who always began to cry whenever a certain woman came to visit. Because a pilgrimage to Spalbeek had not helped, the parents had the child prayed over by the friars. The clergymen also gave the parents blessed rolls. After that the child got better.
186678: A farmer was at his wits' end because his foals were all dying of a strange disease. One day the farmer bought a foal from a Jew from Mechelen. For a long time the foal stayed healthy, but one day it too fell ill. The Jew did not understand why the foal he had sold had fallen ill. So the seller offered to guard the farmer's house, so that the farmer could look after the sick foal in the stable. The next day the Jew said: "Shall I have the woman who is doing this to you come by?" It was a woman from the neighbourhood who always wore a long cloak and came at night to bewitch the foals.
186679: When people had eaten too much, they believed they would be ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) at night. To keep the maar from climbing onto the bed, one had to turn one's slippers upside down.
186681: The people who lived on a farm in Sint-Lambrechts-Herk were firmly convinced that it was a bad omen when a cart with two horses got stuck in front of their house. When this happened again one day, the people were worried sick. A while later the farmer's wife hanged herself from a fruit tree.
186688: A farmhand from Boekhout worked in Mielen-boven-Aalst. When the young man was walking home one evening, he saw a fat hare sitting in a field by the road. As he walked on, the farmhand thought: "I really should have caught that hare. If it's there again tomorrow, it's done for!" The next evening the hare was sitting in the same spot again. This time the farmhand had brought a stick, which he threw at the hare. He missed, whereupon the hare ran to the stick, sat on it and said: "Come and get the stick, if you dare!" The farmhand was so frightened that he ran off like lightning. At that moment hundreds of hares leapt through the grain along the road from Boekhout to Mielen. The farmhand literally fell ill with fear. When he got home he crawled into his bed, and he never came out of it alive.
186690: A boy was visiting his girlfriend. When the boy had fallen asleep, the girl's mother rubbed ointment under her arms and said: "I wish myself over hedges and hawthorns into the Count's wine cellar". Then she said to her daughter: "Come after me!" Although her boyfriend had woken up in the meantime, the girl decided to follow her mother anyway. The girl rubbed ointment under her arms and said: "I wish myself over hedges and hawthorns into the Count's wine cellar". When his girlfriend was gone, the boy too rubbed ointment under his arms and said: "I wish myself through hedges and hawthorns into the Count's wine cellar". When the boy arrived, he was covered in blood.
186692: After mass in Rekem, the sexton locked the church. But he had not noticed that a man had fallen asleep in the church. At night the man woke and discovered that he was locked in. At midnight all the lights in the church came on and the dead priest appeared, dressed all in white. Relieved, the man said: "How glad I am to see you! Please let me out of the church." The ghost answered: "I am glad to see you here. I have been haunting here for eighty years because my soul can find no rest. When I was priest here, I was paid to say a mass that I never said. Please tell the present priest that he must say that mass. Then I will be released." The next day the man went to the presbytery and explained everything to the priest. After the priest had said the mass, the ghost was released.
186703: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his field had to haunt after his death. The farmer could only enter heaven after his neighbour had forgiven him.
186705: A black witch cat often sat on the Zevenbonder in Werm.
186725: A woman could make the table dance. The people who had seen it were so frightened that they never visited the witch again.
186729: A baron lived at Munnik-hof in Boorsem. The baron's daughter had a relationship with the son of the count who lived at the castle of Rekem. Because the count was not pleased with the girl's background, the two lovers jumped into the well so that they could be together forever. Shortly afterwards the baron and his wife left the Munnik-hof, which belonged to the count. The Munnik-hof was sold to the religious order of the Bernateinen. When the nuns went to pray at night, they often saw a ghost wandering about. Because their grounds were haunted, the nuns no longer dared go outside.
186730: When a sow with a chain came past at night, it was best not to go and look. Then the trampling of horses and the clatter of pots and pans could be heard.
186732: A boy and a girl who had met a big dog saw a man who had the threads of a handkerchief between his teeth.
186746: In the H. family a child was ill because it had been bewitched. The pillow the child slept on was full of needles. After the pillow had been thrown away, the child recovered.
186749: One night a priest met a thief who asked for money. The priest bewitched the thief so that he was fixed to the ground, and went home. The next day the priest sent his maid to the thief with the words: "Go and tell that man he may leave." Only then could the thief move again.
186754: In the 1930s a ghostly apparition was often seen wandering along the canal in Boorsem.
186773: The lord of the castle and his servant had gone hunting in Munsterbilzen in a white coach with two horses. On the way back they saw a white nun standing by the barrier. The nun came towards them through the Boskee. A little later she had vanished.
186774: When the white lady walked along the lane, the gate of the castle of Printhagen opened and closed by itself.
186788: A woman was always woken in the morning at the same time by a magpie. When the woman got up a little earlier one day, the magpie came tapping on the window while the woman was at work.
186792: The wife of Geerke N. had been in S.'s stable. The next day all the calves leapt up against the ceiling and their legs were covered in blood. When the friars of Hasselt had given something to put under the threshold, the animals behaved normally again.
186796: When a child was bewitched, it became ill.
186806: When Frans met a cat, he said to the animal: "Ah, pussycat, where are you going?" The next moment Frans was surrounded by a whole pack of cats, who said: "If Frans hadn't spoken so nicely, we would have broken his neck!"
186831: When the moon was full, the witches often held gatherings at the farm of Driek De W. You could then see a good hundred cats at the farm. One day the priest sprinkled the place with holy water and put a statue of a saint by the farm. After that no more cats appeared at Driek's. It was said that the witches held their gatherings in a castle in Hamont from then on.
186836: A mother was troubled that her child cried all week. When the father came home from work on Saturday, the child stopped crying. But as soon as it was Monday, the crying began again. One day Fien S. came to visit the woman. When Fien took the child out of the cradle, she discovered in the pillow a ball of yarn in the shape of a little coffin. Some time before, a woman had come to the mother to borrow yarn. If the yarn had stayed in the pillow any longer, the child would have died. Fien decided to go with the mother to the holy little friar in Hasselt. In the morning the women missed their train. When they wanted to fry bacon, the meat burned at once. On the way to Hasselt the women saw a black dog in front of them the whole time. At the priest's, the mother began to sweat heavily. The clergyman then said: "Yes, you must suffer a little too, for your child has suffered enough!" Because the priest had given the mother a relic, the witch could no longer enter the house after that.
186839: A man on his way to Hasselt met an old woman in Zonhoven, who said: "If I cannot do people any harm, then I have to wring a chicken's neck."
186841: In Binderveld lived a woman who had twins. The little boy had died and the girl had fallen ill too. The misfortune was caused by a witch whom the mother met at the market every day.
186849: After a poacher had shot at a hare, the animal began to play.
186850: A farmer who was ploughing saw a crow fly past, calling: "Hey Jan, hey Jan!" Suddenly the crow came and sat on the ox's yoke. Because a witch lived nearby, the farmer left his field as fast as he could.
186859: Near Noeneldere a werewolf roamed about with chains around its neck. The same werewolf was also sometimes seen on the Bilzersteenweg. After the animal had been chased with a stick, it did not come back.
186866: A man out with his cart suddenly could go no further. The cart stood still because of a witch.
186880: A man from Millen who had gone to play cards at the fair in Mal went home alone in the evening. On the way, to his great fright, the man was accompanied by two witches.
186884: A child always saw a black kitten sitting on the edge of its cradle. "Mother, the pretty pussycat is there again!" the child would cry. But nobody else could see the cat. When the child was three and a half years old, it died.
186893: At the castle of 't Langstuk a ghost always appeared, calling: "Where must I leave it?" One day Suske W. answered: "Where you took it from!" After that the ghost was gone.
186900: A farmer had a lot of bad luck with his animals. In the stable there were a good hundred white mice that tormented the animals and ate all the fodder. The priest advised the farmer to sprinkle all his animals with holy water. Since then no white mice have come into the stable.
186903: Whenever a woman was frying bacon, a cat appeared and took a piece of bacon out of the pan. One day the woman was so fed up that she threw the hot fat at the cat. The next day a woman was going about the village whose face was badly burned.
186904: A boy who was out walking with his girlfriend went away for a moment at midnight. At that moment a werewolf came running towards the girl. After a struggle the werewolf managed to get hold of the girl's red handkerchief. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
186905: Moazere Mina asked a man to walk with her. Because the man flatly refused, Mina said: "You won't be home before me anyway!" When the witch walked on ahead of him, the man suddenly got such pain in his leg that he could go no further.
186907: A man smoking a pipe on a summer evening suddenly saw a burning sheaf of corn floating through the air. A little later the strange apparition had vanished. The next day the man found that one sheaf was missing from the cornfield.
186919: Kato had given a woman from the neighbourhood three beets for the cow. Because the woman did not trust the witch, she buried the beets in the field. The next day, strangely enough, the beets had vanished without a trace. A week later one of the cows lay dead in the stable. The worried woman then went to the priest of Tongeren, who said: "It is good that you came, for the bewitchment would have passed from your cow to your youngest child. I will give you some relics to hang around the children's necks and to put under the threshold."
186921: A woman had once had to carry the werewolf, but she did not mind much. Sometimes she put some food outside, which was always gone the next day. Whoever was tormented by a werewolf had only themselves to blame.
186922: One night gravedigger Jefke P. wet his trousers in fear when he saw a ghost appear in the churchyard.
186926: A man who had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel died before he had kept his promise. The man's brother knew this and decided to go on pilgrimage himself. As soon as the brother arrived in Scherpenheuvel, he broke out in a sweat and fell to the ground, exhausted. Later he was told that he had probably had to carry his dead brother's spirit the whole way. To prevent that, he should have put his stick by the door with the words: "You go ahead, I will follow you."
186937: One evening a man had to go and fetch the midwife for his daughter. When the man was coming back, a kitten jumped onto his bicycle at the Zwarte Lieve Heer. Because the man could no longer ride on, he threw down his bicycle and kicked at the cat. In the end the man had to carry his bicycle all the way home. That cat was a witch.
186944: A man who lived on the Steenberg saw a will-o'-the-wisp appear every day at around half past nine at farmer V.'s in 't Roeren. Each time that will-o'-the-wisp tried to lead the man to the water.
186947: At 't Hoxent there was a sick little child that would not get better. Every time chaplain Kardinaals came to read prayers over the child, a fierce wind rose. When one day a red fox came in, the chaplain said: "Don't be afraid, just pray!" That evening the chaplain left, exhausted.
186949: In Molenbeersel lived a shepherd who went out every day after supper. One evening the shepherd, who often made people carry him on their backs as a werewolf, had been wounded. Because the werewolf had thereby taken on his human form, the shepherd had been recognised. The priest advised people to search for the werewolf's collar. The shepherd had hidden his collar in a tree stump.
186951: At midnight all the animals on a farm became restless. Cats were leaping among the cows. The friars of Hasselt came to read prayers over the farm for ninety-nine years and more. They also hung a large wooden cross in the stable, which was never to be removed. When a wall of the stable was later torn down, the cross was removed after all.
186964: Will-o'-the-wisps often floated above the water. They were the little souls of unbaptised children.
186969: A witch often hung around near the Grevensmolen in Sint-Truiden. That witch had a cat with her that jumped between her legs at every step. One day the miller said: "That's no matter: if you can overtake a witch and then cross your feet over each other, the witch takes on her true form." When Guske A. once tried it, the witch at once changed into Pauline K. Pauline often made people get lost. One evening Tinus B. and Kobe K. met the witch, and she said: "Good evening, men! You're out late, but you're nearly home. Have a good journey!" The men walked on all night without knowing where they were. When it grew light in the morning, they were in Nieuwerkerken.
186989: A man had seen at night how the witches came to dance around a thick tree in Kerniel, singing: "The day is for you, the night is for us!" A short time afterwards the man died.
187011: A man from Overpelt going to Dilsen was followed the whole time by a black witch cat. When the man came to a crossroads, the witch had suddenly vanished.
187014: A young man went with his brother to visit his girlfriend on the Riedijk. Because his girlfriend's sister had had an epileptic fit, the young man stayed longer than usual that evening. When the boy went home with his brother, around midnight he saw two white apparitions wandering about near the Vlooienberg.
187022: By the canal in Hocht people were often jumped by the werewolf, which made them carry it.
187031: In Flanders stood a mill that never turned because its owner had sold his soul to the devil. One day the man left and never returned. At night a rattling of chains could sometimes be heard in the mill. The mill had three owners. Each time a new owner came, all the windowpanes were smashed to pieces at night.
187034: At night a woman heard drumming in the distance. The witches were dancing and drinking wine. When the woman was also offered a cup of wine, one of the witches had to sneeze. Then Claeske S., who was spying on the witches, said: "God bless you!" The next moment all the witches ran away. One of the witches said: "If Claekse S. had not spoken kind words, I would have broken his neck."
187038: Some men who sat talking in the evening on the felled trees lying at the corner by the churchyard suddenly saw a dog with a long chain pass by. One of the men said: "That is something strange. Tomorrow I'll bring a dung fork." When the dog appeared again the next day, however, the man could do nothing with his dung fork; he could not move.
187043: A girl who had struck a werewolf with her knitting discovered a little later that her boyfriend was the werewolf.
187068: A man saw someone standing by the iron crosses in the churchyard with a white sheet over his head. Convinced it was someone trying to frighten him, the man pulled away the sheet and ran off. When the man reached his friends, he found he was holding a shroud with three small black woollen crosses sewn on it. Terrified, the man sought advice from the priest. The clergyman said: "Tomorrow at about the same time you must go back to the churchyard and return that shroud. To protect yourself, it is best to take a child younger than eight with you." When the man went to return the shroud the next day, the ghost said: "Man, you have asked someone for advice, or else I would have you here in my hands!"
187086: Free G. went poaching in Veulenbos. A young goat was wandering about that always frightened the hares away. Free said to the goat: "If you come again, I'll shoot you!" When the goat came again, Free had his gun ready and shot at the animal. Strangely, the shot from the gun flew off in completely the opposite direction. And the goat had vanished.
187089: Two men were visiting the V. family, where they were having fun with some women. As a joke the men had taken the handkerchief of one of the women, whereupon that woman said: "You'll be bringing that handkerchief back!" When the men went home and walked over a bridge, they fell into the water. The men decided to play it safe and quickly bring the handkerchief back. After that they did get across the bridge.
187091: One day the girls had not polished the copper and the tin. In the evening they suddenly heard a strange noise. When they went to look, they saw that the copper and tin had been turned upside down on the cupboard.
187093: One winter evening a man was walking home by moonlight along the Jannestraat. At the Oppenhof the man suddenly saw a large black dog standing on the road. When the man looked back once more, he saw that the dog had grown much bigger. The next day the man was seriously ill, but he did recover.
187105:
Charel had seen that his little daughter could make mice. The priest said to Charel: "Go to the chaplain, because I no longer have the power for that." After the chaplain had poured holy water over her head, the girl could no longer make mice. The child had been baptised wrongly.
Those who were not baptised could do nothing, and those who were baptised could do nothing either. But people who had been baptised wrongly came into the devil's power.
187114: A mother sent her children to the shop to do the shopping. If the children met Nel S., their mother forbade them to say what they had bought, because then the goods would immediately be back in the shop, even though the children had taken them with them.
187117: Nol J.'s mother had died. One evening Nol saw a will-o'-the-wisp in the courtyard, which said: "I had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. Now that I am dead, you must go in my place." When Nol promised his dead mother that he would go to Scherpenheuvel, the will-o'-the-wisp flew high into the sky.
187118: When there were new piglets somewhere, people usually kept watch in the sty. Otherwise a witch might come at night and say: "What lovely piglets!" The next day the piglets would then stand on their hind legs and die.
187138: Two men had to saw down a cherry tree for a little old woman in Koersel. The woman went to look at the tools, took hold of something and said: "That looks like a good hatchet!" When one of the men tried to chop off a branch, he bent the axe completely crooked. When the job was done, the woman said: "You did that well! You are good craftsmen! Come in for a cup of coffee." The men refused and hurried home. It was said that the woman was a witch.
187147: One day Michiel van H. from Zepperen had to carry a werewolf. Michiel said to the werewolf: "There is my stick. You go ahead; I will follow you." At that the animal jumped off his back. If Michiel had not said that, he would have had to carry the werewolf all the way to the church. The werewolf was someone who had promised to go on pilgrimage but had not kept that promise.
187152: Bokkenrijders (goat riders, a gang of robbers said to ride goats through the air) often came to 't Himmelen in Neerglabbeek. One day in Neerglabbeek a priest was secretly preparing mass. One of those present suddenly said: "Give me a mirror and a bucket of water!" The man held the mirror above the water and then cried out: "Come, we must get away from here, because the bokkenrijders are coming! They are already at the Royermolen!"
187154: On the Jonckhold the devil had sat down on a chest of money. When the field guard and the priest came to fetch the chest, the devil said: "If you leave the last living heart here for me, you can have the chest." The priest then tied a crucifix to the devil's back and said: "Here, take that." Because the devil believed he had been given a heart, the field guard and the priest could take the money chest away.
187162: A man walking over the bridge one Sunday evening at about ten o'clock heard a noise as if a hundred horses were crossing the bridge. When the man wanted to go to his girlfriend a few days later, he again heard a hellish noise on the bridge in the 'Hetten'. The man was convinced it was the drossaard (bailiff), and went back home.
187168: Rikus de H. and Ber H. went poaching on a cold winter's day. When they had been out for a while, Ber said: "Rikus, you wait here. I'll go on to the Driebonder, where I'll drive the hares this way." As Rikus sat waiting with his gun in his hand, a hare came running up, but Rikus thought: "I can't shoot now, the animal is already too close; I'd blow it to pieces. I'd better wait until the hare has gone past." But the hare came right up to Rikus, sniffed at his feet and then asked: "Have the other hares come by here yet?" Startled by this talking animal, Rikus ran to Ber and asked whether he had seen the hare too. The hare had indeed also come and sniffed at Ber's gun, and the animal had said: "You'll never shoot a hare again!" Since then Rikuske and Ber never dared to go poaching again.
187170: A man came to a farmer and offered to plough the whole field in exchange for some tobacco. The farmer agreed and was astonished when the work was done in the blink of an eye. The man must have been the devil.
187174: A boy had been given an ice cream. After a witch had made the sign of the cross over the ice cream, his mother would not let him eat it any more.
187178: It was said that an alley in Halmaal was haunted; two girls had seen a white lady there. A mischievous boy wanted to frighten the girls and went and sat in the alley with a white sheet over his head. That evening one of the girls said: "Look, yesterday there was only one ghost and now there are two!" The boy with the sheet looked behind him and saw the white lady. He ran home terrified and died of fright.
187188: Will-o'-the-wisps were caterpillars or maggots found mainly in marshy areas, such as in Koersel. Many people drowned in those marshes in the past. People believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of those who had drowned.
187196: A boy walking home met a cat on the way. He picked the animal up in his arms and stroked it. When the cat jumped away a little further on, she turned into a beautiful girl who said: "You are lucky I did you no harm. Never tell anyone my name!"
187197: In the past the woods of Waltwilder were haunted. Every night a little old woman with a white cap on her head appeared there.
187214: A man from Kotem always had to carry the werewolf in the Bamstraat. Later that werewolf turned out to be a man who disguised himself with an animal skin. If such a skin could be burned in the oven, the werewolf would be released.
187218: One night a farmer heard noise in his stable. When he went to look, he saw that the horses had disappeared. After a long search the farmer found his horses in the fields. But the animals had become so wild that the farmer could not catch them. The horses had probably been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
187220: A man had seen a white lady with a straw hat in a wood in Nieuwerkerken.
187237: A man from the Kempen sleeping in a haystack at night suddenly saw a will-o'-the-wisp appear. He was so frightened that he ran away at once. Many will-o'-the-wisps were found near the Demer. It was said that they were the souls of unbaptised children.
187251: Toon the carpenter's son was coming back in the evening from the fair in Budel. On the way a big black dog suddenly appeared and blocked his path. Toon quickly muttered a short prayer, after which the animal let him pass.
187259: Some people went on pilgrimage to release a dead person who had not kept a promise. Before setting out, the people put a stick against the wall and said to the ghost: "Now you go ahead and we will come after you." Whoever forgot to say this was exhausted on arriving at the place of pilgrimage.
187279: On a fine dry day some people were transporting a number of barrels of petroleum with a horse and cart. When they passed the house of Marie G., the cart suddenly sank into the ground up to the axles.
187282: A boy had fallen asleep in his girlfriend's house. Meanwhile the girl rubbed herself with ointment from a pot that stood on the chimney. Then she said: "May the devil carry me over hedges and hawthorns". As soon as the girl was gone, the boy copied her. But when he reached the other witches, he was badly injured. He had made a mistake when speaking the magic formula.
187297: In Maasmechelen lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. Witches did all sorts of things to harm people.
187301: A man was plagued by the maar (nightmare spirit) for three nights. The first time, the man could no longer move because someone was coming at him with a dagger. Another time, the man was standing on a wall built in the water. When the man knelt down, all the bricks fell out of the wall. The third time, the man felt a tightness because an old woman was lying on him, shaking her dirty hair in his face. Each time the man had woken up sweating because the maar had frightened him so much.
187306: On the road to Piringen sat a werewolf that attacked people. A man coming back from the inn was nearly scared to death when he saw a werewolf with a bearskin. Because the man did not dare to go on, he went back to the inn and said: "I'm afraid, because there's a werewolf sitting there who will take my money!" Two men then decided to take the coward home. By then, however, there was no trace of the werewolf.
187309: A red handkerchief was thrown at a werewolf. The next day a boy from the village still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
187328: A bewitched child that cried all the time was cured by the priest. The priest did not dare go home alone because the witch kept following him.
187343: In Haren there was a haunted house.
187344: A girl said to her aunt, who was asleep: "Look, another cat has come in!" The aunt then threw the cat outside. When the cat was back inside a little later, the aunt threw the animal against a hook on the wall. The next day the aunt met a woman from the village who was wearing a bandage around her head. "You see, I can get you!" said the aunt.
187382: A brother and sister were sitting talking one Sunday when suddenly a miaowing kitten came in. Three times the kitten was thrown outside. But because the animal kept coming back in, the brother threw the kitten into the fire. The next day the brother and sister went to Bergering, where they saw a woman who asked: "What did you do with that kitten?" The woman was burned all over.
187386: A man was walking past the house of Giel van Stien by moonlight. Suddenly a fierce wind rose and a haunted broom bush rolled after the terrified man.
187399: In a farmhouse at midnight a ghost with a chain came down the attic stairs. The ghost walked through the house and then went back to the attic. One night the people saw the ghosts of three little children appear. When they wanted to tell someone about it the next day, they were nearly strangled by the ghosts, who wanted their secret kept.
187400: In Kaulille lived a witch who under no circumstances would let the priest into her house. A bewitched little girl from the neighbourhood had lain in bed all her life because she could not walk. When the witch lay on her deathbed, she had to let the priest in after all, since she could not die. The next day the witch did die. After that the girl gradually recovered.
187417: On the heath lights always appeared by the water. Those lights were the returned dead.
187430: A little child had died in Herk-de-Stad. After a witch had gone to make a little sign of the cross over the child, the dead child was covered in lice.
187433: In Groote-Spouwen there was haunting. One day a girl was playing with her brother in the Rietbos. The children had climbed an apple tree when they suddenly heard a deep voice: "Raise children - raise dogs!" It was said that the voice came from a haunting dog that had been banished by a clergyman because during his life he had not cared well for his children.
187434: A maid who worked at Ter Waarden always put her clogs on one side of the kitchen in the evening. Strangely, the next morning the clogs were always on the other side.
187441: A woman suspected of witchcraft had given a child a big red apple. After the child had eaten the apple, it fell ill. It had a large lump on its head. In the end the child died. It had been bewitched.
187442: At a farm in Mieven there was haunting because someone had hanged himself there. One night all the hens dropped dead on the ground.
187446: A farmer from Weert suspected that his animals were under the influence of the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). Every time Marie T. had visited, the animals pulled at their chains as if possessed. When the farmer no longer let Marie into the stables, the animals behaved normally again.
187451: A man lost his way on a familiar road because of the 'dolende man' (wandering man).
187452: On Gedu lived a gardener who was ridden every night by the maar (nightmare spirit) and almost suffocated because of it.
187456: In the old days there were women who could make rats and mice. In the evenings those women held gatherings, and then the rats and mice ran up the walls.
187470: After his death a man came back to haunt in the shape of a black dog. A friar with a long rope came to banish the ghost. But the dog said: "You should not banish me, for you stole a cabbage yourself," to which the friar replied: "Yes, but I left a stuiver in its place."
187475: Adelain was sawing wood in Vechmaal when suddenly a witch passed by. A few moments later Adelain's saw was broken.
187478: A sorcerer from Kortessem could make people fall asleep without their knowing it. He could even make people undress without their knowing it. The sorcerer could also conjure rats and mice.
187488: A man walking in the broek (marshland) kicked at a cat that suddenly jumped at his feet. The man could hardly get rid of the cat, which clung to his leg.
187496: In a brewery in Widooie no farmhand would stay on; all of them were tormented at night by a black cat that frightened them or burned them. When the brewer had again taken on a new farmhand, his wife said: "He won't stay long either!" But the farmhand had heard the stories about the black cat. As soon as the animal crept in at night through a small hole, the farmhand poured boiling water over the cat. The next morning the brewer's wife lay in bed completely burned.
187497: A man saw a big dog at a turnstile. When the man wounded the animal with an axe, a man from the neighbourhood suddenly stood before him.
187498: Old K. came haunting after his death in his house on the Visweiden. Every evening a light burned in the house. Sighing and groaning could also be heard, as if someone were lying there dying.
187499: At a farm in Boorsem foals died every year. Someone had advised the farmer to cut open the belly of the next foal that died. In the animal's belly they found something that looked like a snake. From then on the farmer had no more misfortune with his foals.
187501: A farmhand from Rotem who worked on a farm always had to carry the werewolf when he came home in the evening around eleven o'clock.
187508: An old woman from Opheers could make a horse stand still by putting her thumb between her index finger and middle finger. Only when the witch wished it could the horse go on again.
187516: In Leut some girls had died. When the father wanted to burn the bedding, he found figures in the pillows.
187532: In the evening many will-o'-the-wisps could be seen in the meadows. It was said that they were the little souls of unbaptised children, asking to be released.
187534: A nun came haunting on a bridge near the Weikes in Munsterbilzen. After a clergyman had spoken with Sister Sjierebegijn, she was seen no more.
187537: Opposite the church of Lauw there was a haunted house. One evening some people heard a strange noise in the attic there. When they went to look, they saw to their great dismay that the spinning wheel was turning by itself. The house stood empty for ten years. After that it burned down.
187547: A nun from France who was looking through the window witnessed a meeting of Freemasons. At a certain moment a gentleman came in and gave the Freemasons instructions. That must have been the devil.
187555: At around half past twelve, one o'clock and half past one a ghost always appeared in a castle in the shape of a skeleton with hollow eyes. It was the soul of the former lord of the castle, who had to guard a chest of ill-gotten money in the cellar.
187568:
A boy who was walking with his girlfriend by moonlight said to the girl at midnight: "Here is my handkerchief. If the werewolf comes at you, throw it into his mouth. Then he will let you go." A little later the girl was indeed approached by a werewolf. After the girl had thrown the handkerchief, the beast disappeared. When the boy reappeared, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
Whoever was bitten by a werewolf became a werewolf too.
187569: A man travelling on foot met a horse that hung its muzzle over his shoulder. The man wanted to hit the horse, but he changed his mind. When the man passed a crossroads, the horse could go no further. The horse was a witch who had turned herself into an animal.
187574: A young man who had met his girlfriend in the evening said to the girl: "Today I must go home alone." When the girl passed a hedge a little later, she saw a big black dog coming at her. At that moment the girl remembered the advice her fiancé had once given her, and she threw a handkerchief at the beast's mouth. When the girl kissed her boyfriend the next day, she saw that he had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
187583: The rural policeman of Molenbeersel had had to carry a werewolf for several evenings. Because the man was gradually getting fed up with it, he decided to take a knife with him the next evening. When the policeman had cut the werewolf, the beast changed into a human: it was the policeman's neighbour.
187588: On the count's orders, V. had taken the felled oak from the castle lane of Wideux to the woods. But the next day the oak was already lying in its old place again. In the end the oak had to be left lying there.
187589: Everyone knew that Trien B. was a witch. After all, she was always nearby whenever something bad happened. One day the innkeeper's wife was so ill that the priest had already given her the Last Rites. Her husband, who still hoped for a cure, went to the healer of Genk, but did not say that the sick woman was his wife because he wanted to hear the truth from the healer. The healer said to the innkeeper: "That woman will not die, but it will take a long time before she is cured." The woman did indeed stay alive, but she had to remain in bed because she had an ailment on her leg that would not heal. People thought the woman was bewitched. At night she sometimes saw a little black cat walking around her room, or she was lifted out of bed by a strange figure. Her husband, who kept watch with a medlar stick, saw none of this. One day a strange man came into the inn saying: "Good day, Hulsbos, you don't know me, but I have been sent here by a brother of your wife. I am staying with him in Bree." After the stranger had drunk a glass of beer, he asked the innkeeper whether he might come and look at the woman's sick leg. Because the innkeeper refused at first, the stranger made ready to leave and said: "Then let her die in the name of God." At that the innkeeper let the stranger, who incidentally had begun religious studies but had not finished them, see his wife after all. When the stranger came to the woman, he wanted water to pour over the sick leg. Strangely enough, the water did not run onto the sheets. Because the water stayed on the leg, the stranger concluded that the woman was bewitched. After questioning the innkeeper about all the old women who lived in the village, he said: "I'll go and fetch the witch." A while later the stranger came back with a wound on his leg: "Damn it, I couldn't bring Trien B. here. She was just cutting bread and she cut my leg with her knife. But it's not so bad; tomorrow I'll come back and then I'll bring the witch here." When the stranger went back to Bree that same evening, he was so afraid that he had the innkeeper accompany him past the hills of Reppel. The innkeeper reassured him: "You don't need to come tomorrow. I'll let you know how my wife is getting on." The man never came back. He had become even more frightened because that same night he had seen the witch appear at his window. The next day Trien came to the inn with her husband. She knelt down and said: "Bless yourselves and pray, for now the witch is here." In the end the police had to remove Trien from the inn. When the innkeeper went to ask the priest for help the following Sunday, the clergyman at first did not want to come. After much insisting the priest agreed to come after all: "I'll come tomorrow before noon, but you must not tell anyone." The priest kept his promise and came to the inn the next day. He asked for holy water and a palm sprig, and then read prayers for a long time in the sick woman's room. From that day on the woman's health steadily improved. She no longer saw the little cat and the woman at night, and in the end she was completely cured.
187592: A man had secretly attended a gathering of the wild hunt. He had seen dancing ghosts who looked like people and who suddenly grabbed their things and vanished.
187602: Three young men from Lummen often went to a farm in Laren where there were three young daughters. One day, however, the girls were not at home. When the boys came outside, they saw three cats leaping about by the well, the bakehouse and the barn.
187607: A man who always went home by the same road got lost one day through the work of the evil hand.
187609: All the animals of farmer Gerard G. fell ill through the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). Because the vet could not cure the animals, the farmer went to the friars of Achel. The friars gave Gerard a relic of a saint which he had to hang in the stable. As a result the animals became healthy again.
187623: A bewitched child was always given a copper coin by a woman. Around midnight the child always started crying until one o'clock. Two friars read prayers over the child in honour of Saint Anthony. After a relic had been put under the door, the witch could no longer come in.
187625: In the evenings a dog with a chain often roamed about in Guigoven. People believed it was a boy who had sold his soul to the devil and therefore had to haunt.
187631: A man was coming back from Gewaai with a friend. Suddenly the friend gave the man his walking stick and said: "Here, take this walking stick, then nothing can happen." The man went on with the stick, while his friend was nowhere to be seen. Further on the man heard a strange jingling. In the middle of the road he saw a dog with glowing eyes. The man fearfully walked past the dog, and when he looked back, the dog had vanished.
187648: On the road to Kiewit lived a witch. A man coming out of the woods with an overloaded cart of wood met the witch, who said: "You won't get far with that! You won't even get halfway to Leoneke's!" The man ignored the witch's warning. A little further on the horse made a few wild leaps and all the wood fell off the cart.
187668: A woman went to catechism class in Ophoven. The children were standing in the church talking to each other because the priest had not arrived yet. When the priest came in, there were mice running all over the floor. One of the girls present claimed that she had made those mice. After the priest had baptised the girl again, she could no longer make mice.
187675: On a farm near Zepperen worked a farmhand who always went out in the evening. One day the farmhand's devil's band was found, and the oven was lit to burn it. When the devil's band was in the fire, the farmhand came running to take his band out of the oven. Since then the farmhand was never seen again.
187693: When the people of Hoeselt went to fetch wood, women sat along the ditches screaming so loudly that the horses did not dare go any further.
187698: At the fair a man was unmasked as a werewolf because he still had the threads of a handkerchief between his teeth.
187701: When someone had died somewhere, people blamed a black cat they had seen the day before. People then said that a witch in the shape of a cat had caused the death.
187708: A man from Rutten had six daughters and one son. When the little son fell seriously ill, the man went to a fortune teller. The fortune teller told the man that his own mother, a witch from Lauw, was causing the child's illness.
187727: A witch looked round if one walked in her footprints.
187730: In Beek all the livestock were afflicted by a strange disease. After a few weeks of illness the animals died. Because the vet could not help, many farmers lost all their animals. One morning a farmer whose animals were not yet ill rode on horseback past a stable. Suddenly the farmer saw a hare jump out of one of the stables. A few days later that farmer's animals were ill too. The problem was only solved after pastor Caris had read prayers over all the stables.
187733: Nol was a man who liked a drink. When Nol was going somewhere, he saw a witches' circle with a pub next to it that had beautiful velvet chairs. The man went into the pub and said: "God in Heaven's mercy!" The next moment the pub had vanished and the man was sitting with a tree stump in his hand.
187736: Old women who lived together were often witches. They could not only harm people but also heal the sick.
187739: Jan C. always found cats in his bed in the evening when his wife Mina was out as a witch.
187753: Because Jan H. had moved a boundary post during his life, he had to haunt after his death. After a man had said that the dead man had to put the post back in the place where he had taken it from, the ghost was released.
187755: A woman had a baby whom she put outside in a pram in fine weather. Suddenly the baby began to have health problems. The doctor tried all sorts of things, but nothing helped. After six months the doctor no longer even wanted to come. The neighbours had already told the woman that the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) might have something to do with it and advised her not to put the child outside in fine weather any more. They sent her to a man who lived on the Spaanse Brug. That man told the woman to make a novena and pray to the Three Sisters. After that the baby got somewhat better, but then relapsed. A while later a procession was held in the village. The woman joined it with the child in her arms, and stayed close to the Blessed Sacrament the whole time. After that the child was cured for good.
187756: In the village there once lived a certain Jan, who had a spotted cow. Lots of cats always roamed around Jan's house. One evening a cat came in and said: "Good evening, Jan-with-the-spotted-cow!" Unafraid, Jan replied: "Good evening, cat. Sit down and burn your bottom". The next evening the same thing happened again. Because more and more cats came in every evening, Jan gradually grew tired of the whole business. One evening one of the cats said: "Shall we?", whereupon Jan took the cooking pot off the fire and poured its contents over the cats. The cats ran outside howling. The next day quite a few women in the village were walking around with burns. Then everyone knew exactly how many witches lived in the village.
187784: Livinus had to come haunting after his death because during his life he had come into possession of zwart goed (ill-gotten goods). A Redemptorist banished the ghost behind a thick wall that was built in a cellar.
187789: A thick oak stood by the barrier on the Bosdreef. Poachers often saw a coach with four horses driving towards the lane there.
187790: In the past a granary in Herderen was haunted. Every night a strange rattling could be heard in the mill.
187810: A little boy was always ill after he had received something from his great-aunt. The friars read prayers over the child. The witch was taken to the Witzusters (White Sisters), where her power was taken from her.
187829: A man coming back from Borgloon in the evening was followed by a big black dog that kept running between his legs. The man had kicked the dog several times, but the animal always came back. The man grew frightened because he suspected the dog was a ghost.
187835: A man had broken up with his girlfriend when he discovered she was a witch. The man eventually married another woman, who had become friends with the witch. But the children of the woman and the man all met with misfortune. The eldest son injured his back in a fall at Belvederie. Six months later the boy died of his injuries. A brother of the man who had once had a relationship with the witch ended up in prison. When the witch died, she was completely alone.
187847: A weaver who worked for people from Heusden, Koersel, Zolder and Meeuwen always took a medlar stick with him when he went to deliver his finished cloth. When the man was coming back from Meeuwen, he saw an enormous dog in Kelchter.
187856: Some men, among them Pierke B., came to a café in Eksel; they could conjure mice and moles. Those men could also make the animals disappear again at once.
187875: It was said that on Christmas night a naked child sat on the wall of the church. People also heard bells ringing under the ground.
187878: On a farm on the Locht worked a farmhand who never did much, yet got all the work done. In one hour the farmhand managed to manure the whole field. When the farmer had gone to the priest for advice, the clergyman had said: "You must burn the clothes the farmhand wears while he works." One day the farmhand was working a long way off. Meanwhile the oven was lit to burn his clothes. Before everything had burnt up, the farmhand was already back. As soon as the farmhand found that his clothes were gone, he left for good.
187883: A boy went to herd the cows with his little dog. When he passed the house of the witch Koekelemie, she called: "Ponijke, Ponijke, come!" At that the little dog jumped in through the window of the witch's house. The boy called his dog back, but the animal did not come. A little later the witch said: "Fons, call now. Your dog will come with you now." And so it happened.
187893: When people could not churn butter, they blamed a witch who had recently visited.
187913: Next to a pond in Rutten lived a witch whom everyone feared. One evening a drunkard came by, to whom the witch said: "Well, you're out late!" At that the drunk man threw the witch into the pond. But the witch did not drown!
187917: Some men, among them Kupke L., went for a drink at Haagdoren. When they were going home, Kupke said near a wood: "If there's something here, let it show itself!" After that Kupke was instantly sober. He never wanted to tell what he had seen there.
187919: On Corpus Christi a man went by way of the Leeuw to Opoeteren. The man got lost and walked as many as three times around the same wood, which was called Dongelroot. Someone else once got lost at the same spot because he had followed a hare.
187923: A witch could bewitch a child by looking into the pram.
187939: A man had an eight-month-old daughter. One day the baby developed a swelling that would not go away. The mother suspected her neighbour of being a witch and therefore went to the priest of Berlingen. The priest said: "You must do penance for nine days and then go and ask the woman you suspect for something, but you will not get it. If the child makes it to the ninth day, it will be cured and then you will see a light burning in the witch's house." The priest went into his garden to pick a herb, a few leaves of which the mother had to tie around the child's wrists. On the ninth day the parents went to ask their neighbour for a jug of beer, but they did not get any. That night a light burned in the neighbour's house. The child was cured for good.
187942: A man from Maasmechelen went to fetch coal in Luik with the cart for the first time. A passer-by said to the man: "If you meet a dog on the way, say nothing, but hold a red handkerchief in your hand." When the man saw a dog, he did as he had been advised. A little later both the dog and the red handkerchief had vanished. In a neighbouring village a young man came to visit his girlfriend, who said: "Why do you have a piece of a red handkerchief between your teeth?"
187944: A man who had moved a boundary post during his life had to haunt after his death. The ghost carried a boundary post in its arms and kept asking: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" After a man had answered: "Where you took it from!", the ghost was released.
187964: A man had got into the church by a ladder in order to steal. When the man crawled through the window with his loot, he could go no further; it seemed as if he was nailed to the ladder.
187968: A man who went poaching saw a clergyman come out of a gate every night, reading.
187974: Some heather cutters from Scherpenheuvel were working in Dilsen. One of the men could conjure up white mice. Another made the plates on the mantelpiece dance without a single one breaking. Those men were probably in league with the devil.
187985: Around the castle of Rijkhoven people often saw a black coach driving, with a gentleman sitting in it. The coaches were always unloaded and loaded again very quickly.
187988: The mill of Lauw was haunted. At night a ghost there wrecked the whole mill. Whatever was repaired during the day was wrecked again the next day. A priest from Tongeren managed to drive the ghost away between midnight and one o'clock. That priest died shortly afterwards.
188019: Near the schans (1) (earthwork fortification) in Boekt a big filthy dog always roamed about. One evening a man on his bicycle was attacked by the animal. The man pulled out his knife and stabbed the dog. Later it turned out that the dog was a wizard from the neighbourhood.
188021: In the K. family in Muizen there was a girl who had entered a convent. Her former sweetheart had taken her out of the convent and married her. When the woman had died, she came to haunt. When the adults were working in the fields, the children in the garden were repeatedly frightened by a white glow. The parish priest advised the children to ask the ghost next time what it wanted. When the white glow next appeared, one girl was brave enough to ask the ghost the question. The ghost answered: "Whoever does good here will find good over there." When a friar came to exorcise the ghost, the woman said: "My children have two plots of land belonging to a poor man. They must give that land back." But because the land had already been sold, it could no longer be returned. For that reason the ghost still could not find rest. In the end the friar banished the woman under an apple tree.
188023: At midnight a glowing ghost wandered about on the tower of the castle of Jageneau.
188024: A man went to the café after work. After a woman had slapped him on the shoulder, the man got terrible pain in his arm. Because the doctor could not help, the man went to the priest, who read prayers over him and gave him a relic. A while later the man no longer had any pain.
188028: A farmer's wife who still had to milk the cow in the evening was visited by Johanna G. Because the farmer's wife still had a lot of work, she was glad that Johanna offered to milk the cow for her. When Johanna had finished milking, however, the cow became very restless. In the end the vet had to take away the cow, which had gone mad.
188029: A family in whose house the pots and pans began to dance by themselves at night consulted a friar. The clergyman came to read prayers over the house and said: "A woman will come to your house, but she will not get over the threshold." A while later a woman did indeed come asking for carrots. The witch could not get over the threshold.
188033: In Herkenrode there was a monastery where a man had been murdered. After his death the man walked back and forth all the time between the quarters and the monastery church. A man from Herkenrode often went to the pub on Sundays. After eleven o'clock the man no longer dared to go home because he was afraid of the ghost that appeared there between midnight and one o'clock.
188036: In the witch house a cat had come in through the hole for the water drain. One day someone managed to wound the cat with an axe. The next day the woman of the house was lame.
188038: At Aater de Steen (1) a dead man who had moved the boundary post of his field came back to haunt. One day people placed a drunkard behind the Steen and said: "When the ghost appears, you just answer him: 'Put it back where you took it from!'" After that there was no more haunting at Aater de Steen.
188045: In Beek lived women who could make mice without tails. When people came back from Beek, they always had great trouble getting home, because the road was blocked by all sorts of strange things.
188049: A forester saw a strange animal in the woods that looked like a roe deer and made great leaps. Terrified, the forester ran away. "I'll never come to that spot again," he decided.
188053: After his death the old miller of the Dalemolen came back to haunt in the shape of a dog. Because the dog sat under the stove all the time, a priest was sent for to banish the ghost. But no priest succeeded, for the clergymen themselves were not without sin. In the end one priest did manage to read prayers over the animal and banish it to the pool.
188071: Some men were planting beets with a machine when suddenly a witch passed by. At that moment the chain flew off the machine.
188077: A farmer from Lauw was fed up with his horses always being untied at night. The farmer had already tried several times in vain to catch the black cat that sat in the manger. One day someone wounded the cat in the paw. The next day the farmer's sister-in-law had a bandage on her arm. The farmer then said to his wife: "It was your sister!" The farmer's wife advised her husband to go to the priest.
188080: On Christmas Eve the farmer went to midnight mass with his family. One of the daughters stayed home because there were sometimes burglaries on such nights. Suddenly the girl heard a loud thump on the door. When she opened the door, she saw a good hundred cats.
188086: In the 'Spiekestraat' (?) and on the Meeswijkerweg there were many tree stumps. Many people were jumped on there by the werewolf.
188089: One evening near a bridge a girl saw a boy dressed all in black. The girl whistled at the boy, who immediately whistled back. The next moment a big werewolf appeared, which ran off again a little later. When the girl whistled once more, the boy no longer responded.
188094: A flower was found under the pillow of a bewitched child.
188102: In Romershoven there lived a witch who could conjure up mice and infest people with lice.
188119: Anyone out at night had better walk between the ruts of the cartwheels. As long as one walked there, one could not be jumped on by the werewolf.
188124: Will-o'-the-wisps could only be seen by certain people. They were the little souls of unbaptised children. A man who saw will-o'-the-wisps by a brook began to baptise the lights until they suddenly disappeared.
188129: By the tram stop on the main road in Herderen there was a haunted house. At night rattling could always be heard in the attic. In the end the house had to be demolished.
188132: At night a beguine came haunting by the little chapel in Beverst. The beguine had not given money to the poor.
188135: A man who had always been badly treated by his son came haunting after his death. The son nearly went mad from it.
188152: Near the chapel of the Hulsberg there was a pond that was used to find out whether a woman was a witch. Women who sank were witches. Women who stayed afloat were not witches (1). Because many women had been wrongly convicted at that place, a chapel was later built there. When people tried to move the chapel, there was much misfortune. The man who was to take the statue of Mary to another place fell from a scaffold the next day.
188156: A family from Herk-de-Stad always had misfortune because a witch often came to visit. The witch consorted with the devil. After they had put a relic above the door, the people had no more misfortune.
188160: If one could make a werewolf that had itself carried bleed, it changed into a human and could be recognised. Werewolves, however, could only be cut with a knife that had first been cut through the ground or through brown bread.
188165: On the Meulder Berghs farm in Molenbeersel there worked a farmhand who could change himself into a werewolf. When the farmhand was taking his girlfriend home one Sunday evening, he said to the girl on the way: "I have to relieve myself behind the hedge." A little later, to her great fright, the girl saw a big dog with glowing eyes rushing at her. The girl remembered the advice her boyfriend had once given her and threw her handkerchief at the beast. The next day the girl noticed that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
188183: The wild hunt was a group of witches who flew through the air in the shape of lapwings.
188184: The V. family in Beek had much misfortune with their cattle. One day a beggar knocked at the V. house and learned that the family was plagued by witchcraft. The beggar then said: "That's no problem at all. I can rid you of the witches if you can show me the stack of brushwood bundles where they live." The beggar threw some spurrey seed into the stack. From that day on the V. family had no more misfortune.
188188: A farmer whose cows were all dying through the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) went to the priest for advice. The priest sent the man to the friars of Achel. The friars gave the farmer a relic of a saint to hang in the stable. After a few days all the animals became healthy.
188191: The werewolf was a man who disguised himself with a sheet and then had himself carried by passers-by.
188192: Whenever the brother of Staaf V.J. came back from visiting his girlfriend in Viersel, he always saw two cats sitting by a well. At that spot the man always got lost. The man had heard someone say that his girlfriend and her mother were witches. One evening, as the man was getting ready to leave, he saw his girlfriend and her mother go out by the back door. At the well the cats were making a racket again. That time the man did not get home until nearly morning.
188198: One evening Theofiel went to a café on the Berg in Tessenderlo. Because Theofiel was drunk, he did not notice that the wife of Pol V.J., a supposed witch, had drunk from his glass. When the man went home, he got lost. He ended up in the deep ditch in the Heistraat.
188213: Someone saw a ghostly woman appear, who shook five-franc coins onto the ground and then vanished again.
188214: In the churchyard of Stamprooi there was often a dog that kept growing bigger and bigger. When people came closer, the dog had suddenly vanished.
188216: A little boy had been stroked by a witch who lived nearby. A few days later the child got a large swelling between his little legs. No doctor could help the child. One day the desperate mother said to the witch: "If anyone could help me, I would treat that person to coffee and currant bread." "Would you really do that?" the witch cried happily. "Yes, I would," the woman answered. Shortly afterwards the child was cured.
188227: A mother whose baby was ill had been advised by someone to cut open the pillow the child slept on. In the pillow a braided crown was found. After the crown had been burned, the child gradually got better. If the crown had been closed, the child would have died.
188235: Whoever had moved the boundary post of his land during his life had to haunt after his death. With the boundary post in his hand the ghost would then call: "Where must I put it? Where must I put it?"
188243: Louis D. went into the woods to fetch a cartload of pine and on the way passed Mie's house. Because Mie was a witch, she could not bear people driving past her house, but Louis paid no attention to that. When Louis had loaded his cart, he found to his great astonishment that the horse was standing back to front.
188261: In Lauw the witches came to dance a few times a year. After the gathering the witches flew away over hedges and hawthorns. One day a man wanted to go along with the witches. But he made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said "through hedges and hawthorns" instead of "over hedges and hawthorns". When the man reached the other witches, he was badly injured.
188266: A woman was plagued almost every night by the maar (nightmare spirit). She would then sweat a great deal because she stood at the edge of a well into which she was about to fall.
188284: A man hardly dared go along the Fontaine lane any more because there was a werewolf there. Werewolves were men with an animal skin on their back. If you saw someone with pieces of a red handkerchief between their teeth, you could be sure it was a real werewolf.
188290: A child who was often given biscuits by a woman fell ill and could no longer walk. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it recovered.
188300: A mother with a small child had been visited by a woman from Lanaken, who had said: "Oh, what a beautiful child!" From that day on the child cried all the time and fell ill. When the mother cut open the child's pillow, she found a wreath of feathers. The woman threw the wreath into the fire. The wreath did not burn but slowly melted away. After prayers had been read over the child, it behaved normally again.
188311: If one had struck a black cat, one could see the witch going about the next day with a cloth around her head.
188317: On the Vlooienberg behind the churchyard of Tongeren there were some old cottages that were haunted. At midnight the ghosts began rummaging about in the attic there.
188339: A man coming home between one and two at night met a woman who grew bigger and bigger. When the man made the sign of the cross, the woman suddenly vanished.
188345: One Sunday a man and a woman were sitting by the stove with their children. When a miaowing kitten came in, the man threw it back outside. Although all the doors and windows were shut, the kitten came in again. The man threw the animal outside again. When the kitten came in for the third time, the man threw the animal into the stove. Two days later he saw a woman who asked: "What did you do with the kitten?", to which the man replied: "Burned it". After that the man never heard anything of the witch again. Together with the kitten he had thrown a piece of a blessed candle into the fire.
188362: Some people lit the fire in the oven to burn the werewolf's animal skin. Before the skin had caught fire, the werewolf was standing beside the oven to save his skin. Three men had the greatest difficulty keeping the werewolf from jumping into the fire. When the skin had burnt up completely, the werewolf was released.
188363: On a farm the drowned son came haunting after his death.
188365: A young man had got an inflamed foot through the doing of a witch. When Kaat and Wiske went to the doctor for the young man, the witch came to ask whether she could borrow the flail. The young man agreed and then showed his inflamed foot. Because the foot would not heal, the flesh eventually had to be cut away down to the bone. After the priest had preached about witchcraft on Sunday, the young man wanted to have prayers read over his foot by a friar. He was not allowed to go, however, because his father feared a scandal in the village.
188366: The farmers of Kessenich went to complain to sheriff V. because all their animals had been killed the night before. A reward of a hundred guilders was then offered to whoever found the culprit. The hunt yielded nothing, however, and for the next eight days all was quiet. On the ninth day the goat of Stieneke, who lived on the Mooileman, was torn open by a strange monster. When the gentleman V.S. came hunting a few days later, he shot the claws off a wolf. He wanted to pick up the paw and found to his horror that it was a human hand with the thumb missing. On that basis a suspicious shepherd who was missing a thumb on one hand was arrested. In court the shepherd finally confessed that he had become a werewolf because the devil had taught him. The shepherd was hanged and then thrown on the pyre.
188378: A boy said to his girlfriend: "If you see a werewolf, throw a handkerchief at his mouth." When the girl saw a dog, she threw her handkerchief.
188385: Some people from Meelberg who had been to Tervant saw a kind of ghost on the way back, and threw a handkerchief at it.
188393: In Wallonia there lived a farmer who kept his money in a pot. Every time the man put some money in the pot, he said: "In the name of the devil". Because of this, nobody managed to take the money out of the pot. One night the man believed he had seen the devil himself appear.
188395: A man walking through the Broek in the evening saw a large dog with a chain lying in the middle of the road. When the man came closer, the animal stood up and jumped back and forth in front of him. The dog followed the man to the crossroads at the Fontaine-dreef. When a storm suddenly rose, the man hurried home.
188398: The witches were holding a gathering on the Grasbeemd near Janke V.T. When one of the witches had to sneeze, a passer-by said: "God bless you." The next moment all the witches had vanished.
188418: On a misty, moonlit evening a man was going across the fields to the mill. Suddenly he saw someone walking over the mist, with his feet a good metre above the ground. When the ghost reached the churchyard, it vanished.
188419: A woman from Jesseren could never find her clothes when she wanted to go to church. A witch made the clothes disappear.
188441: A girl who went to sleep on a Sunday afternoon had a terrible dream. It was the maar (nightmare spirit). It was caused by a heavy stomach.
188450: S.'s farmhand always experienced strange things. One day the reins of his horses suddenly snapped. Once he also suddenly found himself standing in the middle of a great fire. One day a dog as big as a foal came running up to the farmhand's cart. The animal climbed up the side of the cart. The frightened farmhand cried out: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph, help me!" The next moment the witch stood before him in her human form, and he recognised her. "Don't you dare tell anyone about this!" she threatened. The farmhand never revealed the witch's name.
188455: In the old days the people of Peer went to the butter market on foot. When a woman suspected of being a witch passed by, Riekske decided to play a trick on the witch. Riekske placed his feet crossed on the witch's path, so that she could go no further. A little later, however, Riekske got a severe pain in his back that prevented him from moving.
188456: People ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) felt a tightness at night and pain in the heart. Many thought they were going to die, but usually they survived after all.
188459: Some boys going to chop wood in the forest met the witch Stans R. Stans asked: "What have you all got with you?", to which the boys replied: "Only an axe and a saw to fetch wood." When the boys reached the forest, however, they found they no longer had anything with them. When they got home, they saw the axe and the saw lying in the barn.
188461: In Wezet lived a witch who sold bacon. A woman who did not want to buy bacon from the witch fell ill after a while. When the woman had recovered, the witch came by and said: "Look, there's a little mouse under the stone here!" The woman's daughter went up to the witch and cried: "Will you be gone soon, little mouse-under-the-stone, you've done us enough harm already!" After that the witch never came to the house again.
188462: Anna's child cried every night from half past seven until morning. A woman always came to Anna's and stroked the child's head. A relative of the child was praying with the friars when suddenly an old woman passed by and said: "You are sad. If you give me five francs, the child will get better." The next night the child slept peacefully.
188468: In the witch house in Engsbergen there were toads that jumped outside through the drain hole for the water. One night the farmer managed after all to skewer one of the toads on his dung fork. The next day it was found that the farmer's wife Trees was dead.
188475: A man who had spied on the witches and wanted to fly himself made a mistake when speaking the magic formula. Instead of 'over hedges and hawthorns' the man said 'through hedges and hawthorns', so that he arrived at his destination badly injured.
188482: A man from Mielen-boven-Aalst got lost in a large forest. As evening was falling, he went to spend the night in a nearby house. At night the man was woken by the sound of a man's voice. He thought: "That sounds like the voice of our former sexton." When he went to look, he saw the priest and the sexton saying mass. When the priest saw the man, he took him to the entrance of the cellar and said: "Here you will find two chests of money. One chest is for you. With the money from the other chest you must have masses said." The man did what the priest had asked and told his story to a friar. The friar explained to the man why the priest had come haunting. The priest of Mielen had fled from the French. On the way a gentleman had given him money for his keep and for saying masses. Some time later, however, the priest was murdered by the French before he had the chance to say masses with the money.
188493: Renier T., a farmer from Gelinden, had to go on pilgrimage. Someone else had promised to go on pilgrimage, but that person had been unable to keep his promise because he had died. The promise was then passed on to Renier. But the man had still not gone on pilgrimage. When he was walking home one evening, a foal suddenly jumped on his back. Renier had to carry the animal until he was almost home. The next day the man went on pilgrimage.
188499: A man who had to go to Eisden with the cart suddenly could go no further in Laak. The horses stood still as if nailed to the ground. When the man saw a woman standing on the road a little further on, he shouted: "If you don't get out of the way, I'll shoot you dead!", to which the woman replied: "I can do that better than you." The witch had a Brandenburger with her.
188513: A man who wore a scapular did not dare go home one Saturday evening because he had lost all his money at cards. The man was willing to sell his soul to the devil if he could give him the money. "Very well," said the devil, "but you must hang your scapular on a tree and sign the contract with your blood." After the man had done this, he passed a little chapel where he heard Our Lady say that he had to take back his scapular and then go to the priest. After the priest had read prayers over the man, the devil was so angry that he wanted to break the man's neck. But because the man was wearing his scapular again, the devil could no longer harm him.
188516: Tjoën V. was a poacher. One night he lay against a tree stump waiting for a hare to come by. After a while a hare came running up, but Tjoën did not dare to shoot, because the animal kept growing bigger and bigger. The hare sat up on its hind legs and asked: "Have the other hares come by yet?" Then the animal put its paws in its mouth and whistled just as a person whistles on their fingers. Tjoën was so frightened that he ran home like a madman.
188518: A boy was sitting outside on a summer evening while the cat lay asleep on his feet. After a while the cat jumped up and ran off. The boy called the cat back, but it did not come. Instead, a piglet without a tail came running up.
188525: A man walking home on a cold winter evening heard a little bell ringing by the brook. A moment later he saw a big black dog with a rattling chain approaching. The man suspected that the dog was the ghost of the drossaard (bailiff), which had been banished under the bridge for ninety-nine years. When the man ran home in fright, the dog followed him. Suddenly the dog flew silently through a thick thorn hedge. In the middle of the field the dog turned into fire and vanished.
188534: Henri J. set off at midnight because he had to be in Tongeren at two in the morning. When he reached the castle gate, he saw a white lady. The young man did not dare turn back and went on while the white lady walked ahead of him. With his stick he carefully lifted her long dress a little; he saw nothing but fire. At the end of the street the lady turned around and said to the young man: "At night you must not touch a woman, or you will find out what is what! Just this once I will let you go."
188537: A woman was talking to her neighbour, who was said to be a witch. Suddenly a black cat crawled out from under the neighbour's skirt. When the woman tried to chase the black cat away, the neighbour shouted angrily: "Just let that cat go, she'll find her way!"
188547: Will-o'-the-wisps were seen mostly near a marsh. They were the souls of the dead who came back because they still had something to tell.
188557: A girl who had to go and fetch petroleum at Mina's saw a white lady standing on a woodland path. The closer the girl came to the apparition, the bigger the white lady grew.
188559: In Zepperen lived a witch who could change into a black cat. One day a man threw a stone at a cat sitting in a tree. A little later the cat had vanished and the witch was standing under the tree.
188560: A man was accompanied on his way by a witch cat that walked ahead of him the whole time.
188575: The farmhand who worked at the castle of Voort slept in the horse stable at night. Suddenly a violent storm broke out and the farmhand saw that the horses had been untied. A while later everything was normal again. A witch had caused these strange things.
188594: A girl who had been touched by the evil hand began crying every night at twelve o'clock. After the brown friars of Sint-Truiden had read prayers over the girl, she cried no more.
188600: Some women going along the castle lane of Terbos to Hasselt were startled when they saw a werewolf with a chain around its neck lying in the ditch. Without fear Betje said to the animal: "Whether you are of God or of command, we are going on!" The next moment the werewolf crept away behind a tree.
188602: In Heppen the cabbages were always eaten by animals. One day a farmer shot at an animal in his garden. When he went to look, only the witch's handkerchief was still lying there.
