188603: Around Easter, Neer went poaching with some friends. The men set out at about eleven o'clock by the light of the moon. When a hare suddenly came running up, the men's gun did not work. A little later the same thing happened again. The third hare that came past sat up on its hind legs and asked: "Did those other two pass long ago?" Frightened, the men went to another spot. After one of the men had shot a hare there, another put the animal in a sack. Shortly afterwards a hare appeared and said: "Dearie, dearie, where are you?" The dead hare in the sack then answered: "Here with Thei in the little sack." Since then the men never went poaching again.
188617: A man had thrown a handkerchief at a werewolf and then quickly run away. When the man was in the café, he saw someone come in who still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
188620: A man coming round a bend was nearly frightened to death when someone walked along with him arm in arm. The harder the man tried to wrench himself free, the tighter the strange apparition gripped him. A little further on the apparition suddenly vanished. Afterwards, however, the strange creature hung on the man's arm twice more. When the man got home and told his mother, she said in fright: "That was a witch!"
188634: A man who went hunting with his dog suddenly saw a hare running. When the man wanted to shoot the hare, however, his gun did not work. The hare calmly sat down while the man put another cartridge in his gun. The man was nearly frightened to death when the hare raised not a paw but a hand. Even the dog seemed to be afraid of the hare. The hunter went on and met Frans, to whom he told what had happened. Frans replied: "Yes, that must be the same hare I saw recently."
188640: In a stable there was a ghost goat that jumped on the other animals and then vanished. The animals that had come into contact with the goat fell ill. After the priest had read prayers over the stable, the ghost goat no longer appeared.
188655: An engaged couple went for a walk in the fields. At midnight the boy had to go away for a moment. Before he left, he said to his girlfriend: "Here is a red handkerchief with white dots. If you see a beast, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little later the girl's handkerchief was torn apart by a wolf. When the boy came back laughing after a while, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
188656: At 't Jonckhold lived a witch who ran a café. When people sat playing cards in the café, the witch was sometimes suddenly gone. Then only a big white cat could be seen. When the woman came back into the café, her hair was still standing straight up.
188658: The werewolf usually hid behind the brick kiln between Kotem and Boorsem. A man who passed by there was jumped on the neck by the werewolf. After the man had carried the werewolf a little way, he was left alone.
188659: A man who had gone to play cards in Hamont was coming home in the evening. On the way the man saw in fright how a white woman floated towards him. The woman floated past the man without saying anything. Since then the man never went home along that road again.
188663: A little boy could make mice out of a handful of earth. When the schoolmaster saw this, he sent the boy to the priest. After the priest had baptised the child again, it could no longer make mice.
188665: A dead person who had been banished to a chest in the attic came back to haunt in the shape of a chicken that flew through the roof.
188678: One Sunday evening Janneke was going from Rijkhoven to Waltwilder. On the turnstile by Ciliske's house sat two black cats. Six times Janneke tried to hit the cats. But because all his attempts failed, the man went to a nearby café, where he told his story. Janneke had two brave men accompany him, but even the three of them together could not knock the cat off the turnstile. In the end Janneke had to go to Waltwilder by way of the Ketelveld. The following Sunday Janneke was escorted all the way to Waltwilder by a whole pack of cats.
188679: It was said that a werewolf appeared on the road to Donk. A man met a big dog there that howled terribly.
188697: A farmer who was said to be a werewolf always carried a collar with him. When one day the farmer had forgotten his collar, people tried to burn the thing. The farmer felt it, however, and was instantly standing by the fire.
188698:
The villages of Beek and Stamprooi lived at odds with each other for some thirty years because they could not agree on the boundary. Stamprooi wanted to have a piece of the Beker Broek.
On the first Sunday of Lent, the day the fire-men came, the man who would later become mayor often went to Molenbeersel to watch the fire-men. Seven fire-men would then walk one behind the other, exactly along the boundary line between Beek and Stamprooi.
188700: De Pietsoog had a small child that simply would not grow. When people went to the hermitage in Achel on the child's behalf, the father said: "In the pillow there is a doll with pins. When the doll is full of pins, the child will die. You must take the doll out of the pillow, but for the child it is already too late."
188704: A child had fallen ill after a witch had visited. When the witch came by again, the child recovered.
188719: In Sint-Truiden there was a piece of land that was barren because the ghost of a commander of the Teutonic Order came to dance there at night. He danced with a black cat, which was the ghost of his beloved, whom he had never been able to marry because a commander of the Teutonic Order was not allowed to marry.
188723:
In Kerniel there was a witch called Katrien. One day a woman took shelter from a violent thunderstorm in Katrien's house. The woman knew that Katrien was a witch, but the weather was so bad that she had no choice but to take shelter. Katrien was happy when there was thunder and lightning. During the storm the windows and doors of the house opened and closed by themselves. The witch said: "They are coming to visit me. The storm ought to be ten times worse!" Meanwhile the frightened woman quietly prayed the Gospel of Saint John.
When Katrien lay on her deathbed, she could not die. The priest had to read prayers over her for two days.

To recognise a witch, it is best to boil white onions in a brand-new pot until you hear the church bells ring. At that moment the witch will come into the house.
188754: In the park of the castle of Betho there was a haunted little house among the walnut and chestnut trees.
188757: A black cat followed two men from Dilsen all the way to Boyen.
188774: A girl had noticed that her boyfriend had the threads of a handkerchief between his teeth. The girl then said angrily: "Get out of here, for now I see what you are, you ugly werewolf!"
188784: During catechism class in the church, a boy made mice out of a handful of sand. After the lesson the boy had to come to the sacristy. After the priest had baptised the boy, he could no longer make mice.
188789: The road to the Nassenaar field was often blocked by a thick chain stretched across it. To get through, one had to say: "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, break." After saying that formula, the chain would break and the way would be clear again. Anyone who met a ghost could protect themselves by saying: "Luck of all good to soul and body."
188798: A man had four children who died one after another through the doing of a witch. The witch came in, touched a child and said: "Yes, yes, a beautiful child!" After a clergyman had barred the witch from the house, the man had three more healthy children.
188802: A girl could make mice without tails. When people asked her why the mice had no tails, she answered that she had not learned that yet. Later she could also make mice with tails.
188803: A man walking across his field in the evening heard someone calling: "Where must I lay it? Where must I lay it?" Without fear the man answered: "Put it back where you took it from!" Since then the ghost with the boundary post has never been seen again.
188807: A dog with a chain and a bell often walked through the village. The dog would then lie down in a pit somewhere. Many people fought the dog, but they could do the animal no harm.
188809: A man owned a horse that was bewitched. Whenever the man rode the animal on Bocholt territory, the horse always began to limp, while on Beek territory it had no trouble at all.
188813: When a witch stroked someone's head with the words: "My sweet, good man", that person got lice.
188815: A weaver from Boekhout who had many children regularly went poaching to earn a little extra. One night he lay on the lookout behind the Heksenwei when he suddenly saw a hare. The weaver shot, but the hare stood up on its hind legs, waved at him and then ran away. A little later a second hare came and did exactly the same. When a third hare came running up, the weaver wondered whether it was wise to shoot at it. At that the animal waved its paw and said: "Well, weaver, have my friends come by yet?" Filled with mortal fear, the weaver ran home.
188822: When people were in a bad mood because they had not slept well due to something lying heavy on their stomach, it was said: "He has had the nachtmaar (nightmare spirit), leave him be."
188831: Every evening a man was visited by a dead beguine who knocked on the door with her hands and left two blackened prints on the wood. When the man asked her what she wanted, the beguine answered: "I am in hell because not enough people pray for me!" Since then the ghost has not appeared again.
188834: A woman was cutting grain in the field with a sickle. When a hare suddenly came running up, the woman cut the animal with the sickle. The next moment a well-known witch lay on the ground in front of her.
188837: In the 'koekeloereboske' in Maaseik a white friar walked about at night, reading a book. He did no one any harm.
188840: A large stone cross hung on the front of the Hooghuis in Koersel. It was said that someone had once been murdered in that house. Behind the house was a cellar to which the ghost had been banished for ninety-nine years. Whoever passed by there in the evening came back with a torn coat.
188847:
The power of witches can be neutralised by keeping the thumbs clenched in the fists or by putting a coin under the threshold. In 1920 a woman from Sint-Truiden put a coin under the threshold to take away the power of an old beggar woman.
When a witch had come to a child's cradle, the cradle was afterwards full of vermin.
Crossroads were favourite haunts of ghosts.
188852: Wim P. was coming back with Karel and Willem D.B. from the barber, where they had been shaved. When they saw a pig running along on the way back, one of the men said: "Let's try to catch the sow. Whoever gets hold of the animal can fatten it up. Then we'll celebrate with a glass of beer!" But as soon as the sow was past De Welf, it turned into a flame! It was a ghost animal.
188857: When the skin of a werewolf was burnt, the creature was instantly standing by the oven.
188870: A little child lying in bed with a severe headache had been touched by the evil hand. Every time the child laid its head on the pillow, it began to cry with pain. The mother discovered that the feathers in the pillow had formed a thick lump. The child was bewitched.
188894: A man had gone to visit his girlfriend in Wèzet. On the way back the man met a white lady who went along with him. The man, however, lost his way. The next morning he found that he had ended up at the house of C.
188898: In the past a beautiful white lady walked around the castle of Printhagen.
188923: Some children had died because their pillow was full of pins.
188927: In Tongeren a dog roamed about with a chain around its neck. If that dog sat down on the doorstep of a house, someone in that house would die within twenty-four hours.
188930: In the old days people often got lost through the work of a witch. People would think they saw something and walk towards that spot. Only when they heard the church bells ring could they find their bearings again. Usually they were then sitting on a broom bush somewhere deep in the woods.
188933: A widow whose cows got swollen heads and would no longer eat went to the priest. "If you won't come, I'll go to the dean of Peer," the woman had said. After the priest had done something with the cows, the animals were cured.
188942: A shepherd who was spending the night in a hut was visited by a cat. The man said to the animal: "Ah, my dear pussycat, how pretty you are!" The cat replied: "If you hadn't spoken so nicely, I would have broken your neck tonight!"
188946: Some people were coming back from Kermt through the woods when they suddenly saw a fire without flames and without smoke. It was a ghost fire.
188947: A schoolboy who herded a farmer's animals in his spare time had found a little magic book somewhere with which he could turn himself into a magpie. When the parents noticed the boy's strange behaviour, they took the book away from him.
188956: A witch always went knocking on people's doors in the evening, so that the children were very frightened. One day the people decided to chase the witch with axes and dung forks. The witch turned into a cat and climbed into a tree along the Maas. In the end a branch of the tree was chopped off, so that the cat fell into the water and drowned. Later the witch's body was fished out and burned.
188962: At Charel V.S.'s, the cows were always untied and many animals died. The daughter could not make her First Communion because she was suddenly covered in lice. The friar advised the farmer to send the maid away, as he held her responsible for the evil. As soon as the maid was gone, no more strange things happened at the farmer's.
188969: A man working for a woman whose mother was a witch said: "The greatest witch in Limburg may bewitch me." The woman then said: "Then I dare bet you can't walk through the field here," to which the man replied: "You're already just as annoying a witch as your mother!"
188975: A couple went to Liège with their little daughter Sien. The child had accepted a sugar lump from a witch. Because the little girl's face was deathly pale the next morning, the woman took her daughter to the doctor. When the doctor turned out to be unable to help, they went to Zjang from the Vennestraat. But Zjang did not know what to do either. Sien's grandfather suspected that his granddaughter had been touched by the evil hand and advised his daughter to go on pilgrimage with the child. In the end Sien was no longer ill, but the child had got a swollen little foot. A hospital treatment of a year and three months could not cure the foot, however. One day the woman was advised to take her daughter to a certain Harie B. Harrie began praying for a long time, ignoring the continuous knocking at the door. For the woman who had bewitched Sien was standing at the door. "You must put honey and flannel on the little foot. In eight weeks the foot will be healed." The foot did indeed heal, but it never grew again.
188989:
Will-o'-the-wisps seen in dark places in the evening were little souls from purgatory that could not get into heaven because they were stillborn or had died unbaptised for some other reason. People believed that on seeing such a light they had to pray a Hail Mary.
In reality the lights were glow-worms.
188999: A man who was always jumped by a werewolf in the evening was advised by an old man to take a knife with him. When the man managed to make the werewolf bleed, the beast changed into a good friend of his. One day in a café the man addressed his friend with the words: "Damned werewolf". At that the friend left the café and went away for good.
189023: One evening a man from Liège saw witches dancing in a wood in Diets-Heur. The man was afraid and wanted to move on, until one of the witches came up to him and offered him a cup of wine. The man took the cup and said: "God bless you!" The next moment all the witches had vanished. When the man was left alone in the meadow, he looked at the cup and saw that the witch's name and address were in it. The man decided to bring the cup back to Liège. The witch must have known the man would come, for she was already waiting behind the door. After roughly taking the cup from him, the witch promptly shut the door and left the man standing outside.
189047: A man travelling with horse and cart suddenly could go no further. An old woman was working in a nearby field. Because his cart was stuck, the man went to the woman and asked: "Why is this? Does this happen here often?" The woman replied: "Yes, it happens quite a lot, because I do it!" Angrily the man struck the woman with a whip. "Go on now," said the woman, "it will work now."
189049: A man who went to fetch coal with the cart one evening saw a foal with glowing eyes lying on the road. When the foal jumped up, the man stabbed the animal with a nail. The next moment his neighbour stood before him.
189051: A farmer was startled when he heard an owl screech at night. The next day an accident happened in the farmyard.
189066: The maid who worked on a farm in Rummen was a witch. She made all the animals die.
189077: During thunderstorms the vuurman (fire-man) came into places together with a flash of lightning.
189080: In a house in Werm a large black dog sat under the table. Because they could not chase the animal away, the friars were called in. After the friars had exorcised the dog, the animal was gone.
189107: A man saw a fiery man or a shooting star in the sky. According to popular belief, that was an omen of war. Shortly afterwards the First World War broke out.
189113: A woman whose sister had had a baby went to Paal with her brother on a cold winter morning. On the way the two saw a light flying along the road. Later they heard that a woman had died that night. The light had been that woman's soul.
189125: A man who was out late at night was jumped on by a werewolf. After the werewolf had had itself carried a little way, it left its victim alone.
189127: Witches often appeared in the shape of a cat. If one shot at such a cat, the next day one would meet a woman with a wound.
189128: A man who was said to have moved a boundary post during his life came back to haunt after his death. When someone had advised the ghost to put the boundary post back in its original place, the ghost was seen no more.
189131: The bells of the church of Genk had a bad godmother and godfather. On Christmas night the bells were heard ringing in the Molenvijver.
189134: Some boys went to catch squirrels in the pine forest on a Sunday. When they passed the house of a witch, the hag said: "Let the squirrels live." The boys asked: "Why?" The next moment there were seven or eight squirrels in the tree. The boys were so frightened that they ran away as fast as they could.
189146: In the old days there were phantom horses without ears that carried people across the water. A man sitting on such a horse suddenly cried: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph, this horse has no ears!" The next moment the horse had vanished and the man was lying in the water.
189152: A young man was going out with the daughter of Boze Griet. When the boy was visiting his girlfriend one evening with his cousin, Boze Griet asked: "Would you still dare to go to Monmalle now?", to which the boy replied: "Why not?" Then the witch said: "On the Kassei a big black dog might well come after you!" Because the boy was convinced that no dogs were about in the evening, he accepted the challenge. On the way, however, the pair were startled by a big black dog after all. Then one of the boys took a stick and drew a cross on the road with it, saying: "In the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost". The dog could not get past the cross.
189160: In the Biesen castle one of the rooms had been locked because it was haunted. There was always blood on the wall.
189174: By the Brulmolen along the brook, hares often sat clapping their paws. "That is not a good sign," said the miller. Some time later the Brulmolen burned down.
189191: Some people driving a cart of flour past a witch's house in Vechmaal could go no further. Because the cart was stuck, they had to unload all the flour.
189194: In the Rouvènne (?) there was a pike that had moss on its head and that no one could catch.
189203: In Melveren, a hamlet of Sint-Truiden, lived a certain Koopmans. One day Koopmans went with his girlfriend to the fair in Kortenbos. This man, however, had made a pact with the devil, which meant he regularly had to roam about as a werewolf for a few hours. Because Koopmans suddenly felt at the fair that the moment had come, he said to his girlfriend: "If you meet a dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth. That way the beast won't harm you." Because a werewolf cannot cross a cross, he has to unravel the threads of the handkerchief one by one before he can go on. The girl answered: "No, stay with me!", to which her boyfriend said: "No, I urgently have to run an errand." When Koopmans had gone, an ugly black dog came up to the girl. She immediately did what her boyfriend had told her, whereupon the dog tore the handkerchief to pieces. A quarter of an hour later Koopmans came back. His girlfriend told him she had been scared to death while he was gone. Further on the two went for a drink in a café. The girl took a good look at her boyfriend and cried out in shock: "You swine, it was you yourself, because the threads of the handkerchief are still between your teeth!" Koopmans said she was just imagining it, but the girl never wanted to see him again.
189215: Geertrui van de Z. from Neerglabbeek could make mice, but she could not get the tails on them.
189228: Some boys had been visiting a few girls. On their way home the boys came across a black cat. A little further on a cat was scratching at a tree stump. One of the boys kicked at the cat, but he could not hit the animal. Angrily the cat leapt at the boys. Then the animal changed into something that looked like a donkey. Terrified, the boys went into Marie H.'s house. A hellish din could be heard around the house, at which Marie said: "Oh God, those are witches. You had better stay here."
189233: A woman going to the shop met a witch on the way, who pulled leaves off a hedge and said: "Look, these are seven different leaves from one hedge." After long hesitation the woman accepted the leaves. When she got home, the woman found that her house was full of fleas. The friars of Beverlo and Heusden advised the woman to put ferns in the house.
189236: When Grèke E.'s son was standing outside urinating, he saw 'de gleunige' (the glowing one) fly over the pond towards the bridge.
189238: The woodcutters Jan van H. and Frans W. drove with horse and cart from Dorplein to Budel. The men usually let their horses drink at the house of Maria B., who was said to be a witch. Although Maria turned out not to be home this time, Jan and Frans let their horses drink there anyway. When the animals had drunk, however, they stood still as if nailed to the ground. A little later Maria came home and asked: "Why are you standing there?" The men explained that their horses would not go on. Maria said: "Go on, try it again now." After that the horses could go on.
189241: The castle of Gedeu was haunted. One evening a man lay down under a tree near the castle. A few moments later witches and ghosts appeared and began making a racket in the tree. Near the castle there also lay a felled oak, under which a fire was once seen. Whenever the oak was moved, the next day it lay in its usual place again. So people suspected that a ghost had been banished to that oak. One day poachers saw a hare leap into the wood. The animal made a hellish noise as it did so. A little further on ran a black dog, and shortly afterwards a cat came running up. When the poachers struck at the cat with a stick, the animal attacked them. The poachers quickly made off. On a turnstile they saw a hare sitting, which said: "Can you get through? Otherwise I'll get out of the way."
189242: A beggar from Munster had to play the werewolf. When the beggar was away, people found the animal skin he had hidden in an oak. Before the animal skin had burnt up, the beggar died. He was, after all, in the grip of the devil.
189245: A witch visited a mother who had just had a baby. After the witch had stroked the mother's head, the poor mother was covered in lice.
189248: On a dark winter evening a little boy was followed by a witch with a stick. Although the lame witch could not catch up with the boy, she was already standing at the hedge when the boy got there.
189265: In the Peel lay a sunken bell that could be heard ringing at Christmas.
189274: When D. went hunting in Houthalen, he saw two hares playing. When he shot at the hares, his gun did not work. After the parish priest had loaded the gun, the man was able to hit the hares. The animals turned out to be a mother and a daughter, who were both witches.
189278: In Budel it was said that Johanna G. was a witch. A woman whose children cried every night after Johanna had visited went to the priest for advice. The priest came to read prayers over the house and advised the mother not to let Johanna in any more. After that the children no longer cried at night. One evening Johanna knocked at the door because she had fallen. After the mother had tended Johanna's knee and drunk a cup of tea with her, the children began to cry again.
189280:
Whenever the witch Jutemke had spoken to someone, that person always had bad luck.
A man who was picking pears quickly ran off when he saw the witch coming. While running, the man hurt his ankle and had to stay in bed for eight days.
Whenever people walked past the witch's house, they always called out: "Miaow, miaow!"
189282: A little boy could make mice out of a handful of dust. After the priest had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
189284: In Glabbeek a man saw a little white horse running in the meadow at night. The man went outside to catch the horse and tie it up with a chain. The next morning it turned out that the man had chained up his own wife in the barn.
189302: In Kessenich a werewolf was recognised because he still had the threads of the handkerchief his girlfriend had given him between his teeth.
189304: A cat was sitting on a stone at a crossroads on the road from Neeroeteren to Opoeteren. Two passers-by noticed the animal. One of them said: "That's a pretty pussycat; I'll knock her off the stone!", to which the other said: "No, you'd better not do that at this strange hour of the night." But the first would not listen and struck the cat with his stick. As the two went on, they heard the injured cat wailing for hours, which left them both speechless with fear.
189306: A farmer's wife had a complaint in her eye. Some time before, a woman had come peddling, but the farmer's wife had not wanted to buy anything. In revenge the witch had made the farmer's wife ill.
189307: A farmer whose piglets all died sought help from a certain Dignef. When the man had explained the problem, Dignef took scraps of cloth, rolled them up and then threw them into the water. With each scrap Dignef threw into the water, he named a place of pilgrimage. When a scrap sank, Dignef had said "Hasselt". So the man had to go on pilgrimage to Hasselt. After that not a single piglet of his died.
189310: Two brothers who had been in the army for fifteen years cursed all the time and refused to go to church. They worked in a brewery on the Beek. One evening one of the brothers was walking home, shouting: "If there is a devil, let him come!" When the man reached the Spaanse Brug, he suddenly bumped into something. He fell to the ground and felt hair everywhere. Since then the man has never cursed again.
189328: The old master of the mill had died and came back after his death as a werewolf. In the house there was always a black dog that knocked over the chairs and opened the cupboards. Many priests had already come, but none had succeeded in banishing the ghost; every priest had committed some sin or other in his life. One day a young priest came to the dog. The animal said: "You once stole two cabbages." The priest answered: "Yes, but I was only ten years old then. I have long since paid for all those cabbages." A while later the young priest came back with two other priests. Together they managed to drive the dog into a stack of brushwood bundles. Then they set the bundles on fire, so that the dog leapt into the water. The ghost was banished to the Jeker for ninety-nine years. Next year that period is up.
189332: A boy who went to play cards every evening usually came home around midnight. In the stable the boy always saw the ghost of his mother appear. On the advice of a priest, the boy one night asked what the ghost wanted. The spirit answered: "A pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel on bread and water". Afterwards the boy got the money the woman had hidden in the chimney.
189341: A man worked as a hand at a mill in Maaseik. A young priest also lived in the mill. The night before the priest was to say Mass, he could not stay in his bed for a minute because the devil tormented him.
189347: Suske had been out with a friend. When they parted, Suske said: "Sleep well." The friend wandered through the water all night and did not get home.
189354: In the past people often saw lights that went on and off. Those lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
189356: A witch had visited Fin L. and laid her hand on the head of Fin's child. In the evening the child fell ill and in the night it died.
189359: A man going to work in the morning suddenly felt as if sand had flown into his eyes. People were convinced that the witch Leen had made the man blind.
189364: Sint Ool is a hamlet near Opoeteren named after Saint Odilia. It was said that the little church of Sint Ool was destroyed by the Norsemen. Since then the bell was heard ringing from under the ground every year on Christmas night at exactly twelve o'clock.
189384: The postman's wife had just given birth to Philomène, her first child, when she was visited by Ciliake. The witch had picked up the child and then left. As soon as Ciliake had gone, however, the baby began to cry loudly. Because the doctor did not know what to do, they had the witch come to the child again to undo the harm she had done.
189398: A good marksman managed to shoot a hare that nobody could hit. The next moment the marksman saw a woman standing before him.
189402: In Paal lived a witch who could cover someone in lice and who could conjure the house full of little rabbits.
189415: A black cat always appeared in the Seminariebosje in the evening. Because they suspected the cat was a witch, people no longer dared to go there.
189419: The countess of the castle of 's Heerenelderen was a witch. One evening the countess went outside. The watchman also happened to be going for a little walk and saw the countess fly into a tall tree. "I may shoot at anything that flies," said the watchman, and he loaded his gun with devil's dung. The watchman shot the countess's bracelet to pieces. He took the jewel with him and the next day went to ask the count where his wife was. "She is sick in bed," answered the count, whereupon the watchman said: "The countess is a witch, because I saw her fly," and he gave the count the bracelet as proof. The next day the count had his wife burned as a witch on a cart.
189428: In Tongeren lived a witch who had a little shop. When the shopkeeper's children had been given a sugar lump, someone often fell ill. One day the mother of a boy from the village went on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel together with the witch. Because the boy was going camping in Aarschot with a socialist youth movement, he went to his mother hoping to get some pocket money. Then the witch said: "Boy, you have got talcum powder with you, haven't you?" The witch sprinkled some talcum powder in his socks and then said: "I will pray an Our Father in Scherpenheuvel so that you arrive safely in Aarschot." When the boy cycled to Aarschot with his friends, he suddenly had a painful fall, although he was riding on a flat road. The spokes of the wheel were broken. "Damn, that was that rotten witch!" the boy cried. The boy had to pay 130 Belgian francs to have his wheel repaired.
189437: Louis P. kicked at a black cat that was bothering him. The animal then jumped onto his neck and scratched him until he bled. Louis took a stick to hit the cat, but the animal had already vanished without a trace.
189440: A woman who had promised during her life to go to Scherpenheuvel had to come haunting after her death because she had not kept her promise. Every night at twelve o'clock the ghost came knocking on the door. After a while the ghost came knocking on the bed at three in the morning. One night a light was seen appearing around the statue of Our Lady. Then the priest said: "That is a woman who had promised to go on pilgrimage. If she comes again, you must say: 'If you are of the devil, depart. If you are of God, speak.'" After the man had been to Scherpenheuvel, his wife was released.
189441: The wild hunt was really the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a legendary robber band). When the bokkenrijders went somewhere, they were not allowed to know the destination. Their leader would then say: "I swear that we must go through hedges and through hawthorns." The bokkenrijders often held meetings in the Vlaams Huis in Glabbeek. One day two curious men had gone there. Although they had actually come as spies, they had no choice but to join the bokkenrijders. The two men often pretended to go robbing people, but in reality they betrayed the names of the other bokkenrijders. When they went flying one day, they made a mistake when speaking the magic formula: instead of "over hedges and hawthorns" they said "through hedges and hawthorns". When they arrived at their destination covered in blood, they decided never to go along with the bokkenrijders again.
189445: Some men went to steal wood in the forest at night. One of the men prayed a rosary so that God would forgive the theft. Suddenly the men were surrounded by a flock of sheep that they could not feel when they walked into them. The thieves quickly dropped their pine trees and fled home.
189456: A man went to Eksel to find someone willing to go into the army in his place. On the way the man was followed by a strange dog that he could not hit.
189467: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. A man who wanted to baptise one will-o'-the-wisp was pushed into the ditch by the mass of will-o'-the-wisps that also wanted to be baptised.
189472: A man who often played cards until midnight at Lins K.'s always met a cat near an old house on his way back. When the man had crawled through the hedge by his house, the cat had vanished. Since the day the woman from the old house died, the man never saw the cat again.
189477: A man went to buy a calf from a little old woman near the bridge past the Locht. In the end they were only five francs apart. Because they could not reach an agreement, the woman said to the man: "You'll be back anyway!" But on his way home the man got lost. After wandering about for two hours, the man finally came back to the woman's house. "See, I said you'd come back!" said the woman. The man then decided to pay the extra five francs. When he set off home the second time, he found the way at once.
189478: In the Wakkenstraat there lived a sorcerer who could make mice with tails. People often went to the sorcerer to ask for help.
189481: A man who went to fetch hay at night repeatedly struck at a cat sitting in the middle of the road. But the cat always came back and sat in front of the horse.
189484: A man had secretly climbed into someone's fruit tree to eat some fruit. When the man came back down, someone was waiting for him, who said: "You have stolen. But you will not be punished if you give me your body and soul. In return I will give you twenty-five years of happiness." The man accepted the offer and was happy for twenty-five years. One day the man had helped a woman in the woods. In return for his help the man had received a piece of wood, with which he was to strike if he was in trouble. When the devil came to fetch his victim after twenty-five years, the man wanted to have a good meal first. The man climbed into the fruit tree and the devil went with him. When the man came down, he struck the tree with the stick. The next moment the devil was seized by the branches of the tree. In exchange for freeing the devil, the man asked for his own freedom back.
189486: A man who owned a book of magic could make mice. In the end his book of magic was taken away from him.
189497: A man had asked his wife to let him know something once she was dead. When the woman was dead, she always came in the evening to pull her husband's toes.
189505: A farmer who met a cat on his way home said to the animal: "What a pretty pussycat you are! If you're cold, you may come and warm yourself at my place." The cat, however, disappeared immediately. A long time later, the farmer was sitting in his farmhouse one winter evening when that same cat suddenly walked in with the words: "Here I am then, farmer!" The cat sat down for a while and then left again.
189506: By the oak wood at the Motje in Diepenbeek, a castle is said to have sunk long ago. A farmhand walking home at night met a white lady at that spot, who said: "At twelve o'clock I will make you happy..." The man ran away as fast as he could.
189515: Werewolves had a skin in which they went about in the evening to frighten people and jump on them. If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could recognise him. A werewolf who had been unmasked said: "If you dare to reveal me, the red rooster will crow at your place." Werewolves who were betrayed set fire to their betrayer's house.
189517: During the funeral of a family member from Zittaart, Selm entered the church without anyone seeing him. When the priest was blessing the body, a hare came into the church. There was no way the people could get the hare out.
189520: A child saw his dead aunt sitting on his bed every night. The priest advised the people to go to Scherpenheuvel. On the way the child said: "Look, auntie is coming along over the water and it doesn't even splash!" When the people had prayed for a while, the child saw his aunt fly upwards.
189525: The 'yellow woman' of the Luikerpoort bewitched children with her evil hand.
189526: In Kozen lived a witch who tormented people and animals by speaking spells in rhyme.
189530: In the Schulebroek a fire-man roamed about and chased people. A hand was burnt into the gate of the 'dark farm'. That farm once burned down long ago.
189533: When a man in Voort walked past the farm of D., strange things suddenly happened. The tiles fell off the roof, the trees were pulled out of the ground and a hedge blocked the man's way. A little later everything was back to normal.
189545: When Fons S. went outside one evening, he saw something strange. The man went to fetch a stick and struck at the strange apparition. The next day Trien V. said she had ended up under a cow. Everyone believed that Trien was a witch.
189550: A man coming back from visiting his girlfriend saw, between Glons and Sluizen, the white lady appearing in the field and then disappearing again. After the man had not seen the apparition for some weeks, the white lady suddenly turned up again.
189560: A farmer's wife coming back from the forest with her brothers met a woman on the way, who gave her a sprig of cherries from her tree. As soon as she got home, the farmer's wife buried the sprig in the ground because she did not dare eat the cherries. When the farmer's wife came back from church the next Sunday, the woman asked whether the cherries had been tasty. "Oh yes, very tasty," the farmer's wife answered. Then the witch said: "You ugly scoundrel, you stuck the sprig in the ground! You'll never get anything from me again!"
189563: A man who had taken a boy to Tongeren on a cart was followed on the way back by two nuns dressed in white who wanted to climb onto the cart. The man was scared to death, but fortunately he managed to escape from the nuns.
189565: Witches chased children with a broom to frighten them. If a black cat was seen when someone lay dying, that person would soon be dead.
189574: A man who was bewitched always woke up screaming at night. Someone tied a handkerchief with bacon around the man's wrist. The man had to keep the handkerchief on for eight days and pray for eight days. After that the illness was over. The illness was called 'de fieflèn' (?).
189581: In Lafelt a large black dog roamed at night, visible only to the heirs of the owners of the field where the dog stayed. One evening Jan L. went to dig potatoes in that field. Around midnight Jan saw the black dog approaching. Jan had to defend himself with all his might against the dog that came to claim his field.
189586: On the Heike a woman came haunting whose husband refused to ask what she wanted. In the end the dead woman's family was sent for from Liège. The family had to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for her. When that had been done, the ghost was released.
189587: The farmer's little son had come home through the meadow in the evening. The boy had seen a ghost with ugly horns crawling over the ground.
189589: A man who went to fetch willow branches in the evening noticed to his great fright that he was being chased by a big black dog with green eyes a good fifteen centimetres across. When the man reached the little chapel, he saw a flash of lightning in the sky. At that moment the beast vanished. The man had a headache for two weeks afterwards.
189590: Many people called Niel a witches' village. A woman who lived there was bewitched and had been lying paralysed in bed for years. One day they sent for a man who claimed he could help the woman. The man said he would unmask the witch. In the evening he lit a fire in the woman's house. If anyone knocked at the door, she was not to open it. After a while there was indeed a knock, but nobody opened. After the witch had knocked three times, she came in uninvited and sat down on a chair by the fire. The witch could not sit still, however, because the man kept reading aloud from a special book. The witch kept shuffling back and forth with her chair until she came dangerously close to the fire. Then she suddenly said: "Must I burn alive here now?", to which the man replied: "If you undo what you have done to this woman, you are free!" Then the witch went to the woman who had been ill in bed so long and said: "Get up, you've lain here long enough!" The woman got up and was cured.
189606: In Alken, between midnight and one o'clock, a black dog always appeared wearing a chain with little bells around its neck. After seven years or so, there were three men brave enough to deal with the troublesome animal properly. When the dog came running up, one of the men stabbed at it with a dung fork, but he could not hit the beast. Because the dog turned out to be only a phantom, the second attempt to hit it also failed. Furious, the man threw the dung fork on the ground and gave up. The next day the dung fork was found some three hundred metres further on.
189610: It was said that Dien B. was a witch. Dien always wanted to give money to small children. The children, however, were warned by their parents not to accept the money. Otherwise Dien might pass her witch's power on to them. When a child had nevertheless accepted money from Dien, the money was put into the ground.
189615: In Vrijhern lived a girl who crawled up the walls and scratched at everything. Because the parents suspected that little Marie had been touched by the evil hand, they sent for Voddemarie, also called Koekmarie. Voddemarie cured the bewitched child.
189618: A strange woman lived in a meadow in the Bossestraat. When people passed by there around eleven at night, they saw the woman and her two daughters dancing around the pear tree. Sometimes they sat inside playing with coins. The husband was beaten by his wife and daughters, but he himself could not hit anyone.
189634: The witch Bet L. had flooded the house of Anneke de G. In the end the friars had to be called in to exorcise the house.
189637: Because many horses died at the G. family's in the Dorpstraat, a friar was sent for. After a crucifix had been placed under the threshold of the stable, there was no more misfortune.
189640: Some girls coming back from Lafelt were frightened because a black cat followed them the whole way.
189644: Near the old farm lived a man who drowned after driving his cart into a pond. At night the man came haunting in a golden coach with four horses. At midnight he disappeared into the pond again.
189654: A man always heard knocking on the wall of his house. Because his wife was becoming skin and bone, the man decided to go to the abbey of Tongerlo with a friend. The father gave him holy water and a prayer card and told him to say the prayer nine days in a row. When the man said he would like to see the witch for once, the witch appeared. The next day the man's friend laid a holy object by the road. A little later the witch came past on her way to the shop. But she had to turn back because she could not get past the holy object. As soon as the man had removed it, the witch could go to the shop.
189669: A farmer travelling with horse and cart suddenly could go no further. When Toin came to stand beside the horses, the animals could suddenly move on again.
189670: In the house where a sinful woman had died, a black dog came and lay under the table. After the friars had exorcised the house, the dog was not seen again.
189679: Anyone who had touched a witch was afterwards covered in fleas. Witches, however, did not have power over everyone.
189683: A man from Leopoldsburg left for Diest with horse and cart every Wednesday at around one or two in the morning. Because the man claimed to have seen a ghost, people no longer dared go outside in the evening. A sergeant was once stabbed in front of garage H. No one ever knew who did it. After his death the murderer had to come back to haunt to atone for his crime.
189696: A fruit seller always saw a fat white rabbit sitting in the garden of the Minderbroeders (Friars Minor) in Tongeren. One day the man had grabbed the rabbit and taken it home. Once home, the fruit seller found only a big stone in his basket.
189716: Waaslichten (will-o'-the-wisps) were small fireballs that rose up from marshy ground. Devout people baptised the lights, which then went out.
189718: Some children took the animals to graze on the heath in Dorplein. When Fien S. came by, a girl shouted: "Witch, witch!" Fien then took a twig and struck the girl on the back with it. The girl had a thick red stripe on her back, which only disappeared when Fien died.
189722: A man who had moved the boundary post of his land had to haunt after his death. The ghost was invisible, but it kept calling: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" One day, on the parish priest's advice, someone answered: "Leave it where you took it from!" Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
189736: A man always went to Scherpenheuvel on foot because his brother still had something on his conscience when he died. Whenever the man went on pilgrimage, he was always accompanied by his brother's spirit.
189737: Near Kessenich there once lay a large town called Vijvere. Because its inhabitants led a godless life, the devil was able to drag Vijvere off to hell. Afterwards the inhabitants could sometimes still be heard wailing.
189741: In Hermée in Wallonia the devil roamed at night in the shape of a big dog with a long tail. The dog wore red clothes and walked on its hind legs like a person. People were all afraid of 'le diable de Hermée'.
189759: A man walking home at night saw a strange white object lying on a plank over a brook. It looked like a ball of sheep's wool, but when the man came closer, the little ball moved. A few days later another man had the same experience; when he tried to poke the little ball with his stick, it suddenly flew onto the road.
189760: Every evening a horse-drawn coach drove around the earthwork with a gentleman dressed entirely in black. People believed it was the previous owner, who had just died.
189762: A woman who walked down the lane every Sunday evening always saw a white ghost appear behind the haystack.
189773: Two men who had been playing cards walked home together. In a tree-lined lane the men met a werewolf, who asked for a light. The men then gave the werewolf a sound thrashing. The werewolf was Freke G. After the chaplain of Beringen had burned Freke's book of magic, Freke behaved like a saint who went to Mass every day.
189778: Toon K. was seeing a girl who was said to be a witch. One day, as the young man was riding home, he saw a cat sitting by the road. Toon threw a stone at the animal's head. The following Sunday Toon saw that his girlfriend had a plaster on her forehead. After that Toon no longer wanted to see the girl.
189779: Naar was walking with a friend through the woods of Kleine-Brogel to Grote-Brogel. Because his friend was walking ahead, Naar suddenly shouted: "Damn it, the werewolf is on me again!" Because his friend did not help him, Naar had to carry the werewolf until he was home. In the end Naar died by the evil hand.
189780: Aldegonde F. went with her sister to the market in Tongeren. When the women saw a hare sitting on the road to Mopertingen, they picked up the animal and took it with them. But because the hare grew heavier and heavier, they finally had to let it go again. That hare must have been a werewolf.
189783: If you wanted to chase away a werewolf, you had to throw a handkerchief at its mouth. A girl who had done so later noticed that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
189785: A farmer and his wife could not make butter from the cows' milk: the milk kept foaming. One day a woman said to the farmer's wife: "You should go to the priest of Nieuwerkerken. Perhaps he can help you." The farmer's wife went to the priest and took a bottle of milk with her. The priest shook the milk for a good half hour, but it kept foaming. Then the priest said: "It is witchcraft. You must no longer give milk to anyone for free. You must always sell it, even if you only ask half a cent. Also, you must put salt in the milk. You must not lend anything any more either, especially not yeast. The woman who bewitched the milk will come and ask for a slice of bread tomorrow, but you must not give her anything. You will be amazed when you see who the witch is." The witch was a woman from the neighbourhood; she was Route's wife and she was always speaking ill of others.
189786: A child who was often visited by a witch fell ill and died. In the pillow the child had slept on, a wreath was found. When the wreath was closed, the child died.
189788: After someone had struck a cat, the witch Bet had a broken leg.
189799: A newly married couple went to live in the sexton's house. But P., the sexton's relative, was a witch. The witch made the husband and wife fall through the bed on their first night. When the man told someone about it, he was told: "Yes, I can well believe it, you do have such a fat wife!"
189812: When Net came home between midnight and one o'clock, she heard music and saw the witches dancing near Schurhoven. A little later a black cat came and rubbed against Net's leg. The moment Net touched the cat, the animal vanished.
189822: A man coming back from Hasselt by moonlight saw a ghost standing by the road near K. When the man said "Good evening," the ghost answered: "Leave be what stands and let go what goes."
189828: A man was woken at night to go to work with someone else. When the man arrived, it turned out to be only two o'clock in the morning. His wife had done that to him.
189829: A farmer had a farmhand who was a werewolf. One day the farmer sent his farmhand away for five hours, so that he had the chance to burn the boy's collar. When the farmer had thrown the band into the fire, the farmhand was suddenly standing beside him to save his collar. When everything had burnt up, the boy was released.
189830: A man cycling back from Maastricht was suddenly surrounded by a ghostly fire.
189832: A man was afraid of a big black cat that he always saw in the woods. Because the man believed the cat was an evil spirit, he did not dare shoot the animal.
189837: An unmarried woman had a potato field on the 'witches' hill'. The field was full of weeds. In a certain month the weeds were not to be pulled up, because then the witches would make them grow again.
189844: A man who had gone to Luik to buy coal came back at night with his horse and cart. The man was nearly frightened to death when, on the Vrerenberg, he saw a white ghost appear beside the cart and the horse. As soon as the man began to pray, the ghost was gone. Some people also took holy water with them to protect themselves against such things.
189846: When the shoemaker Dolkes V.R. was walking home, he had to carry the werewolf. The man was covered in blood because the werewolf's nails cut into the backs of his knees.
189854: A man travelling with a cart came across a cat, which jumped into the wheel and let itself be spun round. The more the man struck at the cat, the more cats jumped into the wheel. In the end the cart could go no further.
189856: Every time a man passed a witch's house with his ox, the ox stepped into the belly band of its harness.
189866: A man coming back from the fair in Bommershoven around midnight met a woman on the paved road. The man was afraid of the woman, but he thought to himself that he could always hit her in the neck with his stick. Then the woman said: "Is the camp of Beverlo still far? I want to go and look for my son there." The man answered that she should follow the paved road to Sint-Truiden and then ask the way somewhere.
189868: A man driving his cart to the brewer got a fright when in Bovenwezet a cat suddenly jumped onto the cart. Because the cat kept pestering him, the man knocked the animal off the cart. The next moment the cart was full of cats. The man broke out in a cold sweat. At a crossroads the cats all jumped off the cart.
189874: In the past a spirit wandered between Guigoven and Kortessem with a boundary post in its arms. The ghost kept asking: "Where must I throw it?" After the ghost had put the boundary post back, it was released.
189890: A man who had been to visit his girlfriend met a dog in the forest on the way back that was at least 1.30 m tall. The dog kept bumping against the man's trousers. Because he was afraid, the man took a different road than usual. When he looked back, he saw a large crack in the ground. There was no trace of the dog. At home the man told his father what had happened. The father replied: "You should have come home a bit earlier, because between twelve and one all evil rabble is about."
189899: A girl met a witch, who asked: "What have you got in your bag?", to which the girl replied: "A pound of salt." The witch then said: "When you get home, you will have a pound of lice in your bag." And so it happened.
189900: In a spring in the marshy Vetwei in Neerrepen lies a bell. On Christmas night the bell rang at exactly twelve o'clock.
189901: A little boy was coming back with his father from the fair in Hasselt. Suddenly the boy saw a will-o'-the-wisp hovering above the water next to the pine wood. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died unbaptised.
189908: A woman had heard that black cats had something to do with witches.
189910: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a big dog comes at you in the meantime, throw my handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. A little later the girl noticed that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. After the girl had told the priest what she had discovered, the clergyman gave her this advice: "You must spy on that boy and try to find out in which tree stump he keeps his collar. Then you must send the boy away and meanwhile heat the oven with three bundles of brushwood. Two people must pray and the other two must hold the lid ready to slam the oven shut." No sooner said than done. When the werewolf's collar was in the oven, the boy flew against the lid. The boy had to be carried home, but he was cured.
189921: Strange things happened in a farmer's stable. Sometimes the animals refused to eat at all. On other days the feed was gone so fast that the animals could not possibly have eaten it themselves. There were always little mice in the manger, although there had been none at all in the hay.
189926: A man who was loading a cart with wood and straw one evening to go to Maastricht the next day said to his farmhand: "Harie, look over there! Take the lantern and look!" A black lady who said not a word was walking by the road.
189927: At catechism class in Bilzen there was a girl who could make mice out of earth. After the priest had read prayers over the girl, she could no longer make mice.
189959: An old woman from the village was very friendly when she met a mother with a child. A little further on the mother found that the child was covered in lice.
189962: Anyone ridden by the maar (nightmare spirit) could no longer move.
189970: On the Lodderkuil people burnt the band of a shepherd who was out with the sheep. The next moment the man was already standing by the oven to save his band.
189981: A man had seen a white ghost in the churchyard of Rommershoven crawling into a grave.
189989: Many witches used to live in Lauw. One of them always eavesdropped on people at the window.
189990: Werewolves could only be met in the evening in deserted places. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he became human again.
189997: The son of a woman who ran a café had a horse that was dying. Because the animal neither recovered nor could die, the vet advised the boy to go to a witch master in Luik. The witch master held up a mirror to the boy and said: "She has your horse in her power." In the mirror the boy saw the face of his own mother.
190004: A man whose child always cried at night decided to take a look in the attic. The attic turned out to be full of cats. The man broke the leg of one of the cats with a cudgel, whereupon an old woman suddenly stood before him. The next day the whole village was saying that the witch had broken her arm.
190007: The drossaard (bailiff) of the Hobos came back to haunt after his death. At night the horses were untied, and in the morning they were foaming at the mouth in the meadow. In the evening the ghost would come and sit on the threshold or under the fire in the shape of a black dog. When a priest was sent for to banish the spirit, the ghost said: "When you were little, you stole carrots from someone". In the end a friar from elsewhere came and banished the drossaard's ghost under a bridge in Kerkhoven (Lommel).
190010: In the Duivelsput in Tongeren bells were heard ringing at twelve o'clock on Christmas night when you threw a franc into the pit. The Hoogkerk of Tongeren had sunk into that pit. Whoever went to the Duivelsput never came back. Once people tried to measure the depth of the pit with a stick, but they never reached the bottom.
190028: Louis went after the devil with a dung fork.
190031: A farmer's wife who could not make butter was visited by an old woman, who said: "Just keep churning!" The farmer's wife found chaff in the butter churn.
190033: A child did not dare to sleep alone because all kinds of noises could be heard in the attic. Because the house was haunted, an aunt was sent for to look after the child.
190040: There used to be many cats around the witch Bet aan de Zwaan (?). Bet's husband once said: "If she can't torment other men, she torments me."
190043: A man coming back from Eerk by moonlight one evening saw a white lady with a child standing in the lane of Henegouw. It was not a real ghost, but everyone was afraid of that white lady.
190064: Fien N. went to a farmer in Maarheze to buy a cow. Because Fien found the price far too high, she said: "If you don't lower your price, you will end up paying for it yourself." The farmer refused to lower his price, so Fien went home empty-handed. A few days later the farmer's cow gave not a drop of milk, and after a week the animal was dead. That is how people found out that Fien was a witch.
190091: Because V. came back to haunt after his death, a friar was sent for to banish the ghost to the Elckert. The ghost was led to a tree on a chain. At first the ghost still had the strength to break the chain, but after the friar had read his prayers, the ghost could no longer do so.
190094: The late Baroness Sara V.T. came haunting in the Repenstraat, where she had lived. At midnight the ghost told the baron to give a sack of grain to the farmhands and maids. After that the ghost appeared no more.
190097: A farmer from Wellen coming back from Loon in the evening met a smith from Alken on the way. At a toll barrier the smith suggested they rest a while. But the farmer fell asleep because of all the beer he had drunk. When the farmer woke up, he asked: "Smith, where are we now?", and the smith answered: "We're home, farmer!" The farmer could not believe he was already home and found it strange that his leg hurt. Then the smith said: "That may well be, for I held you rather low. On the way you struck your leg against the cross of a church tower."
190112: A man who was attacked by a dog wanted to hit the animal with a stick. He could not hit the dog, however, because it kept jumping between his legs.
190117: A man from Overrepen had gone to visit his girlfriend in Colmont. When he was almost home, he was surrounded by a pack of mewing cats. Near his house, cats were sitting all over the barriers. Those cats were in fact witches.
190121: In the Molenveld lived a farmer who had much misfortune with his sheep. The man also had a horse that could not even pull an empty cart because it had a crooked leg. One of his sons had hanged himself and the other had suddenly died for no explicable reason. The farmer did not trust his wife one bit. One morning she dropped dead while cutting bread. Later the friars of Urmond came to hang a relic in the stable.
190136: A soldier stationed in the Netherlands was allowed to go home for a while. On the way the man was harassed by a werewolf that would not let him cross the bridge. The man then took his knife and stabbed the werewolf in the head on the spot where he had been baptised. The next moment a naked man lay on the ground. It was a farmer who regularly came to spend the night with the soldiers. The werewolf was overjoyed because he had been freed, and he begged the soldier not to betray him.
190147: Long ago a werewolf roamed Lauw, scaring the wits out of people. People had often tried to shoot the werewolf, but the beast seemed invulnerable. When one day the werewolf's skin was pulled off, he became human again and was freed.
190151: On the hill in Bree a man lived with the parents of the parish priest of Gerdingen. Among the shepherds who came there to eat in the evening, there was one who never ate. When that shepherd had been out at night, he was very sick in the morning. When people had spied on the shepherd one evening, they saw him sit down on a tree stump and then turn into a dog. In the tree stump lay a collar that made him a werewolf. On the priest's advice, the people sent the shepherd away the next day, so that they had the chance to burn his collar. When they were about to throw the collar into the fire, the shepherd was immediately standing with them.
190154: Because all of Juul's horses died for no explicable reason, someone said to his wife: "Marie, you must not let anyone into your stables any more!" After a friar had exorcised the stable, the witch could no longer get in.
190156: A witch told a man: "You'll break your legs in a moment!" Two minutes later the man broke his leg.
190187:
Shoemaker Minus L. had four fine pigs. One day Bet V.D.R. passed the sty and cried: "Oh, what lovely little pigs!" A few days later the pigs all had swine erysipelas.
Some time later Bet saw a cow with a full udder and said: "How much milk that cow will give!" The cow had to be sold, because it gave not a drop of milk any more.
190199: One day the mayor sent his farmhand out to fetch clover from the field. When the farmhand passed Betje's door, he suddenly could not go any further. The horses pulled as hard as they could, but it did no good. The farmhand then stabbed the axle of the wheel with a knife, and then the horses could go on again.
190202: A poacher wanted to shoot at a hare, but his gun did not work. The man saw six hares run past. A little later a seventh hare came, which asked whether the other six had passed already. Those hares were witches.
190209: Werewolves had a collar. If you met a werewolf, you had to give it something red. A man who went walking with a woman said on the way: "I have to go away for a moment. If something comes at you in the meantime, throw your red handkerchief at the apparition." A little later a werewolf came running up and tore the red handkerchief to pieces. When the man came back, the woman saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
190210: A woman found a cat under her bed and could not manage to chase the animal away. So the woman took a red-hot hook from the stove and struck at the cat with it. The next day the neighbour woman had a large burn on her arm.
190218: One twin brother was so weak that at the age of two he still looked like a newborn. A woman who was suspected of being a witch always came to visit. After a relic of the Sacred Heart in Hasselt had been placed under the little boy's pillow, the witch could no longer get to the child. The boy eventually recovered completely.
190228: A man who had pulled out the boundary post of his field did not know where to set it down. The man had already walked around with the post for a whole night when he met someone who said: "Carry the post back to the place where you took it from!"
190229: At the corner of the station people heard a ghost ringing a bell. Nobody dared to go and look.
190252: In a marsh behind the Kneèp in Diepenbeek the bells were heard ringing twelve on Christmas night.
190264: If you could make a werewolf bleed, he was freed.
190265: Bosmei had once quarrelled with the neighbour of her friend Beaat. One day Beaat and her neighbour were baking bread. Beaat's bread was well baked, but her neighbour's had failed. When the neighbour wanted to make syrup, she had to boil it for at least fourteen days before it set. Bosmei had caused that.
190267: On the heath in Dorplein stood a farmhouse where two old sisters lived. Anyone walking across the heath at night could hear loud knocking and shouting. Because such strange noises came from the farmhouse, people believed it was haunted.
190270: A woman taking butter to Hasselt saw a will-o'-the-wisp rise out of the ditch in a marshy area. Will-o'-the-wisps appeared mostly near churchyards, because phosphorus rose from the ground there.
190271: A werewolf had itself carried by someone it could overpower. It would then jump onto that person's face. If one could cut a werewolf in its skin, it changed back into a human.
190287: A man walking through the fields saw a woman who was said to be a witch. A little later the man saw a meowing cat with little bells. That was a witch's cat.
190291: A man who had been to the mill was returning with his wheelbarrow in the evening. When he was followed by two cats, the wheel of the wheelbarrow suddenly turned the other way. As soon as the cats had disappeared, everything was normal again.
190292: The church of Oud-Leef sank into the marsh of Zoutleeuw. In the past its bells were heard ringing there on Christmas night. One day the statue of Mary of the Ossenweg was dug up in a nearby field.
190295: A boy had fallen asleep in his girlfriend's house. Meanwhile the girl said to her mother: "Shall we go?" With that mother and daughter set off over bushes and hawthorns to the priest's wine cellar. When the boy woke up, he rubbed his feet with witch's grease so he could go to the wine cellar too. But the boy made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said "through bushes and hawthorns" instead of "over bushes and hawthorns". On arriving in the wine cellar the boy was badly injured.
190298: A woman coming home in the evening suddenly heard the sound of hooves behind her. When the woman started to run, the horse started to run too. At P.'s, the horse struck its hoofprint into the barn door. A cross was made on the door.
190301: A child had fallen ill after being bewitched by the witch Mie G. Because the doctor could not help, Jef went to Tongerlo for the child. The man could hardly reach Tongerlo, and when he stood in front of the abbey, he could not see the building.
190309: In Mechelen-Bovelingen a count came haunting at the castle. On Christmas night the priest went to the castle to banish the ghost. When the count's spirit appeared, the priest held up a cross. Then the ghost disappeared for good.
190313: A woman went to ask Kajt, who lived on the Heikant, something. The woman knocked and went in. Nobody was home, but a cat was sitting on the trough used for kneading dough. When the woman came out, Kajt's children said: "But our mother is inside!", to which the woman replied: "No, there's only a big cat inside!" Kajt was a witch who could turn herself into a cat.
190315: A girl was in a relationship with a boy from Milmort. When the boy went to a nearby meadow for a moment during a walk, he said to the girl: "Here is my handkerchief. If you meet a dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth!" As soon as the boy was gone, a big black dog came running up and tore the handkerchief to pieces. A little later the boy and the girl went into an inn together. The girl saw that the boy still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. She never wanted to see the boy again.
190318: When Pee van Sus was coming back from the fair in Sluizen with two friends, he met two ladies in silk dresses at Sluizen-Kruis. The ladies said to the drunk man: "Hey sir, would you like to be taken home by two gentlemen or by two ladies?" Pee answered: "What would I do with two gentlemen? I'd like two ladies!" Then the ladies came up to him and walked along arm in arm with him. When Pee reached the next house, the ladies had disappeared.
190334: A boy who had met his girlfriend at the cemetery was returning home between midnight and one o'clock. When he reached the 'Heilig-Hart op de Graaf', he saw a black dog cross at the tram stop and walk straight through a black closed barrier. The boy was relieved when he reached the cigar shop in the Maastrichterstraat.
190336: Klaas, a man from Vlijtingen, was often ridden at night by the maar (nightmare spirit). A white figure would then crawl onto his bed, making the man feel very tight in the chest.
190343: When a witch had come to visit, people could not make butter. After the parish priest had given a blessed medal to put under the threshold, they could churn butter again.
190346: In the old days people often spoke ill of each other. A man who stood in front of the mirror by the chimney could see the face of the gossip in the glass. Other people could not see it.
190352: In Meeuwen a man went hare hunting. But every time the man saw a hare, his gun did not work. Someone advised the man to smear some grease from the Easter candle on the gun. The next time the man did indeed manage to shoot a hare; he shot his own daughter dead.
190353: In Vlijtingen a girl had to step aside for a coach with one horse that came past. The girl's father had seen nothing.
190382: A boy walking home met a woman who gave him two cakes. When the boy told them at home that he had been given two cakes, his parents immediately took him to Diest, where the Crosier fathers exorcised him. The boy's parents never let the woman who had given the cakes into their house.
190387: A man saw a black dog in the field and struck the animal on the snout, so that it began to bleed. The next moment the black dog had changed into a man from Spouwen.
190396: A boy who was out walking with his girlfriend felt that he was going to change into a werewolf and said to the girl: "If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." On seeing a dog, the girl did what her boyfriend had advised. When the boy came back a little later, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
190397: When Anneke, a witch from Koninksem, had visited someone, the children fell ill the next day. One day a girl even became pregnant from the witch's visit.
190402: A man noticed that he always had bad luck in the evening when a certain woman had come by. One night the man had seen a mouse and stamped on the animal. The next day that woman had a wound on her leg.
190411: A man from Rotem had hidden in a tree stump the collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. When someone had thrown the band into the oven, the man had to be tied up so that he would not jump into the fire to save the band. As soon as everything had burnt up, the man was saved.
190442: Between midnight and one o'clock the werewolf went out to attack people. On the advice of the friars, a man threw a red handkerchief at the werewolf. Later he met someone who still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
190459: Some men who went to herd the cows saw three witch cats dancing in a ring in the meadow. One of the men said: "Kittens of Minne, where do you come from?" The animals answered: "Had Janneke V. not spoken to us that way, we would have broken his neck."
190462: In Boekhout there once lived a boy who could make mice by stamping on a little heap of earth.
190480: One evening the inhabitants of Rukkelingen were very frightened because a red fireball hung in the sky. When someone died the next day, people said: "That is the fireball's fault."
190486: In the past the dead were not yet banished at their funeral with the Gospel of Saint John. Because of this it often happened that a dead person came back to haunt. And so a man walked about behind the church, asking the whole time: "Où faut-il que je le mette?" (Where must I put it?). For during his life the man had moved a boundary post. One night a drunkard answered: "Va le mettre où tu l'as trouvé" (Go and put it where you found it). Since then the ghost has not been seen again.
190497: If a certain woman had stroked your head, all your hair fell out the next day.
190504: A farmhand who had to play the werewolf had hidden his animal skin in a hollow oak. When the farmhand was away, the others wanted to burn the skin in the oven. As soon as the animal skin caught fire, the farmhand jumped into the oven to save his skin.
190505: Trui V. G. could not bear that the G. family had more cherries on their trees than she did. So the witch made the cherries fall off the G. family's tree.
190511: In Budel lived a witch called Katrien L. Because people were afraid of Katrien, they tried all sorts of ways to get the witch out of her house. When Katrien's uncle knocked on her door one day to take her to a lunatic asylum, the witch said: "I know what you have come for, but I am not going. Besides, you will end up in the place you want to take me to sooner yourself." A few weeks later the uncle did indeed go mad. But Katrien L. never left her house.
190529: Werewolves sometimes had themselves carried by their victims.
190534: A man who was woken at night by a terrible racket coming from the henhouse got up to see what was going on. He saw a mysterious light dancing back and forth in the henhouse. After the man had shot at the light, it was still there. The moment the man stepped into the henhouse, the light had vanished.
190552: Some people keeping watch over a dead woman heard knocking on the shutters. When they had heard the knocking three nights in a row, one of them went to the dean. The clergyman advised them to ask the ghost what it wanted. It answered: "When are you going to build the little chapel?" As soon as they said: "We'll start tomorrow", the knocking stopped.
190555: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. If you wanted to baptise a will-o'-the-wisp, you had to say: "In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit". You were not allowed to add "Amen".
190559: A man peddling leather was looking for the house of a shoemaker in Stamprooi. The man muttered: "I wish I knew where that shoemaker lived". A cat sitting by the road replied: "I can tell you that". The man was so frightened that he ran away, deathly pale.
190570:
In a house in Heppeneert some farmers sat playing cards. Suddenly a stranger came in and asked if he could join the game. A little later all the clubs had suddenly vanished from the deck. When one of the farmers looked at the floor, he saw that the stranger wore no shoes and had two horse's legs with horseshoes instead of feet. The man quickly made the sign of the cross, whereupon the stranger flew through the wall, leaving a great fire behind.
Later the devil appeared to a drunkard who liked a game of cards. The devil offered the drunkard twenty years of luxury in exchange for his soul. The drunkard agreed, but kept praying to Saint Gertrude. When his time was up, the drunkard went to the bridge where the devil stood waiting for him. Because the drunkard was accompanied by Saint Gertrude, the devil could do nothing to him. The man converted and died a Christian death.
190574: Anyone coming back from the fair who walked past a witch's house around midnight was surrounded by cats. Such cats could not be caught or killed.
190576: The M. family made hats. One evening the women were still busy late trimming some hats for a funeral when they suddenly heard wonderfully beautiful music. When they went outside to listen better, they noticed that the sound came from the crooked apple tree in the mayor's meadow. But they could not see anything there. Around that apple tree a circle could always be seen where the grass had disappeared completely.
190578: When Berbke had touched a child, the child was bewitched. When Albert had a relationship with Berbke, he was always covered in boils. The boils disappeared during the period when Albert no longer visited the witch.
190580: Some young men were chopping down trees when suddenly a big black dog came running up. Because the dog might be a witch, nobody dared to kick or hit the animal. A little later the dog had suddenly vanished. In the place where the animal had been walking stood a witch who said: "Good morning, boys!" Nobody dared to say anything. "They all say I'm a witch," the woman said to the boys.
190587: A woman had seen a witch pricking a little doll in order to torment someone.
190598:
Betje, a witch from Overrepen, always tried to get near newborn babies. The children she touched all ended up with a disability, such as a hunchback, a short leg, a hand without fingers, and so on. A woman who had just given birth and was home alone bolted all the doors because she heard Betje trying to get in.
