The witch was not only after children, by the way; whenever someone had a litter of piglets, she was there too.
190619: Two sisters who lived next door to each other heard knocking on the door of the cowshed at midnight. The next night there was knocking on the door of the passage leading to the house. After that there was even knocking on the door of the house. The following night the door of the house opened by itself. Then the women saw the spirit of their dead mother standing there. The women decided to go to the friars of Rekem with their savings and have some Masses said. When the husband of one of the women came back from Maastricht, where he worked, he saw an old woman walking down the street. After a Mass had been said, the spirit was no longer seen or heard.
190623: In Meeuwen a bell once fell from a church tower. When people tried to raise the sunken bell, a little old woman came by and said: "Ah, you've almost got it up!" The next moment the bell fell back down. No one ever succeeded in raising the bell.
190624: A witch had predicted that only crippled children would be born in a farmer's house. The man who came to live in the house had all healthy children, except the eldest son, who had two 'bleinje' (?). That son's eldest daughter had a crippled child, and a man from the village from Mazelhoven had a simple-minded child.
190637: A young man coming back from Riksingen, where he had visited his girlfriend, met a white lady in the Henisstraatje, who walked along arm in arm with him and then suddenly disappeared.
190650: Whenever Charel went to visit his girlfriend in Gessel, a black cat always jumped in front of his feet. That was a witch.
190653: The Geuzentempel in Alken was built by a man who never went to church. In that building there was a window that could not be closed in any way. People believed that the spirits came in through that window.
190657: A man was followed 'op de Motten' near the Riedijk by a large werewolf in the shape of a dog.
190666: A bewitched farmer from Tienen had had himself exorcised and had been cured by it. Because the farmer had led a bad life and had not done penance, he became bewitched again. Sometimes the farmer saw the witch sitting there. She forced him to jump onto the same stone. Another time it seemed as if the farmer was being driven towards the pond. When the man was playing cards, he suddenly could not move. Sometimes the farmer went blind or began to drag his leg. In the end it even went so far that the farmer could no longer speak. The witch made the farmer walk backwards. One day the parish priest said to the farmer: "If you go through that meadow, you will see the witch, but you must not harm her."
190676: One evening Selm had to drive some thirty or forty cats out of his house. One cat was too fat to crawl through the drain hole. So Selm stabbed the fat cat in its backside with an axe. The next day his mother lay in bed with a wound on her backside.
190683: A black cat haunted the road to Halen. A man who had struck at the cat got a paralysed leg.
190691: A hunter who often failed to shoot a hare had a priest bless all the bullets for his gun. From then on the hunter could shoot every hare.
190706: On a dirt road in Hoelbeek, people were often jumped on by the werewolf. That werewolf had itself carried as far as the cross at the end of the road. If people made the sign of the cross, they were also rid of the werewolf.
190709: Everyone knew Dorese L. was a witch. A mother of twins quickly made the sign of the cross with holy water on one of her children when she saw the witch coming. But the mother did not get the chance to make the sign on the other child too. The next day the other child was ill.
190711: A wizard could turn the jack of spades from the deck into a bottle of gin.
190715: When Willem Maesen went to mow grass, a cat suddenly jumped onto the road and bit him in the leg. After the man had kicked at the cat, he heard a rustling in the trees. The next moment as many as a hundred cats appeared, making a hellish din. The man trembled with fear and called for help. As soon as the man spoke the name of Our Lady, all the cats vanished.
190716: A man driving his cart to Bocholt met a little old woman in a cloak at the chapel in Kaulille, who said: "Boy, you're going to get lost here!" The man answered: "I don't think so, I know the way here very well!" A bit further on the man came to a brook, which he crossed easily. The second brook was somewhat wider, but he got across that too. The third brook, however, was so wide that the man had to make a detour. Strangely, the man had never before seen so many brooks between Kaulille and Bocholt. He reached his destination two hours later than planned.
190724: A family whose children all died a few days after birth sent for the doctor. He asked whether the house was properly closed off everywhere. When the people went looking, they discovered that a cat always crawled in through the drain hole. When the hole had been blocked, the animal came in through the front door. Then the farmer broke one of the cat's legs. The next day the neighbour woman was walking around on a crutch. From then on not a single child died in that family.
190732: A man had got lice after an old woman had come to ask him for alms.
190733: In Runkelen a child was once killed by the fire-man. The fire-man had burnt his five fingers into the door of the house.
190750: Isabelle from Beverst often came to a woman in Hoeselt who could heal animals. But Isabelle fell ill after being bewitched by the healer's neighbour. In the end a man from Wèzet came to the girl with a Black Lord (a black crucifix). After three days of praying the girl was cured. She did have to keep wearing a ribbon always.
190752: In the old days a black cat was often seen sitting on a turnstile. Even if you knocked the cat to the ground three or four times, you never got past it.
190754: In the old days people were often jumped on by the werewolf, which had itself carried. Stina always advised people to take a red handkerchief with them. The werewolf would then be unable to harm them.
190757: At Peter H.'s in Mopertingen, a man came haunting who had been beaten to death in Eigenbilzen. When that man's mother went on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, the ghost burned a hand into the woman's handkerchief.
190760: The witch who lived on the hill made everyone's cart get stuck. Only when the witch went back inside could people go on.
190772: In every stable Voddemarie had been in, the animals soon died. The friar exorcised the witch until the sweat dripped from his head.
190776: A farmer's wife taking her cow to the meadow met a witch, who said: "What a fine cow you have!" When the farmer's wife wanted to milk the cow, she could not get a drop of milk from the udder. Although the witch had seen nothing, she knew in the evening what had happened.
190777: Witch cats often went dancing on the heath of Soerendonk.
190797: On a farm there worked a maid and a farmhand who were in a relationship. One evening the farmhand went walking with his girlfriend when he suddenly said: "I'm going to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." When a filthy dog came running up a little later, the girl did as she had been advised. In the evening the farmhand and the maid sat eating together. To her great dismay the girl noticed that her boyfriend still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl never wanted to see the farmhand again. After that the young man left for good.
190798: An attic in the Opperstraat was haunted. At midnight a loud bang was always heard there. In the end the priest had to be sent for.
190810: Because V. had toothache, he went to consult the parish priest of Tongeren. The priest said: "You are V. from Tongeren. Do you owe anything anywhere?", to which V. replied: "Yes, I still have to pay five cents for tobacco at M.'s shop." The clergyman then said: "You must not enter that shop again, or you will get toothache again. Have someone else take those five cents. I can cure your toothache once more, but after that it is over." When V. went to the little shop anyway, he got toothache again. The man had been bewitched by M. from the shop.
190814: When a child fell ill, people always believed the child had been struck by the evil hand. That is why people were always very afraid when they went out with their child or when someone had touched their child.
190815: A man who had to cut down an oak no longer dared to go on chopping because the tree cried "Ow" at every blow. In the end a deaf-mute had to cut down the oak.
190821:
When a woman came near a little child, people were often afraid because they thought that woman was a witch.
Some women could say prayers over people against the evil hand.
190831: At night a ghost coach with a white lady drove from Rapertingen to Kortessem.
190833: People believed that Betje from Maasmechelen was a witch. When Betje went to gather pine cones, she had stroked a child's head. The next day the child had lice.
190847: When a witch saw someone passing with some foals, she cried: "They won't stay there long!" Every morning the foals stood in the brook, so they had to be brought back each time.
190853: A man from Vliermaalroot did not believe that a fire-man roamed the Helstraat. One day a seventeen-year-old boy, terrified, said he had seen the fire-man. The man then went outside and saw the fire-man set a pear tree on fire. After that the fire-man moved towards the Jongebos estate. The next day, however, there was no trace of a fire to be found.
190876: Two women from the café 'in de Boulevard' heard a horse racing through the meadow at tremendous speed. Further on, the horse ran through the forest. Although the women still heard crackling in the forest later that evening, nothing more was to be seen. It must have been a horse from hell.
190900: A man coming back from Wellen was followed by a black cat. When the cat began to speak, the man ran home scared to death.
190906: A woman from Kotem who was suspected of being a witch liked to be near children. Every time that woman had been with a child, the child got a rash. After a cross had been made by the door with sand or straws, the woman no longer came in. People believed the witch could not step over the cross.
190918: In Mielen there lived a wizard who was called "'t politikske". In the evenings the wizard turned himself into a ghost, so that nobody dared to go outside anymore.
190932: A blacksmith who was going on a journey met a black cat. When the blacksmith began to talk to the cat, a black woman with a veil suddenly stood before him.
190946: Six men heard an enormous noise on the border between Beringen and Koersel. All the leaves and branches moved as if something big was passing by.
190963: Two brave men were terrified when they met a black dog possessed by evil at the cemetery of 's Heerenelderen.
190979: Marieke van Bertje had three small children to look after. Because she had little time to work on the farm, a former school friend came to help her for a few days. After that woman had milked the cows, however, the animals gave no more milk, so that in the end they had to be slaughtered. Later people said that the woman was a witch.
190981: Two men walking past the Hemel suddenly heard a priest praying. A little later a procession with a priest and nuns passed by. That procession was often seen flying through the air as well. That was the hellish hunt.
190983: In Tienen stood a Blauwe Schuur (Blue Barn) that the devil had built for a man who had sold his soul. But the devil had not been able to finish his work, so one wall of the barn was missing. The farmer had often tried to build that wall himself, but it would not succeed. Finally he decided to place the beams in the shape of a cross in front of the opening. Then the wall could at last be closed.
190990: A boy had heard that he could recognise a witch by placing his feet crosswise on her footprint. When the boy walked behind a suspected woman and put his feet across her footprint, the woman looked round and boxed the boy's ears. That made the boy certain that the woman was a witch.
191024: In the Boeienaarstraat in Boorsem, Theike M. played the werewolf with a sheet. In Opgrimbie, between Maasmechelen and Rekem, a werewolf that had itself carried by people was also once knocked down.
191026: Louis M. from Schulen was seeing a girl from Nietelbroek. When Louis went home around midnight, he met a white lady. Suddenly the lady disappeared into the bushes. Louis wanted to follow her, but got a blow on the head.
191039: The horses always stood still at the house of X.
191054: In Manshoven, a farm in Broekom, lived a cowherd boy named Masset. When he slept, Masset did strange things: for example, he would crawl through the chairs like a snake. One Sunday Masset was sitting in the inn with the sexton when he fell asleep and began behaving strangely again. Shortly afterwards Masset's mother heard what was the matter with her son, and she went to the priest of Tessenderlo. The priest said prayers over Masset, and since then he has done nothing strange.
191057: A man wanted to drown a white cat because it was eating his chickens. The man put the cat in a sack. When he took the animal out again, the white cat had turned into a black one.
191060: On the lane to Gerdingen there was a thorn hedge that began at the house of Pier Lawijt. When a certain Cornelius was coming back from his work at the tile factory one evening, he saw a cat sitting by the thorn hedge. Cornelius struck at the cat three times, and it gave him a strange look. When the man got home, his worried mother cried: "Cornelius, where have you been so long?" The man answered: "How can that be? I came straight home and didn't stop to talk anywhere!" Because his mother saw a large wound on his finger, Cornelius told the story of the cat. When Cornelius went to mass with his brother the next morning, the cat was gone.
191063: Some people were in the habit of going to the Hobos in the evening to dance and have fun. Usually they left before midnight, but one evening they happened to stay a little longer. At the stroke of twelve all the doors flew open by themselves. At one o'clock the doors closed again by themselves. That had been the ghost of the drossaard (bailiff).
191069: Witches could turn themselves into animals.
191084: On a farm in Velm a dead woman came haunting every night.
191087: A boy who entered one of his pigeons in a race passed the house of a witch, who asked: "Going to play with the pigeons again, boy?" The boy's pigeon never came back after the race. At the next race the boy again passed the witch's house. Because the woman was inside, the boy called out: "I'm going to play with the pigeons again!" That time too the pigeon never came back.
191090: One was not supposed to kick a cat, because the animal could be a witch. If one had wounded a witch's cat, the next day one would see a woman with a wound.
191102: The architect who was to draw the plan for Cologne Cathedral could not get the work finished. One day when he went for a walk, he met a gentleman who was willing to make the plan for him. The architect had to come back the next evening. In exchange for the plan he would receive, he had to sell his soul. The next night the architect could not sleep and finally confessed everything to his wife, who sent him to a friar. The clergyman said: "It is not so bad. With one hand you must take the plan, and with the other hand you must give the devil a relic and pretend it is your soul." When the man did what the friar had told him, the devil became furious and cried: "Cologne Cathedral will never be finished!" The cathedral is still not finished.
191120: Two brewers were driving a horse and cart from Vechmaal to Lauw when a black cat suddenly jumped onto the cart. One of the brewers struck the cat with a whip so that the animal fell to the ground. A little later two black cats jumped onto the cart. Again the man struck the animals with the whip. To the brewers' great fright, a whole pack of cats then jumped onto the cart.
191125: Will-o'-the-wisps were children who had died after birth and had been thrown into the water. Someone who could baptise a will-o'-the-wisp was pulled into the water and drowned.
191132: In Klein Ternaaien a girl was out walking with her disabled sister. A little later the girls' mother was visited by a beggar woman who was said to be a witch. The mother then called: "Girls, come inside quickly, because the witch is here!" The beggar woman replied: "Ah, I may not come in. I'll get you yet!" Some time later the disabled girl got a hunchback.
191133: A woman had found the straw band with which her husband could turn himself into a werewolf. When her husband was out in the field, the woman threw the band into the oven. As soon as the band caught fire, the man was already standing by the oven to save his property.
191148: A boy from Hoelbeek was secretly seeing two girls at once. After visiting the first girl, he went to the house of the second. The boy stood on a harrow and talked to his girlfriend through the bedroom window. Meanwhile a cat walked under the harrow. The next time the boy visited the first girl, she knew everything he had said to the second girl. The girl had turned herself into a cat and eavesdropped on the conversation.
191152: Two men coming back from the Netherlands in the evening walked over a bridge. On the railing of the bridge stood a little jug. One of the men said: "Why is that little jug standing there? I'll knock it off!", to which his friend replied: "No, better not!" But the man would not listen and knocked the jug off the railing. Just as the men had got into bed, the little jug was standing at their door. The men never again came home by way of that bridge.
191180: A man coming back late one evening from Leuven heard wonderfully beautiful music in Hulst. A strange light appeared, and a little later the man was escorted by the most beautiful women to a party where everyone was dancing. When the man said: "In God's name," the whole scene suddenly vanished and the man was sitting with his backside in a bush.
191185: In Veulen the voice of the dead count was often heard as he came haunting in the living room of the castle.
191191: In Veulen a poacher shot a werewolf through the head, so that the beast took on its human form again. The werewolf then lamented: "Now all those years I've spent as a werewolf are lost. I have to start all over again!" When his years were up, the werewolf had to have a friend take over his task. There used to be many werewolves. Since the invention of the revolver, werewolves have died out.
191207: Some women could put someone under the influence of the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's harmful touch). People who read special books could gain magical power. A man who was binding the corn saw a witch standing in the distance and said: "If I could do what she can, I would use my magic to bind the corn." When the man came home with the corn, his hair was full of lice.
191226: At a crossroads in Gors-Opleeuw a black cat always sat in the evening and pestered passers-by. Because people believed the cat was an evil spirit, they were afraid of the animal.
191231: Jannes Hiepkes always had to carry the werewolf. One day, however, Jannes managed to cut the werewolf. When a werewolf lost blood, it changed back into a human. The next day Jannes knew who the werewolf was.
191237: A white madam came haunting in the woods of Vogelsanck. When C. was coming back from Zolder, he thought he had seen the white madam in the woods. Afterwards the man found that it was a white plank.
191243: Betske, Stien's farmhand, was jumped by a dog at the turnpike barrier in Wasseven. Betske took out his knife and stabbed the werewolf. Because the werewolf was bleeding, he took on his human form and Betske could recognise him.
191259: Farmer D. and his farmhands sometimes whistled at the fire-man. One day the farmer decided to forbid his farmhands to whistle at the fire-man any more. The farmhands did it anyway, and so one day the hayloft went up in flames.
191264: People said that 'moeder uit 't Rot' (mother from 't Rot) was a witch. When the witch had literally taken a man 'by the nose', the man's nose swelled up terribly.
191270: A knight who had lost all his money at cards sold his soul to the devil. When the contract expired and the knight had to go to the devil, he was saved by Saint Gertrude, who sat behind him on the horse. The bridge where this scene took place was later called the Sint-Geerterbrug. That bridge was still depicted at the altar of the church of Heppeneert. Moreover, the priest had a stone from the bridge set into the wall, with hearts, diamonds, spades and clubs on the corners.
191282: A family at the Luikerpoort had a small child that cried all the time. The doctors had already given the child various medicines, but they could not find out what was wrong. The child's condition grew worse every day and in the end it died. When she cleaned the cradle, the mother found a doll stuck full of pins in it. That could only have been the work of a witch. She knew who the witch was: it was an old woman from the village. There were also people, for example, who earned nothing all day from their work if they had met that old woman in the morning.
191284: A man who went to visit his girlfriend in Waltwilder around midnight saw a goose sitting on the road. When the man wanted to grab the animal, he saw that it was a goat. The animal kept following the man the whole time. That goat was the werewolf.
191294: A man who had to take a cart full of grain to Bree got stuck on the heath of Helchteren. A farmer working a little further on said: "If you don't hitch my ox to your cart, you'll never get away from here." The man replied: "If it doesn't work with my horse, it won't work with your ox either. Besides, tonight someone from Lillo is coming with a cart and two horses. That man will help me." That evening the man from Lillo did indeed pull the cart loose without effort. The man from Lillo said to the farmer: "And you stay standing there until we come back." When the two men returned, the farmer was still standing in the same spot. The farmer had special powers, but the man from Lillo had even more magic power.
191309: A man out poaching in Wijshagen saw some hares playing in the distance. He sat still, assuming the hares would soon come closer. After a while one of the hares came and tugged at the poacher's coat and then quickly ran off. The startled poacher told his bizarre story to a friend, who laughed at him. So the poacher invited his friend to come along. When the two men sat there, two hares came and tugged at their coats.
191330: While the priest was preaching in the Hoogkerk in Tongeren, the devil came and sat by the window. The priest had already gone round several times with holy water, but the devil calmly stayed where he was.
191338: A man who had to go to the Meisberg at midday to bring the beekeepers their food always had to carry the werewolf on the way. "He's on me again, he's on me again!" the man would shout. "Just hold on to him, I'm coming," another would answer. But the werewolf was always gone before anyone else arrived.
191357: A farmer who had just slaughtered an animal saw a black cat come in. "Go and sit by the fire to warm yourself," said the farmer. When a second cat came in, the farmer said again: "Come on in." In the end sixty cats had come in, all sitting in a row by the fire. Then the farmer took a bucket of boiling water and threw it over the cats. The next day several women in the village had injuries to their heads. They were witches.
191389: In Millen there was a woman who had long suffered from tuberculosis. One day the doctor came and said: "After today the woman will not live much longer, because the magpie has called." That same day the woman died.
191391: Around 1890 people wore a smock. When people were plagued by the maar (nightmare spirit), they were so frightened that they broke out in a sweat. When the maar had gone, the smock fell to the ground in small pieces.
191425: H. went with his maid to take an animal to Diest. In Schaffen the farmer said to the maid: "I have to go and relieve myself. If you see a big dog in the meantime, you must throw your handkerchief at the animal." A little later the girl did indeed see a big dog. The animal seized the handkerchief in its teeth and disappeared. When H. reappeared, he had lots of bits of cloth between his teeth.
191436: Because farmer N.'s cows were always ill, he decided to sell the animals. When the farmer had bought new cows, however, these animals also turned out to be bewitched. After the priest had read prayers over the stable, the clergyman advised the farmer always to sprinkle a pinch of salt into the milk he sold.
191459: In the meadow near L. a black cat sat on a fallen apple tree. Nobody dared to pass by there.
191463: A mother and father went to the parish priest for advice because their son always went out at night to roam about as a werewolf. The priest advised them to send their son away and burn his skin in the meantime. As soon as the skin caught fire, however, the boy was already standing by the oven to save his skin. Several people had to hold the boy back to keep him from jumping into the fire. As soon as the skin had burnt up, the boy was released.
191465: A woman from Zepperen saw a cat near the church at night and said: "Pussycat, where are you going?" When the woman threw some breadcrumbs on the ground, a whole pack of witch cats began to sing.
191467: Giel van Nelis Z. was coming back from Vlijtingen with some friends. Because Giel was strikingly quiet, his friends wondered what was wrong with him. A while later Giel said: "A black lady came along with me from the Heilige Haag, and I just couldn't get rid of her."
191480: In Bommershoven lived witches who could make people stand still. When one said: "Our Dear Lord, help me", one could go on again.
191484: A man asked a woman who owned a book of magic: "Are you a witch?", to which the woman replied: "No, but the person who said that will have trouble yet!" People did indeed run into trouble, such as the deaths of children.
191490: Net K. could not manage to make butter. Her neighbour Klet K. was a witch.
191495: A pregnant woman who went to gather leftover bits of coal passed the house of a witch. The witch said to the woman: "I'll get you, I'll get you!" Shortly afterwards the pregnant woman fell ill. When the woman was in hospital, she thought she saw the witch standing everywhere. Her baby eventually died. The chaplain came by and said: "I can name the witch." The sick woman's sister-in-law then said: "That's not necessary, because I know who it is!" Some time later the parish priest came to visit and said: "It's not serious. I'll shake it into my sleeve here and shake it out again elsewhere." Shortly after the clergyman had said that, the witchcraft was over. Because the witch sensed that people were angry with her, she said: "I'll take the last cow out of farmer X's stable!" A few days later the cow was dead. After people had been given something blessed by the priest to put under the door, the witch could no longer get in. One evening a boy coming back from visiting his girlfriend heard rattling in a horse stable. Strangely enough, there was nothing to be seen. When the door was opened in the morning, the horse was completely drenched in sweat.
191506: Some people going home late in the evening were followed by a dog almost as big as a calf.
191510: When Jan V. was on his way to the mill in Kozen, he saw a hare coming towards him. Jan quickly held his sack open, and the hare ran straight into it. Jan threw the sack onto the cart. When Jan saw another hare a little further on, he thought: "This time I mustn't hold the sack open, because then the other hare might jump out, and I'll be left with none." But the second hare suddenly called out: "Hey cousin, where are you?", to which the other hare replied: "In Jan's sack." Jan was so frightened by this scene that he threw the sack with the hare away as far as he could.
191524: Some fishermen went to have a drink at an old widow's house. When the widow asked: "Don't I get a drink too?", the men replied: "No, there isn't enough in the bottle." The little woman then said: "You won't catch much fish tonight." Instead of fish, the men caught nothing but frogs.
191534: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend in the evening said to the girl: "I have to go away for a moment. If a beast comes at you, throw your handkerchief at its mouth." When the boy was gone, a dog did indeed appear. The girl threw the handkerchief at the animal's mouth, as she had been advised. When they got home that evening, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
191537: A man who always came to sleep in Dilsen on Sundays always heard three cats making a racket. One day his father gave him a club to hit the cats with. When the cats ran off, the father said: "Look how the witches run!"
191542: A man saw a coach with four black horses flying through the air.
191547: In Odeur there lived a big black woman who followed people in the evening.
191552: When Felix T. was walking home one evening, he met a cat that blocked his way. Felix took a stick and hit the cat in the eye. The next day the witch Mang wore a cloth over her eye.
191566: When V. came home in the evening, he saw someone with a white sheet sitting by a turnstile. The man was very frightened and muttered something as he walked past the ghost. A little further on V. heard the ghost say: "Had Jan V. not spoken, we would have broken his neck!"
191577: When Giel W. went poaching by moonlight, he saw a good fifty rabbits sitting by the water, hopping about and jumping into the bushes. Giel fired his gun into the bushes, but the rabbits had vanished without a trace.
191595: A boy had been given a toy gun by his father. One day the boy shot down a sparrow. Although he had seen the sparrow fall, the bird was gone when the boy came closer.
191611: A witch had woven a crown in a child's pillow, which made the child ill. Someone advised the child's parents to cut open or burn the pillow. Fortunately the wreath was not yet closed, otherwise the child would have died.
191620: On a farm there was a dog called Stupke. Whenever the maid had to go and milk the cow, the dog was always sitting on the milking stool. The maid would then say to the dog: "Come on, Stupke, get off that stool, I have to milk!" But no one ever saw how the dog got onto the stool or how it jumped off.
191624: A cat often came to sit on the beer barrels of a brewer from Eigenbilzen. One day the brewer broke the cat's leg. When the man went to eat at midday, his wife lay in bed with a broken leg.
191635: When farmer Jan H. went to buy a cow, he met a woman on the way who said: "Make sure you don't get lost!", to which Jan replied: "No, no!" A little later, however, the farmer did get lost. He ended up in an inn, where he ordered a glass of beer. Then he said to the landlady: "Tell me in God's name where I am!" The next moment everything had vanished and the man was no longer sitting on a chair but on a tree stump. The glass of beer had turned into a cow's horn.
191641: A man coming back from the fair saw a white ghost floating above the road. Because the man was very frightened, he quickly made the sign of the cross. At that the ghost disappeared at once.
191648: When Kobe was coming back from visiting his girlfriend, he saw a pack of dancing cats, who said: "How neat our Kobe looks", to which the man replied: "Just as if you've got a turd in it". The next moment Kobe was set upon by the cats. Afterwards Kobe had to stay in bed for two weeks.
191660: Nobody could walk past Liesje J.'s house without falling.
191662: A man saw a strange cat with a white neck. It was the ghost of a farmer who had been run over and killed and came back to haunt because he had not received the last rites. When someone tried to kill the cat, the animal suddenly vanished.
191665: A wedding party was being held next to the church. One of the guests struck at a cat. The next moment there were as many as fifty cats.
191673: On the Mulkenweg in Tongeren stood a house where a witch lived. If that witch had been in someone's stable, people believed the animals there would die.
191676: In Sluizen there was a witch who always caused people trouble. The least bad thing she did was to give someone lice. Although the witch never went to church, she once walked along in the procession. When the Blessed Sacrament reached her, she fainted. The priest immediately understood what was going on, and from then on he visited the witch again and again until she was willing to confess. When the woman was cured, a grotto was built to thank Our Lord.
191677: A woman came peddling yarn at a house in Opgrimbie. When the woman had been gone for a few hours, the mother found that her little child Annake had lice.
191678: In a house in Donk there was a cat that threw bones down the chimney. That cat was a witch.
191692: A girl had got lice after the wife of L. had pulled her hair. The parents went to the heksenmannetje (witch doctor) to rid the girl of the lice.
191711: Two people on their way to the lof (evening church service) were followed by a black cat. One of them broke the animal's leg. The next day the witch had a broken leg.
191720: At Christmas, at midnight, the chapel of Wellen was haunted.
191721: A man who consorted with the devil owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day someone had found the collar. The moment the collar was thrown into the fire, the werewolf was immediately standing by the oven.
191735: In 'de Klonk' in Diest some men were playing cards. One of the men, who had already lost a lot of money, shouted angrily: "Goddamn, I always lose! The devil must help me!" A little later a stranger came into the café, stood behind the man and said: "I'll help". From that moment on the card player was lucky the whole time. A little later people noticed that the stranger had goat's feet. In the card player's house things got terrible. People constantly heard shouting: "He is mine! No, he is mine!" Because the dean could not help, they sent for the prelate of Averbode. The man's house stank terribly for days afterwards.
191738: A joiner going to work in Mielen-boven-Aalst met a foal on the way. The joiner sat on the foal and hit the animal on the nose, making it bleed. The next moment the foal changed into the joiner's best friend. The friend said with relief: "How happy I am to be released!" The man had found a devil's magic book along the road. By reading in the book, the man had turned into a foal.
191739: In Donk stood a blue barn that burned down several times. Each time the devils rebuilt the barn at night because the occupants had sold their souls.
191740: The werewolf jumped on people's necks and had itself carried.
191765: A man coming back from a party was followed by little dogs.
191768: A nine-year-old girl went with her uncle to buy bread in Hasselt. At the castle of Dominus, at the crossroads of the roads to Diepenbeek, Bevers, Peneel and Jagenbos, stood a white beguine. When the uncle came closer, the ghost said to him: I had promised to go on pilgrimage to Kortenbos. As long as that has not been done, I cannot reach heaven. The uncle then went on pilgrimage for the beguine.
191795: Dré M. was plagued by mice. Even the cats seemed to be afraid of the mice. One day Dré discovered that Trui van de B. was making the mice. After the priest had sprinkled the house with holy water, all the mice had disappeared.
191815: Fons W.'s father often had to carry the werewolf when he walked home in the evening. The werewolf licked the man's neck the whole time. When the man reached the bridge, the werewolf jumped off his back again.
191816: During catechism class the priest saw one of the boys making mice in the church. After the priest had baptised the boy, he could no longer make mice.
191831: A priest came haunting between the church and the presbytery. At night he constantly rode back and forth there on horseback.
191847: Herme had sold his soul to the devil. When his house was about to collapse, the devils came to prop up the building.
191851: On the bridge at the Kiefhoek there once lived a witch who made the farmers' guns fail. It seemed as if the hares there were bewitched.
191853: At the little castle of Robbeneck a hellish noise was heard at twelve noon. A certain Herman from Godsheide claimed to know who was responsible for the trouble, but refused to say. The lord of the castle, D.P., stayed the night at the little castle, while his wife went to spend the night in Hasselt with the maid.
191854: A man was nearly frightened to death when he saw geese walking in the cemetery at night.
191858: In Niel there lived a man who had particularly fine pears on his tree. So that the boys from the neighbourhood would not come and steal pears, the man had tied thorns to the wall. One day, however, some rascals had managed to cut the thorns loose so that they could climb over the wall. But when the boys had climbed into the tree, the branches were suddenly full of cats trying to pull them out of the tree. Luckily the boys were able to jump into a pond; otherwise not one of them would have got out of the tree alive.
191868: A farmer whose cow was due to calve during the night suddenly heard someone knocking on the window. When the farmer went to look, there was a black cat that was not his.
191879: A farmer who regularly found an animal dead in his stable sent for the chaplain of Paal. Although the chaplain did not take the matter seriously, he said: "All right, I'll come round one night." One morning the farmer discovered footprints around the stable. From then on the misfortune stopped. So the chaplain must have come by.
191885: The witch Bet had turned a newborn baby's head back to front. The shoemaker then went to the witch with a knife and forced her to undo the harm she had done. And that is what she did.
191906: Caroline was visiting the witch Tin. Suddenly the witch said: "Watch out, because your brother will soon come looking for you with a policeman, but he won't see you." And that is what happened.
191915: There were always troublesome cats by the coal pit.
191940: In the old days a ghost roamed about in Zepperen.
191948: A woman who had just had a baby was visited by the witch Marie I., who came to bring 'de krommen elleboog' (the crooked elbow, a customary gift) (1). The visitor was offered nothing at all. The next day the young mother fell ill, so that the priest had to be sent for to read prayers over her. The clergyman said: "Be careful not to give anyone anything, even if it is only a sheaf of straw!" A little later a beggar woman knocked at the door. Although the woman begged for a long time, she was given nothing. Two days later that same woman came by with the message that Marie I. was responsible for the mother's illness. After that the sick mother recovered at once.
191957: When Janneke G. drove his cart to Luik, he was followed by a cat. In Vreren Jan got off the cart and struck at the cat, which was sitting against the wall. The next moment a little woman stood against the wall and asked the man whether he dared to do that again. Janneke answered: "In God's name, I dare to do it again!" The little woman said: "Had Janneke G. not spoken so wisely, I would surely have broken his neck." Then the witch vanished.
191975: A farm in Weert was haunted. A white mare often stood in front of the barn door. The farmer had often tried to catch the horse, but he never succeeded. The mare always vanished around midnight.
191990: Dries lived on a farm with a walnut tree beside it. Jef, Dries's son, said that at night something came and lay on him that grew heavier and heavier. Because Jef's bedroom was on the side of the walnut tree, Dries suggested they swap rooms. That night Dries too had an oppressive feeling. When Dries sent for the parish priest, the clergyman said: "You must not speak to me while I am inside, and you must leave the door open." The priest went into the room and began to pray. After that they were no longer troubled by the ghost.
191994: A man met a witch in a velvet dress who was pushing a wheelbarrow. The man was allowed to go with the witch as far as a certain point. When they came back, the witch was pushing only the wheel of the wheelbarrow in front of her.
192002: The meadow by Harieke's house was badly haunted. In the evening a lot of noise was heard there and strange lights were seen. Whenever a horse came by, the animal suddenly began to rear wildly.
192011: One evening Mannes L. met two grey cats. Although the cats did nothing, Mannes was very frightened and the next day told everyone he had seen two witches. The witch cats were Trien V. and the wife of S.
192017: A man saw a little cat walking around near the house of the blacksmith V.R. The man took the animal with him. After a while, however, the kitten became so heavy that the man had to drop it. The next moment a white lady stood before him, who said: "Let go what goes and let stand what stands." Then the lady disappeared.
192020: When Gijske walked home from the station in the evening, he had to carry the werewolf. When uncle Jo went to fetch the man at the station, the werewolf could not be seen. The beast could be heard walking, though. The werewolf wore a chain around its neck, broke wind the whole time and laughed at the men.
192024: If one had been touched by the evil hand, one could no longer get away.
192027: A man who was a werewolf was sent far away so that, with the help of the parish priest, his collar could be burnt in the meantime. The moment the collar was thrown into the fire, however, the farmhand was standing beside the oven within ten seconds to save his band. That is why people said that werewolves could fly through the air.
192041: Two-year-old Theofiel would no longer eat anything because he was bewitched. Because the doctor could not help, Theofiel's father went to the friars of Hasselt. The friars gave the man cakes, which he had to soak in boiled milk and give to the child. After that Theofiel recovered.
192048: A man from Rosmeer coming back from the fair in Hees saw will-o'-the-wisps floating above a pool of water. Such lights could be released by saying: "I baptise you alone, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Amen." Whoever forgot to say this was knocked over by hundreds of will-o'-the-wisps that all came to be baptised. When the man had baptised the will-o'-the-wisps above the pool, he could go on his way again.
192064: A man who was sharpening his scythe saw a woman passing and said: "The darning needle you stuck in my leg, you must take out again or I'll chop your head off!" The next moment the witch pulled a long darning needle out of the man's leg.
192067: The card-playing knight of Heppeneert had sold his soul to the devil for twenty years. When those twenty years were over, the knight had to go to the chapel of Heppeneert. In that chapel the knight had, all his life, burned a candle every Saturday and prayed three Hail Marys to Our Lady. After waiting half an hour, the knight said irritably: "What's going on? If I have to wait here much longer, I'll go back where I came from!" The devil answered: "If you send away that woman sitting behind you on your horse, I will come. Otherwise I cannot come." But the knight saw no one sitting on his horse. The knight dismounted, tied his horse to a tree and went into the chapel to thank Our Lady on his bare knees. The money the knight had received from the devil had turned into leaves.
192082: Three men walking through the fields in the evening saw a black cat. One of the men struck at the cat, whereupon the animal scratched him viciously. The man's wound never healed. After lying in bed for twenty years, the man died of his injury.
192083: Oda Q. from Overbroek had a bewitched cow. People advised her to go to a sorcerer and to fetch something blessed from a monastery and tie it to the cow's horns. Oda also had to carry the churn she made butter with beyond the village boundaries. When Oda had done all that, the cow gave good milk again. The sorcerer she had visited lived in Wellen. His name was Tewes van den R. Tewes knew all of people's problems even before they had told him.
192100: A man returning from the Heggersom in Kinrooi was always followed by a cat in the Paardestraat in Molenbeersel. When the man tried to hit the cat, the trees bent down to the ground. As soon as he reached Kinrooi territory, everything was normal again.
192107: It was said that the sexton of Kermt came back to haunt after his death.
192114: Three unmarried sisters lived in a house. One day the sisters brought oranges to a woman from the neighbourhood. After eating the oranges the woman became deathly ill. Sometimes she was in so much pain that she tore the sheets on the bed. Eventually the woman was taken to a healer from Kleine-Spouwen. The healer gave a little prayer that all the people in the house had to pray from midnight to one o'clock. On the eighth or ninth day the woman was cured. The healer had predicted that the three women would come back and bring oranges again. "You must give the oranges to the neighbours; that can do no harm," the healer had said.
192134: In Herk-de-Stad lived a man named Janneke F. One day Janneke and his wife rode on horseback to the Kempen. On the way a black dog suddenly appeared and stood in front of the horse. When the dog grew bigger and bigger, the horse no longer dared to go on. As soon as the werewolf crept into the ditch and vanished, the horse could continue.
192166: A man who drove with horse and cart to the Kikmolen in Opgrimbie always had to stop at the same spot because the horses would not go on. Fed up, the man struck the wheel of the cart with a whip. The next moment the horses ran on so fast that the man could hardly stop them. The next day a little woman came to the mill with her arm in a sling. She said: "You certainly did me a nice turn last night!", to which the man replied: "Ah, so it was you, you ugly rascal!"
192172: At the Platvijver Henke M. always came haunting with the words: "Give it back! Give it back!" During his life Henke had stolen the money of the mail coach. Because the neighbours grew tired of the noise, they sent for a friar to banish the ghost. A man had to lead the ghost on a chain to a bush without looking back. The bush to which the ghost was banished kept screaming for a long time afterwards.
192173: The architect who was to draw the plans for Cologne Cathedral simply could not design a good plan. One day when he went for a walk, the architect met a gallant gentleman to whom he told his problems. The gentleman offered to make the plan in his place. In return the gentleman wanted the architect's soul. After a night to think it over, the architect accepted the gentleman's offer and signed a contract with his own blood. When the church was nearly finished, the architect became afraid and began to beg Our Lord for help. When the architect went walking at the place where he had met the devil, it suddenly began to thunder and lighten fiercely. Then the contract signed in blood fell from the sky. So the man got the chance to destroy the contract. When he had done so, however, the plan was gone too, so the church was never finished.
192194: A man from Neerrepen coming back from work met the black man of the gravel road on the way. Because the man was afraid of the ghost, he walked on quickly. He believed the ghost was going to the Zips to look at the property he had owned while he was alive.
192218: During the winter the pond opposite the chapel was completely frozen, so that the children often came to play on the ice. Although there was no fresh fruit at that time of year, a witch had laid a beautiful red apple on the ice. Fortunately a woman from the neighbourhood had seen the apple lying there. Before the children had seen the apple, the woman stamped the fruit to pieces.
192220: At school a child conjured up mice by throwing a clod of earth on the ground. When the child was given earth from Scherpenheuvel, it could no longer make mice.
192227: Some people going to Zammelen saw a black cat sitting on a toll barrier. Then one of the boys said to the animal: "Get off that barrier, or I'll beat you to death!" When the boy had broken the cat's legs, the animal changed into his own mother. The boy had to carry his mother home on his back.
192248: In Kotem lived a woman who cared for the sick and kept watch over the dead. One day the woman saw a dead man walking on the little path by her house. After she had told the priest, the clergyman said: "Next time you should go up to him and ask what he wants." When the woman saw the ghost again, she went closer and reached out her hand. But she felt nothing, and a moment later the ghost had vanished.
192254: After a friendly old woman had visited a family in Kerniel, one of the children became very ill. The child had been struck by the evil hand. When the priest had read prayers over the child, it recovered.
192255: A man who came across a will-o'-the-wisp said: "If you are not baptised, I will baptise you". At that moment countless lights came at the man, so that in the morning he lay dead in the water.
192259: A farmhand coming back from Membruggen at about ten in the evening saw a little white cat sitting in a street in Ketsingen. As the man went on, he saw dozens of black cats that all crawled into the sewer. As soon as the farmhand reached the farm, he went to bed. From then on, however, the young man always heard strange noises at night, as if horses were walking in the street. After the farmhand had finished his tasks at the farm, he quit.
192276: A dead woman came haunting on the field path near her house. When the children told their father they had seen a ghost, the man said: "Yes, we still have to make a pilgrimage for mother in her place." After the father had gone on pilgrimage with his children the following Sunday, the ghost was no longer seen.
192277: A dog had bitten off a child's hand. When the child had died, the mother threw it into a hedge. From then on a will-o'-the-wisp always came out of the hedge and flew over the street. When one said: "I baptise you", a thousand will-o'-the-wisps came flying. Because the little souls all wanted to be baptised, one had to say: "I baptise you alone".
192290: A man who had got lice through a witch's doing had died. When they wanted to lay the body in the coffin, they first had to put another shirt on the dead man, because the shirt he was wearing was full of lice.
192300: In the old days, if someone had struck a black cat and shortly afterwards saw an old woman with a wound, they concluded that the woman was a witch.
192306: A witch from Donk had made a girl ill by sticking pins into her pillow. In the end the girl died.
192307: A woman who had a lot of misfortune in her stable sent for the holy little friar. The friar placed a relic under the threshold and said: "The witch will come by within nine days, but you must not do anything to her." On the ninth day a woman from the neighbourhood did indeed come by. Three cows died because of the witch.
192310: In Kortessem there lived a little boy who could make mice. His father feared the boy might be bewitched, and so took him on a pilgrimage to Kortenbosch. On the way they passed a wheat field, and the father exclaimed: "What fine wheat!" At that the son said: "If I want, that wheat will be completely burnt by the time we come back." "No, you must not do that," said the father, "but I would like to know whether you can really do such things!", and he gave his son a small bundle of wheat and asked him whether he could burn it by the time they came back. On the way back they could already see from afar that the bundle of wheat was indeed standing completely blackened among the green wheat. Pastor B. baptised the boy again. After that the child could no longer make mice.
192311: A young man who had gone to visit his girlfriend stayed to chat a while with some boys from the neighbourhood. When the boys went home, the young man wanted to say goodbye to his girlfriend. The young man knocked on the door, but the girl did not open. After banging loudly on the window, the boy heard a voice that said: "Oh, I thought you had left long ago!" Then a fat black cat flew into his face. On the way home the road was constantly blocked by brooks, ditches and cats running about. When the boy finally got home after all, he told the whole story to his father. His father advised him to leave all evil alone from then on.
192328: The white lady was someone who sat with a sheet over her head along the road to Scherpenheuvel. Everyone was afraid of the white lady, because she walked up to all passers-by.
192346: Peer went to the rehearsal of a music society in Vlijtingen. On the way a little hare always jumped up in front of him. When Peer said: "Oh, it's only you!", the animal suddenly vanished.
192347: On a farm where a mouse had got in, a man cut off the animal's tail with a knife. A woman from the neighbourhood had lost an arm.
192357: Because witches always knew everything, people suspected that they consorted with the devil.
192371: Around All Saints' the souls of unbaptised children floated about near the water as will-o'-the-wisps.
192378: People did not dare to go near the castle because the former residents came haunting there.
192384: On S.'s farm in Rotem a headless witte juffrouw (white lady) walked about at night. Everyone who saw her ran away in fear. To drive the white lady away, a procession was held at the farm for a long time.
192398: Long ago a hermit named Monfreer lived on the Hulstberg. Near Monfreer's house stood a little chapel with a statue of the Black Our Lady. The land on which the chapel stood belonged to a rich lady. Because the lady wanted to have a castle built on that beautiful sunny spot, she ordered a new chapel to be built on the other side of the hill. When the new chapel was finished, however, nobody dared to remove the statue of Mary from its old place. In the end a joiner was found who was willing to move the statue. The occupants of the new castle had much misfortune. Eventually all the occupants left the castle, and the building stood empty for fifty years. When the rich lady realised she had done wrong, she went to Lourdes to care for the sick there. After some time the son of the former occupants came to live in the castle. That man, however, died very young of a terrible disease. The joiner who had moved the statue dropped dead on a bridge.
192400: A man who suffered from an ailment of the eyes went to consult a witch. The witch put a small white cloth in a bucket of water and said the name of a saint. If the cloth stayed afloat, it was the wrong saint. If the cloth sank, the sick man would soon recover.
192403: The daughter of Maria B. could make white mice without tails. When the priest noticed this one day, he began to read his breviary. From that day on the child could no longer make mice.
192413: On the Keupkensberg there lived a man who had moved the boundary post of his field to have more land. After his death the man came back to haunt with the words: "Post lost, post lost". When people grew tired of the calling and went to look, they found that the post stood in a different place.
192426: Trien T.'s husband came haunting after his death. Because Trien had several times seen her husband's spirit sitting in front of the statue of Mary, she suddenly remembered that her husband had once promised to go on pilgrimage if the cow gave birth to healthy calves. After Trien had gone on pilgrimage herself, she no longer saw her husband's spirit.
192430: Jan B. had been followed all the way home by some witches while Mieke had laid the washing out to bleach. A black hand was burnt into every piece of clothing.
192439: A man went to spend the night in an empty haunted house. Whoever dared to live in the house would get the house. When the man was baking a pancake, bones fell into the pan. A moment later a complete skeleton stood in the room.
192457: One winter evening a man was led by a will-o'-the-wisp to a swamp, in which he nearly drowned. Some believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children, but they might also have something to do with the devil.
192463: Some people going to Mass in Bree were pestered by cats on the way. When one of the men wanted to hit the cats with a stick, a passer-by warned: "I wouldn't do that!"
192466: To know whether a woman was a witch, one had to walk crosswise in her footprints. If the woman then looked back, she was a witch. That is how a man on the Stokrooiebrug unmasked a witch.
192481: A soldier slept next to a good friend who was always afraid when he had to keep watch at night. "I'll keep watch for you. I'm not afraid anyway," the soldier offered. "Yes, all right," said the friend, "but tonight you will be afraid all the same!" When the soldier was on watch, a big black dog came and sat beside him. After his duty the soldier told his friend what he had seen. "I'll give you my handkerchief," said the friend, "and when you blow your nose, you'll see what kind of dog you're dealing with!" The soldier did as he had been advised and blew his nose with the handkerchief. The next moment the dog changed into his friend, who stood laughing at him.
192482: A man had struck a cat's leg with a gun. The next day an old woman wore a bandage around her arm.
192484: In a village lived a witch who caused the villagers a great deal of misfortune. A farmer whose cattle were often ill went by coach to the sorcerer of Berlingen, who managed to help him. The farmer also told the sorcerer about a child from the neighbourhood who was bewitched too. The sorcerer then clapped his hands and said: "Oh dear, oh dear, why didn't those people come to me sooner? The witch is drawing the marrow out of the little child's bones through its feet. Witches can do that, you see, without even touching the child." The child could no longer be saved and eventually died. When the farmer came back from his visit to the sorcerer, he passed the witch's house. At that very moment the horse began to rear, sweating heavily.
192485: A farmer had been visited by a witch, who had stroked the animals saying: "You have fine cattle!" Some time later four cows died in the stable. Witches passed their arts on to their eldest daughter.
192494: A farmer was often visited by a woman who was suspected of being a witch. One day the woman asked: "Has the cow calved?", to which the farmer replied: "Yes." The next day the cow lay dead beside her calves.
192502: The farm of W. was haunted. At midnight all the doors flew open and a coach with two horses appeared.
192508: In 't Vèn lived a man who was said to consort with the devil. In a single night the man could dig over ten ares of land by hand.
192524: Werewolves were people who changed into dogs when they put on their collar. Werewolves often had themselves carried. If one managed to cut a werewolf in the paw, the next day one knew who it was. A farmhand who was also a werewolf had hidden his collar in a linden tree. The maid, however, had found the collar and thrown it into the oven. At that moment the farmhand came running and jumped into the fire.
192526: On Geneuth people had found the skin of a werewolf and thrown it into the oven. Meanwhile the farmhand who played the werewolf had been sent to a faraway place. As soon as the skin caught fire, however, the werewolf was already standing by the oven to save his skin.
192527: A man working in the field with his horse saw a large black dog jump in front of the horse. After the man had made the sign of the cross, the dog had disappeared.
192538: A farmer could not make butter because his milk was bewitched. After the priest had come to bless the milk, there was no more problem.
192541: If a witch got the chance to touch you, she could cover you in lice. To get rid of the vermin, one then had to have a priest read prayers over one.
192563: A family from Munsterbilzen had a fine cow that gave a lot of milk. One day Fien van het Jonckholt came to visit and said: "What a fine cow!" From that day on the cow gave no more milk, so that the animal eventually had to be sold.
192568: In a farmhouse in Rijkhoven, knocking was always heard in the attic, although nothing could be seen. When someone asked what was the matter, a voice said: "Before I died, I had promised the maid an apron." After the maid had been given an apron, no more strange noises were heard.
192578: Above marshes and water will-o'-the-wisps sometimes appeared, moving up and down. Such lights sometimes appeared in the meadow too. They were ghosts.
192587: Two farmers going to fetch wood with horse and cart met a witch on the way, who advised them not to load the cart too heavily. When the horses walked past the witch's house, they suddenly stood still. "Just give the horses a piece of bread, then they will pull the cart!", said the witch. After the farmers had done so, the horses indeed went on.
192593: On the road by the little chapel a black dog always appeared, which followed every passer-by. One day a certain Pieter K. was walking along that road when he too got the dog behind him. He made a sign of the cross over the dog, after which the animal immediately disappeared.
192596: A farmer had to have a priest read prayers over his cows. A witch had made sure the animals no longer gave a drop of milk.
192599: A man claimed that witches, both men and women, gathered at night in a remote meadow. There the witches danced around naked to beautiful music and committed all kinds of mortal sins demanded by the devil. In the morning, at the place where the witches' sabbath had taken place, a large circle could be seen where the grass had been completely trampled flat. In the old days, when people heard beautiful music, they did not dare to look up. Otherwise they would get 'the spot' on their eye, people believed.
192613: On the Engsteen a ghost appeared beside the ditch after one o'clock.
192619: A man who wanted to know what the wild hunt was went to spy on some witches. He saw them rub ointment from a little pot on their feet and then say: "We fly over hedges and thickets". Then they flew away on their broomsticks.
192623: Whenever Dirk R. had to manure the field, he manured only a small patch and then said: "Now everything apart." The next moment the whole field was manured.
192630: Sometimes witches went from house to house to ask people for something. If someone then opened the door with a baby in their arms, they had to get the child to safety quickly. Otherwise the witch would say: "If I get nothing from you, I'll cast misfortune on the baby."
192635: Feelke R. believed he had ridden around on a calf all night. The next morning, however, Feelke was sitting on a piece of wood. The man was bewitched.
192648: A certain Reynders worked together with Pieter Piekes as a farmhand on a farm. When Reynders came back one night from the fair in Millen, he saw a man lying on top of the door of the horse stable. Reynders thought it was Pieter, but when he went inside, he found Pieter asleep in his bed. Together the two farmhands went to examine the horse stable, but there was nothing strange to be seen anymore. It also often happened that they heard the horses snorting at night because there was a strange horse in the stable. In the morning the strange horse was gone, and the manes of the other horses were completely tangled. Sometimes in the morning the cows' tails were tied together as well. One day Pieter's wife climbed onto the hay when she felt someone strike her on the back. The woman turned around, but there was no one to be seen. At night Reynders and Pieter Piekes sometimes also heard strange noises in the loft, as if someone were bowling. Eventually the farmer sent for a friar from Maastricht, who made the ghost disappear by saying: "Here no stone shall remain upon another." From then on all was quiet on the farm.
192650: After a witch had tapped him on the shoulder, Louis's arm was completely stiff.
192655: Anyone who had been touched by the black hand could still see the black fingerprints on his neck. The devil had also burnt his hand into many church doors.
192659: During a hunt Charel H. finally managed to shoot a hare that had often been too quick for him. When he got home, Charel found his wife in bed with her arms and legs wrapped in cloths. The woman's wounds were full of shot.
192667: One day an archery contest was held in Ophoven. An old woman came in who claimed that nobody would be able to shoot down the main bird. The woman was proved right. When the old woman came by again in the evening, she shot down the main bird herself. People claimed that the woman was a witch.
192668: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend suddenly said: "Wait here a moment, because I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little later the girl saw a dog approaching. As her boyfriend had advised, she threw a handkerchief at the animal's mouth. When the boy reappeared, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
192670: A woman from Voorshoven went on pilgrimage with her baby to Sint-Huibrecht in Glabbeek. In Glabbeek the mother met a strange woman who stroked the baby over the shoulder, saying: "Jesus, what a beautiful baby you have!" When the mother came back with her baby, it had a crooked neck. That never went away.
192671: A child had made mice at school. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it could no longer make mice.
192695: People said that the Pekelsheg in Dilsen was haunted.
192701: Suzanne died in childbed shortly after her newborn child had died. After her death Suzanne came haunting. Her relatives remembered that during her pregnancy Suzanne had promised to offer a box of candles if all went well. After the candles had been offered, the ghost was not seen again.
192706: In Piringen lived a family that always had bad luck. One day someone advised the people to lay a cross in front of the door, so that the witch could no longer come in. After that the people had no more bad luck.
192709: A woman from Mopertingen who had been bedridden for forty years sent for a friar. When the friar cut open the mattress, he found all sorts of little woven figures.
192712: In the Greunstraat in Rekem there stood a big tree. Next to that tree was a lime pit. In the evening a white woman appeared at that spot. Perhaps it was someone who had fallen into the lime pit and was white because of it.
192715: A man who saw a large dog appear in the churchyard said to the animal: "If you are from God, speak. If you are from the devil, go away".
192730: A fire-man was a land surveyor who had to come back as a ghost because he had not measured the land properly. Only when he had put right all his mistakes could the dead man be admitted to heaven.
192742: At farmer Willem V.V.'s, all the animals had died within a short time. After the friars of het Loo had read prayers over the farm, no more strange things happened.
192746: In the meadows there was a devil's pit where bells could be heard ringing at midnight on Christmas. A man who went to look never came back.
192751: A woman walking from Opitter to Tongerlo met a strange apparition on the way. It was a white animal sitting by the road that kept coming closer. The woman said: "If you are of God, stay. If you are of the devil, go away." Immediately after these words the strange animal disappeared.
192758: Moen, Meng's grandfather, was a miller. One evening Moen went to visit his friend in Waterschei for a chat. After a few hours his friend's wife said: "Moen, go on home now, because I don't think you'll be home right away." "Why not?" asked Moen. The woman then patted his leg with her hand and said: "You'll have something happen to you yet." Before Moen had gone two hundred metres, he suddenly felt a terrible pain in his leg. The man could no longer stand and crawled on hands and knees back to his friend's house. "Call your wife, because she has to make me better again. Otherwise I'll set your house on fire." A few moments later the woman came downstairs and asked: "Moen, what's wrong with your knee?" Moen answered threateningly: "You did this to me, you filthy witch! If you don't undo it at once, I'll kill you!" The witch stroked the knee twice with her hand. After that Moen had no more pain.
192777: A man went to a place where he knew a little white horse regularly came. He would sit on the little horse and say: "Hoepel, kapoepel, over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Cologne". One day he told a friend his story about the little white horse. The friend said: "I'd like to come along once too and have a good drink there!", to which the man suggested: "The little horse comes to the Osseweg in the Zwartaardebos. If you like, come along there some time." The very next evening the man went to the place he had been told, and he already saw the little white horse coming. Although his friend was not there yet, he jumped on the animal's back and said: "Hoepel, kapoepel, through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar in Cologne". When the man arrived, he was covered in blood because he had been terribly battered on the way. The little white horse was unharmed. The man had learned his lesson: when he wanted to come back, he made sure he spoke the right words!
192778: In the Kempen, witches could be seen dancing at night between twelve and one o'clock in the shape of cats. If someone managed to wound one of the cats, the witch could be recognised the next day by the scar.
192797: A farmer drove a cart to the mill to have his grain ground. On the way a witch made the farmer's cart stand still.
192812: A married woman from Helchteren had an affair with two men. One night the woman and her children were murdered with a razor. After her death the woman came haunting with a big black dog. A pregnant woman who had been frightened at the sight of the ghost gave birth to a child with a dog's head. The woman had to smother the child. The priest banished the dog and the woman for ninety-nine years and more.
192817: Between 1900 and 1920 two old witches lived in Sint-Truiden. V., the elder of the two, had the worst reputation. She was very withdrawn and sought contact only with the village children. It was said that some children got lice after V. had stroked their heads. The other witch was called S. and was less feared by the villagers. Later in life she married a newcomer of unknown origin. It was claimed that S. never went to church.
192821: The castle of Nerem was haunted.
192837: In bewitched children, a wreath was often found in the pillow of the cot.
192848: In Nieuwerkerken lived a woman suspected of being a witch. After she had struck a boy on the shoulder with a hook, the boy was constantly ill. In the end he even died.
192876: Children born with a hunchback or hydrocephalus had been touched by the evil hand. A witch caused as many as ten to twelve children in Membruggen to be born with a disability.
192887: In the old days people put the forks and spoons in their clogs at night. On a farm that had much misfortune in the stable, the cutlery was heard rattling in the clogs at night. Because a murder had once taken place there, people believed someone came haunting the farm. The parish priest buried (banished?) the ghost in a lonely spot in the woods.
192896: Marie van 't Weverke from Grote-Brogel was suspected of being a witch. When Strooien Bert went hunting, he shot a hare. The man went to look but saw nothing. On his way home Strooien Bert met Marie, who had only one eye left.
192899: Every evening a hare came to nibble the cabbages in Driek P.'s garden. Dries had often tried to shoot the hare, but the animal seemed to be invulnerable.
192903: A boy returning from a visit to his girlfriend met a woman on the way who said: "I'll make sure I'm home before you". The boy could go no further because he had a strange feeling in his leg. Only when the strange woman was home could the boy move again.
192904: The witches often held gatherings on the Sleeberg in Lauw. Where they had danced, a large ring was found the next day. One evening a man was walking home from Grootloon. On the way he saw the witches dancing on the Sleeberg. One of the witches came to fetch the man to join the dance in the ring. After the dance the witches drank wine from a chalice. The man had also been given a chalice, but when he was about to drink, he said: "God be praised!" Suddenly the man stood alone in the field, the chalice still in his hands. When he got home, the man studied the chalice closely: it was made of gold and bore the name of a lady from Hasselt. The next day the man went to Hasselt, where he asked whether anyone knew the lady. He was sent to an elegant shop in which many women were standing. When the man asked for the lady because he had something for her, he was led to a small room. On seeing the chalice, the lady in question was very startled and said: "You must keep quiet about this! If you tell no one about this chalice, you will get a reward from me." The man promised to keep silent and received three new tailor-made suits.
192907: S., a man who had been a minister, came haunting in the hedge after his death.
192919: A man swung his clogs at a black cat sitting in the house. The man cried: "Fin, the devil is in the house!"
192923: When Harie S. was mowing, he struck at a cat with his scythe. The next moment there were as many as a hundred cats in the field. As soon as the man began to pray the Angelus, the cats vanished.
192931: A witch had come to buy flour from a miller. Because the witch had stood by the child's cradle for a while, the miller's neighbour advised sending for the chaplain. The woman knew that this witch had elsewhere conjured a cradle full of maggots. In the old days, however, children slept on a sack filled with straw, so maggots were often found in the straw without any witch having come by.
192941: A man travelling with horse and cart between Lozen and Hamont was hindered by a black cat that jumped between the spokes of the wheel. The horse began to sweat heavily and could barely pull the cart. When the farmer arrived in Hamont, the place was swarming with cats.
192949: A man who was warming himself saw a cat come in and said: "Come on, pussycat, come and warm yourself". A moment later a whole pack of cats was sitting inside, and they began to sing: "Had Jan K. not spoken so nicely this evening, we would have broken his neck tonight".
192952: Two young men went to visit their girlfriends in Beek. When one of the men tapped on the little window of the house, nobody opened. When the man called out, two cats or two birds suddenly came flying in. After that the door was opened.
192953: The electrician of Budel was repairing a wire up a pole when Trien B. walked past. Trien said to the man: "Mind you don't fall!" A little later the man fell to the ground.
192955: In a house in Maastricht a friar was called in to drive out the devil. "No, no," said the devil, "just go and return those apples you stole!" When another friar was called in, the devil said: "No, no, just go and return those pears you stole!" In the end a very old little friar who read from a book and prayed managed to drive the devil out.
192956: Herkenrode was haunted. After midnight a white lady walked past, who then suddenly disappeared again.
192975: One day a man went to Luik with his friend Schoof by horse and cart. On the road to Koninksheim the horse suddenly stopped. From midnight until one o'clock the horse stood motionless. Meanwhile the two men heard a little bell ringing, although nothing could be seen anywhere around. When the ringing stopped, the pair heard a whooshing sound and then a loud bang. After that the horse went on again. When the men drove back home, they saw that at that very spot stood two pear trees whose leaves were all lying on the ground.
192976: Liza worked as a maid for a lady in Martenslinde. A woman often came by, and Liza had to give her a loaf of bread. One day Liza was cleaning the oven while her mistress opened the door to the woman and said: "I'm sorry, but we haven't baked bread this week. Next week you'll get two loaves." The woman came in and saw Liza cleaning the oven. She said: "So, and you're just polishing the oven!" and she stroked the girl's head. The following Sunday the maid was forced to go home, because her hair was full of lice. The Holy Little Father of Hasselt freed the girl from the vermin. But Liza had been so frightened by what happened that she died at the age of twenty-two.
192977: The drossaard (bailiff) came haunting at the Hobos. In the end the ghost was banished under a bridge for ninety-nine years.
192980: Katoke V. lived in the witches' alley. Whenever this witch came near children, they were covered in lice.
192995: Two friends had agreed that whoever died first would give the other a sign from the hereafter. When one of the friends had died, he came back as promised. The ghost was dressed entirely in white, but had two black fingers. The other man came back after his death with only one black finger.
193013: A farmhand who was a werewolf could do heavy work effortlessly. One day the farmhand was sent to Weert with a cart full of wheat. Meanwhile the farmhand's collar was thrown into the oven. A moment later the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his band.
193018: After a woman had touched a child, the child's little feet were completely twisted.
193021: In the Bosstraat in Maaseik lived a woman who was said to be a witch. One day the woman had visited a child. By evening the child was paralysed. The child's parents then had the witch come back and forced her to undo the harm.
193025: In Grote-Spouwen there was a haunted house. A brave man decided to spend the night in the house. When the man was preparing his food over the fire, a bone suddenly fell down the chimney. "Let it fall," said the man, "but not in my cooking pot." A little later something else fell down the chimney. The man threw all the bones that had fallen down the chimney into a corner. Meanwhile the skeleton was complete. The man stayed standing by the fire, because he knew that in a haunted place one must never look behind. After a while the ghost had vanished.
193033: Near Neeroeteren or Opoeteren lived a farmhand who was away every evening. One day the farmer found the farmhand's collar in a hollow tree stump. The farmhand was sent to the field with the horse, so that the farmer could burn the band in the meantime. The farmer had to hold the farmhand back so that he would not jump into the oven to save his collar. When everything had burnt up, the farmhand was released.
193055: A woman was in the habit of spinning in the evening after her husband had gone to sleep. The woman always heard a tapping on the window and a little later a voice that said: "I spun day and night and now I only get a shirt with one sleeve." It was the man's first wife who came to haunt.
