She found no rest because she had been buried in a shroud with one sleeve. One night the man put out the light and said to his wife: "Come to bed quickly." The woman never had to spin again.
193082: A young maid worked on a farm in 't Roeren in Opitter. Whenever the maid was churning butter, the building shook to its foundations. When the police kept watch there, the same thing happened again. Although the maid was only fifteen, she already had the powers of a grown witch.
193091: Some men who went to fetch hay with their horses could not get out of the meadow because the witch Zwarte Fles had bewitched the animals.
193093: At midnight a man came to haunt a farm and filled the trees with birds.
193096: A farmer had bought a field and sown it with grain. When the farmer walked past his grain field some time later, he met Trees Zontrop there, a woman who was said to be a witch. Trees said to the farmer: "What fine grain! Let's hope you can harvest it like that." Two weeks later the grain lay flat on the ground, just as if there had been a heavy hailstorm.
193099: A man got up in the night to mow the grain. He had been woken by the light of the full moon, convinced it was already morning. When he was in his field, he was suddenly surrounded by cats. At that the man quickly ran back home.
193103: One day a farmer from Stamprooi was visited by a woman who was said to be a witch. The farmer told the witch that the brook behind his garden was full of rats. The witch listened carefully and then said the rat plague would soon be over. The next day all the rats lay dead in the brook.
193105: An old lawyer had been banished into the cellar of L. The lawyer was extremely rich, but he had unlawfully acquired much of his land. When the lawyer had died and his body had been laid out, the corpse suddenly disappeared. So as not to cause panic among the villagers, the coffin was filled with stones and buried that way. After his death, however, the lawyer came to haunt a cellar. A Redemptorist banished his ghost to a part of the cellar, which was then walled up. Because someone who was not properly buried can always come back to haunt, the priest now banishes every dead person into their grave.
193143: The meadow along the road to Repen was haunted. A man passing there was followed by a large black cat. The man struck at the cat, but the animal kept walking in front of him. The man then hurried home.
193147: A man from Heur-le-Thyx went poaching at night in the count's wood in Rutten. Suddenly the man saw something strange in the ditch by the side of the road. It looked like a sack filled with something. The man was terrified when the sack rolled towards him and made a whistling sound. The man hurried home as fast as he could. The man fell ill from fright and died a short time later.
193165: In a café in Berg sat a man who could conjure mice out of his handkerchief. That man was in league with the devil.
193170: The alvermannen (elf men) often made people lose their way. If you prayed the Our Father, you soon found your way back.
193172: A thief from Munsterbilzen who had broken into the church of Zutendaal could not get away; he was stuck in the window. A painting was made of the scene, and it still hangs in the church.
193192: A boy out walking with his girlfriend saw a witch in the shape of a dog sitting in a ditch. When the boy wanted to hit the dog, his girlfriend cried: "No, you mustn't hit it!" Then the dog said: "No, you mustn't hit me, for I am a neighbour!"
193195: On a lane near the Weertbergske in Opgrimbie a black friar always walked in the evening without saying a word.
193201: Some men went with a cart and two oxen to fetch hay in the meadow. When they came back with the fully loaded cart, they had to drive past a witch's house. The witch would then come out with a slice of bread for the ox. Once the animal had eaten the bread, the cart could go no further.
193214: A man sitting in a café said to his friends: "Whoever dares to chop into the trunk of a weeping willow will hear the tree groan." One of the men took up the challenge. After the man had chopped into the trunk, he heard a voice saying: "You are going to kill me." The man died of fright.
193216: Someone who had moved a boundary post to have a bigger field had to come haunting after his death. The same happened to people who had promised to have a mass said but had never kept that promise.
193223: A farmhand returning from a visit to his girlfriend was warned by a woman: "Make sure you get home quickly, or else the werewolf will come after you!" When the boy saw a large dog a little further on, he was scared to death. At the crossroads the boy made the sign of the cross over the road and over himself. The dog could go no further.
193231: At the place where the gallows used to stand, a man on horseback often rode by. People also called the horse 'the fire horse'. One day a brave man struck the strange rider on the head with a medlar stick. Since then the man on horseback has not been seen again.
193277: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend by the canal said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a big dog comes at you, throw my handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. When the boy came back a while later, he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
193281: A little boy who sometimes went with his father to work in Sint-Truiden had to come home alone in the evening. When the boy was on the Hasseltseweg in Bokrijk, he suddenly saw a headless dog coming towards him.
193283: In the past many little books of magic were sold. Such books could never be got rid of; even if one threw away or burned a book of magic, it always came back. In Neerpelt lived a man who could make people stand still in the street with the help of his book of magic.
193319: A girl had gone with her boyfriend to buy clogs. On the way back the young man said: "Wait here. I have to relieve myself." The boy gave his girlfriend a handkerchief and said: "If you meet a big dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth. Then the dog won't be able to harm you." Further on the girl did indeed meet a dog. She threw the handkerchief at the animal. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl never wanted to see the boy again.
193337: A man coming home by moonlight saw a large white cat sitting on the road. After a while the cat crawled into a drain hole of a house.
193339: In the old days many wells were haunted. Almost every well had a ghost that rattled chains at night or pulled passers-by who came too close into the well.
193342: When Fin had just been washed, she went out for a short walk. When she came home, Fin was full of lice.
193348: A child from Mechelen had become seriously ill after being touched by the evil hand. Since the doctor could not help the child, it eventually died.
193349: Because all the animals in her stable were dying, a farmer's wife went to the friars for advice. When a friar came to read prayers over the stable, he said: "Just look up and you'll see the witch." Indeed, the neighbour woman was sitting on the stable roof. The prayer had forced the witch to come.
193370: The Freemasons held meetings with the devil and had to sign their names in blood.
193379: Someone had hanged himself in the cottage near Aat on the Loch. Because people believed the suicide came back to haunt, hardly anyone dared go near the cottage. When Gust Verpoortere from Eigenbilzen came onto the Loch, he saw the ghost lying on the hedge.
193385: Farmer W. had a farmhand who owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. When the farmhand was at work in the field, the oven was lit to burn the collar. As soon as the band caught fire, the boy was standing beside the oven. It took four people to hold the boy back until the collar had burnt up completely.
193401: Some men went to visit a roofer far from home. The men had barely sat down when the mother of one of them came in, saying: "Isn't our x here?" That mother must have been a witch, because she could hardly walk and yet she had got to that café so quickly.
193405: A man on his way to Vliermaal suddenly saw a will-o'-the-wisp. He laughed and said mockingly: "Come and light the way for me." At that the will-o'-the-wisp flew into the man's eyes and burned his whole face. The man quickly made the sign of the cross and then the will-o'-the-wisp was gone.
193406: A sick child in whose pillow a wreath was found could not be helped by the doctor.
193411: In Hamont the priests banished a ghost for ninety-nine and a half years. The clergymen took a small shovelful of earth from the place where the ghost wandered to the property of the deceased. That property was a marshy meadow that was under water in winter. After that the ghost once came gliding around there while clapping its hands.
193412: The devil usually appeared with goat's legs and a tuft for a tail. That tail could never burn, not even when burning oil was thrown on it.
193429: In Meeuwen lived a man in whose garden two hares were always running about. Because the hares were always nibbling his vegetables, the man wanted to shoot the animals. But he could not, for his gun never worked when the hares were nearby. A friend advised him to sprinkle the gun with holy water. When the man saw the hares in his garden again, the gun did work: he shot his wife and daughter dead.
193432: A young man walking along the brook on the Berg in the evening met a white lady, who walked on with him arm in arm. One day a farmer found a lot of money under a stone lying among the roots of a tree. Once that money was gone, the white lady no longer appeared.
193434: The P. family had a baby that began to cry every night at twelve o'clock. A clergyman sent the parents to a friar of Achel. The friar advised the mother to make sure Fien M. could no longer get near the baby. From then on the child no longer cried at midnight.
193439: A young man had been given food by a witch. At midnight his mother heard the food rattling in the dish. She then poured holy water into the dish and burned the food.
193441: A child's bed was always full of ants. The priests advised the parents not to give anything to anyone who came asking for something. When one day a woman came by to ask for something, the man said: "If you don't get out quickly, I'll kick you out of the house!" At that the witch left. When a witch had something belonging to someone, she had power over that person.
193445: A boy was digging potatoes with his father when Monne K. suddenly came up and said: "That's a fine horse!" A little later the horse stumbled, fell and got the 'link' (?) in its haunch. When the children went singing at New Year, they would not accept the cakes they were given by the witch Monne. To protect themselves against the witch, people often went to fetch blessed objects in Tongerlo.
193468: When a witch stood in front of the mirror, she knew all sorts of things she could not normally have known.
193470: In a family living next to the churchyard a little child had died. As tradition required, the child's grave was decorated with paper flowers. Every time the parents saw the paper flowers, they were so moved that they nearly died of grief. The old grandfather wanted to ease the parents' suffering a little by taking the paper flowers off the gravestone at night. But when the grandfather had taken the flowers away at night, he could no longer find the way out of the churchyard. He wandered around the whole time and kept coming back past the child's grave. When it was nearly morning, the grandfather decided to put the flowers back on the grave after all. After that he found the exit of the churchyard at once.
193475: A witch who did not get on with her neighbour made the vegetables in his garden swarm with pests.
193476: A man who came back to haunt kept saying: "Where must I go with my boundary post? Where must I go with my boundary post?" Finally someone answered: "Put it where you took it from". After that the ghost appeared no more.
193478: When M. from Vorst went peddling, he always passed the house of a witch on the Wetsberg. One day, when the man took the witch's dung fork, a cat suddenly flew onto his shoulders.
193487: A man coming back from the café was suddenly jumped on by black cats, which disappeared again a little later.
193490: Strange things happened at K.'s in 't Roeren. The little turn-latch that kept the window shut kept flying off for no apparent reason. A carpenter from Beek decided to keep an eye on the latch for a while. After an hour and a half nothing had happened yet. Suddenly the carpenter closed his eyes for a moment because he had to sneeze. When he opened his eyes again, the latch was gone. In the end the parish priest was sent for. The priest made sure that the bewitched latch stayed on the window from then on.
193492: Someone asked a dead man who had returned what the afterlife was like. The ghost replied: "Strictly reckoned and little forgiven!"
193508: In an office in Germany, during the day, people suddenly heard a sound as if someone were rubbing a wet finger over the windowpane. One of the men went to look and turned deathly pale. "My father appeared to me," the man said, "and he told me that I must prepare myself, because I will die within twenty-four hours." The man quickly went home and anxiously stayed indoors. He paced about restlessly. When he went to take a look on the balcony, the railing broke off. The man fell down and was dead.
193513: A man who went to work in Hougreye often saw a witch in the shape of a cat on the way.
193521: In Elen, people always used to have to carry the werewolf. When they came to a stream, the werewolf pushed its victim into the water.
193525: A man who was guarding the laundry was jumped on by a werewolf that had itself carried.
193541: If you could hit a werewolf on the forehead, he changed into a human and you could recognise him.
193548: The Langeren-Langerenplaats and the Langerenmolen were owned by friars. Because the friars feared their property would be confiscated by the French, a deed was drawn up transferring the whole monastery to a certain P. After the French Revolution, however, P. would not give the monastery back to the friars. When P. had died, he had to come back to haunt. A strange rattling was often heard in the monastery.
193568: A man had a farmhand who owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. After the man had sent his farmhand away for an hour and a half, he took the collar out of the tree stump and lit the oven. As soon as the collar caught fire, the farmhand jumped into the oven to save his band.
193571: Hendrikske was invited by his girlfriend to go with her to the fair on the Meeuwer-hei. The young man did not know, however, that his girlfriend was a witch, and that all the witches of the area gathered on the Meeuwer-hei. After a few hours of celebrating, the witch abandoned Hendrikske, leaving the young man all alone on the heath. Hendrikske tried several times in vain to take a path to the Zwartberg in Genk. Only much later did the man get home.
193574: Gon was known as a neat woman who always wore a little white cap. However, Gon had a woman in her family who had a bad reputation. One day the woman said to Gon: "Filth will eat you up, just as you sit there!" Some time later Gon was plagued by countless fat lice that had settled on her head. Nothing helped to get rid of the vermin. Shortly afterwards Gon died.
193576: In the old days, when a baby died, it was often a witch's fault. In Opgrimbie, for instance, there lived a witch named Bet. To know for certain whether the child had been bewitched, one had to examine the sheets in the cot after the child's death. With bewitched children, the shape of a heart or of a child's body could be seen in the sheets.
193599: In Kessenich the alvermannetjes (elf men) set fire to Jef G.'s haystack because his family had become too poor to provide the dwarfs with food. From then on no resident of Kessenich gave food to the alvermannetjes any more, so the dwarfs eventually left.
193625: A woman with a bad reputation went up to a man who was working in the field. The next day the man had a spot in his eye.
193628: In the shepherd's meadow in Piringen a ghost crawled through the hedge. Walkers who had seen the ghost could not get through the hedge.
193631: On Caberg there lived a wood seller who always went to fetch wood in the Kempen. One day the man ended up in a meadow with his cart. Only the next morning did the lost man get out of the meadow. "I was bewitched," the man said afterwards.
193637: Because Suzie was terrified of a witch who lived in the village, she begged her mother not to let the witch into the shop any more. Above the door hung a cross that had been blessed in Scherpenheuvel, and the priest gave them a little cross to put under the floorcloth by the threshold. When the witch then tried to come in, she tumbled into the cellar. The witch said angrily: "I could have broken my neck over that floorcloth!"
193641: A farmer whose house was full of rats and mice recited the Saint John prayer. The next moment all the rats and mice had disappeared.
193652: In Wilderen lived a witch who infested the children with lice.
193657: Some men who saw a cat sitting by a stone cross said: "Shall we knock that kitten off the cross?" When one of the men struck at the animal, there was a sound as if someone had hit a bucket. The cat followed close on the men's heels until they were home.
193672: A girl who worked on G.'s farm was in a relationship with the farmer's son. When the young man was out walking with his girlfriend, he said to the girl: "You go on ahead. I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at the beast." When the girl met a dog further on, she did what her boyfriend had advised. That night, however, the girl could not sleep. In the morning she packed all her clothes and left. The farmer never managed to keep a maid in service for long.
193676: Marie's baby had become seriously ill after sleeping on a pillow in which a witch's wreath was hidden. Fortunately the child recovered and was given new bedding. After a while a woman from the neighbourhood decided to fetch the pillowcase from Marie; people were not well off and things could not simply be thrown away. But when the woman put the pillowcase in her child's bed, the child began to scream loudly: "There's something in bed with me!" In the end the woman threw the pillowcase away after all.
193678: A man setting off for the woods in the morning met a woman on the way, who asked: "Are you going to the woods?" The man answered: "Yes, I'm leaving early so I'll be back early." The woman said: "Yes, but you won't be back so soon!" The man got lost in the woods and by evening he was still not home.
193720: In Budel stood a house that was haunted. When people tried to drive past the house with horse and cart, the horse sometimes stopped dead. Because the horses would not go past the house, the farmers often had to make a detour. In the end the house was torn down.
193724: A father whose child always wanted to lie on a plank suspected that his child was bewitched. So the child's parents went to the friars of Wijk, north of Maastricht. On the way the couple fell twice. When the friars saw the man's torn trousers, they said: "That was an invisible hand that pushed you over. We will start praying. When you get home, the child will be sitting upright in its cot." And so it happened.
193725: Katrien from Rosmeer went with a friend to lift beets in Tricht-Wolder. Suddenly Katrien said to her companion: "There comes old Bocken with his black horse. Shall I make him turn around?" Katrien sat down in the middle of the road, dug a little hole and drew a cross over it. When the horse reached that spot, it began to foam at the mouth and rear. Bocken forced Katrien to undo the harm she had done. Then the other woman said to Katrien: "Now I believe what people always say about you. You are a witch!"
193727: During the German occupation the soldiers had to keep watch at night. Strangely, the men were found dead in the morning. When one evening a soldier saw a big black dog coming towards him, he struck the animal on the muzzle. The next day the commander had a wound on his head.
193732: In the Laker vin lay a bell that had been stolen by the French and thrown into the marsh. On Christmas night the bell could be heard ringing at midnight.
193743: A witch had bewitched a baby's head so that it faced backwards. When baker G. learned of this, he threatened the witch and forced her to undo the harm she had done. The witch then turned the baby's head the right way round again.
193744: In a house a woman was found wrapped in sacks, making strange noises. When the sacks had been thrown into the fire, the woman said: "Well, what have you come here for?" It was a witch who had been out and about.
193748: Harrie P.'s calves would not grow. Because the vet was at a loss, Harrie sent for the parish priest. After the priest had read prayers over the stable, the calves grew normally, as they had been freed from the evil hand.
193749: A man going home in the evening got lost and ended up in Zonhoven towards morning. A witch was to blame.
193769: Jan V. was a musician who was coming back from the fair in Bommershoven with his violin. On the way a young cat began to rub against his legs, whereupon Jan V. said: "Pussycat, where do you come from?" At that moment the cat grabbed Jan's violin and flew up into a tree full of witches. The cat played the violin and sang: "'Pussycat, where do you come from?', Jan V. asked of me." The other witches sang after the cat in chorus.
193787: A farmer's wife had twenty-seven young chickens. When she went to feed her chickens one Sunday, she found to her horror that all of them were dead. A little later the witch came by, saying: "People say you have such fine chickens!"
193790: A weaver went on foot to deliver clothes to a customer. On the way a little hare jumped between his legs. When the weaver struck at the animal, it suddenly vanished. When the weaver told his customers what had happened to him on the way, they offered to let him stay the night. The weaver was not afraid, however, and decided to go home by another road. This time the weaver met dozens of mewing cats. When the weaver was home, he saw through his window a sow with a chain around her neck coming along. When the man shot at the animal, so many sparks flew from his gun that his house caught fire. The fire could only be put out with holy water.
193804: On the road from Gingelom to Montenaken stood a house where a witch used to live. That witch could stop the train from a kilometre away.
193805: In a lane running through Rikbos, people heard a spirit calling: "Raise dogs, raise children!"
193828: A woman who had been infested with lice by a witch could not get rid of the creatures.
193839: A friar who saw the devil sitting on a remote road asked: "What are you doing here?", to which the devil replied: "I've come here to catch souls". The friar then said: "Then you'd better go to the pine wood". But the devil answered: "Enough sinning goes on there already!"
193844: In Eigenbilzen there was a sick child whom the doctor could not help. The little boy became skin and bone and hovered between life and death. In the end a friar was sent for, who read prayers for half a day and then said: "The boy will not live much longer. At the moment he dies, a woman will come to ask for something you don't have." When the boy died, hoarse Trijn came by.
193859: Around 1890 or 1891 the rich farmer Jan B. fell dead in his bakehouse in Heppen. After his death Jan B. came haunting. Later two thousand francs were found in a drawer in the barn.
193865: In villa Labaer there were always stones lying on the floor of the bakehouse in the morning. At midnight the ghost from the Maas came, with a white sheet over its head, and threw stones down the chimney.
193882: A girl was always afraid when she saw a little hare sitting on a path in the dark in the evening.
193894: Witches who wanted to fly took something from the chimney and then spoke the following magic formula: "Over hedge and hawthorn to the wine cellar of Aachen". A man who had spied on some witches wanted to try it too. He took something from the chimney and then said: "Through hedge and hawthorn to the wine cellar of Aachen." Because the man had made a mistake, he was badly hurt and never reached Aachen.
193895: A man going to Halen with his wheelbarrow suddenly saw a headless foal walking beside him. Because the man believed the foal was a ghost, he took out his rosary and began to read the Gospel of St John. As long as the man kept praying, the foal could no longer be seen. As soon as he stopped praying, the animal appeared again.
193903: A woman went to the friars about a problem she suspected was caused by witches. On the way the woman suddenly could not move forward; it was as if she were nailed to the ground. Then the woman began to pray. Only when she had prayed almost a whole rosary on her beads could she move forward again.
193907: A farmer who could not keep a single farmhand had given up hope that anyone would still want to work for him. One day the farmer nevertheless took on a new farmhand. As the farmhand lay sleeping in the stable, he heard a cat meowing at midnight. The farmhand stroked the cat and then stabbed the animal with his knife. The next morning the farmer's wife lay wounded in bed.
193919: People who were bewitched got lice. They tried to fight the lice with paraffin or vinegar.
193920: Anyone who has to go and fetch a midwife at night had better not go alone, for he may experience strange things. Midwives also never walk home alone in the dark, not even if they live close by. One night two men had taken a midwife back to her house in Mielen-boven-Aalst. On the way back the pair suddenly lost sight of each other. They had both lost their way, and in the morning one arrived at Sneyers chapel and the other at Borremans chapel.
193921: Anna was said to be a witch. When people were going to bake bread, they were not allowed to tell anyone. Otherwise Anna would make sure the fire in the oven would not stay lit.
193955: A bricklayer and his son were coming home from work in the evening. When they passed the churchyard, the father said: "You'd be scared here, wouldn't you!" The son wanted to prove his courage and wandered about to find out what fear really was. Further on the young man reached a castle where he wanted to spend the night. But he was warned: "No one who has been here ever dares to come back!" "That is just what I was looking for," the young man answered bravely. That night, on the stroke of twelve, the young man saw bones falling down the chimney. He said: "What's this? Soon I'll be able to play skittles! I only need a ball." The next moment a skull rolled down. "Now I need company to play skittles," said the young man. At once more than ten silent ghosts appeared in the room. The young man asked: "Who wants to play skittles with me?" Because not a single ghost said anything, the boy shouted in annoyance: "Idiot, open your trap then!" The next moment the ghosts flew angrily around and knocked everything over. When the lord of the castle asked the young man in the morning whether he had enjoyed himself, he replied: "Yes, but I still don't know what being afraid is." The same scene took place during the second night. During the third night the young man was chased into the cellar by the ghosts. Then some ghosts came and said: "In that corner is a pot of gold for the lord of the castle. In that corner is a pot of gold to have masses said for the ghosts. And in that corner is a pot of gold for you. We must thank you, for now we are released. We needed someone who dared to stay here for three days." The young man went home and said to his father: "Now you never have to work again, because we are very rich. But I still regret that I don't know what fear is."
193960: People believed that the café owner's wife was a witch, since the woman could take on all kinds of shapes.
193966: A soldier who had been out asked a farmer for shelter and said: "Just let me lie in your barn". The farmer answered: "I don't know if you'll be able to stand it, because something always happens in my barn." At night the soldier heard a tremendous noise coming from the cellar under the barn. In the morning the soldier said to the farmer: "Next time I will rid you of that ghost". Eight days later the soldier came back with a black billy goat. At night the soldier threw the goat into the cellar with the words: "That is for you and the rest is for me". The soldier left the barn with a treasure of gold coins. The ghost that made itself heard every night had in fact been coming back to count its money. The soldier had delivered the ghost.
193991: A man coming back from Bergering had caught a cat on the way. When the man came to the little chapel, he saw about a hundred cats there, who called: "Poeske Vanderminne!" The captured cat answered: "I'm here in the sack!"
194013: For the kermis (village fair), a farmer and his wife had invited their neighbours over for a piece of tart. Afterwards they all went to look at the animals in the stable. Because the farmer knew that one of those present was a witch, he said: "Keep your hands off the cows!" But it was already too late, for the woman had already stroked the animal's back. Three weeks later the cow was dead.
194015: A woman had promised to go on pilgrimage. However, she died before she could keep her promise. After her death the woman's spirit went along with a walking stick on pilgrimage with her family.
194018: A man coming back from Kaulille on a winter evening heard a strange rustling in the woods of Grote-Brogel. Suddenly the man saw a headless white figure appear in a clearing in the woods, which came at him violently. When the man held the cross of his rosary towards the ghost, the apparition vanished.
194033: When J.S. was returning from a visit to his girlfriend, he met a man who said: "I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little later a dog did indeed come, and J.S. did as he had been advised. A little later both men went to an inn. J.S. saw that his companion still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. J.S. was not allowed to tell anyone that he knew who the werewolf was, for then he would die.
194054: A gentleman who was a director in Ougrée-Mariehaye went to teach the farmers in the Kempen how to fertilise their fields. A man who had spread too much fertiliser on his field was amazed that no grain grew there. Because people believed the field was bewitched, the man sold his land. The following year, however, the new owner brought in a rich harvest; the excess chlorine had in time disappeared from the soil.
194057: Some men were digging potatoes in the field when a cart with two horses drove past. One of the farmhands said: "Shall I make that cart stand still?" The next moment the horses could not take another step. The carter got off the cart and lifted the horses' legs. Then the horses could pull the cart again. The farmhand said: "That man can do more than I can."
194059: A large farm built in the eleventh century was run by monks. One day one of the monks met the devil, who was carrying a heavy stone and asked whether he was still far from Tongeren. "Four more hours," the monk replied. The devil then said: "That's too far for me, my stone is so heavy!" and he threw the stone into the moat. The stone, which is so hard that axes break when people strike it, still lies in the moat today.
194084: One day Jan S. was passing through Nieuwenhovenbos when he suddenly heard beautiful music. He followed the sound and came to a house where women were drinking and dancing. Jan made the sign of the cross, and suddenly everything had vanished. Jan was sitting with his backside in a thorn bush.
194089: A farmhand who worked at Spikelspaai was told by his master to go and fetch faggots for an old woman. Because people believed that woman was a witch, they said to the farmhand: "You'd better hurry, or you'll run into her! You're sure to meet a cat!" When the boy came to the three kings, he did indeed see a cat appear, which said: "I came to see where you'd got to". At that the boy ran away as fast as he could.
194105: Heksebetje came into a house where the barber was cutting someone's hair. She rubbed the barber's head and said: "What a lovely head!" When the barber came home, his hair was full of lice.
194107: On the Hondsberg, Zjang van Zjänke often saw a werewolf in the shape of a black dog. When Ida van Thijs took her son Eugène to the college, she too was often followed by a large black dog. Anyone followed by a werewolf was not allowed to speak. That way the animal could do its companion no harm.
194123: Three men wanted to take an animal to Meeuwen together. The mother of one of the men was said to be a witch. When two of the men went to fetch the third in the morning, they saw lots of cats crawling out through the drain holes. The men then went on alone.
194143: In the mattress of a restless child, a little doll was found that did not yet have an arm.
194151: At night ghosts flew around the legs of walkers.
194152: The Peeës family had a strange farmhand. One day one of the children was playing in the horse stable. In that stable the girl found a book that the farmhand had hidden there. The child, who was fourteen at the time, took the book to the garden and began reading it eagerly. After a few hours her father grew worried and decided to look for his daughter. When he finally found her, the girl could not move: she seemed nailed to the ground. The chaplain, who was praying in his summerhouse across the street, quickly came to look. The chaplain established that the girl had been reading a book of magic and had given herself over entirely to evil. After the clergyman had said prayers over the girl for a long time, she could stand up again. The farmhand was dismissed on the spot.
194156: A man who had to fetch wood with his horse could not reach his destination. In the Hommelenven in Genk the man met the brother of a witch, who boxed his ears. Then the man's cart suddenly lay upside down.
194164: In Stal an old woman lived opposite her daughter's house. When that old woman crossed the street, one had to put one's foot across her track. The old woman would then look round.
194174: A man walking through the fields was followed by a few black cats. A few moments later there were suddenly twenty cats. When the man walked past a crossroads and saw that the cats did not follow him, he realised that the animals were witches.
194176: A man who had been to see his girlfriend was walking home. As he came through a meadow, a foal ran into him. A little later the man came to a gravestone. He lost his way and could not get out of the meadow. Only at daybreak did the man find the gate of the meadow. The foal and the gravestone had vanished.
194180: A man coming home late in the evening met a white lady whose skirt rustled in the wind.
194209: A man struck twice at a cat sitting on a tree stump. Each time the cat jumped back onto the stump. When the man had struck for the third time, the cat said: "Now strike once more."
194210: While pregnant, Lena went to the market in Maastricht with her sister Bet. On the way Lena met a strange woman who claimed that the Belgian five-centime coins were no longer worth anything. From that day on Lena woke up every night at twelve o'clock. She saw ghosts and witches coming in through the window. Because Lena would then say: "In God's name, be gone!", they could not harm her. Yet Lena eventually died. Because the witch could not die, she asked the parish priest to go to the friar in Rekem.
194231: An eleven-month-old child had died because of a witch. After a medal was placed under the threshold, the witch no longer had any power in the house.
194249: A man was jumped on by the werewolf near the Spekbrug. The man had to carry the werewolf as far as a crossroads. Then the werewolf laughed at him. The beast was black and extremely heavy.
194252: A girl who went to fetch fodder met a woman who said: "Give me some fodder." When the girl refused, the woman said: "Then you won't get your sack full!" And indeed, the girl could not fill her sack.
194266: Near the castle of Opleeuw a white horse and a dog with a chain were always roaming about.
194288: A girl had to tend the cows in the meadow. When Marketrien came by, all the cows suddenly vanished. The girl began to cry, whereupon Marketrien said: "You needn't cry, for in five minutes all the cows will be back here." And so it happened.
194290: A woman who had gone to buy two pigs at the market in Tongeren passed a witch's house on the way back. At that moment the witch came out and asked: "Are they nice pigs? May I have a look? How much do they cost?" The next day the pigs lay dead in the sty. A week later the woman went to Tongeren again to buy two new pigs. Before setting off, however, she went on pilgrimage to Mulken in honour of Saint Giles. After Mass she had a five-franc coin blessed. At the market the woman made the sign of the cross over the animals with the blessed coin, after which she went to offer the coin to Our Lady in the Hoogkerk. When she went home with the pigs, she took the Kastanjelarenstraat so that she would not have to pass the witch's house. This time the pigs stayed healthy.
194297: Marcus or Markske came to haunt 'De Graaf'. The ghost was banished there for ninety-nine years.
194309:
Some farmhands working at the farm on the Kruissteenweg were sitting outside in the evening when an old woman came along. One of the farmhands said: "Hey Witte, let that woman walk past. Then follow her for ten steps, and she'll turn around and get angry. That is, if you dare, because she'll make you pay for it afterwards!" Fearless, Witte accepted the challenge. At the tenth step the woman did indeed turn around and said: "You rascal! This will cost you dearly!" When Witte was painting the front of the house on a ladder a week later, the woman passed by again. At that moment Witte could no longer move. It was as if he were nailed to the ladder. The farmhand had no choice but to stay on the ladder until the woman came back from town. On her return the woman touched the ladder, and luckily Witte could move again.
The woman was a witch who had sold her soul to the devil.
194312: The H. family was followed by a ghost dog in the evening.
194333: At a quarter past twelve at night the dead baron came haunting the castle grounds of Jongebos in a coach drawn by six horses. The baron drove around the castle three or four times and then disappeared again.
194334: A man whose little child cried all the time went to the priest, because he feared a witch was responsible for the trouble. But on the way the man got lost, so that he only reached the priest after several hours.
194336: A witch who had been at a farm had bewitched the horse. The next day the horse's mane was braided.
194347: A witch had bewitched a pregnant girl. When the baby was born, it turned out to have a crooked little head. The priest claimed that a witch was capable of such evil.
194354: A woman from Maaseik was suspected of witchcraft. The clergy decided to test her by having her take communion at Mass on Sunday. As people had expected, the witch spat out the host. When the sexton's wife tried to pick up the host, her finger stuck to the floor. After a while the priest managed to free her.
194363: A farmer whose wife had died was visited by a woman who wanted to come and live with him. One day, as the farmer was cleaning the stable, he saw a plank with a little knot in it. The woman came closer and said: "If you take that knot out, I can get through." After the farmer had removed the knot, the woman disappeared. He never saw the witch again.
194398: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who found no rest because they had died unbaptised.
194399: In Tiewinkel, a hamlet of Lummen, a witch always came to borrow all sorts of things from Rik L. The witch always brought back what she had borrowed. But because the people could no longer make butter, they went to the friars in Hasselt. There they were advised no longer to accept the borrowed things the witch came to return. That way, after all, the witch would lose her power.
194402: Some people went to keep vigil at night beside a deceased neighbour. After the people had drunk a few glasses, the dead man suddenly said: "It is fitting to pray and be silent beside a dead man." The people replied: "It is fitting for the dead to be silent," and they gave the dead man a box on the ears.
194412: A man who had to take the midwife back to Genebos at night met a cat just before 't Zand. When the man had struck at the cat, there were suddenly a good thousand cats blocking his way. After the man had said: "In God's name," the cats vanished with a great deal of noise.
194419: A farmhand who played the werewolf had hidden a dog's skin in a meadow. When the farmhand had gone to Brussel, people wanted to burn the dog's skin in the meantime. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was standing by the oven.
194424: In a meadow near the church in Sluizen, people often heard the sound of a witches' drum. That drum was the signal for the witches to gather to dance.
194427: A man found two small balls of yarn in the field. His wife forbade him to pick up the yarn, or else the children would lose their eyes. But the man would not listen and picked up the yarn anyway. The children went blind.
194432: In Heppeneert some men were playing cards when suddenly the devil came in to fetch someone who had sold his soul to him. The devil said to his victim: "Chase away that woman behind you!", to which the man replied: "I can't chase anyone away, for I see no one." The man was protected by Our Lady.
194450: One of the hens in the henhouse had chicks. Because some cats were prowling about, poison was put down near the henhouse. The next day a grey cat lay dead by the poison. A few days later a black cat was seen eating the poison and apparently staying perfectly healthy. Since people suspected the black cat was a witch, some holy water was poured around the henhouse. The black cat never came back.
194459: A poacher who had shot a hare at night was frightened to hear another hare ask: "Rik, where are you?" At that the poacher dropped everything and went home.
194467: A little woman who went sewing in Hees was followed by a dog as far as the Heilige Haag.
194479: On a little bridge in Stevoort a white lady sometimes appeared at night. Most people were terrified of the apparition and ran away when they saw the white lady. One night, however, there was a man who was not afraid. He said to the lady: "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, step aside." At that the lady stepped off the bridge to let the man pass.
194480: A farmer whose animals were all dying was given a relic by the priest to place under the stable door. "A woman will come by who will ask you for three things. You must give her those things," the priest predicted. The next day a woman did indeed come asking for three things, including a clog and a sack of buckwheat flour. After the farmer had given the woman everything she asked for, he had no more misfortune. Moreover, because of the relic, the witch could no longer get into the stable.
194488: Two people from 't Moosbroeck in Mopertingen had gone to fetch hay at the 'heksenkruiske' (witches' cross) in the evening. Suddenly two black cats came running up. The next moment two women were sitting there and began to rub themselves with ointment. They were witches.
194489: When a devil was born in Herselt, the child was smothered in the mattress.
194492: Because it rained on Sunday, it was decided not to hold a procession, for fear that the statue of Mary would get dirty. On Monday morning it was found that the mantle of the statue of Mary was covered in mud.
194497: One could recognise a witch by putting a blessed palm sprig under the door, since witches could not step over it. One could also recognise a witch by placing one's feet crossed in her footprint.
194503: A man coming home at night saw the white lady walking in the street. Convinced the apparition was his sister, the man called out: "Hey, Trui!" But the white lady walked past in silence.
194504: A farmer from Nerem had a mare that was about to foal. Because there were problems, the farmer went to fetch a man from Koninksem. Because the farmer was followed by a dog on the way, he said to the animal: "You may walk beside me, but if you dare touch me, I'll stab you to death with my knife!" When the man was almost in the village, the animal jumped at him anyway. The farmer then stabbed the werewolf in the place where he had been baptised. The next moment a naked man stood before him, who begged the farmer not to tell anyone.
194510: A witch turned a bowl of potatoes into live mice without tails.
194522: A woman came into a house in Zepperen and said: "At Fin's in Zepperen there are two doctors because she cannot give birth." Although Fin lived in Zepperen and the woman was in Sint-Truiden, she still knew what was going on. After all, she had bewitched the woman herself.
194523: A woman from Mal saw a werewolf through the window at night. It looked like a dog as big as a calf. The beast wore a chain around its neck and had clogs on its paws.
194524: A woman who still had to milk the cows at her work in Vechmaal sent her little daughter to the baker for two currant buns. As the woman walked home, she saw her daughter playing in the meadow with some neighbourhood children. The daughter had passed the witch's house. Although it was Saturday, the witch had infested the poor child with lice.
194528: Around midnight a castle in Gotem was haunted. A lot of noise was heard and the lights came on by themselves. People believed that the dead came to haunt it.
194534: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children. In the meadow along the road to Kozen will-o'-the-wisps were often seen.
194550: A poacher who heard a magpie laughing at him at night shot at the creature. The magpie fell out of the tree and broke its wing. When the man came home in the morning, he found that his wife had a broken arm.
194552: A deceased relative came to haunt a family in Waltwilder. For example, the cows were untied and the pitchforks thrown on the ground.
194553: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself. You go on ahead. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." On seeing a black dog, the girl did what her boyfriend had advised. When the boy came back a little later, the girl saw that he still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth. The boy was a werewolf.
194558: In the evening, farmer Mitchie set out a dung fork to bring in the hay from the field the next day. But the witch Belke had taken the dung fork and replaced it with a beet fork. Because the farmer could not work properly with the beet fork, he fell and broke his shoulder. The farmer said to Belke: "You did that to me again, didn't you?", to which the witch replied: "I'll do even more to you!" The next day Mitchie's horse died after jumping onto a gate bar. The priest gave the farmer this advice: "When the witch comes by again, you must not give or lend her anything anymore."
194568: A child had fallen seriously ill after being touched by an old witch. The priest had to be called to read prayers over the child.
194581: A werewolf who consorted with the devil was released after his band had been burnt.
194594: A man going to Maastricht with the Witte van Kesselt saw a coach with two grey horses approaching at the Pannepoel. In the coach sat four big fellows who gave the Witte a little book. The man could not get rid of that book. His wife had burned it many times, but it always came back. In the end the friars of Rijkholt released the man from the book. Every time the man came outside Maastricht, he saw that coach.
194597: On the Harlas two ladies dressed in white came to dance between midnight and one o'clock.
194601: A witch asked a farmer how the butter was going. The farmer replied: "We can't make butter unless you get a blow from this plate!" After that the farmer could churn butter.
194604: A person who had accepted something from a witch was in the witch's power.
194618: A baby whose pillow was full of roses lay crying all night.
194656: At night noise was heard in the attic of an empty house that stood in the fields.
194658: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to go somewhere for a moment. If a beast comes at you, throw my red handkerchief at its mouth." When the boy came back, the girl saw to her great dismay that he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
194674: When a man had called Kateau van de H. a witch, he suddenly got a terrible toothache. The man went to the dentist, but he could not help him. In the end the man went to ask Kateau for forgiveness. After that the toothache disappeared at once.
194675: Some men walking towards the canal in the evening suddenly heard a sound as if a horse with chains was going over the hedge. Because the dogs were frightened too, they ran between their master's legs.
194677: A woman from Glons went peddling in Herderen. With her basket the woman went into a house where there was a baby. The woman said to the baby: "Give me a nice little hand!" When the baby had given the woman its hand, it got a little chain from her. From then on, though, the baby behaved strangely; it was remarkably quiet and had a swollen little face. After the mother had taken away the chain, the baby became as lively as before.
194684: A woman came to a farm to buy piglets. When the woman went to the stable with the farmer's wife, the neighbour suddenly came running up. As soon as the woman had left, the neighbour asked: "What was she doing here?", to which the farmer's wife replied: "Buying piglets." The neighbour then cried out in fright: "But she's a witch!" From then on, not a single piglet could be kept alive on that farm.
194708: A big black man walked across the field with a boundary post on his neck, calling: "Where must I lay it, where must I lay it?" A passer-by answered: "Lay it where you took it from". With that the ghost was released.
194711: An inn in Waltwilder was haunted. Around midnight the ghost went to the cellar. Perhaps a treasure was found in that cellar, because nobody knew where else those people had got their wealth. The ghost was banished to the meadow behind the inn.
194722: A girl cried because a little sheep always came after her. At the bridge the little sheep disappeared. The girl's parents made the sign of the cross, but it did not help.
194728: Anyone who was jumped on by a werewolf could no longer get rid of the creature.
194734: A woman who saw a fine hare sitting among the cabbages went to fetch Jan H. to shoot the animal with a gun. Although Jan had hit the hare, there was nothing to be seen when he went to pick up the animal. The next day Jan heard that Mie V.D.H. was dying after someone had shot her. Fortunately the woman did not die of her wounds after all.
194737: A man said to a magpie sitting in a tree: "If you've come to tease me, you'll be in for something!" At that the magpie began to laugh. It was a witch.
194738: A boy who was returning from the fair with his girlfriend said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at the beast." When they got home, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
194741: A pregnant woman with two children had been widowed during the First World War. As the woman lay asleep with her children, she suddenly woke because one of the children had become restless. The woman opened her eyes and saw her husband's spirit standing in the room. She said: "Sooi, is that you? Leave me in peace. I am lying here with my children. There is no one who can help me. And I cannot wash myself. I will go on pilgrimage for you." The next moment the ghost had vanished.
194742: In a forest a black friar appeared who kept walking back and forth.
194744: At a farm in Horpmaal they were bringing in the harvest when a woman passed by and said: "Don't load the wagon too heavily. Otherwise you may get stuck somewhere and have to throw everything off the wagon again." When the farmhands tried to drive into the farmyard, a wheel of the wagon did indeed get stuck. The farmhands were about to start unloading the cart when the swineherd from Wellen came along. That man took a piece of wood and struck the back of the wagon hard with it. He struck so hard that a plank of the wagon broke. The next day the rumour went round that a witch was lying in bed with a broken arm.
194768: A man coming home from work at night was startled when someone suddenly threw earth at his head. But there was no one to be seen. By the side of the road a chest of money lay buried. After the treasure was found, the ghost no longer appeared.
194769: A man had moved the boundary post of his field in Neeroeteren. After his death the man had to haunt. The ghost held a boundary post in its arms and kept calling: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" When one day a passer-by answered: "Leave the boundary post standing where it stands!", the dead man was released and haunted no more.
194771: Treeske D. often visited a family with a small child. One day Treeske had put the child's mouth on the back of its body. The child's father was so angry that he built a large fire and threatened the witch with a dung fork until she had undone the harm.
194786: A woman whose house was full of fleas because of a witch was given this advice by a man: "Put six fleas in a little box and throw it away between midnight and one o'clock with the words: 'Go back where you came from'." When the woman had done this, there were no more fleas in her house.
194788: In the past a werewolf roamed near Overrepen. It was a man who threw an animal skin over himself at night. When the man went to work during the day, he hid his skin in the oven. When one day someone had lit the oven, the man came running in despair, saying: "My skin! My skin! Now I have lost my soul!" The skin had burnt up completely.
194795: Fien suspected that her child was bewitched. During a visit to her mother, Fien became very restless and suddenly said: "Mother, I'm going home, because something has happened to my child. When I get home, I'll empty his pockets." A red glove was found in the child's pocket.
194797: A young man went walking with his girlfriend. The young man, however, had to roam about as a werewolf at regular times, and so he said to the girl: "I have to relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth; then it can't harm you." A little later a big dog did indeed come running towards the girl. She threw her handkerchief at the beast, which tore the cloth to pieces. When the young man came back ten minutes later, the girl said: "You were gone such a long time!" The boy answered: "Oh, that doesn't mean anything!", but he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
194803: A man and a woman went on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel because after four years of marriage they still had no children. When the man and the woman passed a witch's house, they suddenly heard a little bell that followed them as far as a crossroads where someone had once dropped dead. The man and the woman later had eleven children.
194817: A woman whose husband had stayed elsewhere found three lice in his shirt. A while later the woman herself was also full of lice. On her neighbour's advice, the woman threw all the clothes in a tub and sprinkled salt in the water, for it was a witch who had caused the plague of lice. Shortly afterwards everyone was rid of the lice.
194822: A girl told her confessor that her dead mother came haunting every night. The priest then asked whether the girl had dressed her mother in a shroud. When the girl answered "no", the confessor said: "Then throw a shirt over her head as soon as you see her again." After the girl had done so, her mother stopped haunting.
194839: A woman going to church in the dark in the morning heard something as big as a horse approaching. When the woman looked round, the apparition had disappeared.
194841: Anyone who was touched by a witch had to hit the witch on top of her head at once.
194848: A man walking home at about half past nine saw a little light burning among the bushes. By looking at the light, the man lost his way. A little later the man saw a werewolf walking. When the man heard the church bells ringing in Biesen, he found his way again.
194853: A man coming back from visiting his girlfriend wandered around the fields all night. A witch had led him astray.
194869: A family in Lanaken always had misfortune in the stable. The goats, pigs and sheep all died. Next door to these people lived a woman and a mother who were suspected of being witches. When all the animals were dead, the people had misfortune in their house. Their three-year-old son got pneumonia. The mother was advised by a woman to go to the fathers of Godsdael in Val-Dieu. "Those fathers have more power than the brown friars," the woman said. The brown friar who had come to read prayers over the child had admitted this himself. The father of the mortally ill child set off by bicycle at five o'clock to the fathers. When he arrived at ten o'clock, the clergyman began to pray and said: "Do not weep, my friend. Your child will not die. The woman who made your child ill will have to undo the harm she has done." At that moment the sick boy, who had not been able to speak for a long time, called out: "Mother, I want a drink!" Right after that the woman suspected of the harm came in and said: "I must go and see the boy for a moment." The child's mother replied angrily: "You ugly good-for-nothing! You have no business there at all!", and she sent the woman outside. When the father returned from his visit to the fathers, he had each child wear a medal of Saint Benedict. He also placed a medal under the threshold bar and covered it with some earth. From then on the witch never came in again.
194871: A man returning from Hees in the evening met a black lady in a rustling silk dress at the little wooden cross by the 'Heilige haag'.
194878: The B. family had always done well, until a witch made the animals die. The witch had even driven a flock of sheep mad.
194902: A treasure lay hidden in Suske's meadow. Every time treasure hunters tried to bring the chest up, however, it fell back into the hole they had dug.
194909: A boy who went walking with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "Go on ahead, I have to relieve myself behind the hedge. If a beast comes at you in the meantime, throw my handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been advised. When the boy came back, he had the threads of the red handkerchief between his teeth.
194923: It was said that a witch lived on the hill in Ophoven. One day a merchant from Kessenich was given a beating near the hill by an invisible figure.
194937: A woman could make mice and then make them disappear again.
194938: In Batsheers lived a farmhand who was cutting straw with a machine. Suddenly a dog jumped onto the machine, which then kept working by itself. The farmhand was also seen lying on his back in the grass with the dog beside him, while the horses ploughed the field by themselves.
194942: Opposite the Bungalow in the meadow is a pit called the Grondeleer. Once a man with a horse and cart fell into that pit. The horse managed to save itself, but the man drowned. Several people who went to the pit on Christmas night never came back.
194944: A bell once sank into the 'putvenneke' in Achel. Soldiers had pushed the Our Lady bell into the ground. On Christmas night at twelve o'clock that bell could still be heard ringing underground.
194954: A man sometimes went to the café of a witch's daughter. One evening the man had seen through the stable window how the daughter lay rooting about in the straw like one possessed. When that daughter had her fits, she sometimes did not go outside for three or four days.
194963: At midnight the bells could be heard ringing on Kneip, although no one was there.
194964: A carpenter who had a job to do for a farmer stayed there for eight days until the work was finished. In the evenings the carpenter always went visiting people in the village. When the man came back to the farm one evening, all the doors were already locked. So he went to lie on the hay in the barn. A little later the carpenter heard a strange sound. He reached towards where the sound came from and felt the fur of a cat. The carpenter threw the unusually heavy cat into the gap between the haystacks. When the carpenter went to breakfast in the morning, the farmer told him that the farmer's wife was in bed. She had been in the stable during the night and had badly hurt her head. Then the carpenter said: "You'd better find someone else, because I'm leaving today."
194966: A farmer who could not make butter went to the friars of Sint-Truiden. The friars advised the farmer to let no one in anymore and to place a relic under the stable door.
194967: Neliske had a farmhand who cursed all the time. One night the farmhand woke up and screamed that the devil was standing by his bed.
194985: At the home of the parents of a man from the Bosstraat, a werewolf's band was burnt.
194990: A woman who was plagued by the maar (nightmare spirit) almost every night put a knife beside her bed to stab the maar to death. The next night the woman saw a cat come into the room and, a little later, jump out of the window. The woman, however, could not move.
195003: In Stokkem lived a woman who was said to be a witch. One day the woman had washed someone's child and put clean clothes on it. The next day the child was ill. Three weeks later the child died. The poor woman got the blame.
195013: In the old days a werewolf roamed Jesseren. It was a man from another village who could change himself into a dog. One evening a late walker was attacked by the werewolf. After a fight the man managed to make the werewolf bleed. At that moment the werewolf changed into a human.
195016: Some people from Lauw went on a pilgrimage with the priest to Scherpenheuvel or to Banneux. But after a quarter of an hour the bus already had a flat tyre, so everyone had to get out. The woman who always got on and off last was suspected of being a witch. As soon as everyone had got off the bus, the priest made the sign of the cross. When everyone got back on, the priest went in last. After that nothing strange happened anymore.
195021: Old women were often suspected of being witches. When a witch had touched a child, she could make the child ill. The witch who lived in Uikhoven had even caused a child to die. The witch always tried to get near children. At the place where the witch had worked, three children had already died.
195031: A poacher had shot a hare dead. When the man went to pick up the hare, the animal had vanished.
195049: Every year in autumn the count of Bovelingen came to haunt the area around the castle. When there was a thunderstorm, the windows and doors of the castle flew open. The count, with fiery eyes, would then drive around in a burning coach with black horses. Each time the count disappeared into a pit in the woods. The count's soul could find no rest because during his life he had unlawfully acquired much property. Many friars had already tried to banish the ghost, but they had failed because the clergymen themselves were not without sin. In Batsheers, however, there lived a holy priest who had never committed a sin. When autumn came, the priest went to pray by the pit into which the ghost always disappeared. When the count came driving up in his coach, he asked: "Well, what are you doing here?", to which the priest replied: "I have come to banish you in the name of God." The ghost then said: "Yes, but that won't work. You once cut a cabbage in someone's garden." The priest answered: "That is true, but I left half a franc in its place." After that the count never came to haunt again.
195058: A woman who had twelve cats threw a red handkerchief at a dog that came in. The next day she saw a man who still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
195059: Two brothers went from Kotem to the Boorseveld to mow. After the midday nap, Koeb said to his brother: "You stay lying down a bit longer. I'll set off now, because I can't walk as fast as you." On the way Koeb met a woman who had a basket with her and held a rooster in her lap. "Going mowing, Koeb?" the woman asked. "Here are a few apples for you." At that moment Wullem came running up. He shouted to his brother: "Watch out, you mustn't eat those apples!" The woman then said: "That crazy Wullem!" and went on her way. The witch knew that Wullem knew something about her mischief.
195067: A farmer's horse had died because of a witch.
195068: The brother of Mathilde V. had seen a kitten whose legs kept getting longer.
195076: Because all of Jan van E.'s animals were dying, the farmer went with his wife to a priest in Tongeren. But the priest said: "You should bring your daughter along." The next time Jan van E. went to Tongeren with his daughter. After the priest had read prayers over the daughter, the farmer's animals stayed healthy. From then on everyone believed that the farmer's daughter was a witch.
195077: There used to be as many as twenty black cats in the 'Wijngaardbos', living in rabbit burrows. Recently Hubert H. saw two of those witch animals.
195116: A man coming back from the butter market saw a cat sitting there and said: "Puss, what are you doing here so late?" The cat replied: "Had you not spoken, I would have broken your neck!" Terrified, the man went on. He resolved to hit the cat if it turned up again. When, a little further on, the man saw ten cats, he said: "What are you going to do?", to which the cats answered: "We are going to rob the wine cellars in Cologne". The cats climbed onto a broom and flew away.
195117: A farmer was making butter while a woman from the neighbourhood stood beside him. But the butter turned out to be of poor quality. When the same thing had happened several times, the farmer went to the parish priest for advice. The priest advised the farmer not to let the woman in any more. But suddenly the woman was standing beside the farmer again, although not a single door had opened. The next time the farmer kept holy water by him when he made butter. From then on the butter was of good quality again.
195121: A man from Vliermaalroot had been given a card that he could not get rid of. The man had already tried to burn the card, but the next day it was back in his pocket. After a priest had read prayers over the man, he was finally freed of the card.
195134: In Borgloon there lived a girl who could make mice out of a lump of earth. After a friar had read prayers over the girl, the devil was driven out.
195140: A farmer who had to take his bull to Calix got lost through the work of a witch who lived in Gerhees.
195156: A mother was worried because her little son always went to eat and play at the home of a certain Agatha. The woman never did the boy any harm. Yet in the past children had died who had gone to eat porridge at Agatha's.
195158: A father who had discovered at a tree stump that his son became a werewolf in the evening sent the boy to the heath for a few hours. Meanwhile the father lit the oven and threw his son's collar into the fire. The next moment the boy was standing beside the oven to save his collar. When everything had burnt up, the boy was released.
195161: Anyone who wanted to sell his soul to the devil had to stand at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen.
195164: A boy on his way to the fair met an old woman in the woods who had a basket of rosaries with her. After the boy had thrown the basket on the ground, the woman said: "You'll regret that!" When the boy lay in bed, he began to cry because he kept hearing chains rattling. The priest could not drive away the devil. A priest from another village, who was stronger, drove the devil away. But the boy died all the same.
195169: Louis W. saw a coach come out of the castle cellars and drive towards Wasseven. That night Louis was so frightened that he could not find his way home.
195180: In Thiewinkel a mare was about to foal. Because a woman stood watching in the doorway, the mare could not deliver her foal. After the woman had been sent away, the foal was born.
195212: A black witch cat always appeared on the path in front of the door. If you stroked the cat, she did no harm.
195215: On a farm, strange things happened to the horse. The animal was always drenched in sweat and every morning its mane was braided. Something was also wrong with the farmer's little daughter. A bumblebee had flown up to her and said: "Little one, are you still ill?" The child died shortly afterwards. In the end the farmer and his wife sought advice from the friars, who gave them a medal. A few days later, strangely enough, the medal lay in front of the door of the horse stable. The cows were not spared either; in the mornings they were tied not by the horns but by the neck.
195218: Farmer Felix T. never had problems making butter. One day, however, it simply would not work; no matter how long he tried, the milk kept foaming. His wife went to the fathers of Hasselt and told them what was wrong with the milk. The fathers said: "Let your husband put his hand into the cream up to his wrist; then he has the witch by the throat, and she will leave you alone." Because the man did not believe in witches, at first he would not try it. When he was at his wits' end, his wife did manage to persuade him to put his hand in the cream. After that they had no trouble at all making butter from the milk.
195220: A man coming home from work met a black dog that blocked his way, growling. When the man began to pray, the dog went away. The man suspected the dog was a witch from the neighbourhood.
195221: At T.'s there worked a farmhand who could turn himself into a werewolf. One evening the farmhand jumped on his master's neck. The farmer, however, was not afraid and beat the werewolf with an iron bar until it bled. When the werewolf took on his human form, the farmer said: "There, now you've surely learned your lesson!"
195230: When Ber C. was coming back from the wool factory, he was jumped on by a werewolf at the Planken Brug. The werewolf grew heavier and heavier, so that in the end the man could no longer bear the weight. When the man jumped over a furrow of 20 to 30 centimetres, the werewolf fell off him.
195233: A woman who was ridden by the mare went to the friars for advice and said: "I saw two little cats rolling on the floor at the foot of my bed." One of the friars replied: "You must not believe in that. We will read prayers over you, but you must not believe in that." After the friars had read prayers over the woman, she was no longer troubled by the mare.
195234: On the Royerheide a bell could be heard ringing underground at night. A man who had said, 'I'll get that ghost out of there', found a chest of money. When he had almost pulled the chest out of the pit, a voice rang out: "You have them on the rope, but not yet on the bank!" The next moment the rope broke and the chest fell back down.
195236: A farmer did not dare to buy new animals because he feared his stable was bewitched. After all, all the animals in the stable had died. After the priest had come to read prayers over the stable, things went better for a while. When the problems started again some time later, the farmer moved away.
195239: A miller from Veerle found it strange that a hand could always be seen between the mill sails when he stopped the mill in the evening. One evening the man struck at the hand with a knife. When the miller went inside, he saw that his own wife was missing a hand.
195248: A farmer and his wife went to the fathers in Maastricht because their maid was ill and no doctor could help. The maid had 'het fieflèèn'. Strangely, there was always a cat in her bedroom. The priest advised the maid to go to the chapel for nine consecutive days and pray in penance. The maid did her very best, but only managed to reach the chapel on the ninth day. After that her health improved visibly. The cat had disappeared from the bedroom.
195273: Gjotterke, who was born in Hoelbeek and had moved to Waltwilder, could make mice.
195274: A man coming home at night had to fight a werewolf. When the werewolf began to bleed, he changed into a human. The werewolf turned out to be a friend of the man.
195279: Will-o'-the-wisps floated about in places where animals or unbelievers were buried.
195282:
Two people from Membruggen went to a clergyman because they were always being harassed by werewolves. The clergyman said: "The werewolves are your neighbours. If you look under the bundles of brushwood in the meadow, you will find their clothes and their animal skins there. When you meet a werewolf, you must throw a handkerchief at its mouth." When the people met the werewolves again, they did what the clergyman had advised. The next day their neighbours still had the threads of the handkerchief between their teeth.
If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could recognise him.
195284: A werewolf was an ugly beast that jumped on people's necks. Others claimed the werewolf was a person who wanted to frighten others. The werewolf always sat in the little lane leading to the church of Lanaken.
195296: When a man who lived on the Molenveld came back from the fair, he suddenly got a terrible pain in his knee. Since neither the priest nor the doctor knew what to do, someone went to the mannetje van Genk (the little man of Genk, a folk healer) on the man's behalf. The little man went to see the patient and sent everyone out of the room. A little later the man lay sleeping peacefully. The man's pain had been caused by a darning needle stuck in his knee. When the man was coming back from the fair, he had met a man without a head. That was the witch who had conjured the darning needle into his knee. The little man said that the priest did have the power to solve the problem, but that he perhaps had not wanted to.
195301: The Duivelskruis in Vrijhern was haunted. At that crossroads stood a stone where people were hanged. It was said that witches came there too.
195311: Two women always went on pilgrimage to Stokrooie to be rid of a ghost. After the women had fetched a branch from the forest on Christmas night, a dog came to lie in the arm of one of the women in bed. A friar from Hasselt exorcised the ghost and banished it to the other side of the sea. After that the women saw no more ghosts.
195320: Two girls brought a spinning wheel to the grave of their dead sister. But the skirt of one of the sisters got caught in the wheel. The dead girl must have done it. Shortly afterwards the girl died of fright.
195325: A family had been on a pilgrimage with a bewitched child. When the people came home, they found that their whole house had been turned upside down.
195326: A man from Veldwezelt had pulled the boundary post of his field out of the ground. After his death the man came back to haunt with a boundary post in his hands. The ghost kept asking: "Where must I lay it? Where must I lay it?" When one day a drunkard answered: "Lay it where you took it from!", the ghost was released.
195344: A beggar woman from Vroenhoven always visited newborn babies. One day the parents found a newspaper under their baby's pillow. The parents then quickly went on a pilgrimage, for otherwise the child would surely have died.
195346: A man walking from Loon to Gotem in the evening met a witch on the way. The man decided to go on together with the witch. But after walking for two hours the man was still not in Gotem. Suddenly the witch had vanished. Only towards morning did the man find the way back to his house.
195347: When some women saw a vuurkat (fire cat), Maria said: "Something is going to happen." That same week the mother of one of the women died.
195362: A man returning from Piringen at night saw a black cat on the Colmontberg. Because the cat got under his feet, he kicked the animal. The cat miaowed but kept following the man. When the man met other people, the cat had suddenly disappeared.
195364: Because all his horses were dying, farmer George sent for a friar. After the friar had prayed for a whole day, he had the mangers torn down. In this way it was discovered that the mangers were full of pins.
195365: Near Landwijk castle a dead man came haunting with a boundary post in his hands. During his life that man had moved the boundary post of his field. When someone took the boundary post from the ghost, the dead man was released.
195379: In a house where two women had been visiting, the tobacco suddenly turned out to have disappeared. One of the women was accused of the theft. That woman was old and always unwashed. People believed she was a witch. The other woman was asked not to visit anymore, so that the witch would stay away too. They wanted to burn the witch's clothes because the witch was crawling with lice.
195383: When Door met Bet one Saturday evening, the woman said: "Door, you're out late! Mind you don't get lost!" The man walked about all night because he could no longer find his bearings. Only when the cock crowed in the morning did Door know where he was. Bet was standing beside her house and called: "Door, you're up early!" Door did not answer. He was ill for eight days.
195386: A quarrelsome man from Trekschuren went to a café to settle a dispute. When the man had smashed everything to pieces, he said: "I'll fight anyone, even if I have to fight the devil!" On the way back, at a turnstile, the man was jumped on by something strange that let itself be carried until the man was home. When he got home the man saw that his coat had been scratched to shreds by the devil's nails.
195387: When a woman had been in the cowshed, the cows often became swollen. Only the witch could undo it.
195388: Witches caused a great deal of trouble. When a child was to be born somewhere, people had to make sure a blessed object hung in the house. Otherwise no one would manage to fetch the midwife when the time came.
195404: A man could make mice out of a handful of earth. After the priest had read prayers over the man, he could no longer make mice.
195405: Mie, a girl from Diepenbeek, could make mice out of a handful of earth. After the priest had read prayers over the girl, she could no longer make mice. In Herk there also lived a man who could make mice.
195422: On a farm all the piglets died after a witch had come to look in the sty. Nor could butter be made any more until the witch was forbidden to enter the shed again.
195446: Three men who wanted to play cards kept moaning: "If only we had a fourth man! Even if we have to play with the devil!"
