The next moment a man appeared who went on playing cards with the three until the next morning. The three men lost time after time. When one of them bent down to pick up a fallen card, he saw to his great dismay that the fourth man had cow's legs: it was the devil.
195449: A woman walking home with her little son suddenly could not go on because a cat kept running between her legs. When she got home, she saw four or five cats sitting on the cupboard. Her husband lit a paraffin lamp and chased the cats out with a broom. A little later he came back in and, to his great surprise, saw six or seven cats sitting on the windowsill. After he had chased those away too, no fewer than twenty-five cats sat on the wall. When an ugly old woman walked down the street that evening, the children sang: "The old woman of the pipe, she had a little tail with copper wire, how it stood!" At that the witch ran furiously to the woman's house, wailing: "They're calling me a witch! They're calling me a witch!" The woman took a broomstick and said threateningly: "Will you get out now!"
195467: One day a farmer drove with horse and cart past the house of the witch Mie. At the spot where Mie had drawn a little cross on the ground, the horse stood still. Only when Mie wished it could the horse go on.
195494: A man had caught a rabbit and put it in the pocket of his coat. When the man got home, he found a block of marl in his coat.
195499: In a house in the Lindesteeg in Gelinden a strange knocking was always heard. Between midnight and one o'clock music was heard there. One night the ghost suffocated a little child. When the oven was broken open, a heap of money was found there. After that, pastor M. from Zonhoven came to exorcise the house.
195509: On a cold winter's day Jef H. saw a cat sitting there. Jef said to the animal: "Come and warm yourself at my house. The stove is burning nicely there." When Jef was home, he heard the kitten scratching at the door and saying: "I've come to warm myself". The frightened man let the kitten in. After the animal had sat by the stove for a while, it went outside again.
195511: In a café there were some men who wanted to play cards. Because they were one player short, Freke said: "I'll make sure someone else comes in. But one of you must open the door." A little later there was a knock and a fine gentleman came in who wanted to play cards. When the landlady picked up a fallen card, she saw that the gentleman had goat's legs.
195523: One evening by a brook a man met a little old woman. She asked him in Walloon the way to Kortijs and to a village that lay in completely the other direction. When the old woman wanted to pick up her bag, she bent down with such difficulty that the man offered: "I'll help you if it's too heavy." "That's not necessary," said the woman. The next moment the woman had vanished without a trace.
195527: A boy saw a cat walking opposite the house of a witch. When he wanted to follow the animal, his mother said: "No, don't go after it, because that's a witch!"
195530:
When fruit trader Zjang D. was coming back from the market in Sint-Truiden at night, a heavy thunderstorm suddenly broke. The man took shelter behind a house. When the storm had passed a quarter of an hour later, the man wanted to go on. But he could not, for he could not move a foot. From one until three in the morning it was as if the man was nailed to the ground. After that he could go on again.
Through the ringing of the Angelus, all those ghosts have disappeared.
195544: A man rode on horseback to Genk in the evening to deliver some goods. When he reached the Kneip, his horse suddenly refused to go on. A little later many cats came out of the forest, stood in front of the horse and began to miaow. The man no longer dared to go on and began to pray the Gospel of St John. He firmly resolved to travel together with his wife next time.
195547: One evening some men were sitting outside talking at the sawyer's in Neeroeteren. Suddenly the wild hunt was heard flying through the air with wondrously beautiful music. Hem de W. called out: "Hey, wait, I'm coming with you!", to which a voice replied: "Whoever wants to hunt with us must also gnaw with us!" The man was buried under a heap of gnawed bones.
195568: A farmhand got help from the devil with his work. When the farmhand had to manure the field, for example, the devil would say: "If you give me a packet of tobacco, the field will be manured tomorrow."
195574: Near the presbytery stood a tree that was always full of will-o'-the-wisps. People believed they were the souls of unbaptised children, but they might also simply have been butterflies.
195575: A woman always heard strange knocking in the house at night. One night the woman saw the spirit of her mother come in. Later that woman's daughter said jokingly to her children: "Make sure you pray well for me, or else I'll come back to haunt you!"
195584: In Beverlo a woman had burned her backside when she fell into a griespot (1). That same evening a witch from Stal was able to tell what had happened in Beverlo.
195590: A man walking one evening from the Vrietselmolen (?) to Dilsen came across a small cat. The man took out his knife and cut the animal in the leg. The next moment the man saw a woman standing before him with a wound on her arm. The woman begged the man never to betray her.
195595: A four-year-old girl had got a hunchback through the doing of the witch Stien. The girl did not remember how the hump disappeared again a while later.
195614: In Voort stood a house that was haunted. In the evening a terrible noise was heard in the house.
195619: A man who had been bewitched by a certain Anneke was ill for a long time.
195625: On the mutsaard (heath where brushwood was cut) an old woman always appeared who asked people to go on pilgrimage for her. Those people had in fact forgotten their promise. After someone had gone on pilgrimage for the old woman, the dead woman no longer appeared.
195635: After a witch had rooted about in a molehill, mice crawled out of it.
195641: Every night a white lady went to the hermitage in Oetsloave and to the one in Vrijhein. When the lady walked through the Oude Berg, she said: "Make way for me! Make way for me!", and the hedges opened for her.
195645: A man who one Sunday had refused to go to the fair with a woman met a cat in the evening that kept getting under his feet the whole time. One day the man went poaching in the woods. When he saw a hare running, his gun did not work. The next time the man took his brother along poaching. But his brother's brand-new gun did not work either. On a friend's advice the man put a piece of a silver half-franc coin into his gun. This time the man did manage to hit the hare. Although the animal limped awkwardly away on three legs, the man could not catch the hare. In the woods the man found the woman who had asked him to go to the fair. The woman had a gunshot wound and said: "You mustn't tell anyone about this!" From then on the man was no longer bothered.
195660: Witte Nol's mother was startled when a pack of mewing cats suddenly came in. Although it was summer, one of the cats said: "I fell through the ice". Then Witte Nol's mother said: "Jesus, Mary, Joseph!" The next moment all the cats had disappeared.
195671: A man went with his horse from Overpelt to Sint-Huibrechts-Lille to fetch a cartload of sand. When the horse suddenly stood still on the way, the man unloaded the cart in vain. The witch Trien, who lived in a house nearby, came outside and asked: "Won't he pull?" Then Trien came closer and made a movement as if she were turning the wheel. The next moment the horse could go on without any trouble.
195680: In Congo (Genk) there lived a witch whom everyone feared. One day a black cat came into a neighbour woman's house. Because the woman was annoyed by the animal, she threw fire on the cat's head. The next day the witch from Congo had burns on her face.
195689: Some men had made a bet. One of the men had to spend a night in an empty castle. When the man began baking pancakes in the castle, bones suddenly fell out of the chimney. The man threw all the bones into a corner and went on baking. A little later a complete skeleton stood in the corner and beckoned the man to follow. The man followed the ghost through all kinds of secret passages. In the cellar the ghost lifted a large stone, under which lay three bags of money. One bag was for the poor, one for the church and one for the man. After the money had been divided, the ghost could finally find rest.
195695: When Neel T. was walking home drunk one evening, he accidentally stepped on the tail of a cat sitting by the road. The cat said: "If you weren't such a drunken sod, I'd kill you on the spot". At that moment Neel was instantly sober.
195701: After his death a poor market trader came back to haunt the barn where he had hanged himself.
195707: A farmer usually went for a drink at Nel J.'s in the evening when he had finished his work. One day, however, the man wanted to go straight home. When he passed Nel's house, his horse would go no further. Nel came out and said: "Oh, just come in for a moment. Then the horse will want to go on." After the man had had a drink, his horse was willing to go on.
195710: A man who had secretly gone to cut down pine trees in a wood suddenly heard a horse wheezing. But there was nothing to be seen.
195715: In Herk stood a haunted castle called the Geuzentoren. In the barn of that castle all the animals and people died.
195722: Anyone who saw a cat in the evening did not dare to strike at it.
195724: Niel was once known as a bewitched place. Often the wind would suddenly start blowing there, or doors would fly open for no reason.
195727: In the fen behind the church of Budel lay a sunken bell that could be heard ringing twelve times on Christmas night.
195743: If one had seen a black cat or a magpie, something bad would happen.
195748: A woman stroked a child's hair, saying: "What lovely hair you have!" The next moment the child was full of lice.
195750: A man coming back from Beverst by moonlight had to pass the house of a friend who had died a while before. By the house stood a man wrapped in a white sheet. Because the apparition looked exactly like his dead friend, the man, frightened to death, hurried home.
195752: The castle of Hoepertingen used to be haunted. At night the horses could be heard snorting in the stables and it seemed as if skulls were being thrown about in the attic. In the morning the cows in the byre were found with their tails tied to the manger. One day the maid's clogs were found in a jug with a neck as narrow as a bottle's. After a while the Friars Minor of Sint-Truiden exorcised the castle. After that it was no longer haunted.
195758: A young man from Geetbets had gone to visit his girlfriend in Hulst. Because the young man still wanted to go home late in the evening, he was given a horse. On the way the young man said to the animal: "My, little horse, you do run fast!" The next moment the horse was gone and the man was lying on the ground. Perhaps it was a horse used by witches, and that was why it ran so fast.
195763: A midwife who had to go somewhere was accompanied by a man who, unknown to her, was a werewolf. The midwife had to carry the werewolf the whole way. Since then no midwife has let herself be accompanied by a man.
195767: The woman who lived in Albert J.'s farmhouse had heard chains rattling on two evenings in a row. On the third evening two men came with a dung fork to keep watch. When the rattling was heard again, the men quickly opened the door. A ghost with large fiery eyes came out. The spirit went along the Dorpstraat and the Bekemstraat to the Mistemke. The men were so frightened that they could not catch the ghost.
195773: The old lord of the castle came to haunt after his death. He would lie with his arms crossed on the hedge along the castle avenue.
195794: The horses always stopped at the house of Heksebetje. Only when the witch came out and pushed against the wagon could people go on.
195805: A Jew lived in the Rechtestraat in Stokkem. He always went to a man from the village to buy cattle. When there was a mission in the village, the man said to the Jew: "I really don't understand why you never go to church". The Jew always went to the little Jewish temple in Beegd. The man offered to teach the Jew something from the catechism, so that he could go to church. When the Jew and his wife had been taking lessons from the man for eight days, they woke up frightened one night. The room was full of ugly black devils who did not want the Jew and his wife to convert.
195806: In a house in Vlijtingen a ghost appeared every night to count its money. One night a man followed the ghost, saying: "You must go first!" The man carried a blessed and an unblessed candle in his hands. When the ghost had led the man to a pot of money, it said: "Now I am delivered". The unblessed candle had gone out, but the blessed one could not be put out in any way.
195811: Some men had to catch moles at the house of Griet, the mother of Pee D. Frans D.W. said: "Where there are moles, people will soon die." When Griet came home that evening, she saw a good seven or eight moles, for the men had not been able to catch a single one.
195812: In the meadows will-o'-the-wisps were often seen flickering. People believed they were the spirits of people who had died long ago.
195816: A woman came back after her death in the shape of a spirit. The spirit arranged all the furniture in the house as in a chapel. The woman had once promised to build a chapel, but she had never kept that promise. After her descendants had a chapel built, the woman was released.
195830: A man from Stokkem was married to a girl from the Molenveld. People believed that the man's mother, who lived with her son, was a witch. The man indeed had nothing but bad luck. His horse, cows and pigs all died. A while later even his wife died.
195832: A witch lived in Gors-Opleeuw. The children bewitched by that woman fell ill and died.
195855: The little castle near Alken station was haunted. Every time a pane had been put into the window, the pane lay on the ground the next day.
195859:
There were certain ways to recognise witches. When the priest turned round in church with the words "Orates frates", it became clear who the witches were.
If one placed one's right foot crosswise on a woman's path and the woman then looked round, she was a witch.
195868: When there was a newborn baby, no strange women were to be let in. Witches seemed to sense where a child had been born.
195869: One day Koon said: "When Betje, my own wife, puts her hand on my shoulder, I feel listless for the rest of the day."
195878: A woman who saw two hares sitting among the cabbages at midnight warned her son. The boy put powder and blessed salt in the gun and stuck a sprig of blessed palm on the barrel. When the boy had hit the two hares, two women appeared who ran away screaming.
195881: A drunk man cycling past the Zwarte Lieve Heer in Waltwilder at nightfall saw a woman dressed in white sitting in a tree by the road. The man was so frightened that he arrived home drenched in sweat and stone-cold sober.
195883: An elderly woman often stroked the children's hair, saying: "You have lovely hair!" When those children came home, their hair was full of lice. The woman also often gave the children sweets. People warned their children about that witch. One day a boy, against his better judgement, walked in the witch's footsteps. At the fifth step the witch turned around, and the boy ran away terrified.
195888: A twenty-year-old girl had given herself over to the devil by reading a book. When the girl lay in bed, she often began to cry out: "There they are again!" The others could see nothing, but they did hear strange noises. The girl suffered so terribly from these torments that people even came all the way from Sint-Truiden to see her. Neither the priest nor the holy friars could help her. In the end the girl had to be taken to the Witzusters (White Sisters) of Sint-Truiden, where she was smothered between two mattresses. There was no other solution. A few years later the house where the girl had lived burned down.
195892: Werewolves had a collar that they usually kept in a tree stump. Werewolves often jumped on someone's back. When a werewolf's collar was burned, the man was released.
195902: At the Wienerhof farm in Ophoven worked a farmhand called Zeverkubbe because he used to peddle colanders ('zeven'). Zeverkubbe was allowed to go to the fair in Opitter on condition that he first manured the field. Zeverkubbe went to the field, set his dung fork by a small heap of manure and said: "A dung fork at every dung heap, and then do as I do." As soon as the farmhand had spread one heap, the whole field was manured. The farmer, who was spying on the farmhand, could hardly believe what he saw. The farmer and his wife told the friars about the strange goings-on with the farmhand. One morning, when the farmer and his wife went to mass, they saw the road blocked by a blown-down oak. After mass, strangely enough, the oak stood upright again. Zeverkubbe had set the tree upright. The farmer sent his farmhand to Maastricht with a cart of potatoes so that meanwhile he could burn the werewolf's collar. The moment the band caught fire, the farmhand was already at the oven to save his belonging. Fortunately the farmer was able to hold him back. As soon as the collar had burned up completely, the farmhand was released. Nevertheless the farmhand quit and went back to peddling colanders.
195922: A farmhand went to listen to the witches' music in the meadow. When one of the witches handed him a cup, he took it, saying: "God bless you." The next moment all the witches had vanished. Since the farmhand was left alone in the meadow, he decided to take the cup home. His master advised him to sell it for a lot of money. The next day someone came asking for the cup. The farmhand got a lot of money for it, because the witches needed the cup; otherwise they could no longer be witches.
195926: People who had bad luck with their animals had the shed exorcised by someone from Leuven. The clergyman said: "Someone will come with a little basket. That woman will come to ask you for something." And so it happened. The visitor was the witch responsible for all the misfortune.
195947: The children were all afraid of the blue goat.
195949: A man who saw a cat sitting on a turnstile said to the animal: "Is that Lébeses's kitten?", to which the cat replied: "That's none of your business!" The man was so badly frightened that he made a long detour.
195950: A man who met a werewolf began to sweat with fear. When the man took out a red handkerchief to wipe off his sweat, the werewolf seized the handkerchief and tore it to pieces. Some time later people knew who the werewolf was; the man had been recognised because he still had the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
195951: A girl who went to herd the cows had to pass the house of a witch. At that spot one of the cows suddenly fell down. Nele began to cry, whereupon the witch came out laughing and said: "Never mind, girl, that cow will be well again in a moment!" When the witch went back inside, the cow did indeed get up again.
195953: A werewolf in the shape of a dog had chased a man.
195967: People placed holy objects and holy water under the threshold so that witches could not enter. When a witch nevertheless once got into a house, the woman living there cried: "Keep your paws off everything!" But the witch had secretly dropped something into the cooking pot hanging over the fire. The contents of the pot were given to the cow. A few days later the cow was dead.
195972: A woman who came peddling speculaas (spiced biscuits) was rudely sent away by a miller with the words: "I don't need your biscuits!" The woman replied: "Well, then you'll get your speculaas tonight!" That evening the miller fell out of his mill.
195989: On a farm there was always noise, and a black dog was often seen roaming about. One day the man managed to lock the dog in the pigsty. With a pocketknife the man stabbed a hole in the animal's head. A few days later people said that a man from Hees was wearing a bandage around his head.
195991: One evening a man passed a place that was haunted. The leaves and branches of the trees blew back and forth, and the dog was so frightened that it crept between the man's legs.
195994: In Stamprooi lived two sisters who were exceptionally miserly. When one of the sisters had been dead for some time, a tremendous thunderstorm broke out. The dead woman appeared to her sister and said: "I am in hell because I was so loveless in life. For you it is not too late, but you must act quickly, because you do not have much time left." The sister, frightened to death, then gave all her possessions to charities. Half a year later she died too.
196012: In Hendrieken lived a fifteen-year-old girl who was bewitched and as a result could no longer even get out of bed. Because the people of the neighbourhood knew that the girl's own mother was responsible for the misfortune, they sent for the priest of Offelken. The people rode with the priest in a horse-drawn carriage to the girl's house. But as soon as the horses entered the territory of Hendrieken, they would not move another step. The priest then went on on foot. After the priest had exorcised the girl, she got out of bed completely cured. Her mother then lay down in the bed herself and never got up from it alive again. In the pillow on which the girl had lain all that time, a rose was found.
196037: The skimmer at the dairy in Rutten was broken. When the smith had gone with a friend to fetch the skimmer, he met Ann on the way. The smith said to his friend: "Look, there's Ann! They say she can do anything!" "I don't believe a word of it," said the man, "if she can do anything, let her make the skimmer fall through the basket." When the smith was almost home, the witch laughed loudly. The skimmer had fallen to the ground.
196038: A man from Bocholt who lived with the Paggers family often went poaching in the evening. One night the woods were full of hares. Yet the poacher could not manage to shoot a single one. When he finally did hit a hare, a voice rang out: "Janneke, where are you?", to which the shot hare answered: "In the bag." The next moment all the hares had vanished.
196039: Neerke V.T. from Overpelt lived by a haunted crossroads. When one day Neerke saw a large ghost dog walking by the ditch, he said: "God, you ugly beast, what is that?" At that moment the dog disappeared.
196055: In the old days the churchyard was haunted. Once a man got such a fright there that he ran off in great haste and left his clogs behind.
196060: Between Heibricht and Neerharen, people often had to carry the werewolf.
196071: People who saw a will-o'-the-wisp in the churchyard believed it was a soul flying away.
196105: A boy was in a relationship with a girl who was said to be a witch. Because the boy wanted to know the truth, he went and sat in the stable. A little later a grey kitten was walking around in the stable. When the boy saw his girlfriend later that day, the girl said: "We did have a lot of fun in the stable!" At that moment the boy knew he was in a relationship with a witch.
196130: Above the meadow in Rijkhoven the witches flew through the air on a broomstick.
196131: In Neerrepen a ghost roamed about that people had often tried to catch. It turned out to be the donkey belonging to the count's children.
196136: If you could make a werewolf bleed, he took on his human form and you could recognise him.
196153: In 1964 a group of people went on pilgrimage by bus. Five hundred metres outside the village they found that the bus had a flat tyre. Everyone got out except one woman. After the tyre was repaired, the bus could go on. A little later, however, the bus had another flat tyre. This time too the same woman did not get out. When the bus had a flat tyre for the third time, people said: "That woman who always stays in the bus is a witch. She doesn't want us to go on pilgrimage". The priest forced the witch to get out and read a prayer beginning with the words: "Virita Jezus, virita Jezus, ...". After that the bus had no more flat tyres.
196159: On a farm the milk was bewitched. When the cream was poured off, the milk became like leather.
196160: A man from Bernissem-Broek was walking home through a meadow in the evening. At a turnstile he saw a man from his wife's family sitting there, who had not long been dead. The man told his story to the priest, who said: "You must not run away from that dead man; you must ask what he wants." When the man saw the dead man again, he asked: "What do you desire?" The ghost answered: "When I was ill, my family promised that three of them would go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. As long as they have not gone, I can find no rest." The next day three relatives of the dead man made a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. The man who had seen the ghost was with them too. The whole way to Scherpenheuvel he saw the dead man walking ahead of him. The others saw nothing. When the ghost went around the altar in the church of Scherpenheuvel, the man asked: "Is it all right now?", to which the ghost answered yes. The other relatives, who did not see the ghost, asked for a sign. Then the dead man threw down a white silk cloth with his fingers burned into it. From this his relatives concluded that he must be in purgatory.
196178: The mare had something to do with a dream.
196182: A farmer from 't Roeren constantly had bad luck with his livestock. Because the ox was ill, the farmer put a blanket on the animal's back in the evening. In the morning the blanket lay folded in the feeding trough. After pastor N. had been in the shed, the misfortune stopped. The pastor never wanted to say what was going on; he had only advised the farmer to close up a hole in the wall of the shed.
196184: A dog always came to a farm and left its paw prints everywhere. One day the dog lay down on the baby's cradle, and the child died. The dog must have been the spirit of a dead person.
196193: Marie's chickens had been enchanted by a witch. When Marie opened the door of the henhouse, it suddenly filled with vapour so that not a single chicken could be seen. The chickens often escaped through a hole in the henhouse. Marie also often lost her chicks. The animals would then be lying in the meadow with their legs tied together. Because Marie was at her wits' end, she had to send for a clergyman.
196196: A girl made mice during catechism class in the church.
196205: When a child was ill in Zolder, the witch Trees K. was blamed.
196208: Whenever there was a full moon, a fiery horse was seen running in Ophoven. People believed that the devil rode that horse to the witches' gatherings.
196209: A man going from Sint-Huibrechts-Lille to Grote-Brogel came across a black cat that kept walking ahead of him the whole time. When the man had struck the cat with a stick, the animal disappeared behind a hedge. A little later the cat came walking back and said: "Now strike once more!" But the man no longer dared.
196210: In Rutten there was a haunted house. Every night a white billy goat came there to dance.
196211: Adamske van H. worked in Vrolingen. When Adamske was walking home one evening, he came across a sweet little kitten on his way. He picked up the kitten and put it on his shoulder. A moment later dozens of cats came running up, calling: "We want our pussycat back. Pussycat, where are you?" The kitten answered: "I'm on Adamske's back." Adamske threw the kitten on the ground and got away as fast as he could.
196216: A woman whose children all died mysteriously went to the mannetje (little man, a folk healer) of Genk. The little man said: "You must come back next week with the little cap and some other clothes of the child". A week later the little man said a prayer over the clothes and then told the woman to throw them into the Booneput. If the clothes sank, the child would live. If they stayed afloat, the child would die before she got home. When the woman stood at the Booneput and saw to her great dismay that the clothes stayed afloat, she pushed them under water with a stick. Whatever she did, the clothes kept floating back up. When the woman was almost home, she saw a big black ghost with a white bundle come out of her house and run off. The child had just died. The woman had seen the devil, who had come to fetch her child's little soul.
196220: A werewolf jumped on passers-by's backs and had itself carried. To prevent being jumped on by a werewolf, farmers painted a St Andrew's cross on their backs. Later, for the same reason, farmers crossed their clothing on their backs.
196226: A farmer who suspected that his cowshed was bewitched put medals everywhere. The cows were always untied by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
196229: A strange woman knocked at the door of a mother with a child. "Give the lady your hand," the mother said to her child. When the visitor had left, the child's little arm was twisted.
196235: A woman who suspected her husband was a werewolf had obtained a powerful prayer somewhere, called 'the prayer of Emperor Charles'. When the woman began reading the prayer one evening, her husband became very restless. He paced back and forth the whole time while foam came to his mouth. The woman kept praying until her husband was rid of his pact with the devil.
196240: A thirteen-year-old boy was taking a sack of grain to the mill in a wheelbarrow. On the way the boy met a woman who said: "That's far too heavy for you. Put the wheelbarrow down, I'll help you." The woman pushed the wheelbarrow a little further and then said: "There, now you'll manage the rest." The next day the boy had a blue stripe on his shoulder where the strap of the wheelbarrow had been. A heksenmeester (witch doctor) helped the boy.
196252: In a farmhouse in Beverst it was the custom to pray the rosary after the meal. Before they had started praying, they found a black dog with thick paws under the table. When the people had finished the prayer, the dog had suddenly disappeared. A few days later the dog turned up again while the people were praying. Because the lantern had suddenly gone out, the farmer went to fetch candles. After the sign of the cross had been made over the dog with a blessed crucifix, the animal ran off. The next day a horseshoe was burnt into the door. That dog was the devil.
196275: A child constantly had headaches because it had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft). The pillow the child slept on turned out to be full of pins. Because the child did not get better after the pins were removed, the child had to be exorcised by the pastor.
196282: Will-o'-the-wisps moved up and down in a meadow. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
196292: A man who went to mow the grass in the morning met a grey cat, which said: "Kormiaan, kormiaan!" That cat was a witch.
196295: At midnight old Co always saw a beguine hanging out the washing in the churchyard of Spouwen.
196296: In autumn a witte juffrouw (white lady) appeared on the Titskesberg near Negenbonder. It was said that she was the ghost of a dead person.
196302: In the fifteenth century monks travelled through Western Europe to collect money. With that money they went to North Africa to buy the freedom of slaves. Many people freed from slavery gave their shackles to Our Lady out of gratitude. Those shackles still hang behind the altar of Our Lady. Some slaves who always prayed to Our Lady of Tongeren were found one morning in shackles by the steps of the statue of Mary.
196311: Whenever Moazere Mina touched a boy, he was full of fleas the next day. Nobody dared to accept anything from the witch.
196312: When Hendrik was working, he was often visited by Florent W. Because this woman had the habit of scratching herself all over, Hendrik said: "Why do you always do that?", to which Florent replied: "Oh, it's just a habit." Annoyed, Hendrik said: "Well, it's a strange habit, because other people don't have it!" "If you don't have a strange habit," said Florent, "then I'll send you one." The following Sunday Hendrik was full of fleas.
196333: Rosalie had been to the cinema with her brother. When the two had just got home, Rosalie saw a white lady appear through the window. She immediately told her brother, who wanted to go outside to investigate. As the boy came closer, the white lady moved back. As soon as the boy went inside, the apparition came closer again.
196335: In Boekhout a werewolf roamed about who still had the red threads of the handkerchief that had been thrown at him between his teeth.
196337: A farmer had a deep pit behind his farm. One evening, when the farmer looked out of the window, he saw a white, shapeless figure floating above the pit.
196342: When people were frightened, they sometimes thought they saw a white lady.
196354: The F. family was coming back from Tongeren with a cart full of coal. At the Wad near Printhagen a fire-man appeared and set the cart on fire.
196360: In Gorsem a witch was burned who had given children the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft).
196388: One evening a widower came to the parish priest of Lanaken saying: "My wife has come back. She is standing in the kitchen." Because the man no longer dared go home, the priest went with him. Although nothing could be seen in the house, the priest blessed the place. The man stopped going to church and feared that his wife would come to complain because he did not pray enough for her.
196411: A man did not dare to go to Klein Mal, because on the way he always saw a goat floating through the air.
196415: Anyone who crossed the bridge in Gotem in the evening or at night was thrown into the water by an evil spirit.
196418: In Tongeren there lived a child who could make mice. The priest then baptised the child again and placed it in an institution. Children who could make mice had something to do with a witch.
196420: A woman lying in bed was overpowered by a ghost that kept her from screaming. When her husband felt the ghost, he went to fetch a knife. After the man had stabbed the strange apparition with the knife, the ghost was gone.
196424: A man had quarrelled with a woman suspected of being a witch. The next day the man got a pain in his shoulder, and a day later his arm was paralysed. Because the doctor was at a loss, the man went a few months later to the friars of Wijk. The friar prayed for a while, blessed the arm and gave the man a medal that he was always to keep on him. A week later the man had recovered enough to go back to work.
196435: A boy visited a friend in Maasmechelen whose mother and sister were suspected of being witches. When the boy came back home, he was followed by two cats.
196439: A man from Henis had attacked a soldier from Napoleon's army and thrown the body into the well at the bend by the little chapel. The soldier had been carrying money to buy food for the soldiers. The thief had built a new farm with the money. But that farm was haunted; the pillow never lay still on the bed, and at midnight the wind began to blow so hard that the man had to get up. Many animals also died.
196441: When someone was bewitched, people often went to 'het menneke' (the little man) of Genk. Usually the people then had to go on pilgrimage to Koersel. Nine days later the influence of the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) was gone.
196442: A man saw the ghost of a priest in the forest on the Schelfheide. The closer the man came, the smaller the figure became.
196456: A boy from Widooie had once promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, but he had not yet kept his promise. Every time the boy came back from his girlfriend's, he met a woman. When one day the boy asked: "What do you want from me?", the woman answered: "Well, you still have to go to Scherpenheuvel." After the boy had gone on pilgrimage, he never saw the woman again.
196458: By the Caetsbeek behind the baron's wood stood a little chapel where it was haunted. The baron had promised his first wife to restore the chapel. But the woman died before the baron had kept his promise. When the baron had remarried, his first wife came haunting at the chapel. Two men saw the white figure appear. After the chapel had been restored, the ghost was never seen again.
196462: A werewolf jumped into the oven because he did not want his skin to be burnt.
196463: The great-grandfather of the first count came to haunt the castle of Boekhout. At midnight a coach appeared with two black horses that had fiery eyes and were incarnations of the devil. The ghost of the count sat in the coach. No priest managed to banish the count. The saintly little priest K., who had only ever stolen a little book at the age of seven, was able to banish the count.
196466: Cats were witches. If you could make a cat bleed, she took on the shape of a woman.
196479: In de Maten a ghost could always be heard screaming in the evening. It was the spirit of a man who had drowned in the marsh.
196487: A man whose cows were under the influence of the kwade hand (the evil hand, witchcraft) lost all his animals to a disease.
196491: At night a farm was so badly haunted that people thought someone was tearing the farmhouse down. The cows all backed away and did not dare go near the manger. The place was haunted.
196493: The G. family always laid their washing out to bleach on a small meadow next to the house. One day Trui V.G. came by and said the washing was nice and clean. When the family wanted to bring the washing in that evening, there were a good fifty toads on it. They were convinced the witch had caused it.
196496: Every night on his way home a man saw a white rabbit sitting on the turnstile by the field path he had to pass along. One night the man brought a club and struck the rabbit down with it. Suddenly the creature grew bigger and bigger, and it attacked the man with superhuman strength. The man fled with a bleeding face. Afterwards the man even went blind as a result of the fight.
196499: In Rutten stood a farm that was haunted. One day meat had been put in the oven. A little later the meat had inexplicably vanished.
196502: A man was trimming a hedge close to the house of a witch. The man had been in the witch's house a few times. After a while the man got a swollen leg that would not heal. In the end the man had to walk on crutches, and later he even died of the disease. The man was convinced that the witch was responsible for this misfortune.
196519: Jan worked on a farm in Lens-sur-Geer. Because a girl from the farm was ill, nine other girls went on pilgrimage for her. On the way, however, the girls had fun instead of praying. A few days later one of the girls died. As her soul could find no rest, she came haunting one of her friends. That friend woke at night because she heard footsteps, but she saw nothing. This happened several nights in a row. For a spirit can only move forward one step each night. The frightened girl went to the priest, who said: "It is nothing serious. When your dead friend comes haunting again, you must ask her what she wants." The girl did as she was told, and the ghost answered: "It is me, the late Julia. You must go on pilgrimage again, or else I can find no rest." The next day nine young girls went on pilgrimage. This time there was no playing on the way.
196521: Whenever a farmer had made butter, the butter had always vanished as soon as he opened the butter churn. Someone who knew the witch of Herk advised the farmer to put chaff in the butter the next time. Because that did not help, the farmer went to see the witch. The witch then said to the farmer: "You spread butter with chaff!"
196540: A boy from Meers was in a relationship with a girl who was suspected of being a witch. One evening the boy decided to spy on the girl. When the boy met a dog in the street, he threw a handkerchief at the animal. A little later the boy noticed that his girlfriend still had the threads of the handkerchief between her teeth. "Now I know who you are!" the boy said angrily. The girl answered: "Wherever in the world you may be, I will follow you everywhere!"
196541: A boy who was in league with the devil made mice out of a handful of earth during catechism class. At that the priest said: "You have not been baptised!" Once the boy had been baptised, to his great regret he could no longer make mice.
196544: A man found it strange that his wife and daughter were always out in the evening. One day the man pretended to have fallen asleep drunk at the table. When the woman came in, she wanted to be sure her husband really was asleep. So she put two hot boiled eggs in his hand. Because the man held on to the eggs, the women went ahead and rubbed themselves with witch's grease. Then they said: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Aachen". As soon as mother and daughter had vanished, the man also rubbed himself with witch's grease and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Aachen". When the man arrived in Aachen, he was badly injured and his shirt was completely torn. His wife and daughter were so startled that they dropped their witches' drum and fiddle. The man walked home.
196546: A man from Piringen passed a toll bar on which a black dog was sitting. A little further on the man met a white lady. When he got home, the man saw that he had a red handkerchief between his teeth.
196564: A cowherd from Vreren worked with a farmhand who never came home until night. One night, at about one o'clock, the farmhand was climbing over the gate when he saw a big black man behind him. The farmhand was so frightened that he never again stayed out until night.
196571: Two boys had agreed that whoever died first would come and tell the other what things were like in the hereafter. A few years later one of the boys was dead. One day, when the other boy was working in the bakehouse, he heard a noise and saw a fireball appear, which said: "Everything is counted strictly and nothing is forgiven."
196574: When bailiff H. was returning from the village, he saw a white lady standing beside a brook. The man fainted from fear.
196577: There used to be a small church in Mulhem. Saint Willibrord passed by that church and baptised the people of Mulhem in Noteborn, which means 'spring in the wilderness'. For years the baptism was commemorated on Easter Monday. The sans-culottes (radicals during the French Revolution) demanded the church's bells. But the people of Mulhem had hidden the bells in the Sint-Jansbron spring, where they can still be heard ringing at night.
196598: A farmer heard a strange noise in the cowshed at night. When he went to look, he saw the cows standing with their tails in the air. Someone had bewitched the cows during the night.
196622: A werewolf was a man who dressed in a sheepskin in the evening and went out to frighten people. If one met the werewolf on a Sunday evening, one had to carry him.
196629: In the past, many farmers from the area around Hasselt were members of the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a band of robbers said to ride goats through the air with the devil). Nolleke van G. from Opitter was a man with special powers. Nolleke sometimes wrote threatening letters to people to get money from them. In the evenings Nolleke often invited friends to play cards and drink gin. One evening Nolleke said to one of the farmers: "Would you like a bottle of gin? The jack of spades from the deck will go and fetch it. But you must promise me to take the bottle at the door, or else we will all die." One of the farmers promised Nolleke he would take the bottle. In no time the jack of spades had vanished from the deck. A few moments later there was a loud bang on the door. Unfortunately the farmer was too afraid to take the bottle. It cost Nolleke a lot of trouble to get the jack of spades back into the deck.
196640: A man went for a drink at the house of a woman of whom it was said that she could be stopped by drawing a cross on the road. When the man went inside, he let his horses walk on because he knew they knew the way well. "The horses will wait", the woman had said. And so it happened.
196641: A young mother was visited by a witch, who said: "You must lay the child on its side, otherwise it will become cross-eyed." The mother quickly laid the child on its side. Not a minute later the child was already cross-eyed.
196646: A man who suspected a woman of being a witch was advised by the priest to make three signs of the cross behind the woman's back. After the man had done so, the witch looked round angrily. This confirmed the man's suspicion.
196649: After a witch had bent over the cradle of a newborn baby, the child fell ill. The baby wasted away completely and finally died. When the child's pillow was cut open, a wreath of roses was found.
196650: A little boy from Langerlo lost his hair because Mina had bewitched him. After the boy had been exorcised by the friars of Hasselt, Mina always walked past the house because she could no longer come in.
196655: A white lady often appeared on a bridge at night. She walked back and forth and then sat down in an armchair. One day three rascals decided to play a trick on the white lady. The boys quietly took the armchair away and ran with it to a farm. Immediately afterwards a loud blow sounded on the gate of the farm. The gate flew open and the frightened boys had to give the chair back.
196656: People who could not make butter and had found toads in the butter churn went to the friars. "Haven't you lent out a ladder?" the friars asked. The people had indeed lent out a ladder. "When the woman comes to return that ladder, you must not accept it. Moreover, you must hang a holy object in the butter churn," said the friars.
196661: A woman who lived in an old house saw all kinds of vermin in her house one evening. She went to a neighbour and said: "You really must come and see what's in my house!" The neighbour said: "Never mind, just go home and it will be gone." And so it was.
196663: In Tongeren lived a woman who was suspected of witchcraft. If that woman had touched a child, one had to immediately place one's hand higher up. Otherwise the child was bewitched.
196676: Because Frans T. was a scoundrel who had heaps of money, everyone suspected that he had made a pact with the devil. One day Frans vanished without a trace. The devil must have come to fetch the man because he had not kept to the contract.
196684: In the past witches were easy to recognise, but not anymore. Now they are often women who pray the rosary all day. Witches can make people ill or cause them pain. They can also foretell the future.
196693: When the witches danced around a pot, the devil came to them. After the magic formula "over hedges and hawthorns" was spoken, the devil carried the witches away. But one witch had made a mistake: she had said "through hedges and hawthorns". When that witch reached her destination, she was badly injured.
196696: A poacher who had already shot at an animal three times in vain said to himself: "Oh, that's a ghost sitting there." With that the poacher went away.
196707: A bewitched little girl had small sores all over her skin. After the pastor had prayed a novena and the mother had done a severe penance, the child was cured.
196712: The rural policeman's grandfather went mowing in the field with a friend. One of them deliberately lagged behind, then killed an animal in the meadow and ate half of it. When the man came back he could work three or four times as fast as his friend. The man said to his friend: "Well, you're not doing much today, are you?", to which the other replied: "No wonder, you've just eaten half a calf!" The man suspected his friend of being a werewolf.
196717: A man on his way to visit his girlfriend saw a kitten lying on the ground by the white chapel. Because the kitten kept getting under his feet, the man kicked at the animal. Further on so many black cats appeared that the man could go no further.
196718: In Gestel there was a horse that was very restless. When the farmer saw that a black cat was sitting on the horse's back, he struck the animal to the ground. The next day a woman had three broken ribs.
196727: A big black dog had completely wrecked a man's garden. When the man had thrashed the dog with a flail, the animal walked away unharmed.
196729: A man going from Boorsem to Kotem one evening suddenly saw a gentleman standing on the road, dressed entirely in black. The man tried to catch up with the black gentleman, but could not. A little further on the man saw that the gentleman had vanished. So the man went to the hedge and said: "You're in this hedge!" But that was impossible, because the twigs of the hedge grew very close together.
196733: A woman who went to dig potatoes for someone in the morning was surrounded by as many as fifty mewing cats. "The witches are awake already too," the woman said.
196737: By the chapel at the castle of Wideux lay a felled oak. Whenever people tried to move the oak, it rolled back to its original spot. In the old days ghosts were said to have been banished to that oak. In the end the count had a tall barbed-wire fence put up around the estate.
196742: In a hollow under a house on the Moorsberg, also called 'the Labyrinth', lived an old woman who had been given the name 'Die G.'. The woman had a long pointed nose and a hunched back. Die G. was a witch who could turn herself into a cat to eavesdrop on conversations in people's houses. Die G. often smoked a pipe of chestnut leaves and went begging. Anyone who refused to give the witch alms was full of lice twenty-four hours later. On Friday the thirteenth there was always a meeting at Die G.'s, whose house was then full of cats. The cats came from Glabbeek, Oeteren, As, but mostly from Dilsen. On such nights the women of the village did not dare stay in Niel. The men kept a blessed candle burning all night. During a witches' gathering in April the village men set fire to a bundle of straw in front of the witch's hole. A terrible screeching of cats followed. Most of the cats managed to escape through the flames. The next day all the women of Niel had burns. In Die G.'s hole lay a large dead cat with a hunched back and crooked legs.
196751: In the café of the witch Mie, people often played skittles for money on Sundays. One of the men, who spent all his money on drink, managed to knock down all the pins every time. "Mie did that," his friends would say, "because you don't bowl that well!" Mie did indeed help the man, because she knew he would spend all his winnings in her café anyway.
196753: A man coming home from a card evening suddenly heard chains rattling behind him. The man looked round but could see nothing. Because it was December, the man at first believed it must be Sinterklaas and Zwarte Piet. But when the rattling grew louder and louder, the man ran home in fright.
196758: In Tongeren lived two fortune-tellers who used cards, and people said they were witches. The two women were always very dirty. There were so many drips on the coffee pot and the cups that you could hardly tell what colour the pot and the cups were.
196772: A mother was with her child at the house of the witch Mina C. The witch stroked the child's head, saying: "Oh, what a beautiful child you have!" Two days later little Edgard had a bald patch on his head. The child screamed day and night and could no longer sleep. A doctor from Diepenbeek established that the child had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's harmful touch). A certain Matthieuke freed the child from the kwade hand (the evil hand).
196785: On a farm there was a horse that was drenched in sweat every morning and whose mane and tail had been braided. The horse also kept getting thinner. One day a man came by who said: "A witch comes and rides your horse at night, but she is invisible. Hang two crossed sticks above the door of the stable. The witch will come knocking and ask for something you don't have." In this way they discovered who the witch was: a woman of the B. family. From then on nothing strange happened to the horse any more.
196796: A man gave a girl a red handkerchief to throw at the werewolf.
196807: A woman had rubbed a cow or a bull on the head, saying: "Ah, lovely little cow!" Afterwards the farmer's wife found that the cow was ill and stood trembling on its legs. The farmer and his wife went to the witch and blamed her. "It's nothing," said the witch, "just go back home." When the farmer and his wife got home, the cow was cured.
196814: When a witch had patted a child on the head, saying: "You are such a good child!", the child would have a swollen head the next day. The only way to protect your child was to make a little cross on it with holy water.
196816: Around half past eleven, Letje from Zand was walking by the light of the full moon from Maaseik to Opoeteren. When Letje reached the kattebeek by the woods at the stroke of midnight, a hairy beast suddenly jumped on his back. Letje had to carry the drooling werewolf until he was out of breath. At that moment Letje got the chance to cut the werewolf with his pocket knife. Because the werewolf bled, it changed into a human. The man, whom Letje had recognised at once, begged Letje not to betray him. Letje agreed, on condition that the man stopped such tricks. The werewolf went to the friars, who freed him from his problem.
196822: In Berg near Ketsingen stood a haunted house. Although nothing strange was ever seen there, at night the wooden floorboards could be heard rattling.
196824: Near the Maas a witch who had turned herself into a lowing cow always walked about in the evening. In the evening the witch sat in a hollow tree stump.
196840: A boy from Lanaken who was going to Smeermaas with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "I have to go relieve myself. Here is a red handkerchief. If a werewolf comes at you, throw that handkerchief at its mouth." A little later a werewolf did indeed come up and snatched the handkerchief from the girl's hand. When the boy came back, he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
196845: In Overrepen there lived a little boy who could make mice. When the boy took a few corks in his hands and then blew on them, little mice appeared. After the priest had read prayers over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
196868:
A man and his son were binding faggots when suddenly a witch passed by. At that moment the son said: "Father, I can't bind a single faggot anymore, because my cord keeps breaking." So the man gave his cord to his son and carried on working with the rotten cord himself. A little later the son complained again that his cord had broken.
When a witch passed by, you had to keep your thumbs inside your fists. A newborn child also always kept its little thumbs inside its fists. The witch could then do the child no harm.
196883: A brewer's hand coming back from a café one evening walked home past the farm called Moskou. Because the farm had once belonged to friars, people said it was haunted. On the way the young man saw a human leg lying on the road. When he had passed it, he heard loud screaming.
196890: Between Hocht and Smeermaas there used to be a werewolf that jumped on people and had itself carried as far as the fields. That werewolf was said to have been a woman.
196898: A boy out walking with his girlfriend announced that he had to go relieve himself and gave the girl a handkerchief. If a werewolf came at her, she was to throw the handkerchief at the animal's mouth. When a dog came up, the girl threw the handkerchief at its mouth. Later the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. At midnight that boy always turned into a werewolf.
196899: Hubert V.B. worked in a sentry house in Liège. At midnight something could always be heard knocking in the house.
196903: When a man went to the castle in Leut in the evening to fetch bread for the dogs, he was jumped on by the werewolf.
196922: A man could not sleep because he was full of lice. Since the priests could not help him, the man himself put a holy object under the threshold, for then the witch would no longer be able to come in.
196924: An old couple lived in a cottage on a plot of land belonging to Tinuske M. When the woman had died, the chaplain provided a fine shroud with a special collar. Some time later the widower saw his wife appear in that shroud. The ghost told the man that he had to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. After the man had done so, he never saw his dead wife's spirit again.
196925: Two wandering soldiers were looking for a place to spend the night. When they knocked at a house, a man opened and said: "A bit further on there is a castle, but I must warn you: it is haunted, and everyone who stays there dies of fright." The men were not afraid, however, and went to the castle with some food and a deck of cards. When the soldiers had played cards until nearly midnight, one said: "Let's lay our heads on the table and pretend to sleep, whatever happens." At twelve o'clock three ghosts came in, took two chests of money out of a cupboard and began to count it. Then the ghosts said to the soldiers: "Choose which pile of money you want!", but the men pretended to be asleep. The three ghosts then put the money back in the chests and said: "This money is kept here in the name of the devil; no one can get it unless he brings a black billy goat without a single white spot on it." When the ghosts had gone, the soldiers decided to look for a black goat. When they had found a suitable goat, they went back to the castle and set the animal in front of the cupboard, which then opened by itself. The soldiers took the money and locked the goat in the cupboard. After a few days of enjoying themselves, one of the soldiers said: "That goat will starve; let's give it something to eat." When the two entered the castle, they saw from afar that the cupboard had been smashed to pieces. Of the goat only some blood and hair were left; that is how the devil had mauled it.
196946: A man going to Eigenbilzen saw a cat sitting on a post along the way. The man knocked the cat to the ground and went on. Further on, the same cat was sitting on another post. When the animal said: "Now strike once more!", the man quickly ran away. From then on that man was called 'Kattegiel'.
196950: In the Hasseltsestraat a ghost wandered about in the shape of a dog with a chain. Everyone was afraid of that dog.
196953: While the women were herding the cows, they often sat in the grass talking together. One of the women said: "Say, Kaat, all sorts of things are said about you in the village," to which Kaat replied: "Do you know what they say about you? That you're a witch!" The next moment Kaat was completely covered in lice. That woman was a witch. The parish priest later died in her house.
196970: A family in Weert often had chickens disappear from the henhouse. Because the postman had often said that Nel Mertens was eating chicken soup again, they suspected the witch was coming to steal the chickens. After the man had forbidden Nel to steal any more of his chickens, he sometimes found a dead chicken in the henhouse.
196975: On a farm worked a farmhand who could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmer went with his other farmhand to a hollow tree by the ponds, where the werewolf had hidden his animal skin. The moment the skin was thrown into the fire, the other farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his property. The werewolf took the animal skin out of the fire and ran off crying.
196981: A man coming back from Tongeren saw three big black men approaching in a sunken lane. The man was so frightened that he went home by another road.
196982: A boy from Beek often went hare hunting. One day the boy came angrily into a café where his friends were playing cards. "I'll teach those witches. I just couldn't catch those devil's children, but now I'll outwit them!" said the boy. He had chased a hare but had not been able to hit the animal, because his gun did not work. The boy then took a piece of a blessed candle and attached it to his gun. But he still did not manage to shoot the hare.
196986: A young man who had gone to fetch clover with a wheelbarrow met a witch on the way back, who said: "What a lovely wheelbarrow!" When the witch had passed, the boy could no longer push his wheelbarrow because his hand had swollen up completely.
196988: The drossaard (bailiff) who wiped out the bokkenrijders (goat riders, a robber band) came back to haunt after his death in the shape of a black dog with a pen behind its ear. In the morning the horses stood in the stable drenched in sweat.
196998: A man called his sister's name: "Net, Net!" The next moment a cat came crawling out of the drain hole. The man struck at the animal's back with his axe. Afterwards Net lay wounded in bed.
197014: A man who worked in Eisden had to walk through the woods to Opglabbeek every evening. Every evening at a certain spot the man met a cat or a little old woman. Sometimes there were as many as a hundred thousand magpies in the woods, and when the man then looked around, he saw the shade of an old woman without a head. One evening the man had a gun with him and shot six times at the strange apparition. His gun, however, did not work. Because the man was at his wits' end, he went to the chaplain, who claimed it was all imagination. After much insisting, the chaplain was nevertheless willing to bless one of the bullets from the man's gun. When the man walked in the woods that evening, he pulled the trigger of his gun. Then the man heard a gust of wind, and a few moments later the little woman stood beside him saying: "Good evening, you're out late." The man did not answer, for he recognised his neighbour.
197035: Everyone was afraid of the witch Tjenne, because she harmed adults, children and animals alike. In the end the witch was burned under a tree that was later called 'the Tjenneboom' (the Tjenne tree).
197042: At X on the Maas, a child had been bewitched by a woman from Boyen. When the curate came to bless the house, he found a crown in the pillow.
197046: When Stinus was coming back from the Kamp, he saw something moving in the brook that made a whistling sound. The apparition, which looked like a star, passed under the bridge towards Beringen.
197052: A will-o'-the-wisp often floated about in the castle stables. The farmhands were then very frightened, because they believed it was the soul of an unbaptised child.
197054: In Muizen a nun had left the convent to marry and have children. After her death the nun came to haunt at night because she wanted people to pray for her. The ghost would then say: "Whoever does well will fare well."
197055: At the Zwarte Lieve Heer (Black Lord, a crucifix) a woman came haunting with a child on her arm. That woman had promised to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel.
197059: An empty house in Millen was haunted. Passers-by often fled because they saw light in the house.
197078: On a farm in Mopertingen worked a farmhand who always went out in the evening. Because the farmer was very curious, he decided one evening to spy on the farmhand. So the farmer saw the farmhand crawl into a hollow pollard willow and come out again a while later with a skin on his back. Then the farmhand set off for Waltwilder. While the farmhand was at work the next day, the skin was taken out of the tree to be burnt. That evening, after supper, the farmhand went out again. He never came back.
197091: Muize Giel could make mice after he had come into contact with a pedlar. When Muize Giel had made mice during catechism class in Eksel, he had to go with the priest to the sacristy. After that the boy could no longer make mice.
197098: The witch Mina said to some boys who were going to draw lots to decide who would have to do military service: "Yes, yes, boys, draw well, because you will all draw odd numbers!" And so it happened; all the boys had to do their military service.
197099: The twin sister of a woman from Viversel had died after a witch had touched her and said: "Oh, what a beautiful child!"
197111: In a meadow in Val-Meer beautiful music could always be heard in the evening. People forbade their children to enter that meadow because those who had done so had never come back. It was believed that the music in that meadow was made by the spirits of the dead, who appeared in the form of a fire or a little flame.
197117: In the Kempen there lived a milk seller who always added some water to the milk. After her death the woman had to haunt. Near a pond she would cry out all the time: "I gave milk with water! Oh God, I have forgotten my soul!"
197120: A farmer returning from Gelinden met a hare on the way that jumped between his legs. The man was so frightened that he took another road home.
197139: Braddel B., a witch from Hasselt, had made a child ill. After the mother had put a relic under the threshold, the witch could no longer come in and the child was cured.
197145: A curious hunchbacked man stood watching witches dancing to wonderfully beautiful music. When the dance was over, the witches asked the hunchback what he wanted as a reward. The witches freed the man from his hump. But there was another hunchback living in the village. When he saw this man, he wanted to be rid of his hump too. So that hunchback also went to watch the witches' dance. After the dance, however, the man got no reward but a punishment: he was given the first hunchback's hump as well, so that he now had two humps!
197176: A girl who was buried wearing only a little shift came haunting the churchyard after her death. At midnight a woman went to take the dead girl's shift. The next night she came to give the shift back to the girl. The woman did not live long after that.
197182: A man who had gone to steal in the church could not get away; he was stuck in the window.
197183: A man who had taken his brother to Borgloon station in the evening was returning home alone. On the way, at about half past eleven, he saw a light appear in B.'s field. Because it was All Saints', the man suspected the apparition might be a soul. The fire disappeared and appeared again a little further on. It must have been the soul of an unbaptised child.
197197: A man coming home from work in the evening was pestered by a cat that kept running between his legs. The man tried several times to hit the cat with a stick, but the animal always outwitted him.
197198: In the old days there were werewolves that jumped on people and had themselves carried. This happened especially often in Maasmechelen. Later, people sometimes played the werewolf as a joke.
197205: In some alleys dogs and cats always roamed about in the evening. Sometimes it was so bad that people made a detour out of fear.
197207: In the castle of Damerus there was a ghost table. When someone asked the table: "How old am I?", it would move up and down, for example, seventeen times.
197218: A farmer's wife who had gone milking heard her name called. The farmer claimed he had said nothing. When the farmer's wife heard "Marie!" called for the third time, she asked: "What is it?" The answer came: "Go to Scherpenheuvel." After the farmer's wife had been to Scherpenheuvel, the ghost was no longer seen.
197242: In Dorplein the body of a man whose head had been split with an axe was found under the snow. No one ever knew who the murderer and the victim were. But a shade had often been seen at the place where the body was found. That must have been the soul of the murderer, who could find no rest anywhere.
197249: A woman could make mice by throwing a handkerchief through the house.
197252: The werewolf often lay in wait near the dung heap. Anyone who went there to relieve themselves was sometimes jumped on by the werewolf. Once the werewolf had had itself carried a little way, it left its victim alone again. But it also happened that the werewolf murdered its victim.
197267: A farmhand and a maid worked for farmer Bèrke D. Because the farmhand was pestered by a cat every night when he went to bed, he decided once to take his pocketknife to bed with him. When the farmhand cut the cat in the mouth, the animal changed into the maid who worked on the farm. The frightened maid said: "If you ever dare to betray me, I will do you something terrible. Leave it as it is." The next morning the farmer asked his maid how she had got that wound on her mouth. "Oh, I fell face first onto a broken bottle," the maid lied.
197280: A werewolf was a man with an animal skin who jumped on people and had himself carried. In Boorsem a werewolf from Maasmechelen was once unmasked.
197282: A certain Moens from Kerniel had come to live in Hopmaal. One day, as Moens was walking through Heks-bos, he came across some witches sitting and eating. Moens quickly stood behind a tree to spy on them. The witches drank to their hearts' content until their beer barrel was completely empty. A while later Moens saw another man approaching. The witches noticed him immediately and locked him in the empty beer barrel. After the witches had polished off the last scraps of food, they began to dance and make music. Some dogs that had smelled the food came to gnaw the discarded bones. When one of the dogs came sniffing at the beer barrel, the trapped man managed to grab its tail. The dog ran off, but the man would not let go of the tail. The barrel flew against a tree and burst into a thousand pieces. That is how this clever man managed to free himself.
197283: After a girl's death, the death owl came and screeched under the windows of the house.
197309: Two men went together to 't Roeren one evening. On the way the men were startled when the branches of an oak hedge suddenly began to shake. When the men reached the farm, they heard a hellish din. At the little chapel a thousand chickens all began cackling at once. "Lay some eggs for me too," said the man. The next day two cows lay dead in the byre.
197314: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of stillborn children. Whoever followed a will-o'-the-wisp got lost or was led to the water.
197318: At 't Mullem there was a farm that was bewitched. The witch came into the stable and touched one of the animals, saying: "Oh, what a fine beast that is!" A short time later the animal died.
197320: W.'s farmstead was haunted. Whenever people walked past it, they always heard a strange humming. Perhaps there was a witch there.
197328: To avoid being ridden by the mare at night, one had to place one's clogs with the heels facing the bed.
197360: When Frisse of the castle of Vogelsang had died, he drove around the castle in a glowing coach, calling: "Give me the Hout- en Paalbos, then I will be released."
197372: In Gingelom lived a witch who could make people die or recover through a prayer.
197384: In the old days, when people saw a cat, they often believed the animal was a witch.
197387: Some men out with a horse and cart got lost after they had met a witch.
197393: A man was visited by a witch from Rutten, to whom he gave some butter. The witch had run her hand over the man's head. The next day the man found that he was full of lice.
197398: Six men heard a strange noise in the woods that came closer and closer. On the Kruisdreef the sound seemed to move downwards. Then one of the men said: "We'll go on the right-hand side of the Kiezel." The sound moved past the men and went towards a brook. Yet the men saw nothing. Then the sound moved to the Herkenrodeplaats, where it seemed as if the oak trees were being shaken about. The sound went past the big pine to the road to Genk and then to Godsheide.
197411: Between midnight and one o'clock Melanie always began to cry and call out: "Mama, I see them!" Every day a little old woman with a harelip came to visit to ask for some milk. On that woman's advice, the child's pillow was cut open. In it they found a chicken's foot made of feathers, horsehair and gold thread. In the pillow of Fin, the child's sick mother, they found the beginning of a wreath. After they had been given a relic by the brown friars to put under the door, the witch could no longer come in. Fin prayed a novena and on the ninth day she lit candles and sprinkled the whole house with holy water. In the end Fin moved away. Whenever Melanie saw 'Marike den duvel' (Marike the devil), she ran away from the witch.
197421: To recognise a witch, one had to place one's feet crosswise on her footprint. The witch could then go no further. A certain Edward unmasked a witch this way during a procession.
197437: A butcher on his way to Waltwilder was surrounded by four cats along the way. When the man had to climb over a barrier, the cats jumped away. The man had to say three times: "In God's name, make way" before he was allowed to strike at a cat. After the man had hit one of the cats with his axe, a woman suddenly stood before him and said: "You have hit me on the head! Now you have taken my witchcraft from me. I am going back to my eternal resting place."
197440: Toin always sang about the devil. One night Toin was struck by something, although he could not see anything.
197446: A lost man carrying a lot of money was given shelter in the hut of Janneke van de Platvijvers. Because Janneke and his wife Mieke lived in poverty, they decided to murder their guest in his sleep and take his money. After that Janneke and his wife sat counting their money every evening. When Janneke had died, he had to come back to haunt. The ghost kept crying: "Give it back, give it back!" In the end the ghost was banished to the Maten.
197462: Whenever Gra was milking the cow, a cat always appeared in the stable. One day Gra struck the cat away. The next day one of the women from the village had a cloth around her neck. That woman was in any case already suspected of being a witch.
197464: A soldier walking home by moonlight was followed by a woman who was in love with him. Because the man refused to go with her, she said: "Then I'll be home before you". When the woman went on, the man suddenly got a pain in his leg, so that he could go no further. Only when the woman was home could the man walk again.
197465:
A man called Boon-Pee was hanged on the gallows, so called because he had always loved eating beans. The day after Boon-Pee was hanged, a farmer was mowing in the field. When the farmer ate his bean soup at midday, he said: "Boon-Pee, come and eat beans now!" The next moment he saw the corpse come down from the gallows to eat with him. When the dead man had finished eating, he said: "Tonight at twelve o'clock I invite you to my dinner." The farmer did not know what to do and went to ask the parish priest for advice. The priest advised the farmer to take a small child under two years old with him. When the farmer came to the gallows that night, Boon-Pee said: "If you had not brought that child, you would have been dead!"
After that night it was haunted near the gallows for a long time. A farmer from Genoelselderen once walked past and saw a man walking with his head under his arm. At the foot of the Galgeberg the dead man stood still. The farmer crept past him and then ran without looking back to the crossroads of Genoelselderen.
197468: A man from Tongerlo went to Mariahof in the Netherlands to buy tobacco. When the man came near the Lossing, he needed to relieve himself and squatted among the bushes. Since the man had no paper with him, he wanted to take some grass. But by accident he grabbed a hare by the ears. The man was so startled that he threw the hare across the Lossing. When the man went on, he saw that by throwing the hare he had killed four partridges. The man took off his boots and found twelve kilos of eel in them.
197478: Jan M. worked as a farmhand for Christiaan M. At midnight the window of Jan's bedroom opened and a ghost came in. The ghost went back out again of its own accord.
197498: A woman asked the postman what time it was and patted him on the shoulder. Shortly afterwards the postman was full of lice.
197527: All the animals of the V. family died. After a friar had read prayers over the farm, they had no more misfortune.
197546: A boy from Laak got lost at a place he passed every day.
197547: In Stamprooi lived a farmer who always had bad luck. Because people believed the bad luck was caused by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's harmful touch), the farmer decided to move. On his new farm the farmer had no more bad luck.
197550: In the Broek in Sluizen a goat with a green tongue came haunting at night. The animal grew bigger and bigger until it could reach the leaves on the branches with its green tongue.
197554: Whenever a man passed the witch's house with his donkey, the animal became very restless.
197561: A girl had to fetch a hundred cabbages from a woman who sold vegetables. The girl wanted to pull up the cabbages on her own, but the woman said: "No, we'll do it together, it'll go faster!" At a certain moment the woman said: "That's enough. That's a hundred." Strangely enough the woman was right, although she had not once looked to see how many cabbages the girl had pulled up. At home the girl told her mother what had happened. The mother did not dare eat the cabbages because she thought the woman was a witch.
197564: When the children came near a witch, they put their foot across her track.
197581: In the Jannestraat there was a tree stump that squeaked at night. It was a spirit.
197591: A woman went to the friars because her husband Toon was ill. She suspected that a witch had made him ill. On the way, however, the woman could go no further; it was as if she were nailed to the ground. The woman went back home. The next day she reached the friars without difficulty. Unfortunately it was too late by then, for Toon the carpenter's son died shortly afterwards.
197597: At night a foal with a chain walked about.
197599: Every morning a farmer found his horse with a braided tail. However hard he tried, he could not undo the braid. When the farmer entered the stable with a blessed candle, the braid came loose by itself.
197601: When someone was discontented or behaved disagreeably, people often said: "The mare is riding him."
197614: When Lewie was coming back from the Groenmolen around midnight, he saw a whole pack of cats. If Lewie had not met his father at that moment, he would have died of fright.
197615: A woman who had been visiting people in Stevoort met a witch on the way back, who said: "You're going the wrong way; you're walking away from home!" The woman got lost and wandered around Nieuwerkerken until three in the morning.
197618: A man known for his bossiness and lust for power had once lived on a farm. When the man was dead, he came to haunt the farm gate. When someone knocked on the gate, the ghost came out. Lovi de W. had bet some friends that he dared to knock on the gate. His friends sat watching under a bridge. Lovi went up to the gate, knocked and called: "Krellekuutje, come out! Krellekuutje, come out! Krellekuutje, come out!" Then the ghost came riding up on a horse.
197627: Rikus R. from the Zuidstraat came to haunt his wife after his death.
197636: A man who stood on Bergering at midnight with a black hen saw a large coach full of fire approaching.
197639: A sick child from Neerharen had been struck by the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's harmful touch).
