After a friar had read prayers over the child, the clergyman said: "I don't know if I can save the child, but you should look in the pillow." In the pillow they found a wreath of feathers that was almost closed. After the threshold had been sprinkled with holy water, the witch could no longer come in.
197656: A man who had shot a hare in the field was astonished to see the hare get up again and run away. It must have been a ghost hare.
197665: Some people drinking coffee in a house in Mechelen were astounded when they saw the cups dancing on the table.
197707: Between Vechmaal and Heks lay a meadow where the witches came at night to shake the fruit from the trees.
197721: A man walking across the fields to the barber heard lids and tin boxes rattling behind a hedge. That must have been a ghost.
197726: A shepherd from Rutten was walking home with his black dog. On the way the man heard a heated quarrel in a house, in which someone shouted: "May the devil come and take you!" At that the shepherd threw his black dog in through the window. Suddenly it went deathly quiet; the people were convinced that the black dog was the devil.
197747: In Opgrimbie lived a rich man with a long beard who never went to church. The man lived in a dilapidated house that eventually burned down. Behind the man's house stood an elderberry bush. One day two boys saw a devil with a long tail sitting in the bush. Terrified, the boys ran away.
197750: One evening a man was walking with two boys along the road to Berbroek. When they suddenly saw a black cat in the pine wood, one of the boys shot at the animal. The cat flew two metres into the air and then vanished. It was a witch.
197756: In a haunted house, at midnight a whole lot of black cats came in through the drain. The cats kept calling: "What we want, we shall do!", to which the occupant of the house replied: "We'll see about that!" Then the man poured boiling water over the cats. The next day almost all the women in the neighbourhood had burnt faces.
197788: A man had already been ridden by the mare three times at night. Once the man could no longer move because someone with an axe was threatening him. Another time the man was standing on a wall that stood in the water. The man felt that someone was trying to push him into the water. When the man got down on his knees, the bricks fell out of the wall. The third time the man could not move because an old woman with filthy hair was sitting on him.
197793: A man got up at half past four in the morning to play the werewolf. The people of Zonhoven took the train to their work in Winterslag. The werewolf crawled into a tree near Bokrijk station and then jumped onto the back of a passer-by, shouting: "Werewolf! Werewolf!"
197802: Witches' gatherings were often held at the Tolkesboom. It was said that women from Beek came there too. One day a young lady from France left her silver sword behind at the tree in a panic because she had been frightened by the witches.
197804: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his land came haunting after his death, saying: "Where must I carry it? Where must I carry it?" One evening a drunkard answered the ghost's question: "Carry it back, damn it, to the place you took it from!" The ghost then replied: "Thank you, my boy, now I am saved!"
197820: On a fine autumn day a witch came begging at a house where a child was sitting on the doorstep. The witch stroked the girl's head. Afterwards the child became so ill that she had to stay in bed for two months. The girl was tired all the time and would not eat. In the end the child did recover.
197823: A werewolf who was going to Tongeren with his girlfriend said on the way: "Go on ahead. I have to go relieve myself." The boy gave his girlfriend a handkerchief and said: "If you meet a big dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." Further on the girl did indeed meet a dog. She threw the handkerchief at the animal, saying: "Unravel the cloth as it was woven." When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. The girl did not dare say anything right away, but after that day she never wanted to see the boy again.
197843: When G.W. went hunting in the evening, he shot at a cat. At that moment the cat leapt up at him. G. accidentally struck his fingers with the butt of his gun, giving himself a wound that was very slow to heal.
197849: When Jan H. was travelling, he knocked at an old woman's door and said: "If you give me a kilo of flour, I can bake pancakes", to which the woman answered: "Over there is a castle, but it is haunted. Don't go there, or you won't come out alive". Jan went to the castle anyway and began to bake. While Jan stood by the fire, a number of human bones fell down. A little later a complete skeleton stood in the room. Jan said: "If you come from God, speak. If you come from the devil, go away". The ghost answered: "I have been haunting here for so many years and now I am finally delivered. Everything you see here is yours. I have also buried a treasure somewhere. Because it was brought in with a Spanish goat, it must also be taken out with a Spanish goat. You must try to decipher this treasure map and walk three times across the threshing floor in the barn". Jan found the treasure, so that he could spend the rest of his life in luxury.
197852: One day Nol and Frey were walking along the gravel road with a big dog. When they reached the Groemelingenstraat, the dog crept fearfully between the men. A little further on the dog ran ahead again. That street must have been haunted.
197854: A boy had fallen ill after he had been given a drink by Lisa van T.
197875: In the woods lived a witch who was called Bosmie. When Bosmie saw someone she did not like driving past, she made that person's cart tip over.
197882: Some men and women from Diepenbeek used to play cards in the evening. After the game the company went home drunk. One evening, while Pauline was playing cards, she felt a big black dog rubbing against her legs. Rik then said: "I'll throw that black devil out!" But because the man did not manage to drive the animal away, they all went home. The next evening they heard the dog panting again. Rik then went to the brown friars of Hasselt to tell what had happened. The next card evening was attended by a brown friar who read from a thick prayer book until the sweat dripped from his face. As soon as the dog began to howl, the friar took a crucifix in his hands and drove the dog outside.
197886: A woman had had a splitting headache for several days. When she woke up one morning, the woman saw rats in her room with yellow caps on their heads. The frightened woman quickly made the sign of the cross, after which the rats were gone. Then the woman ran downstairs and cried: "Now I have seen the devil in the shape of rats with yellow caps!" Since then the woman never had a headache again.
197888: A child that was bewitched lay crying all night. After a relic had been placed under the door, the child could sleep peacefully again.
197890: A man who had no money to build a house was complaining in an inn when suddenly a distinguished gentleman came in and said: "I will help you, on condition that you give me what you are expecting. Then I will build you a house that will be finished before the cock has crowed tomorrow morning". The man accepted the proposal and went home. When the man had told his wife the story, she replied: "Have you no sense? Now you've sold our child!" That night the wife did not go to sleep. At midnight she began to shout until the cock in the henhouse began to crow. At that moment the house was not quite finished. The hole that still had to be closed could never be repaired.
197891: A man who woke up at night said to his wife: "Mie, there's a will-o'-the-wisp here. I'm going to release it." The man went downstairs while the will-o'-the-wisp went down the stairs ahead of him. At the pump the man baptised the will-o'-the-wisp. Once a will-o'-the-wisp was released, the light went out, and the person who released it was entitled to a place in heaven. Jan, Mie's brother, also met a will-o'-the-wisp one evening, but he was not clever enough to baptise it. He came within a hair of drowning in the pond the will-o'-the-wisp had led him to.
197894: A man saw a cat sitting on a turnstile and said: "I could knock you off there!" The cat replied: "That would cost you dearly!"
197896: Some boys went to play with a girl in Kiewit. When the girl saw that she had lost the gold brooch her mother had given her, she accused the boys of theft. A little later the girl's mother came outside and said: "Oh, why would those boys have your brooch? There it is!" The woman pushed some oak leaves aside with her foot. Strangely enough the brooch was lying there on the ground. And that while the boys had searched there so often.
197899: Because the K. family could no longer make butter, the farmer's wife went to the friars, who gave her a relic to put under the door. The next day someone came to visit who was able to tell the farmer's wife who was responsible for the misfortune. When that woman was no longer let in, they could make butter again.
197906: A mother impressed upon her daughter that she must never leave an old woman with a child. For the mother had once seen an old woman touch a child and how the child had got a deep wound from it.
197908: Every night a woman dressed in white came haunting behind the little chapel.
197911: In Niel, many witches' gatherings used to be held at a linden tree. A man whose house was always full of cats decided to do something about this plague. He brought a bowl of water to the boil and then called: "Hey, pretty pussycats, come and sit cosily by the fire!" When the cats came running, he poured the boiling water over the animals. The next day almost all the women of Niel lay in bed with burns.
197915: A woman herding cows in the Waterbroeck happened upon a ball of blue yarn. She kept pulling on the thread until it broke. At that moment she heard a bell fall. On All Saints' Day that bell always rang at midnight.
197920: A woman found it strange that her husband always left the bed at about the same time at night. At the place where the man worked, a werewolf band was discovered in a chicken's nest. One day the man was sent away so that his band could be burnt in the meantime. As soon as the band caught fire, the man stood stark naked in front of the oven. As soon as everything had burnt up, the man cried: "Now I am released!"
197929: Witches always looked for an excuse to visit people. When a witch came to borrow or return something, for example, she had the chance to touch the child. As soon as the witch had gone, the child fell ill. A bewitched child could only be cured if a clergyman read prayers over it.
197936: A boy from Meeswijk went to break up with his girlfriend from Dilsen. As the boy walked back home, he was suddenly seized by panic. A few days later the boy was dead. The girl from Dilsen was a witch.
197947: A man who urgently had to go to the vet one evening thought that the Bievele farm was on fire. A little later, however, the fire had vanished without a trace. It had been the fire-man.
197948: A sick man who lived on the Zichemseweg was annoyed by a grey cat that came into his house every day in some inexplicable way. One day the man's wife roughly threw the cat out. The little old woman who lived a bit further along lay in bed with a broken leg and a broken arm.
197950: After Mozart had hanged himself in the Gallingenbos, he always had to come back to haunt there.
197954: In Maastricht the Freemasons held meetings. The devil appeared in their midst, recognisable by the smell of sulphur and by his goat's feet.
197971: When two men were returning from a sale at the sexton's, they stumbled into the Maas and drowned. Since then the inhabitants of Dilsen believed that the two men called at night: "Ferry over! Ferry over!"
197988: A man coming back from the fair suddenly felt two paws of a werewolf on his shoulders. The man had to carry the werewolf a thousand metres.
197996: A man who was accompanying the midwife to a house where a woman was about to give birth said on the way: "I have to go relieve myself." A little later the midwife saw a werewolf appear and threw her handkerchief at the beast. When the man came back, the midwife found that he still had the pieces of the handkerchief between his teeth.
198012: Anyone touched by a witch was covered in filth.
198013: In Kozen there was a farm that was so badly haunted that nobody dared walk past it in the evening. The farmer who used to live there, de Mot, came to haunt near the farm after his death. Sometimes he was accompanied by two dogs with eyes like fire. Other times de Mot drove around in a ghost coach drawn by four horses. Sometimes de Mot walked, dressed all in black, from the castle of Wijer to the churchyard of Kozen. One night people were woken by the sound of the coach. The ghost coach stopped at the farm and as many as ten people got out. The people went inside and held a great feast in the farm. In the end a friar was sent for, who banished de Mot for ninety-nine years to a wasteland in Alken.
198017: Jefke, the butcher's son, always laughed when people talked about witches. One day Trien B. warned the man that he should not mock witches. A few days later Jefke was found dead in his bed. Everyone knew it was the fault of the witch Trien B.
198026: When S. went towards a will-o'-the-wisp with a spade in his hand, the light came at him. As soon as the man had fled inside, a loud bang sounded on the door. On the door was a red handprint that could hardly be removed. The priest told S. that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
198044: The Geestbaan was a dirt road that ran through the Gruitrode woods and the Meeuwen heath to Hasselt. One day a miller was transporting four fat pigs along the Geestbaan with a horse and cart. Suddenly the horses stood still. A little later a man came by who saw at once what was wrong: "There's a spoke in the wheel axle that is blocking the wheel!" After the man had pulled the invisible spoke out of the wheel, the horses could go on again.
198047: People believed they would have a bad day if they saw a black cat in the morning.
198055: Anyone who had struck a witch's cat was surrounded by many cats.
198056: In Laakbos a drunkard heard a ghost calling: "Where must I leave it, where must I leave it?" When the drunkard answered: "Put it where you took it from!", the ghost replied: "I thank you a hundred thousand times!"
198065: A woman went to bake bread at her parents-in-law's. While the woman was working, Johanna G. dropped by briefly. When Johanna had gone, they said laughing: "Let's hope the bread doesn't go wrong now!" When the woman wanted to take the bread off the tray, it stuck to it.
198074: A boy out walking with his girlfriend suddenly said: "I have to go away for a moment. If anything comes at you in the meantime, throw this old handkerchief at the apparition." When the girl saw a werewolf, she threw the handkerchief at the beast's mouth, and it tore the cloth to shreds. A little later the boy came back to his girlfriend. To her great horror, the girl found that her boyfriend still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
198075: Some men walking in Klotbroek in the evening suddenly saw a ghost animal. A white heifer came out of the marshes and stood still in front of them.
198083: Whenever Boze Griet (Wicked Griet) came along, all the children ran off, because everyone believed she was a witch. One day a pig had been slaughtered somewhere and they were making black puddings. Boze Griet had been in the house and had laughed when she saw the sausages. The sausages were boiled in a pot on the stove. When the woman looked into the pot to see if the sausages were done, the pot turned out to be empty. The witches met in a meadow. They sat together around a white cloth, onto which they conjured the black puddings. So the witches had a feast of black pudding without anyone knowing.
198113: A man who had moved the boundary post of his land during his life came haunting after his death. The ghost held a boundary post in his arms and kept calling: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" When one day a drunkard answered: "Throw it, damn it, where you took it from!", the dead man was released and haunted no more.
198116: At the sparrow's nest Renier saw a little light appear every evening. At that moment a hellish din could be heard in the attic, although there was nothing to be seen. As soon as people came back downstairs, the din could be heard again. Pastor Geukens from Eksel did not believe any of the strange events. After the pastor of 't Lindel had come to the house, nothing strange happened any more. But by then Renier had already had so much misfortune that he had to leave the house penniless.
198119: A man was chased by a bull thrusting its horns forward menacingly. In the end the bull fell. The man claimed the bull was a witch.
198131: A woman said to a witch who came asking for milk: "I have none," to which the witch replied: "Yes, you do." The witch turned the milk into ash.
198132: Whenever M. went to Membruggen, he heard the hedges creaking.
198136: A man coming out of the café suddenly saw the witch Kait, who was looking for her son and asked him: "Haven't you seen Drees?" The man replied: "No, we haven't seen anyone," and went on with a friend. A little further on the witch suddenly stood in front of them again, asking: "Haven't you seen Drees?" Kait could move faster than ordinary people.
198161: Some drunken miners were walking past the little chapel on the Dijken when one of them said: "Let's knock Mary out of here!" After the men had pounded on the chapel door a few times, they fell to their knees and could not stand up again. Only when the men had crawled around the chapel on their knees and offered their last coin did they hear a voice: "Go now".
198184: A child had fallen ill after being bewitched. In the pillow the child slept on, they found a wreath that was not yet finished. If the wreath had been closed, the child would have died.
198201: A girl with blond curls met a witch, who stroked her hair and said: "Oh, what lovely curls!" When the girl came home, her hair was full of lice.
198212: Some men returning from a meeting in the evening met a whole pack of cats on the way that blocked their path.
198229: A cowherd who had struck a werewolf was nearly frightened to death when his own brother suddenly stood before him.
198230: A couple in love were walking past the devil's cross one evening. Suddenly the boy said to the girl: "Here is my handkerchief. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." When the boy came back a little later, the fibres of the handkerchief were still hanging between his teeth; he had been the werewolf himself.
198232: When the uncle of Beaat's first husband was coming in from the field, he met Bosmei's mother, who asked: "Are you going home?" The man said "Yes," and the witch answered: "If only you get home!" A bit further on the man blundered into the meadow with his horse, so that he got lost. After the man was found the next morning, he lived only two more days.
198233: Farmer H., who lived on Kievit, saw a woman picking apples in his meadow. After the farmer had thrashed the woman with a whip, the woman said: "You'll be sorry for that!" The next day twenty pigs lay dead in his sty. A few days later four or five heifers died. The animals were examined, but it was found that they had not been poisoned. In the end farmer H. had to move away.
198243: In Beringen there lived a girl who could make mice out of a handful of sand. When the priest learned during catechism class what was going on with the girl, he took the child to the presbytery. After the priest had read prayers over the girl, she could no longer make mice.
198251: In Opoeteren there were many rotten tree stumps, some of them as much as five hundred years old. But there was something strange about the thickest stump: nobody dared to walk past it, because it seemed as if the stump was chewing the cud.
198266: A boy who was going to the fair with his girlfriend one evening said to the girl on the way: "I have to go relieve myself. If a beast comes at you, throw my handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been told. When the boy came back a little later, the girl found that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
198275: The people living on a farm could not sleep at night because they kept hearing strange noises in the stable. When they were at their wits' end, they tore down the whole stable. In the stable they found the skeleton of a woman. That woman must have been a witch.
198302: A farmhand walking past a shed was startled when a cat suddenly jumped on his shoulders. The farmhand beat the cat until it bled. The next moment the farmhand saw his neighbour lying on the ground. By wounding the cat, the farmhand had set his neighbour free.
198313: On the Molenveld there was a little child who began to cry every night at twelve o'clock. The parents took the child to the mannetje van Genk (the little man of Genk, a healer). As long as they were on the territory of Stokkem, the child was so heavy that the father could hardly carry it. As soon as they had left Stokkem, the child became light as a feather again.
198318: A witch from Repen had laid her hand on a little child's head. After that the child had become very ill.
198342: A witte juffrouw (white lady) came walking out of the church. This lady had been buried under the communion rail.
198346: A man who came across a black cat during a walk kicked the animal. Further on the man saw the cat sitting on the road again. He kicked the cat and went on. When the man saw the cat for the third time and wanted to kick the animal again, the cat said: "One more time." The man was so frightened that he left the cat alone. A little later the man came across a little old woman wearing a shawl. That must have been the witch.
198349: The witch Johanna G. had had three husbands. People claimed that Johanna was responsible for the deaths of all her husbands. Johanna's second husband had died when he wanted to go to a beer festival. Johanna had forbidden him to leave the house before she was back. But the man would not listen and set off for the inn. After he had drunk a few glasses, the man said that he was afraid of Johanna. No sooner had he said it than the man fell from his chair. He was dead on the spot.
198353: A man taking his pig to market met a woman on the way, who said: "You won't get to market with that pig!" A little later the pig could go no further.
198355: A woman came to fetch milk at Roos V.B.'s in Deurne. The woman rubbed one of the cows on the back and said: "I want milk from this cow." The next day the cow gave hardly any milk. Although a wedding ring had been placed under the butter tub, they could no longer make butter either.
198358: A farmer who saw a tomcat sitting by the fire said to the animal: "There, my kitty, warm your bottom." The next moment the cat turned round and said: "Farmer, if you had not spoken so nicely, I would have broken your legs."
198370: A child had fallen ill after the witch Bet K. had stood beside its cradle. Later the priests read prayers over the child.
198373: When the witches held a gathering in the evening, wonderfully beautiful music could be heard. The witches could be heard flying in from far away. When the witches flew through the air, there was so much wind that it seemed as if all the leaves would be blown off the trees. In the morning, however, there was nothing to be seen, except the witches' circles where the grass had completely disappeared from the dancing.
198383: Pier V. had seen the white lady in the meadows of 't Motje, who said: "Come back here tomorrow and I will give you a key." The woman, who was only allowed to appear at that spot once every hundred years, wanted to be released. Because Pier was afraid of the strange apparition, he asked the parish priest to go with him the next day and accept the key in his place. But where Pier had seen a shade the day before, he now saw a snake with a key. The priest saw nothing at all and said to Pier: "Go on, take it." Pier was far too frightened to go up to the snake and he ran home as fast as he could. When he got home Pier was ill. Three days later he was dead.
198386: On Terlocht worked a farmhand who had to play the werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent to Luik to buy coal. Meanwhile the farmhand's collar was taken out of an oak to be burnt. When the collar caught fire, the farmhand was instantly standing by the oven to save his band.
198388: A farmer who was always visited by Zwarte Fles, who came to fetch bundles of firewood, said to the witch: "See to it that you have your own!" The next day the farmer's bundles of firewood had disappeared.
198389: One day Trui V.G. came to ask a farmer whether she could lay her washing out in his meadow. The farmer answered that it was not possible because his animals were in the meadow. Trui replied: "That doesn't matter. Then you'll just have to put the animals somewhere else." But the farmer refused. Some time later the grass in the meadow withered, so that the farmer could not let a single animal graze in his meadow.
198393: Frisse, who lay buried by the big trees on the Bolderberg, came to haunt Vogelsang. Some men returning from the fair in Bolderberg said: "Let's go and visit Frisse." When the men got there, one of them said: "Frisse, give me your hat to piss in." When a hat appeared behind the tree, the men ran away terrified.
198398: The Monnikenhof in Boorsem was haunted ever since two lovers had drowned themselves there. Because their father would not let them marry, the lovers tied themselves together and jumped into a well. The souls of the two suicides could find no rest.
198400: A farmer whose stable was bewitched had a parish priest come to bless the stable. The priest cried: "And now get out!", whereupon a voice answered: "I won't get out!" This happened three more times before the evil was driven out.
198401: A man coming home at night heard a dog rattling a chain. The man went to fetch his gun. When he came back, he saw a big dog leaning with its front paws on a barrier. At that the man suddenly became so frightened that he did not dare to shoot.
198404: Whenever Heksebet came to a child's cradle, something always went wrong with the child. When Heksebet walked through the village, the children drew crosses on her footprints.
198413: Will-o'-the-wisps were children who had died unbaptised. The lights flew about a metre above the ground.
198424: In Halen cats came to dance around a pond every evening. One evening white ladies were seen to appear there. The cats had been witches.
198425: The castle of Trockaert in Ulbeek used to be haunted. At midnight the gates flew open and a coach with four horses drove around the castle. A clergyman later banished the ghost.
198431: In Koninksem there used to be many witches who roamed about at night in the shape of a cat.
198439: One evening some farmhands lay in wait for the werewolf to give him a good thrashing. When one of the farmhands was jumped by the werewolf, another struck the creature down with a club. The next day a dead man was found at that spot, who had disguised himself as a werewolf with a cow's head and a sheet.
198441: A woman who could not manage to churn butter walked from Geleen to Tongeren. The woman had been given relics by the priests to put in the butter churn and to hang above the door.
198446: A werewolf only attacked people who were weaker than he was. When a boy had wounded a werewolf with a stick, the beast took on its human form.
198449: During his life a man had moved the boundary post of his field to enlarge his land. After his death the man came haunting with a boundary post in his hands, calling: "Where must I put it?" One night a drunkard answered: "Put it, damn it, where you took it from!" With that the ghost was released.
198455: After a heavy thunderstorm, the road from Bolderberg to Vogelsang was full of fish. The zuiger (sucker) of the storm, which looked black like a dark cloud, scooped water out of the fen and then rose up again.
198456: A priest who had not said one of his masses properly had to haunt after his death. One night the sexton saw the priest appear in the church. After the priest had lit the candles and made the sign of the cross, he began the mass. At the end of the mass the sexton said "Amen". After that night the priest never came to haunt again.
198482: At S.'s there used to be a large chest in which a dead man who had returned was banished. The people pulled the house down because the ghost tormented them so badly.
198518: Every night at the stroke of twelve an untidy woman came and sat on the threshold of the Sint-Janskerk. The place was haunted.
198522: Against the wall of the chapel in Wideux lay a tree trunk that could not be moved. The trunk always returned to its old place by itself. It was a ghost.
198547: A man who went fishing sometimes saw small lights floating. People believed those lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
198551: In a meadow a man was surrounded by twenty cats holding a witches' meeting. When the man said a quick prayer, the cats suddenly vanished.
198568: At J.'s place in Sledderlo there was a werewolf. Whoever dared to whistle at the werewolf was murdered. The werewolf had a bladder filled with blood hanging on his chest. If you could cut the werewolf in that spot, he became human again. Near R.'s house in Sledderlo a man had whistled at the werewolf. The man had fled and locked himself in his house. The next day the werewolf's hand was burnt into the door.
198580: When the witches flew through the air, they sang: "Nif-njef, nif-njef, poe-koe, nif-njef, nif-njef, poe-koe!" One day in Grimmertingen a man was lying on the hay under the roof. He heard the witches singing and began to imitate them: "Nif-njef, nif-njef, poe-koe!" An hour later the man heard the witches flying past again, and they said: "Just now you sang along, so now you can eat along with us too!", and a piece of human flesh fell from the sky.
198582: In Lutselus a ghost appeared in the evenings and at night and kept calling: "Where must I put it? Where must I put it?" One evening a drunkard answered: "You stand there shouting all the time. Put it back where you took it from!" The ghost then replied: "Now I am happy." Since then there has never been any haunting in Lutselus again.
198587: A young man was fed up with a cat always walking around the house. One day the young man cut off one of the cat's legs. Afterwards, however, it turned out that the man had cut off his own mother's hand.
198611: When five men were sitting in a café, one of them said: "A sixth must come, even if it's the devil!" A little later the devil came in in the shape of a man with cow's legs.
198613: A man had asked a will-o'-the-wisp what it wanted. The light answered: "I only want to be baptised". The man took a little water, poured it over the will-o'-the-wisp and said: "I baptise you in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit". The light thanked the man and disappeared. Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children who could find no rest. When baptising a will-o'-the-wisp, one always had to say: "I baptise you alone". Otherwise one would never get away, because all the unbaptised souls would come to be baptised.
198614: Pier van K. took the game of the poachers and hunters to Hasselt. Between 'Bongerd' and 't Geneuth the man always had to carry the werewolf.
198617: A man met a hare that stood up on its hind legs and asked him the way to the church.
198640: Werewolves jumped onto the backs of passers-by and then had themselves carried until their victims were exhausted.
198642: In Gingelom lived a certain Vica, of whom it was said that she put the evil hand on children.
198665: An old woman from the Zavelberg sometimes gave the children a sweet that made them vomit. When she touched the children, they were afterwards full of vermin.
198674: A woman who thought she was bewitched went to the priests of 'Gerardus Mazjella'. The woman had already been to several doctors, but that had not helped. The prayers the priests read over her did not help either, because the woman did not believe in them.
198686: During the fair, a Dutch beggar knocked at the door of a certain Grommen from Opleeuw and asked Grommen whether he was troubled by rats, which he could catch. "What do you want in return?" asked Grommen, to which the Dutchman replied: "A good meal will do." Then the beggar took a bundle of straw and began reading from a book with strange signs whose meaning Grommen could not make out. After a few moments rats came running from all over the neighbourhood, and they all crawled into the straw. The beggar said: "There are more!", and he read on until the last rats had crawled into the straw. "Now pour petroleum over it, and all the rats will burn up," said the beggar. Grommen, who did as he was asked, was dumbfounded, because not a single rat ran out of the burning straw.
198688: In winter the cats danced on the ice of a pond. One day a woman went with a crucifix to watch the witches' dance. Suddenly all the cats had vanished.
198694: The sexton went to fetch the friars of Weert to come and preach in Beek. On the way the clergymen saw a fire-man in the distance. One of the friars said to the sexton: "Shall I make him come closer?", and he whistled at the fire-man. When the fire-man stood close to them, the friar said: "No closer," and then sent the fire-man away again. "Sexton, what I have just done you must never do yourself," said the friar. One evening, however, the sexton did whistle at the fire-man. The next day the fire-man's claws were burnt into the door. When the sexton had to go and fetch bricks somewhere seven years later, the fire-man broke his neck.
198704: A man who spent all his free time on the brass band often annoyed his wife by it. One day the man was to fetch his wife from her mother's when rehearsal was over. When the man finally arrived there after a long time, his wife said: "I wish the devil would come and take that concert!", and she went home alone with her little son. On the way the woman saw a big dog sitting in the Opheimstraat, which frightened her. The woman decided to take a detour by the bridge. When she reached the bridge, however, she saw the same dog sitting there. At that moment the woman thought of her curse, and she feared that the dog might well be the devil. When the woman told a passer-by what she had experienced, both women quickly made off.
198705: A horse had stopped right in front of a witch's house. Then a maid came out and said to the farmer: "Don't try now. Wait until tomorrow during High Mass". The next moment the horses went on again.
198709: A man walking to his field saw an old woman standing in the distance, who went away without a word. When the man wanted to go back home, he got lost. After wandering about for an hour, the man came to a farm where they showed him the way.
198713: A midwife caused all the children she had delivered to die. That midwife was a witch. The devil's hands were visible on the child's little head.
198714: A man coming back from Tiewinkel with Betsie met two young foals on the way, which led him astray.
198720: A farmhand walked up to a maid who was busy manuring the field. The farmhand said to the girl: "Just turn your face over that way for a moment." When the maid looked back, the whole field was manured.
198737: Maeske, a ten-year-old boy, had learned to do magic by means of three words on a note he had been given by an old woman. At midnight Maeske had to get out of bed, whether he wanted to or not. He then had to fetch the calves from the stable and walk around with the animals. If Maeske was not yet awake at midnight, the chains in the stable would already start rattling. When Maeske spoke the three magic words, he could walk up the walls. The boy could jump from a high roof with ease without hurting himself. Against the church, however, Maeske was powerless. He always ran his head into the stones. When Maeske had made little mice after catechism class, the priest said: "Come with me, Maeske, you will get a two-franc piece if you make little mice again". However hard Maeske thought, he could no longer remember the words with which he used to make mice.
198744: At farmer P.'s they could not make butter because the milk was bewitched.
198755: At the crossroads of the road to Dilsen and the road to Lanklaar, a man saw three kittens dancing. Because the kittens would not move aside, the man's horse could go no further. When the man came home, an old woman from the neighbourhood said: "Say, lad, you mustn't harm those kittens, you hear."
198760: In the Ven in Maaseik swam a pike with antlers on its head. On a certain day the bells could be heard ringing at midnight, and then the sunken chapel rose up again.
198764: Frans the shoemaker had fled to Eigenbilzen with a girl. In a churchyard near Brugge the pair saw two spirits fighting each other. The spirits said that they had run up debts and had to wander the churchyard every night from twelve to one until the debts were paid off. As soon as Frans had accepted the bill, the spirits were released.
198765: Betteke said to a man: "Behind the wall you will come to a standstill." When the man had passed the wall, his cart broke in two.
198800: After Jefke, the witch's daughter's son, had been run over and killed by a cart, the witch said: "Now Jefke N. won't live long either!" Jefke N. got a swelling and died.
198803: Some men were playing cards in a café when suddenly an unknown man dressed in black came in and asked if he could join the game. The company played cards for hours without saying a word. At a certain moment one of the men noticed that the stranger had a goat's foot. Suddenly the stranger had vanished. They had been playing cards with the devil himself.
198811: A man coming home by way of the marsh saw something that looked like a tree stump without bark. So the man took his spade and struck at the apparition, which he took for a ghost.
198827: When a witch laid her hand on someone's shoulder, that person would get lost.
198830: Many farmers who made their own butter went to Wallonia in winter to sell it there for 2.5 BEF per kilo. So a farmer went to Wallonia together with a Walloon friend from Millen. In Rukkelingen-op-de-Jeker the road was in bad condition, so they had to continue along the ditch. At that moment they saw a horse-drawn coach come out of the field, heading straight for them. As the coach came closer, it turned into a dog cart, and when it had passed, the two men saw only a rolling barrel. The Walloon said: "It was a werewolf. If I had a pistol, I would have shot it." But the farmer with him knew it was not a werewolf, but a ghost.
198846: Some heifers were grazing in a meadow. When the police came past, a white foal suddenly stood there. That was a ghost.
198852: A man with five children had a ten-year-old daughter who had been touched by the evil hand. Because the girl did not get better, the parents had the parish priest come. The priest wanted everyone to sit in a circle while he said his prayers. No one was allowed to get up until the priest had given permission. While the clergyman sat praying, there were two knocks on the door. Each time the father wanted to get up and open the door, but he was not allowed to. When there was a knock for the third time, the priest opened the door himself and said: "Come outside now, for now it is gone." From that day on the girl's health improved visibly.
198855: An old woman bet a man that he could not make her bleed with a stab of a knife. When the man cut the woman's arm, indeed not a drop of blood appeared.
198865:
Witches always turned themselves into cats and never into cows or horses.
In Langven lived a farmer who always had misfortune with the animals in his stable. One day farmer C. struck with his dung fork at a cat that was always in his stable. The next day C. found that his neighbour's wife had a broken arm.
198872: In a house in Ophoven, a ghost always appeared at midnight with a rosary in its hand. One day one of the neighbours suddenly remembered that Toon van O., a man who had recently died, had promised during his life to go on pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. After someone else had gone to Scherpenheuvel in Toon's place, the dead man no longer came haunting.
198899: In a castle lane a fiery phantom coach with eight horses drove at night. It was the dead lord of the castle riding around in his coach at night.
198902: Jan was looking for a place to sleep and the mayor told him: "Here stands an old haunted castle. If you dare to spend the night there, you will get the castle". Fearlessly Jan accepted the offer. In the castle Jan immediately began baking buckwheat cakes. Suddenly Jan heard a voice from the chimney: "I'm falling!", to which Jan answered: "Fall then, but not in my cake!" When a heap of bones had fallen out of the chimney, a skeleton suddenly stood behind Jan and said: "Come with me to the cellar". In the cellar the skeleton dug up three chests. One chest held gold coins, a second silver coins and a third copper coins. The next moment the ghost had vanished. When Jan was sitting in the garden the next morning, a gentleman came by and said: "You must keep all that money", to which Jan answered: "No, I won't". From that day the castle was no longer haunted. Jan lived a long time.
198907: A man who saw a werewolf lying in the field picked the beast up and carried it a little further.
198911: When the miller saw a black figure approaching in the distance, he said: "Oh God, oh God, there's the flying ghost again!", and he slammed the door shut. A moment later there were three knocks on the door. The next morning a black hand was burnt into the door. That was the work of a witch who flew through the air on a broom.
198914: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
198916: A girl from Tongeren was married to a werewolf. Because the man had sold his soul to the devil, he had to go out as a werewolf at midnight. One night the woman was out with her sister when she suddenly saw a big dog appear. The woman then threw a red handkerchief at the animal's mouth. The next day at the midday meal, the woman saw that her husband still had the red fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
198932: In Meeswijk lived a witch who could infest people with lice.
198935: A man ploughing near Panis' Haagske was always followed by a hare. When the man threw his handkerchief at the hare, the animal burned its teeth marks into the cloth.
198945: A lady dressed all in white always walked along the dike of the little Maas.
198952: In Hasselt stood a haunted house. Between midnight and four o'clock shouting could be heard in that house.
198969: A woman from Deurne was suspected of being a witch because almost all her children had died.
198986: A young man from the Gerkenberg went to the fair in Bree with his girlfriend. The young man, however, had to roam as a werewolf at regular times, so he said to the girl: "I have to go relieve myself behind the hedge. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth; then it can do you no harm." A little later a big dog did indeed come running towards the girl. She threw the handkerchief at the dog, which tore the cloth to shreds. When the young man came out of the bushes a little later, he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
198987: A man walking from Alken to Hasselt saw a large dog appear near the Geuzentempel. The animal's eyes grew bigger and bigger until they almost looked like balls of fire. When the man had made the sign of the cross, the dog had disappeared.
199000: A man who had sold his soul to the devil got everything his heart desired. But when his time had come, the man had to die and go with the devil.
199004: The Tilkesjacht were witches who flew through the air. The witches sat on the jawbone of a donkey and then said: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Cologne". The witches went everywhere drinking up the wine. A farmer who had seen one of the witches return one morning took the jawbone and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns". The farmer arrived at his destination badly injured.
199014: Anyone who went alone to the midwife at night was always pestered by cats.
199015: A dead woman came as a ghost at night and lay in her husband's bed. The woman could find no rest because her husband had once promised to go on a pilgrimage for her. The man promised the ghost that he would build a little chapel. As soon as work on the chapel began, the ghost was released.
199042: Next to a farm in Vreeren stood a small house in which a witch lived. On the farm worked a farmhand from Neerrepen, who one day had quarrelled with the witch Leenke. Some time later Rikus, the farmhand, became seriously ill. Leenke said to him: "Rikus, you will suffer a lot before you recover from that illness!" No doctor could help Rikus, and a man from Maastricht said: "It is Leenke's evil hand." Rikus suffered greatly and finally died of his illness.
199045: Two men walking through the snow saw seven wailing cats sitting along the ditch. When one of the men threw something at the cats, one stayed sitting there. The other man then said: "Leave them be, that is a witch."
199052: A farmer from Weert had seen that hares had come to nibble his cabbages at night and asked his farmhand to keep watch. When the farmhand saw a hare at midnight, he shot the animal. But the hare got up again and ran away. The next morning small spots of blood could be seen in the snow, leading to the house of a woman who lay wounded in bed: the woman still had the shot in her buttocks.
199067: In Schulen there lived a boy of five or six who could conjure mice out of his cap by speaking a magic formula. After prayers had been read over the boy, he could no longer make mice.
199072: When Staf V.D.W. was sitting by the stove in his girlfriend's house, there was suddenly a knock at the door. Staf went to open the door, but he saw nothing.
199088: A woman went to pray by moonlight at the grave of her late husband. When she left, the woman always said: "Good night, Harry!" One night, however, an answer rang out: "Good night, Minneke!" From that night on the woman no longer dared to go to her husband's grave.
199093: A man coming back from the fair with his wife felt that he was going to turn into a werewolf and said: "If you see a werewolf, throw something made of silk at its mouth and leave the beast alone." When the woman saw a werewolf a little later, she threw her neckerchief at the animal. A little later her husband appeared with the fibres of the neckerchief between his teeth.
199102: A man who was out at eleven o'clock at night heard a rustling in the hedge. When the man suddenly saw a foal standing in front of him, he went on in fear. A little later the foal stood before him again. The man was so frightened that he no longer dared to go home and stayed the night in the nearest café.
199112: On a farm in Diets-Heur there worked a farmhand who slept in the hayloft at night. Because the farmhand was annoyed that a cat always went up with him, he hit the animal on the head. The next day the maid sat in the kitchen with a bandage around her head.
199119: When Jef P. was walking home, someone said: "You're bound to get lost." Unbelieving, Jef walked on. A while later the man saw water all around him and could no longer find his bearings. Only when a dog began to bark did Jef know where he was again.
199163: Harie P. always had to take his cows past the house of Marianne van H. Although Marianne was said to be a witch, Harie often stopped to chat with her. One day, when Harie took his cows to the meadow very early, Marianne was not yet awake. The animals stood still at the witch's house. Only when Marianne was awake would they go on.
199171: A man and a woman travelling with their little child were surrounded the whole time by rats and mice. When the father wanted to strike at the animals, his wife reminded him that they had a child with them. When they came to a bridge with two posts, they saw a cat sitting on each post. The father struck one of the cats down with a stick. When the mother said: "And now the other one too!", the man became so frightened that he no longer dared to strike, for he suspected that the cats were witches.
199172: One evening some men were playing cards in a café. When one of them bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw a dog lying under the table with eyes as big as saucers. Because they could not chase the dog outside, the next day they sent for a brown friar from Hasselt.
199175: An officer was billeted with the S. family. During that time a baby was born to the S. family. After much insisting, the officer was allowed to be the baby's godfather. When the child was about two years old, however, strange things happened: when the child sat playing in the dust, the dust turned into mice. So it came about that nobody wanted to play with the child any more. When the child was six, the officer came to visit and asked: "How is my godchild?" "She is plump and well fed," the parents answered. But when the officer saw his godchild playing, he knew what was going on, for when the child was baptised he had heard the priest forget a word. The officer took his godchild by the hand and went with her to the priest to have her baptised a second time. Then he let the child play and asked: "Make some little mice again!", but she could no longer do it.
199180: The two farmhands who lived in the drossaard's (bailiff's) house slept in the same bed. One farmhand stayed in bed a little longer while the other had already got up. Suddenly the farmhand still in bed cried: "Why do you have to hit me like that!" The other farmhand, however, knew nothing about it.
199181: Four men regularly came to play cards in café de Helm on the Speelhof: the sexton, the alderman, the little weaver Noben, and the owner of the Helm. When the alderman failed to turn up one day, Noben said: "If only we had a fourth man for cards, even if it were Jan the devil." No sooner had he spoken than a tall man with a black beard came in. Because the stranger always won, the sexton grew suspicious. When the sexton bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had horse's feet. The sexton turned deathly pale and cried in terror: "Holy Mary!", whereupon the stranger replied: "That name may not be used during a card game", and he stood up and leapt out through the window. The café stank of sulphur and pitch, and all the food and drink had gone bad. A brown friar from Holland exorcised the café and sprinkled everything with holy water.
199185: One morning a man saw black cats and thought: "Oh God, that is not good!" When the man came back from work in the afternoon, he was run over and killed. The man's wife had also seen those cats all day.
199201: In the past people believed that a witch could infest children with lice. Those children then had to go to the priests to have prayers read over them. In reality the plague of lice was simply due to poor hygiene.
199202: A man was walking home through the woods at eleven at night. After he had picked up his hat, which had blown away, he suddenly could no longer find his bearings. Although he was only a hundred metres from his house, he lost his way. The 'dolende man' (wandering man) had caused this.
199219: Behind a farm in Val-Meer people always heard music. Two people who wanted to know where the music came from never returned.
199237: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised. Because the lights wanted to be baptised, they pulled people into the water.
199240: In Rachels a witch caused a child to get a big lump.
199256: A woman who often sat praying one day saw the ghost of an unknown girl come in through a closed door. The woman believed she had released a poor soul from purgatory.
199257: The children believed that a witch could not harm them if they kept their thumbs inside their fists. But the old witch said: "You can put your thumbs in your fists or up your backside; I can always give you nits and lice!"
199261: A woman from Gelinden could cure people who had got the 'fivelein' (a witch-caused ailment) through a witch's doing.
199268: The werewolf often hid behind a bush or a hedge. As soon as he got the chance, he jumped onto people's necks and had himself carried for a while.
199274: Three men who wanted to play cards were sitting in the Wildeman in Dilsen. When a gentleman came in a little later, they asked him whether he would join them as the fourth player. When one of the men went to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the gentleman had a horse's foot. At the cry "Jesus, Mary!" the gentleman flew out through the window. A stinking vapour hung in the inn.
199276: Will-o'-the-wisps were lost little souls that flew over the plains.
199292: The farmhand Harrie claimed that the castle of Dessener was haunted. After the priest had blessed the castle, no more strange things happened.
199307: A man going fishing met a friend, who showed him a medal from the friars of Hasselt. The friend said: "I always carry this medal with me, and I'll tell you why. When I was working in Wallonia with some others, something strange happened. We ended up in the water with the lorry because we had seen something black on the road. Every time we had almost got out of the water, that black apparition appeared again."
199314: In Treselt a horse stood still in front of a witch's house.
199315: Whenever Arnold D. went to Eigenbilzen, he had to carry the werewolf. As soon as the man got home, the werewolf had disappeared.
199321: A woman who went to fetch her daughter Ida in Overrepen around midnight often saw the white lady walking back and forth in an alley. Although the white lady did nothing, the two women were very frightened.
199328: Some men who had been visiting somewhere had each been given an apple by the hostess. When the men got back, someone told them the hostess was a witch. Some time later the horse of one of the men was due to foal. All night long cats could be heard yowling in the stable. Suddenly the man felt cats crawling all over his bed. He grabbed hold of the cat. The next moment the man was soaking wet and the cat had vanished.
199340: A man from Valmeer had heard that his girlfriend was a witch. Because the man wanted to know whether it was true, he went to visit his girlfriend. When the man tapped on the girl's bedroom window, there was no answer. A little further on, the man saw a cat walking among the bean poles. A little later the man went back to the window, where his girlfriend appeared and said: "I was just in a deep sleep." The man did not believe her, however, and never wanted to see the girl again.
199345: A man returning from his parents-in-law saw a ghost on the way. The white ghost rose above the trees and then vanished into the sky.
199354: When Lange Han came peddling with her basket, in one particular house she always went straight to the child's cradle. After a few months the little boy suddenly could no longer walk. The parents went to pastor T. to have prayers read over the child. Someone had also told them: "Get a blessed candle from the sexton that has burned at the altar and draw a cross on the threshold with that candle. That way the witch will not be able to get in any more." When Lange Han came by the next day, she could not get in. Since that day the witch never came by again. The little boy soon recovered.
199375: A family who were to leave in the morning by horse-drawn coach were woken early by the sound of hooves. The mother said: "Pier, get up, we're late! Koob is already here." They clearly heard a horse walking and even saw a horse appear at the window. When the man got up, the horse had vanished. The hoofprints were still clearly visible in the earth.
199376: A girl from Heusden who was boiling buttermilk at seven in the evening saw her dead mother appear in the corner. The mother wore a kornet (a traditional bonnet) and looked just as she had lain in her coffin. When the mother appeared again, the girl called her father, who asked what the ghost wanted. The dead woman answered: "I promised to go on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. Only when you have fulfilled that promise will I be at rest."
199385: At Nol S.'s place some healthy calves had died through the evil hand. One evening Nol saw a black cat fleeing from the stable. Because the cat never came back, Nol had no more misfortune.
199388: A few boys were playing cards by the woods during Sunday morning vespers. Whoever lost had to go and fetch a bottle of gin. Because after a while still nobody had lost, one of the players threw down his cards, saying: "Come on, this has gone on long enough. Jack of spades, go and fetch a bottle of gin quickly!" A little later the jack of spades had vanished from the deck. After a while something came out of the woods saying: "I am the jack of spades and I've come to bring a bottle." Later that day the landlady of a nearby pub found that a bottle of gin had mysteriously disappeared from her cellar. That card player owned a little book of magic.
199396: Two people walking to Scherpenheuvel came across a black cat on the way. When one of them wanted to throw something at the cat, the other said: "No, don't, that's surely a witch!"
199398: Gust W. from Entbroek had bought a cow in Berlingen. When he had milked the cow, however, the milk turned out to be worthless: it was watery and even contained blood. Gust went to ask the sorcerer from Nieuwerkerken for advice. The sorcerer asked Gust: "Didn't you meet a woman who touched the cow with her hand?", to which Gust replied: "Yes, when I came past the Keienberg with the cow, the old wife of C. came walking by and asked, 'Gust, where did you buy that fine cow?' Meanwhile the woman patted the animal's back with her hand." The sorcerer gave Gust the following advice: "For three weeks you must not lend anything. You must go on pilgrimage with a bottle of oil to the Holy Sacrament in Hasselt. Everyone living in your house, and the cow too, must drink a spoonful of the blessed oil. You must also put a bottle full of cream on the chimney. If anyone asks why you are doing that, you must answer that it is none of their business." Gust followed the sorcerer's advice. After three weeks the cow's milk was normal.
199414:
At the fair a man found a magic book in his trouser pocket. From then on the man noticed he had special powers. When he went walking with his girlfriend, he said to the girl: "I have to go to the toilet. If a dog comes along, just throw my handkerchief at it." A little later the man appeared in the shape of a dog.
In the end the man took his book to the priest to have it burned. But when the man got home, the book was already lying on the table again. Only when the priest burned the book for the third time did it work. Such books could only be got rid of by secretly putting them in someone else's pocket.
199418: A man who had been shot dead came to haunt in the Gestelbroek. No one dared go to that place any more.
199428: A witch who had taken the shape of a cat could not be hit.
199433: The procession always passed by S.'s farm in Rotem because something strange had once happened at that spot. One day a black cat with glowing eyes lay on the ground there and would not go away.
199438: A farmer had a farmhand who always went out in the evening. The farmhand would then sit down on a tree stump and turn into a werewolf. One day the farmer had sent his farmhand to the meadow, so that he could burn the farmhand's collar in the meantime. The moment the farmer was about to throw the collar into the oven, the farmhand was standing beside him. When the collar had burnt up, however, the farmhand was released.
199439: A girl who was sewing received a visit from a woman. The girl went out to the yard for a moment. When she came back, she found on her chair a wreath with pins stuck in it. The moment the girl burned the wreath, she heard a loud scream. After a cross had been hung above the door, the witch could no longer come in.
199441: A young man returning from a visit to his girlfriend in Gelinden saw a ghost in a white sheet appear near the churchyard. The young man heard chains rattling. When he threw a thick stick at the ghost, he heard a loud scream. The next moment the ghost had vanished.
199444: When a strong wind rose because a thunderstorm was coming, a man said: "Look, there's the heivrouw (heath woman) again!"
199451: A girl who was in a relationship with a werewolf decided to play a trick on her boyfriend. The girl had learned witchcraft from her mother. When her boyfriend came, she put a broomstick with a mop in a corner and went away. The boy took the mop on the broomstick for his girlfriend.
199459: To know whether a woman consorted with the devil, one had to place one's foot crossed on her footprint. A witch would then turn round and ask why you had done that.
199483: A man saw a funeral procession with a coffin come out of the woods and head towards the church.
199507: With the Luys family in Beek there was a farmhand who was helped in his work by the devil. When the farmhand had to manure the field, he manured a small patch and then said: "Come on, now all of it!" The next moment the whole field was manured. To be able to do such things, however, the farmhand always had to wear a collar. One day someone took the collar away to burn it. Before the collar was even in the fire of the oven, the farmhand came running to save his collar.
199510: At the Duivelsput (Devil's Well) in the woods there was haunting in the evening and at night. A black man always sat on the rim of the well then.
199534: A man whose foals, calves and piglets all died had a mason from Lauw come to do renovation work on the stable. The mason said that he often worked in Wallonia, and that there it was the custom to have prayers read over the stables before putting animals in them. The man then also had the parish priest come to read prayers over the stable. Since then all the animals stayed healthy. The old witch must have been responsible for the misfortune.
199538: When mass was over, a fine black horse was standing on the bridge in the Jekerstraat. As soon as someone had climbed onto the animal's back, the horse flew up into the air. The bystanders advised the man to let himself fall. Luckily the man did so, for who knows where he might otherwise have ended up!
199543: In the Uukeverveldje a spirit wandered about, calling: "Where must I put it? Where must I put it?" When Driekske walked past that field drunk one night, he answered: "Put it where you took it from!" and made the sign of the cross. Since then the spirit has never been seen again.
199550: On the road to Beverlo stood a haunted castle. A brave young man had bet his friends that he dared to sleep a night in the castle. When the boy wanted to cook food in the castle, a bone suddenly fell out of the chimney. The boy threw all the bones that had fallen into the pan into a corner. A little later a complete skeleton stood in the corner. The young man followed the skeleton to the cellar, where a chest of money was dug up. The next day the boy was visited by a gentleman who said: "You must keep all the money for yourself". But the boy kept only part of the money and gave the rest to the poor and to the church to have masses said. This delivered the skeleton.
199561: The mother of the recently deceased joiner from the Brokkesteeg was frightened half to death when she saw her dead son sitting at the workbench one morning. The mother said: "What are you doing here?", and the ghost answered: "I had promised to go on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. Now you must go in my place." The next morning the mother set off for Scherpenheuvel at five o'clock. The ghost that accompanied her said: "You go in front, or else you will have to carry me the whole way." Since then the mother never saw the ghost again.
199575: Some men who had gone to fetch coal in Genk saw a priest appear, haunting together with an altar boy. Long ago a priest had fallen off the roof there.
199578: Because Bet L. was still standing in the street between midnight and one o'clock, a man said to her: "Now then, little woman, shouldn't you go to bed!" The next moment the witch had vanished.
199598: Some men who had gone to buy milk in Diets-Heur met a witch on the way, who touched the milk jugs with her hand. When they got home the men found that the milk had gone sour.
199602: The inhabitants of Gotem were tormented every night in various ways. The cows and horses were untied and driven into the marsh, where they drowned. A witch was responsible for all that misfortune.
199606: In the old days the road to Sint-Truiden was haunted.
199630: In Maastricht a Jew lived with Catholic people. When the Jew had died, a dog lay on the deathbed. Because the ministers were at their wits' end, they fetched a friar, who had hidden the Holy Sacrament under his cloak. "You must name a place where I should send the dog," said the friar. After the friar had prayed something in Latin, the released dog ran away.
199641: In a house in Kuringen a witch came at night to untie the cows.
199646: Franske R., a joiner from Gelinden, worked in Boekhout. One evening he had stayed a little longer to play cards with the people he worked for. When Franske walked home in bright moonlight, he met a hare. Franske threw something at the hare, whereupon the animal changed into a dog. The dog went along with Franske as far as the Broeksteeg in Gelinden. Because the animal walked so close to Franske's feet, it was wounded by a buckle on his shoe. When the dog lost blood, the animal changed into a human. It was a man with whom Franske had played cards that very evening. Franske never dared to tell anyone the werewolf's name, because the man had threatened him: "If you ever mention my name, it will be your death."
199648: In Diepenbeek there was a toll barrier that always opened by itself. One day a brave man went there and asked: "In the name of God, tell me who always opens this barrier here. Tell me what I must do to help you." A voice answered: "Yes, my boy, you are the first who dares to speak to me. During my life I promised to walk to Scherpenheuvel. But I was never able to make that pilgrimage, and so now I can find no rest." After the man had gone on the pilgrimage for the dead person, the ghost was never seen again.
199653: People who had bought a cow had paid too little. Because the cow kept getting sicker, they had to sell the animal. The cow was bewitched.
199658: A man coming back from the café saw a lantern swinging in a corner of the wood. The next moment the witch stood beside him, saying: "You're out late too, eh!"
199662: A farmer had a foal that would not drink milk from the mare. The farmer had the witch master from Hasselt come. After the man had been with the foal for a while, the animal was willing to suckle.
199677: In Kuttekoven a roofer was working on a thatched roof. When the man went home one evening, a cat jumped onto the road in front of him. The man played with the cat as he walked on. After a while a second cat appeared, then a third and a fourth, and so on. When one of the cats began getting under his feet, the man struck at the animal. At that moment the man was attacked and beaten from all sides, although there was no one to be seen anywhere. The man was found half dead. A few days later he died of his injuries.
199679: Every night at about the same time a man saw his dead father appear.
199686: In the evening something strange wandered around the wheelbarrow, so that the dog was terrified and did not dare jump off the wheelbarrow.
199688: A man cycling home from the fair in Soerendonk suddenly heard music in the beet field. Yet there was nothing to be seen anywhere. The man was so frightened that he rode home quickly.
199697: A man coming home in the dark was jumped by a werewolf. When the man stabbed at the werewolf with pins, the werewolf took on his human form and threatened the man. The man never dared to betray the werewolf.
199700: Trien B. could conjure up rats and mice and make livestock die. At 'Hulstbosch', a farm in Bocholt, one cow died after another. Trien could only die after she had passed her arts on to her daughter through the keyhole.
199705: A farmer who had to fetch the ground flour from the miller at midnight suddenly could go no further. Whatever he did, the wheelbarrow would not move. When the man told his neighbour what had happened, the neighbour laughed at him. Some time later the neighbour went to fetch a tub with his wheelbarrow. At that same spot the wheelbarrow was pushed off the road by a strange force.
199714: In Rijkel (Zepperen) lived a man who was said to be able to turn himself into a werewolf. Because the man owned many books and was the only one who could read, people took him for a sorcerer. When someone was accompanying the man, he said: "Now I must change into a wolf. But let me bite your handkerchief, and I will become human again."
199715: Herme W. had put a piece of an Easter candle on his gun so that he could shoot at a witch's animal. The next day cross-eyed Jen lay in bed. She had lost an eye.
199727: A little child always began to cry at midnight because music and cats' wailing could be heard outside. One night the father went outside with his gun. He saw a whole pack of cats sitting there and shot at a big black one. But the man's gun did not work. Then the man heard someone laughing. After the man had sprinkled his gun with holy water, it worked again. The following night the man struck at one of the cats with an axe. The next day a woman was walking about with a bandage on her leg.
199729: A werewolf roamed the highway in Overrepen. The beast had itself carried by passers-by, who were given precise directions about where they had to go. When the werewolf reached its destination, it left its victim alone.
199731: A man sitting beside his house saw an old woman in a velvet gown walk past. When the woman had passed, she was followed by a foal and a horse.
199732: In the Rikboswei people always saw a man whose plough was pulled by two glowing horses. When they went to look in the morning, there was nothing strange to be seen.
199742: A man poaching with a lamp shot at a hare that had come to sit close to him. Because the hare had fled at the shot, the man went looking for it. Instead of the hare, the man saw a beautiful foal in the moonlight.
199751: Some boys and girls had been to the fair in Tongeren. One of the boys, together with his friend, took his girlfriend home, because she lived in Ketsingen and still had to milk the cows. Because the girl's parents kept an inn, the boys did not go home until one or two in the morning. But the two friends got lost. When they saw a strange light coming towards them on the way, the boys were scared to death. The following Thursday one of the boys met the woman from the inn at the cattle market, who said with a grin: "You saw something on the way, didn't you!" That woman was a witch.
199766: When the old butcher came into the Bjilmen with his cart, he saw countless will-o'-the-wisps. They were the souls of unbaptised children.
199783: A man drove with horse and cart via Paal to Schoten. At Clet G.'s place the man drove into the brook. Fifteen people tried to pull the team out of the brook, but it would not work. When Clet G. was called, the cart could be pulled out of the brook effortlessly.
199795: In the evenings strange creatures roamed about in Rijkel. They were very large ghosts with a little light on their heads. They followed people and made a lot of noise.
199800: A tailor walking home in the evening met a werewolf on the way. But the man was not afraid and wounded the werewolf with his ruler until the beast bled. He never saw the werewolf again after that.
199817: Some people keeping vigil beside a dead woman suddenly heard the body breathing. That must have been a spirit.
199827: If one had seen a black raven or magpie, one would have bad luck. If one saw two, a wedding would take place.
199836: A man returning from Genendijk around eleven or twelve at night with his flail on his shoulders met a cat and said: "Puss, you're out so late." The cat replied: "Yes, Janneke V.G., if you had not spoken to me so kindly, I would have broken your neck."
199850: A man who was going to Donk was surrounded along the way by cats that ran between his legs. When the man arrived in Donk, all the cats had suddenly disappeared.
199851: On the road to Membruggen there are two wide ditches on either side of the street. One day Free was walking along that road with a friend when he saw a witch sitting there, combing her hair. The two men crept on along the ditch so that the witch would not see them. When the two had to go home again in the evening, one of them said: "I'll wait until early tomorrow, because I'm afraid." So that evening Free went home alone. The witch was still sitting in the same place combing her hair. To be on the safe side, Free jumped into the meadow beside the road. But the man was almost literally wetting himself with fear, so he quickly sat down behind a tree. As Free sat there, the witch suddenly jumped on his back. Free had to carry the witch until he was almost home. Once he got home, the sweat of fear was dripping down his back.
199861: When Freke was playing cards, he had the jack of spades from the deck fetch a bottle of gin. When there was a knock, nobody dared to take the bottle. So Freke went outside himself. He came back in as pale as death.
199871: A man coming back from the shop was followed by a black cat that bit him in the leg. The man then cried: "Ugly witch, why do you have to bite me?" After a few days the wound began to fester. Because the doctor did not know what to do, the man went to the priest. After the priest had sprinkled the wound with holy water, the man's leg healed completely.
199877: A man kicked at a cat that had crept out of a hedge and kept walking between his legs the whole time.
199883: The rural policeman of Koninksem was often startled by a jingling he heard in a meadow in Tongeren. It was cows wearing chains.
199913: In Heurne-Sint-Pieter a boy was bewitched. The witch also had the animals in the stable in her power, for the cows sometimes rolled their eyes very strangely. The boy's parents sent for a blind fortune teller, whom they brought to their house in a wheelbarrow. The fortune teller said: "Shall I show you the witch in a bucket of water?" But the father did not want that; if he knew who had done his son all that harm, he would be capable of murdering the witch. A short time later the boy died. Afterwards the witch's howling could be heard in the chimney.
199917: A man working between Neeroeteren and Maaseik saw a cross standing at the spot where someone had once been murdered. When the man passed that spot, he felt something walk past him. In the evening the man told the people he was lodging with what had happened to him. They replied: "Something does indeed come there, but you need not be afraid, because it does no harm."
199931: A man who always shot down the main bird at the darts game was astonished when a woman told him: "By Sunday your luck will turn. Then you won't win any more!" And so it happened.
199933: The devil had crept into the Dalemolen in Lauw. The miller fetched the priest, but he could not drive the devil out. Finally they threw the devil into the Jeker, but because he stopped the mill wheel there, they had to take him out again. Some time later a young priest came, to whom the devil said: "You aren't without sin yourself. You used to steal lots of rolls from the baker!" The priest replied: "Yes, but I paid for those rolls three times over afterwards! And now you must leave!" The next moment the devil had vanished.
199957: A man got stuck in the mud with his horse and cart. He was about to unload all the goods from the cart when a woman passed by and said: "Now it will work." The next moment the horse pulled the cart out of the mud without any trouble.
199963: A man pushing his wheelbarrow through a wood in Diepenbeek got a fright when a cat was suddenly sitting on the wheelbarrow. A little later the wheelbarrow was full of cats, so that the man could hardly push it any further.
199976: A man who went to fetch branches in the meadows in the evening was followed by a large growling dog. When the man passed the little chapel at the crossroads, the dog could go no further.
199992: M. could not make butter because a witch lived in the neighbourhood.
200000: A girl was allowed to buy a new coat to wear when she went along to the Allerheiligenberg in November. When the shop assistant's mother saw the girl, she cried: "Oh God, a new coat!" and patted the girl on the shoulder. In the evening, going to bed, the girl kept seeing the witch standing before her. She told her father, who said: "I'll go outside with my dung fork. The first cat I see, I'll stab to death!" When the girl came back to that shop a while later, the shop assistant's mother did not dare to show herself!
200006: Some people were sitting outside when they suddenly saw a woman in a black silk dress walking by. One of them asked the black lady if he could go with her. The lady held out her hand and said: "Come along as far as over there; then you will never again ask to go with me." Then no one dared to go with her.
200011: On the Hemelsveld in Alken worked a farmhand who did nothing all day. He claimed that the crows did the work for him. One day the farmer had seen that the boy had a skin for roaming about as a werewolf. When the farmhand was away, the farmer threw the skin into the fire. Immediately the farmhand was standing beside him and began to scream: "My skin, my skin!" Some men held the boy, who was foaming at the mouth, tightly. When the skin had burnt up, the boy fell down dead.
200021: It was often said of old women that they were witches.
200041: In the evenings a black cat always sat on the steps of the churchyard. One evening a man was attacked by the cat. The man was convinced that the cat was a dead person who had come back to haunt.
200069: A man who had gone to see the play 'Kaïn' in Eigenbilzen went home through the snow by moonlight. After a while the man got lost. He thought of asking the way at a little house covered with leaves. But the man changed his mind because people said a witch lived in that house. When the man went on, a strong wind suddenly began to blow. The man did not get home until the next morning.
200081: On Christmas night the lord of the castle of Rouvenne went to rob the sacred vessels from the abbey of Sint-Jansberg. At twelve o'clock the castle sank into the ground with a great noise. Where the castle had stood there was a large mud pool. Every year on Christmas night the castle rose from the water and the bells in its tower could be heard ringing.
200084: On the Weerd between Uikhoven and Daaluikhoven stood pollard willows where someone came to haunt in the evening.
