200089: The count of Mechelen had died shortly after buying land at a ridiculously low price. After his death the count always came haunting in autumn. The castle gate would then open by itself and a black rider drove around the castle grounds in a large coach with six horses.
200090: In Aalst people claimed that black cats were witches.
200100: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised and therefore found no rest. The lights appeared by the water because they wanted to be baptised.
200103: Two men returning from Hasselt between midnight and one o'clock saw a dog come out of the hedge. When one of the lads went back to the same spot the next day, strangely enough he saw no tracks on the ground.
200116: Next to a café in Hoeselt lay beams that people used to defend themselves against ghosts. A man coming back from the café was followed at the chapel by a small white dog. After the man made the sign of the cross, the animal suddenly vanished.
200120: After a witch had stood beside a child's bed, the child was full of lice.
200142: When a witch could not work her power on a stranger, she harmed her own child. It was said that a witch's daughter had died on the day of her Solemn Communion.
200145: Some boys went to visit a girl who lived with her grandmother. The boy who had sat next to the girl could only get off his chair after a quarter of an hour and was drenched in sweat.
200159: A werewolf who lost his band was powerless. A boy whose collar had been found knew instinctively that someone was trying to burn the band. Furious, the boy ran to the oven to save his collar.
200171:
The bokkenrijders (goat riders) of Wellen were robbers who dealt with evil and worshipped a goat, hence their name. The bokkenrijders sat on a barrel and then said: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Heers." One day a man had spied on the bokkenrijders. When they were gone, the man said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Heers." The man arrived in Heers covered in blood.
When the bokkenrijders went somewhere, they rode horses shod back to front, so that people did not know in which direction they had ridden.
In the end the bokkenrijders were all burned in the Bonderkuil in Wellen.
200195: When Manen was going from Opoeteren to Opglabbeek one evening, he was jumped by a werewolf. When the man cut the werewolf in the place where he had been baptised, he changed into a human. The werewolf was very grateful to Manen because he had been set free.
200204: A boy who often went to play at Sofie V.D.M.'s house was advised by his grandfather never to answer "yes" three times in a row to questions Sofie asked. The grandfather believed that Sofie was a witch.
200205: In the D. family on the Hondsberg there was a child that cried incessantly. The child's grandmother went with her sister to the parish priest of Offelken. The priest advised them to burn the mattress of the cradle, with the following warning: "While you are burning the mattress, a woman will come by and ask what you are doing. That woman is the witch, but you must not do anything to her." They burned the mattress in the ditch next to Suske's meadow. In the mattress they found wreaths, little crowns, bits of fur and stuffed birds sewn together. Gillis M., a policeman from Ordingen who was related to the child, had said: "I'll take my gun and shoot the witch dead!" On the priest's advice, Gillis M. was prevented from killing the witch.
200207: In the old days a werewolf often jumped onto the necks of passers-by and had itself carried.
200230: Moen's father was out poaching and shot at two hares. The two animals, however, stood close together, sneezed once and laughed at the poacher. The man was terrified and quickly made himself scarce.
200231: A man returning from Wijchmaal saw a strange apparition at a crossroads that had nothing human about it. The man was terrified when the beast kept following him and stood up on its hind legs in front of him. So the man hurried along the lane past B.
200233: In Tiewinkel, a hamlet of Lummen, there stood a tree. When people pulled at its branches, it cried: "Ow, ow, ow, release my soul!" It was a dead person who had returned.
200235: Two lovers sat on a bench talking about the future and their wedding plans. When the girl came home, her mother asked: "Are you getting married?" Yet neither the boy nor the girl had told anyone about the wedding plans. While the couple sat on the bench, however, they had seen a toad sitting nearby.
200241: A werewolf was a dead person who had to come back in the form of an animal as punishment. A werewolf could only become human again if someone made him bleed.
200248: A woman coming back in the evening from a visit to her sister was followed by a black cat that walked between her legs. Because the woman was afraid of the animal, she hurried home.
200255: At the brook between Opitter and Tongerlo people always had to carry the werewolf. Yet whoever searched for the werewolf never found him.
200266: In Koersel a little child could no longer walk after a strange woman had shaken its hand. The friars advised the people to pray a novena and to keep the child away from other people. After that the child gradually recovered.
200281: The Freemasons held meetings in the Spinveld castle in Metsteren. The men of the D. family were the most important members of the Freemasons. The wife of a man from the lodge threatened divorce if her husband would not leave the Freemasons. One day the woman went to the castle herself. D. gave her a knife and showed her the wall on which the Freemasons had written their names in blood. In a rage the woman stuck the knife into the wall where her husband had signed. When she came home, she found her husband with a knife in his chest; she had stabbed him to death herself.
200282: On Christmas night bells could be heard ringing in the pond at midnight. A woman would then appear who gave the key to a hidden treasure chest to the person who dared to speak to her.
200324: Bet worked as a maid on a farm. One day when Bet was baking bread, the farmer's wife saw Bet go rigid with a staring look in her eyes, as if she were dead. A little later a bee flew into her mouth, whereupon Bet said: "Oh, how tired I am today!" Bet was a witch, for wherever she went the cows died and people lost their hair.
200331: In Maasmechelen there was a house where a witch named Antrien lived. Although the thatched roof of the house had no support at all, it did not cave in. When the house was demolished, it was discovered that the roof was held in balance by a goat's testicles hidden in the straw.
200339: A man who was out poaching with a friend was nearly frightened to death when an owl came and sat on the barrel of his gun. That owl must have been a witch.
200357: Witches could change into a cat. If one struck that cat, one could recognise the witch by her injuries.
200368: A Russian came to haunt a street in Herderen. The parish priest had reassured a frightened passer-by and advised him to pray an Our Father.
200387: A man who did not believe in ghosts pulled a sheet over himself to frighten people. When some people came by, the man heard them say: "Look, there are two ghosts sitting there!" Because the man did not understand why they were talking about two ghosts, he looked behind him and saw a second ghost sitting there. At that the man ran after the frightened passers-by, followed by the second ghost.
200389: A man who had gone to buy coal in Liège suddenly could go no further in Tongeren. The witch who lived there had made the man's cart stand still.
200390: A girl made mice in the church of Zepperen by throwing her clog on the floor. The priest baptised the girl again.
200407: A man and a woman had murdered their child and then eaten it. After that crime the murdered child came to haunt the attic, saying: "My mother beat me and my mother ate me."
200409: When Mil N. had gone to fetch grain, he met a little woman who warned him: "Watch out, the witch is coming! Keep your thumbs tucked in your fists!" The wagon of grain tipped over all the same.
200428: A woman from Rijkel had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, a witch's curse). Whenever the doctor came by, nothing was wrong. But as soon as he left, the woman was paralysed again.
200429: After a boy had been hanged in Velm, a light always appeared on the roof. That will-o'-the-wisp was the boy's soul.
200453: The wild hunt was the howling of witches' cats flying through the air.
200459: In an old house, every evening at about the same time, the lid of a salt chest opened and closed. Because the residents were afraid, one day they asked: "If something must be done for someone, let us know. Should we perhaps go to Scherpenheuvel?" At that moment the lid of the chest stopped moving. After the people had walked to Scherpenheuvel, the house was no longer haunted.
200462: Some men from Zonhoven returning in the evening from visiting a friend in Koersel always met cats on the way. One evening one of the men hit a cat with a cudgel. The next day a woman lay in bed with a broken arm.
200476: The Hobos was haunted. A man who stayed the night there was startled when at one o'clock all the windows and doors flew open. That had been the spirit of the drossaard (bailiff). The ghost was banished to the bridge between Eksel and Overpelt.
200477: A man whose son was ill went with his child to a healer. The healer predicted that a woman from the neighbourhood would bring a pear and advised them not to eat it. The man did as advised and buried the pear. The next day the witch knew exactly where the pear was buried.
200481: A man who went hunting in the snow spent the whole day chasing a rabbit that he just could not catch. When the man walked home at sunset, his wife came to meet him with the words: "Now you've been walking around all day, and you still have nothing!" Aldegonda H., a little woman from the neighbourhood, had already told the wife that her husband had caught nothing on the hunt. Perhaps the rabbit had been Aldegonda herself.
200485: A ghost wandered about at the T. family's home in Diepenbeek, throwing the animals into the manger. The friars advised the people to go on pilgrimage for the ghost. When they set off, they had to put a walking stick by the door and let the ghost go ahead.
200499: A young man walking home with a girl was followed by a meowing cat. The lad had often kicked at the animal in vain. At the bridge over the Stiemer the animal vanished.
200501: The Freemasons often met at night in Liège. The meeting took place in a large mansion on the hill near the Place Saint-Lambert. The Freemasons signed an agreement with the devil in blood in exchange for money. Over time the name on that agreement was erased letter by letter. When the name had completely disappeared, one had to commit suicide. Thus the father of a certain Marken had hanged himself in his summer house, where a lawyer from Tongeren found him.
200537: A woman who had lain ill in bed for two years could not be helped by any doctor. At midnight the woman would begin to sweat heavily and felt as if two people were sitting on her. One Saturday night a big grey cat came into the house. However people tried to chase the animal away, the cat would not leave the house. On Sunday evening as many as fifty cats sat in the attic making music. The husband loaded his gun and went up to the attic to shoot the cats. But the man did not hit a single cat. Because the cats were there again the next day, the man went to the Brown Friars of Hasselt. The friars said to the man: "That cannot be. A woman with two baskets sometimes comes past your house. You must let that woman go on her way. I will give you a relic to put under the threshold and one to give to your wife." From then on the woman with the baskets no longer came in. She stayed standing at the threshold. One day the witch asked the man of the house: "Louis, why may I not come in any more?", to which the man replied: "You needn't come complaining to me. It is the Holy Little Father who has forbidden you." From then on no more cats came into the house either. The wife recovered and lived another 47 years.
200544: A boy who had walked his girlfriend home went on alone. When he passed the house of a witch, such a strong wind suddenly rose that his cap blew away. In the morning the boy woke up next to the pen where the witch's calves were kept.
200555: In the old days many witches appeared in Diets-Heur in the form of birds. Those birds often made people wander around the fields all night.
200561: A werewolf who was in Maastricht came back quickly because he felt that someone had thrown his collar into the oven.
200585: A tailor who claimed not to be afraid of the dead went to keep watch over the body of a man who had died in the village. Because time passed only slowly, the tailor began to sing. Suddenly the dead man said: "When one keeps a wake, one does not sing!" The tailor answered: "And when one is dead, one does not speak!"
200589: At the bend towards Colmont the carter's horses always stopped, because Heksebetje lived there. A man from Zepperen was warned by the carter: "You won't get past that spot!" The stubborn man set off with his horse and cart anyway. At the bend towards Colmont the cart did indeed stop. The man then stabbed the axle of the wheel with a knife, after which he heard the witch screaming with pain in her house. Since then the witch has not stopped a single cart.
200600: Between Voort and the Buiting in Gessel there was a double hedge with a path between. When people walked along that path, they were followed by a ghost.
200603: Beggar women were often suspected of being witches in the past. People who were bewitched usually went on pilgrimage. Many went to the friars of Rekem. The friar would then say a short prayer and sprinkle the visitor with holy water.
200609: On the road from Beverst to Hasselt a mail coach had lost money. Because the finder had not returned the money, people heard a voice at night calling: "Give it back, give it back!"
200630: When some men were driving a wagon of straw from Monnikenhof to Vechmaal, a witch made the cart tip over.
200633: In Pedonk (Borgloon) there once lived a witch called Mie L. A child had fallen ill after being bewitched by Mie L. After the parish priest had read prayers over the child, the witch no longer had any power.
200636: In Mielen will-o'-the-wisps appeared at night. Because it was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the dead, nobody dared go near.
200653:
Old Henkes had nearly finished mowing his field. The man decided to keep working a little longer, when suddenly a meowing cat was standing beside him. Because the cat annoyed him, the man struck at the animal. The next moment there were as many as twenty-five cats in the field.
Since the Gospel of Saint John, such evil fortunately no longer exists.
200668: At the village policeman's house in Schulen, two cats were always fighting in the attic. One night the policeman broke a cat's leg with his sabre. The next day one of the neighbour women had lost an arm.
200681: After his death the drossaard (bailiff) came every night at twelve o'clock to throw the windows open. Eventually the ghost was loaded onto a cart with a shovelful of earth, but they did not manage to take it away.
200684: A newborn child from Wijer did not grow because it was bewitched. The parents prayed a lot and went on pilgrimage to the friars. When they cut open the child's pillow, they found a wreath that was not yet closed.
200690: A woman visited a family where a newborn baby lay in the cradle. After the woman had stroked the child's head, it began to cry. The parents took the child to the Heilig Paterke (Holy Little Father) in Hasselt to have prayers read over it. But the friar said: "You have come too late, it is the kwade hand (evil hand, a witch's curse)". In the end the child died. Every time that witch had been in the stables, one of the animals died.
200698: A man who was out hunting hares asked a woman: "Do you happen to know where any hares are?", to which the woman answered: "Yes, there's one there." The man then ran after the hare. At that moment the woman called out: "Run away quickly, mother, or they'll catch you!"
200707: In Mechelen - Bovelingen noise was always heard in the castle at night. The gate opened by itself when the dead count came driving up in a coach with four horses.
200708: Will-o'-the-wisps were small white flames that appeared above marshes and dirty water. The lights were the souls of unbaptised children who wanted to be released. At the bottom of the marsh lay an oak chest containing a treasure. If someone dared to bring up the chest and give the money to a monastery, the souls would be saved.
200725: In Leut a witch had infested a little child with lice.
200760: During the night that a witch from Herk-de-Stad died, the roof of the house was full of black crows. Because the witch's daughter was later always seen with a black cat on her lap, people suspected that she had taken over her mother's arts.
200765: A boy who was in a relationship with a witch did not want to walk his girlfriend home. "Then you'll have to wait here until I'm home", said the girl. The boy could not move until he heard the door of the house slam shut.
200771: While War G. had gone to Maastricht, someone had found his collar. As soon as the band was thrown into the fire, War was standing next to the oven to save his possession. And this while War's horse was still in Maastricht.
200794: A family from Weert had moved to Molenbeersel and had a large orchard there. But every first Sunday of the month a strong wind rose in the afternoon and blew all the fruit off the trees. The people became so poor that they had to move again.
200796: At the L. family's house in Bilzen, people heard noise at around half past twelve at night. There was a heifer standing in front of the door. After a man had hit the heifer on the head with a hammer, his best friend stood before him.
200801: A vagrant came to a castle where a parrot sat on the door, saying: "Go away, go away, neither hell nor devil passes here." Although the vagrant was a little afraid, he decided to spend the night in the castle anyway. At midnight a man with a long white beard came in, sat down on a chair and took out a razor. After the vagrant had shaved the ghost's beard, the spirit was released. The man with the grey beard had to haunt because during his life he had murdered many women. The released ghost said to the vagrant: "All this is for you, but you must have that well full of blood filled in."
200806: The witch Tonia V.D.S. often used to visit people for a chat. One had to be careful then not to say "yes" to the witch three times in a row. Otherwise she would get that person in her power.
200827: Bertina had a little child that cried constantly whenever it lay in its cradle. When she picked it up, it fell silent and could sleep peacefully. The child's parents went to a clergyman, who said the child was bewitched. The parish priest read prayers over the child, but that did not help. A certain Antonie advised the parents to cut open the child's pillow. At first Bertina thought this advice was nonsense, but after a while she did let her husband open the pillow. Inside they found feathers and the head of a bird. When they threw it all into the fire, it would not burn, not even with petroleum. Once they had sprinkled everything with holy water, it did burn. Antonie had said the parents would find out who the witch was. The parents immediately thought of the late Betje, but it was not her. In the house where the child lived, a candle burned for several days. During that time it was noticed that the aunt of de Witte, a woman who always came to fetch eggs, no longer came by. When the candle had burned out, the woman came again. Since then the parents always kept a candle burning, so that the woman no longer came. The parents told everything to the parish priest, who said: "Evil exists, but one must not speak of it. With the Gospel of Saint John the power of evil was born."
200831: A man who suffered from back pain could not be helped by any doctor. He had got the pain when an old woman had poked him in the back with a straw. The friars of Rekem said at once: "You have been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, a witch's curse)". The man then had a friar read prayers over him. The friar kept praying until the sweat dripped from his face, blessed the man three times with holy water and then said: "If the pain still does not go away, you must come back again". After a few visits to the friar the man had hardly any pain left. When the man stopped going to the friars, the pain grew worse and worse until the man finally died.
200842: A woman got a stiff leg after she had been touched by a witch.
200848: Overpelt was badly haunted. In a certain street people always saw a 'wolzak' (wool sack) moving.
200849: One night Pier-Jentje from Geisteren went poaching. When he saw a hare and wanted to shoot it, however, his gun would not fire. A second and a third attempt also failed.
200861: A werewolf was a man who owned two collars. One of those bands could be burnt. If that happened, the werewolf was released.
200867: A child was bewitched after accepting a sweet from a witch. The child could no longer sleep because there was a wreath of feathers in its pillow. After the parish priest H. had blessed the child and placed a little cross under the doormat, the witch could no longer come in. At that moment the wreath disappeared from the pillow.
200870: A man was surrounded by a pack of cats that blocked his way. When the man began to pray, the cats ran off.
200872:
A man from the K. family always had to carry the werewolf. The man would then shout: "He's got me again!" Because the werewolf squeezed the man's shoulders so hard, the cigars the man carried in his waistcoat were always squashed flat. Although the man made a great fuss, other people did not see the werewolf. One day A., the miller of the K. family, went to the police to ask permission to carry a revolver. But A. was not granted a licence.
It was said that a werewolf turned back into a human when you could make him bleed.
200911: A spider was in essence an evil spirit. If two threads in a spider's web formed a cross, one would have bad luck.
200927: Jan S. could change himself into a werewolf. He was also married to a witch. When people came back from Mass on the first of May, they saw a dog running over the hill. A little later the dog changed into Jan S., who asked whether he was already too late for High Mass. A bit further on, Jan changed into a werewolf again.
200936: The Klitsberg in Paal was haunted. When someone rode past there on horseback, the horse was always stopped by a strange apparition.
200959: All the horses fell ill after eating flour ground in the mill of Lauw. The devil was in that mill.
200962: Some men playing cards with a stranger saw that the stranger had horse's feet.
200989: Trui V.W. did not want her husband to build a barn behind their farm. She told everyone that the barn would never be finished. When the barn was almost finished, it collapsed one night for an inexplicable reason.
201001: Three men and three women were coming back from the fair in Rutten at about half past eleven at night. A cat sat meowing beside the ditch. The men kicked at the cat, but they did not manage to hit the animal. Further on they could still hear the cat meowing. Then one of the men said: "Shall we call the cat to see whether it comes back?" As soon as they had called the cat, the animal was sitting beside the ditch again. When the company went past a crossroads, the cat could go no further.
201002: Suske M. was a poacher. One night when he was out poaching, he suddenly saw a hare playing in the beam of his lamp. Suske loaded his gun and shot at the hare. But the animal took a run-up and jumped over Suske's head into the corn. A little later three hares came, and Suske tried to shoot at them too. But those hares also jumped over Suske. A few moments later dozens of hares came running up. Suske wanted to try his luck one more time and shot. After that Suske did not know what was happening to him: all those hares began jumping back and forth over him. His courage failed him, he threw away his gun and ran home as fast as he could. The next day Suske only dared to go and look once it was light. His gun still lay where he had thrown it down, but otherwise there was nothing unusual to be seen. Suske had expected the corn to be completely flattened by all those hares, but there was no sign of that at all.
201006: Two men going from Wijchmaal to Eksel around midnight heard a pack of mewing cats in the distance. But the men could not find the cats and got lost.
201007: Eufrasie M. was a Walloon woman who lived with a clergyman in the house of P. After Eufrasie had died, she came back to haunt the house in the shape of a white lady. The house was sold for eight thousand BEF to a couple with children. Before they moved into the house, the buyers went there for a few evenings to play cards, to see whether a ghost really roamed about.
201013: Three men had been visiting their brother, a curate in 's Heerenelderen. On the way back one of them fell behind because he wanted to squat behind a tree to relieve himself. While the man was sitting there, he saw a woman pass by, dressed in a black dress that rustled in the wind. When the man had caught up with his brothers, he told them what he had seen. The brothers had not seen the woman, although she must have walked past them.
201015: If people could not make butter, they sent for a heksenman (witch doctor).
201020: A newborn child that cried all the time could not be helped by a nurse. The child's parents were advised to go to the parish priest. Because the priest was ill at the time, they went to the chaplain. The chaplain took his book and began to pray at the three corners of the house. After that the child was cured. The witch's husband could not get along with his wife either. One day he said: "I'm going to jump in the well", and he threw a piece of wood into the well and hid. When the witch heard the splash, she ran outside wailing.
201025: A man from Piringen was followed in 'Sha-bos' by a large dog that would not go away. As soon as the man came out of the woods, the dog had disappeared. The man firmly believed that the dog had been a werewolf.
201026: To know whether a woman was a witch, one had to place one's feet crossed in her footprint. The witch would then have to look round before she had gone ten steps further.
201035: On a farm there worked a farmhand who went about at night as a sheep. The sheep untied the livestock and jumped onto the backs of both people and animals. The farmer and his wife had long suspected that something was wrong with the boy. Their suspicion was confirmed when they found his skin in the barn. When they had thrown the skin into the oven, the boy suddenly stood beside them. The boy was held by seven men so that he would not get hold of his skin again. When the skin had burned up, the farmhand said: "Let me go now; I'm rid of it. Now I am happy."
201038: Three friends from Wimmertingen often went to Diepenbeek to fight. One Sunday the three were, as usual, at the café 'Het Planken weike'. When by midnight the men still had not had the chance to fight, one of them said: "I must get a fight in today, even if it's with the devil!" A little further on, a creature suddenly jumped onto that man's back. Because the creature riding on him grew heavier and heavier, the man said in annoyance: "If you don't leave soon, I'll teach you a lesson. Whether you're a dog or a devil, I'll attack you!" But the creature would not go away and became so heavy that the man fell to the ground. When the man realised the creature was probably the devil, he said: "Let me go, devil. What could you do with me anyway?" Because his words had no effect, he began to pray until the sweat dripped from his face. Then the strange apparition jumped off his back. But the creature followed the man all the way through the Tomveld and through Mattes meadow. When he got home the man said: "Now you won't follow me any longer! If you dare come in, I'll give you a good thrashing!" Then the creature attacked the man. When the fight was in full swing, the man's father came outside and said: "What's going on here? You've probably brought this on yourself again! That'll teach you!" But the son kept shouting: "Dad, come and help me!" When the father came outside, he saw an ugly creature sitting in the ditch. After the man had stabbed at the creature in vain with a dung fork, he gave up. Father and son kept praying until the creature crawled out of the ditch. That night nobody in the house slept a wink. The next morning a black imprint of the creature was burnt into the door.
201044: A man who wanted his barn finished in time had made a pact with the devil. The man would have to give up his soul if the devil managed to build a barn before the cock began to crow in the morning. Because the man had grown afraid, at half past two he slapped his buttocks until the cock began to crow. Since the barn was not yet finished then, the man was allowed to keep his soul.
201064: On the Houbrug in Hoesselt sat a black cat that attacked passers-by after midnight.
201091: The Kôanket was a kind of witch who made people get lost in the fields. In the end the witch was banished to Monnikenhof.
201099: In Brustem lived a little woman who peddled umbrellas. She could change herself into a cat and jump into her house through the window.
201104: On the Egelsberg opposite the Sint-Jansberg in Maaseik stood the castle of Zilverkruus. In that castle there once lived a baron who had sold his soul to the devil. One day the castle sank and the baron in his horse-drawn coach also sank into the pond. On Christmas night the castle bells could be heard ringing and the baron could be seen wandering on the pond.
201110: A man returning from the field with horse and cart suddenly heard music that seemed to come from the corn. The frightened man drove home. When his household went to look, there was no more music to be heard.
201112: Because it was raining on the day of the procession, the statue of Mary had not been taken along. The next day the statue was strangely covered in a layer of mud. On the steps were small footprints of the statue's little shoes. The statue of Mary had gone out alone during the night.
201123: It was said that witches flew through the air on a broomstick.
201134: Seven people set off early in the morning by moonlight on a pilgrimage to Hechtel. On the way they met Trien B., who asked: "Pilgrimage?" The people walked on in silence. A while later the group got lost. When they began to pray on hearing the church bells of Bocholt, they found the way again. But two of them missed the tram in Reppel, so that only five of them could go to Hechtel.
201145: In Meershoven stood a little house where witches lived. The witches gathered there and went through the woods to Krundel. Witches could change themselves into cats.
201150: A woman going to church in Sint-Truiden was given this advice by her husband: "If you meet a werewolf, throw a handkerchief at its mouth." The woman did indeed meet a werewolf. It was her own husband.
201151: When Rikus V.H. went poaching, he shot twice at a hare in vain. With the third shot Rikus recited the Gospel of Saint John. The next day the man met a woman who said: "Well, my lad, you shot out one of my eyes! I'll make you pay for that!"
201155: A man from 's Heerenelderen returning from an inn in Mal in the evening was followed by a woman in a black satin dress. The woman jumped into his arms but did not answer when the man asked her anything. Suddenly the woman was gone.
201156: Witches in the shape of cats always came into a farmhouse through the drain hole. One day the farmer struck with his axe at a fat cat that had got stuck in the hole. Then it was known who the witch was.
201166: Near Knijnjan people often saw burning coaches driving.
201169: A man broke his arm the day after he had met Metsje van Millen.
201172: When Teuneke was out hunting, he shot at a few hares. The next moment, however, there were many more hares. After the man had laid devil's herb on his gun, he did manage to hit the hares.
201183: When a man was coming home from the fair around midnight, he suddenly heard noise underground at the 'duvelskot' (devil's hole). He put his ear to the ground and heard the bell of the chapel of Averbode ringing. That chapel had once sunk into that marsh.
201186: An old man with a grey beard came to haunt the woods of Rodenpoel.
201202: A man from Munsterbilzen saw a will-o'-the-wisp come out of the ground and then slowly fly upwards. As soon as the light reached the tops of the pine trees, it went out. It was the soul of an unbaptised child.
201217: In Wijshagen looters had taken the bell from the church tower. When the thieves came outside, the bell sank into the ground. After that the bell could be heard ringing twelve times every year on Christmas night.
201221: A man whose horse could no longer pull the load said to the witch of the Loêise Berg: "People believe you are a witch; see to it that this horse can go on". The next moment the horse could pull the load again.
201236: One morning a man was walking from the station of As to Niel. When the man saw a werewolf sitting in a hedge, he said to the beast: "Come here, I like you." The werewolf thought the man would carry him and came closer. But then the man hit the werewolf with his cudgel. He then forced the werewolf to come along to the inn, where it had to lie under the table and was kicked twice by every customer. That werewolf was never seen again.
201246: In the old days, if one had seen a raven on getting up, one would invariably have bad luck that day.
201260: Near the castle of Wideux lay an old oak that had been blown down. People said that the ghost of the countess came to sit on that oak. So the tree could not be removed.
201273: A man who met a cat in the evening said to the animal: "Puss, you're still out so late," whereupon the cat stood on its hind legs and replied: "Yes, Janneke V.G., if you had not spoken to me so kindly, I would have broken your neck!"
201278: Because her son was bewitched, a woman went to the brown friars to have prayers read over the child. A friar from Hasselt read the Gospel of Saint John over the child. Then the friar said: "Go home now. He will rest". When the woman had been churched after the birth, the neighbour wanted to see the child. From that day on the boy cried without stopping for fourteen days and fourteen nights. Because the doctor could not help, someone advised the woman to put a blessed statuette at her back door. Whenever the witch needed something after that, she tapped on the window and said: "Come outside!" Some time later the witch died in hospital at the age of eighty-three or eighty-four of a fractured thigh. After that the child no longer cried.
201285: In Opheers a witch on her deathbed suffered terrible pain. The parish priest had come to hear her confession, but he understood at once that the witch first had to pass on her art before she could die. To let her die, the priest said to the daughter: "You take over her art, and I will free you from it later." When the woman had been dead a few days, the priest went to see the girl and asked her: "Well, shall I take the witchcraft away from you now?", but the girl did not want to lose her powers, for she had already had far too much fun with them.
201286: A man passing the house of a witch was surrounded by cats that blocked his way. When the man went on, all the cats had suddenly disappeared.
201293: When Toon W. was coming back from a football match, he was bitten in the hand by a black cat. The wound would not heal and began to fester. In the end the man's forearm had to be amputated.
201295: The wizard Freke G. had a bottle of gin brought. "One of you must take the bottle," Freke had told his friends. But nobody dared to open the door. After there had been three knocks, the door flew open and Freke got the bottle of gin in his face.
201304: In a house where someone had just died, people heard a strange voice saying: "Carefully reckoned and little forgiven."
201330: A man walking through the meadows was nearly frightened to death when he was followed by a kitten that said: "Gisebert T. says I am a good little pussycat." The man had once stroked the kitten and said: "Hello, my good little pussycat."
201379: An old woman had asked a pilgrim to bring back a piece of the cross of Christ from Rome. When the old woman had received the piece of the cross, she always saw a big black dog. Supposing the dog was the devil, the woman took her relic to drive the dog away. Then she heard a voice say: "A good thought is worth a lot. Even if it is only a piece of hoof wood."
201381: At the gate in a meadow in Mal a foal used to haunt. Every time that happened, a violent storm rose as if all hell had broken loose.
201391: A woman from Groot-Loon came home in the evenings from her work in Bommershoven. Every evening she was accompanied by a ghost that threw earth in her face.
201408: A man going home in the evening saw a cat by the church that kept growing bigger and bigger until it was almost as big as a horse.
201415: In the Troefelstraat a priest came haunting with three altar boys.
201416: A man went to Liège with horse and cart. He had taken along a stick he had received from a witch. When at a certain moment the horse could go no further, the man threw the stick away. After that the horse could go on.
201425: On a farm in Nerem they could not make butter. Because the farmer was at his wits' end, he went to the bishop of Liège, who said: "You must have the priest come to the farm, because it is the evil hand that is causing all this trouble." After the priest had read prayers over the stables, the farmer had excellent butter within a quarter of an hour.
201433: On the Hekpad in Koersel there was something strange in the hazel hedge.
201446: A farmer's cows had fallen ill after being struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, a witch's curse). When the parish priest had blessed the stable, all the cows were suddenly cured.
201469: Some people were praying the rosary in a house when suddenly a little black dog came in. Because the dog walked around three times, the people believed that one of those present had a mortal sin on his conscience. Around ten o'clock a restless man left the house.
201474: One day Frans R. came to the little chapel in Russelt. He saw a headless nun, dressed entirely in black. When Frans came closer, the nun jumped over the hedge and vanished.
201476: A white cat was walking by the toll bar in the Waardestraat. When the cat came closer, the toll bar strangely opened by itself. In the evening a white lady wandered about near the toll bar.
201482: A man going to fetch hay with a cart and an ox visited a woman on the way, who said: "But lad, you won't get home". Indeed the ox would no longer pull the cart, so the man had to hitch the ox behind the cart and pull everything himself.
201488: A pig that had been struck by the kwade hand (evil hand, a witch's curse) would not eat and squealed all the time. After Stieniske had read something from a book, the pigs were cured.
201495: A man working in the afternoon suddenly saw a yellow light fly past at great speed, low to the ground. A moment later the light had vanished.
201500: A man from Rutten could not sleep at night because his dead sister came to haunt his room. The ghost said to the man: "You must pray for me, or I won't leave you in peace." From then on the man prayed a great deal, and so he could sleep.
201503: A brewer kept having bad luck with his farmhands: every so often a hand fell into the brewing kettle and was burned. The man was planning to close the brewery when suddenly a new hand arrived. The brewer told him what had happened to the other hands at night, but the new hand was not put off and was taken on. The following night he had to work in the brewery together with another hand. At a certain moment a small cat came walking into the brewery and the other hand said: "Now watch closely!" The little cat rubbed against the hands' legs with a strength as great as a person's. The new hand took a pitchfork and broke the cat's two front legs. The next morning the brewer's wife lay in bed with two broken arms. It was this witch who had pushed the other hands into the kettle at night. But this time it had failed.
201518: The castle of Dessener was terribly haunted. At night the doors and windows flew open and shut by themselves. The animals went wild and broke their chains. After a while everything in the castle returned to normal.
201543: A man coming back from work had to carry the werewolf. When the man was drenched in sweat, the werewolf left him alone. The next day there was no trace to be seen at the place where the werewolf had run off.
201549: If there was a witch nearby, the horse could not go on.
201554: Witches came in through the water drain in the shape of a dog or a cat.
201560: Two men walking in the 'Buts' suddenly saw a white lady appear. One of the men started talking to the lady and wanted to walk on arm in arm with her. But the lady said: "Let go what goes and stand what stands," and she vanished.
201564: A woman had prayers read over her child because it had been struck by the zwarte hand (black hand, a witch's curse).
201565: Two men from Mopertingen went to visit their girlfriends in Hoelbeek. After the men had tapped on the window, two cats appeared. The next moment the cats changed into girls.
201566: Between midnight and one o'clock the border between Budel and Hamont was haunted. A white figure then floated up and down.
201587: One day shopkeeper Leo went to the witch Bet van Pierke to sell some goods. When the witch offered Leo a glass of beer, he refused, saying: "No, give that to Pierre!" A week later Leo called on the witch again. But Bet found the goods too expensive and said: "Get out of here or I'll fill your head with rats!" Leo was barely outside before the rats were gnawing at his shoes. After that the shopkeeper no longer dared to enter the witch's house.
201612: One day Neel T. had caught a small white rabbit. He put the animal in his bag and went home. When Neel got home, his bag contained only a large cobblestone.
201619: When Free V.G. was playing cards, he had the jack of spades from the deck fetch a bottle of gin. But Free was the only one who dared to drink the gin. Pastor V. burned Free's books of magic.
201623: One day a black cat walked across a farmer's yard. The dog, which usually attacked all cats, ran away in fear. When the farmer saw the cat near the house of Nel M. a while later, he understood why the dog had been afraid: Nel M. was a witch, after all.
201625: At the devil's stone in the woods the heipastoor (heath priest) appeared at night. He was a very large black priest who silently walked past people.
201626: Peter K. lived in the Bergstraat in Zepperen. Farmer Peter had much bad luck, for his cows kept dying. Because he suspected witchcraft was involved, he sent for the friars. The friars read prayers over the stable for five hours and behind the planks they found a good hundred little bows of every colour. Earlier the farmer had also had a sick foal. When he led the animal down the street, it dropped dead in front of the witch's house. That same evening thirteen dogs ran one after another to the churchyard. That too must have been the witch's doing.
201627: If you were alone in the evening and saw a black cat in a tree, it was usually a witch.
201634: A man had seen some people kick a cat and chase it out of their house. A little later the cat had already come back in through the attic, although there was no door or window anywhere. The next moment the man saw the cat lying at his feet.
201644: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer breathe, so that they felt they would suffocate. After a while the mare went away again.
201646: On a farm on the Winner animals died every day. A friar had advised the people to give away their last cow. After that, however, the misfortune moved from the stable to the house. The son, the daughter and the father all three died shortly after one another. After that the misfortune finally stopped.
201656: A man playing cards with his friends said: "Whoever throws the jack of spades has to go and fetch a bottle of wine." When the friends claimed that was impossible, the man said: "If I throw the jack of spades, I promise that card will go and fetch a bottle of wine. When the card comes back, there will be a knock on the door, but I mustn't open it." When there was a knock, none of the friends dared to open the door. The man opened it himself and had to fight the devil. The devil burned his hand into the door.
201662: X's wife was suspected of being a witch. A man from Rotem was poaching in Treselt on a cold winter's day. The man shot at a hare but missed. Not ten minutes later X's wife stood before him with the words: "You ugly, filthy man, what are you doing here shooting at my cows!"
201664:
A farmer had three farmhands. Because one of them always went off somewhere after supper, the farmer decided to go to the parish priest. The priest suspected that the farmhand was a werewolf and wanted the farmer to spy on him. After a few days the farmer found the farmhand's collar. On the priest's advice, the farmer sent his farmhand away so that he could burn the collar in the meantime. When the band lay in the oven, the farmhand was immediately standing beside him to save his band. When everything had burnt up, the farmhand thanked his master for releasing him.
It was said that werewolves received their collar at a crossroads.
201666: A woman from Broekom was nearly frightened to death when she saw a ghost in a white sheet walking in the moonlight.
201674: One evening a shepherd was going with his two dogs from Maaseik to Stevenswaart (?). When the man saw a cat sitting on the embankment in Stokkem, he said: "What are you still doing here so late?" and struck at the animal with his stick. A few metres further on the man was surrounded by dozens of cats. What's more, his new smock was completely smeared with mud.
201677: Jo H. from Schoten was a witch. For Jo could make a pig dance around a broomstick.
201684: On a calm day a heivrouw (heath woman) suddenly flew high into the air. She kept spinning and spinning, and as soon as she fell to the ground, she turned into a little heap of sand.
201691: In Rijkhoven a fire-man had set a pollard willow on fire. The fire-man moved from one tree to the next and finally went off towards the waterfall.
201701: A woman whose mother often had a neighbour visiting had said many times: "Mother, I don't understand why you have anything to do with that witch!" One day the woman laid a broomstick across the doorway. The witch could not get over it. Then the woman said: "Now do you see, mother, that she is a witch!"
201713: An unbaptised boy from Jeuk could conjure mice out of a clod of earth. For that reason the boy was baptised again.
201715: In the churchyard a ghost with bells walked from one cross to another.
201739: A woman from Vucht had been given two apples by someone. A few hours later the woman saw that the apples had turned into frogs.
201744: A man from Opleeuw was walking home when he saw a black cat by the chapel. After the man had struck the cat three times, the animal said: "Do that again, Willy!" The cat turned out to be his best friend.
201764: A man staying in Germany received a telegram saying that his wife had given birth and that he had to come home. At the border post in Maastricht the man was nearly frightened to death when a werewolf suddenly stood in front of him. Because the werewolf did him no harm, the man still got home safely. When the man returned to Germany after a while, one of his friends said: "Door, I know where you were scared!" The man replied: "Damn it, you bastard, that was you!" The werewolf never ate with the other men in the evening, because he had to go out. In the morning they would find the bowl of soup half empty. While the werewolf was staying in Belgium for a while, the man's bearskin was found in Germany. As soon as the skin was thrown into the oven, the werewolf stood by the fire to save his skin. After everything had burnt up, the werewolf thanked his friends. The man then went to the friars to confess all his sins. He also gave the friars the little book he had received from the devil. It was very hard to get rid of such a magic book, because, for example, it could not be burnt.
201790: A witch could make her hens lay as many eggs as she wanted. Every time she stroked a hen over its back, an egg fell out.
201798: A cat had crept into a house through the drain hole. When the people were about to shoot the cat, it changed into a woman from the neighbourhood.
201802: A drunkard walking home in the evening was chased by a glowing gravestone.
201803: The old mayor of Neerglabbeek once had a relationship with a girl from Meeuwen. Although everyone warned the young man that the girl was a witch, the lovestruck youth visited his girlfriend as often as he could. When one day he walked from Meeuwen to Neerglabbeek, he was surrounded the whole time by dozens of magpies. On parting, his girlfriend had asked him whether he had never seen magpies on the way home. Since then the young man never went to see the girl again.
201817:
A girl cycling to the fair in Tongeren saw a flock of magpies in the meadow. Her father said it was a bad omen. That same evening the war broke out.
If someone died on a Sunday, another person in the same village would die within six weeks.
201821: A woman whose cow no longer gave milk sent for the parish priest. After the priest had read prayers over the animal, he said: "It was high time, little woman! Your neighbour is the cause of the evil". The clergyman gave the woman a medal so that the neighbour could no longer come in. Even so, the neighbour still had the nerve to come and ask for a cup of coffee regularly.
201823: A boy who had sold his soul to the devil was sitting in an inn with a friend. Because they had no money left, the boy went outside and stood at the northern boundary post of the village with his hands in the air. Every time he called on the devil, the boy got money. When the boy came back into the inn, someone said: "I don't know how you come by all that money; it must be from the devil..." When his contract with the devil came to an end, the boy had to commit suicide, but he did not want to. When the boy once again asked for money at the boundary post, the devil dashed him against the post. Later the dead boy was found there, completely charred black.
201827: On the Hobos, where the drossaard (bailiff) had lived, there were still many gallows on which innocent people had been hanged. The ghost of the drossaard had been banished to a bridge between Kerkhoven and 't Kamp. A girl walking over the bridge suddenly heard the sound of a horse, although there was nothing to be seen.
201832: Louis M. was cleaning the oven and decided to quickly fetch some sticks from the woods to make the work easier. Although it was broad daylight, the man lost his way. He had wandered so far off course that he had to walk for an hour before he was home again. The 'dolende man' (wandering man) had made him lose his way.
201833: A werewolf was a man who threw an animal skin over himself and jumped onto the backs of passers-by at night. After you had carried the werewolf for a while, you were left alone.
201844: At a spot in Val-Meer people always heard music. A married couple who wanted to see where the music came from never returned.
201852: When the priest turned round with the words "Dominus vobiscum", he saw all the witches in the church with a beehive on their heads. There were also other ways to recognise witches. A witch, for instance, always avoided coming across a cross on her path. If one placed one's feet crosswise in a witch's footprint, the witch would turn round.
201862: Some men guarded the laundry laid out to bleach at night with a gun. Suddenly something strange appeared near the laundry.
201883: A midwife saw a light coming towards her in the field. After the woman had baptised the light, she was suddenly surrounded by countless lights. Because the midwife could no longer move, she said: "I baptise you all together".
201887: At a farm a dead woman always came to haunt at midnight. She wanted to be released through prayer.
201890: An old witch who had lived with a veterinarian infested a man's underpants with lice.
201906: On damp summer days will-o'-the-wisps sometimes appeared in low-lying areas, moving back and forth. It was said that those lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
201908: Three men who wanted to play cards were sitting in the Wildeman in Dilsen. When a gentleman came in a little later, they asked him whether he would join them as the fourth player. When one of the men went to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the gentleman had a horse's foot. At the cry "Jesus, Mary!" the gentleman flew out through the window. A stinking vapour hung in the inn.
201913: A witch once lived in Uikhoven. Later a woman from Wezent who came peddling thread was suspected of witchcraft. Somehow witches always knew how to lure children to them. In Uikhoven a little child became half paralysed because of a witch. The child recovered, but was left with a handicap in its leg.
201927: Koob, the shoemaker's son, had to haunt after his death. Because Koob had always been a good man, nobody knew what the ghost wanted. One day some people saw the ghost going to a nearby shop. Koob had a debt at that shop that had not yet been settled. When someone else had paid the dead man's bill, the ghost finally found rest.
201932: The witch often came at the time the cows were due to calve. It was always best to avoid a witch. If a witch came to steal, people went to fetch holy water.
201942: A man who lived by the Planken Brug cursed all the time. One day a violent wind suddenly rose, so everyone went inside. The next moment a large dog lay on the roof of the house where the man lived.
201947: A woman who had a little rabbit on her lap was surprised that the animal suddenly began to grow heavier and heavier. The rabbit turned out to have changed into a stone.
201949: A man had had to carry the werewolf.
201950: A man going to play cards at Max V.J.'s had to pass a turnstile on which a cat was sitting. When the man had struck at the cat twice, the animal said: "Now strike again if you dare!" At that the man ran away in fear.
201962: A woman came to visit a family in Deurne every day. After the woman had rubbed the child's head, the child was full of lice. When a blessed candle had been put under the threshold, the woman could no longer come in. After the people had received a scapular from the Holy Little Father in Hasselt, the child was rid of its lice.
201968: In the past will-o'-the-wisps were often seen in the ditches. They were the souls of unbaptised children. The lights still seen today are glow-worms.
201973: A man from Sluizen worked in the coal mine in Liège. Because the man felt that he had to turn into a werewolf, he hurried home to fetch his animal skin. When the man went for a walk with his girlfriend, he asked her to wait for him a moment. Meanwhile the girl was frightened at the sight of a beast coming towards her. The girl quickly threw her handkerchief at the animal's mouth. A little later the girl's boyfriend came back. To her great horror, the girl saw that he still had the fibres of her handkerchief between his teeth.
201974: A man who wanted to mow clover was pestered the whole time by a hare that kept running under his feet. The man then said: "Devil's child, I'll beat you to death!" The next moment as many as sixty hares appeared.
201983: A man had slept at the house of his girlfriend, who was suspected of being a witch. The next day the man was full of lice. When the witch went to Mass on Sunday, he let the witch come in and forced her to undo the harm she had done. The witch did as she was asked.
201992: The house of 'Kobas' was haunted. Sometimes the plates moved by themselves.
201997: Between Mechelen and Opgrimbie there was a place called 'de Geest' (the Ghost). A smith who never went to church and believed in nothing claimed that one night between twelve and one o'clock he had seen a white lady appear at 'de Geest'. The smith had said: "Well, miss, you are out late," but there was no answer.
202005: Wizards sometimes secretly crept into bed with a woman. Wizards were sometimes invisible to certain people.
202012: Trien S. from 't Kamp was a witch. For Trien had murdered her eleven children.
202025:
At the Wijershof there was a farmhand who had to carry the werewolf every Sunday. One day the farmhand asked the farmer to leave the door open. When the farmhand came home that evening, he carried the werewolf right into the house, struck him and took off his collar. Because the werewolf was bleeding, he turned back into a human: he turned out to be a man from the neighbourhood.
Sometimes it also happened that a werewolf's collar was thrown into the oven and the werewolf then jumped into the fire to save his collar.
202027: When Jan V. noticed he was being followed by a dog, he hurried home. As soon as the man was inside his house, he heard the dog fling itself against the door. The prints of the animal's paws were on the door.
202042: People said that Peer, Koenraad's grandfather, consorted with the devil. One day the man had to muck out the stable on a farm. Peer loaded the cart so full that the horse stubbornly stood still. Then Peer said: "I'll pull that cart out of the stable myself." Peer had superhuman strength.
202049: A man returning from Rosmeer at about ten in the evening was followed in the Diepe Straat by a thick chain that had fallen from a pollard willow.
202064: A farmer's wife going through the woods to the shop met an old woman, who asked for a sweet. The farmer's wife gave the woman a sweet and went on. When she met the old woman again a while later, the woman again asked for a sweet. The farmer's wife answered: "But I already gave you one just now!" The woman said: "Well, now you shan't get out of the woods!" The farmer's wife got lost in the woods.
202078: In the evening you were not supposed to call to a cat, because that cat might well be a witch.
202083: Everyone knew that old Trien Kai was a witch. It was also said that a certain Nierke Gemers had a relationship with the witch. One day a man went and tapped on the witch's window. Trien shouted: "If you don't keep off my window, I'll let you feel my hand!" The man tapped on the window a second time and then quickly walked on. Although it was a fine day and it had not rained for a long time, the man suddenly fell into a big mud puddle in his new clothes. The witch must surely have conjured up water.
202103: A man had often tried in vain to shoot a hare in his garden. When the man had had his gun blessed by the priest, he did manage to hit the animal. The hare's blood lay on the ground, but the animal itself had vanished. A few days later the man heard that the postman's wife had been in bed for some time and that it looked as if she had shot in her leg.
202120:
A man walking to the factory was followed the whole time by a cat that ran between his legs. The man had tried several times to kick the animal, but he never managed to hit the cat. When the man came to a crossroads, the cat could go no further. Eighteen days later the cat appeared again. This time the cat screamed the whole time. A rustling was also heard, as if a lady in a silk dress were standing there. On another day the cat appeared in the shape of a werewolf near Hognoel. A man then took off his coat and threw it on the ground, for the werewolf could not go any further until it had unravelled all the threads.
People who had been badly baptized had to do such evil.
202122: Nare, a man from Sint-Truiden, could drive away mice and rats with a special book. One day Nare asked a man: "Don't you have rats?", to which the man replied: "Yes, there are lots of them here!" Nare began reading aloud from his book of magic. He did so in three corners of the house in turn. "I must leave one corner open," he said, "so the rats can leave that way, because otherwise they are shut up in this house."
202124: A witch congratulated a man on the sow and seven piglets he had just bought. Not long afterwards, however, the sow had to be slaughtered because she was ill.
202126: The husband of Fin, a woman who lived to be a hundred and two, was a pig dealer. One day the man had bought dozens of pigs in Wallonia. Because the animals had got loose at night, the man and his wife Fin tried to drive the pigs back to the sty. At the corner of the street Fin suddenly saw a big black dog whose tail dragged along the ground. The dog knocked Fin over and stepped over her. Where her husband was searching for the pigs, the hedges suddenly began to creak strangely, so that the man became afraid and dared not search any further. Only at dawn did Fin and her husband dare to continue looking for the pigs.
202131:
Some people made a pact with the devil, so that for seven years they received a lot of money and could commit all kinds of mortal sins. Those people had to roam about at night wearing a wolf skin and a wolf's head. If such a person died before the seven years were up, he went straight to hell.
On a farm there worked a farmhand who had to commit all kinds of mortal sins at midnight: prostitution, taking part in a witches' sabbath, and so on. One day, however, the farmhand's animal skin was found. At the moment they wanted to throw the skin into the fire, the farmhand stood by the oven saying: "Don't do it, don't do it! My seven years are almost up! Otherwise I'll have to start again, and I'm so glad it's almost over".
202134: A witch lived in the house of Jef V. in Wasseven. One day the witch gave a little bowl of milk to a child. A week later the child was dead.
202136: A mother always carried her four-month-old child out of the room whenever a witch came to visit. When the witch was going home, she met the child's father and said: "Your wife always leaves me sitting alone in the kitchen. She picks up her child and puts it in another room when I'm there. But I'll make her dance yet!" The man did not believe that the woman was a witch. The worried mother's daughter did later get a serious inflammation of her neck, from which she still has scars.
202138: When Koob P. and Maarten V. drove to the Houthalen heath with an ox, they said: "Surely we won't get bewitched." A while later the men ended up in Hengelhoef. At nine o'clock they landed in Meeuwen. In the end the oxen were too tired to make it to the heath.
202142: A family in Kinrooi had a newborn baby lying in the cradle. One day an old woman came by and stroked the child's head. A while later the child got red spots in the places where the woman had touched it.
202147: In Diepenbeek a werewolf roamed about, tormenting people. This werewolf was in fact a returned dead person. Whenever the werewolf walked past an oven, the fire went out. After the werewolf's skin had been burnt, the beast was never seen again.
202148: Farmer Luys's farmhand had to go and manure the land, but did not feel like it. The farmhand said to the farmer: "Even before you are ready to plough, the land will be manured." The farmhand manured a small patch of the land and then said: "Now all of it!" The next moment the field was manured. At every little heap of manure a small red man had appeared.
202169: A man taking a basket of butter to town met a woman on the way. Just as the man passed the woman, his basket fell to the ground. At that the man shouted angrily: "You damned witch!"
202173: A man was asked by the woman who ran the café to go and look at the tap in the cellar. After the woman had briefly touched the man, he was full of lice.
202184: A man going to fetch hay with a cart met a witch who asked him for something. The man refused and drove on. A little further on the man's cart fell over.
202187: A child who wanted to buy a cake had stolen a quarter and hidden it behind a stone of the house. After the child died unexpectedly, a strange noise was always heard behind that stone. As soon as the quarter was found, the child was allowed into heaven.
202196: Because the V. family could not make butter, they sent for Vranken. Vranken read something from the gospel and then crawled up the stairs on his bare knees. The next moment the witch had disappeared.
202213: A woman had crept unnoticed into a farmhouse in Hommelen while the farmer and his wife were working outside. When the farmer's wife came in and saw a strange woman standing by her child's cradle, she asked: "What are you doing here?" The woman replied that she had come to borrow something. When the woman had left, the child began to cry loudly. Some time later the child died. Two years later the farmer's wife went to have a newborn child baptised in the church. On the way she met the same woman, who asked if she might see the child. At that the child's godfather said angrily: "Get out of here!" This time the child remained unharmed.
202218: Some men had made a bet in a café. Whoever could curse the loudest would see the devil appear. When the man who had cursed the loudest came out of the café, he saw a foal. The foal put its forelegs on the man's shoulders and let itself be carried. That was the devil.
202234: In Gestel there was a bush that moved when there was no wind.
202245: One evening a man went to visit his parents. When he reached the church, he heard the sound of hooves and thought: "The castle coachman is still out in this bad weather." Then the man heard the coach drive past, but he saw nothing. The next day he learned from the castle coachman that he had not been out.
202246: The witch Peer could lead people astray.
202250: One morning a village policeman from Limburg went to the mayor to tell him what had happened to him the night before. As the policeman passed the churchyard, he had seen thirteen cats, one of which was exceptionally large. The large cat pointed at the policeman, whereupon the other cats attacked the man. With great effort the man managed to beat the cats off. A little further on, the policeman saw that the large cat wanted to attack him. The man quickly shot the large cat dead. When the mayor and the policeman went together that morning to look at the place where it had happened, the policeman's wife was lying there dead. At that moment everyone believed that the woman had been a witch. Four months later the policeman had already remarried.
202267: A girl had gone cycling on the heath. Whenever she came to a certain spot, the chain kept falling off her bicycle. When the girl came home, she was blind. Her parents took her to the parish priest of Niel. The priest prayed and sang for the girl until the drops of sweat ran from his forehead. After that the girl was cured.
202268: A boy made mice during catechism class. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it could no longer make mice. In the old days priests sometimes forgot something during baptism.
202283: At Sus G.'s place they could no longer make butter. Strangely enough, there was always a witch nearby whenever they were churning butter. One day someone struck the cat on the neck with a stick. The next day a little woman was walking around the village with a bandage around her neck. That woman had long been suspected of being a witch.
202292: Neske B. was in love with a girl who was seeing someone else. One evening the girl's boyfriend had two accomplices beat his rival to death on the Planken Brug. Neske's dead body was carried to the marsh. Ever since, a black horse always lay on the bridge.
202295: Whenever Nel M. was in the house, the chimney would not draw the smoke, so the stove did not work properly. When Nel was no longer let in, all the problems were solved.
202306: The dead steward of the castle of Vogelsang came haunting with coach and horse in the woods by the bridge over the brook. Because people were afraid of the ghost, the clergy banished it.
202322: A man was standing outside his house looking on when the baker came on his horse to bring people their bread. The man quickly went inside and began reading his book of magic, so that the baker's horse suddenly stood still. When the man came back outside, he said to the baker: "You don't know anything about horses either, do you!", and he gave the horse a sugar lump and a pat on the neck. Then the animal could go on again.
202340: In the Bosstraat in Maastricht lived a family who had adopted a child. One day the child would no longer eat and became very thin. Because the doctor did not know what to do, they asked the child what was wrong. The child answered: "Every night someone comes and stands beside my bed." A clergyman advised the child to ask the spirit next time what it wanted. Everyone living in the house had to go to communion. When the spirit appeared again the next day, the child said: "Well, we have all been!" But one of the farmhands had only gone to communion for appearances. After that farmhand had gone to communion again, the spirit was no longer seen.
202343: The little gate by the church was haunted. A frightened passer-by quickly made the sign of the cross, and the ghost vanished at once.
202359: In a haunted house all the doors and windows flew open at night. The man who had lived there had made a promise during his life that he never kept. That is why the man had to haunt after his death.
202368: Werewolves were people who wore an animal skin and jumped on passers-by. After having themselves carried for a while, the werewolves left their sweaty, frightened victim alone.
202384: A man returning from Zutendaal at night saw a black figure coming towards him. Frightened, the man said: "If you are of the devil, go. If you are of God, stink." The next moment the figure had vanished. The man smelled the stench of sulphur.
202387: A man going to play cards passed the house of a witch and suddenly saw a thousand cats appear there. When the man reached a sewer, the cats had all at once disappeared.
202408: A man walking home in the evening was attacked by a large dog that leapt out of the bushes. The man fought the werewolf for his life.
202409: In Widooie the witches regularly came to dance in a meadow. You could hear music then, but you could not see anyone. Afterwards a large round circle was found around a tree. The grass was also always flattened where the witches had danced. During their dance the witches sang: "Pliereplareploe, pliereplareploe!" Some farmhands from a nearby farm sang after the witches: "Pliereplareploe!" The witches replied: "You sang along with us, now you must drink along with us too!" Then the witches threw something at the farmhands. The farmhands thought it was a drinking cup, but it turned out to be a cow's leg.
202420: On the Bokt lived a woman who could not sleep at night because she had been touched by the evil hand. Pier, who often went hare hunting in the evenings, had been advised by someone to take a look in the friars' wood. "But be careful," they had said, "because the witch Trina often walks around there." "That doesn't matter," the man had replied, "I can handle that, because I have been to the bishop!" A few days later a woman in the village had her backside full of shot. Then the woman of the Bokt could sleep.
202454: After Bèr died, he had to haunt. When the ghost was asked what it wanted, the dead Bèr answered: "Two people must go on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel for me. They had promised to, but they never did. As long as that promise is not kept, I am a lost soul." Two of Bèr's relatives then went on the pilgrimage, and the ghost was released.
202462: Werewolves were men wearing a sheepskin who jumped onto the necks of passers-by and then had themselves carried. If you could make a werewolf bleed, he disappeared.
202478: In Gingelom lived a witch named Vica, who caused her own children to die.
202482: In Tongeren lived a witch who infested the children with lice and sprinkled hairs in the food.
202510: A shopkeeper whose eldest son had died went to the friars of Rijkel because he suspected the boy had been bewitched. The friars said a little prayer and advised the man to give the witch what she asked for the next time and otherwise say nothing. When the witch next came into the shop, she took her goods and left. Since that day the woman was never seen again.
202543: A child from Vliermaalroot was seriously ill because a witch regularly came to visit. When a blessed wedding ring had been placed under the threshold, the witch could no longer get in.
202551: In a café in Antwerp a mother always put her little child outside. When a witch had touched the child, it began to cry without stopping.
202565: A poacher stood with his back against the wall waiting for a hare to appear. When he suddenly saw a hare among the cabbages in the garden, he raised his gun to shoot the animal. However, he missed. A second hare appeared, but again the poacher failed to hit it. When a hare appeared for the third time, the animal sat up on its hind legs and asked: "Have those other two gone by long ago?" It was the old woman who lived there.
202583: A woman came to visit Rosalie E. and said: "What a beautiful cow you have!" Shortly afterwards the cow fell ill and died.
202589: Five sisters who were witches always sat in a circle around the fire at a certain house. When the sisters came in in the shape of cats, people had to praise them for their beauty. When the cats left, they said: "If that gentleman had not spoken so nicely, we would have broken all his legs."
202592: Gerard, the husband of Trien B., was chopping wood when his wife called him inside to eat. Because Gerard did not come at once, Trien went outside. At that Gerard fell down dead. Although the doctor claimed that Gerard's death was caused by heart problems, many people believed that the witch had made her husband die.
202595: A man walking through the fields at night had to climb over a barrier. Suddenly a pack of cats came running up, which seemed to be trying to stop the man.
202597: It was said that in Gestel a child had been bewitched by a certain V.
202598: Theo P. went poaching in Heks-bos together with Tinus P. and Martin K. Suddenly the men heard a little bell ringing, although there was nothing to be seen. It was quite a different sound from that of the bottles the castle residents hung in the trees to scare off poachers. Theo shot at the spot the ringing came from, but it did no good. The further the poachers went into the woods, the louder the sound rang out. When the men reached the Perenwei, the ringing stopped.
202612: A man returning from Diest in the evening with his covered wagon met a white lady on the way, who walked silently alongside the wagon. The ghostly apparition looked like a nun wearing a white cloth on her head. Because the horse got scared and began to pull hard, the man went home as fast as he could.
202623: A man saw a witch go into his neighbour's stable. But when the man went to look, there was nothing to be seen. The witch must have made herself invisible.
202627: A farmer's wife who went milking was always followed by a large dog. When anyone came closer, the dog suddenly vanished.
202642: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children who floated about in the woods in the evening.
202646: On the castle lane of Wideux lay an old felled oak where the count came to haunt.
202649: A witch could even infest a dead person with lice.
202650: The castle of Dessener was haunted in broad daylight. Once, during Sunday mass, a coach came driving up. A woman who thought it was the counts of Gors-Opleeuw quickly jumped up to put on a different apron. She heard a voice: "Aunt Zeur, Aunt Zeur!", but when she went to look, there was nothing to be seen anymore. Out of fear the woman moved to Kortessem. Coaches were also regularly sighted near the castle. Sometimes cats came to dance near the castle in the evening. At night there was so much noise in the stables that it seemed as if the ghosts were breaking the animals' necks. The cows were so nervous that their milk hardly contained any cream. It is said that the ghost was later banished by a friar.
202666: Some men had often tried to catch a little hare. Even though they sat in a circle around the hare, the animal always managed to escape. That hare must have been a witch.
202667: A schoolmaster told the sexton that his son was such a fearful child. "That's no matter," said the sexton, "let him come and ring the bells tonight." When the boy rang the bells that evening, nine bones and a skull suddenly fell to the floor. As in a game of skittles the skull began to roll and knocked over four bones. When the skull began to roll for the second time, the boy said: "I bet a coin that five skittles won't fall."
202670:
A boy had been wounded while roaming about as a werewolf.
When a werewolf died, someone from his family had to swear that he would become a werewolf too. Only a priest could free a werewolf from the evil.
202676: At a crossroads near the mill of Maaseik, people were often jumped by a werewolf. One evening a man had tied a knife to his back to teach the werewolf a lesson. When the werewolf jumped on the man, its belly was ripped open by the knife. Because the werewolf was wounded, he took on his human form and could be recognised.
202685: During his life a man had moved the boundary post of his field to enlarge his land. After his death the man came haunting with a boundary post in his hands, calling: "Where must I put it?" One night someone answered: "Put it where you took it from!" With that the ghost was released.
202695: At the sisters' convent in Lanklaar all the doors flew open at midnight, although there was no wind. After the sisters had a Mass said for the dead person who made the doors fly open, the haunting stopped.
202703: A boy was sitting with his girlfriend in a café at a crossroads in Overpelt. Suddenly the boy said to the girl: "I have to go relieve myself. If anything comes towards you in the meantime, throw this handkerchief at the apparition." The boy himself was afraid that as a werewolf he would attack his girlfriend. When the girl saw a werewolf, the beast tore the handkerchief to shreds. When it grew light in the morning, the girl saw that her boyfriend still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
202726: A friar who had given false testimony said: "If it isn't true, then I'll drink seven devils". Friars had to be called in to drive out the devils. Only a holy friar who had committed no sins could drive them out.
202729: Because several of R.'s cows had already died, he sent for the sorcerer from Zepperen. When he came, he said to R.: "It is the evil hand. You must go on pilgrimage to St Wivina in the Monnebruren church. The first person you meet is the cause of your misfortune. You must also all go to confession and take communion.
