And break down the mangers in your stable and see whether you find anything strange there." R. believed none of what the sorcerer said. He sent for several vets, but they could not help him. In the end R. went on the pilgrimage after all. The first person he met was the mother of a girl who had been thrown out onto the street because she could not leave any man alone. When R. had broken down the mangers, he found all sorts of rags and other strange objects, which he set on fire. When everything had burned up, R. was covered in lice. From then on R. had no more problems with his cows.
202750: A woman always got up at night and shouted that her cows had broken loose or that a calf was about to be born. It was never true. The woman would then go knocking on everyone's door. People believed she was a witch.
202755: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his land came haunting after his death, saying: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" One day a drunkard answered: "Where you took it from!" Since then the ghost has never been seen again.
202757: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field had to come haunting after his death. The ghost held the boundary post in his arms and kept calling: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" The owner of the field at the time grew so tired of the calling that he went to ask the priest for advice. The priest advised the man to answer the ghost's question the next time. The next night the man answered: "Put the boundary post back where you took it from." With that the dead man was released and haunted no more.
202759: A woman who had four rabbits in her basket met a witch, who asked: "Have you got rats in your basket?" The woman answered: "No, they are rabbits." When the woman opened the basket, four rats jumped out.
202781: A man coming back from the pub with his wife saw a cat on the way. The man hit the cat on its paw with a stick. The next day Gun, a woman from the village, had a broken arm.
202784: Some people dressed up in a white sheet and then had themselves carried as a werewolf.
202825: One evening Kobes set off somewhere with his horse and cart. He was on the road for half the night because the cart kept turning round and round. In the morning Kobes noticed that one wheel of the cart had one more spoke than the other.
202847: A boy going to the field met an old woman who laid her hand on his head and said: "You are a good boy". The next moment the boy was covered in lice.
202849: A farmhand visited his girlfriend every evening after work. When the farmhand came back, he was often attacked by a werewolf. He had already had to carry the werewolf several times.
202855: A seamstress from Rutten was coming home from work one evening when she suddenly met a werewolf. The girl quickly threw a handkerchief at the werewolf, which unravelled the cloth completely. When the girl met her boyfriend the next day, she saw that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
202869: A man who was always stopped by a werewolf managed one day to make the werewolf bleed. The next moment his best friend stood before him, who began to cry and said: "Why did you have to make me bleed? Now I have to start all over again! It was the very last day of the nine years for which I had sold my soul to the devil!"
202871: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend in Vliermaal passed the house of the witch Hubertine and muttered with a laugh: "If witches exist, then go ahead and bewitch me!" That evening the man got lost so that he could not get home. The following Sunday the same thing happened.
202874: In Lanaken lived a witch who was called 'Bosmie'. A man who was out with a horse and cart had stood talking with Bosmie. At a certain moment the man said: "I have to move on now, or it will get too dark and then I won't be able to put the horse in the stable." To this Bosmie replied: "Yes, but you're not home yet, you know!" The man blundered into a meadow and only reached his house the next morning. After that the man lived only two more years.
202876: In Neeroeteren lived a woman who claimed she was afraid of nothing. A man who wanted to play a trick on the brave woman slaughtered an animal and threw its skin over himself. In this way the man crept on hands and knees through the hedges. When the woman noticed the strange apparition, she bashed the man's head in without hesitation. Since then that place has been haunted.
202884: Katrien B. was a witch. The woman did go to church, but she behaved strangely and had an ugly hairy face. Katrien had passed her witchcraft on to her only daughter. As a result the girl could make mice without tails by laying a handkerchief on a molehill. Children who had such skills were usually taken to the priest to have prayers read over them. The farm where Katrien lived was bewitched. The rotten tree stump that stood nearby was called 'Neringensoets' (1), because it made a sound like that of ruminating animals. Many animals also died on the farm. Although things went much better on the farm after Katrien's death, people there were still regularly ill. Katrien's brother, for instance, lay ill in bed for fifteen years. On Shrovetide the boys always went round with the 'rommelpot' (friction drum). The piece of tart the boys got from Katrien they always threw away to be safe. Ties G. was stopped three times on the road from Goolder to Bocholt-Damburg by the witch, who was disguised as a Capuchin friar and looked the man straight in the eyes under his cap.
202892: A boy out walking with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "I have to go relieve myself. You go on to the café. If you meet some beast or other, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." The girl did as she had been told. When the boy came into the café a while later, he still had the bits of the handkerchief between his teeth. If the girl had not thrown the handkerchief at the wolf, she would have been dead.
202906: A man was troubled by a ferret in a hole, so he went to borrow a spade from Joop. Joop's stable door was open. To his great fright, the man saw a fireball in the stable. Joop then said to the fireball: "Off you go!" Joop had often seen fire on his farm, and strange dogs that ran between his legs. Some time later a skeleton was found in Joop's stable.
202908: While digging, Jan K. brought up a strange hard object that was neither wood nor metal. Convinced it was a ghostly thing, Jan said: "If you are of God, [speak], if you are of the devil, be gone." Then the object sank back into the ground.
202915: At a farmer's in Budel there worked a farmhand who always went off at night. The farmer had discovered that the farmhand had a belt, which he had hidden in the hayloft. The parish priest advised the farmer to send the farmhand away and meanwhile throw the belt into the oven. At the moment the belt caught fire, the farmhand stood by the oven to save his belt. When it turned out to be too late, however, the farmhand said: "Now I am lost", and he ran off to the heath. The farmhand must have been Lucifer.
202918: On a hot night at harvest time, a man and a woman from Balen went to the field to mow grain. Suddenly the couple saw two little nuns appear in the field, wearing a white cloth on their heads, who said: "Friend, the night is for us and the day is for you!" The man and the woman then ran home as fast as they could.
202927: A man was persuaded to spend the night in a bewitched house in exchange for a cow. At night the man lit the stove in the house and put a pot of oil on it. A while later a cat came in and said: "Good day, man of the cow!" Shortly afterwards another cat arrived, which also said: "Good day, man of the cow!" When at last there was a whole pack of cats in the house, the man poured hot oil over the animals. The next day a good many women from the neighbourhood had burns.
202928: An old man from Horpmaal saw a will-o'-the-wisp one evening. He followed it to the water and then said: "In God's name, what do you want?", to which the light replied: "I want to be baptised. Your hand is by the water; you only have to scoop." When the man had baptised the will-o'-the-wisp, the light went out and a child appeared that looked like a little angel. The child said to the man: "In three days you will die. But your chair will be ready in heaven next to mine."
202930: A child became paralysed after a witch had come peddling. After the child had lain in bed for seven years, it died. The child's pillow was full of pins.
202933: It was said that Fien H. was a witch. One day Fien had stroked the head of Neel T.'s newborn child. That same evening the child fell out of its cradle as many as five times without suffering any injury.
202936: A boy was walking home with a girl in the rain. On the way the boy's cap blew away. Because it was dark the two could not find the cap, and the girl suggested fetching the lamp from her home. The girl's mother asked why they needed the lamp, and the girl answered: "He has lost his cap." The mother then said: "But he has his cap on his head!" And so he did. The woman was a witch.
202952: The farmhand of H. in Meeuwen saw a hare in the garden every evening. The farmhand could not manage to shoot the animal, because his gun never worked when the hare was nearby. The farmhand told his story to a friend, who decided to shoot the hare himself. The man attached a consecrated object to the gun and nearly shot H.'s daughter dead.
202953: A white lady walked about in a field in Spalbeek. Whoever met her and stood still had their legs paralysed. When the white lady went away, one could go back.
202954: Saint Lambert prophesied: "Tongeren will perish and Maastricht will rise". The church of Tongeren did indeed sink. On Christmas night its bell could be heard ringing at twelve o'clock.
202959: A farmhand told his master that his friend had to roam about as a werewolf every night. The farmhand wanted to find his friend's band, because he had heard that a werewolf could be released by burning his band. In reality the farmhand's friend went poaching every night.
202967: A woman from Heerlen always came to fetch eggs at a farm in Dilsen. Because that woman was a witch, many children died on the farm. When the witch stopped coming by, no more children died.
202969: A little child from Romershoven fell ill after being touched by a witch. A few hours later the child died.
202984: On the Molenveld lived a boy who was a bit simple-minded. One day the boy did not come home. The neighbour believed the boy had drowned, but his mother kept praying for her son. In the evening there was a knock. The boy came in, his body covered in mud. When his mother asked where he had been, the boy answered: "I was at the old Maas and I saw the devil. The devil wanted to shake my hand and pull me into the water. That didn't work because I wouldn't throw away my rosary." Since then the boy went to pray in the chapel of Stokkem every evening.
202992: A brave woman who worked as a maid in Kesselt let herself be dared to go and draw a cross on the church door around midnight. When the girl had drawn the cross that night and turned around, a ghost in a white garment stood before her. As soon as the ghost took off the garment, the maid recognised her dead grandmother.
202995: A miller coming back from the town council one evening heard a pack of cats howling. The man struck at the animals with his stick and went on. The next day the miller met a woman who said: "If you ever see something like that again, leave it all alone. If I hadn't been there, you wouldn't have got off so lightly!"
203001: In Beegd (?) people always heard someone calling by the Maas in the evening: "Ferry over! Ferry over!" A man had drowned there when he came closer because he thought he had seen the light of the ferry.
203027: A man who always went to play cards near the church had said he would like to meet the werewolf some time. And so one evening the man was jumped by the werewolf, which had itself carried. Another evening the man was jumped again, by a big dog. He threw the animal into an apple tree. When the dog was already in the broeken (marshy low ground), it could still be heard howling.
203036: Between midnight and one o'clock the witches came to dance at Niere's pool opposite B. On the way the witches took the shape of black cats. The cats walked one behind the other, standing on their hind legs, holding the tail of the one in front with their front paws.
203055: A witch went to dig up a dead person in the churchyard.
203060: Four animals belonging to the S. family had died for no apparent reason. The friars of Weert established that a witch from the neighbourhood was responsible for the misfortune.
203062: On the castle estate of Bovelingen a ghostly coach drawn by horses often drove around at night. One day a passer-by asked the coach: "Why do you always come here? What do you want?", and a voice answered: "The day for you and the night for me." A Norbertine canon who was parish priest of Batsheers banished the spirit into an oak. Before he succeeded, the priest had to endure a great deal, for the spirit pushed him into a brook several times on the way. Afterwards the priest said: "Luckily I knew my Our Father well, otherwise the little devil would have given me a nasty beating!" Although the spirit was banished, the children born at the castle had misfortune all their lives.
203087: A man was coming back from a wedding around midnight. When the man saw a white cat jump out of the meadow, he said: "If you come out of the meadow again, I'll hit you with my umbrella!" At that the cat vanished.
203090: A man who had to go and fetch a borrowed measuring rod in Opglabbeek never got there. A second man who tried also got lost.
203093: On a farm they were salting a pig when Stien F. came by and said: "You may perhaps be able to eat from that for a long time." The farmer was surprised that Stien had used the word 'perhaps', and he already feared the woman had bewitched the pig. When they later wanted to eat from the pig, worms crawled out of it.
203096: A man from Helchteren kept calling: "What am I to do with it? What am I to do with it?" A passer-by answered: "Put it where you took it from." People who had committed a sin had to come back after their death.
203099: A farmer whose cows had all become barren was told by a man: "Close that window in your stable! Otherwise a witch's cat can get in!" The farmer closed his window and went to the friar of Hasselt. Shortly afterwards the cows were fertile again.
203123: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field was tormented by the fire-man. One must not whistle at a fireball, for then the fire would fly against the houses.
203146: In a house in Lommel a piece of ham had been hung in the chimney. When the rope broke, the devil fell down together with the meat. The priest chased the devil away by reading from a little book and saying: "Satan, depart from here".
203151: The meadow where the school was later built used to be haunted. The horses behaved strangely and at night the ringing of bells was often heard in the meadow. It must have been werewolves.
203170: Some men secretly went to pick cherries in a walled meadow. One of the men had tied a white handkerchief to the wall so he could easily find the exit again. Another man was frightened at the sight of the handkerchief and ran off screaming. In his haste the man fell onto a horned beast, which suddenly stood up and ran off with him on its back. The man was convinced that the beast was the devil.
203173: A man out for a walk with a friend saw a little rabbit in the meadow. When the man tried to catch the rabbit, it jumped away behind the hedge. Then a woman appeared who was said to be a witch.
203177:
A witch lived in Rekem. At four o'clock in the morning this woman met someone in the Tombos.

a) In Opgrimbie lived two witches who caused people to have a lot of bad luck with their animals.

b) In Opgrimbie a witch went about in the shape of a dog.

c) A little boy always had to go to the field with a witch. But the witch had no power over the boy.
The witch had given a man a hunchback.

A certain G. had refused to give the witch anything during the war. "You will regret that," the witch had predicted. Some time later the man got an ailment in his foot. Because the doctor could not help, the friars of Rekem prayed for the man until they were drenched in sweat. The painful foot was ten centimetres shorter than the other, and all sorts of little bones came out of it. In the end the man's foot did heal.
203201: A boy out walking with his girlfriend said to the girl: "Go on ahead, because I have to go relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief with white dots at its mouth." When a dog did indeed come up a little later, the girl did as she had been told. When the girl saw her boyfriend again, she found to her great dismay that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
203213: In the past it often happened that someone had made a promise or borrowed something from someone, and then died unexpectedly. The dead person could then find no rest until the promise had been kept or the borrowed item returned.
203221: Because Driek's horse had gone wild, the man sent for the parish priest. "The horse has been struck by the evil hand," the clergyman established. In his Sunday sermon the priest had pointed out that not only women but also men can possess witchcraft. Driek's horse had been bewitched by Jaak.
203225: The rural policeman of Tongeren was startled when he heard jingling in a meadow in the evening. It was probably just the cows' bells ringing.
203244: In the past people believed that will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of the dead.
203245: It was said that the witches often held gatherings at the Tolkesboom in Bree. The witches' magic spell went as follows: "From here to there, to Cologne in the wine cellar."
203248: In the old days people believed in werewolves, which jumped on passers-by and had themselves carried.
203252: In Kozen a werewolf was shot dead one night. The next day the body of a dead man was found.
203273: Every day after work in Widooie, Tinneke was picked up by her boyfriend. On the way the young man suddenly said: "Go on ahead. I have to go relieve myself. If a dog comes at you, throw this handkerchief at its mouth and say: 'Tear the cloth as it was woven!'" When the girl met a dog, she did as her boyfriend had told her. When her boyfriend rejoined the girl in Koninksem, she saw that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth. Indignant, the girl said: "Go away! You needn't come back!"
203278: A man could not grow fruit because his fruit was bewitched. The witch made all the pears fall from the tree.
203279: Nol was walking on the main road with his dog in front. At the Groemelingenstraat the dog walked fearfully behind its master. Once they were past it, the dog went in front again. That street was haunted.
203288: Jan H. was working in the woods with three woodcutters. When it was Jan's turn to make the food, he decided to bake pancakes. Suddenly Jan heard a voice calling: "I'm falling", to which Jan answered: "Fall then, but not in my cake!" A little later some bones and a skull fell down one after another. While Jan was baking his last pancake, he saw a big grey man standing behind him. The man tapped Jan on the shoulder and beckoned him to come to the cellar. "A treasure lies buried there. But that treasure was brought in with a Spanish goat, and so it must also be taken out with a Spanish goat", the man then said. The grey man could not bring up the treasure himself because a Spanish goat was hard to find.
203324: Some people going to the market always saw on the way a rider on a white horse riding back and forth between the Boskee and the Marktstraat.
203340: In Leut there lived a witch with whom a man had a lot of trouble. Witches could, for example, give people a hunchback or infest them with lice.
203348: Everyone was afraid of Mie from Loon, because that witch could infest people with lice.
203357: The farm of de Waal was bewitched. Although it was not damp there, everything went mouldy. The farm was occupied by a woman from Rosmeer, four of whose children had died. Through the help of a friar the fifth child survived.
203380: Because farmer Kees H.'s animals were all falling ill, the man sent for a vet. The vet could not help, however, and suspected that the evil hand was the cause of the misfortune. When Kees's wife also fell ill, the farmer went to a priest, who came to pray over everything and sprinkled the whole farm with holy water. After that the farmer's wife and the animals recovered.
203383: A girl who had to go and fetch a jug of milk by moonlight got lost. When the girl stood in the middle of the road and said: "In God's name", she knew where she was again.
203392: A man had gone to help somewhere with work in the fields. At midday the farmer's wife asked him: "Will you have a bowl of soup with us?", to which the man replied: "No, there is food waiting for me at home." The witch would not listen, however, and ladled the hot soup into the bowl with her bare hands. That house was always very dirty. The woman was very thin and had grey hair that was never combed. Everyone was afraid of her.
203398: A farmer who had bought piglets was very afraid of the witch who lived nearby. One day the witch said to the piglets: "Piglets, alive and kicking!" At that the piglets began jumping around wildly.
203403: A man walking on the Broekberg got a terrible fright when a wild boar ran into him. The man crawled home on his knees in fear. A white goat also often came haunting in the Broek, coming from the Sint-Gillisweg. A certain Gust van A. once saw the goat among the trees of the Fonteindreef.
203409: A man had a pigeon loft that was haunted. Feathers lay all over the stairs. When the man came back from the neighbours', his pigeons had all disappeared.
203421: Jan T. went to the priest for advice because he believed a witch was keeping his pigs from getting fatter. On the way Jan was stopped by a strange force. So the man went back home. When the priest came to see him himself some time later, it was already too late. The pigs died shortly afterwards.
203433: A man who was often ridden by the mare had been advised by someone to put his shoes upside down beside the bed and to put a glass of water on the bedside table. It did not help, however.
203441: A farmer whose horses were always sweaty in the morning and stood in the stable with braided tails decided one night to spy on the horses through a little hole in the ceiling. At midnight a woman came into the stable through the keyhole. It was his wife.
203444: A man coming home from the fair met a foal on the way. The foal pushed the gate open with its hoof.
203445: A woman sat talking the whole time with the spirit of her late husband.
203458: At the Munnikenhof in Heks a maid had hanged herself. It was said that the girl came back to haunt after her death. One day Rikus de M. saw cats with little bells, which followed him as far as the first house of Bommershoven. Because the devils walked about there in the evening with the maid's ghost, nobody dared go there alone.
203459: A man on his way to church got lost along the way. The man was bewitched.
203471: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his land had to come haunting after his death, saying: "Where to leave it? Where to leave it?"
203475: A man who had an ailment in his toe went to the friars of Geleen because the doctor could not help him. When the man came to the friars, he explained that in his opinion the ailment was the work of a witch. "You shouldn't believe that," said the friar, to which the man replied: "Do you use holy water in the morning before you go to the altar?" The priest answered: "Yes, against evil." The clergyman blessed the man's foot and said: "Go on home. In eight days you will be able to work again."
203481: The little child of Anna V. from Lanaken had been bewitched by a neighbour. After the friars of Lanaken had prayed over the child, they discovered a ball of thorns in the pillow the child slept on.
203483:
At farmer Fiel's on 't Geneuth there worked a farmhand who played the werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent to Maastricht so that his skin could be burned in the meantime. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven.
After a chase, a claw was also once burnt into the door at Fiel's.
203488: Some men who had to keep watch at night over the laundry laid out to bleach were frightened to death when they saw some hares put the caps on their heads and hop about in them.
203497: In Opgrimbie there was a house that was haunted. At around one or half past one, all the doors suddenly flew open. The mill for grinding grain began to turn by itself. One day the man nailed the doors shut, but that did not help. In the end the occupants of the house moved away.
203516: On a farm in Lanaken there was a plague of rats. One day a ghost appeared that told the farmer what he had to do to get rid of the rats. The farmer followed the advice and poured boiling water over the rats. When the farmer went to mass the next morning, he saw that half the women had burns on their heads. They were witches.
203518:
Geenke D. was often woken at night by the sound of the witches' drums. A little later he would hear music in the Roosweide. The next day circles were found in the meadow where the witches had danced.
One day a man from Velm, on his way to Brustem, passed the Roosweide just as a witches' dance was going on. Luckily one of the witches knew the man, and she said: "Wilveren, wilveren, neeveren, neeveren, it's Pie-Ber the carpenter," and then the witches let him through.
203519: A man going from Maasmechelen to Opgrimbie was followed the whole way by a large dog that kept bumping against his legs. When the man went into his house, the dog suddenly vanished.
203521: When a mother died, the death owl came and sat on the children's heads.
203540: At 't Geneuth along the Maas there worked a farmhand who was known to be a werewolf. One day the farmhand was sent to Maastricht with a cart of straw. Meanwhile the farmhand's collar was found in an old willow stump. At the moment the collar was thrown into the fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven. They had the greatest difficulty stopping the farmhand from jumping into the oven. When the collar had burnt up completely, the farmhand cried out in relief: "Now I am saved!"
203541: A man walking home in the evening was nearly frightened to death when he saw a black dog sitting in an apple tree. The people who lived there claimed that the dog was the devil, come to fetch the soul of a dead person.
203548: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. That is why will-o'-the-wisps often led people to the water.
203549: After the witch Trien had been in W.'s stable, all the animals died.
203555: The farm 'de Krang' in Molenbeersel was haunted. In the mornings the horses always stood in the stable sweating and with braided manes. People going on pilgrimage to Stamprooi did not dare pass the Krang without praying aloud.
203573: In the Zakstraat there was a haunted farmstead. At night the poachers always heard music there. People believed it was the ghost of the former occupant.
203598: A woman was coming back from Tongeren through the water. A man who was reading from a book of magic suddenly made the woman go backwards. When the woman said, annoyed: "You did that to me!", the man replied: "I can make you go all the way back to Tongeren, but if you behave, you may go forward again now." The woman went on as far as the smith who lived by the church. Because the smith had put a fine cart outside, the woman said: "What fine tyres on that cart!" At that moment the tyre burst. The smith then said angrily: "If I see you here one more time, I'll kill you!"
203600: In the past there were often will-o'-the-wisps in the meadows at night. They were ghosts.
203609: In Runkelen there was a hedge that started shaking every night, even when there was no wind.
203615: The mayor of Houthalen had bought the freedom of many soldiers held by the French. In return for his help the mayor always asked for a piece of land or something similar. After his death the mayor came back to haunt on a horse. When people were praying the rosary somewhere, they heard a knocking on the door. When they opened it, they saw the ghost of the mayor sitting on a horse. In the end the ghost was banished to the Laambroek.
203623: In Lanaken there lived a boy who was suspected of consorting with the devil. Whenever the boy was locked up somewhere, he could break the locks open without any effort. One day the boy was sitting on a cart with some men and asked: "Would you like some sausage?", to which the others replied: "Yes, why not!" The next moment a dish full of sausages appeared. "Careful, you mustn't eat any of it!" said the boy. Then the boy took a piece of sausage and threw it off the cart. The men were so frightened that they all flew off the cart.
203635: At the farm 'de Donnerslag' the doors always flew open. The farm was haunted because a small child had once been murdered there.
203648: Whoever met Metsje and shook her hand had a head full of lice and fleas a little later.
203649: A family from Heiselt had a six-month-old child that cried all the time. Only when the child slept in a different bed was it quiet. In the child's pillow they found a bird that was missing just one wing. They tried to burn the bird, but the thing only caught fire after it had been sprinkled with holy water. When a cross had been put under the door, they discovered who the witch was. A woman from Rukkelingen who had often come to bring the child something could no longer get in.
203659: To recognise a witch, one had to place one's feet crosswise in the suspected woman's footprint. At the fifteenth step the witch would then look round. A child who recognised a witch from the neighbourhood this way was frightened half to death. From then on the child no longer dared accept sweets from that witch.
203669: The werewolf jumped on someone's back and then had itself carried. If you could make the werewolf bleed, he changed into a human.
203674: A woman who went to catechism class was always struck on the neck by the devil.
203678: When Harie V.D.H. was going from Bilzen to Hoelbeek, he knocked a cat off a post. Further on the cat was sitting on another post and Harie struck at the animal again. The same thing happened several more times. Finally the cat said: "Now chase me away once more, if you dare!"
203689: Strange things always happened on a farm in Roeren. One time the cows had been untied, another time a hellish noise was heard. One evening, when the maid was churning butter, the glass suddenly flew out of the windows.
203702: Because Bert was fed up with a strange cat always coming into his house, he struck the animal away. The cat turned out to be the witch Berbke.
203717: A farmer whose animals were all falling ill decided to go to a fortune teller. The fortune teller claimed that the misfortune was caused by a neighbour woman. One evening the farmer happened to see a hare hop into the stable and leap up against the animals. When the farmer had caught the hare, his animals all stayed healthy.
203719: A girl always boasted to her friends that she was afraid of nothing. One day the friends were so tired of it that they wanted to put her to the test. They dared her to walk around the church three times at night and strike the church door with her hand each time. The girl accepted the dare without hesitation. But when she had walked around the church for the second time, she saw a white shape in the churchyard. Convinced it was one of her friends trying to frighten her, the girl walked straight up to the shape and pulled away the white sheet. When she got back to her friends, however, she learned that none of them had been away. The girl was so terrified that she went straight to the parish priest. He advised her to bring the sheet back and, for her own safety, to take a newly baptised child with her. After much pleading, someone gave her a baby to take along. When the girl came to the churchyard, she saw the skeleton of her own mother. When she threw the sheet to the ghost, it said: "If you had not brought that innocent child, I would have torn you to pieces." The girl was so shaken by these words that she eventually died of grief.
203738: At Willem's in Rosmeer there worked a farmhand who always went off in the evening. When the farmer spied on the farmhand one evening, he saw the lad turn into a dog and crawl into a crooked poplar. After the farmer had burnt the werewolf's clothes, the farmhand came to him wailing for two weeks. After that he never heard from the farmhand again.
203750: A woman from Viversel came to bring people apples. After eating those apples, everyone fell ill.
203760: Werewolves were people who disguised themselves in an animal skin. If you could wound a werewolf, he took on his human form again.
203761: Old Geel had to come back to haunt after his death. The ghost screamed like an animal and kept crying: "Old Geel is there! And how is that."
203788: A mother whose child was always ill and could no longer sleep went to pastor T. of Montenaken. When the parents entered the church with the pastor, carrying a candle, the witch was standing by the holy water font. Since then the witch never visited the people again.
203805: A farmer from Caberg was troubled by a plague of rats. The farmer had heard that a man from Briegden could drive away rats. When the man came, he laid some straw in the meadow and said: "Come on, rats, come along!" When all the rats had crawled into the straw, the man set the straw on fire with a match.
203825: The ghost of a lawyer was banished into the cellar of L. The lawyer had grown rich by seizing other people's land and throwing away the boundary posts. When the lawyer died, people suddenly found that his body had disappeared. Because they did not want this to become known, they filled the coffin with stones. After his death, however, the lawyer came to haunt someone's cellar. A Redemptorist banished the ghost and walled it up in the cellar.
203842: A man coming back in the evening from the fair in Munster met a cat on the way that blocked his path. A little later the cat suddenly vanished.
203843: A man saw a vuurman (fire man) flying through the air in the field near Smisberg. You were not allowed to whistle at a vuurman, for then he would chase the person who had challenged him. When the man got home, he just heard the vuurman fly against the closed gate. It was claimed that such apparitions were the souls of unbaptised children.
203864: When there were cats in a tree, a table with delicacies stood beneath its crown. As soon as the cats were gone, the table had disappeared too.
203867: The alley by the boys' school was haunted. One evening two sisters were walking arm in arm through the alley when two black cats suddenly appeared.
203869: A drunkard had fallen asleep in the church. When the man woke up in the night, he saw the spirit of a Witheer (Norbertine canon) appear, who said: "Is there anyone here who can serve mass?" During his life the priest had forgotten to say a mass. The ghost said to the man: "You will die on this same day, but I will not say in which year." When the spirit had vanished, the man repented and decided never to drink again.
203884: In Rutten there lived a little boy who could make mice out of earth. The priest took that gift away from the boy.
203891: A tanner had died in Weert. A few days after his death a strange noise was heard in the tanner's house. A man went to look and saw the dead man tanning leather in his usual place. The man then sent for the priest. When the priest went to look in the house, however, the ghost had already vanished. The ghost was never seen again.
203908: At the T. family's home in Sledderlo, the windows and doors flew open by themselves at midnight. The B. family's home was haunted too.
203912: A witch could only bewitch her victim if she could touch it.
203914: When Pol L. from Koersel came home from the fair, a white sheet flew after him until he was home.
203915: Two men from Elen went to Heppeneert to visit their girlfriends. On the way a strong wind began to blow and the men were chased by clover that grew in the field.
203919: A witch made sure that butter could no longer be made on a farm in Tongeren. Only after the priest had sprinkled the farm with holy water was the problem solved.
203945: Sometimes you had to carry the werewolf.
203948: In Herk-de-Stad lived a married couple of whom the wife was a witch and the husband a werewolf. Whenever that couple had been in a stable, the animals fell ill. The werewolf often appeared in the evening in the shape of a dog.
203950: In the Rue St. Henri Berger in Brussels there was a house that was terribly haunted. At night the windows and doors flew open and something rattled in the attic, although nothing could be seen. Before the house was sold, the priest had said he wanted to bless the building "because such strange people had lived in it".
203963: A boy who went home in the evening was always hindered by cats that jumped in front of his feet. One evening the boy took a knife with him and said: "If they come now, I'll cut their throats!" When that evening the boy was accompanied by a very large black cat, he did not dare to move.
203972: The people who lived in the Reitje did not dare to walk home past the churchyard in the evening. They had once seen the devils Lucifer, Jan Klavier and Madeloen sticking their heads over the churchyard wall.
203973: The castle on the Osseweg was haunted, and so it stood empty. Whoever could deliver the ghost would get the castle as a reward. A certain Rekom from a farm wanted to win the castle at all costs. He asked his master to come along, but the master did not dare. Arriving at the castle, the farmhand began baking cakes from the flour his master had given him. When at midnight a skeleton without a head or limbs fell down the chimney, Rekem said: "Pity you have no head; otherwise you could have kept me company." Rekom put the skeleton in a corner and went on baking the cakes. A little later the ghost's arms and legs fell out of the chimney. When the skull also fell out of the chimney, Rekom asked: "Won't you have some cake?", at which the ghost shook its head and said: "First you must go to the cellar; there is a chest of money there." Rekom answered: "Go yourself then; if you fetch the money, it's yours. The money is hidden there in the name of the Red Goat." And because there were no red goats, Rekom went on: "In the shop further on they sell red cloth. If I hang that cloth over a goat, it will be the Red Goat." The ghost was afraid Rekom would leave in the meantime and said: "You may not leave here until I am delivered." Rekom went to buy a piece of cloth, hung it over a goat and said to the ghost: "Now go with the goat." The ghost went to the cellar with the animal. Already on the third step the ghost called for help, but Rekom thought: "If I help, I'm done for." After a while the sweating ghost appeared with the chest. The ghost said: "Half is for you and the other half is for the faithful souls." Then the ghost was delivered and Rekom had earned the castle.
203974: A girl was covered in lice after she had been struck by a witch.
204002: A girl claimed she could make mice from a molehill. A soldier who had heard the girl talking did not believe her. Then the girl made forty mice without tails appear from the molehill.
204008: A man had bought a few roosters from Fien F. At that time the man did not yet know that Fien was suspected of being a witch. When the roosters were slaughtered, they stank so badly that they seemed rotten.
204011: A dead woman returned in the shape of a bird that sat in a tree by her house.
204018:
A shy boy who never dared to go anywhere was visited by a man who was said to be a werewolf. The man asked: "Do you have a girl yet?", to which the boy replied: "No, I don't need a girl." Nevertheless, the man promised he would bring the boy a girl. When the boy went outside one evening, a beautiful girl was waiting for him, dressed all in white. The girl walked with him for a while, but the boy was too shy to speak to her. After a while the girl said she had to move on.
"She looked into my eyes so kindly...", the boy said afterwards.
204019: At eight o'clock in the evening two black women stood talking in the village. One woman was from Rutten, the other from Koninksem. A curious man who wanted to know who the women were got a slap from one of them.
204023: Some men went with a woman from Beek to bind the straw into bales. When the men suddenly saw a squirrel, they tried to catch the little animal. But the squirrel outwitted them every time, and after a long chase it suddenly vanished. The woman from Beek said to the men: "Just leave that squirrel alone!"
204024: On a farm in Dilsen there worked a farmhand who owned a collar with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. Every evening at about the same time the farmhand went to the old tree stump in which he had hidden his band. When the farmer and his wife had discovered the farmhand's secret, they sent the lad away to do a job somewhere. Meanwhile they fetched the band, which was hidden under the earth in the tree stump. At the moment the collar was thrown into the oven, the farmhand was already standing by the fire to save his possession. The farmhand managed to pull his collar out of the fire, so that he could carry on with his werewolf practices. One day, however, the farmer and his wife hid the collar in a place where the farmhand would never find it again.
204039: On the Hobos a big black dog with a chain around its neck always used to appear and frighten people. The animals were untied and stood trembling in the stable in the morning. That dog was the late drossaard (bailiff).
204043: A man walking along the Talderstraat was jumped by a werewolf. When the man had carried the werewolf a few metres, he hit the beast on the head with his fist. The next moment the werewolf turned into a naked man, whom his victim recognised.
204044: In the old days cats often sat wailing by the houses. When someone struck at such a cat, the animal jumped away and turned out to be a witch.
204049: After visiting his girlfriend, Jef left at half past twelve for the church of Schoten (Tessenderlo) to go on from there to Gerhagen. On the way, however, Jef got lost. After wandering through the woods for four hours, he decided to go straight to Tessenderlo station, where the train left that would take him to his work in Liège.
204055: It was said that ghosts walked about near the Heilige Haag in Hees.
204062: Some men who went catching finches at night heard creaking and shrieking by a linden tree, though there was nothing to be seen. That must have been the wild hunt.
204065:
In Niel there used to live many witches whom everyone feared. At the S. family's house, people from the neighbourhood often came round in the evening to chat by the fire. Later in the evening cats would come in and sit with their backs to the fire. Because people were afraid the cats were witches, they left the animals alone. One day, however, father S. had had enough of the cats. He did not dare hit the animals with a broom, because then they would climb up the handle and scratch his hands and face. The man scooped a little heap of wood shavings out of the fire and threw it over the cats. When the man walked through the woods the next day, he met many women whose faces were completely burned. From that day on all the witches in Niel were known, except one.
That one witch belonged to a German noble family and lived in the Moorsberg in Niel. She often visited people, so everyone anxiously kept their children away from her. The witch also often changed herself into a cat. One day the cat was burned by some brave men, and so people were rid of the witch.
204080: A child cried all the time because the midwife was a witch. A wreath was found in the child's pillow. As soon as the child was baptised, it stopped crying.
204082: In a meadow in Werm there was a barrier that opened by itself whenever a witch passed by and said: "Open for me".
204088: Nobody dared to sit in a haunted chapel. One night, however, a boy sat in the chapel. At midnight a priest appeared and said mass. After the service the priest said: "I thank you, for I was damned for a hundred years. You have released me. Now my soul can find rest."
204098: On a farm in Opglabbeek there worked a farmhand who owned a band with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. One day the farmer sent his farmhand to Dilsen so that meanwhile he could burn his band. As soon as the band caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven and pulled his band out. Because of this the farmhand was still not released.
204104: In the evening will-o'-the-wisps could often be seen in the meadows and hedges. Some people had forgotten that they had promised to go to Scherpenheuvel. The will-o'-the-wisps appeared to remind people of their promise. After the man had been to Scherpenheuvel, the will-o'-the-wisps were no longer seen.
204106: Ever since the father of a man from Millen had died, his house was haunted. Although rattling was always heard in the attic, nothing could be seen. Some time later, however, the man did find that the boards in the attic had been removed.
204109: When Nol went to visit his girlfriend in Hees, he saw a little child appear on the way, slapping its hands in a puddle of water. The man believed it was a child that wanted to be baptised.
204116: On the Heikant people used to be jumped by the werewolf, which had itself carried a short way.
204117: A man from Mal, whose mother was suspected of being the mare, had been advised to hold a knife on his chest at night with the point upward. The next morning his mother lay dead on his chest.
204127: One Saturday a man went with his father to fetch fodder for the ox. Suddenly the horse stopped for no clear reason. Then the animal jumped over an obstacle the driver could not see. The same thing happened on the way back.
204134: At midnight the witches would sing and dance in a meadow. When the dance was over, the witches flew home over hedges and hawthorns. But one of the witches had made a mistake when speaking the magic formula. Instead of "over hedges and hawthorns" she had said "through hedges and hawthorns", so she got stuck on the way.
204136: A little boy had been given a holy picture by a witch to pin on his cap. The boy went blind, had constant misfortune and cried out all the time: "Mummy, she's stabbing me!"
204151: In Paal lived a witch who sometimes went about in the shape of a cat. One day someone broke the cat's leg. The next day the woman had a broken arm.
204153: A werewolf was a man in a bearskin who roamed the Colmont woods. When the werewolf stood in the middle of the street, people did not dare to pass. If you could make a werewolf bleed, you could recognise him.
204159: When people had crossed the bridge between Borkel and Schaft, they were sometimes chased by a large headless dog. The dog never harmed anyone, however.
204161: One day Renk saw a large pack of cats coming down the hill. The man resolved to stamp the next cat he saw to death. A little later a cat appeared with terrifying glowing eyes. Renk was so frightened that he did not dare to harm the animal.
204169: One evening two farmhands went poaching in the 'Roeren'. One of them carried a sack holding two dead hares. Suddenly the farmhands heard a voice from the sack saying: "Anne-Katrien, where are you?" The farmhands ran home as fast as they could.
204178: Fat Rik went somewhere one evening to fetch a kitten. When Rik came back over the bridge with the animal, he suddenly heard a voice saying: "Marianneke, Marianneke, where are you?" Another voice answered: "In Fat Rik's sack." Rik was so frightened that he promptly dropped the cat and ran home.
204180: A farmer's wife had a maid who could not get her work done alone. When the maid was churning butter, she struck the wall with the spatula. The next moment white mice were crawling up the wall. Then the maid struck the wall with the spatula again, whereupon all the windowpanes suddenly fell to the ground. She was a witch who had learned her arts from a little book.
204190: A soldier on guard duty at night saw a white lady with a long veil walking back and forth. A few days later the soldier found the courage to ask the apparition: "Madam, what do you want? Have you lost your way?" But the white lady did not answer. On the fourth night the man said to the apparition: "If you are of good, speak. If you are of evil, vanish!" At that the white lady vanished. The soldier never saw the apparition again.
204199: A woman coming home from the fair in Neerweert suddenly heard chains rattling behind her. But when the woman saw nothing, she ran home in fright.
204210: White cats were always roaming near the house of the witch Mina C.
204213: Although Rikus S. did not own a horse, there was always horse dung in his meadow. Because Rikus wanted to know whose horse was coming to eat his grass, he kept watch one night. As Rikus stood there, he suddenly heard a voice and someone struck him hard in the face. Yet there was no one to be seen far and wide. Rikus knew very well who the witch was, but he believed nothing could be done against someone who was invisible.
204217: A man returning from a visit to his girlfriend in Rekem saw a little light on the way that followed him the whole time. At a certain moment the light went out. Then the man was accompanied by a large dog. After the man made the sign of the cross, the dog had disappeared.
204244: When Toon V. was walking from Dorplein to Budel one evening, a werewolf suddenly jumped onto his neck. After Toon had carried the werewolf for a while, he carefully strangled the creature.
204248: In Neerpelt lived a little boy who was always climbing on everything. One day a woman said: "Let me help you", and she pushed little Jan up with her hand. At that moment the boy felt a terrible pain. Jan had an open wound that never healed.
204253: In a house in Beersel a rat had come in through the drain hole for the water. When a man tried to catch the rat, the animal suddenly vanished. That rat was probably a witch.
204262: In the Genkstraat and on the road to Rutten there used to be haunted houses.
204280: A man from Kerkhoven was coming home late one evening. When he saw a big black cat on the way, he said: "Puss, you're chasing mice so late!" The cat replied: "Yes, if you had not spoken, I would have broken your neck!"
204285: In Overrepen lived a little boy who could make as many mice as he wanted. When the priest saw after catechism class that the boy could make mice, he had the child overlezen (exorcised by reading prayers over him).
204304: A witch tormented a hunter by making sure his gun did not work. After one of the hunters had his gun blessed by the priest, a hare cried: "Are you going to shoot me dead now?"
204307: At the farm by the little castle of Eversel, the dog always started barking at nine o'clock in the evening. The chaplain then put something under the thresholds.
204308: Every evening a phantom coach drove around the yard of a farm. But when people went outside to look, they saw nothing. The doors of the farm opened by themselves.
204322: A woman worked in a café in Tongeren that was haunted at night. The glasses could be heard rattling then, and in the morning the drawers had all been pulled open.
204330: A witch lived with the C. family. A large black dog always lay on the threshold of the house. One day the witch struck a man who was visiting her. The man's wound would not heal. After a few months the man had pastor N. read prayers over the wound. The wound healed in the end, but the man was left with a scar.
204335: A woman always carried a pincushion with her. Every time that woman came visiting somewhere and moved one of the pins to another spot, a sheep lay dead in the stable.
204347: In the Kruisstraat lived people who could not make butter. A strange old woman always came to ask for buttermilk. After the people, on the pastor's advice, stopped giving the woman anything, they could make butter again.
204348: Every evening a woman found little pieces of kindling wood in her bed. Because she did not know how the wood got into her bed, she went to the priest for advice, who said: "It is a dead person who comes to haunt. Next time you must ask what the ghost wants." When the woman did as she was told, a voice answered: "You still have to go on a pilgrimage to Sint-Gillis above Liège." The woman recognised the voice of her aunt, who had died not long before. The next day the woman went on pilgrimage to Liège together with a shepherd. On the way the woman said: "Do you see my aunt walking there, praying?", but the shepherd saw nothing. When the woman had prayed in the church in Liège, she saw a vapour rising and said: "Look, now she is released. She is going to heaven."
204352: A six-week-old baby whimpered all the time because it had been touched by the evil hand. It was so bad that the mother prayed that Our Lord would come and take the baby. At her wits' end, the mother went with a neighbour to a fortune teller in Liège. The fortune teller said: "Your child has been touched by the evil hand. In nine days it will vomit or get diarrhoea. After that the baby will recover. I will make sure the witch no longer comes into your house. But you must never say 'Come in' to her." The fortune teller was right and the baby recovered. The witch turned out to be a neighbour, Mie. One Sunday the woman was quarrelling with her husband while Mie was lingering in front of the door. The children, who did not know that Mie was a witch and could no longer come in, pulled the woman into the house. The witch, however, was extremely restless and could not sit down. The witch went back outside and never came back.
204367: At the Fagar farm two men met a dog and a cat. The cat jumped onto the dog's back and sat upright like a rider on a horse. Frightened, the men went on until they came to a café. In the café the men told what they had seen. When the others went outside to look, however, the dog and the cat had already vanished.
204371: A boy was spying on his girlfriend and saw her rub herself with witch's grease together with other witches. Then the witches said: "Over hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Aachen". When the witches had flown away, the boy also rubbed himself with witch's grease and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns to the wine cellar of Aachen". The poor boy arrived in Aachen covered in blood.
204377: One day the castle guard stopped a man. The guard asked: "Where do you come from?", but the man did not answer, stamped on the ground and went on along the railway. When the guard came back, he saw a man lying on the railway tracks a little further on. Before the guard could wake the man, the strange apparition had already stood up.
204388: Witches could give people lice. Anyone who was bewitched had to have the priest read prayers over them.
204389: On the Poeteveld (?) in Neeroeteren a ghost walked about that had been banished from the farmyard for ninety-nine years. When that period was over, the ghost would come and break everyone's neck.
204397: On Christmas night at twelve o'clock the church bells could be heard ringing underground in Mulhem.
204404: When Bel V.G. was going to the fair in Vlijtingen, he saw a white lady at the Heilige Haag who disappeared at the Lippenberg.
204411: Will-o'-the-wisps flew through the air above the Kranewijer. They were the little souls of unbaptised children. In the middle of the Kranewijer the lights came back down.
204421: Witches could fly over the Maas and the Rhine all the way to Cologne after saying: "Over hedges and thickets into the wine cellar".
204422: Farmer B. had sold a fine, healthy horse. When the farmer had to deliver the horse, the animal stood paralysed in the stable. The horse had been touched by the evil hand. The next day the horse was healed.
204445: Witches flew about on a broom after saying: "Over hedges and hawthorns". A man who wanted to imitate the witches made a mistake when speaking the magic formula and said: "Through hedges and hawthorns". The man had severe injuries to his face.
204455: A man returning from Bree through the Bocholterstraat quickly hid in a hedge when he saw thirty bokkenrijders (goat riders, a gang of robbers said to ride goats through the air) plundering a farm. The man had recognised the bokkenrijders by a certain sign. One of the robbers had to keep watch outside with a bucket of water to which a knife was attached. If the knife began to tremble, they had to flee like lightning, because then someone had betrayed them.
204461: Witches could be recognised in various ways. One could, for example, make the sign of the cross behind a woman's back. If she then looked round, she was a witch, and one had best make oneself scarce as quickly as possible.
204464: A woman was pushing a wheelbarrow full of beets home. On the way the woman met a witch, who laid her hand on the wheelbarrow. The next moment the wheelbarrow was empty. Then the witch said: "You must not tell anyone about this. I will help you fill the wheelbarrow again".
204473: A man had been given a bowl of milk by a woman who was suspected of being a witch. While the man was eating his milk, he tasted it slowly turning sour.
204474: A man whose child lay crying all the time said furiously: "If he dares to cry once more, I'll wring the witch's neck!" After that the child did not cry anymore.
204479: A little boy could make little mice from a handful of sand. After the priest had overlezen (read exorcism prayers over) the boy, he could no longer make mice.
204482: A man who lived at the castle farm had been to the fair in Hoepertingen. When he got home, he went to the kitchen to get something to eat. But when he came into the kitchen, he saw a white lady leaning against the chimney. The man went upstairs in fright, hoping the lady would not follow him. When he entered his bedroom, he heard a loud crash as if the whole house were collapsing. The next day nothing strange could be found. The baron of the castle also claimed that white ladies often appeared. This happened because someone had once wrongfully taken possession of the castle.
204485: A sick baby that cried all the time could not be helped by the doctor. Because people suspected the child was bewitched, the neighbour advised cutting open the child's pillow. The pillow turned out to be full of feathers. Then the pastor came and read prayers over the child until the sweat dripped from his face. Relics were also placed under the door. When the child died, it was full of lice.
204489: Stef V. was known everywhere as a man with sticky fingers. So when some rabbits were stolen in the neighbourhood, Stef was suspect number one. When Fons van Trui K., in a drunken mood, accused the man of the theft, Stef cried out furiously that the devil could come and fetch him if he had really committed the theft. Since that day Stef has never been seen again. The devil must really have come to fetch him.
204503: Moazere Mina came out and stroked a horse that was drinking. After that the horse could go no further; it was as if the animal were nailed to the ground.
204520: A man sitting and talking in a house in Achel suddenly felt a fierce itching on his back. When he got home, he found he was covered in fleas. The woman of that house had done it to him.
204544: A mother had been to the fair with her son. On the way back the son had to go relieve himself. Meanwhile the mother saw a werewolf coming and threw her red handkerchief at the beast. When her son came back, the mother saw that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
204545: A man saw a white lady who called out: "The days are for you and the nights are for me."
204547: The area around U.'s farm was haunted. Sometimes at night a white singing figure was seen floating around the farm.
204553: A man walking home through the snow in the evening saw a grey werewolf walking on the Zavelberg.
204557: Two men coming back from the woods saw lots of kittens.
204595: Witches were women who did evil and consorted with the devil. They had power especially over children. A wreath of feathers was often found in the bed of a bewitched child. Pastors were very often consulted to read prayers over bewitched children. Witches never wore a cross and they could not enter a house where a cross hung.
204605: A woman coming back from Schurhoven heard beautiful music and saw cats dancing.
204608: A man saw a castle floating in the sky. Because the castle seemed to be coming straight at him, he made the sign of the cross. The next moment the castle had disappeared.
204614: A little boy could make mice from earth. He could do it until he was baptised.
204617: A ghost used to roam in Gotem. A farmer crossing a bridge with horse and cart was pushed into the water and drowned.
204631: In a little street in Neerharen there was a hedge that sometimes chewed the cud like an animal.
204632: Some boys walking home in the evening saw ghosts in white sheets sitting by the road. The boys were so frightened that they went on by another road.
204635: At the D. family's in Bloir, the animals were always breaking loose. One morning they discovered that the best bull was dead. A witch lived nearby.
204639: Two men from Stokkem went to Maaseik to fetch the midwife. On the way the men met a black cat. That was surely a witch from the neighbourhood who wanted to bring the devil upon the child. The child's parents had to be very careful, because witches were always the first to come and visit a newborn child.
204647: In the churchyard around the castle of Rotem a clergyman and his sexton came to haunt with a bell. Everyone who had seen the ghosts fainted on the spot. The ghosts took curious people with them to the castle tower.
204649: In the old days near Maarheze there was a werewolf that stole chickens. The werewolf often had itself carried by jumping onto people's necks. If you provoked the werewolf, it bit through your neck. Someone managed to strangle the werewolf.
204650: Little Dries lay crying all night and often sat up in his cradle. After a pastor had read prayers over the child three times, it slept peacefully.
204656: A boy coming back from the fair with his girlfriend turned into a werewolf. The girl threw a handkerchief at the animal's mouth. The next day she saw to her great dismay that her boyfriend still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
204659: Ever since the day a man had come to stroke the cows in the stable, all the cows were barren.
204670: The count of Bûlingen (?) came back to haunt after his death. The ghost came riding in a coach with four horses. All the doors would then fly open. The priest banished the count with chains between stones.
204673: A man saw a little cat sitting on a bridge. When the man tried to kick the cat into the water, he was scratched. In the end the man died of his wound. That cat was a witch.
204674: A man from Opgrimbie claimed that his house was bewitched. When the man left a cigar on the table in the evening, the next day the cigar was full of maggots.
204675: A man drove along the Hooiweg with a horse and cart. Strangely enough, the horse left an imprint of its horseshoe in a stone.
204688: A boy was courting a girl from Repen. Every time the boy went back home, his girlfriend walked part of the way with him. As soon as the girl turned back, a little grey cat appeared and accompanied the boy further. One day the boy discovered that his girlfriend was a witch who could change herself into a cat.
204710: In the millers' quarter people were afraid when a donkey with jingling bells passed by at night.
204713: In a meadow in Berg the horses were completely covered in sweat every morning. When people kept watch in the meadow at night, they saw the horses begin to gallop wildly at midnight. When someone stabbed a knife into the horse's mane, a woman suddenly fell to the ground.
204716: A man out at night met a little dog. When the man struck the animal, it began to bleed and changed into a human.
204725: When Bernard V.L. came out of church, he said to his wife: "When I am dead, I will come back." Later people said that Bernard had indeed come back to haunt after his death.
204740: When a witch went to ask a woman for buttermilk, the woman answered: "Later". The next moment the barrel was full of toads.
204741: An old woman on her deathbed wore a leather bandage because her shoulder was broken. She asked her daughter to offer that leather bandage at Scherpenheuvel after her death. The daughter promised to go to Scherpenheuvel with her husband Guillaume. But because the funeral had brought a lot of commotion, the daughter did not go to Scherpenheuvel right away. One night the daughter was terrified to see her dead mother walking back and forth beside her bed. She went to the priest, who said: "Yes, the body dies, but the soul does not. The night-time apparition was surely your mother's soul. You must go to Scherpenheuvel." The next day the woman went to Scherpenheuvel with her husband, where they offered the leather bandage. After that all was quiet.
204745: When a man rode his bicycle over a spot where a witch had just spat on the ground, the bicycle fell over.
204761: When Pieke saw a dog lying at a turnstile, he reached for his knife. The next moment the dog ran away.
204767: A farmer whose cows always fell ill sent for the pastor. The pastor took good care of the sick cow and in the evening laid a blanket over the animal's back. In the morning, however, the blanket lay folded in the manger. Then the pastor said to the farmer: "You must close up that hole in the stable properly, so there is no more draught." Once the farmer had closed the hole, all his animals stayed healthy.
204768: A witch sat in the chimney and dropped soot into the food.
204770: One evening a man from Borgloon was walking home along the Kattensteegje near the Donkerstraat. A foal lay on the ground blocking his way. Because the man had heard of witches who could change themselves into horses, he took his stick and said: "Let me pass, in the name of God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Spirit!" The foal turned so that the man could walk on. The man had gone only a few metres when the foal called: "Come back, come back!" But the man went on without looking back.
204779: A woman who had watched a moving television report in the evening was tormented by the mare all night.
204785: In Laak a little woman with a little black dog always came to visit people. When the schoolchildren saw the little woman, they shouted: "Witch woman!" One day the little woman was, as usual, drinking a dram in the café. After she let one of the children drink from her glass, the child got a swollen throat.
204788: Trui V.G. often came to play cards with a family in Stamprooi. Because Trui was a witch, however, her company was not much appreciated. One day they did not let Trui in, since there were already enough players for cards. Although all the doors were locked, Trui still got in. To do that she must have changed herself into a cat.
204799: Drikes M. from the Kamert went with his brother to visit his girlfriend in Zolder. When the boys saw a cat sitting on a post along the way, Drikes knocked the animal to the ground with a medlar-wood stick. A little later the cat jumped back onto the post and said: "Damn it, strike me again if you dare!" But the boys were so frightened that they quickly ran away.
204804: A boy was going out with a girl from Eggertingen. Although people had already warned him that the girl was a witch, the boy did not want to end the relationship. Every evening the boy went to the girl's house: he would knock on her window and wait until she appeared. One day the boy arrived at the girl's house only late. The boy tapped on the window several times, but the girl did not come. Because the little window was ajar, the boy pushed it open and leaned in. With a long stick he felt around in the girl's bed, but it was empty. When the boy was about to go home, a small white kitten came running up. The animal jumped onto the windowsill and went into the room. A little later the boy heard someone snoring in the room. He called his girlfriend's name, which woke her up. To be sure, he felt in the bed with the stick again, and this time he felt her. The girl came over to see him. After that evening the boy never went to see the girl again.
204805: In the Hondsstraat in Rutten there was a haunted house. The husband of the woman who lived there had died.
204810: A witch often untied the animals in the stable.
204815:
In Limburg 118 witch trials took place. Among the witches were 6 men.
On a bridge over the Jeker a black dog always sat panting with its mouth open. One Saturday evening, in a nearby café, a bet was made in which a man was challenged to go and put a handkerchief in the dog's mouth. After the man had done so, a strange fellow came into the café and ordered a glass of beer. When he opened his mouth, they saw that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
204822: Jang worked for an old woman for whom he had to carry toads out of the cellar every evening. When Jang got swollen hands one day, he left the old woman.
204825: The men of M.'s farm were threshing grain. Suddenly one of them walked to the meadow. In the meadow lay the carcass of a calf that had just died and still had to be buried. The man took out a knife and began cutting big pieces of meat from the calf. He ate almost half the animal. When the man came back, he said: "I feel so sluggish today!", to which another said: "I can well believe it; you've eaten half a calf!"
204826: To find out whether a woman was a witch, you had to place your feet crossed in her path. If the woman looked back, you knew she was a witch. If the witch then made that person stand still as if nailed to the ground, some misfortune would befall him that same day.
204829: The lord of the castle, M., was a socialist. When a woman had to prepare the man's deathbed, she was frightened because the light suddenly went out while there was still paraffin in the lamp. The same thing happened a second time. On the ground floor lay a large black dog, which disappeared a little later.
204833: Some people were sitting around the fire one evening telling stories when suddenly a beautiful coach with white horses appeared. A little later the coach had vanished again.
204850: A baron lived at Munnik-hof in Boorsem. The baron's daughter had a relationship with the son of the count who lived at the castle of Rekem. Because the count was not pleased with the girl's background, the two lovers jumped into the well so that they could be together forever. Shortly afterwards the baron died of grief. After the baron's death the castle was given to the friars. Ever since the suicide of the two lovers, the castle was haunted.
204856: In Bommershoven lived a woman whose child was bewitched. The feathers in the pillow the child slept on had all formed wreaths. Shortly afterwards the child died, and a few days later the woman's husband died too.
204859: A mother went with her sick baby to a clergyman in Sint-Walburg (Liège). The clergyman said: "Madam, I am going to light a candle. In a moment someone will ring the bell. Your child must then open the door." A little later the bell did ring and the child went to the door. At that moment the clergyman could see in the candle wax the hand of an old woman pinching a child's little ear. Then the clergyman said: "Madam, you will find out who the witch is. Tonight she will call on you and ask to light the stove." And so it happened. The next day the witch came by again. This time she brought little statues of saints to lay on the sick child. Because the baby was very restless at night, the mother put the statues in the little bed. The father, who had seen it, became angry and made his wife take the statues away again. That night the witch died. When the parents went to the clergyman in Sint-Walburg again, the man said: "Luckily you took the statues away. Otherwise the baby would have died together with the witch."
204867: Will-o'-the-wisps moved up and down in a meadow. They were the little souls of unbaptised children.
204874: A man was driving to the field with his farmhand in the morning. Suddenly the farmhand said: "May God hold you," and the man asked: "What's the matter with you?" The farmhand said: "Didn't you just see those three white beguines above the Canadian poplars?"
204876: In the old days a man often met a white lady on the road to Vliermaal. She never spoke a word and did no one any harm.
204877: When a man had thrown a cat down through the attic window, he heard the animal cry: "You might well have killed me!" The cat was the man's neighbour.
204896: A farmer who had gone to Widooie to fetch bundles of brushwood heard, on the way back, the music of witches holding a gathering on Sleiberg. Suddenly the horses stopped as if nailed to the ground. Since the animals would no longer pull the cart, the farmer told his farmhand to unhitch them. When the farmer and the farmhand went to fetch the cart the next day with two horses, they saw a witches' circle in the distance. A man from Lauw found a golden cup there with a name and address on it. The man took the chalice back to the owner of a fabric shop in Hasselt. As a reward he received two free tailor-made suits, on condition that he tell no one about the chalice.
204911: A farmer whose animals always lay tangled in their chains in the stable sent for a clergyman. When a woman entered the stable, the clergyman forced her to undo the harm she had done. Otherwise she would be burned alive. A little later the animals were standing up again.
204920: Jamar's farmhand was often followed by a strange dog. On the advice of his friends, the farmhand one day threw a red handkerchief at the animal's mouth. If the animal was stopped by the handkerchief, the farmhand would know for certain that it was a werewolf. The next day the farmhand saw that his roommate still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
204921: One day a goat with a chain came out of the meadow at the V. family's home. The goat came into the house and went up the stairs.
204936: During the war Theike went to have a few sacks of grain ground at the miller's. On the way Theike met a widow, who offered to help him carry the sacks. "But how can this be?", said Theike, "Just now I carried the sacks all by myself, and now that you are helping me, I can't manage anymore! Let go of those sacks!" Then the witch let go of the sacks while laughing at the man.
204938: Peter and Michiel S. went to take two girls to Hoelbeek. On the way back it seemed as if both men had sulphur in their hair. Moreover, a strange thistle stood in the middle of the road. The next day Peter and Michiel saw a cat, which said: "If you had trampled that thistle, we would not have been done with you yet!" The two girls had turned themselves into a cat.
204943: Four merchants and a young man sat in a café talking about a bush that was haunted. Because the young man did not believe in ghosts, they made a bet. The young man had to go and cut a branch from the bush at twelve o'clock at night. When the young man was about to cut into the bush, he heard a voice calling: "Ow ow ow!" The young man immediately dropped his knife and ran away.
204949: A woman was visited by a witch who was hawking safety pins. When the woman refused to buy anything, the hawker became angry and threw the pins on the table. Some time later the woman's baby died. The woman had used the safety pins after all to fasten the child's nappies. The pins were probably bewitched.
204963: A woman who had visited her daughter in Hamont was walking home in the evening. When the mother came to the castle of l' Escaille, she suddenly saw something moving among the trees. She thought she saw an ugly old woman with long teeth. Although the mother was afraid, she came a little closer. Among the bushes lay the black handkerchief of the lady of the castle, who had died a week before.
204965: A woman cutting grass had laid her baby on the ground beside her. When a big dog came running up, the woman cut off one of its paws with her sickle. Strangely enough, a human hand then lay on the ground. The next day a man with one hand was walking around the village.
204994: In Grootloon lived a witch who was said to harm her own children. As long as her children were under twelve, they had no problems. But from the moment the children had received Holy Confirmation, their mother struck them on the shoulder every day, so that they got a hunchback and grew a little smaller each day. In the end the children collapsed completely and died. When the witch herself died, she had a child who was not yet twelve and so had not yet been exposed to the evil. That child stayed healthy and lived to a very old age.
205001: The witches often held gatherings and parties in the woods of Stamprooi. One day a man saw witches dancing near S.'s farm. The witches held hands and danced in a circle. After the man had made the sign of the cross, the witches vanished at once.
205006: In Rutten lived a woman who always wore a little white cap. One day the woman caused a merchant from Lauw to drive his cart into a pond.
205018: In Zonhoven lived a witch who had caused two of her three children to die.
205025: A hunter had shot a hare and thrown it by the side of the road. A little later he heard a hare call: "Hey Trien, where are you?", whereupon the shot hare answered: "Here I lie!" The hunter threw his gun on the ground and quickly took to his heels.
205028: At the castle of Alden Biesen there was always a little rabbit sitting in front of the barrier. Nobody managed to catch that rabbit.
205031: On a farm in Membruggen the master, the farmer's wife, the farmhand and the maid had made a bet. They had dared each other to fetch a skull from the churchyard. The master decided to go to the churchyard first. But just as the man was about to take a skull, a voice rang out: "That is my head!" The man threw down the skull and ran away. The same then happened to the farmer's wife and the farmhand. Because the master, the farmer's wife and the farmhand had been scared to death in the churchyard, they advised the maid not to go. But the girl was determined to win the bet. When the maid picked up a skull in the churchyard, the voice again called: "That is my head!" The clever maid replied: "Surely you didn't have four heads!" The girl took the skull and won the bet.
205043: The wild hunt that flew through the air had something to do with the devil. A soldier who preferred reading his devil's book to going to church was carried off by the wild hunt in the Dorpsstraat in Rotem. The soldier saw lots of beautiful women dancing and having fun. When the soldier said: "Serdju," all the women suddenly vanished.
205057: Will-o'-the-wisps were lost little souls that could not enter heaven.
