205079: A man who always got sweets from an old woman saw an owl come in through the chimney one night. The man did not manage to catch the owl. Shortly afterwards the man's daughter fell ill. The child had fallen ill because of the witch who had changed herself into an owl.
205083: When Pier was going to Zonhoven station, he was jumped on by something at the Planken Brug.
205084: A man who had been playing cards walked home in the evening. By a ditch the man suddenly saw a strange horse come walking up. A little later the horse had vanished.
205085: Bert W. had bought a horse at the market in Weert. When Bert passed the house of Nel J., the horse suddenly refused to go any further. Nel came outside and said: "Come and have a drink, then the horse will want to go on." When Bert had had a drink, the animal could indeed go on again.
205086: In Berg lived a woman who was said to be a witch. A man from Beersel had gone into the woman's house and drunk a cup of coffee there. Afterwards the man was beaten by an invisible figure.
205088: A man going to the police in the evening suddenly saw six large white cats walking ahead of him.
205108: When the church of Budel was taken over by the Protestants, one of the five bells flew out of the tower. In the Kattenkuil the sunken bell could still be heard ringing on Christmas night.
205109: Two friends were out walking when one of them suddenly said: "I have to go relieve myself." When a black dog appeared a little later, the other threw his red handkerchief at the animal's mouth. When the men were back together, the first still had the red fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
205112: Every evening a werewolf came tapping on the window at H.'s house. When the people came to look out of the window, the werewolf ran away laughing. One day, however, H. had caught the beast. Huygen carried the big black dog on his back to the priest. Because the dog struggled so much, the man did not dare to cross the Demer for fear of falling into the water. So he had to let the dog go.
205115: The castle of the Oude Biezen in Rijkhoven was haunted. Every night the horses left their stable for no explicable reason. People could drive all the horses back inside except one. One night some farmhands were once again trying to coax that one horse into the stable. The horse jumped over the dung heap and grew bigger and bigger. A black cat also often sat on a wall by the castle. One day some men had knocked the cat off the wall. When the men came back past that spot, there were at least ten cats, which chased them. During the mobilisation not a single soldier of the 8th artillery wanted to stay near the castle. In the past a land commander of the Teutonic Order had lived in the castle. The man had got into financial difficulties and had sold his soul to the devil. The room where the devil had murdered the man was haunted for a long time. The room was opened for the first time in 1914 for a German officer.
205118: A woman stood next to a witch in the shop. The woman could no longer move a foot, after which the witch said: "You'll just have to stay standing for a while."
205125: After a man had shot at a hare, the animal sat up on its hind legs and beckoned to him. Another time the man's gun did not work.
205132: At night four ghosts appeared in the Spouwerstraat, took a coffin out of G.'s farm and carried it to Triene N.'s house.
205133: Nier and Mie went to pray in the chapel of Membruggen to be cured of their toothache. Suddenly Nier saw a witch standing behind them. It was a woman of the Meumerke family. The witch seemed to float and she blew over the two praying women. Nier and Mie then quickly fled. When she was back home, Mie no longer had toothache.
205142: A man who gave drama lessons in Maaseik in the evenings always had to carry the werewolf on the way home. Later it turned out to be his pupils, who wanted to frighten him.
205154: A man from Berg had not kept his promise to go on a pilgrimage. After his death the man walked back and forth as a ghost along the pilgrims' road.
205159: Werewolves were only seen at night. They were people who could change into a dog.
205162: Heksebetje lived on the road to Trootsje. Whenever a carter drove his wagon past Heksebetje's house, the horses always stopped. Only when the witch went inside could the horses go on again.
205166: A man and a woman walking along a sunken lane saw a calf lying in the middle of the road. When the pair came closer, the calf jumped up. A little further on the man and the woman looked back and found that the calf had vanished and a meowing cat was standing in the road.
205171: A girl learned from her father that there were different kinds of stars in the sky. Besides the Mary stars there were, for example, the seven stars and the wagon star. One day, however, they saw a star with a tail. Such a star was considered an omen of war. Shortly afterwards the First World War did indeed break out.
205172: An old man went to pray at the chapel for nine days. On the third day the man saw a beguine approaching with a golden key in her hand. After the old man had told the pastor everything, he found the courage to go back to the chapel. There the beguine stood again and said: "Now you must follow me. I have wandered here for a hundred and fifty years, but I never had the chance to show anyone the money hidden in the cellar. You must not leave a single coin behind". The man went home immensely rich.
205181: Because the friars of Rekem wanted to build a new church, they went to fetch a heavy stone in the woods of Lanklaar. When the friars reached Opgrimbie, a black cat suddenly ran under the cart. The moment the friars ran over the cat with their cart, the two horses fell dead. That heavy stone was later called 'the Duivelssteen' (Devil's Stone).
205195: A ghost always appeared by the church and said: "I promised to go on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel, but I was never able to fulfil that promise. You must do it for me."
205197: A child who had been touched by a witch fell ill and got a fever. That same night the child died.
205224: The castle of Printhagen used to be haunted. At midnight a coach drove through the lane and came back a little later. The castle gates opened and closed by themselves.
205244: A boy who had shot at a hare discovered that the animal was his own mother.
205246: A farmer who suddenly could no longer churn butter went to the fathers in Belgium, since it was said of those fathers that they could overcome the evil hand. After the farmer, on a father's advice, had sprinkled salt around the spout of the churn, he could make butter again.
205249: A man who was ill sent for the bishop, because people believed the man was bewitched. A key hung on the wall, and at the stroke of twelve it began to turn. The key did not turn all the way round, for then the man would have died. After the bishop had come, the key had disappeared. The man soon recovered.
205254: In a small Walloon village lived a girl whose predictions all came true. One day a friar visiting the parish wanted to talk with her. When the friar came in, the girl said: "You are Father N.", and she went on to tell all sorts of things about him. The friar then asked her: "Can you also tell what time it is on my watch?" The friar did not know himself, because while he was talking he had deliberately turned the hands. The girl knew. Then the girl told the friar that she was always beaten by a figure with a cloth around his head, invisible to other people. The friar went to the bishop, who granted him special powers, and he advised the girl to ask the figure next time who he was. "I am Satan," the apparition answered, "and if you saw me, you would die at once." While the friar tried to drive out the devil, the girl was flung to the ground. The friar succeeded in delivering the girl, but he himself died a few days later.
205256: In Koersel there lived a witch who had two fireballs standing on her wall. Parents advised their children not to make the witch angry, because that was dangerous. A boy who would not listen went to tease the witch anyway. After the witch had tapped the boy on the shoulder with a little stick, the boy walked to a meadow, where he kept walking round and round in a witches' circle. Only after two men had gone to fetch him was he saved.
205262: A man going alone to fetch the midwife was startled when a black cat suddenly jumped onto the back of his bicycle. The man knocked the cat to the ground, but it always jumped back onto the bicycle. The man believed the cat was the devil, waiting for the child that was to be born. Suddenly the cat changed shape and said that something would happen if the man struck one more time. Since then nobody dared to go and fetch the midwife alone.
205274: At the Tingerhoeve there was a farmhand who turned into a werewolf. When the farmer had found his farmhand's collar in a tree stump, he sent the farmhand to Maastricht so that he would have the chance to burn the collar. When the collar caught fire, the farmhand was instantly standing by the oven.
205280: Some men, among them Free V.D., went mowing at the castle of Heylandt in autumn. At night the men slept in the barn opposite the watermill, so that they could start mowing at four in the morning. One evening one of the men went home with a friend to fetch clean clothes. On the way back the men met a pack of cats that would not leave them alone. When the men finally got into the barn, they could no longer find their sleeping place. Suddenly one man said to the other: "Stand still or you'll fall off the loft." It was Free who had made them no longer know where they were.
205282: In the evening people were often jumped on by cats that gave them lice.
205286: A man tried in vain to catch a kitten that was walking beside him on the road. Only Ber and Maria, two women suspected of being witches, could catch the kitten.
205287: A timber merchant from Nieuwerkerken went to the Kempen to fetch pine trees. In the pine forest he came upon dozens of women, among them three ladies from Nieuwerkerken. When these three women saw him, they threatened: "If you tell anyone you have seen us here, things will go badly for you." Back in Nieuwerkerken, the timber merchant asked everyone whether the three women had been away. He was told that the women had stayed in the village all day. The timber merchant only dared to tell his story once the three women were dead.
205292: A man coming back from Zutendaal saw at the foot of the hills a priest walking and praying with a breviary in his hands. The man said "Good evening", but the priest did not answer. It was the 'heipastoor' (heath priest), who had to come back to haunt after his death as a punishment.
205308: A man who often went to the pub in the evening was always jumped by the werewolf. Because the man was rather sturdily built, people would not believe he had had to carry the werewolf. "You go and walk down that street yourselves!" the man would then shout angrily.
205310: At a haunted brook, people all came to pray. A little boy claimed he saw a ghost holding out a book to him. The boy's father said: "If you take the book, I'll give you a watch." But the ghost had changed its place. After a while the ghost no longer appeared.
205312: The wild hunt always passed Gijsen-Kapel heading towards Neerglabbeek. Then wonderfully beautiful music was heard, in which all the birds were imitated.
205313: A tree grower from Alken was walking through the fields to Stevoort. A boy of seven or eight named Philtjens always saw a child appear by a thick oak in Stevoort. Many curious people had come to look, but only Philtjens could see the ghost. One evening the tree grower decided to take a look at the oak himself. Philtjens was there too and claimed that the ghostly child was standing in front of him with a book in its hands. The tree grower then said: "Take the book. If you can show it to me, I'll give you a watch." Philtjens, however, did not want to take the book. A little later Philtjens claimed that the ghost with the book was standing in front of the tree grower. However hard the tree grower tried, he felt nothing in his hands when he tried to grab the invisible book. Eight days later the tree grower passed the oak during a thunderstorm when he suddenly saw a strange dog appear. It looked as if the animal had no legs. When the man tried to hit the dog, the animal ran away. A little later the man heard a rustling in the hedge, but nothing appeared. The man was convinced that all these bizarre events were a punishment for the time he had tried to grab the ghostly child's book.
205324: When werewolves were teased by people, they made rats and mice.
205333: In a farmhouse there was a hole in the wall through which a black dog always came in. That dog was the devil. People had often tried to brick up the hole, but they never succeeded. No farmer wanted to come and live in that farmhouse any more.
205342: Jef V.L. was going out with a girl whose mother was suspected of being a witch. One day the boy did not go to his girlfriend but to someone else. Meanwhile Jef's sister happened to call on his girlfriend's mother and asked: "Isn't our Jef here?", to which the mother replied: "No, he's over there!" That evening the sister learned that her brother Jef had indeed been at that very place.
205350: The will-o'-the-wisps seen by the water were the souls of unbaptised children.
205355: In the Repenstraat lived a woman whose newborn son cried all the time. The neighbour, who was half a witch, said to the weary mother every morning: "You didn't get any rest again last night, did you?" And in the evening she said: "Sleep well this time!" When the witch had broken her leg, the mother visited her neighbour in hospital. After the mother had had the friars read prayers over her child, it slept peacefully.
205356: In Rosmeer, earth from the churchyard was once taken to the Klein Veldje. Since then, will-o'-the-wisps were seen appearing on the Klein Veldje around midnight.
205366: A man told the sexton that he had often seen a hare running about but had never managed to hit it. "Wait a moment," said the sexton, "I'll give you a nail from the Easter candle to put in your gun." The next day the man shot the hare. When the man came home, he found his wife lying in bed with a bandage around her head.
205372: In Wellen there was a house that was haunted. Whoever stood in the house felt the ground sink away beneath their feet.
205379: Four men from Kerkhoven visited a family in Vlasmaal one evening. On the way back the men saw a black cat in the Kiefhoek. One of the men said to the animal: "Hey, pussy dear, where do you come from?" When the men met the cat again at a café further on, the animal said: "Well, Rik F., didn't you say pussy dear, where do you come from?" The men turned deathly pale and did not dare say another word. The cat went on: "If Rik F. had not spoken so nicely, I would have broken his neck."
205391: A child saw a dead woman sitting on a rustas (a pole resting across the beams) in the barn. The child ran inside and said: "I saw auntie sitting on a rustas." But the others did not see the apparition. The dead woman had promised to go on a pilgrimage, but she had not kept her promise. The next day the people went on pilgrimage to Koersel for the dead woman. "Look, auntie is coming across the water too," said the child.
205408: A witch made mice by throwing the earth of a molehill on the ground.
205412: In Paal lived a farmer whose cabbages were always eaten by hares. One day the farmer shot at a hare with his gun. The next day a neighbour woman lay sick in bed.
205418: On Broekberg the white lady walked back and forth in the evening.
205421: Veterinarian Jan D. had to go and tend the horse of Heksentrijneke in Hoelbeek one evening. When Jan walked back home, he saw that one of the Canadian poplars in the Witstraat was full of cats. The cats were quarrelling and one of the animals said: "Shall we get him, shall we get him, shall we get him." Then another cat said: "Yes, we'll get him, we'll get him, we'll get him." Next a third cat said: "We won't get him, we won't get him, we won't get him, because it's Janneke who cured the cow and who is now curing the horse too." Despite the third cat's protest, another cat still wanted to bewitch Jan. Because the cat blocked his way, Jan hit the animal on the head with his walking stick. When Jan came to Trijneke's the next day, he saw that she wore a bandage around her head. It had been Trijneke herself who had wanted to bewitch Jan.
205429: Witches could make people and animals fall ill and die.
205432: A woman whose son had died a month earlier was visited by her neighbour, who said: "Fien, your son's spirit is hanging above your house. I saw a big light". The next day a joiner came running up, drenched in sweat, and cried: "I was chased the whole way by a headless calf!" This frightened the woman so much that she no longer dared to go outside.
205439: Frans and Rik had gone poaching on the Kogelshei. When the two men reached the crossroads where Fien V.D.B. lived at night, Rik felt a big skinny tomcat rubbing against his legs. Because the men could not manage to chase the tomcat away, they suspected the animal was a witch. The men went on while the tomcat kept blocking their way. After a while Rik shouted in annoyance: "If you don't clear off now, damned tomcat, I'll shoot you dead!" The next moment the tomcat had disappeared.
205447: The witch Mie V.D.K. ran a café. When people came past the café with a horse and cart, they had better go inside for a moment. Meanwhile Mie came to give the horse a sugar lump. If people did not stop for a drink in the café, the horse could not go any further.
205448: Harie van Neel V. could do magic. He could make white mice and he could also conjure the money out of someone's purse. The priest took Harie's arts away from him.
205471: Karel W. was pestered by a cat that kept getting under his feet. When Karel struck at the cat, the animal ran to a hedge. As Karel passed the hedge, the cat called out: "And now just try striking me again!" Karel was so scared that he never dared strike a cat again.
205481: A woman carrying a bundle of beet leaves on her shoulders had to pass a little gate. When the gate opened by itself, the woman said gratefully: "God will reward you!" A voice replied: "I have waited a hundred years for that. Now I am released."
205483: People who were tormented by a witch found in the morning that their house had been turned completely upside down.
205489: A witch had bewitched her nephew's children. When the little ones had died, their cradles were burned. Fortunately, the children born after that did survive.
205501: A witch had caused a whole village to burn down.
205510: On the road to Piringen a young kitten always walked in the evening, following passers-by. A man had tried to catch the kitten, but had not succeeded. People hardly dared to go to that spot in the evening anymore.
205533: A witch from Nieuwerkerken had touched the rabbits in a hutch. The next day all the animals lay dead.
205537: Two men had caught a goat and stuck the animal into the ground by its horns. A little later an old woman came by, who said: "You won't be home soon!" The men wanted to go to the Planken Brug, but they ended up in Kiewit.
205541: On a farm where a woman often came by, a cow had fallen ill. The farmer went to the friars of Heusden to fetch a medal to put under the door. After a while, however, the cow died anyway. The witch never came by again.
205548: When a child was born, people always had to go to the midwife in pairs. It was very hard to get there, because the witches tried to stop people in all sorts of ways.
205550: When a cow had been struck by the evil hand, it could no longer stand up in the stable.
205554: If there were magpies somewhere, people knew that misfortune would come.
205557: Stijkmarie was often tormented by the mare at night. Some people put their clogs upside down beside the bed in the evening, so that the mare could not get onto the bed.
205565: A man had bought pigs from a woman who was said to be a witch. Most of the pigs soon died.
205567: In Zwartberg (Houthalen) lived a little child who could make mice because the chaplain had not baptised it properly.
205589: In the castle lane of Wideux lay a thick felled oak. Whenever the oak was removed, it lay back in its old place the next day. People believed it was a ghost oak.
205590: Some men were playing cards with a stranger in an inn in Horpmaal. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had cow's feet: it was the devil.
205608: A woman cutting spurry with a sickle was hindered in her work by a cat. Annoyed, the woman said: "Get away, or I'll cut you with the sickle!" Because the cat did not leave, the woman cut the animal on the snout. The cat then ran off meowing. The next moment the woman saw the witch standing behind her with a bloody nose. "Tell no one that it was me who pestered you like that. Otherwise I will wipe out your whole family," said the witch. When the woman went to church on Sunday, she told someone what had happened anyway. She urged that person not to pass the story on. The witch appeared in church with a bandage around her nose.
205614: A man out walking his dog passed a remote house where a witch lived. At that spot the dog suddenly stood still. When the man had made the sign of the cross, the dog could go on again.
205637: A man walking on the Bilzersteenweg between midnight and one o'clock suddenly saw a little rabbit on the road. When the man had picked up the rabbit, it immediately jumped away again and grew bigger. A little later the man picked up the rabbit again, after which it grew somewhat bigger once more. This happened several times until the man no longer dared to pick up the strangely large rabbit.
205658: A man coming home along a side path heard someone say: "Where must I put it?" After the man answered: "Well, put it where you took it from," a large stone suddenly fell to the ground behind him.
205659: In Guigoven lived some unbaptised children who could make mice from earth because they associated with the devil. After the children had been baptised by the priest, they could no longer make mice.
205673: A young man got lost every time he came back from a visit to his girlfriend. The boy always had to pass the house of an old woman. When he passed it, he suddenly found himself in a beautiful tree-lined lane. Only towards morning did the boy get home again. Someone advised the boy to take off his coat at the witch's house and stand on it. When the boy did so, everything stayed normal.
205684: On a farm there worked a farmhand who was a werewolf. One day the farmer sent the farmhand away for three hours to mow the heath. Meanwhile the farmer threw the farmhand's collar into the oven. When the band lay in the fire, the farmhand suddenly stood next to the oven, and it took four people to hold him back so that he would not pull the collar out of the fire. When everything had burnt up, the lad was released.
205685: Kait's daughter had an infection on her finger that would not heal. One day the girl met a woman who advised her to go and see her Kait, for people suspected that the girl was being bewitched by her own mother. So she went to her mother, who said: "You thought you didn't need your mother any more, didn't you, but now you see!" Two days later the girl's finger had healed.
205690: Anyone who wanted to join the witches and other agents of evil had to go out in the evening with a black hen. If one then met the devil, one could sell one's soul.
205706: At midnight some men heard banging in an old haunted castle. A big black man in boots came in and led the people to the cellar. In the cellar the ghost said: "Lift that lid". When the men answered: "Lift it yourself", the ghost had vanished.
205709: A woman who had gone to fetch a sack of wood or coal met a witch on the way back. The witch bewitched the sack onto the woman's shoulders.
205712: The castle of Opitter was haunted. At night the gates, doors and windows flew open and a hellish noise rang out. One day a certain Jan, a brave soldier just back from the army, wanted to spend the night in the castle. When Jan was baking cakes in the castle in the evening, a human head suddenly fell into the batter. Jan took the skull out of the batter, threw it into a corner and went on baking. A little later an arm fell into the batter, then a leg and finally even a whole torso. After Jan had thrown all the limbs into the corner, he saw that they had grown together. The skeleton wanted Jan to come closer, to which the soldier replied: "If you need me, you'll have to come yourself." The ghost came closer and led Jan to the cellar. In the cellar the skeleton lifted a stone under which three barrels of money were hidden: one for Jan, one for the pastor and one for the lord of the castle. Jan got thoroughly drunk on the money and then went to buy a new spinning wheel for his mother. Since then the castle of Opitter has no longer been haunted.
205721: A mother always received cabbages from a woman in the neighbourhood. Because the child always fell ill after eating the cabbage, the friars put a medal under the threshold so that the neighbour could no longer come in.
205741: A man walking through the meadow one morning was astonished to see his dead sister wandering about there. When he asked her what she wanted, the ghost answered: "I want a pilgrimage." During her life the woman had promised to go on a pilgrimage. But she had not kept that promise, so after her death she could find no rest.
205742: A farmer's wife simply could not make butter from the cows' milk. From a sorcerer she received a note that she had to put under the milk tub when she was going to make butter. One day a tailor was working at the farmer's wife's house, and he had seen a note being slipped under the milk tub. The tailor was so curious that he waited until the woman was away for a moment so he could quickly take the note. The tailor got a fright when the woman came back in, and in a panic he put the note in his mouth. When the woman began to stir the milk, butter ran out of the tailor's mouth. The note had so much power that it drew the butter, so that the witches could not spirit it away.
205745: A woman standing by a farm with a boy suddenly saw cats everywhere. The boy was bewitched. In the end a pilgrimage had to be made for the boy.
205755: A man who had it in for someone could turn himself into a werewolf and have himself carried by that person.
205762: A woman put some dishes of fresh butter on the floor when suddenly a cat came in and licked the butter for a moment. When the cat had gone, the woman cut off the top layer of the butter. By evening, however, the butter had turned completely red and stank terribly.
205763: Near Erpekom there was a werewolf that people had tried to shoot several times. Every time they tried, the gun did not work. After a blessed candle had been put into the gun, they were able to hit the werewolf. The beast was covered in blood and a little later took on its human form. It turned out to be a man from East Flanders or West Flanders.
205778: A man told a woman that every night he woke up sweating and could hardly breathe. When the man then wanted to call out, no sound came from his throat. The woman judged that the man was being ridden by the mare. "As long as you lie on your side, the mare can do nothing to you," the woman said. When the man asked what he could do to drive the mare away, the woman said: "You must make three signs of the cross over the bed with holy water in honour of the Holy Trinity. Then you must pray three Hail Marys and make three signs of the cross yourself as well. Then the mare will be gone." The man did what the woman had advised him. From then on he could sleep peacefully again.
205781: A man working in his field got a fright when a witch suddenly stood before him. She had laid her hand on his shoulder, after which the man was covered in lice. In the end he had to have the fathers of Sint-Truiden read prayers over him to be rid of the lice.
205782: A man walking to the airfield saw a black cat sitting on a wooden barrier. When the man tried to hit the cat with a stick, the animal sprang up and scratched the man's hands so that he had to let go of the stick.
205793: In the old days, when people saw an old woman or a black cat, they believed it was a witch.
205798: A girl had an inflamed wound on her knee that would not heal. One day a farmer's son from Arendonk came to visit, and the girl's mother told him about her little daughter's ailment. The farmer's son said: "I know someone who can cure that. Tomorrow I'll send a cart to pick up your little daughter." The next day mother and daughter set off in the evening to the healer. During the night, however, they got lost, so that in the morning they were back at the Vosvijvers where they had started. So the people decided to travel by day. When mother and daughter had arrived, the Menneke examined the knee and said: "I will pray over the knee a few times, and then the wound will heal. To be safe, you must stay here for a month." At night the mother slept with Lange Han, the farmer's wife, who was suspected of being a witch. "You needn't be afraid," the Menneke had said; "she may stroke your head, but I can master her." When the girl's knee had healed a month later, the Menneke said to the mother: "When you are home, the witch will come and ask how the child is. I will give you something to put under the threshold. That way the witch will not be able to come in." The next day Lange Han came by to ask how the girl was. Although Lange Han normally always came in, this time she stayed outside. For the first nine days the child's mother had to find three brown slugs and rub them on the girl's knee. The first two slugs then had to be buried; the other had to be thrown into the fire. The third slug had barely landed in the fire when Lange Han was at the door again. This time too, however, she could not come in. On the ninth day the girl's knee was completely healed. Lange Han was never seen again.
205802: The husband of a woman who had got lice through a witch consulted a sorcerer. The sorcerer went to the witch and thrashed her until she agreed to take the lice away again.
205803: An unbaptised boy threw a handful of ash from the stove on the ground and conjured mice. After the boy had been overlezen (exorcised by reading prayers over him) by the holy little father, to his great regret he could no longer make mice. The boy was so sad about this that he died shortly afterwards.
205804: A farmhand working on a farm met a werewolf and struck at the animal with a hook. When the werewolf took on his human form, it turned out to be the farmer's son.
205806: Martin S. always got lice whenever his girlfriend Thomas M. had patted him on the back.
205826: A farmer had a farmhand who went off every afternoon. The farmer had seen the farmhand crawl into a willow tree and then turn into a dog. In the willow the farmer found a collar. When the farmer was about to throw the band into the fire, the farmhand was instantly standing by the oven to save his band.
205838: In Stokkem there lived as many as five or six women who were said to be witches. A man from Stokkem always heard knocking on his door at night. From a fortune teller in Maastricht the man learned that the strange events had to do with a witch who lived nearby.
205850: When the sexton came back from the fair in Gelinden, he saw a large dog on the way. When the man reached the elm, the dog had suddenly vanished. The dog was the ghost of a dead man who had never gone to church.
205862: On Christmas night at twelve o'clock bells could be heard ringing in the spring of Membruggen, called 'de Kelderkes'. A monastery of the Templars once sank into that spring. People once tried to reach the bottom of the pit with a rod, but the pit was too deep.
205864: In Laar a man was mowing his field. That man could mow as much in half a day as five people normally can. Moreover, he also managed to bind and stack all the grain. That man consorted with the devil.
205878: A man coming back from the café met a white woman, to his great fright. The man ran home scared. Because he met the white woman several more times after that, he went to pray to Saint Roch in the little chapel. The man promised the saint that he would make an iron door for the chapel. After that the man never saw the white woman again.
205886: After his death the drossaard (bailiff) came back to haunt in the shape of a big dog. The animal would sit in a corner with a pen behind its ears. When a clergyman tried to banish the drossaard, the ghost said: "When you were a student, you once cut a stick in a ditch. If you had not done that, the stick could have become a mill post". Then another clergyman was sent for, who prayed until he was drenched in sweat. Next a cart of sand was fetched, which the spirit had to walk behind. In the end the clergyman banished the ghost for ninety-nine years under a bridge in Balen.
205889: A man driving a horse and cart past a witch's house was angry when his horses suddenly stopped. When the witch said: "Let them go on!", the horses walked on again.
205890: In Diepenbeek there was a bush to which a ghost had been banished. Whenever someone broke a twig off that bush, a voice rang out: "That is mine!"
205907: A workman who was staying with a farmer for a while found a little cat in the hay at night. The workman grabbed the cat and threw the animal to the ground. The next morning the farmer's wife had a large wound on her head.
205910: In a castle in l'Andenne lived a rich couple whose sons had killed each other in a fight. Because the lord of the castle thus had no more heirs, he decided to leave the castle to the municipality. His money he gave to the devil. No one has ever succeeded in bringing up the three chests of money.
205913: At night the mare lay down on people's hearts, which gave them a feeling of tightness. When the mare was gone, people woke up sweating and could not get up.
205922: A werewolf always had to go out at midnight. One day someone threw the werewolf's band into the fire. The werewolf still wanted to save his band, but they quickly slammed the oven door shut.
205928: A mother was visiting a woman with her child. After the mother had breastfed her child, it fell asleep. When the mother came home, the child was still asleep. Because the child would not wake up, the father said: "Go back to that woman and demand that she undo the harm. Otherwise I'll come and cut her throat." When the mother was back at that woman's house, the woman said: "But I haven't done anything wrong! Just go home, for your child is already awake." And so it was.
205941: A witch who had had her shoes mended by the shoemaker was charged too much. Then the witch blew at the shoemaker, whose face turned white and hurt badly.
205943: A man herding sheep suddenly saw a big black dog approaching. When the man had stabbed the werewolf with a knife, the beast changed into a human.
205970: A hunter had shot at a rabbit several times in vain. After twelve shots the rabbit said: "Haven't you seen my brothers run past?"
205976: Between midnight and one o'clock the dead baron of Betho came driving over the Beukenberg in a burning coach with four horses.
205979: After farmer W. had slaughtered a horse, the farmhand was lying in the hay in the stable. When the hellish hunt passed by a little later, the farmhand heard a voice saying: "Whoever helped to hunt must also help to gnaw". The next moment a horse's haunch fell to the ground. Then the hellish hunt had disappeared.
205993: A farmer in Boorsem had already lost many animals because the stable was bewitched.
205995: A man who consorted with the devil could change himself into a werewolf. One night his father shot at a beast roaming the meadow with a red handkerchief in its mouth. A little later the man's son came in wounded.
206002: A man from Diets-Heur was walking along the road to Vreren to the station. On the way he had to pass a barrier on which a black cat was sitting. The man did not dare to go on because he suspected the cat was a witch.
206017: In Maasmechelen ten men tried in vain to push a gate open. After a while a little old woman who lived across the street said: "Wait a moment, lads, I'll give you a hand." The next moment they got the gate open without any effort.
206018: One day Harie H. accidentally knocked Marie van de B. down with his cart. Although it was an accident, Marie sought revenge. Some time later all the animals of farmer Harie died. Only then was the witch satisfied.
206027: Many people had already come to the castle of Colmont to search for a hidden treasure. One day even clergymen from Luik came to look for the treasure. In the tomb beside the castle witches in the shape of cats always danced. The witches gave instructions to blindfold a young girl and to dig for the treasure meanwhile. The blindfolded girl would then be able to give directions. In the end the treasure chest was found. But whenever they tried to pull it up, it fell back down each time. At the moment the chest came into view, the blindfolded girl fell dead on the ground. The next day the chest had vanished without a trace. It was a treasure that the witches had to guard.
206033: It was said that will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of unbaptised children. A man who was too afraid to baptise a will-o'-the-wisp and ran home found the next morning that a hand had been burned into the door.
206046: Some men playing cards were frightened when the paraffin lamp suddenly went out after there had been two knocks on the door. Because the men were afraid, they quickly went home. On the way one of the men met a large black dog.
206048: Fien van de B. was a witch with exceptional power. Fien could change herself not only into a cat but into many other animals as well. After Fien died, there was no longer a black magpie in the tree.
206049: An old man who lived in a castle always saw a light flickering and always heard screaming. On the castle door was a handprint that could not be removed in any way.
206054: Werewolves owned a little book of magic that they could never get rid of, not even by throwing it in the oven. A man out walking with his girlfriend suddenly said: "I have to go away for a moment. If anything comes at you, throw your handkerchief at the beast." When a werewolf suddenly appeared, the woman did as she had been told. A little later her boyfriend came back, and the woman found that he still had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
206057: A man who suspected that a dog was coming to steal his chickens kept watch by the henhouse at night. At one o'clock in the morning the man saw the dog and shot at it with his gun. Although the man had hit the animal, it still ran on. The next day the man heard from his wife that their maid Marie V. was in bed because her buttocks were full of shot.
206071: An old farmer went to bring in the hay. A little way off stood a woman who kept looking up. When the farmer had loaded the cart half full, a wheel got stuck. The horses were completely drenched in sweat and pulled as hard as they could, but it did no good. A little later a man came by who was surprised that the cart had got stuck on level ground. The man asked: "Did you happen to see Net?", to which the farmer replied: "Yes, she's standing over there." The man took a hammer and struck the axle of the wheel with it. At that moment the woman let out a loud shriek and cried that someone had hit her in the back. The farmer cracked the whip and the horses went on without any trouble.
206072: A boy out walking with his girlfriend suddenly said: "Wait here a moment, because I have to go and pee. If a dog comes at you, throw this red handkerchief at its mouth." As soon as the girl saw a werewolf coming, she did as she had been told. A while later her boyfriend came back. When the two arrived at the girl's house, the boy smiled at his girlfriend. The fibres of the handkerchief were still between his teeth.
206075: A man was always attacked by a black bird whenever he passed the house of a witch. The man would then quickly say a short prayer.
206095: A woman always came to draw water from the well at a married couple's house. In time the couple's child began to grow backwards: the back of its head grew towards its heels. The child's father forced the witch to cure the child, threatening her with the stake. The man built a big fire in his garden and held his dung fork in his hand. A little later the supposed witch came and asked: "How is the child?" The father replied: "I'll tell you how it is! You make sure the child gets better or you go into the fire!" At first the witch denied having anything to do with it. After a while she gave in and said: "If it must be, then!" After that the child was cured at once.
206097: In the Beesteven the oldest inhabitants of Peer and Meeuwen had set the boundary posts. The man from Peer, however, had not respected the legal boundary and had set the post much too far. After his death the man from Peer had to come haunting. At night the ghost could be heard calling: "Where must I leave it? Where must I leave it?" After a while the ghost stayed away of its own accord.
206099: Lieske took a newborn baby in her arms, saying: "Oh, what a pretty little curly head you are!" From that day the child cried for six weeks. When a German friar had read prayers over the child, a long ribbon fell out of the cradle. The friar took it away and tied it around a tree. From then on the child stayed perfectly healthy.
206102: A young man told his father that he had seen a ghost by the road. The father did not dare go back to look.
206105: The witch Tinneke L., who lived in the woods, infested everyone with lice. The only way to prevent it was to keep your hands closed under your apron when you came near her.
206123: A man had hidden a collar in a tree, with which he could turn himself into a werewolf. When someone made a fire with bundles of brushwood to burn the collar, the man was instantly standing by the oven to save his band.
206126: After Kait had given a girl some sweets, the child fell ill. The child would no longer accept anything from anyone except Kait. When the girl lay on her deathbed, the witch kept walking back and forth. The child's father slapped Kait in the face. A wreath was found in the girl's bed.
206129: A young man went for a walk with his girlfriend. The young man, however, had to roam as a werewolf at regular times, so he said to the girl: "I have to go relieve myself behind the hedges. If a dog comes at you, throw your handkerchief at its mouth; then it can do you no harm." A little later a big black dog did indeed come running towards the girl. She threw her red handkerchief at the dog, which tore the cloth to shreds. When the young man came out of the bushes a little later, the girl told him what had happened, to which the boy said: "Well now, surely that can't be true!" When they got home, the girl saw that the red fibres were still hanging between her boyfriend's teeth. She never wanted to see him again.
206137: A man got lost at night because he was bewitched. Only the next morning could the man find his bearings again: he had ended up at the workshops of the mine.
206147: Three men who wanted to play cards were sitting in café de Helm. A gentleman in the café offered to join in as the fourth player. When one of the men bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the gentleman had a goat's foot. The fourth player was the devil.
206159: A man was left alone with a child after his wife died in childbed. Every night, when the woman came to haunt, she took the baby out of the cradle. After a while the man remembered that his wife had once promised to go on a pilgrimage to Scherpenheuvel. The man decided to go on the pilgrimage himself and said: "I'll go in front, just follow me!" At that his wife jumped into his pocket to go along on the pilgrimage. From that day on the ghost was not seen again.
206166: A man going to Hasselt to fetch ham met a horse with fiery eyes at Joffer G.'s café.
206185: The Groemelingenstraat in Neerrepen was haunted. One day some men on their way to the fair saw a black dog appear in the Groemelingenstraat that walked between them.
206191: In Pietersheim a small child had fallen ill after being touched by a witch. The witch had stroked the child's head and had also given it all sorts of things. After a few days the child was dead. In the pillow a wreath of feathers was found, completely closed.
206193: Behind the church in Vreren a silk lady - une madame en soie - walked back and forth in a rustling dress.
206210: If one laid a broom in front of the stable, no witches could come in.
206213: At B.'s place the sheep and cows lay on the ground with snakes around their necks. Under the thresholds of the doors the friars discovered little wreaths and bunches of flowers.
206220: A man working in the marshes of Houthalen suddenly saw a red silk thread. He pulled on the thread and said: "What sort of devil will come out of here?" The next moment the bell sank back to the bottom. The bell had been thrown into the marsh during the French Revolution.
206227: A boy going to the fair with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "I have to go relieve myself. If a big dog comes at you in the meantime, throw my red handkerchief at its mouth." Then the boy crawled into a hollow tree stump and changed himself into a dog. When the boy reappeared a while later, the girl found that he still had the red fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
206239: It was said that a treasure lay buried behind the castle in Nieuwerkerken. Many treasure hunters had found the chest, but as soon as they tried to lift it, it fell back into the hole they had dug.
206243: Between Budel and Maarheze stood a house that was haunted. The house had had many occupants, but nobody wanted to stay there, because at night footsteps and strange music were heard. The priest had sprinkled the house with holy water several times, but it did not help. In the end the house was demolished.
206254: When Sooi E. walked on the road to Paal, he could only be seen from behind. From the front the man was invisible.
206256:
In the old days people were often jumped by a werewolf sitting somewhere behind a tree or a hedge. Between Uikhoven and Boorsem and along the road to Maastricht there were often werewolves. When the werewolf had had itself carried a few hundred metres, it left its victim alone.
A werewolf was a human who had to give in to an irresistible urge.
206260: A woman who came to haunt at night asked for a towel. When she was given one, she said: "I do not want that towel, for it was ironed on a Sunday." The woman was given another towel and burned her hand into it.
206261: A man who saw a cat in a sunken lane said to the animal: "Pussy, pussy, are you coming along?" The cat jumped up at the man and went with him. The next day the man met a woman who said: "Well, you were out late too!"
206278: The witch Belke worked for farmer Mitchie. The witch laid straws in the shape of a cross and predicted that the farmer would have an accident before evening. That same day the farmer fell off the haystack. He was left with a dislocated shoulder from the accident.
206279: A boy going shopping with his girlfriend said to the girl on the way: "If you meet a dog, throw this handkerchief at its mouth." A little later a dog did indeed appear. The girl did as she had been told, whereupon the dog tore the handkerchief to shreds. When the dog turned back into a human, the girl recognised her boyfriend.
206284: A child from Vrijhern cried all the time because it had been struck by the evil hand. Three weeks later the child died.
206291: A werewolf was released after someone had burnt his band in the oven.
206303: A white lady always appeared by the mill of Lummen and disappeared again after a while.
206306: The church of Tongeren once sank near the Waterbroeck. When the roads were laid out there, they followed the pattern of the paths in a churchyard.
206315: A woman from Koersel said to a man: "You won't live much longer." A few years later the man was dead.
206319: Some people could not make butter after a witch had come to visit.
206324: A man who had once challenged a fire-man was walking through the Tierstraat to the shop one evening. The fire-man attacked the man and killed him.
206325: Werewolves could make mice and rats.
206327: In Herk-de-Stad there was a small child who began to cry every night at twelve o'clock. The child could sleep peacefully again after a friar had given a relic to put under its pillow.
206333: A man cycling to Leopoldsburg saw a black cat sitting there and said: "Pussy, be a good one and move aside, for I might run you over." On the way back the man saw the cat again. The animal said to him: "You are lucky you spoke to me so nicely earlier, or else I would have broken all your bones."
206353: Two women had once drowned in a small pond in Diepenbeek. Some people did not dare go near that pond because they feared the dead women would come to haunt.
206383: A farmer often boasted that he was a strong and healthy man. Fien Van S. had heard it and began to laugh. A few days later the man broke out in a rash all over. Because doctor S. from Hamont could not help, the man went to the parish priest. The priest advised the farmer to pray a novena and not to let Fien Van S. into the house any more. And so the man finally got well again.
206384: One evening a man went ferreting with a certain H. When a ferret had crawled into a tree, the dogs suddenly began to bark. The man climbed into the tree and tried to hit the ferret with a stick. The animal then cried out in the Vucht dialect: "Mother!" Because the men were so frightened, they prayed the Gospel of Saint John and then quickly made off.
206398: A farmer had lost three goats after a witch had stroked the animals' backs.
206405: A man walking through the meadow saw a cat sitting on a barrier gate. The man struck at the cat three times, but each time the animal jumped back onto the gate. After the third time the cat said: "Now strike again!" But the man became so scared that he went back the way he had come.
206408: In Kotem there was a child that could not die. So the people decided to visit a defrocked friar in Rekem. The clergyman said to them: "Go. Before you get home, the child will be dead. Don't be afraid when you see a dog on the dike. Step over the dog and go home". When the people got home, the child was indeed dead.
206431: A Walloon farmer walked in the field with a boundary post in his hands. The ghost kept asking: "Où vais-je le mettre?" (Where shall I put it?) One day someone answered: "Où vous l'avez trouvé" (Where you found it). Since then the farmer has not been seen again.
206435: A man was chased at night by a pig that tried to catch him. At the church the pig suddenly vanished.
206444: A woman suspected of witchcraft by the inhabitants of Maaseik was subjected to the ordeal by the parish priest. When the witch went to communion, the host fell out of her mouth. The sexton tried to pick up the host and his finger stuck to the ground.
206453: It was said that a witch from Lauw had bewitched her own son.
206466: Clet G. knew when animals had got loose somewhere without having been there. Clet would then call out: "Go and help over there quickly, the cows have got loose!"
206473: When one lay in bed at night, one could be ridden by the mare. One then heard noises and wailing the whole time and could not move.
206495:
A girl did not know that her boyfriend was a werewolf. During a walk the boy suddenly said: "I have to go away for a bit, because my time has come." When the boy came back half an hour later, the girl saw that he had the threads of a handkerchief between his teeth. Werewolves were wicked people who had to bite into everything they came across.
Sometimes a werewolf also had itself carried.
206506: In the old days will-o'-the-wisps were often seen near marshes. It was said that they were the little souls of unbaptised children.
206507: In Berbroek lived a woman who was said to be a witch. Music could always be heard in her stable and in the air. At a neighbouring farm a strange noise was always heard at night. In the morning the cows stood with their tails tied to the manger. The farmer decided to ride on horseback to the holy little friar of Hasselt. On the way, however, he met the witch, who begged him not to go to the friars. The witch promised she would do no more harm. And so it was.
206524: A card-playing knight had sold his soul to the devil so he could always win at cards. When the knight went to the devil's bridge, where the devil sat waiting for him, Saint Agnes or Saint Gertrude sat behind him on the horse to protect him. For the knight had always prayed to this saint.
206533: A man was going out with a witch's maid. That is how the man found out that the witch put little balls of yarn in the hay.
206537: In a meadow in Nerem, music could always be heard at exactly midnight. Two men of the Loewes family always got up at night to go and listen. In the morning a fine ring was found where the witches had danced.
206538: When Rietsemie lay dying, she did not want the priest to touch her. At the moment the woman died, a flame came out of the stove, although the stove was not lit. In the evening a large black dog sat by the corpse. The next day there was a loud bang, after which the corpse fell off the bed.
206543: A man who was manuring the field was pestered by a cat. Because he could not chase the cat away, the man stabbed the animal with a dung fork. At that the cat suddenly vanished.
206550: A man walking home in the evening saw a hare sitting by the side of the road. The man took the hare and put the animal in his bag. When the man got home, he found only a few stones in the bag.
206558: One evening a rattling was heard in the attic at T.'s. The next day T. heard a watch ticking behind a painting. The priest said to T.: "That is nothing bad. It is a good soul asking for a mass."
206562: A girl from Kleine-Spouwen was going out with a boy who was said to be a werewolf. The boy always had to leave at midnight. When the boy came back, he had the fibres of a red handkerchief between his teeth. That is how the girl knew that her boyfriend really was a werewolf.
206570: In Hamont lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. A man who had already lost five or six sheep went to the dean for advice. "That woman will come by," said the dean, "but you must not chase her away. She will ask you for three things, and you must give her those things." Half a day later the woman did indeed come to ask for two sheaves of straw. The dean had predicted that one more sheep would die, and that after that the misfortune would end. And so it happened.
206571: Will-o'-the-wisps were the little souls of children who had died unbaptised. These children came haunting so that they could still be baptised after their death. It was very difficult to catch hold of a will-o'-the-wisp.
206594: A man driving a horse and cart through Hoelbeek passed the house of Anneke B. At that moment a little black cat jumped onto the road. The horses could go no further until Anneke B. came outside.
206596: In 1887 a baby was born on the Spaanse Brug. When the child was three years old, it turned out to be an incarnation of the devil. After the priest had read prayers over the child, it was delivered.
206597: On a farm in Klein Membruggen lived a man who was friends with a werewolf. In the evenings the werewolf came in the shape of a foal and lay whinnying with its legs on the windowsill. When the man was angry, he could easily master the werewolf.
206599: When a certain Nirkes met the white lady, the man said: "Come, pussycat, come!" At that the lady floated past him and vanished.
206601: To recognise a witch, one had to place one's feet crosswise on her footprint. If the woman in question was a witch, she would look round. Afterwards one had to move on immediately, or else one would be in the witch's power.
206608: A witch could make white mice by scattering earth on the ground.
206613: A woman who was six months pregnant went to visit Bet in the hospital. Bet gave the woman a strange look. Because of the witch, the woman had a miscarriage.
206616: Whoever came into contact with a witch met with misfortune a short time later. When they found no stranger to bewitch, they brought misfortune on their own family.
206618: In the Langsteeg there were many bushes along the road. A man passing by there heard the wood creaking as if a strong wind were blowing.
206629: At midnight the castle gate opened by itself to let in four horses.
206630: The spirit of the drossaard (bailiff) was banished under the bridge for ninety-nine years. After that the drossaard was to return in the shape of a dog.
206635: Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children that floated about in the form of a ball of fire.
206636: By the little chapel in Veulen sat a werewolf in the shape of a dog. It was a man who had not been baptised, and who stopped passers-by.
206648:
Lomme lived by the Ziekeren convent. Siska Vos was a distant relative of his. She also lived in the neighbourhood, and it was said that she was a witch. For example, Siska could predict without fail when Armand, Lomme's father, would win at cards. Because Siska's son Fons was the same age as Lomme, the boys often played together with the neighbourhood children. Sometimes someone would say: "Fons, your mother keeps all sorts of strange things in a chest!" Everyone believed it, because the boy who lived on the Spaanse Brug would know: he had once looked in the chest. When the boys came home, Siska saw them, and she began kicking and hitting the boy from the Spaanse Brug: "That'll teach you, you brat! I won't have you gossiping about me!"
One day Lomme let some pigeons fly out for the first time. Siska saw it and said: "Oh, what lovely pigeons! I hope they don't fly away!" Lomme never saw his pigeons again and got a clip round the ear from his father into the bargain. Whenever Lomme and his friends wanted to play with the pigeons, they had to walk past Siska's house. Out of fear they carried the best pigeons through the meadow, while they went past Siska with the other pigeons. But the witch knew it, every single time.
When Lomme's uncle went poaching in the Ziekerenveld together with Frans Daniels and two others, Siska caught them and began to laugh. The poachers each sat down at a corner of the field. Suddenly a hare came towards Lomme's uncle. The uncle shot but could not hit the animal. The hare went to each of the other three in turn, and they did not manage to shoot it either. Because none of the four poachers could hit the hare, they said: "We'd better go, this is no good: the hare must be Siska."
206650: A woman from Schulen regularly came to a farm to get cheese for free. One day the farmer's wife said she could not give the woman any cheese because she had already promised it to a certain Lambert. At that the woman said angrily: "Well then, you'll be churning butter for a damned long time!" For a whole year the farmer's wife could not make butter because of the witch. When the witch came back a year later, the farmer's wife asked her for half a franc and went on pilgrimage to the chapel of the beech tree in Schulen. After that the farmer's wife could make butter effortlessly again.
206652: Some women were taking a sewing course in Vechmaal. Usually their father, who worked at Munnikenhof in Heks, walked home with them. One day, however, the women had to come back alone. When they passed the Homos farm, they saw a horse standing in the middle of the road. The horse snorted and made a hellish noise. One of the women said: "Make the sign of the cross." When all the women had made the sign of the cross, the horse vanished.
206653: The ghost of Linkhout wandered about at night with a white sheet.
206656: Most black cats cannot get past a crossroads. Anyone who sees a black cat stop before a crossroads knows at once that the animal is a witch.
206662: A little child who had lain sick in its cradle for a very long time could not die and cried all the time. One day the father took the child's bedding to the meadow to burn it. When the man got to the meadow, the witch suddenly stood beside him.
206664: Whenever a cow somewhere was about to calve, the vet's wife always went along with her husband. Strangely enough, each time something was wrong with the calf; one time it had a liver complaint, another time it had been struck by the evil hand. In the end the woman was forbidden to come along with her husband any more. Then the vet said to his wife: "I didn't know you were a witch."
206680: A man grabbed a wandering foal by its lower lip and said: "Go away, in God's name!" The foal immediately ran off. It was a werewolf.
206703: A woman went to the market in Maastricht with her pregnant sister. Suddenly a saleswoman grabbed hold of the pregnant woman and said: "Watch out with those five centimes!" The sister replied: "Oh woman, for God's sake leave my sister alone!" From that day on the pregnant woman woke up every night at twelve o'clock. For two hours she would lie screaming in her bed, claiming that women were coming in through the window. The child she gave birth to a short time later had the face of an old woman. When the child was a year old, it died. Three weeks later the mother died too.
206707: A man went by way of Mal and Sluizen to his work in Liège. When the man was at the bridge in Mal, a cat kept getting under his feet. When the man had struck at the cat, the animal said: "Now strike again", but the man no longer dared.
206729: A girl had to go to the shop late one evening to buy sugar. The girl came back without sugar, because neither of the two shop assistants was there. Outside sat two cats that looked at the girl with a piercing gaze. The shop assistants were witches who could change themselves into cats.
206734: A man who wanted to go in somewhere pushed the key into the keyhole. The man felt feathers everywhere and could not get in. The man was married to a witch who was denying him entry to the house.
206762: At the farm of M. in Nerem a white horse came at midnight. The horse always went to stand between the same two horses. A farmhand had often tried to chase the white horse away, but he never succeeded. When the white horse came for the last time, all the doors and windows began to rattle and then flew off.
206784: A farmer fell every time he passed the house of a witch.
206786: When Trees went to milk the cows on a farm in Bloir, she met Julienne from Mal, who asked: "Do the cows give a lot of milk?" Trees replied: "Not bad at all. I get more than three pounds of butter every day." The next day, however, the milk curdled so badly that Trees could not make butter. The fathers had already come to read prayers over the farm, but that had not helped. A certain Nicolaers from Berg said to Trees: "You are bewitched! You must go and ask for pieces of the Easter candle." From sexton Harry D., Trees got a small piece of the Easter candle. After Trees had thrown the piece into the cream or rubbed the cow's udders with it, she could make butter again.
206791: Along a narrow road with many bramble bushes and tree stumps there was often a werewolf that had itself carried by passers-by. If you did not go fast enough, the werewolf kicked its victim in the calves.
206824: In a house a cat came secretly every day to drink the milk. One day the people cut off one of the cat's legs. The next day a woman from the neighbourhood wore a bandage around her arm. The woman claimed she had fallen, but the people knew better...
206826: Because Toon van E. had had severe toothache for days, he went to consult the parish priest. On the way, however, he was held back by a strange force; it felt as if he were wading through water. Toon went back home and set off for the priest a second time the next day. This time he did reach his destination. If Toon had turned back on the second day too, the priest could no longer have helped him.
206828: In the old distillery there was a stable with ten horses in it. At night a strange noise was heard in the stable. When people went to look, they saw that the horses were standing with their legs in the air and their chains were all tangled. A black dog came into that stable.
206831: Near Kortessem stood an oak that growled when people passed it.
206940: Castle built with buckwheat flour; underground passages from the castle; hidden treasure.
207385: Witches make mice; a witch who is not yet fully trained makes mice without tails.
207386: A person is forced by an inexplicable power to walk into the water, and believes that people who can do more than others are the cause.
207394: When passing a cross of straws, a witch jumps over it and looks round.
207404: A witch's wreath disappears when the wreath is put in a cloth; after a blessed palm is stuck in the keyhole when a horse is ridden by the nightmare, the witch is discovered.
207412: Witch causes someone to get lice; how the lice disappear; fear of the witch.
207416: Underground bells, fire-man, little lights in the woods that are the souls of unborn children.
207423: In the evening a dog jumps on someone's back and lets itself be carried; a dog or cat that walks in front of people is often a witch.
207441: The narrator does not know what a hengstespoor and a hengstepad are.
207443: Some people can send mice wherever they want.
207444: Fear of people who can crawl through a drain hole or keyhole, or who stand listening at a closed window.
207713: At the place where a witch lives, a carriage drives into the water.
207714: A witch prevents the transport of wood, so that horses refuse to take a certain road. When another road is taken, the witch is seen flying.
207720:
A story about little men, as big as toddlers, who lived in Eerselsberg. They were shy of people. You did not see them during the day. At night the men fetched food in Tongerlo and then brought the stone pots (which had held the food) back clean.
The narrator once looked into the little men's den himself, although his father had actually forbidden him to go there. They had a bed of planks and straw, a table and chairs made of posts and planks, and a spread (a kind of mat). There was also an iron chain with a hook and a thing to put a pan on. The narrator does not know what they used as fuel.
The little men did not help people. They did nothing.
The little men had beards and wore a blue smock, a red scarf, sometimes with a bow and a matchbox attached, and a black silk cap with a peak.
They left when bells were put in the tower and began to ring, because they could not bear that ringing.
The narrator does not know whether there were also women, but there were certainly no children.
There must also have been little men in Helden. The narrator once saw four little men pass by, coming from Helden. The little men marched towards Venlo, but the narrator does not know exactly where they were going. The little men carried a small knapsack on their backs, wore "high clogs" and said nothing.
207740:
The narrator tells of his experience with witches. A witch had made one of his children ill by touching it. The child had diarrhoea for twenty-one days, day and night. He went to the parish priest. At first the priest dismissed it as superstition, but then advised the father to go to the Kavaaiberg (according to the accompanying text the Kalvarieberg; Calvarieberg) with eleven men. As soon as the men had arrived there and started praying, the child was cured.
Another witch, a woman from Helden, also lived next door to him.
207743: Proof that someone is a witch: she looks round if you step crosswise in her footprints.
207751: There are said to be witches even now. The narrator once experienced the following. It sounded as if rijksdaalders (two-and-a-half-guilder coins) were clattering onto the roof of the barn, sackfuls of them, and then falling to the ground. But nothing was to be found on the ground. This was a witch's trick.
207798:
Stories about witches.
A man kicked at a black cat sitting on the path and said: "Go away, black witch." Then as many as a hundred black cats appeared and tried to scratch his eyes out.
Witches sometimes flew on broomsticks.
You can shut a witch in by means of a little cross and a blessed palm branch through the door. Then she can no longer get out.
Every evening a woman came to visit a man with an open sore on his leg to commiserate with him. At some point people realised that she was a witch and was preventing the leg from healing. She was shut in the house by means of a palm branch through the door and had to promise to let the leg heal. The next evening the wound on the leg had closed.
207807: A woman regarded as a witch praised a man's fine new trousers and touched them. A little later the man was crawling with lice. The woman had done it.
207814: In the morning a returned dead person can be seen, who vanishes when the Angelus is rung.
207818: In the narrator's region the werewolf was not a wolf-man, as it is often depicted elsewhere, but someone who jumped on lonely travellers at night and had himself carried on their backs.
207819: A house fire was seen as a harbinger of a death in the family.
207820: Certain things were seen as omens of an accident or disaster, such as a magpie chattering by someone's house, breaking a mirror, or scissors lying crossed on the table. Finding a safety pin foretells a quarrel.
207822: Werewolf that jumps onto people's backs turns out to be a farmhand in a skin. After the skin is burned, the farmhand is released.
207823: After a gift is refused to a beggar woman, pebbles on the harrow prevent the ox from being harnessed.
207827: One morning the horses stood in the stable with their manes tied together. This was the work of a witch.
207828: After a short talk with a woman, a man was suddenly crawling with lice. The woman was seen as a witch. The priest's blessing rid the man of the lice.
207831: A ball of fire, the soul of an unbaptised child, tries to push people into the water.
207832: A black cat vanishes after being told it must disappear if it is the devil.
207834: A phantom wagon drives at great speed through a gate into a cellar where money is always being counted.
207835: A farmer pulls down his farmhouse after being struck by a witch's spell. During the rebuilding the witch bricks marl from the demolished farmhouse into the wall, so the misfortune continues.
207840: Meeting a black dog with a bell around its neck in a cemetery.
207841: Werewolf stays away after a thrashing.
207845: Werewolf jumps on people and has itself carried; band that gives power is hidden in the oven.
207852: After a farmer's wife is murdered by bokkenrijders (goat riders, a band of robbers), she haunts the abandoned farm.
207854: Sighting and description of a ghost.
207856: Release from the compulsion to be a werewolf.
207858: A witch who is not given an apple prevents the apples from being picked and leaves the pickers stuck in the tree.
207860: That a stuck cart can move on after the spokes are struck with a whip points to a pact with the devil.
207862: The narrator, who does not believe in witches, hits a black cat without anything happening.
207863: Thought that a ghost is walking along, but the cause is the rubbing of the ribs of corduroy trousers.
207866: At his funeral mass a dead man walks with the trees he stole during his life.
207869: Ghosts in various places and in various forms.
207876: A boundary-stone mover returns as a ghost after death; release comes when the stone is put back in the right place.
207877: A witch causes all kinds of misfortune.
207880: Meeting a white woman floating through the air.
207885: A talking hare refuses in the end to do its trick.
207895: Lifting a spell by praying and blessing with holy water.
207899: Warding off a witch and bewitchment with a relic.
207908: On Christmas night a flock of sheep suddenly appears and disappears.
207909: Person who says he is not afraid of the werewolf falls ill after encountering the werewolf.
207910: A witch turns someone's head back to front by magic.
207911: After the narrator shoots at a black cat, his cats die and a plague of mice breaks out. A witch advises him to have cats brought in to stop the trouble.
207912: A cat keeps walking along until a wayside cross, disappears, comes back; a dog does not dare to attack the cat.
207913: Meeting a wit wijf (white woman) at night.
207915: A kettinghond (chain dog, a phantom dog dragging a chain) roaming the village.
207917: Belief that a Freemason was murdered by the devil.
207921: After a black cat is struck, several cats appear and injure the man.
207922: Werewolf lies still after a fight; the next day men's clothes are found at the spot.
207923: Stabbed werewolf turns out to be a man in disguise.
207925: Experiences in a haunted house with a ghost in the form of a rabbit.
207926: A horse is halted by a witch; the witch gives an iron ring, after which the horse goes on and there are no more problems.
207927: Black fellows vanish after a formula is spoken and a cross is made, leaving a smell of sulphur behind.
207930: Seeing a large black phantom dog.
207931: A black cat, a crow, a howling dog, or seeing a white horse is a voorloop (an apparition foreshadowing an event) of a death.
207937: At the place where a ghost asks where the boundary stone should be put back, a horse refuses to go on. The next day there is a deep hole at that spot.
207938: The devil fetches witches from a gathering with the wild tram, the devil's coach.
207940: Werewolf jumps on someone's back and makes itself carried.
207943: A ghost driven out by a priest's blessing; haunting caused by hidden money that was unlawfully earned.
207944: Dying people who have played dice die with a great deal of noise when clergymen visit them.
207945: Bewitchment after giving something away for free; after blessing and laying a straw on the threshold the ghost can no longer get in.
207946: The nightmare (mare) stays away after the stable is blessed.
207947: A priest who does not say the thanksgiving after celebrating mass returns after his death to say mass.
207952: Cart is halted by a gentleman dressed in black; after it is seen that the wheel has thirteen spokes, the cart can go on.
207956: Conjuring mice by magic; meeting a phantom dog.
207962: After being struck, a phantom dog turns into a human; threatens death if betrayed; the man dies a short time later.
207963: A black dog walks along with a sorcerer and someone possessed by the devil.
207964: Magic tricks of a sorcerer; release from the ability to do magic after overlezen (exorcism by reading prayers) by friars.
207965: A wagon is halted by a witch.
207976: Black men at a haunted spot.
207977: In the evening a tree bends to the ground.
207979: Finding a wounded man after shooting a hare.
207984: A reader of bad books comes into contact with the devil through them and becomes possessed; cured by clergymen.
207986: During Mass the hare cannot be hit, afterwards it can; the hare is a wounded witch, who points out that a sin was committed by missing Mass.
207988: Wounded cat turns out to be a witch.
207989: Inexplicable crying of a child must be the work of the devil.
207990: Breaking a spell after a blessing by a father (priest).
207994: A wizard in league with the devil disappears after someone holds their finger on the cross of the rosary.
207996: A haunted gate that strikes turns out to be men who think they are fighting the gate but have attacked each other.
207997: A banished parish priest must wander as a ghost; each year he may take one step towards the church where he will find eternal rest.
207999: Meeting a large black dog with a jingling chain, the kettinghond (chain dog).
208004: The seventh thresher is suspected of being in league with the devil and disappears after being confronted about it.
208010: After losing her castle, the owner haunts the place.
208017: A ghost hit with a club turns out to be someone playing ghost.
208018: If butter-making fails, go to the fathers for holy water.
208019: The ability to work magic disappears after a man returns to the faith.
208021: A boundary-stone mover haunts and is released by the answer to put the stone back.
208022: A witch as a cat or another animal on a turnstile.
208024: A witch halts a horse and wagon; they are freed by blessing with holy water.
208027: After the thirteenth spoke is broken, the cart can go on; the next day a wounded woman is seen.
208030: Breaking a spell by putting something obtained from the fathers into the bewitched butter.
208033: A priest reads prayers over a bewitched farm after a banished hare returns.
208040: The way in which it is discovered that someone is a werewolf.
208044: A witch predicts the return of pigeons, and failing and passing an exam.
208045: Spell on a churn disappears after hanging up medals from the fathers, praying and chasing away a strange cat.
208046: While reading the Gospel of St John, a priest sees who consorts with the devil.
208047: Dog walking alongside says the man must carry it and jumps on his back.
208051: Werewolf makes itself carried and relieves itself while being carried; the farmhand is the werewolf.
208053: Witch in the shape of a black cat walks ahead of a woman.
208058: An unhittable hare is shot after all with a blessed candle on the gun barrel.
208065: Haunted place where poaching with a gun at midnight does not succeed.
208070: A person possessed by the devil loses his devil's tooth after friars drive out the devil.
208074: A man possessed by the devil cannot get to the church.
208075: Pursuit by a white ghostly figure.
208077: A boundary-stone mover finds rest when he puts the boundary stone back.
208080: In the evening a lady dressed in black walks along with someone.
208085: A hare that was shot and wounded turns out to be a witch.
208086: Men in animal skins jump on passers-by; getting rid of the skin by burning it in an oven.
208093: The belief that a witch injured a cow's udder out of revenge.
208097: Appearance of a werewolf, someone wearing a sheepskin.
208099: A stranger gets a great deal of work done without ever being seen working.
208101: Gnomes work at night; they stay away after tripping over scattered peas.
208104: After an iron ring someone wears is burned, the person is released from magic power.
208106: Heard talk about cats, a carter, a way to recognise witches.
208107: The sound of rubbing corduroy trouser legs causes fear.
208109: Fire-man chases the person who called out to him; hand burnt into the door.
208112: Witchcraft that makes it impossible to make butter.
208113: A person possessed by the devil wants to be rid of the devil's power but cannot reach the church.
208115: Fake werewolf who makes himself carried is struck down.
208117: Man walks all night long; only gets home in the morning.
208119: Bewitching of cows; warded off by overlezen (reciting prayers over someone).
208126: Rustling fabric suggests a ghost walking along.
208127: Girls lose each other and get lost; they hear a bell ringing.
208128: At midnight hauntings at various farms; praying to ward them off.
208135: Fear of haunting, in reality moving trees and the rubbing sound of corduroy trouser legs.
208141: Although there are twelve people, thirteen are counted; after a recount there are twelve again, but the imprint of a goat's hoof is seen.
208142: At a bedridden witch's home, the shutters open by themselves, the house is clean and there seems to be no one lying under the sheets.
208151: Haunting at a well at night.
208152: A cart is halted by a werewolf in the wheel; its power is broken by prayer and blessing with holy water.
208155: After a black cat is wounded, a woman turns out to be injured the next day.
208157: The haunting is the sound of a basket on someone's back.
208159: A person who cycles over a sign of the cross at a crossroads does not get home until morning.
208160: Because of a bewitched turnstile, the narrator does not get home until the next morning.
208161: A black fellow in the field turns out to be a plough.

208473:
A rich farmer, known as Duutsje Jan, was not too particular about honesty. In his lodging house with a sheepfold, for example, he was said to swap his guests' best sheep for his own worst ones.
Duutsje Jan did not go to church either. All sorts of stories went around about him: the winnowing mill, for example, turned by itself, and a big black dog was seen twice, by the maid who was milking the cows and by a neighbour who came into the yard. It is suggested that this may have been Duutsje Jan himself.
In the end things went badly for Duutsje Jan. All his livestock died. He was wealthy enough to buy new livestock, but that livestock died too. This kept happening.

208489:
A witch would sometimes fondle a child and give it a sweet or some fruit. It was thought that a child could fall ill from this. If the mother heard about it, the child had to hand over the pear (for example). The mother cut the pear in half. If there were no pips in it, the pear came from a witch.
If a child was ill, you had to look in the child's pillow and you would find a witch's wreath there. If the wreath was not quite finished yet, the child might still be saved. Often the parish priest or a friar was called in. He would then say that the people should pray well or go on pilgrimage, and then the folk were calm again.

If you walked crosswise in a woman's footprints (that is, with your left foot on the print of her right foot and your right foot on the print of her left foot) and the woman looked round, she was a witch.
Witches could not leave a house past a crucifix. Sometimes a crucifix was hidden under the threshold so that no witch could enter.
The narrator lived with his parents in a very old little farmhouse. On the front door was a 'Greek cross' as protection against evil. This cross was painted on the door afresh every year with the whitewash brush.

Story about the witch's scales. If you weighed less than fifty kilos you were a witch. Expression for skinny girls: she's just above witch weight.
If you were that light you were practically floating already, hence also flying on the broom.
Funny story from Blerick: the witches there are modern; they had already invented the wheel. The young witches there floated in the wooden rim of a sieve instead of on a broomstick.

209117: Stories about working in the coal mine. Underground you were not allowed to whistle, and in the lift cage you had to be quiet. Women in the mine was really not done. If you did not keep to the rules, you could anger the mountain spirit or bring misfortune on yourself. Long ago miners wore special clothing, including a kind of monk's hood. This made them look somewhat like gnomes. The narrator also mentions kobolds, bergmunchen (mountain monks) and venediger (Venetians, treasure-seeking spirit miners). The work in the mountain and underground was surrounded by an air of mystery.
